11. Red lines programmers and tech workers can easily cross19 items

If the company doesn't pay monthly compensation after you leave, press it in writing; after 3 months unpaid you may terminate it; if your role never touched trade secrets, you can ask to have the clause declared invalid13Code written on work time or with company resources belongs to the company; build your own open-source projects on your own time and devices, and keep company code out14Building a product on GPL and other open-source code: open-source as the license requires or change licenses; don't assume 'nobody will notice'15For apps, collect only the personal information the service requires; get guardian consent for under-14s; write the privacy policy clearly16Complete ICP filing before a website or app goes live, and keep logs for at least 6 months under classified-protection requirements17Before offering generative AI services to the public, run the required security assessment and algorithm filing, and label AI-generated content18Don't make or distribute tools that auto-skip or block other apps' ads — even free and offline, they can be judged unfair competition19Don't run 'AI relay stations' reselling overseas large-model APIs at low prices: a station operator in Shanghai has already been criminally detained
12. Startups and business: don't lose the family fortune24 items
1Start up only with money you can afford to lose; don't touch the family savings and don't borrow to open2Don't sign personal guarantees for company loans — spouses above all shouldn't sign3Choose the right entity before opening: sole proprietors and partners are liable to the last cent; only limited companies are 'limited'4Don't be a nominee shareholder; don't hold equity on someone else's behalf5Before buying a franchise, check the MOFCOM filing, obtain written disclosure, and write a 'cooling-off period' into the contract6Before registering, settle the name, premises, business scope, and registered capital; with complete paperwork you can get the license on the spot7In trades that need permits, don't open until the permit is in hand8In the food business, first find which tier you're in: production and catering need licenses; selling only prepackaged food needs only filing; fresh meat and vegetables need no permit9Bag it and sell it, and it's prepackaged food: the label must carry production date, shelf life, and ingredient list — not one missing10Ordinary food may never claim to cure disease: labels, manuals, ads, and livestream scripts all count11Food has a criminal threshold: selling diseased meat or substandard goods is already a crime; adulterating with toxic or harmful substances means 5 years minimum, regardless of amount12Getting the license starts your filing duty: even with no income, file a zero return on time (submit the all-zeros form)13Invoicing follows real transactions only; as a small-scale taxpayer, use your full tax-free quota14Anyone claiming to be the tax bureau pressing you to pay or file is a scammer; handle taxes only through the e-tax bureau or 1236615When collecting money, contract a forfeitable deposit, not a refundable advance; spell out the penalty amount; and vet credit terms like a lender16Sign a written contract within the first month of hiring and complete social insurance registration within 30 days17Pay wages per contract and law; put raises, loans, and bonuses in writing18Sell before you build: validate demand with presales and small orders, then fund production19Once the sample is made, run it through a mass-production checklist before talking about starting production20For every batch you buy, keep the invoices and the supplier's details; refuse goods priced clearly below market: when an employee sources fakes, it's the boss who gets sentenced21Artwork on products, packaging, tags, and promo images must be your own or licensed; changing a color or adding an icon doesn't count as 'changed'22Follow the procedures on the job; for goodwill beyond the procedures, first think through who bears the responsibility23When it loses money, exit by procedure: deregister the simple way if you can, go bankrupt if insolvent — don't just leave it there24Before paying for shop-management services, opening courses, or 'no-inventory' models, ask what extra charges come later and where the sales will come from
13. Emergencies: what to do first44 items
1Someone collapses and isn't breathing: start hard chest compressions immediately, and have a bystander call 120 and fetch an AED2An elderly person falls or someone collapses: crouch down, speak to them, and call 120; don't rush to lift them. With strangers, walking away is also legal — but if you stop, don't move the person yourself3Sudden facial droop, one-sided arm weakness, or slurred speech: call 120 immediately — don't wait, don't drive yourself4Sudden violent dizziness, double vision, one eye going dark, or a finger that can't find your own nose tip: treat as stroke and call 1205One eye suddenly blacking out like a curtain falling — even if it clears in minutes — still means the ER that day as a stroke6One eye aching, pressurized, and red, with a rainbow ring around lights plus headache and nausea: same-day eye emergency7Chest pressure, pain, or tightness lasting more than 15 minutes: call 120 — don't tough it out and don't drive yourself8Sudden tearing pain migrating from chest to back to flank: call 120 and say clearly that 'the pain is moving'9A sudden 'worst headache of your life' hitting peak within an hour: go to the ER now for a head CT10Two weeks to months after a head bump, an older person becoming unsteady, sluggish, drowsy, or weak on one side: get a head CT11One leg suddenly swollen, tight, and tender to the touch: see a doctor promptly; add sudden breathlessness or chest pain and call 120 now12Heavy bleeding: press the wound hard with your hand first; if a limb can't be controlled, apply a tourniquet — and call 12013Bitten or scratched by a dog or cat: alternate rinsing with soap solution and running water for 15 minutes, then get the vaccine that day14Burn: immediately flush with cool running water for 20 minutes; no toothpaste or soy sauce15Sudden whole-body rash, breathlessness, or faintness: treat as anaphylactic shock — call 120 right away and say why16Someone convulsing: clear the surroundings, lay them on their side, time it on a watch, and put nothing in their mouth17A diabetic suddenly shaking, cold-sweating, or slurring: give 15 grams of sugar first, then recheck after 15 minutes18Someone electrocuted: cut the power first, then move the source away with a dry stick or the like; never grab them bare-handed19CO alarm sounds, or everyone in the room has headache and nausea at once: get outside first, then call20Swallowed cleaner, pesticide, or medication: don't induce vomiting; bring the bottle and get care immediately; splashed in eye or on skin, flush with plenty of water for at least 15 minutes21Acids, alkalis, and other chemicals on skin: strip contaminated clothing and flush with plenty of running water; for eyes, hold the lids open and flush — finish the full time before leaving22In heat: dizziness, nausea, no sweating, or confusion — move to shade at once, remove clothing, douse with water to cool; if confused, give no water and call 12023A heatstroke victim who's still alert: give cool lightly salted water or a sports drink in small, frequent sips — no gulping, no alcohol or sugary drinks24In a fire: crawl low, touch the door before opening — if it's hot, don't; take the stairs, never the elevator; once out, don't turn back25Seeing someone drowning: first call for help and dial 110/120, extend a pole or throw flotation — don't go in yourself26Someone choking and unable to speak: stand behind, give 5 back blows plus 5 abdominal thrusts; if they collapse, start CPR27Lost or broken down in gobi, desert, or uninhabited areas: stay put or stay by the vehicle, report your location first, then shade and insulate yourself, ration water, and don't wander28Shivering, slurred words, unsteady steps mean hypothermia: change out of wet clothes, wrap up, warm the trunk first, and drink hot sweet drinks — no alcohol29Snakebite: sit down and stay still, remove rings and watches, reach hospital fast for antivenom — no cutting, no sucking, no tight binding30In an earthquake, first note what building you're in: in structures built to seismic standards, shelter in place; in old buildings that may collapse with a door a few steps away, get out31Meeting bears, wild boars, or packs of feral dogs: don't run, don't scream, don't make eye contact; back away slowly at an angle32Thunderstorm in the open: get inside a hard-topped vehicle or a building; avoid ridgelines, lone trees, water, and metal33Going to altitude: ascend slowly by sleeping altitude (how high you sleep each night); descend if symptoms worsen — don't push through34Tick embedded: pull it straight out with pointed tweezers close to the skin; no oils, no burning35Boil all wilderness water before drinking; a rolling boil for one minute suffices — no need to boil longer at altitude36A stranger demands money in the wild: give it, don't fight, note their features, and call the police once you're clear37Stumbling on a group brawl: walk away; don't break it up, don't gawk, don't pick up anything off the ground; to report, retreat to a safe distance and call 11038Possible HIV exposure: get post-exposure prophylaxis within 72 hours — the earlier the better39Injured or out of pocket from rescuing someone: first go after the wrongdoer and medical insurance, then apply for good-samaritan recognition40Knife, rebar, or glass stuck in the body: press around it to stop the bleeding — never pull it out41Suspected fracture: stop moving it, support it in place, ice for no more than 20 minutes, and never straighten it yourself42After sexual assault: get somewhere safe and call 110; don't shower, don't wash clothes, don't tidy the room before the forensic exam, and get to a hospital within 72 hours43An infant under 1 who's choking and can't cry: 5 back blows face-down, then 5 chest presses face-up, alternating — never the abdomen44An infant under 1 unresponsive and not breathing normally: call 120 on speaker and do infant CPR — 30 compressions, 2 breaths
14. Account and information security10 items
1Turn on two-factor for email, payment, and social accounts; prefer phone pop-up confirmation, with SMS codes as the fallback2Your email gets its own password, never repeated on any website3Set a lock-screen passcode on the phone and a PIN on the SIM4Phone lost? Do this in order: suspend the SIM, lock it remotely, change passwords, report to police, freeze bank cards5Card fraud: report and freeze first, then police, then demand the bank compensate — proving 'it was you who spent it' is the bank's burden6Review each account's logged-in devices and authorized apps every so often; clear out the ones you don't use7Don't click 'agree to all' just to use an app: they cannot refuse you service for declining to share non-essential data8You may view, copy, correct, and delete your personal information — and sue if refused9You don't have to accept facial recognition: where alternatives exist they can't offer face-only, and if you refuse they must give you another way10Never hand code, keys, or private data to 'AI relay stations' of unknown provenance — above all when letting AI execute commands automatically
15. Renting and buying a home9 items
1The deposit amount, refund deadline, and deduction conditions must be written into the contract2Utilities cut, locks changed, or threats to force you out: call the police and preserve evidence first — regulations forbid forcing you out this way3Agents may not collect or pass on rent and deposits; pay the landlord directly4Before renting long-term apartment housing, check its supervised escrow account; don't pay a year up front to save money5If the place is sold during your lease, the lease still holds — you don't have to move6Before signing, check the title deed and mortgage status; run all payments through bank transfers with the purpose noted7For second-hand homes where the agent collects the purchase money, it must go through the agent's dedicated escrow account at a bank8Don't rent partitioned units: the smallest lawful rental unit is a room as originally designed; kitchens, bathrooms, and balconies may not be lived in9Urban hukou holders who want to live in the countryside: rent rural houses only; don't buy homestead land or houses on it
16. Living with a chronic illness9 items
1Take the full course as prescribed; don't quit just because you feel better2Get the outpatient chronic/special disease designation first, then the cross-region filing; hypertension, diabetes, radio- and chemotherapy, dialysis, and anti-rejection treatment can then settle directly away from home3Do follow-ups at the intervals the doctor sets, and record every reading in the same notebook4Don't suspend proper treatment to try folk remedies or supplements5For a stable chronic condition, a community hospital can dispense up to 12 weeks of medication at a time6Before signing with a community family doctor, ask what's covered by insurance and what's out of pocket7Once diagnosed with diabetes, get a retinal exam, then follow-up at the doctor's intervals; check your feet once a year8After kidney stones, drink 2.5–3 liters of water a day and keep salt under 6 grams9Once diagnosed with gout, take urate-lowering medication long-term and keep blood uric acid below 360 µmol/L for good
17. When there are elderly at home9 items
1While the elder is still lucid, designate their future guardian in writing2Make the will; remember a later will overrides an earlier one, and notarized wills no longer take priority3Keep the elder's money in a separate account, with a two-person confirmation rule for large spending4Equip the elder with a line they can always say: 'I need to go home and discuss it with my family'5Any 'invest in retirement' scheme that wants money up front is untouchable: cards, beds, senior apartments, resort stays, senior products — all the same illegal fundraising6Beyond the insurer's reverse-mortgage pension product, touch no 'house-for-pension' schemes, and never mortgage the house to buy wealth products7With an elder long bedridden or severely disabled, apply to the medical insurance authority where they're enrolled for long-term care insurance; it is not only for the elderly8With someone long bedridden, treat pressure sores as public enemy number one: get an alternating-pressure air mattress, turn them at set intervals, and check the bony prominences once a day9When the elder's cataracts impede seeing the road, get an eye evaluation for surgery; with both eyes affected, don't delay the second too long
18. Is Raising a Kid Cost-Effective?6 items
1Count what you can claim first: the national childcare subsidy is 3,600 yuan per child per year, paid up to age 32Maternity leave is 98 days; the maternity allowance comes from the maternity insurance fund, based on your employer's average monthly employee wage of the previous year3Know this rule: no pay cuts or dismissal for pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding4Do the time math by 'whose time gets used up', not by 'how hard it feels'5Split the money math into three stages: ages 0 to 3, compulsory education, and everything after6A child for your parents, a child for the marriage, a child for your old age — keep a separate ledger for each
19. Employment, Departure, and Work Injuries18 items
1Overtime pay runs at 1.5x, 2x, or 3x; if it isn't paid, complain to the labor inspection authority — late payment adds another 50% to 100%2Annual leave is 5, 10, or 15 days by total years worked; days you couldn't take convert to cash at 300% of your daily wage3Probation has legal caps, pay can't drop below 80%, and it can only be agreed once4If you're laid off, first work out your N: one month's wage per full year, and half a month for less than six months5If the company fires you without 30 days' notice, it owes you one extra month's pay6If the company terminates you unlawfully, compensation is twice the standard severance amount7Don't sign 'resigning voluntarily for personal reasons' — sign it and your N is gone8Before you leave, save your payslips, attendance records, labor contract, social insurance records, and chat logs9Before taking a post with dust, noise, or chemicals, check whether the contract names the hazards; the three occupational health checks are arranged and paid for by the employer10Damage from dust, noise, and chemical toxins is irreversible: the employer must provide protective gear, and you can refuse work with no protective measures in place11Injured at work or hit on your commute: the first step is a work-injury determination — if the employer won't file, file it yourself12Don't believe 'it only counts if you make it to your desk': if you suddenly feel unwell, call 120 first — don't rush to clock in13If your employer never paid into work-injury insurance, you still get the same benefits, paid in full by the employer at the same standard14Once your condition stabilizes, get a labor capacity assessment; the disability grade converts directly into money15Keep straight the three payments for a death at work: the funeral allowance, the dependent-relatives pension, and the one-time death-at-work benefit16If you're long bullied, insulted, or obstructed at work, don't tough it out: document everything first, then complain, call the police, or seek arbitration depending on the nature of it17When you leave, get a separation certificate from the employer stating your contract term, departure date, position, and years of service18When you get severance, check the income tax first: it's tax-free up to 3 times the local average employee wage of the previous year; the excess is taxed separately, not folded into that year's salary
20. Caring for a Newborn13 items
1Baby sleeps on their back, on a firm surface, in your room but not your bed, with nothing soft in the crib2Get the first hepatitis B vaccine dose within 24 hours of birth3Complete every vaccine in the national immunization program — it's free throughout; if you miss one, only the missed doses get made up4For the first 6 months, breastfeed only — not even water; from 6 months, add solids and keep breastfeeding5Mix formula with water at 70 ℃ or above, let it cool before feeding, and throw out what's left6No honey before age 17The vitamin K shot at birth is a must8A baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38 ℃ goes straight to the hospital — no watching and waiting at home9Never shake a baby, no matter how exhausted or angry you are10For diapers, judge by three things, not the brand: the fit, how often you change them, and whether the brand has ever failed a spot check11For big items, go in order: borrow, buy secondhand, buy new — don't kit out everything at once12If your child has severe eczema or an egg allergy, don't avoid peanuts — introduce them early under a doctor's guidance, but never feed whole peanuts13Watch for jaundice warning signs in a newborn: yellow within 24 hours of birth, getting more yellow, can't be woken and won't feed, or pale stools — go to the hospital that day
21. Going Abroad, Travel, and Safety Overseas11 items
1Before departure, check the foreign ministry's travel advisories once; anywhere marked 'do not travel' — don't go2Save the 12308 hotline and the local embassy or consulate's consular-protection numbers in your phone, and keep a paper copy in your wallet — don't wait for trouble to look them up3Know what consular protection can and can't do: it can arrange visits, it can't get you out, and you pay your own costs4Buy insurance that covers overseas medical care and medical evacuation, not just flight delay5Treat every 'high-paying job overseas' as a scam; people tricked into online-fraud work can face exit restrictions even after returning6Overseas cash withdrawals can't exceed 100,000 yuan a year — and that's all your cards combined7Photograph your passport, visa, and ID and store a copy in the cloud; if lost, report to the police first, then apply for a travel document8Before driving abroad, confirm the destination recognizes a Chinese license; 'international driving permits' sold online are mostly worthless paper9Before using an agency for visas, study abroad, or immigration, ask whether it's registered with the immigration administration10Don't issue invitation letters for strangers, and don't let anyone use your name for entry-exit procedures11Before leaving the country, send your itinerary, lodging, and travel companions to a family member, and agree on how often you'll check in
22. How to Unwind: Entertainment Venues and Stress Relief10 items
1Before entering a KTV, bar, or escape room, spot the emergency exits; if they're locked or blocked, go somewhere else2Ask for the price list before ordering; entertainment venues must post prices — no 'play first, settle later'3If anyone in the venue passes you 'something', leave at once — harboring or supplying drugs isn't 'helping a friend'4Don't take candy or snacks from strangers, don't drink anything that left your sight, and don't accept a vape pod handed to you5For script-murder games and escape rooms, skip ones housed in residential buildings or below the second basement level6When your mood sinks, go walk or run — the antidepressant effect size (how big the effect is) scales with intensity7When anxiety disrupts your life, a mindfulness-based stress reduction course works as well as common anti-anxiety medication8To recover on the spot, spend 5 minutes on 'cyclic sighing': a two-stage inhale, then a drawn-out exhale9Treat regular time with people as a health expense — don't reach out only when you feel bad10If you live near green space, use it — walking, strolling, or just sitting all count
23. Which Skills Are Worth Learning23 items
1Under 16, 'going to work' isn't an option: an employer who hires you is fined 5,000 yuan a month — anyone willing to hire you is running illegal labor2Put 'is school worth it' into the mortality math too: each additional year of education cuts adult mortality risk by about 1.9%3Before judging whether degrees have depreciated, look at the national education mix: only 15,467 in every 100,000 people have a college education4Before saying school is 'unaffordable', run the numbers on policy: vocational high school tuition is mostly free, the grant is 2,300 yuan, and student loans go up to 20,000 yuan a year5Not getting into academic high school isn't a dead end: vocational schools offer integrated through-track admission and separate exams, and skilled-job hiring can lower its education requirements6Turn 'study or work' into a calculation: three years of early wages weighed against decades of annual income difference7Start from the baseline: each extra year of education brings an average global private return (the part landing in your own income) of about 9% a year8Before paying for a certificate, check it's in the national occupational qualification catalog or on the list of assessment bodies filed with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security9For training, use government-subsidized channels first — don't jump straight into self-funded commercial courses10When picking a skill, favor ones that need hands-on work and on-the-spot judgment — those are hardest for automation to displace11Before learning, confirm the skill has a graded assessment and whether the grade can be turned into money12Don't take 'they say it pays well online' as proof of demand — check the local shortage-occupation list and subsidy catalog13For the same money and time, choose short-cycle programs that lead straight to a job14When you finish studying, close the book and test yourself first — don't go back and reread15Spread the same study time over several days — don't cram it all into one go16Don't rely on highlighting, rereading, or summarizing as your main study methods17Mix question types as you practice — don't grind twenty of the same kind in a row18Don't pick study methods based on 'I'm a visual learner, he's an auditory one'19For what you must memorize, test yourself with questions shaped like future use — don't just recite it once verbatim and call it done20Before applying for a professional title, work out which series and which level you fall under, then find the application channel matching your employer's type21Junior and intermediate titles like accounting come through the national unified exam — check your education and work years before registering22No agency-obtained titles, no ghostwritten papers, no faked materials: if confirmed, the title is revoked and you're flagged in the integrity records for 3 years23A title doesn't automatically mean a raise: first ask whether your employer fills posts by quota, or grants titles without necessarily appointing you to one
24. Medical Care: How to Spend Less and Avoid Detours12 items
1For common illnesses, start at the community clinic and get referred up level by level — your inpatient deductible carries on from where it left off2Within the same pooling region (where your insurance is enrolled), the lower the hospital tier, the higher the reimbursement rate — a gap of about 10 percentage points3To get into a big hospital, use primary-care referral or the hospital's referral center — never appointment scalpers4Before going out of province for care, ask locally first; in principle the necessity must be assessed by an associate chief physician or above5After every visit, keep your own copies of medical records, test reports, and imaging6If you have doubts about your care, demand the records be sealed on the spot — both sides present, an inventory drawn up, one copy each7For acute, serious conditions go straight to the ER triage desk, not the registration window8No money, no ID, can't say who you are — the ER must still treat you first9Get disability assessed only after treatment ends; too early, and your grade comes out lower10If treatment leaves real functional impairment, apply for a disability certificate at the county-level disabled persons' federation where your household is registered11Thank the doctor who saved you with a letter, a banner, or a satisfaction rating — not a red envelope: the rules ban money and gifts, not gratitude12Before getting dental implants, ask exactly what the package price includes; prefer providers that have committed to the price-governance program, and don't trust low-price ads
25. What to Handle After Someone Dies10 items
1If someone dies at home or elsewhere, first tell normal death from abnormal: for accidents, unknown causes, or anyone living alone found dead, call the police immediately and don't touch the body or the scene2The death certificate unlocks everything that follows: whoever provided treatment issues it; for a normal death at home, go to the community health service, which signs it within one day3Body transport, storage, and cremation go only through a funeral home; hospital morgues don't handle funerals, and storage generally can't exceed 3 days4If you dispute the cause of death, request an autopsy within 48 hours and have the medical records sealed at the same time5Canceling the household registration has statutory deadlines: before burial in cities, within one month in the countryside6Funeral services divide into basic and non-basic items; basic items have a published list with fees set by law7If you run into forced bundles, markups above listed prices, or one service split into several charges, write it down and complain8Intermediaries for funeral agency, supply purchasing, and ceremony planning must register with the county-level civil affairs department9Go claim the money scattered in different places one by one: housing provident fund balance, social insurance benefits, work-injury benefits10Close relatives can request to view, copy, correct, or delete the deceased's account data and personal information
26. Building a Website or Platform: Licenses, Filing, and Servers11 items
1A platform shouldn't collect money itself and pass it to sellers — route payments through a licensed payment institution that settles directly2Most fee-charging websites need a license; if you only sell your own goods and don't host other sellers, you don't; matching third-party trades calls for a different license; free sites just need ICP filing3Live streaming needs a network culture business license; the audiovisual program license is one private firms essentially can't obtain4Servers inside the country require ICP filing, and your access provider must hold a value-added telecom license in its own name5Let users sell on your platform, and you must verify and register them, report the information, and keep records for three years6User-posted content is your responsibility: moderation mechanisms, a reporting channel, and immediate takedown and reporting when something illegal turns up7Offer information publishing or instant messaging, and you must require users to provide real identity information8No livestreaming accounts for anyone under 16, with tips handled in age-based tiers9Deal with infringement notices promptly; if nothing follows within 15 days after the counter-statement is forwarded, put the content back up10Don't casually move user data abroad; data exports carry statutory conditions and headcount thresholds11Choosing a server: first ask if you can tolerate its downtime, then whether anyone maintains it, and only then compare prices
27. Pregnancy and Childbirth: From a Positive Test to Discharge and Paperwork16 items
1Start 0.4 mg of folic acid daily when trying to conceive, and keep taking it through the first 3 months of pregnancy2Before week 13, open your Maternal and Child Health Handbook at the community health center and use up the free prenatal checkup quota3At the first prenatal visit, get the three tests done — HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B; free intervention is available even if positive4No cigarettes and no alcohol at all during pregnancy, and no one smokes indoors at home either5With high-risk factors for preeclampsia, start one low-dose aspirin a day after week 12 of pregnancy6At week 24 or later, do the gestational diabetes screening — don't skip it over the sugary drink7Memorize this 'go to the hospital now' list — it applies during pregnancy and for a year after birth8If your water breaks, lie flat where you are, prop your hips up, call 120 — no walking around, no showering9If you want an epidural, say so — it doesn't raise the risk of cesarean10Don't ask for a cesarean without a medical indication, and don't schedule surgery to pick an auspicious date11Before getting pregnant, confirm your maternity insurance status; an unemployed spouse can also claim childbirth medical expenses12Get the Medical Certificate of Birth done before discharge — decide the name early and don't get the characters wrong13Don't decline the newborn heel-prick screen or the hearing screen14Once you have the birth certificate, enroll the baby in resident medical insurance — don't wait until the household registration is done15Register the birth at the local police station within one month of the baby's birth16Don't skip the 42-day postpartum checkup — it doubles as postpartum depression screening
28. Don't Wreck Your Body for Your Looks9 items
1Don't control weight with crash diets, fasting, or vomiting on purpose; if you want to lose, lose on the exercise side of the ledger2Before injections, thread implants, or surgery, check two things: whether the facility's license includes 'medical cosmetology', and whether the person operating is a qualified attending physician in charge3For facial fillers, avoid the nose bridge, between the brows, and the forehead — and never cut corners with unlicensed injections4Don't buy weight-loss pills, diet coffee, slimming candies, or enzyme plums that promise 'fast slimming'5Don't use anabolic steroids ('muscle-building shots', 'oral pills') to gain muscle6If you need weight-loss medication, get a prescription at a hospital — don't buy from online shops that ship without one7Use sex-hormone medications only with a doctor's prescription and regular follow-ups — never buy online or increase the dose on your own8If 'feeling ugly' has reached the level of constant mirror-checking and constant urges to fix something, get a body-image assessment before discussing surgery9For teeth straightening, see an orthodontically qualified doctor for in-person checks and regular visits — don't buy aligners online and wear them at home
29. After a Major Blow13 items
1In the first days after a loved one passes, don't stay alone; if you have heart disease, hypertension, or diabetes, keep taking your medication, and call 120 for crushing chest pain2In the week you're told a serious diagnosis, don't collect the report alone, and put off decisions beyond treatment3After losing your job, first lock in a routine, your medical insurance, and a job-search rhythm — don't stay home all day4If a loved one died by suicide, accident, or violence, don't expect to tough it out — actively seek professional help5In the first six months of widowhood, hand meals, sleep, chronic-disease medication, and checkups to one fixed person to watch over6With no family and no friends, swap 'the one person who checks on you' for three things: a neighbor who can enter your home, a community visiting list, and emergency contacts in your phone7When a parent dies, tell the child the truth, let them join the farewell, and don't send them elsewhere to 'change the scenery'8If grief is still stuck in place after six months and life is unlivable, book a psychiatry or clinical psychology appointment9Don't pay for grief counseling straight away; first check whether your grief is genuinely stuck (the symptoms in item 8)10After separation or divorce, don't let your medical insurance lapse and don't prop yourself up with alcohol11For someone to talk to, call 12356; minors and teenagers call 12355; to see a doctor, book a psychological outpatient clinic12For the first three months after a major upheaval, push every irreversible big decision to later13Don't use death as a way to repay debts: life insurance won't pay out within the first two years, work-injury status won't be recognized, and debts still come off the estate first
