1. Don't die early

42 items

This section covers three things: deaths from accidents and injuries such as car crashes, fires, and poisoning; the few vaccines and screenings backed by the hardest evidence; and signals from your body that mean you should get checked. The numbers in the Benefit column come from randomized trials, studies that followed large groups of people for many years, or official statistics. The Cost column is the author's rough estimate at market prices, meant only for comparing entries with each other — don't quote it elsewhere. The entries in this section are grouped by topic below; item numbers appear in parentheses. On the road: wear a seat belt (item 1), wear a helmet (item 2), don't speed and don't drink and drive (item 9), child safety seats (item 10). Fire, gas, and electricity at home: install smoke alarms (item 3), replace gas hoses when due (item 4), don't push e-bikes into stairwells (item 6), keep a fire extinguisher and first-aid kit ready (item 26), fit the guard before using an angle grinder (item 42). Accidents: children, the elderly, and the outdoors: window restrictors (item 11), children near water never out of sight (item 12), balance training after 60 (item 13), no wild mushrooms (item 5), no picking up metal pieces of unknown origin (item 36), measure ice thickness before stepping onto natural ice (item 41). Vaccines: hepatitis B blood panel (item 14), tetanus (item 15), HPV vaccine (item 16), flu vaccine (item 20), shingles vaccine (item 21), pneumococcal vaccine (item 22). Screening and checkups: measure blood pressure (item 7), fasting blood glucose (item 8), breast cancer screening (item 17), cervical cancer screening (item 18), colorectal cancer screening (item 19), H. pylori testing (item 23), low-dose chest CT (item 24), bone density testing (item 39), anti-osteoporosis medication (item 40). Body signals and sexual health: visible blood in the urine (item 27), erectile problems — check the cardiovascular system first (item 28), weight loss and quitting smoking improve erectile function (item 29), condoms and no shared needles (item 30), HIV testing (item 31), pre-exposure prophylaxis (item 38). Psychological crises: suicidal thoughts — call 12356 (item 25), tell one person about suicidal thoughts first (item 32), borrowing to keep gambling (item 37), the cost of surviving pesticide ingestion or gas poisoning (item 33), the cost after a fall from height (item 34), the cost of getting by on one kidney (item 35).

1

Wear a seat belt, front and back seats alike

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Buckle up in the front seat and your odds of dying in a crash drop by about half. In the front seat of a light truck, they drop by about 60%. Of the people who died in vehicles in the US in 2022 whose belt use could be determined, half were unbelted.

Cost
Costs nothing. Adds 2 seconds each time you get in the car.
Benefit
NHTSA, the US traffic safety authority, estimates that seat belts cut the risk of fatal injury for front-seat occupants of passenger cars by 45%. For front-seat occupants of light trucks, 60%. Among people who died in passenger vehicles (cars carrying people) in the US in 2022 whose belt use could be determined, 50% were unbelted. The World Health Organization's (WHO) figure: seat belts reduce the risk of death for vehicle occupants by up to 50%. WHO estimated 248,099 deaths from road traffic crashes in China in 2021, equivalent to 17.4 per 100,000 people.
Note
Buckle up in the back seat too. In the same report, 60% of people killed in the second row were unbelted. The 45% and 60% figures are estimates NHTSA derived from crash databases (citing Kahane 2015), not randomized trials. WHO's China death toll is a modeled estimate, several times higher than what police traffic records register. The two sides count different things; this book uses only WHO's figures.
Sources (3 references)
NHTSA (2024). Occupant Protection in Passenger Vehicles: 2022 Data (DOT HS 813 573). https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPublication… ; WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traff… ; WHO GHO RS_196/RS_198 (China, 2021). https://ghoapi.azureedge.net/api/RS_196?$filter=SpatialDim%…
2

Wear a helmet on motorcycles and e-bikes, and buckle it up

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Wear a helmet with the strap fastened and a motorcyclist's odds of dying in a crash drop by about 40%. Head injuries drop by about 70%. Fasten the strap snugly — a helmet loosely perched on your head doesn't count as wearing one.

Cost
A helmet costs 100 to 300 yuan. 5 seconds each time you put it on.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled multiple studies. For motorcyclists, helmets cut the risk of death by 42%. Point estimate OR 0.58, confidence range 95% CI 0.50 to 0.68. Head injuries fell 69% (OR 0.31, 95% CI 0.25 to 0.38).
Note
Fasten the strap; a helmet hanging on the handlebar doesn't count. The data above come from motorcycles. There is no direct research on e-bikes; the numbers are extrapolated, because head injuries occur the same way in a crash.
Sources (1 reference)
Liu BC et al. (2008). Helmets for preventing injury in motorcycle riders. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004333.pub3
3

Install smoke alarms; if you burn coal or heat with gas indoors in winter, add a carbon monoxide alarm

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A working smoke alarm cuts the odds of dying in a house fire by about 60%. In four fires out of ten, someone was asleep — your nose alone won't wake you. If you burn coal or use gas indoors in winter, add a carbon monoxide alarm. In 2018, 11,500 people in China died of carbon monoxide poisoning; in the three winter months, 70% of those deaths happened at home.

Cost
A smoke alarm costs 30 to 100 yuan; a carbon monoxide alarm 50 to 150 yuan. Change the battery once a year after installation.
Benefit
A North Carolina study examined a set of residential fires and compared households where someone died with households where no one did. With a working smoke alarm in the home, the risk of death fell about 60%. Point estimate OR 0.39, confidence range 95% CI 0.18 to 0.83. In the US from 2018 to 2020, among fatal fires in occupied homes, 24% had no smoke alarm, and in 41% someone was asleep when the fire started. China reported 11,523 deaths from carbon monoxide poisoning in 2018; of these, 72.59% in December, 67.42% in January, and 66.48% in February occurred at home.
Note
Why Grade B: the smoke-alarm side rests on a single study that compared affected and unaffected households retrospectively, not a randomized trial. For carbon monoxide alarms specifically, no study shows a mortality reduction. The benefit here is inferred from the fact that poisoning deaths cluster in winter and at home.
Sources (3 references)
Marshall SW et al. (1998). Fatal residential fires: who dies and who survives? JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.279.20.1633 ; USFA (2022). Fatal Fires in Residential Buildings (2018-2020), Topical Fire Report Series 22(2). https://www.usfa.fema.gov/downloads/pdf/statistics/v22i2.pdf ; You J et al. (2020). Number of Deaths due to Carbon Monoxide Poisoning by Month and by Place of Death — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly. https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2020.008
4

Replace gas hoses and stoves when due, never modify the piping yourself, and feel free to flatly refuse gas company door-to-door sales

Grade CValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A compliant hose costs a few dozen yuan. Replacing it when due is a user obligation written into the Urban Gas Management Regulations. Modifying the piping or dismantling the gas meter yourself is explicitly banned by the same regulations. They also say the gas company cannot require you to buy the products and services it designates. A door-to-door pitch claiming you "must" replace something can be flatly refused.

Cost
A compliant gas hose costs a few dozen yuan. Stoves are replaced every few years. While you're at it, check whether anything is past its service date.
Benefit
The regulations make "promptly replacing gas-burning appliances and connecting hoses that the state has explicitly phased out or that have reached the end of their service life" a user obligation: when your stove or hose is past its rated years or has been phased out nationally, you replace it. The regulations also list "installing, altering, or dismantling indoor gas facilities and gas metering devices without authorization" as prohibited acts — DIY pipe modifications and dismantling the gas meter both fall under this. They further state that gas operators may not require users to purchase their designated products, nor require users to accept their designated services.
Note
The regulation text can be checked verbatim, but it only says replacing the hose when due is your obligation — not how many accidents replacement prevents. No official statistics were found on how much replacing hoses by their rated life reduces gas accidents, hence only Grade C. Some people come door-to-door in the name of a "safety inspection" and then pitch shutoff valves and alarms. Article 20(6) of the regulations forbids the gas company from requiring you to buy its designated products; you can refuse, and you can complain. If you smell gas: first close the main gas valve — for bottled gas, close the cylinder valve. Then open doors and windows to ventilate; do not switch on the exhaust fan. Don't turn lights, range hoods, or any other appliances on or off, and don't touch a lighter. Then leave, and call the gas company's emergency line only after you are away from the scene. Carbon monoxide poisoning is a separate matter; see Section 13.
Sources (3 references)
State Council (2010). Urban Gas Management Regulations (State Council Decree No. 583). Article 27: "Gas users shall observe safety rules for gas use, use qualified gas-burning appliances and cylinders, and promptly replace gas-burning appliances, connecting hoses, and the like that the state has explicitly phased out or that have reached the end of their service life"; Article 28's prohibited acts include "(1) operating public gas valves without authorization", "(2) using gas pipelines as load-bearing supports or grounding leads", "(4) installing, altering, or dismantling indoor gas facilities and gas metering devices without authorization"; Article 20 forbids gas operators from "(6) requiring gas users to purchase their designated products or accept their designated services"; Article 29 lets users complain to gas administration and other departments about fees and service, and "the relevant departments shall process complaints within 15 working days of receipt". http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2010/content_1758214.htm; Shenzhen Housing and Construction Bureau (2024). Safe Gas Use Tips (2): "immediately close the main gas valve at home", "quickly open doors and windows to ventilate", "never turn lights, range hoods, or other appliances on or off", "people should evacuate quickly, move to a safe place, and promptly call the gas company's emergency line". https://zjj.sz.gov.cn/zcjzts/content/post_11882410.html; Zhangjiagang Emergency Management Bureau (2024). Gas Safety Knowledge: "do not turn on the exhaust fan in a panic to ventilate", "call for help only after getting well away from the scene". https://www.zjg.gov.cn/zjgszwz/yjaqzs/202411/72b4fad7399c48…
5

Don't pick, buy, or eat wild mushrooms; no folk method of identifying them holds up

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

In 2025 alone, China logged 828 mushroom poisoning incidents, 2,165 people sickened, and 13 deaths. That year also added 34 mushroom species never before recorded as poisonous. Silver-needle testing, "if insects ate it, it's safe", "only brightly colored ones are toxic" — none of these hold up.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is giving up a seasonal wild delicacy.
Benefit
In 2025 the China CDC investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents involving 2,165 people, with 13 deaths. Case fatality rate 0.6%, meaning 0.6% of those poisoned died. From 2019 to 2024 there were 276 to 676 incidents a year, with case fatality between 0.87% and 2.86%. 2025 alone identified 138 poisonous mushroom species, 34 of them recorded in China for the first time as causing poisoning.
Note
If you've eaten one, induce vomiting immediately, then go to the hospital with the leftover mushrooms or photos of them. Poisonous mushrooms cause several distinct syndromes; identifying the species directly determines how the doctor treats you. New species are recorded as toxic every year, so the premise that "locals know them well" doesn't hold. Silver-needle testing, boiling with garlic, "insects ate it so it's safe", "only bright colors are toxic" — none hold up.
Sources (2 references)
Mushroom Poisoning Outbreaks — China, 2025. China CDC Weekly (2026): "In 2025, China CDC investigated 828 mushroom poisoning incidents across 27 provincial-level administrative divisions (PLADs), affecting 2,165 individuals and causing 13 deaths - a case fatality rate of 0.6%, the lowest of the past six years. In total, 138 poisonous mushroom species were identified, including 34 newly recorded in poisoning incidents in China." "From 2019 to 2024, the annual number of incidents ranged from 276 to 676, and the case fatality rate ranged from 0.87% to 2.86%." https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2026.120; the same journal's 2024 annual report https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2025.106
6

Never push e-bikes into stairwells or elevators, and never charge them at home

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Pushing an e-bike into a stairwell or elevator, or charging it at home, is explicitly banned by the Ministry of Emergency Management's Fire Safety Management Regulations for High-Rise Civil Buildings. Those who fail to correct it face fines of 500 to 1,000 yuan for individuals and 2,000 to 10,000 yuan for businesses. The fine is the small part; what matters is that this kind of fire burns exactly on your only escape route.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is parking at the centralized charging point downstairs every time, a few dozen meters farther to walk.
Benefit
The ministry's rules state verbatim: "Parking electric bicycles or charging them in the public lobbies, evacuation corridors, stairwells, or safety exits of high-rise civil buildings is prohibited." In lobbies, corridors, stairwells, and safety exits, neither parking nor charging is allowed. Those who refuse to correct violations face fines of 500 to 1,000 yuan for individuals and non-business units, and 2,000 to 10,000 yuan for businesses.
Note
Don't buy modified batteries, don't use off-brand chargers, and don't leave it charging overnight unattended. Once a lithium battery catches fire, it engulfs everything within dozens of seconds while giving off highly toxic smoke. If the bike catches fire in the stairwell, what burns is your only escape route. Figures published by the Ministry of Emergency Management: 18,000 e-bike fires nationwide in 2021, killing 65 people. Of these, 3,782 fires burned inside buildings, killing 60 — the victims were almost all indoors. After the 2024 crackdown, fires fell 42.2% from the previous year and casualties fell more than 90%; that year's absolute numbers were not published.
Sources (3 references)
Ministry of Emergency Management (2021). Fire Safety Management Regulations for High-Rise Civil Buildings (MEM Order No. 5, Articles 37 and 47). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/01/content_562…; Ministry of Emergency Management (2023). Reply to Proposal No. 00969 of the Fifth Session of the 13th CPPCC National Committee: "In 2021, 18,000 e-bike fires were reported nationwide, causing 65 deaths and 222 injuries, with direct property losses of 221 million yuan; 3,782 of these fires occurred inside buildings, causing 60 deaths and 175 injuries". https://www.mem.gov.cn/gk/jytabljggk/zxwytadfzy/2022zx/2023…; Ministry of Emergency Management (2025). Press conference of January 15, 2025: "Fire counts fell 42.2% year on year, and casualties fell more than 90%". https://www.mem.gov.cn/xw/xwfbh/2025n01y15xwfbh_6337/
7

Measure your blood pressure; if it's high, take medication to bring it down to target

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Every 10 mmHg your blood pressure comes down, the odds of a major cardiovascular event drop about 20%, stroke 27%, heart failure 28%, and death 13%. Among Chinese aged 35 to 75, 44.7% have hypertension, and only 7.2% have it truly under control.

Cost
A digital blood pressure monitor costs 100 to 200 yuan. Each reading takes 1 minute. Most blood pressure drugs run a few to a few dozen yuan a month. The hard part is staying on them with no symptoms.
Benefit
Pooling 123 trials and over 610,000 people: every 10 mmHg reduction in systolic pressure cuts major cardiovascular events by about 20%. Point estimate RR 0.80, confidence range 95% CI 0.77 to 0.83. Systolic pressure is the higher of the two blood pressure numbers. Stroke down about 27% (RR 0.73). Heart failure down about 28% (RR 0.72). All-cause mortality down 13% (RR 0.87, 95% CI 0.84 to 0.91). China screened 1.7 million people aged 35 to 75: 44.7% had hypertension. Of those, 44.7% knew they had it, 30.1% were on treatment, and only 7.2% had it controlled.
Note
Go get your blood pressure measured once. In China fewer than 1 in 10 people with hypertension has it controlled, so this single measurement is one of the highest-value actions in this book. Where the target should sit (130 or 140) is still debated, but "knowing you have high blood pressure and bringing it down" is not in dispute.
Sources (2 references)
Ettehad D et al. (2016). Blood pressure lowering for prevention of cardiovascular disease and death: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Lancet. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)01225-8 ; Lu J et al. (2017). Prevalence, awareness, treatment, and control of hypertension in China (China PEACE Million Persons Project). Lancet. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(17)32478-9
8

After 35, if you're overweight get a fasting blood glucose test; even if normal, retest every three years

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

A few dozen yuan buys a vial of blood that can catch prediabetes while you have zero symptoms. The official US screening advice: get tested between ages 35 and 70 if you're overweight or obese. If the result is normal, retest every three years. The US sets overweight at a body mass index of 25, lowered to 23 for Asians; China's standard counts 24 as overweight.

Cost
Fasting glucose costs a dozen or so yuan; HbA1c a few dozen yuan. One blood draw at the hospital covers it.
Benefit
The US Preventive Services Task Force is the official US body that issues screening advice. Its current recommendation: screen adults aged 35 to 70 who are overweight or obese for prediabetes and type 2 diabetes, even with no symptoms at all. Overweight means a body mass index ≥25, obesity ≥30. For Asian Americans it recommends lowering the threshold to BMI ≥23, because at the same BMI, diabetes risk is higher in Asians. China's industry standard: BMI between 24.0 and 28.0 counts as overweight, ≥28.0 as obesity. This recommendation carries a Grade B rating. It also states: "for adults with normal blood glucose, screening every 3 years is a reasonable approach".
Note
A prediabetes diagnosis doesn't automatically mean medication. A substantial share of people can turn it around with lifestyle changes alone. Among Chinese adults, those who know they have diabetes have always been a minority; many only find out when complications appear.
Sources (2 references)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2021). Screening for Prediabetes and Type 2 Diabetes. https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recomm…: "at a lower BMI (≥23) if the patient is Asian American"; National Health Commission General Office (2024). Explanatory Notes on Core Knowledge for Residents' Weight Management (2024 edition): "Under the industry standard Criteria for Weight in Adults (WS/T 428-2013)... BMI 24.0 to under 28.0 is overweight, BMI ≥28.0 is obese". https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202407/P02024070348151…
9

Don't speed and don't drink and drive

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Every 1% higher the average speed, the odds of a fatal crash rise about 4%. With alcohol there is no "just one drink is fine" safety line. Risk starts climbing while your blood alcohol is still very low.

Cost
Costs nothing. Drive a bit slower and a trip takes a few extra minutes. The hard part is drinking less at dinner parties.
Benefit
Per the World Health Organization (WHO): every 1% increase in average speed raises the risk of a fatal crash by 4%. The risk of drinking and driving starts rising from very low blood alcohol concentrations.
Note
The 1%, 4% speed-and-death figures are derived from crash models, not randomized trials. On drunk driving WHO gives direction only, not numbers. This section did not verify the primary literature on "how much drinking, how much extra risk".
Sources (1 reference)
WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traff…
10

Use a child safety seat for children under 4; don't hold them in your arms

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: a lotTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

For infants under 1, a child safety seat cuts the odds of fatal injury in a crash by about 70%. For children 1 to 4, by about half. Holding them in your arms provides none of this protection — in a hard braking event you can't hold on.

Cost
A seat costs 300 to 2,000 yuan and lasts years. Budget 1 extra minute per trip to strap the child in.
Benefit
NHTSA, the US traffic safety authority, estimates that child safety seats cut the risk of fatal injury for infants under 1 in passenger cars by 71%. For toddlers aged 1 to 4, 54%. The World Health Organization's (WHO) figure: infant deaths down 71%.
Note
Install the seat exactly per the manual; a wrong installation is as good as none. Under 1 year old, install rear-facing with the child facing the back of the car. The numbers above are official US estimates from crash data.
Sources (2 references)
NHTSA (2024). Occupant Protection in Passenger Vehicles: 2022 Data (DOT HS 813 573). https://crashstats.nhtsa.dot.gov/Api/Public/ViewPublication… ; WHO (2025). Road traffic injuries fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/road-traff…
11

With small children at home, install window and balcony restrictors; insect screens don't count as protection

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A pair of restrictors costs a few dozen yuan. New York City installed window guards free for high-risk households and followed up with in-home education; reported child falls in one borough halved in three years. New York later went further and legislated that landlords install guards in apartments with children. Insect screens pop open with a push — they are not protection.

Cost
A pair of window restrictors or child safety locks costs a few dozen yuan. Ten minutes to install.
Benefit
From 1972 New York City ran a program called "Children Can't Fly", distributing window guards free in high-risk neighborhoods along with door-to-door education. Reported falls in the Bronx fell 50% from 1973 to 1975. New York City later amended its health code to require landlords to install window guards in apartments where children 10 and under live.
Note
Keep beds, sofas, and boxes — anything a child can climb — away from windows and balcony rails. Screens only stop mosquitoes; they pop out with a push, so don't treat them as guards. And this isn't only for high floors: in the US data, most falls were from a second story or lower.
Sources (2 references)
Spiegel CN, Lindaman FC (1977). Children can't fly: a program to prevent childhood morbidity and mortality from window falls. American Journal of Public Health: "Significant reduction in falls resulted, particularly in the Bronx, where reported falls declined 50 percent from 1973 to 1975"; the 1976 revision of the New York City health code "to require that landlords provide window guards in apartments where children ten years old and younger reside". https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.67.12.1143; (2021). Unintentional Window Falls in Children and Adolescents. Academic Pediatrics: January 2007 to August 2017 national electronic injury surveillance system, 38,840 emergency department visits, "The majority of falls occurred in children under the age of 6 and were related to falls from a second story or below". https://doi.org/10.1016/j.acap.2020.07.008
12

Never leave children out of sight near water; wear life jackets when boating or swimming in open water

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Fall into the water wearing a life jacket and your odds of drowning are roughly half what they'd be without one. Drowning remains the leading cause of death for Chinese children aged 1 to 14. The rural drowning death rate is about twice the urban rate.

Cost
A life jacket costs 50 to 200 yuan. Plus the attention it takes to keep watching your child.
Benefit
A study using US Coast Guard data matched comparable people in pairs. Among people who fell from recreational boats, wearing a life jacket cut drowning risk by about half. Point estimate: adjusted RR 0.51, confidence range 95% CI 0.35 to 0.74. China's drowning death rate for those under 20 fell from 6.60 per 100,000 in 2013 to 3.28 per 100,000 in 2021. Rural is about 2 times urban. Drowning remains the leading cause of death for children 1 to 14. Of injury deaths at ages 0 to 19 in 2021, drowning accounted for 31.1% and road traffic 27.9%.
Note
Grade A covers only the life-jacket half. "Never out of sight" is common-sense consensus; on its own it's only Grade C — there is no randomized trial, and there never will be. China's drowning deaths concentrate in rural areas, in summer, and among males aged 15 to 19. For winter ice play, see item 41 (measure natural ice thickness first).
Sources (3 references)
Cummings P et al. (2011). Association between wearing a personal floatation device and death by drowning among recreational boaters. Injury Prevention. https://doi.org/10.1136/ip.2010.028688 ; Li Z et al. (2023). Unintentional Drowning Mortality Among Individuals Under Age 20 — China, 2013–2021. China CDC Weekly. https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2023.198 ; Zhou J et al. (2024). Injury Mortality of Children and Adolescents Aged 0–19 Years — China, 2010–2021. China CDC Weekly. https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2024.057
13

After 60, train balance and leg strength; adapt your bathroom and stairs for safety

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Practicing balance two or three times a week — tai chi, for example — cuts older adults' fall frequency by about 23% and the share of people who fall by 15%. Making the home slip-resistant and adding handrails trims another 20% or so. Falls are the leading cause of injury death for Chinese over 65, and more than half happen right in their own homes.

Cost
2 to 3 sessions a week, 30 minutes each of tai chi or balance training. Bath mats, handrails, and night lights run tens to hundreds of yuan. The hard part is sticking with it long term.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled 108 trials and 23,407 people. Exercise cut older adults' fall frequency by 23%. Point estimate: rate ratio (RaR) 0.77, confidence range 95% CI 0.71 to 0.83. The share of people who fell fell 15% (RR 0.85). Having professionals come home to assess and modify safety cut fall rates about 20% (RR 0.81, 95% CI 0.68 to 0.97). Tai chi cut fall risk about 29% (RR 0.71). In China, falls are the leading cause of injury death for those over 65. Of older-adult falls monitored in 2018, 55.97% happened at home.
Note
This applies to people over 60 living in their own homes, not in nursing homes. The studies counted falls, not deaths. For an older person, the road from a fall to a hip fracture to death is short. Poor vision also means more falls; for cataracts affecting sight, see Section 17, item 9 (cataract surgery). For whether your bones can take a fall, see item 39 in this section (bone density testing).
Sources (3 references)
Sherrington C et al. (2019). Exercise for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD012424.pub2 ; Gillespie LD et al. (2012). Interventions for preventing falls in older people living in the community. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007146.pub3 ; Lu Z et al. (2021). Characteristics of Falls Among Older People — China, 2018. China CDC Weekly. https://doi.org/10.46234/ccdcw2021.013
14

Get a hepatitis B blood panel; if you have no antibodies, get vaccinated

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Testing costs a few dozen yuan. In the Qidong trial with 30 years of follow-up, people vaccinated against hepatitis B at birth were 84% less likely to develop primary liver cancer later, and 72% less likely to carry the virus. Adults who test without antibodies get three catch-up shots over six months for one to two hundred yuan.

Cost
Testing: a few dozen yuan a time. Three adult hepatitis B vaccine shots total 100 to 300 yuan. Complete them within six months.
Benefit
The Qidong trial was randomized by cluster, not by individual, with 30 years of follow-up. Newborn hepatitis B vaccination cut primary liver cancer by 84%. Confidence range: 95% CI 23% to 97%. HBsAg (hepatitis B surface antigen) positivity fell 72% (95% CI 68% to 75%) — positivity is the share of people found to be carrying the virus. China's whole-population HBsAg positivity fell 52% from 1992 to 2014, and 97% among children under 5.
Note
This applies to adults born before 1992 who were never vaccinated or whose antibodies have faded. The 84% liver cancer figure comes from those vaccinated at birth. In the same trial, catch-up vaccination in adolescence was only 21% effective at preventing virus carriage. Adult vaccination is mainly about never getting infected; don't apply that 84% directly. For people already infected, vaccination is useless — get regular follow-ups at a hepatology clinic. How to tell you're already infected: the hepatitis B surface antigen (HBsAg) line on your lab report is positive.
Sources (2 references)
Qu C et al. (2014). Efficacy of neonatal HBV vaccination on liver cancer and other liver diseases over 30-year follow-up of the Qidong hepatitis B intervention study. PLoS Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1001774 ; Cui F et al. (2017). Prevention of Chronic Hepatitis B after 3 Decades of Escalating Vaccination Policy, China. Emerging Infectious Diseases. https://doi.org/10.3201/eid2305.161477
15

Pierced by a nail or wood splinter, or a wound contaminated with soil? Get it treated the same day and ask whether you need a tetanus shot

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Once tetanus takes hold, roughly 1 in 10 dies. Deep wounds and soil-contaminated wounds carry the highest risk. If the wound is dirty and it's been 5 or more years since your last shot, get one booster. Same-day treatment costs only a few dozen yuan; don't wait until the wound swells up.

Cost
Registration plus wound care: a few dozen yuan. If the doctor says a shot is needed, vaccine or immunoglobulin runs tens to hundreds of yuan.
Benefit
Among US tetanus cases, about 1 in 10 is fatal. Deep wounds and soil-contaminated wounds are riskier. China's 2024 clinical protocol sorts wounds into two tiers. Superficial wounds treated within 6 hours with no contact with soil, feces, or animal saliva are low risk. Wounds treated after more than 6 hours, contaminated with any of those, or puncture wounds, avulsion wounds, crush injuries, burns and scalds, frostbite, or wounds with retained foreign bodies are high risk. If you've had 3 or more shots and the last was under 5 years ago, nothing more is needed. At 5 to 10 years, one booster for high-risk wounds. At 10 or more years, one booster regardless of wound tier. If you haven't completed 3 shots or can't remember, complete the vaccine series, and for high-risk wounds also receive passive immunization (immunoglobulin or antitoxin — shots that deliver antibodies directly).
Note
At the hospital, let the doctor judge; don't decide yourself, and don't skip the question out of inconvenience. Not every wound needs a shot. The doctor will grade the wound, ask when you were last vaccinated, and then decide. "Vaccinated as a kid, covered for life" is wrong. If the wound is dirty, 5 years since the last shot calls for a booster. So before you go, think about what year you last had a tetanus shot.
Sources (3 references)
US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Tetanus: "Tetanus bacteria can get into someone's body through broken skin, usually through injuries." "Tetanus can lead to death (1 in 10 cases in the United States are fatal)." "People who didn't complete the primary series or who aren't up to date with their 10-year tetanus booster shots are also at increased risk." "Vaccination also helps prevent tetanus in people with wounds, depending on their tetanus vaccination history." https://www.cdc.gov/tetanus/about/index.html; National Health Commission General Office (2024). Notice on Issuing the Clinical Protocol for Non-Neonatal Tetanus (2024 edition) (GW Ban Yi Ji Han [2024] No. 381; risk grading on page 16 of the annex, Table 4 on page 20). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/content_6982262…; Annex PDF (scanned copy). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202410/P02024102348342…
16

Women: get the HPV vaccine — the earlier the better

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: a lotTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In Swedish data on 1.67 million women, those vaccinated against HPV before 17 later developed invasive cervical cancer at about one-eighth the rate of the unvaccinated. Even those vaccinated at 17 to 30 got roughly half. So the earlier you get it, the more it's worth.

Cost
Domestic bivalent runs a bit over 300 yuan a shot; imported 9-valent about 1,300 yuan a shot. 2 to 3 shots in total. Each visit takes half a day.
Benefit
Sweden followed 1.67 million women statistically: vaccinated women had lower rates of invasive cervical cancer than the unvaccinated. Vaccinated before 17: about 88% lower (IRR 0.12, 95% CI 0.00 to 0.34 — the parentheses give the point estimate and its confidence range). Vaccinated at 17 to 30: about 53% lower (IRR 0.47, 95% CI 0.27 to 0.75).
Note
Biggest benefit at ages 9 to 14. At 17 to 30 there's still more than a 50% reduction. After 30, the benefit keeps shrinking. Even vaccinated women still need cervical cancer screening; the vaccine doesn't replace screening. See item 18 (cervical cancer screening for women 30 and over).
Sources (1 reference)
Lei J et al. (2020). HPV Vaccination and the Risk of Invasive Cervical Cancer. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1917338
17

Women: breast cancer screening from age 40, with a mammogram every two years

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

For women 40 to 74, a mammogram every two years is explicitly recommended in the official US screening advice. For 75 and older, and for adding ultrasound and MRI for dense breasts, the official verdict is that the evidence isn't there yet. When a checkup package tries to sell you these add-ons, you can pass.

Cost
A mammogram costs two to three hundred yuan a time. Many areas have free screening programs. Half a day every two years.
Benefit
The US Preventive Services Task Force is the official US body that issues screening advice. Its current recommendation: "biennial screening mammography for women aged 40 to 74 years". Mammography is what's commonly called a molybdenum-target mammogram. This recommendation carries a Grade B rating. For women 75 and older, and for supplementary ultrasound or MRI for dense breasts, it judged the evidence "insufficient".
Note
Starting ages differ across countries; some Chinese guidelines and local programs start at 45. Those whose parents, children, or siblings have had breast cancer, and BRCA mutation carriers, are high-risk and need a plan worked out with a doctor individually — this item doesn't apply to them.
Sources (1 reference)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2024). Breast Cancer: Screening. https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recomm…
18

Women 30 and over: get cervical cancer screening, with HPV testing preferred

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In the rural India trial, women who got a single HPV test in their lifetime were about half as likely to die of cervical cancer, and about 50% less likely to be found with late-stage cervical cancer. One test costs one to two hundred yuan, and a negative result holds for 5 years.

Cost
An HPV test costs 100 to 300 yuan. With a negative result, once every 5 years is enough. Sampling takes minutes.
Benefit
The rural India trial was randomized by cluster, not by individual, covering women aged 30 to 59. A single round of HPV testing for screening cut the risk of dying from cervical cancer by about 48%. Point estimate HR 0.52, confidence range 95% CI 0.33 to 0.83. Risk of being found with late-stage cervical cancer fell about 53% (HR 0.47, 95% CI 0.32 to 0.69).
Note
Even people who've had the HPV vaccine need screening, because the vaccine doesn't cover every viral type. What makes this study rare: it was a randomized screening trial that used deaths directly as the outcome, and it screened only one round.
Sources (1 reference)
Sankaranarayanan R et al. (2009). HPV screening for cervical cancer in rural India. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa0808516
19

Colorectal cancer screening starting at 45 to 50: a fecal immunochemical test for occult blood, or a colonoscopy

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

A few dozen yuan of fecal occult blood testing every one to two years cuts the odds of dying of colorectal cancer by about 16% — by 25% among those who completed at least one round. People invited for one colonoscopy saw their 10-year risk of colorectal cancer drop from 1.20% to 0.98%.

Cost
Stool testing costs a few dozen yuan, every 1 to 2 years. Colonoscopy runs several hundred to over a thousand yuan; with a negative result, once every 10 years is enough. Set aside a day for bowel prep beforehand.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled multiple studies: people screened with fecal occult blood testing were about 16% less likely to die of colorectal cancer. Point estimate RR 0.84, confidence range 95% CI 0.78 to 0.90. Those who took part in at least one round: about 25% lower (RR 0.75). Now the NordICC randomized trial: people invited for colonoscopy saw 10-year colorectal cancer incidence fall from 1.20% to 0.98%. Point estimate RR 0.82, confidence range 95% CI 0.70 to 0.93.
Note
Contested. NordICC counted people who were "invited" for colonoscopy; colorectal cancer deaths were 0.28% versus 0.31% (RR 0.90, 95% CI 0.64 to 1.16) — a difference still within the error margin. This suggests colonoscopy's mortality benefit was previously overstated. Stool testing actually has the harder evidence on mortality. Starting ages in national guidelines range from 45 to 50. Those with affected family members should start earlier.
Sources (2 references)
Hewitson P et al. (2007). Screening for colorectal cancer using the faecal occult blood test, Hemoccult. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001216.pub2 ; Bretthauer M et al. (2022). Effect of Colonoscopy Screening on Risks of Colorectal Cancer and Related Death. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2208375
20

People with cardiovascular disease and older adults: get a flu shot every year

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In the trial of flu vaccination after heart attack, the share dying within a year fell from 4.9% to 2.9%. People with cardiovascular disease and older adults: get a shot every autumn for 50 to 150 yuan.

Cost
A shot costs 50 to 150 yuan. Once every autumn.
Benefit
One trial was run after myocardial infarction, with 2,571 people randomized. Neither doctors nor patients knew which shot was given. Those vaccinated against flu had 12-month all-cause mortality of 2.9%; those given placebo, 4.9%. Point estimate HR 0.59, confidence range 95% CI 0.39 to 0.89. A placebo is a control injection with no active ingredient. The HR for cardiovascular death was 0.59. Another study pooled multiple studies. Major cardiovascular events: 3.6% among the vaccinated versus 5.4% among controls. Point estimate RR 0.66, confidence range 95% CI 0.53 to 0.83. Cardiovascular death RR 0.74 (95% CI 0.42 to 1.30 — a difference still within the error range, not statistically significant).
Note
Contested. Grade A applies only to people with cardiovascular disease. For otherwise healthy older adults, the Cochrane review offers only one conclusion: influenza incidence over a season fell from 6% to 2.4%. It rated confidence in this evidence as "low" and the mortality evidence as "very low". The review is the Demicheli V et al. 2018 paper.
Sources (3 references)
Fröbert O et al. (2021). Influenza Vaccination After Myocardial Infarction: A Randomized, Double-Blind, Placebo-Controlled, Multicenter Trial. Circulation. https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.121.057042 ; Behrouzi B et al. (2022). Association of Influenza Vaccination With Cardiovascular Risk: A Meta-analysis. JAMA Network Open. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2022.8873; Demicheli V et al. (2018). Vaccines for preventing influenza in the elderly. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD004876.pub4 (the Cochrane review mentioned in the Note)
21

Get the shingles vaccine after 50

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: a lotTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In the phase 3 trial, this vaccine blocked 97% of shingles cases, about the same across age groups. The catch: two shots costing three to four thousand yuan, all out of pocket. That money buys a 97% cut in incidence.

Cost
The recombinant zoster vaccine needs two shots, about 3,000 to 4,000 yuan in total. This money is entirely self-paid.
Benefit
A phase 3 trial spanning 18 countries enrolled 15,400 people, randomized to two groups — vaccine or control injection — and followed an average of 3.2 years. Shingles occurred in 6 cases in the vaccine group versus 210 in the placebo group. Converted to per 1,000 person-years: 0.3 versus 9.1; per 1,000 person-years means the number of cases arising among 1,000 people observed for one year. The paper states: "overall vaccine efficacy against herpes zoster was 97.2% (95% CI 93.7–99.0, P<0.001)". Efficacy across age groups ranged from 96.6% to 97.9%.
Note
It ranks low on value because of the price. Shingles itself is rarely fatal; the trouble is post-herpetic neuralgia, which can hurt for months to years. After vaccination, injection-site pain and fever were both fairly common. The most severe tier (grade 3 symptoms) was 17.0% versus 3.2%.
Sources (1 reference)
Lal H, Cunningham AL, Godeaux O, et al. (2015). Efficacy of an adjuvanted herpes zoster subunit vaccine in older adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(22), 2087-2096. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1501184
22

Get the pneumococcal vaccine after 65

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In a trial of 84,500 older adults, the 13-valent pneumococcal vaccine blocked about 46% of the pneumonia types it covers, and 75% of the most dangerous invasive infections. But it showed no effect on "pneumonia from all causes" — don't expect it to cover every pneumonia.

Cost
A few hundred yuan. Free for older adults in some areas.
Benefit
The Netherlands randomized 84,500 adults over 65 into two groups for comparison. The vaccine used was the 13-valent pneumococcal conjugate vaccine. Its efficacy against vaccine-type pneumonia was 45.6%. Confidence range: 95.2% CI 21.8–62.5. "Vaccine type" means the strains this vaccine covers. Efficacy against invasive pneumococcal disease was 75.0% (95% CI 41.4–90.8) — the most dangerous class of infection. Against pneumonia from all causes combined, it had no effect.
Note
It only prevents the types the vaccine covers; getting the shot doesn't mean you never get pneumonia. Chinese seniors usually get the 23-valent polysaccharide vaccine, which is not the same product as the 13-valent conjugate used in this trial — the efficacy figures above cannot be transferred directly.
Sources (1 reference)
Bonten MJ, Huijts SM, Bolkenbaas M, et al. (2015). Polysaccharide conjugate vaccine against pneumococcal pneumonia in adults. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(12), 1114-1125. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1408544

Get tested for H. pylori; if positive, get eradication treatment

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

In the Linqu, Shandong trial with 22 years of follow-up, people who eradicated H. pylori were about half as likely to get stomach cancer later, and about 40% less likely to die of it. Testing costs one to two hundred yuan; eradication means two weeks of pills.

Cost
The carbon-13 or carbon-14 breath test costs 100 to 200 yuan. Eradication means taking four drugs at once, 200 to 500 yuan for the two weeks of medication. The hard part is taking the full two weeks exactly on schedule.
Benefit
The randomized trial in Linqu, Shandong followed participants for 22 years. Those who received H. pylori eradication treatment were about half as likely to develop stomach cancer. Point estimate OR 0.48, confidence range 95% CI 0.32 to 0.71. Risk of dying from stomach cancer about 38% lower (HR 0.62, 95% CI 0.39 to 0.99).
Note
Reinfection after eradication is possible, so have the whole household tested and treated together. The trial's population lived in a high-incidence stomach cancer area. People in low-incidence areas will see much smaller real-world benefit.
Sources (1 reference)
Li WQ et al. (2019). Effects of Helicobacter pylori treatment and vitamin and garlic supplementation on gastric cancer incidence and mortality: follow-up of a randomized intervention trial. BMJ. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.l5016
24

Heavy smokers: get a low-dose chest CT once a year

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Eligible heavy smokers who get a low-dose CT every year are 20% less likely to die of lung cancer than those who only get chest X-rays, and 6.7% less likely to die overall. The price is the follow-up scans after suspicious findings, and the anxiety in between.

Cost
200 to 400 yuan a scan, done in 10 minutes. Also count the follow-up testing after a false alarm, and the worrying through that stretch of time.
Benefit
The US NLST randomized trial enrolled 53,454 people, all aged 55 to 74 with a smoking history of 30 pack-years or more who had quit no more than 15 years ago. A pack-year is a unit for measuring smoking: one pack a day for one year. The results were as follows. Low-dose CT, compared with chest X-ray alone, cut lung cancer deaths by 20.0% in relative terms. Confidence range 95% CI 6.8 to 26.7. All-cause mortality fell 6.7% in relative terms, confidence range 95% CI 1.2 to 13.6.
Note
This applies only to high-risk smokers. In the same trial, 24.2% of the low-dose CT group had suspicious findings, and 96.4% of those were false alarms. For non-smokers, this test is paying money for anxiety.
Sources (1 reference)
National Lung Screening Trial Research Team (2011). Reduced Lung-Cancer Mortality with Low-Dose Computed Tomographic Screening. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1102873
25

When depressed or having suicidal thoughts, call 12356; don't stockpile sleeping pills or pesticides at home

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Removing lethal means from arm's reach keeps gathering stronger evidence: after analgesics were restricted, related suicides fell 43%; where barriers were installed at frequently used jumping sites, they fell 86%. So don't stockpile sleeping pills or pesticides at home. When things feel unbearable, call 12356 first — it works nationwide and is open at least 18 hours a day.

Cost
Costs nothing. One phone call. Also lock up medications, and keep pesticides out of the house.
Benefit
A review systematically covering the last 10 years of research: the evidence for restricting people's access to lethal means keeps strengthening. After analgesics were brought under control, analgesic-related suicides fell 43%. After barriers went up at frequently used jumping sites, they fell 86% (79% to 91% — the parentheses give the confidence range). School-based cognitive programs cut suicide attempts by about 55% (OR 0.45, 95% CI 0.24 to 0.85). Antidepressant medication and psychotherapy are important parts of suicide prevention. From May 1, 2025, dialing 12356 anywhere in China connects to a psychological assistance hotline open no fewer than 18 hours a day.
Note
Why Grade B: the evidence on means restriction is mostly ecological studies comparing numbers before and after policies; the hotline itself has no evidence of lowering mortality. The impulse behind suicidal thoughts often lasts only minutes to hours, so moving lethal means one step out of reach is itself an intervention. For data on that time scale, and long-term outcomes after an attempt, see item 32 in this section (the moment suicidal thoughts surface, tell one person nearby first). For what remains after being saved, see item 33 in this section.
Sources (2 references)
Zalsman G et al. (2016). Suicide prevention strategies revisited: 10-year systematic review. Lancet Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(16)30030-X ; National Health Commission (2024). Notice on Adopting 12356 as the National Unified Psychological Assistance Hotline Number (GW Yi Zheng Han [2024] No. 259). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6994470…
26

Keep a fire extinguisher, fire blanket, escape respirator hood, and first-aid kit ready; check them once a year

Grade BValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Fire extinguisher, fire blanket, escape hood, and first-aid kit are all on the Ministry of Emergency Management's 11-item home emergency list. A set costs a few hundred yuan, bought once. In the studies that did in-home safety education, injury rates ran about a quarter lower.

Cost
Extinguisher, fire blanket, one respirator hood per person, plus a first-aid kit: a few hundred yuan for the set. Buy once, then spend ten minutes each year checking it all.
Benefit
The Ministry of Emergency Management's National Basic Recommended List of Household Emergency Supplies has 11 items. "Fire extinguisher and fire blanket" are for "fighting incipient fires", and the list notes "the fire blanket can be draped over the body to escape". "Respirator hood" refers to "a fire-filtering self-rescue respirator for use in fire evacuation". "Topical medicines" means "styptic powder, adhesive bandages, gauze bandages, and so on, for treating wounds". Cochrane pooled 98 studies and 2,605,044 people. Home safety interventions brought injury incidence down to IRR 0.89. Confidence range: 95% CI 0.78 to 1.01. Among them, interventions delivered in person at home cut injury incidence about 25% (IRR 0.75, 95% CI 0.62 to 0.91).
Note
Contested. In the same Cochrane review, interventions that did not hand out equipment lowered injury rates about 20%. Point estimate IRR 0.78, confidence range 95% CI 0.66 to 0.92. The group that did hand out equipment didn't do better. What reduces injuries is mainly in-home education and modifications, so equipment's benefit is logged as "medium", not "large". When buying an extinguisher, look for the CCC mark; on stored-pressure types, the gauge needle should sit in the green zone. For smoke and carbon monoxide alarms, see item 3 in this section. For tourniquet use, see Section 13, item 12. For how to choose each item, where to keep it, and how often to replace it, see [docs/家庭应急装备清单.md](../docs/家庭应急装备清单.md)
Sources (3 references)
Ministry of Emergency Management (2020). National Basic Recommended List of Household Emergency Supplies. https://www.mem.gov.cn/kp/shaq/202011/t20201129_372149.shtml ; Kendrick D et al. (2012). Blood in your urine visible to the naked eye — even painless, even gone the next day — still deserves a checkup

Grade BValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: small

After one episode of visibly bloody urine, a person over 60 has about a 2.8% chance of eventually being diagnosed with bladder cancer; at ages 40 to 59, about 1.2%. Not high numbers, but high enough that a checkup is mandatory. Even if the bleeding is gone the next day, still go get checked.

Cost
Urinalysis costs a few dozen yuan, urinary tract ultrasound one to two hundred. If the doctor thinks it's needed, add a cystoscopy at around 1,000 yuan.
Benefit
A UK study used electronic records from community general practice (primary care): 4,915 bladder cancer cases against 21,718 controls. Among people with visible blood in the urine, the share eventually diagnosed with bladder cancer was: 2.8% for those over 60, confidence range 95% CI 2.5 to 3.1; 1.2% at ages 40 to 59, range 0.6 to 2.3. This measure's technical name is positive predictive value. Blood visible only under a microscope carries meaning too: odds ratio 20, confidence range 95% CI 12 to 33, with a rate of 1.6% for those over 60, range 1.2 to 2.1.
Note
"Painless" is the key word. Hematuria from stones or infection usually comes with gripping flank or abdominal pain, or frequent, urgent, or painful urination. Tumor-caused bleeding often feels like nothing at all, and it stops on its own for days before returning — many people let it go on that account. Being on anticoagulants is no reason to skip the check. After vigorous exercise, or around menstruation, one repeat test first is reasonable. Benefit is logged as "small" because there is only a detection rate, no effect size for "how many deaths early testing prevents".
Sources (1 reference)
Price SJ, Shephard EA, Stapley SA, Barraclough K, Hamilton WT (2014). Non-visible versus visible haematuria and bladder cancer risk: a study of electronic records in primary care. British Journal of General Practice, 64(626), e584-e589. https://doi.org/10.3399/bjgp14X681409
28

If erectile function falters, get your cardiovascular system checked first; don't treat it as purely a bedroom matter

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Men with erectile dysfunction later develop cardiovascular disease about 40% more often than others, and heart attacks about 60% more. The younger the man, the bigger the gap. The problem often shows up before chest pain does. So get blood pressure, blood sugar, and blood lipids checked first; don't just buy something to paper over it.

Cost
Registration: a few dozen yuan. Blood pressure plus blood tests for glucose and lipids: one to two hundred yuan. One trip to the hospital, results in a few days.
Benefit
A meta-analysis pooled 14 cohort studies totaling 92,757 men, followed an average of 6.1 years. Compared with men without erectile dysfunction, those with it had the following later risks. Major cardiovascular events about 44% higher (RR 1.44, 95% CI 1.27 to 1.63 — this is the confidence range). Heart attack about 62% higher (RR 1.62, 1.34 to 1.96). Cerebrovascular events about 39% higher (RR 1.39, 1.23 to 1.57). All-cause death about 25% higher (RR 1.25, 1.12 to 1.39). Cardiovascular death showed no clear gap (RR 1.19, 0.97 to 1.46). The younger the age, the higher the multiplier. Men whose baseline cardiovascular risk was medium had higher multipliers than both the high-risk and low-risk groups. Studies using questionnaires gave a multiplier of 1.61 (1.38 to 1.86); studies asking a single question, 1.27 (1.18 to 1.37).
Note
All 14 are studies following groups of people over time, not randomized trials, so the "40% more" is an association, not causation. An occasional off day doesn't count; only a problem persisting beyond three months does. What to check is the same list as items 7 and 8 in this section: blood pressure, fasting glucose, plus lipids, smoking, and waist size. Don't buy "male enhancement" supplements online. The legitimate drugs are prescription-only, and their labels list nitrates as contraindicated — anyone using nitroglycerin or the like must not take them together, as the combination can crash blood pressure. For improvement, see item 29 in this section (losing weight and quitting smoking can improve erectile function). Benefit is logged as "medium", not "large": 44% is the risk gap between two groups, not "how many deaths one checkup prevents". Nor as "small": the signal in item 27 of this section (visible blood in urine) has only a detection rate, whereas the hypertension, diabetes, and dyslipidemia found here all have ready-made treatments.
Sources (2 references)
Vlachopoulos CV, Terentes-Printzios DG, Ioakeimidis NK, Aznaouridis KA, Stefanadis CI (2013). Prediction of cardiovascular events and all-cause mortality with erectile dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes, 6(1), 99-109. https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCOUTCOMES.112.966903; DailyMed (the US National Library of Medicine's drug label database). VIAGRA (sildenafil citrate) tablet, CONTRAINDICATIONS. https://dailymed.nlm.nih.gov/dailymed/lookup.cfm?setid=d905…
29

Losing weight, quitting smoking, and controlling blood pressure and blood sugar can improve erectile function too

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: small

Get your cardiovascular risk factors under control and erectile function improves on its own. On a standard questionnaire, the average gain is 2 to 3 points. The questionnaire tops out at 25 points, with 22 or above counted as normal.

Cost
Costs nothing, may even save money. The hard part is the long haul: controlling what you eat, getting moving, quitting cigarettes.
Benefit
A meta-analysis pooled 6 randomized controlled trials and 740 men. The interventions were lifestyle change, or medication to control cardiovascular risk factors, with at least 6 weeks of follow-up. Result: scores on the erectile function questionnaire (IIEF-5) improved an average of 2.66 points (95% CI 1.86 to 3.47 — this is the confidence range). Excluding the 2 statin trials among them (143 men), the remaining 4 lifestyle-only trials (597 men) still improved 2.40 points (1.19 to 3.61). The IIEF-5 is a 5-question questionnaire scored 5 to 25. The paper divides scores into five bands: 22 to 25 counts as no dysfunction, 5 to 7 as severe.
Note
The 6 trials' interventions differed — some were weight loss plus exercise, others medication controlling blood pressure and lipids — and there were only 740 men in total. So the direction is clear, but how much any one person improves varies. Benefit is logged as "small" because the only endpoint was a questionnaire score, with no numbers on "how much illness avoided later". The same moves have hard endpoints elsewhere: quitting smoking, see Section 2, item 1 (quit smoking, the sooner the better); weight loss, see Section 2, item 32 (keep BMI at 20–25); blood pressure, see item 7 in this section (measure blood pressure, medicate if high). Medication itself is not off-limits, provided it's a doctor's prescription. "Supplements" sold online often smuggle in these ingredients at unknown doses; how to tell them apart, see Section 28, item 4 (don't buy diet pills promising fast weight loss).
Sources (2 references)
Gupta BP, Murad MH, Clifton MM, Prokop L, Nehra A, Kopecky SL (2011). The effect of lifestyle modification and cardiovascular risk factor reduction on erectile dysfunction: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Archives of Internal Medicine, 171(20), 1797-1803. https://doi.org/10.1001/archinternmed.2011.440; Rosen RC, Cappelleri JC, Smith MD, Lipsky J, Peña BM (1999). Development and evaluation of an abridged, 5-item version of the International Index of Erectile Function (IIEF-5) as a diagnostic tool for erectile dysfunction. International Journal of Impotence Research, 11(6), 319-326. https://doi.org/10.1038/sj.ijir.3900472
30

Use condoms for the whole act of sex; never share needles with anyone

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Wear one for the whole act, every time, and the odds of heterosexual HIV transmission drop by more than 70%. "Most of the time" is barely better than not at all. Syphilis, gonorrhea, and the rest get blocked in the same stroke.

Cost
One or two yuan apiece. The hard part isn't the money; it's using one every time, and putting it on from the very start.
Benefit
One study pooled 25 studies covering 10,676 heterosexual couples, all with one partner infected with HIV and the other not — serodiscordant, in the technical term. Compared with those who never used them, couples who consistently used condoms every time had about 71% lower risk of HIV transmission. Point estimate RR 0.29, confidence range 95% CI 0.20 to 0.43. Compared with intermittent users, about 77% lower (RR 0.23, 95% CI 0.13 to 0.40). The authors concluded that although condoms are imperfect, "consistent use can reduce HIV transmission by more than 70%". The same layer of protection covers syphilis, gonorrhea, chlamydia, and other sexually transmitted infections.
Note
"Irregular use" and "no use" are nearly the same; it works only every time, all the way through. Sharing needles is another independent, highly efficient transmission route with nothing to do with sex — injecting drugs, tattoos, and piercings all count. People at high risk can also use pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP): taking medication in advance to block infection. Pooling 18 studies, in trials where more than 70% took the pills on schedule, those on PrEP had about 70% lower risk of HIV infection than those on placebo. Point estimate: risk ratio 0.30, confidence range 95% CI 0.21 to 0.45. Trials where few took the pills on schedule showed no protective effect. PrEP is prescription-only; ask at an infectious disease clinic or the CDC, don't buy it online. For what to do after an exposure has already happened, see Section 13.
Sources (2 references)
Giannou FK, Tsiara CG, Nikolopoulos GK, et al. (2016). Condom effectiveness in reducing heterosexual HIV transmission: a systematic review and meta-analysis of studies on HIV serodiscordant couples. Expert Review of Pharmacoeconomics & Outcomes Research, 16(4), 489-499. https://doi.org/10.1586/14737167.2016.1102635; Fonner VA et al. (2016). Effectiveness and safety of oral HIV preexposure prophylaxis for all populations. AIDS. https://doi.org/10.1097/QAD.0000000000001145 (pre-exposure prophylaxis, PrEP)
31

Had a high-risk exposure? Get an HIV test — free and confidential at the CDC

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Getting an HIV test at the CDC costs nothing. Without your consent, no organization or individual may disclose your name, address, workplace, or medical history. A positive result is not a death sentence: people who stay on medication and keep the virus undetectable do not transmit HIV to sexual partners. That study followed more than 700 couples through over 70,000 condomless sex acts — zero transmissions between partners.

Cost
Costs nothing. One trip to the CDC or a designated medical facility, one vial of blood. The hard part is taking the step of asking for the test.
Benefit
Article 23 of the HIV/AIDS Prevention and Control Regulations states it: health authorities of local people's governments at or above the county level designate medical institutions, and these institutions "shall provide free counseling and initial screening tests to people who voluntarily seek HIV counseling and testing". Early testing has practical value: current antiretroviral therapy can press the virus below detection. The World Health Organization's position: "people on antiretroviral treatment with an undetectable viral load do not transmit HIV to sexual partners". The PARTNER study followed 782 gay couples, each with one infected and one uninfected partner — serodifferent, in the technical term. Total: 1,593 couple-years (each couple's follow-up years added together). Over that period there were 76,088 condomless sex acts and 15 new infections. After phylogenetic analysis comparing viral genes, none of the 15 came from the partner — transmission between partners was zero. Article 39 of the regulations provides: "Without the consent of the person concerned or their guardian, no organization or individual may disclose the names, addresses, workplaces, portraits, medical histories, or other information from which the specific identity of people living with HIV, AIDS patients, or their family members could be inferred."
Note
The window period determines when a test counts. Guangdong CDC's figures: nucleic acid testing can detect at about 1 week, fourth-generation combined antigen/antibody testing at about 2 weeks, third-generation antibody testing at about 3 weeks. The advice: test no sooner than 2 weeks after, and retest at 2 to 4 week intervals. Once 3 months have passed since the last high-risk act, infection can be ruled out for more than 99.99%. A positive self-test kit is not a diagnosis; it must be rechecked at the CDC or a proper institution. Article 3 of the regulations states that no organization or individual may discriminate against people living with HIV or their families, whose rights to marriage, employment, medical care, and schooling are protected by law. Article 38 also requires people living with HIV to "promptly inform those they have sexual relations with of the fact of their infection or illness". For pregnancy-period screening for the three diseases and mother-to-child transmission blocking, see Section 27.
Sources (4 references)
State Council (2006). (2019). Risk of HIV transmission through condomless sex in serodifferent gay couples with the HIV-positive partner taking suppressive antiretroviral therapy (PARTNER): final results of a multicentre, prospective, observational study. The Lancet, 393(10189), 2428-2438. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(19)30418-0; Guangdong Provincial Center for Disease Control and Prevention. Public education on the HIV testing window period. https://web.archive.org/web/20260915151957/https://cdcp.gd.… (the window-period figures; the original page is offline, the link is a web archive from 2026-09-15)

The moment suicidal thoughts surface, tell one person nearby first and hand those minutes over to them

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Nearly half of people who attempt suicide say no more than 10 minutes passed between the first thought and the act — so what you usually have to get through is those few dozen minutes. Three-quarters had contact with someone nearby during that window; they just didn't say anything. Of people hospitalized for self-harm, about 2% die by suicide within 1 year and about 7% over 9-plus years — the vast majority do not go on to die by suicide.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is speaking up in the moment, and admitting you can't be alone for the next few hours.
Benefit
82 suicide attempters were interviewed within 3 days of admission: 47.6% (39 people) said no more than 10 minutes elapsed between the first suicidal thought of this episode and the attempt itself. Those whose process stretched longer scored significantly higher on suicidal intent. Impulsivity scale scores had no relation to how long the process took. 76.8% (63 people) said they had some contact with a partner, family member, or friend during that time. The authors' conclusion: the window for intervention is usually very short, leaving professionals limited room to step in at that stage, so recognizing the signals and knowing the interventions must be spread to ordinary people. A separate systematic review pooled 90 follow-up studies. Among people who sought care for self-harm, the median rate of non-fatal self-harm repetition at 1 year was 16%. Death by suicide at 1 year: 2%. With 9-plus years of follow-up, about 7% died by suicide.
Note
Why Grade B: Deisenhammer's study had only 82 people, from a single hospital, relying on participants' after-the-fact recall. Owens's review reports the median across 90 studies with varying methods, not a single pooled number. The same paper states plainly that self-harm patients' suicide risk remains several hundred times that of the general population. So "the vast majority do not go on to die by suicide" describes this group overall — it is no guarantee for any one person, and the illness still needs proper treatment. For moving lethal means out of reach and 12356, see item 25 in this section. For the first things to do when feeling low, see Section 3, item 18. For the aftermath of being saved, see item 33 in this section. For what you can do when someone near you voices such thoughts, see Section 8, item 15.
Sources (2 references)
Deisenhammer EA, Ing CM, Strauss R, Kemmler G, Hinterhuber H, Weiss EM (2009). The duration of the suicidal process: how much time is left for intervention between consideration and accomplishment of a suicide attempt? Journal of Clinical Psychiatry, 70(1), 19-24. https://doi.org/10.4088/JCP.07m03904; Owens D, Horrocks J, House A (2002). Fatal and non-fatal repetition of self-harm: systematic review. British Journal of Psychiatry, 181, 193-199. https://doi.org/10.1192/bjp.181.3.193

Don't count on 'being saved' as a fallback: after drinking pesticide or inhaling gas, the ER can save your life but not your lungs or brain

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Paraquat has no antidote; more than 40% of those who drink it don't survive. It inflames the lungs and slowly stiffens them, and the kidneys and liver take damage too. Among people rescued from gas poisoning, nearly half had worse brain function six weeks on — even with hyperbaric oxygen, a quarter still did.

Cost
Costs nothing. Just knowing this in advance.
Benefit
A systematic review of paraquat poisoning: case fatality is extremely high, because the substance itself is highly toxic and effective treatment is lacking. It is actively pumped into lung tissue against a concentration gradient — active uptake up the concentration gradient, technically — resulting in pneumonia and pulmonary fibrosis, while also causing kidney and liver injury. The review states: gastric lavage should not be performed. Hemodialysis and hemoperfusion are unlikely to change the clinical course. The evidence for steroids and immunosuppressants is very weak. The review adds one more line: "case fatality is high at all centers despite wide variation in treatment". Ten tertiary hospitals in Bangladesh admitted 1,420 cases from 2013 to 2024; among the 257 analyzable cases, case fatality was 43.2%. Common presentations: leg swelling from acute kidney failure 71.2%, vomiting 65.8%, abdominal pain 58.0%. The acute carbon monoxide trial was double-blind and randomized, 76 people per group. Neither doctors nor patients knew the assignment. At six weeks, cognitive sequelae remained in 19/76 (25.0%) of the hyperbaric oxygen group. The normobaric oxygen group: 35/76 (46.1%), P=0.007. After adjusting for other factors, OR 0.45 (95% CI 0.22 to 0.92 — the parentheses give the confidence range). Another study observed 73 consecutive cases: 30% had cognitive sequelae, and 12% developed white matter hyperintensities. From July 1, 2014, China revoked the registration and production license of paraquat aqueous solution and stopped production. From July 1, 2016, the aqueous formulation stopped being sold and used domestically. From September 26, 2020, sale and use of soluble gel formulations were banned within the country. The documents state that "suicide incidents from paraquat ingestion occurring from time to time" was the direct reason for tightening regulation.
Note
Why Grade B: these studies covered poisoning patients generally, not a single suicide-attempt population — the carbon monoxide trial also included accidental poisonings. So the sequelae percentages above cannot be taken directly as "the probability of outcome for a suicide attempter". What can be said with certainty: no method leaves no lasting damage. For on-scene handling of carbon monoxide, see Section 13, item 19. For accidental ingestion of pesticides or drugs — don't induce vomiting, bring the bottle, seek care — see Section 13, item 20. For not stockpiling pesticides and sleeping pills at home, see item 25 in this section. This book does not compare the lethality of different methods and does not describe any specific method.
Sources (5 references)
Gawarammana IB, Buckley NA (2011). Medical management of paraquat ingestion. British Journal of Clinical Pharmacology, 72(5), 745-757. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2125.2011.04026.x; Chowdhury FR et al. (2026). Clinical and Laboratory Profile of Paraquat Poisoning: A Toxicological Crisis in Bangladesh. American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene, 115, 176-182. https://doi.org/10.4269/ajtmh.25-0719; Weaver LK, Hopkins RO, Chan KJ, et al. (2002). Hyperbaric oxygen for acute carbon monoxide poisoning. New England Journal of Medicine, 347(14), 1057-1067. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa013121; Parkinson RB, Hopkins RO, Cleavinger HB, et al. (2002). White matter hyperintensities and neuropsychological outcome following carbon monoxide poisoning. Neurology, 58(10), 1525-1532. https://doi.org/10.1212/wnl.58.10.1525; General Office of the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (2018). Notice on Effectively Strengthening Paraquat Supervision (Nong Ban Nong [2018] No. 17). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/31/content_544…

Don't bet on 'a few days of rest' after a fall from height: most people who enter a trauma ICU survive, but the price is counted in years

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortality rateMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Of people who fell from height and entered a trauma ICU, only 5.5% died — but the injuries are severe and the treatment long. Nearly half injured three or more body regions at once, a bit over a third went on ventilators, and the longest ICU stay was 132 days. Half fell from no more than 3 meters. Of the severely injured, fewer than 60% later returned to work.

Cost
Costs nothing. Just seeing this ledger clearly first.
Benefit
A trauma ICU (intensive care unit) in southern Xinjiang compiled statistics. From April 2020 to July 2024 it admitted 289 fall-from-height cases, with an average age of 40.3. Median fall height was 3 meters; 26.6% fell from above 5 meters, 11.4% from above 10. Median injury severity score (ISS) was 24 — the higher the score, the worse the injury — and 63.3% had an ISS above 20. 47.1% injured three or more body regions, 18.3% four or more. 36% needed mechanical ventilation, median duration 103.5 hours. Median ICU stay was 8 days, shortest 1 day, longest 132 days. In-hospital or 30-day mortality was 5.5% (16/289). A German trauma center admitted 84 polytrauma patients with ISS ≥ 25 — polytrauma meaning multiple body regions injured at once. Within follow-up, 58% returned to work. Age, length of ICU treatment, and self-rated health were predictors. In 2024 the average hospital inpatient expense per admission nationwide was 9,870.0 yuan, down 4.3% from the previous year at current prices. Total national health expenditure that year was 9,089.55 billion yuan, of which out-of-pocket health spending was 2,500.75 billion yuan, 27.5%.
Note
Why Grade B: the falls group is one hospital's retrospective chart review, with accidental and intentional falls not separated. The return-to-work group has only 84 people, and it is in Germany. Neither can serve as "what happens to a person after jumping from a height". The per-admission expense is an average over all hospitalizations nationwide, not the cost of fall injuries — cited only to give a verifiable floor. The original study gives only this group's height distribution, so no height-to-outcome mapping is written here. For pressure sores — the top thing to watch during long bed rest — see Section 17, item 8. For deep vein thrombosis and pulmonary embolism, see Section 13, item 11 (one leg suddenly swells). For what to do when the thought surfaces, see item 32 in this section. For the consequences of poisoning, see item 33 in this section (don't count on 'being saved' as a fallback). Below is the author's own experience: fell from the fourth floor, expecting to be fine in "a dozen or so days"; in fact a year in hospital, four surgeries, plates and screws, half a year unable to turn over or sit up unaided, and the family went into debt for it.
Sources (3 references)
