The 13.8% figure and the 1.8-to-2 multiple were calculated by this book following the People's Bank of China's method; the method is documented in the verification notes. With private lending, steer clear of loan sharks; see also Section 7, item 15 (don't borrow at usurious rates).
Sources (5 references)
People's Bank of China (2020). Notice on Advancing the Market-Based Reform of Credit Card Overdraft Rates (Yin Fa [2020] No. 327). https://xining.pbc.gov.cn/zhengwugongkai/4081330/4406346/46…; People's Bank of China (2021). PBOC Announcement [2021] No. 3 (Articles 1, 3, and 4; Annex "Examples of Calculating the Annualized Loan Rate Using the Internal Rate of Return Method," Example 3). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-03/31/content_559…; Supreme People's Court (2nd amendment, 2020). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases (Articles 1, 25, and 26). http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/94b6623974526df7d2430a3… (Supreme People's Court Gazette); Supreme People's Court (2020). Official Reply on the Scope of Application of the New Judicial Interpretation on Private Lending (Fa Shi [2020] No. 27). https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/285171.html; National Interbank Funding Center, authorized by the People's Bank of China (2026). Announcement of the Loan Prime Rate (LPR) for August 20, 2026. https://www.chinamoney.com.cn/chinese/rdgz/20260820/3399885…
8

No tipping streamers, no topping up games, no impulse orders

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Gamers in China spend about 480 yuan a year on games per person, and once spent the money is basically unrecoverable. The law only lets minors get back money spent without a parent's consent; adults have no such clause. The easiest defense is to set it up in advance: turn off password-free payment, set per-transaction and daily limits, and unbind your payment methods.

Cost
Nothing. Spend a few minutes doing three things: turn off password-free payment, set per-transaction and daily limits, and delete the payment methods bound to the platforms. The hard part is resisting that one tap in the moment.
Benefit
This is a big line item. In 2024, China's games market took in 325.783 billion yuan in actual sales revenue, with 674 million users — about 480 yuan per person (computed by dividing the two figures above). Money spent is basically unrecoverable. Only one exception exists: tips and top-ups made by a person of limited civil capacity (here, a minor) without the guardian's consent — when the guardian demands the money back, "the people's court shall support" the claim. Tips and top-ups by adults themselves have no such provision. Also, minors were already allowed to play online games only on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory holidays, for the single hour from 8 p.m. to 9 p.m. each day (China, 2020 and 2021)
Note
Rated B because no one has directly measured "how much not tipping saves"; only industry-wide totals exist. Turning off password-free payment and setting limits are folk practices, rated C on their own. The full text of Articles 19 and 145 of the Civil Code is quoted verbatim in item 9 (a child topping up games and tipping streamers on a phone). Not investment advice.
Sources (3 references)
National Press and Publication Administration (2024). China's games market revenue tops 325.7 billion yuan this year, a new high (from the Games Publishing Working Committee of the China Audio-Video and Digital Publishing Association, "2024 China Games Industry Report"). https://www.nppa.gov.cn/xxfb/ywdt/202412/t20241216_877445.html; Supreme People's Court (2020). Guiding Opinions (II) on Trying Civil Cases Involving the COVID-19 Epidemic According to Law (Fa Fa [2020] No. 17, Article 9). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/230181.html; National Press and Publication Administration (2021). Notice on Further Strict Management to Effectively Prevent Minors' Addiction to Online Games (Guo Xin Chu Fa [2021] No. 14). https://www.nppa.gov.cn/xxfb/tzgs/202108/t20210830_666285.html
9

If a child tops up games or tips streamers on a phone: large sums spent by those over 8 without parental ratification can be reclaimed

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Money spent by a child over 8 is void — and refundable — whenever the amount is clearly out of proportion to the child's age and intelligence and the parent neither consents nor acknowledges the transaction. Children under 8 cannot legally decide to spend money on their own at all. And a parent who never takes a position is treated in law as not acknowledging it.

Cost
No money, but it takes time to gather evidence and negotiate with the platform, which usually refuses first and refunds later. If talks fail, your only option is to sue — that starts at several months, and lawyer's fees come out of your pocket. So get your materials complete first; going through the platform and 12315 is the better deal. The hard part is when the child won't talk; you have to ask patiently until it's clear.
Benefit
Minors over 8 years of age are persons of limited civil capacity, meaning they may do on their own only what suits their age and intelligence. Civil juristic acts that do not suit their age and intelligence take effect only with the consent or ratification of their statutory agent: a parent must nod beforehand, or acknowledge it afterward. Children under 8 are persons without civil capacity; they cannot decide anything for themselves, and their affairs are handled by their statutory agent on their behalf. If the statutory agent makes no statement, it is deemed a refusal to ratify: a parent who stays silent the whole time is treated as not acknowledging the transaction
Note
Everything turns on evidence: you must show it was the child operating the phone, not you. Useful materials: top-ups clustered during school hours or the parents' working hours, the device's usage logs, the child's chat and game records, and the child's own statement. There is no uniform money line for "appropriate to age and intelligence" — a game skin worth a few dozen yuan is not the same as tips worth tens of thousands. Preventing it up front is easier: set a cap on password-free payment, turn on youth mode, and never tell the child the payment password. For your own impulsive tipping and top-ups, see this section's item "No tipping streamers, no topping up games, no impulse orders."
Sources (1 reference)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code. Teach your child one sentence: anyone who asks you to pick up a parent's phone and operate it, or to read out a verification code, is a scammer

Grade BValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The six scams below all work differently, but the final step is always the same move: get the child to take a parent's phone and transfer money, or read out a verification code. So one taught sentence is enough: whoever tells you to touch a parent's phone or read out a code is a scammer. Add one more: "If you get scammed, tell me first — I won't scold you." Only if the child dares to speak up the same day does the money have a chance of being recovered.

Cost
Nothing. Walk the child through the six categories below, then agree on the sentence "If you get scammed, tell me first — I won't scold you." At the same time, set a cap on password-free payment, turn on youth mode, and don't tell the child the payment password. The hard part is holding back your anger after a scam actually happens.
Benefit
The Quanzhou anti-fraud center, together with the Quanzhou education bureau, broke down six scams that specifically target young people. They work differently, but the last step is the same move: get the child to take a parent's phone and transfer money. Category 1, low-price private trades of game accounts and gear. Xiao Wang privately transferred 260 yuan; the other side claimed "transfers by minors violate the rules and the account will be frozen," and he tapped a "verification link" with his dad's phone — over 30,000 yuan was moved out of the account. Category 2, "removing the anti-addiction restriction." The scammer threatened "transfer the money to cancel it, or your parents go to jail"; the child transferred 7,000 yuan with his mom's phone. The source states that anti-addiction limits are set by the authorities, and "there is no such thing as a private unlock channel." Category 3, tipping refunds. A scammer posing as "official customer service" says a minor's tips can be refunded and demands "refund only after you send gifts to a designated livestream from a parent's Alipay" — 73,000 yuan was tipped out of the mother's account, and she was blocked. The source says "if someone contacts you asking you to send gifts for a refund, it is 100% a scam." Category 4, impersonating classmates or teachers. The scammer steals an account and sends a voice message naming the person to borrow money. At back-to-school time they also slip into class groups posing as the teacher, posting "pay 500 yuan in school fees," with the same avatar and nickname as the real teacher, plus a planted "shill" in the group saying "already paid." Category 5, celebrity fandom. The scammer pulls the child into a "star's fan group, claim an 888-yuan red packet," first gets the child to transfer 48.88 yuan for "verification," then frightens them: "a minor taking part violates the rules, the platform will freeze 80,000 yuan, and your parents go to jail." In total 16,000 yuan was swindled. The source says "real police and lawyers will never contact a minor online for an investigation, let alone ask to operate a parent's phone." Category 6, luring people off secondhand-marketplace platforms with low-priced goods into private transfers. The same material lists three red lines for kids themselves. First, never lend, sell, or rent out bank cards or phone cards: a card used to move illicit funds may constitute the crime of assisting information-network criminal activity, and a criminal record can affect graduate-school and civil-service exams. Second, "phone-port" side gigs are illegal. Third, overseas "high-paying jobs" — you may be controlled the moment you arrive (nationwide, October 2025)
Note
Rated B because what officials provide is a breakdown of scam scripts plus individual cases — no incidence rates, no statistics on prevention effect. Keep this distinct from item 9 (a child topping up games and tipping streamers on a phone): money a child spent on top-ups and tips itself can be reclaimed under the Civil Code. Money swindled out by scammers doesn't fall under that provision — you can only report to the police and request a payment freeze under Section 8, item 2. Whether it can be recovered depends on whether the money is still in the account. The scammer's core scare line to kids is "you broke the rules and your parents go to jail." Say this up front: that sentence itself is the hallmark of a scam, which works better than grilling them afterward. And really honor "tell me first, I won't scold you." In these cases, the common reason losses snowballed was the child fearing a scolding and staying silent. For the adult version — impersonation of acquaintances, and AI face swaps — see Section 8, items 3 and 4 (hard anti-fraud rules; if it involves a transfer, hang up first). Adults are the same: never read out verification codes or do face scans for anyone; see Section 8, item 45 (reading out verification codes).

Decline extended warranties on electronics

Grade BValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Extended warranties typically sell for 10% to 50% of the original price, and the seller's margin is more than ten times that of ordinary goods — that gap is the extra you pay. Major components like washing machine and refrigerator motors are already covered by national rules for 3 years. When you see a very cheap extended warranty, divide the warranty price by the cost of one repair: the result is how high the odds of at least one breakdown in those years must be to break even.

Cost
Nothing. The trade-off is that after the warranty expires, a repair comes out of your own pocket — though that's unlikely.
Benefit
Extended warranties are typically priced at 10% to 50% of the product's original price. Industry estimates cited in the research put the average gross margin on extended warranties at 50% to 60%: of every 100 yuan sold, 50 to 60 is profit. That's roughly 18 times the gross margin on ordinary goods. In 2003, extended warranties were only 3% to 4% of Best Buy's revenue yet contributed over 50% of its profit (US, 2000s retail data). If you see a warranty priced far below that range, do your own math: warranty price ÷ cost of one repair = the breakdown probability needed to break even. It's worth buying only if you estimate the odds of at least one failure during the warranty years exceed that number. For example, a 25-yuan warranty with a hypothetical 300-yuan repair needs a better-than-8% chance of at least one breakdown to break even. The 300 yuan here is an example, not a statistic. Before calculating, subtract the part national rules already cover. The statutory "three guarantees" period runs from the invoice date: for washing machines and refrigerators, 1 year for the whole unit and 3 years for major components. A washing machine's major components are the motor, timer, program controller, and capacitor; a refrigerator's are the compressor, thermostat, and so on. The stretch where an extended warranty overlaps the three guarantees is paying for something you already had (nationwide, since 1995)
Note
The gross-margin figure is an industry estimate the paper cites from someone else (Business Week 2004), not something the paper measured itself. The calculation above fits ordinary people who can absorb one repair bill out of pocket. If you live off a single device with no backup, run your own numbers. Phone screen-crack insurance needs separate math too: first estimate how often you drop your phone, then judge whether the premium is worth it. A very cheap extended warranty costs only a few dozen yuan even if it's a bad buy; before purchasing, check three things: the start date (if counted from the purchase day, the first years overlap the three guarantees), whether coverage comes from the retailer, the brand, or a third-party company, and whether call-out and parts fees are billed separately. Also check the manual and warranty card — the brand's own promised coverage may be longer than the statutory period.
Sources (2 references)
Chen T, Kalra A, Sun B (2009). Why Do Consumers Buy Extended Service Contracts? Journal of Consumer Research 36(4):611-623. https://doi.org/10.1086/605298; State Economic and Trade Commission et al. (1995). Provisions on Repair, Replacement, and Return Liability for Certain Goods (Guo Jing Mao [1995] No. 458; Article 8: the three-guarantees period runs from the invoice date; Annex "Catalog of Goods Subject to the Three Guarantees (First Batch)": washing machines and household refrigerators, 1 year for the whole unit, 3 years for major components). Administrative normative document of the State Administration for Market Regulation. https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/zc/xzgfxwj/art/2019/art_f…

Prefer generics that passed consistency evaluation and drugs chosen in centralized procurement

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The second centralized-procurement round cut drug prices 53% on average, with the steepest cut at 93%. By April 2026, 11 rounds had been held, covering 490 drugs. When a drug is prescribed or you buy one, ask one extra question: "Is there a centralized-procurement version, by generic name?" Same active ingredient, a lot less money.

Cost
Nothing. When the doctor prescribes and when you buy, ask one extra question: "Is there a centralized-procurement drug under the generic name?"
Benefit
In the state-organized centralized drug procurement, the second round cut prices 53% on average and up to 93% at most. As of April 2026, 11 rounds had been carried out, covering 490 drugs. Drugs that passed or were deemed to have passed consistency evaluation reached 1,695 — roughly two-thirds of chemical drugs in common clinical use (China, official data 2020–2026)
Note
The controversy: people often say "consistency evaluation compares only the ingredients, not the efficacy." That's half right. The method recruits healthy volunteers, draws blood to get the concentration curve after the drug enters the bloodstream, and compares that curve with the originator's — falling within 80% to 125% counts as a pass. Drugs where a small dosing error causes harm face stricter requirements. Excipients — the fillers and coatings beyond the active ingredient — are allowed to differ from the originator's. The rules require only that the active ingredient, dosage form, way of taking it, and therapeutic effect be the same. So it is indeed not "give it to patients for a while and see whether they get better." That question is answered by a different line of research. The National Healthcare Security Administration had hospitals run real-world studies: by December 2024, covering 63 procured drugs, nearly 100 top-tier (Grade III-A) hospitals, and more than 300,000 patients. The results showed no difference from the originator drugs. For metformin, the rate of reaching the glycated hemoglobin target was 83.4% in the generic group versus 78.9% in the originator group; for fasting blood glucose it flipped — 83.8% generic versus 87.6% originator. The two groups each led on some measures. In January 2025, doctors publicly claimed that procured drugs "don't lower blood pressure, anesthetics don't put you to sleep, laxatives don't work." Healthcare security and drug regulators inspected 7 hospitals in Shanghai and concluded the claims mostly came from hearsay and personal impressions — the named laxative wasn't even in hospital use at the time. The same review did acknowledge that problem drugs had been caught in sampling: of the more than 1,600 winning products across the first 9 rounds, 9 were disqualified for quality risks. Of these 9, 6 were imported (including 3 originator drugs) and 3 were domestically made. Two things you can act on. First, if you want to stay on the originator drug, it's usually still prescribable: procurement covers only 60% to 80% of a hospital's purchasing volume, the rest is up to the hospital, and originator drugs are not banned — the cost is paying more yourself. Second, after switching drugs for a chronic condition, don't judge by feel: watch blood pressure, blood glucose, and HbA1c as in Section 16, item 3 (record every reading in the same notebook). If things truly get worse, see your doctor and ask them to report an adverse drug reaction — don't stop the medication on your own.

Set up family account sharing once in the medical insurance app, and the money in your employee-plan personal account can pay for your spouse's, parents', and children's medical care

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

One setup, and the money in your employee medical insurance personal account can pay for your spouse's, parents', or children's doctor visits and prescriptions. Without it, that money can only be used by you, sitting in the account.

Cost
Nothing. In the medical insurance app of the place where you're insured, or at a service office, set up family account sharing once.
Benefit
Money in the personal account can pay the out-of-pocket share of medical fees when you yourself, or your spouse, parents, or children, receive care at designated medical institutions. It can also pay the out-of-pocket share when buying drugs, medical devices, and medical consumables at designated retail pharmacies. The document also proposes exploring use of the personal account to pay family members' individual premiums for urban and rural resident medical insurance
Note
Many people have thousands of yuan lying in their personal account while elderly family members pay for medicine out of pocket. One setup stays valid long term. Most places call it "family mutual aid"; you can do it in your local medical insurance app. Note the red line on the flip side: the personal account cannot be spent on fitness or wellness consumption. Using it to buy health supplements at a pharmacy as a cash-out is insurance fraud.

Drink boiled tap water; don't buy bottled water all year round

Grade CValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Beijing's first-tier water price works out to 0.005 yuan a liter. Bottled water at 1 yuan per 500 ml is 2 yuan a liter — a 400-fold difference. Tap water is governed by a mandatory national standard; day to day, boil it and drink it. If the water source really fails and the water smells or turns murky, that isn't something a few extra minutes of boiling will fix: stop drinking it and report it.

Cost
Buy a kettle. Each boil takes a little time, plus a small amount of gas or electricity.
Benefit
Beijing's first-tier residential water price is 5 yuan per cubic meter, or 0.005 yuan a liter. Bottled water at 1 yuan per 500 ml is 2 yuan a liter, 400 times the price of tap water. Drinking water is governed by the mandatory national standard GB 5749-2022, issued March 15, 2022 and effective April 1, 2023. The responsible authority is the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration (China, 2015 water prices and the 2022 standard)
Note
The controversy: "meeting the standard" tests water leaving the plant and water at pipe ends. When the source or the pipe network has a problem, that can fail briefly. On July 16, 2025, raw water entering the Renhe plant in Yuhang, Hangzhou smelled wrong, and tap water turned foul in some Renhe and Liangzhu neighborhoods. The official finding was that algae decomposing in low-oxygen conditions produced sulfur-ether compounds. After the source was switched, total coliforms and E. coli in the finished water were not detected, and all items met the drinking water standard GB 5749-2022. Seven officials were held accountable afterward, July water bills were fully waived, and filter cartridges were replaced free. But fecal coliform counts at the same water source had been climbing for months before the incident: 10 per liter in April, 7,300 per liter in May, and 16,000 per liter in June at the Yongsheng intake on the Tiaoxi. The GB 3838 Class III surface water limit is 10,000 per liter. That same month, Siling Reservoir at 28,000 per liter and Mantoushan Reservoir at 24,000 per liter also exceeded it. Boiling kills microbes but cannot remove odor compounds, nor chemicals dissolved in the water. If you smell something off, or the water runs yellow or murky, stop drinking it, report it to the water supplier and via 12345, switch to bottled water temporarily, and don't expect a few extra minutes of boiling to carry you through. But this was a localized, one-off accident, and the locality compensated incident by incident — it still isn't a reason to buy bottled water year-round. The "sewage pipe cross-connected" story circulating online was a forged police bulletin, and its publisher has been criminally detained (see Section 9). The 1-yuan-per-500-ml bottled water price is an assumption set up for the arithmetic — redo it with your own city's actual price. In older complexes where secondary water supply facilities fall short, you can add filtration, or buy drinking water only in that situation. Water prices differ across cities; Beijing's figure is only for scale.

Don't trade stocks frequently; trade even less during wild market swings

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The US households that traded most frequently earned just 11.4% a year, while the whole market did 17.9% over the same period — the gap was almost entirely fees. In China's 2014–2015 boom-and-crash, the 85% of households with the smallest accounts traded too often. They earned 250 billion yuan less than buy-and-hold would have — about 30% of their capital.

Cost
Nothing. The hard part is resisting the itch to act on every headline, and the urge to pile in more when everyone else is making money.
Benefit
This study looked at 66,465 household accounts at a US discount broker, 1991 to 1996. The most frequently trading group earned 11.4% annualized — that is, 11.4% a year on average. Over the same period the whole market did 17.9% and the average household 16.4%. The average household's turnover was 75% a year, replacing three-quarters of its holdings in a year. Gross returns (what was earned before fees) barely differed between frequent and infrequent traders, so the gap came mainly from the transaction costs paid while buying and selling (US, 1991–1996). The China data: the study used daily account data from the Shanghai Stock Exchange covering all roughly 40 million accounts. The sample ran 18 months, July 2014 to December 2015. In those 18 months the Shanghai Composite first rose more than 150%; it peaked at 5,166.35 points on June 12, 2015, then fell 40% by the end of December. Household accounts were sorted into four tiers by opening market value. The smallest tier held 85% of all household accounts, the largest 0.5%. The two tiers' opening stock values were similar — 880 billion yuan and 808 billion yuan. The result: the smallest 85% lost 250 billion yuan to active trading, while the largest 0.5% gained 254 billion yuan. "Loss" here means compared with holding everything and doing nothing through the same market stretch. Each figure is about 30% of that tier's opening stock value — 28% for the former, 31% for the latter. For contrast, the two and a half years before June 2014 were calm: any 18-month stretch there showed a gap of only 1% to 3% of opening value. In this episode, household accounts on average turned over their holdings about every three weeks — nearly 18 times a year (Shanghai, China, 2014–2015; comparison period 2012–2014)
Note
The US data is from the 1990s, and A-share commission and stamp-duty structures differ from it, but the principle "the higher the turnover, the lower the return you keep" is the same. The China study does not say don't buy stocks. It computes that, within the same market stretch, the more actively the small-account end trades, the more money flows to the other side of the trade. Nor was the money taken by institutions — it went to the largest group of individuals: over this period, about 90% of SSE trading volume came from retail accounts. The "90% of retail investors lose money" claim circulating online has no verifiable official statistic behind it, and this entry doesn't use that number. Put the turnover rates side by side: in this episode Chinese household accounts traded nearly 18 times a year, while the US households replaced only three-quarters of their holdings in a year. In calm years, this gap in China was only 1 to 3 percentage points of opening value, so the time to hold back hardest is when the market runs hottest. Not investment advice.
Sources (3 references)
Barber BM, Odean T (2000). Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth: The Common Stock Investment Performance of Individual Investors. The Journal of Finance 55(2):773-806. https://doi.org/10.1111/0022-1082.00226; An L, Lou D, Shi D (2022). Wealth redistribution in bubbles and crashes. Journal of Monetary Economics 126:134-153. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jmoneco.2022.01.001; The same authors' publicly posted working-paper version (October 2021; the China figures were verified word for word against it). https://personal.lse.ac.uk/loud/AnLouShi.pdf

Don't invest borrowed money, don't leverage up, and don't buy what you can't understand

Grade BValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Borrow to buy stocks, and once you fall below the line and can't top up the money, you get force-sold. A paper loss becomes a real loss on the spot — you don't even get the chance to "wait for it to come back." Under the rules, people whose account has been open less than six months, or whose average daily assets over the last 20 trading days are below 500,000 yuan, cannot open a margin account. The threshold itself says it isn't for ordinary people.

Cost
Nothing. The hard part is, in a good market, resisting the thought of "borrowing a bit to earn a bit more."
Benefit
Leverage means buying with borrowed money, and it magnifies losses. After you buy on margin, the market value of your collateral can fall below the maintenance guarantee ratio line — a line drawn by the broker, governing what you have pledged to it. Cross below that line and fail to top up collateral in time, and you get force-liquidated: the broker sells it for you directly. The paper loss becomes a real loss on the spot, with no chance to "wait for it to come back." Under the rules, clients who "have engaged in securities trading for less than six months, lack the capacity to bear risk, or hold daily average securities assets below 500,000 yuan over the last 20 trading days" may not open credit accounts. The threshold itself says it isn't a tool for ordinary people (China, 2015)
Note
The line "don't buy what you can't understand" has no direct literature behind it — it's consensus, rated C on its own. Investing with consumer loans or cash advanced from a credit card is leverage in disguise; for their rates, see this section's item 7 (don't pay only the credit card minimum). Not investment advice.

Use broad-based index funds instead of actively managed funds for your long-term core holdings (the money you hold and never touch)

Grade BValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The pile of stocks that active funds hold in aggregate is already very close to the whole market. But the extra fees they charge come straight out of your net return. When fund performance is treated as luck and resampled over and over for comparison, very few funds earn enough excess return to cover the fees they charge.

Cost
Nothing. The cost is giving up the possibility of "picking the star fund manager." The hard part: when the index falls, you take the fall too — you can't run away midway.
Benefit
US active equity funds in aggregate hold a portfolio close to the market portfolio: the stocks these funds own together look much like the whole market. But the high cost of active management passes through, undiluted, into investors' lower net returns (what you keep after fees). The study used bootstrap simulation, reshuffling performance randomly over and over to see what pure luck could achieve. It found that few funds generate excess return sufficient to cover costs: the part a fund earns above the market falls short of the fee it charges (US, published 2010). S&P Dow Jones Indices tallies this every year: in 2024, 65% of US actively managed large-cap stock funds underperformed the S&P 500. It has 24 years of statistics, with an average of 64% underperforming each year. Over the 15 years through end-2024, no category saw a majority of active funds beat the index
Note
The controversy: one paper reexamined this conclusion. It argues that the Fama-French style of resampling doesn't resample enough. By its math, even a fund whose excess return is genuinely clear could be judged "indistinguishable from luck." So the conclusion "almost no funds have skill" may be drawn too strongly. China's numbers are less lopsided than America's. S&P Dow Jones, as of June 2025, has A-share large-cap active funds underperforming the S&P China A 300 index by 60.5% over 1 year, 69.6% over 3 years, and 50.8% over 5 years. These statistics only go out to 5 years; longer numbers aren't available. So in China, whether active funds lose to indexes over the long run isn't settled — but the low fees of index funds hold all the same. Not investment advice.
Sources (7 references)

Among similar funds, pick the one with lower fees

Grade CValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Each extra 1 percentage point of annual fees means about 18% less money in hand after 20 years, and about 26% less after 30. Picking the lower-fee fund within the same category is the one thing about this decision you can know in advance.

Cost
Nothing. Before buying, take one extra look at how much the three items "management fee + custody fee + sales service fee" add up to.
Benefit
Fee differences eat into the principal bit by bit through compounding, meaning the little skimmed off each year stacks up year after year. An extra 1 percentage point of annual fee means the terminal value after 20 years is 0.99^20 ≈ 18.2% smaller — terminal value being what's left in the account at that point; after 30 years, about 26% less. China has pushed public fund fee reform since 2023, lowering the fee caps on active equity funds (the kind that mainly buy stocks, with a fund manager picking the stocks). From July 7, 2023, newly registered funds of this type charge management fees of at most 1.2% and custody fees of at most 0.2%. All 136 fund companies also cut these two fees on their older products to that line or below
Note
This calculation is straight from the formula, on the premise that the two funds earn the same before fees. In practice, also count purchase fees, redemption fees, and the sales service fee on Class C shares. Not investment advice.
Sources (3 references)
China Securities Regulatory Commission (2023). Head of the relevant CSRC department answers reporters' questions on public fund fee reform. http://www.csrc.gov.cn/csrc/c100028/c7418692/content.shtml; Xiamen Securities Regulatory Bureau (2024). "Newly registered active equity funds uniformly apply the cap standard of "management fee rate not above 1.2% and custody fee rate not above 0.2%"". http://www.csrc.gov.cn/xiamen/c105636/c7511608/content.shtml; Fama EF, French KR (2010). See item 11. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.2010.01598.x
19

Don't stake your money on one stock, one platform, or one property

Grade BValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

As long as a few assets don't rise and fall perfectly together, spreading the money across them keeps what you earn on average unchanged while the swings of your account get smaller. Conversely, put everything into one stock, one platform, or one property, and when it goes wrong, all of you goes wrong.

Cost
Nothing. The hard part is accepting one thing: you won't happen to stake on the single biggest winner.
Benefit
As long as several assets don't rise and fall in perfect lockstep, spreading money across them leaves expected return (what you earn on average) unchanged while volatility (the account's ups and downs) gets smaller. This is the basic result of portfolio selection proposed by Markowitz in 1952, and it has been used ever since. Conversely, stake everything on one stock or one platform, and its variance is your entire variance: it moves as much as you move. When it goes wrong, there is no hedge, and no other asset to make it up
Note
Rated B because that classic paper is a purely mathematical derivation; it never computed a practical number for "how much less you lose by diversifying." Diversification only makes your account's swings smaller; it does not guarantee you won't lose. Buying broad-based index funds (see this section's item 17) is itself the easiest way to diversify. Not investment advice.
Sources (1 reference)
Markowitz, H. (1952). Portfolio Selection. The Journal of Finance, 7(1), 77–91. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1540-6261.1952.tb01525.x
20

If you pay income tax at 10% or above, open a personal pension account: up to 12,000 yuan a year is deductible pre-tax; paying no income tax or only 3%, it isn't worth opening

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

For every yuan you put in, the tax saved is "your bracket rate minus 3%." Saving the full 12,000 yuan a year: a 10% bracket saves 840 yuan, 20% saves 2,040 yuan, 30% saves 3,240 yuan. For those in only the 3% bracket, the tax saved is paid right back when you withdraw — locked up until retirement for nothing. Those who pay no income tax even pay 3% on withdrawal: a net loss.

Cost
Opening the account costs nothing. The real cost is that the money is locked until retirement and can't be taken out midway.
Benefit
Contributions — up to 12,000 yuan a year — are deducted as truthfully reported from comprehensive income or business income: whatever you put in comes off the income you owe tax on. Investment gains earned inside the account are, for now, not subject to individual income tax. When withdrawn later, they are not merged into comprehensive income but taxed separately at 3%. So what you save is "your marginal rate minus 3%" times the money you actually contribute. The marginal rate is the bracket rate applied to each extra yuan you earn. The math: a 10% marginal rate saves at most 840 yuan a year, 20% saves 2,040 yuan, 30% saves 3,240 yuan. Those who already pay no income tax (annual comprehensive income below the threshold after all deductions) save nothing when contributing, yet pay 3% on withdrawal — a net loss. A marginal rate of only 3% isn't worth it either. Annual comprehensive income after all deductions of no more than 36,000 yuan falls in this bracket. These people save 3% when contributing and pay 3% when withdrawing — an exact wash, with the money locked away until retirement for nothing. Having income tax withheld from your monthly pay doesn't mean you're in the 10% bracket; go by the full-year figure after deductions. The annual contribution allowance accumulates by calendar year and is recalculated the next year; amounts not used up in a year cannot be carried over. The policy has applied nationwide since December 15, 2024 (nationwide)
Note
This account runs "closed": once money goes in, it can't come out. Only four situations allow withdrawal: reaching the age for basic pension, complete loss of working capacity, settling abroad, and other circumstances set by the state. So it isn't an investment product — it's a tax arrangement locked up for many years. The tax saving is taken only once, while the money stays locked until retirement; the farther you are from retirement, the smaller the benefit spread over each year. Back-of-envelope: a 10%-bracket person saves 0.07 yuan per yuan contributed — with 30 years to retirement, that spreads to just over 0.2% a year. A 20%-bracket person saves 0.17 yuan per yuan contributed — with 10 years to retirement, about 1.7% a year. First work out how much tax you pay on each extra yuan, then decide how much to contribute. Don't lock your emergency fund in just to grab the perk (emergency fund: see item 27). The money in the account still has to be invested in products you choose yourself, and it can lose money. The product-picking rules are the same as this section's items 17 and 18 (broad-based index funds; prefer lower fees). The deduction voucher is issued by the personal pension information management service platform. You can choose when to claim the deduction: either when tax is withheld from that year's paycheck, or at the following year's reconciliation (reconciliation: item 2).
Sources (3 references)
Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration (2024). Announcement on Implementing the Individual Income Tax Preferential Policies for Personal Pensions Nationwide (MOF and STA Announcement 2024 No. 21, December 12, 2024). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6992498…; Five departments including the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2022). Implementation Measures for Personal Pension (Articles 7, 8, 9, 12, and 13). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-11/05/content_572…; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (7th amendment, 2018, Table 1 of individual income tax rates). http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2018-09/05/content_2…

Pay per session or in short cycles at the gym, unless you have a stable attendance record of more than a year

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In that three-year US dataset, members on contracts with monthly fees above US$70 averaged just 4.3 visits a month — over US$17 per visit. A 10-visit pass bought per session cost only US$10 a visit. On average these members paid US$600 extra over their membership. Unless you already have more than a year of steady attendance, paying per session or buying short-term is the better deal.

Cost
Paying per session, the per-visit price is somewhat higher than what an annual card works out to. Be honest with yourself about how many times a month you'll actually go.
Benefit
This study looked at 3 years of data on 7,752 members at 3 US health clubs. Members on contracts with monthly fees above US$70 averaged only 4.3 visits a month — over US$17 per visit — while a 10-visit pass cost US$10 a visit. On average these members paid US$600 extra over their membership. Also, the share of monthly-payment members who had not canceled after more than a year was 17% higher than for annual-payment members (US, three-year panel data)
Note
This is one study, with US data. But the underlying principle is universal: people overestimate their future self-control. If you already have a full year of going at least twice a week, the annual card really is cheaper.
Sources (1 reference)
DellaVigna S, Malmendier U (2006). Paying Not to Go to the Gym. American Economic Review 96(3):694-719. https://doi.org/10.1257/aer.96.3.694

Sign a written contract before paying any prepayment; stop paying in when a merchant shows signs of risk, and you have the right to your unspent balance before they abscond

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

A merchant taking your prepayment must sign a written contract with you, spelling out how refunds work. When the merchant's business runs into serious trouble, it should stop taking money; if it plans to close or move, it must tell you in advance. At that point you can demand continued service, or a refund of your unspent balance. Merchants that violate these rules face fines.

Cost
Nothing. The hard part is insisting on a written contract on the spot and not accepting "just top up first, we'll sort it later."
Benefit
The regulation requires merchants taking prepayments to conclude a written contract, and to stipulate the refund method in the contract. A merchant facing major business risk should stop collecting prepayments. A merchant deciding to close or relocate should inform consumers in advance. Consumers have the right to demand continued performance, or a refund of the unspent balance. Violations can bring a fine of 1 to 10 times the illegal gains; where there are no illegal gains, a fine of up to 500,000 yuan
Note
The regulation gives you grounds for a fight after the fact; it can't prevent the loss up front. If a merchant really absconds, the money is mostly already gone. So first top up less, per this section's item "Pay per session or in short cycles at the gym," and use this regulation to defend your rights once something actually happens. Article 27 of the same regulation also requires merchants collecting deposits to agree in advance on the refund method, procedure, and time limit, and forbids imposing unreasonable conditions on refunds.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2024). Implementation Regulations of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Consumer Rights and Interests (State Council Decree No. 778, effective July 1, 2024). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_6940159… Article 22: "A business operator providing goods or services by collecting prepayment shall conclude a written contract with the consumer, stipulating the specific contents of the goods or services, the price or fees, the method of refunding the prepayment, liability for breach, and other matters." "Where the operator fails to provide the goods or services as agreed, it shall perform as agreed or refund the prepayment at the consumer's request." "Where the operator faces major business risk that may affect its normal provision of goods or services as contracted or per trade custom, it shall stop collecting prepayments. Where the operator decides to close down or relocate its premises, it shall inform consumers in advance... The consumer... has the right to demand that the operator continue to perform its obligation to provide the goods or services, or to demand a refund of the unspent prepayment balance." Article 50, penalty provisions

Put a 24-hour cooling-off rule on big non-essential purchases, and make full use of the 7-day no-reason return for online shopping

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

What you save are the things you wouldn't want the very next day. Goods bought online can be returned for any reason within seven days, counting from the day you receive them. A few categories can't be returned: items custom-made to your specifications, fresh and perishable goods, digital products you've already unsealed, and newspapers and periodicals.

Cost
Costs nothing. The thing you want arrives a day later. Return shipping is usually on you. The hard part is holding off on placing the order that day.
Benefit
What you save is the share of impulse purchases you "no longer want the next day." No single percentage can be given for how big that share is. Goods bought online can be returned for any reason within seven days of receipt. Four categories are excluded: custom-made items, fresh and perishable goods, already-unsealed digital products, and newspapers and periodicals (China, in force since 2017)
Note
The "cooling-off period" itself is a rule of thumb with no direct literature support. For purchases the cooling-off period failed to stop, the 7-day no-reason return is still available. Before returning anything, confirm two things: whether the item is on the non-returnable list, and whether the packaging is still intact.
Sources (1 reference)
State Administration for Market Regulation (2020 revision). Interim Measures for the Seven-Day No-Reason Return of Goods Purchased Online (SAMR Order No. 31). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-11/03/content_555…
24

Don't stockpile for 'crossed-out prices' and mega-sales

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

People judge how expensive something is by the first number they see, and any later adjustment falls short. That's why "was 999, now 499" makes you systematically overestimate how cheap it is. And under the rules, the only valid baseline for a discount is the lowest transaction price at that store in the seven days before the promotion. The crossed-out price may never have actually been charged.

Cost
Costs nothing. The trade-off is that you pass up some genuine discounts too. You have to remember the everyday prices of the few things you buy regularly. The hard part is resisting the stockpile on sale day.
Benefit
Human judgment gets anchored on the first number seen, and later adjustments usually fall short. So "was 999, now 499" systematically inflates your estimate of how much you're saving. Regulators require that the baseline for a markdown be the lowest transaction price at the same store within the seven days before the promotion, with the discount size measured against the lowest price the store actually sold at in those seven days. The crossed-out price may never have been charged at all (China, in force since 2020)
Note
The anchoring effect is a laboratory finding; nobody has calculated how much stockpiling actually loses you. Stockpiling also carries costs you'll never book: things expiring, space taken up, and "it's in the house anyway, so I might as well use more." Only stockpile things that meet all three conditions: long shelf life, certain to be used up, and a unit price genuinely lower than before.
Sources (2 references)
Tversky A, Kahneman D (1974). Judgment under Uncertainty: Heuristics and Biases. Science 185(4157):1124-1131. https://doi.org/10.1126/science.185.4157.1124; State Administration for Market Regulation (2020). Interim Provisions on Regulating Promotional Activities (SAMR Order No. 32, Article 21). https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/fgs/art/2023/art…

Prefer pure-protection insurance; treat 'cash returns' and 'dividends' as the non-guaranteed part

Grade CValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The dividend and cash-return portion of your money is not guaranteed by the insurer. The product brochure must state in bold that "future policy dividends are non-guaranteed benefits." The extra premium you pay for a return-of-premium product amounts to handing money to the insurer to hold for you: the return isn't guaranteed, and getting it out isn't easy.

Cost
Pure-protection insurance pays nothing back at maturity, which can feel like "that money was wasted." You have to arrange the saving yourself. The hard part is accepting that this money won't come back.
Benefit
Regulatory rules require that the brochure for a dividend-paying product state in bold: "future policy dividends are non-guaranteed benefits, and their distribution is uncertain." The dividend illustration is the projection table the insurer shows you; its interest-spread cap is 4.5% minus the product's pricing interest rate — the rate locked into the contract. The extra premium paid on return-of-premium and dividend-paying products amounts to savings the insurer holds in trust for you. The return isn't guaranteed, liquidity is poor, and withdrawing isn't easy (China, in force since 2023)
Note
Contested: for people who genuinely cannot save, return-of-premium insurance forces regular payments, and that function has real value. The advice above is for ordinary people who can control themselves. Exactly how much better "buy pure protection and invest the premium difference yourself" beats "buy return-of-premium" depends on the specific product; this section has no systematic data to cite. Not investment advice.
Sources (1 reference)
China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2022). Disclosure Rules for Personal Insurance Products of More Than One Year (CBIRC Regulation [2022] No. 24). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2023-01/04/content_573…

Buy enough third-party liability coverage: compulsory insurance limits are uniform nationwide and low, and anything beyond comes out of your own pocket

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: a lotTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

When you're at fault, compulsory traffic insurance pays at most three items: 180,000 yuan for death and disability, 18,000 yuan for medical expenses, and 2,000 yuan for property damage. The three are tallied separately and can't be shifted between each other. Compensation for injuring someone easily exceeds these limits, and anything beyond comes out of your own household's pocket — so buy enough commercial third-party liability coverage.

Cost
Commercial third-party liability insurance runs a few hundred to a thousand-plus yuan a year. The higher the coverage you buy, the cheaper the premium per yuan of coverage.
Benefit
Compulsory traffic insurance applies uniform liability limits nationwide. The limits are split into four items calculated separately: death and disability, medical expenses, property damage, and the payout when you are not at fault. After the 2020 comprehensive auto insurance reform, the current total liability limit is 200,000 yuan. Within that 200,000 yuan: 180,000 yuan for death and disability, 18,000 yuan for medical expenses, and 2,000 yuan for property damage. When you are not at fault: 18,000 yuan for death and disability, 1,800 yuan for medical expenses, and 100 yuan for property damage. Amounts beyond the limits are borne by the party at fault — whoever hits someone pays out of their own pocket. Without compulsory insurance, your vehicle can be impounded and you face a fine of twice the premium due
Note
The limits are set by the financial regulators and are subject to adjustment. These figures are the current values after the September 2020 comprehensive auto insurance reform; double-check before buying a policy. The key is the structure: compulsory insurance pays item by item, and if one item's limit isn't used up, the remainder can't be moved to cover another. Compensation for injuring someone can far exceed the total, and no insurance covers the excess. This book won't tell you a number for how much third-party liability coverage to buy. But this is one of the few places in the book where "a few hundred yuan more buys off an event that is very unlikely and would crush a family if it actually happened."
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2006, revised 2012). Regulations on Compulsory Traffic Accident Liability Insurance for Motor Vehicles (State Council Decree No. 462, amended by Decree No. 618), Article 23: "Compulsory traffic accident liability insurance for motor vehicles applies uniform liability limits nationwide. The liability limits are divided into the death and disability compensation limit, the medical expenses compensation limit, the property damage compensation limit, and the compensation limit where the insured bears no responsibility in a road traffic accident." "The liability limits are set by the insurance regulator together with the public security, health, and agriculture departments under the State Council." Article 21 covers compensation within the limits; Article 39, on the uninsured: "the motor vehicle is impounded by the traffic management department of the public security organ ... and a fine of twice the premium payable for insurance at the minimum liability limit as prescribed is imposed." http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2131962.htm; China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2020). Guidance on Implementing the Comprehensive Auto Insurance Reform (CBIRC Fa [2020] No. 41, IV(4): "the total liability limit of compulsory insurance is raised from 122,000 yuan to 200,000 yuan, of which the death and disability compensation limit is raised from 110,000 yuan to 180,000 yuan, the medical expenses compensation limit from 10,000 yuan to 18,000 yuan, and the property damage compensation limit remains unchanged at 2,000 yuan"). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5567758.htm (State Council Gazette)

First save an emergency fund of 3 to 6 months of living expenses, kept somewhere you can withdraw any time

Grade CValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Keep 3 to 6 months of living expenses somewhere you can withdraw at any time. Then if you lose your job or fall ill, you won't need to borrow money that costs 18% interest a year, or sell your investments at a loss. Money in the bank is covered by deposit insurance — up to 500,000 yuan per bank.

Cost
Costs nothing. The trade-off is giving up higher returns on this money: it can only sit in a demand deposit, a money market fund, or a withdrawal-any-time deposit. The hard part is leaving it alone while you build it up.
Benefit
With an emergency fund, you won't need to borrow if you lose your job or fall ill, and you won't have to sell investments at a loss. For the annualized rates on consumer loans and credit card minimum payments, see item 7 in this section (don't pay only the credit card minimum). Money in the bank is protected by deposit insurance, which pays out up to 500,000 yuan per bank (China, 2015)
Note
"3 to 6 months" is the common rule of thumb; no official or academic primary source was found for it, hence Grade C. Base the amount on your own monthly fixed expenses, not on your income. Not investment advice.

28

Before prepaying your mortgage, work through the comparison; don't go on gut feeling

Grade CValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Prepaying your mortgage is the equivalent of earning your mortgage rate risk-free. So ask exactly one question: is the stable after-tax return you can reliably earn over the long run higher than your mortgage rate? If yes, don't rush to prepay; if no, or you can't say, prepay. With equal-installment mortgages, interest takes the biggest share in the early years, so the earlier you prepay the more you save. Your bank app's "prepayment calculator" gives you the exact numbers.

Cost
Costs nothing. Half an hour of arithmetic. You have to honestly estimate the stable after-tax return you can actually achieve.
Benefit
Here is the method. Let r be the annual interest rate on your mortgage, as your contract specifies. On August 20, 2026, the 5-year-plus LPR was 3.5%; the rate actually charged is the LPR plus or minus a spread. Now let g be the after-tax annualized return of your best available alternative investment: the average yearly percentage this money could earn somewhere else. The guaranteed return on prepayment is exactly r — every sum you prepay earns r risk-free. If g is consistently above r, the money does better left invested. If g is below r, or simply unknowable, prepaying locks in a risk-free r. With an equal-installment mortgage, most of what you pay in the early years is interest, so the earlier you prepay, the more interest you save. See the numbers directly with your bank app's "prepayment calculator" (China, 2026 rates)
Note
This gives the method, not a verdict. Investment returns that reliably beat the mortgage rate are the exception, not the rule. But whichever side you pick, keep enough emergency cash set aside first. Also check whether your contract has a prepayment-penalty clause. Not investment advice.
Sources (1 reference)
National Interbank Funding Center, authorized by the People's Bank of China (2026). Announcement of the Loan Prime Rate (LPR) for August 20, 2026. https://www.chinamoney.com.cn/chinese/rdgz/20260820/3399885…

When shopping online, rely on platform rules and the law, not on streamers and 'glowing reviews'

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

If a merchant defrauds you, they owe three times what you paid — or 500 yuan if that's less. A platform that knows a seller is infringing and does nothing compensates alongside them. A deposit can be at most 20% of the contract value: break the deal and you lose it; the seller breaks it and owes you double. Fake orders and fake reviews in livestreams carry liability, and big-data price discrimination is explicitly banned.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before ordering, take an extra look at the after-sales terms and deposit rules. After delivery, keep the order records, livestream replay screenshots, and chat logs. The hard part is not getting swept up in the streamer's atmosphere.
Benefit
Where a business commits fraud, compensation is three times the price paid, or 500 yuan if that is less. A platform that knows or should know a seller is infringing and fails to act bears joint liability — you can claim this compensation directly from the platform. Livestream rooms and streamers must not fabricate transactions, follows, views, likes, or similar traffic, nor publish false information; where damage results, they bear civil liability. Organizing fake transactions or fake reviews to burnish someone's publicity draws a fine of up to 1 million yuan; in serious cases 1 to 2 million yuan, plus possible revocation of the business license. A deposit may not exceed 20% of the contract value. If you fail to perform the contract, the deposit is not returned; if the seller fails to perform, they must return it double. Automated decision-making using personal information may not impose unreasonable differential treatment on transaction prices and similar terms — the practice commonly known as big-data price discrimination (nationwide)
Note
"Which platform offers the best value and the least chance of buying shoddy goods" has no official comparison data to cite, so this book gives no platform rankings. All that can be checked are overall spot-check results (see item 32, national spot-check announcements). After the 2025 revision of the Anti-Unfair Competition Law, false advertising moved from old Article 8 to Article 9, and the penalty provisions from Article 20 to Article 25. The new law took effect October 15, 2025 — don't copy the old article numbers when you write up a complaint. In the Shandong case batch, one company organized "brushers" to run 75 fake transactions totaling over 680,000 yuan in principal and was investigated and dealt with; the announcement doesn't give the fine amount. For the 7-day no-reason return, see item 23 in this section (make full use of the 7-day no-reason return for online shopping).

Something bought in a livestream went wrong? First ask the platform for the seller's and promoter's information — it must provide it

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Something bought in a livestream went wrong, and the most common deadlock is that you can't find out whom to sue. At that point you can demand directly that the platform provide the livestream operator's and the promoter's information, plus the related business records. The platform must comply.

Cost
Costs nothing. Just make the request to the platform.
Benefit
When a consumer dispute arises, the operator of the livestream marketing platform must, at the consumer's request, provide the relevant information on the livestream room operator and the livestream promoters, along with the related business activity records. The most common difficulty in pursuing a livestream complaint is not knowing whom to hold to account; once you have this information, you know exactly whom to pursue
Note
Before ordering, screen-record the livestream and the streamer's promises. When something goes wrong, first ask the platform for the seller's and promoter's information, then decide whether to complain or sue. The same regulation also sets three more rules. One: merchants may not expand on their own the list of goods "not covered by the 7-day no-reason return." Two: they may not make "no-reason returns not applicable" the default option. Three: without your confirmation, they may not refuse your return.

Bought unsafe food? Besides the refund you can claim ten times the price; if that added compensation is under 1,000 yuan, it counts as 1,000

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Bought expired or spoiled food? The food itself, the packaging, and the receipt are your evidence — don't throw them out in a hurry. You can claim compensation of ten times the price or three times your loss, and if that's under 1,000 yuan it counts as 1,000. Whether to go after the seller or the manufacturer is your choice, and the one you approach must pay first — no passing you to the other.

Cost
Costs nothing. Keep the food, packaging, and receipt — don't discard or wash anything — and photograph everything on the spot. Start with the merchant or the platform; if that goes nowhere, call 12315. If it truly reaches a lawsuit, that takes months. The hard part is resisting the urge to throw the stuff out first.
Benefit
If you are harmed by food that fails food safety standards, you can claim damages from the seller or from the producer. Whichever party receives your claim operates under first-to-pay responsibility: it must pay first and may not pass the buck — whoever you take your claim to has to pay you first, not push you onto the other party. Beyond damages, you can demand ten times the price or three times your loss as compensation, and "where the added compensation is under 1,000 yuan, it is 1,000 yuan." One exception exists: "except where a defect in the food's label or instructions does not affect food safety and would not mislead consumers." Judicial interpretations add several rules. First, three conditions must all be met: the buyer purchased for personal or household consumption; the food failed food safety standards; and there is no evidence they knew it when buying. Met, the court awards "punitive damages of ten times the price, calculated on the price actually paid." Second, those who bought knowing the food failed standards and then claimed compensation get support from the people's court only "within the range of reasonable living consumption needs"; for repeated purchases and repeated suits, the total across the multiple purchases is assessed within that same range. Third, for several kinds of defects the court does not support punitive damages, provided they do not mislead the consumer about food safety: nonstandard font sizes, and typos, extra or missing characters; nonstandard labeling of net content and specifications; and missing storage-condition labels on foods with no special storage requirements (nationwide)
Note
The order of evidence matters more than the amount. Photograph and video first — packaging, production date, the foreign object, the purchase record — then contact the merchant or platform. Don't throw out or wash anything before you've been in touch. 12315 mediates; it doesn't adjudicate. If the merchant flatly denies everything, a lawsuit is the only road left; for how small-claims procedure works, see section 8, item 22 (scammed in online or secondhand transactions). Also note: whether a foreign object such as a hair or a bug counts as "failing food safety standards" is normally for the market regulator to determine or for expert appraisal to decide — it's not your call. So "find one hair and pocket a guaranteed 1,000 yuan" doesn't hold. Fraud with ordinary goods pays three times the price, or 500 yuan if less — see item 29 in this section (rely on platform rules and the law). Selling food you made yourself has its own rules on which licenses you need, how labels must read, and why you can't claim it cures illness; see section 12, items 8–11 (food licensing, labels, therapeutic-claim red lines, and criminal lines). Conversely, turning claims into a business has clear red lines. One: deliberately staging the appearance of a merchant's illegal production or operation and then extorting compensation through complaints or lawsuits is suspected extortion, and the court must transfer the leads and materials to the police. Two: suing on the staged appearance gets your claim dismissed; where it constitutes false litigation, fines or detention follow according to severity, and the merchant can counterclaim for defamation. This item's beneficiaries are the top tier: yourself and your family.
Sources (2 references)

Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Cases Involving Punitive Damages Disputes over Food and Drugs (Fa Shi [2024] No. 9, Articles 1, 6, 7, 8, 12, 13, 14, 15, and 16, effective August 22, 2024). http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/bf531a70471f10d377788f2… (Supreme People's Court Gazette)

Before buying big-ticket items, check national spot-check announcements, 3C certification, and energy-efficiency labels

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In 2024, national spot checks covered 25,250 batches of products, and 14.3% failed. E-commerce did worse: 7,297 batches checked, 23.5% failed; physical stores were at 15.1%. Before buying a big-ticket item, spend a few minutes checking the spot-check announcements and verifying that the 3C certificate is genuine. Products that should carry an energy-efficiency label must not lack one.

Cost
Costs nothing. A few minutes on the SAMR and CNCA official websites.
Benefit
In 2024, national supervision spot checks covered 25,250 batches of products, with a failure rate of 14.3%. Of these, 7,297 batches came from e-commerce channels, with a failure rate of 23.5%, up 1.8 percentage points from the year before. Physical stores: 8,055 batches, a failure rate of 15.1%. Certificates of compulsory product certification (3C) can be checked for authenticity under the "Certification Results" section of the CNCA website. Energy-efficiency labels are mandatorily managed by product catalog; the label must carry the energy-efficiency grade, the efficiency indicators, and the energy-efficiency information code. Forging or misusing energy-efficiency labels, or failing to display one where required, is penalized under the Energy Conservation Law (nationwide)
Note
A spot check is the regulator picking part of the goods to test; the result is not the whole market's pass rate and can't be used to rank platforms. There is no research on "how much less shoddy goods you buy by checking," hence Grade B. The CNCA's query platform cx.cnca.cn would not open when this section was fact-checked; treat the cnca.gov.cn homepage as the entry point. Spot-check announcement figures update yearly — check the latest release when you use them.

Count beads, jade, luxury watches, and designer toys as money spent, not money saved

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

These prices already carry a consumption tax inside: watches at 10,000 yuan or more each are 20%; gold, silver, and platinum jewelry and diamonds 5%; other jewelry and jade 10% — VAT is separate. That tax doesn't come back when you resell. If you truly love it, buy it as consumption, not as investing.

Cost
Costs nothing. Just don't count "it will appreciate later" among your reasons for buying it. The hard part is resisting a bigger budget in the name of "value preservation."
Benefit
Start with the buying side. The Consumption Tax Taxable Items and Rates Table sets these rates: "high-end watches" 20%; within "precious jewelry and jewelry jade," gold and silver jewelry, platinum jewelry, and diamonds and diamond items 5%; other precious jewelry and jewelry jade 10%. "High-end watches" means "all watches with a sales price (VAT excluded) of 10,000 yuan or more per piece." Now the cashing-out side, under the Administrative Measures for Pawnbroking. Article 36: a pawn term may not exceed 6 months. Article 37 covers the pawn-loan interest rate — the interest on the money the pawnshop lends you — converted from the People's Bank of China's published 6-month statutory loan rate over the pawn term. Interest may not be deducted in advance from the money handed to you. Article 38: for pawn loans secured by movable property (watches, jade and the like), the monthly comprehensive fee rate may not exceed 42‰ of the loan — a monthly comprehensive fee of no more than 4.2% of the amount borrowed; real estate mortgages are 27‰ and property-rights pledges 24‰. Article 40: if within 5 days after the term expires you neither redeem nor renew, it becomes a dead pawn, and the item will no longer wait for you. Article 43: dead-pawned items appraised at 30,000 yuan or more may be consigned to auction. Auction proceeds first cover auction costs and the pawn loan's principal and interest; the remainder is returned to the pawnor, and any shortfall can still be recovered from the pawnor (nationwide)
Note
Pawning means doing the math: the monthly comprehensive fee cap is 42‰ of the amount borrowed — roughly half the loan over a year — and interest on the loan comes on top. That "half a year" figure is a rough estimate from multiplying the monthly rate by 12, good for a sense of scale, not a precise annual rate. The tax rates and fee rates are written numbers. But whether such items appreciate over the long run has no citable official statistics; this book makes no forecasts and comments on no categories. What it wants to block is only the investment rationale bolted onto consumption: buying because you like it and enjoy wearing it is fine; padding the budget because it "holds its value" or "will sell for more later" is where money is lost. Gold splits in two as well: investment bullion traded by gram weight and jewelry sold by the piece are not the same thing. Jewelry prices include design and workmanship fees, which buybacks usually don't credit. Listed prices on secondhand platforms aren't transaction prices — don't read them as the market rate.

Notice on Adjusting and Improving Consumption Tax Policies (Cai Shui [2006] No. 33). http://www.mof.gov.cn/zhengwuxinxi/zhengcefabu/2006zcfb/200…; Ministry of Commerce and Ministry of Public Security (2005). Administrative Measures for Pawnbroking (Order No. 8 of 2005, Articles 36, 37, 38, 40, and 43). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2005/content_93074.htm

For jewelry and jade, accept only test reports bearing the CMA mark, and verify the lab on the issuing authority's website

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Certificates can be faked, so what you check is the lab that issued the certificate. A testing lab must be accredited to issue reports externally, and the report must bear the CMA mark. The accrediting authority publishes the list of accredited institutions on its website, so you can check for yourself whether the lab is on it. Among the cases officially investigated, some "national inspection certificates" accompanying the goods were made by contacts the sellers arranged themselves.

Cost
Costs nothing. One check of the certifying lab's credentials before you order — a few minutes is enough.
Benefit
First the rules, under the Administrative Measures for Qualification Accreditation of Inspection and Testing Institutions. Article 2: qualification accreditation is the evaluation and licensing of inspection and testing institutions that "issue probative data and results to society" — first the institution is reviewed, then granted the qualification to issue certificates. Article 15: the qualification accreditation mark consists of the CMA emblem and the qualification accreditation certificate number. Article 21: an institution issuing probative data or results externally must mark the accreditation mark on the test report. Article 22: the accreditation authority must publish on its official website the information of accredited institutions, noting certificate status. Article 34: issuing probative data or results externally without lawful accreditation draws a 30,000 yuan fine. Article 37: forging, altering, or misusing an accreditation certificate or mark draws a fine of up to 30,000 yuan. Now the official cases, from the SAMR's June 4, 2026 release of typical "counterfeit-clearing" cases in traditional craft markets. One: a livestream room in Donghai, Jiangsu, claimed what it sold was "natural, non-acid-washed, untreated, Burmese Grade A" and flashed a "national inspection certificate." Testing showed quartzite jade (dyed), jadeite (treated), glass, and plastic. The certificate had been produced by contacts the party arranged itself. Two: another case in the same county seized 469 items of suspected counterfeit "natural crystal" products; 210 tested as natural crystal and 259 as synthetic crystal. Three: a shop in Zhenping, Henan, made an unauthorized display board for its livestream, reading "GIA CMA Zhongyu Jewelry and Jade Appraisal Center — Certified Partner," and bought 181 "National Gems & Jewelry Testing Center" conformity labels online, sold bundled with bracelets (nationwide)
Note
Names of jewelry and jade follow a national standard. Test conclusions come written in the bracketed form "quartzite jade (dyed)" or "jadeite (treated)" — the words inside the brackets are where the price gap lives. "Grade A," "old pit," and "untreated" are seller patter, not appraisal conclusions; the dyed-quartzite livestream above used exactly that script. The same case batch had more tricks: staged mine sites with actors playing "miners" on camera, hired shills warming up the livestream chat, and scripts about "needing money urgently" or "a seriously ill relative." Others claimed products could "prevent and treat rheumatism, boost immunity, improve sleep quality, and unblock blood vessels" — handled as false advertising. For the general check on big-ticket items, see item 32 in this section (check spot-check announcements and 3C certification). For whom to turn to when a livestream goes wrong, see items 29 and 30 (rely on platform rules and the law; ask the platform for the information).
