Don't believe 'willpower is like a muscle that runs out with use'

Grade AValue: HighBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The popular story: do one self-control-taxing task and you'll slip more easily afterward, so ration your willpower. 23 labs re-ran the experiment on 2,141 people with the same protocol, and the effect was nearly zero. Stop explaining yourself with "my willpower ran out today," and don't pay for courses that promise to build your stock of it.

Cost
Costs nothing. What changes is one story you tell yourself.
Benefit
A multi-lab preregistered replication — 23 labs, 2,141 participants in total — re-ran the sequential-task paradigm under the standardized protocol of Sripada et al.: first a task that drains self-control, then a second task that needs it. The pooled result showed the ego-depletion effect to be tiny, with the 95% credible interval containing 0 (d = 0.04, 95% CI −0.07 to 0.15). On that basis the authors discussed whether the model of "self-control as a limited resource" still stands. A second replication, also preregistered in advance — 36 labs, 3,531 people — found an effect size of d = 0.06, likewise too small to count.
Note
What's being rejected is the model of "self-control as a resource that gets used up," not "people get tired." Too little sleep and long stretches of work lower performance — a different matter, handled by the sleep and working-hours items in Section 3. What randomized trials do support is changing the environment and changing the wording: Section 4, item 10 (move what you don't want to touch farther away) and Section 4, item 1 (write it as "at what time, in what place, when X happens, do Y"). Fixing what you wear and eat is still worth doing, because it costs almost nothing. What it saves is the minutes and the rounds of dithering, not willpower — don't expect it to make your afternoon judgment better. Other items in this section count money; this one counts time and energy, and the two aren't converted.
Sources (2 references)
Hagger MS, Chatzisarantis NLD, Alberts H, et al. (2016). A Multilab Preregistered Replication of the Ego-Depletion Effect. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 11(4), 546–573. https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691616652873; Vohs et al. (2021). A Multisite Preregistered Paradigmatic Test of the Ego-Depletion Effect. Psychological Science. https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797621989733
26

Don't count on breakfast or 16:8 intermittent fasting to control your weight; pick a meal window you can keep up long-term

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

The popular claim: skipping breakfast makes you gorge at lunch and dinner, so the day's total ends up higher. Trials say otherwise: breakfast-skippers ate over 200 kcal less per day and weighed slightly less. Compared with simply eating less, 16:8 showed no weight difference over a year. Long-term breakfast-skippers do have about 17% more cardiovascular disease, while total mortality shows no difference.

Cost
Costs nothing. What it saves is the mental energy spent wrestling with meal times every day.
Benefit
First, the claim that "skipping breakfast makes you eat more later." One meta-analysis pooled 13 randomized trials. People assigned to eat breakfast took in 259.79 kcal more per day than the breakfast-skippers (95% CI 78.87–440.71, the uncertainty range), and weighed 0.44 kg more (0.07–0.82). The skippers did not make it up at lunch and dinner. These trials were all short: 7 weeks on average where weight was measured, 2 weeks where intake was. Now to 16:8-style eating only within fixed hours. One trial gave 116 overweight adults 12 weeks: the group eating only from noon to 8 p.m. and the group eating three regular meals a day differed by −0.26 kg (−1.30 to 0.78), not significant. Another, run in Guangzhou, enrolled 139 patients with obesity and followed them for 12 months. Time-restricted eating plus calorie control beat calorie control alone by 1.8 kg (−4.0 to 0.4), also not significant. Finally, is long-term breakfast skipping harmful? Across a pooled 2.38 million people, breakfast-skippers had about 17% higher cardiovascular disease risk (OR 1.17, 1.09–1.26) and about 49% higher cardiovascular death (OR 1.49, 1.20–1.84). But these are record-only studies without randomized groups. In the original study with 17 to 23 years of follow-up, the all-cause mortality hazard ratio was 1.19 with an uncertainty range of 0.99 to 1.42 — crossing 1, so no difference can be claimed.
Note
Controversy. The 17% cardiovascular figure comes from record-only studies without randomized groups. Breakfast-skippers are already more likely to smoke, drink, sit all day, and earn less, and those factors can't be fully adjusted away — so how much of that 17% is the breakfast itself can't be pinned down. The all-cause mortality figure crossed 1 to begin with. 16:8 has its own controversy: pooling 30 trials and 1,341 people, with both groups eating the same amount, the time-restricted group lost an extra 1.46 kg (−2.65 to −0.26), at the cost of 0.41 kg of lean mass. But most of those trials were short; the longest and strictest, a twelve-month trial, found no difference. Long fasting windows also touch the gallbladder. In a cross-sectional survey of 6,547 people, each hour later in the day for the first meal came with about 5% more detected gallstones (OR 1.05, 1.02–1.08); those whose first meal came between 9 a.m. and 2 p.m. had about 49% more than earlier eaters (OR 1.49, 1.24–1.77). The mechanism: the longer bile sits in the gallbladder, the more readily stones precipitate out. But this is a same-time-point survey, so it may also be that a gallbladder problem came first and the eating habits changed after. The Kailuan cohort in China followed 5.6 years with 369 gastrointestinal cancers: breakfast-skippers had 2.32 times the colorectal cancer risk (1.34–4.01) and 5.43 times the gallbladder and extrahepatic bile duct cancer risk (1.34–21.93). That second number's uncertainty range runs all the way to 21.93, meaning too few events — treat it as a lead only. Put together: for weight control, meal timing matters very little — don't spend energy on it. As for whether skipping breakfast entirely long-term is good for you, all the existing evidence is associations that can't prove causation, but the direction consistently leans unfavorable; the safe play is to eat normally — just don't expect breakfast to help you lose weight. The main causes of gastritis and stomach ulcers aren't empty stomachs but H. pylori and long-term painkillers; test as in Section 1, item 23 (test for H. pylori and eradicate it if positive). What to do about gallstones found on a checkup that have never hurt: item 20 in this section (don't remove the gallbladder preventively for stones found on a checkup that have never hurt). For weight control, what actually has evidence is what you eat and how much: Section 2, item 27 (eat 5 servings of fruits and vegetables a day), Section 2, item 28 (cut back on ultra-processed food), and Section 2, item 32 (keep BMI at 20–25). Not applicable to people with diabetes, people on glucose-lowering drugs, or pregnant women — a missed meal can mean low blood sugar; follow medical advice. Extreme fasting and vomiting are a different matter: Section 28, item 1 (don't control weight with extreme dieting, fasting, or vomiting).

Don't believe 'masturbation ruins your health' or 'you must abstain to get better'; what matters is whether it costs you sleep, work, or relationships

Grade BValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

No study shows masturbation damages health. A large US study instead found that men who ejaculated more often had about 20% less prostate cancer. A UK study found higher risk among those frequent in their twenties and thirties — so neither side can be booked as a form of exercise. Many people who feel "addicted to porn" are mostly colliding with their own morals.

Cost
Costs nothing. It saves the money spent on "kidney-tonifying" folk remedies and abstinence courses, plus the anxiety of long-term self-blame.
Benefit
First the body. A US study followed 31,925 men through 2010. Each reported how many times a month he ejaculated, and was grouped by count. Compared with men at 4 to 7 a month, those at 21 or more had prostate cancer HR 0.81 (95% CI 0.72–0.92, about 19% lower) — computed from frequency at ages 20 to 29. Using frequency at ages 40 to 49: HR 0.78 (0.69–0.89, about 22% lower). Most of what dropped was low-grade prostate cancer. The counterpoint is a UK case-control study comparing 431 patients diagnosed before 60 with 409 controls. Those frequent in their twenties and thirties had higher risk; those frequent in their fifties had lower risk. Now pornography. One systematic review with meta-analysis concludes that many people who feel "addicted" are mostly experiencing behavior clashing with the morals they believe in, not simply watching too much (US / UK).
Note
Controversy. Both prostate cancer studies are record-only, without randomized groups, and the frequency is the person's own recollection — so the conclusion reaches only "no evidence of harm seen," and can't be flipped into advice to do more. The UK study's authors themselves note that the fifties dip may be illness cutting the frequency. The pornography paper's abstract gives no effect size, so only the direction is stated here. Benefit is rated small because what drops is mainly low-grade prostate cancer, not death. The real signals for a psychiatric or psychological consult: losing sleep over this, missing work, hurting the relationship with your partner, and wanting to stop but being unable to. On late nights: Section 3, item 9 (don't lose sleep over games, short videos, or porn). Worried that porn has caused erection problems: get checked first per Section 1, item 28 (erection problems — check cardiovascular health first). The legal consequences of posting to group chats or selling files: Section 9, item 4 (porn videos — keep them to yourself). The beneficiary is you yourself.

Don't pay for 'sexual orientation correction' or 'gay conversion therapy,' and don't send family members to one

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

After reviewing the research, an American Psychological Association task force concluded that this kind of conversion doesn't change sexual orientation and can harm people. In a US survey, those who had been through conversion were nearly 90% more likely to have had suicidal thoughts. In China, a psychiatric hospital forcibly admitted a man under the label of "sexual preference disorder"; the court found a rights violation and awarded 5,000 yuan.

Cost
Costs nothing. It saves the fees of conversion institutions, psychology clinics, and "de-gay" programs. What's hard is when family members insist on sending someone.
Benefit
The American Psychological Association's 2009 task force report found that efforts to change sexual orientation "are not likely to be successful and involve some risk of harm." For putting minors into coercive or residential conversion programs, the report advised that neither parents nor children should consider it. A nationally representative US survey interviewed 1,518 sexual-minority adults; about 7% had undergone conversion, four in five of them at the hands of religious practitioners. After adjusting for age, adverse childhood experiences, and other factors, those who had been through conversion had lifetime suicidal ideation OR 1.92 (95% CI 1.01–3.64, about 90% higher). Planning suicide OR 1.75 (1.01–3.06). Suicide attempts with no injury or minor injury OR 1.88 (1.01–3.50). Another study interviewed 245 young people aged 21 to 25. Among those never subjected to conversion in adolescence, 22.0% had attempted suicide. Where the parents themselves tried to change their child's orientation: 48.1%. Where the parents also sent the child to therapists or religious figures: 62.8%. The WHO's disease classification ICD-10 states: "sexual orientation by itself is not regarded as a disorder." In 2017 the Yicheng District court in Zhumadian, Henan, heard a case: a psychiatric hospital had forcibly admitted a man under "sexual preference disorder." The court held that he "had a mild condition, with no suicide attempts, harm to others, or property destruction, and did not meet the conditions for compulsory treatment." The court ordered the hospital to apologize publicly and pay 5,000 yuan in emotional-distress compensation (US / China).
Note
Controversy. Sullins 2022 re-analyzed the same data, excluding suicidal thoughts that existed before the conversion. On that reckoning, conversion and suicidal ideation were no longer positively associated (OR 0.44, 0.20–0.94). Sullins's institution takes a stance against homosexuality, and the original authors wrote a response. So how large the harm is remains disputed, but for "it can't change orientation" no counter-evidence has appeared. Grade B because the harm figures all come from surveys relying on later recollection. Legally, hospital treatment runs on the principle of voluntariness; compulsory admission requires a severe mental disorder plus a danger of harming oneself or others. Psychological counseling personnel are not allowed to perform psychotherapy. Deliberately sending someone who does not have a mental disorder into hospital for treatment carries liability for compensation. In 2014, a man was hypnotized and given electric shocks to "treat" his homosexuality at the Chongqing Xinyu Piaoxiang psychological counseling center, and later sued. The Beijing Haidian District court ordered the center to apologize publicly and compensate his financial losses. Reports say the ruling stated that homosexuality is not a mental illness, and that the center's promise to cure it was false advertising. Only The Paper's reporting survives this case; the full judgment couldn't be found on the court's website. If this has caused you lasting distress, you can go to a psychiatry or clinical psychology department — the goal is relieving the distress. How a family should respond when a child comes out: Section 30, item 15 (your child says they like the same sex). The beneficiaries are you yourself and your family.

Don't expect 'proper lifting posture' classes to prevent back pain; what you cut is how much and how often you lift — and exercise more day to day

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Workers trained in lifting posture didn't have less back pain afterward than the untrained. Nor did people who bent their backs more while lifting show more back pain. What tracks with back pain is lifting heavy and lifting often: each extra 10 kg per lift or 10 more lifts a day raises risk by about 10%. People who exercise regularly have 30–45% fewer back-pain flare-ups.

Cost
Costs nothing. No more agonizing over whether your back stayed straight while lifting, and no money for back-safety courses or back belts. What to do instead is two things. Split heavy loads, use a cart, or find someone to help — that costs only a few extra minutes. Set aside time to exercise a few times a week — that needs long-term commitment.
Benefit
First, training. Cochrane's 2011 systematic review pooled 9 randomized trials with 20,101 workers in total. Across 7 trials and 19,317 people, those trained in manual handling reported later back pain about the same as those given nothing (OR 1.17, 95% CI 0.68–2.02 — the uncertainty range crosses 1). Compared with people who only watched a video: RR 0.93 (0.69–1.25), also about the same. The evidence quality was moderate. The authors' conclusion: manual handling advice and training, whether or not assistive devices are provided, does not prevent back pain or the disability it causes. Next, bending. A 2020 systematic review pooled the studies of how much the back bends during lifting; evidence quality low. In the single follow-up study, the maximum lumbar flexion angle differed by only 1.5 degrees (−0.7 to 3.7) between people who later had back pain and those who didn't — not significant. In 9 of 11 studies, no difference appeared between the groups. Another 7 studies, using a different way of measuring, found people with back pain actually bent 6.0 degrees less (−11.2 to −0.9). The authors' conclusion: there is no evidence that bending more invites back pain. Finally, what to do. One meta-analysis pooled 8 follow-up studies: each 10 kg heavier per lift, back pain risk OR 1.11 (1.05–1.18, about 11% higher). Each 10 more lifts a day, OR 1.09 (1.03–1.15, about 9% higher). Another pooled 21 randomized trials and 30,850 people. Exercise plus education brought flare-up risk down to RR 0.55 (0.41–0.74, about 45% lower), evidence quality moderate. Exercise alone RR 0.65 (0.50–0.86, about 35% lower), evidence quality low to very low. Education alone RR 1.03 (0.83–1.27) and back belts RR 1.01 (0.71–1.44) showed no effect. The UK Health and Safety Executive's (HSE) official guidance also states: training alone cannot assure safe handling, and good handling technique does not replace assistive devices or improved tasks and loads.
Note
Controversy. On lifting heavy and lifting often, the evidence splits. A 2010 systematic review found 9 high-quality studies, 4 showing an association and 5 not. Its authors judged that occupational lifting is unlikely to cause back pain on its own. So "lift less heavy" has only associative evidence and cannot prove causation. The bending review's studies are low quality, most comparing two groups at a single moment. The training review's uncertainty range is wide, and it also notes that no randomized trial has tested whether training can treat existing back pain. HSE still teaches a technique: keep the load close to the trunk, feet planted, don't twist, don't yank. Start the lift with back, hips, and knees all slightly bent — better than bending fully or squatting fully. Following it does no harm; just don't expect it alone to prevent back pain. Benefit is rated medium: the reductions from exercise would qualify as large, but the evidence for exercise alone is low quality, exercise plus education showed no reduction in sick leave, and back pain isn't fatal. How to exercise: Section 2, item 16 (do 30–60 minutes of strength training a week) and Section 2, item 11 (walk 7,000–8,000 steps a day). The beneficiary is you yourself.

7. How to live when you have no money

22 items

This section is about money and safety nets. How much you can claim, how much you can be excused from paying, what services you can get, and what conditions you must meet — it's all written here, not converted into lifespan. Policies change every year and differ from place to place, so go by the amounts and thresholds your locality publishes for the current year. The entries are ordered: those that cost nothing, involve little paperwork, and work fast come first. Those that require building up long-term eligibility, or vary widely across localities, come later. Those based only on experience, with no official documents, come last. The entries in this section are grouped by topic below, with entry numbers in parentheses. Lost your job: apply online for unemployment insurance benefits (entry 1), certification as a person with employment difficulties (entry 12), claim vocational-training subsidies (entry 13). Owed wages: complain to labor inspection first (entry 2), apply for legal aid (entry 3), work out who employed you first (entry 22). Emergency backstops: go to a relief station (entry 4), apply for temporary assistance (entry 6), apply for the subsistence allowance (entry 7), the two disability subsidies (entry 8), replace a lost ID card immediately (entry 11), nowhere at all to sleep (entry 21). Medical and social insurance: don't let resident medical insurance lapse (entry 9), for serious illness use medical insurance and medical assistance first (entry 10), don't panic over gaps in social insurance (entry 18), add a medical or critical-illness policy (entry 20). Finding work and starting over: public employment services and gig markets (entry 5), job hunt with a system (entry 14), no deposits and no documents as collateral (entry 15), prison and bankruptcy still leave a way back (entry 19). Housing and food: get on the public rental housing list (entry 16), squeeze housing and food to the minimum (entry 17).

1

If you lose your job, first apply online for unemployment insurance benefits

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

If your employer and you have paid in for at least 1 year, and you didn't quit voluntarily, you can claim money once you complete unemployment registration. Paid in 1 to under 5 years: up to 12 months. 5 to under 10 years: up to 18 months. Over 10 years: up to 24 months. While the money comes in, the unemployment insurance fund pays your employee medical insurance for you.

Cost
It costs nothing. You can submit the application from your phone through any of three channels: the "Palm 12333" app, the electronic social security card mini-program inside WeChat or Alipay, or the National Social Insurance Public Service Platform. All you need on hand is a social security card or ID card; in most areas you don't have to show up in person. The prerequisite is completing unemployment registration first.
Benefit
Three conditions must be met at once. First, unemployment insurance has been paid, by your employer and you together, for at least 1 year cumulatively. Second, you didn't resign of your own initiative (the law calls this "interruption of employment not due to the person's own will"). Third, you have completed unemployment registration and are willing to work. How long you can claim depends on contribution years. At least 1 but under 5 years: up to 12 months. At least 5 but under 10 years: up to 18 months. Over 10 years: up to 24 months. The monthly amount is set by each provincial government and differs from province to province. It is below the local minimum wage and above the urban subsistence allowance. The national goal is to raise it gradually to 90% of the minimum wage. While you receive unemployment benefits, you remain enrolled in employee basic medical insurance and keep its benefits. The basic medical insurance premium due comes out of the unemployment insurance fund; you pay nothing personally (nationwide; regulation in force since 1999)
Note
If you quit voluntarily, it doesn't count as "not of your own will," and you can't claim. So when you leave a job, don't sign a "resignation for personal reasons" — see section 19, entry 7. Benefits are counted from the day you complete unemployment registration; register a month late and you lose a month's money. Registering is the first thing to do after walking out. Registration requires a separation certificate issued by your employer — see section 19, entry 17 (separation certificate). For whether to honor a non-compete agreement and what to do when the company pays no compensation, see section 11, entry 12 (signed a non-compete). While you claim, the unemployment insurance fund pays your employee medical insurance. Provincial amounts differ a lot; go by what is published where you are insured. The "90% of minimum wage" figure comes from the 2017 guiding opinions of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Ministry of Finance (MOHRSS Fa [2017] No. 71), whose exact words are "gradually raise the unemployment insurance benefit standard to 90% of the minimum wage." That is a goal, not a rate paid today. The original page on the MOHRSS website wouldn't open on this machine; the quote was checked against the citation in a Liaoning provincial department document.
Sources (5 references)

2

Owed wages? Complain to labor inspection first, then apply for labor arbitration; both routes are free, and most cases conclude within months

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Both routes are free. First call 12333 or file a complaint with labor inspection at the human resources and social security bureau. Once the case is accepted, the investigation must finish within 60 working days, and the company can be ordered to pay within a set deadline; if it misses the deadline, it owes 50% to 100% extra in damages. If that fails, apply for labor arbitration, which must conclude within 45 days. But "concluded" doesn't mean "paid": if the company has no assets or the boss has vanished, you can win and still get nothing.

Cost
It costs nothing — neither the complaint nor arbitration charges a fee. Gather your labor contract, payslips, attendance records, transfer records, and chat logs, and make 1 to 3 trips to the HR and social security bureau or the arbitration commission. There is a 1-year time limit for applying for arbitration (the law calls it the arbitration limitation period). If you still work at the unit and wages are in arrears, the 1-year limit doesn't apply. If you have already left, you must file within 1 year of your departure date. The hard part is the repeated trips and hunting down documents one by one; it's easy to lose heart along the way.
Benefit
Step one is the complaint. Dial 12333, or go to the labor inspection office of your local HR and social security bureau. The law requires the investigation to finish within 60 working days of case acceptance, extendable by 30 more working days for complex cases. If the arrears are verified, the company can be ordered to pay within a deadline. If it still hasn't paid when the deadline passes, it must pay an additional sum of 50% to 100% of the amount due. In 2024, inspection agencies nationwide investigated 137,000 cases and recovered 8.65 billion yuan in wages for 654,000 people. If you hold an IOU or a wage sheet and the facts of the arrears are clear, you can also apply directly to a primary court for a payment order — a court command to the company to pay, issued within 15 days of acceptance. Step two is arbitration. The law requires conclusion within 45 days of acceptance, extendable by 15 days. Wage claimants can apply for advance enforcement: part of the award is executed before the whole case is finished. If the amount owed is no more than 12 times the local monthly minimum wage, the award is final: once arbitration rules, the matter is settled and the company cannot sue. In 2024, 4.257 million cases were handled nationwide, 4.156 million concluded, with 93.47 billion yuan in concluded amounts. The mediation success rate was 79.6%, the arbitration conclusion rate 98.2%, and the arbitration finality rate 73.7%. When people say this can drag on "six months to a year," they mean the cases that go on to court after arbitration: 6 months at first instance (3 months under the simplified procedure), plus 3 months at second instance. In 2024, courts concluded 88,000 labor-remuneration claim cases and recovered 28.54 billion yuan; 998 people were sentenced for the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration (nationwide)
Note
The complaint and arbitration do work, but keep "concluded" and "paid" apart. The 98.2% conclusion rate only means the procedure ran its course. If the company has no assets or the boss has fled, you win and still get nothing. The Supreme People's Court publishes only the total sum actually enforced (2.3 trillion yuan in 2024) and a statement that the "completed-enforcement rate remains high"; there is no official figure for how much of the wage-arrears money actually reaches the claimants. The term "arbitration finality rate" is not defined in the communiqué; this entry reads it as "no further trip to court after the award." Once arrears reach certain amounts, criminal filing becomes possible. One scenario: one person owed for more than 3 months, in the amount of 5,000 to 20,000 yuan or more. Another: 10 or more people owed, totaling 30,000 to 100,000 yuan or more. In either case, if the employer still doesn't pay after being ordered to, the case qualifies for filing. Each provincial high court and provincial procuratorate sets and publishes its own exact figures within these ranges; check your province's numbers before complaining and raise them in person when you file. Migrant workers on construction sites are separately covered by dedicated wage accounts and the rule that the general contractor clears wages first; going after the general contractor works better than going after the labor gang boss. Both routes presuppose an employing unit. Unlicensed workshops and shops still count — you can complain and arbitrate. Private work for a household or individual, such as being a nanny, is not an employment relationship; go to court — see entry 22 (work out who employed you first). Migrant workers applying for legal aid over wage claims are not means-tested. The texts of the Labor Contract Law and the Civil Procedure Law are quoted from reposting pages of the State Taxation Administration and the Guizhou Provincial Market Regulation Bureau (both gov.cn), because the NPC website pages wouldn't open. Fetching Criminal Law Amendment VIII from the NPC website failed, so it was opened and checked with curl

3

Can't afford a lawsuit? Apply for legal aid: wage claims, alimony, and work-injury cases are already within its scope

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Claiming unpaid wages, alimony, social insurance or subsistence-allowance benefits, or losses suffered while acting heroically — all of these can get free legal aid. Call 12348, or go to your local legal aid center. You no longer need to go back to your place of origin for a proof of financial hardship; stating your situation truthfully yourself is enough. Defendants facing a possible death sentence, and defendants who are blind, deaf, mute, or minors, are assigned a lawyer in every case.

Cost
It costs nothing. Legal aid never charges the person receiving it a cent.
Benefit
The State Council's regulation spells out the six categories of civil matters legal aid covers. Its exact words: "those who lawfully request state compensation; those who request social insurance benefits or minimum-living-guarantee benefits; those who request the issuance of survivors' pensions or relief payments; those who request payment of alimony, child support, or maintenance; those who request payment of labor remuneration; and those who assert civil rights and interests arising from acts of heroism." In plain terms: state compensation, social insurance or subsistence-allowance benefits, survivors' pensions and relief payments, alimony and child support, unpaid wages, and losses from acts of heroism. On the criminal side, defendants facing a possible death sentence, and defendants who are blind, deaf, mute, or minors, are assigned a lawyer regardless of financial status
Note
The Legal Aid Law took effect on January 1, 2022, with one change. Previously you had to "submit a proof of financial hardship." Now you only need to truthfully state your own financial situation; no more going back to your place of origin for paperwork. Entry points are local legal aid centers and public legal service centers, or call 12348
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2003). Legal Aid Regulations (State Council Decree No. 385, Articles 10, 11, and 12). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_694...; Official of the Ministry of Justice (2021). Press questions and answers on implementing the Legal Aid Law. http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2021-12/29/content_5665114.htm
4

Out of options? Go to a relief station: food, shelter, and a homebound ticket are provided

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Relief stations provide food and lodging, send you to a hospital if you fall ill, and help you contact your family. If you can't afford a ticket home, they give you one. Stays generally don't exceed 10 days. You come and leave voluntarily — this is not detention, and no cash is handed out. Tickets are issued to your registered residence or habitual residence, so decide where you're headed before you go.

Cost
It costs nothing. Go to your local relief and custody station and ask for help yourself, or tell a police officer or the civil affairs department and have them take you. On entering, you must truthfully register your name and belongings. The hard part is telling someone you have no money and nowhere to go.
Benefit
Relief stations provide food and lodging that meet hygiene standards. Those who fall suddenly ill in the station are sent to a hospital for treatment. They also help you contact relatives and your employer. Those who can't afford a ticket back to their registered residence or habitual residence are issued travel (boat) vouchers — that is, bus, train, or boat tickets. Registered residence means your hometown; habitual residence is where you actually live now. Assistance generally lasts no more than 10 days; it can be extended for those waiting for family to collect them, waiting for treatment, or waiting for placement. When police and other administrative personnel on duty encounter vagrants and beggars, they must tell them they can seek help. People with disabilities, minors, the elderly, and those with limited mobility are to be guided and escorted there (nationwide, since 2003)
Note
Seeking help and leaving the station are both voluntary; this is not detention. What's given is basic food and lodging, not cash. Travel vouchers are issued to your registered residence or habitual residence, so decide where you're headed before asking for help.
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2003). Measures for the Administration of Assistance to Vagrants and Beggars without Means of Support in Cities (State Council Decree No. 381, Articles 5, 6, and 7). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2003/content_62246.htm; Ministry of Civil Affairs (2003). Implementation Rules for the Measures for the Administration of Assistance to Vagrants and Beggars without Means of Support in Cities (Ministry of Civil Affairs Decree No. 24, Articles 11 and 12). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2003/content_62510.htm

For finding work, use the free public employment services and gig markets first; don't use paid agencies

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Public institutions like employment service centers and human resources markets don't charge anything for job referrals, career guidance, policy advice, or employment and unemployment registration. The law expressly forbids them from making money off these services. Registering and posting information at gig markets is free too. Take care of your unemployment registration while you're at it — you'll need it for unemployment benefits and for certification as a person with employment difficulties.

Cost
It costs nothing. Register at a public employment service agency at the county level or above, such as an employment service center or human resources market. Your local gig market works too. If you don't know the address, call 12333.
Benefit
The law stipulates that the following are all free: advice on employment policy; information on who is hiring and where workers are needed; career guidance and job referrals; employment and unemployment registration; and employment assistance for people with employment difficulties. These agencies must not engage in for-profit activities or make money from these services. Registering and posting gig-work job information is also provided to the public free of charge and now falls within the scope of public employment information services. Gig workers with long idle spells (i.e., those who go long stretches without landing work), low-income households, and other gig workers in difficulty are to receive extra support (nationwide)
Note
Unemployment registration is a prerequisite for unemployment insurance benefits and for certification as a person with employment difficulties, so get it done while you're there. For gig work paid by the day, check the pay on the spot and keep the other party's contact details and a record of the work done.
Sources (2 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2007, 2015 revision). Employment Promotion Law (Article 35). https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647636.htm; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and four other departments (2022). Opinions on Strengthening the Building of Gig Markets and Improving Job-Seeking and Recruitment Services (MOHRSS Fa [2022] No. 38). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-07/09/content_570...

After a sudden calamity, apply for temporary assistance first

Grade BValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If something sudden hits your family — a fire, a car crash, a member stricken with serious illness — and basic living is temporarily crushed, you can apply for temporary assistance from the township government or subdistrict office. You don't need to already be a subsistence-allowance household. It is usually a one-time payment, and amounts vary widely by locality.

Cost
It costs nothing. Apply to the township government or subdistrict office and explain clearly what happened — for example a fire, a traffic accident, a family member's sudden major illness, or a sudden surge in unavoidable everyday expenses. After review and public notice, the county civil affairs department approves. Prepare materials per the local checklist; usually 1 to 2 trips.
Benefit
Two kinds of families qualify for temporary assistance. One: families who, because of accidents, a member's sudden major illness, and the like, cannot for the moment cover even the most basic expenses of food, housing, and medical care. Two: subsistence-allowance households whose unavoidable expenses suddenly rise beyond what they can bear. Which situations are covered and how much is paid are set and published by local governments at or above the county level (national system; amounts set locally; since 2014)
Note
You don't need to already be a subsistence-allowance household. It is usually a one-time payment; amounts differ a lot by locality, so go by what your locality publishes for the current year.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2014, 2019 revision). Interim Measures for Social Assistance (State Council Decree No. 649, Articles 47, 48, and 49). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5468952.htm
7

If your income is below the local minimum-living line, apply for the subsistence allowance

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Divide household income by the number of people; if it's below the local minimum-living line, and the family's assets also meet the rules, you can apply. At the end of 2024, the national average urban line was 798.1 yuan per person per month; rural, 593.9 yuan. What's paid is the difference between the line and the household's per-person monthly income. Owning a home, a car, or savings, or having children who can support you, may get you turned down.

Cost
It costs nothing. A household member living together with you submits a written application to the township government or subdistrict office where your household is registered. If applying yourself is inconvenient, you can entrust the village or residents' committee to do it for you. You must undergo a household income and asset check. Usually 2 to 3 trips, bringing your ID card, household register, and proof of income and assets. The hard part is opening up your family's finances to inspection, and waiting out the public notice.
Benefit
Divide household income by the number of people; if it's below the local subsistence standard, and the family's assets fall within the rules, you qualify. At the end of 2024, the national average urban standard was 798.1 yuan per person per month; rural, 593.9 yuan per person per month. The urban allowance covered 6.250 million people; the rural allowance, 33.615 million. The allowance is paid monthly as the difference: the local subsistence standard minus the household's per-capita income. For example, if the local standard is 798.1 yuan and the household's per-person monthly income is 500 yuan, each person receives 298.1 yuan a month — not 798.1. The standard is set like this: take the local residents' per-capita consumption expenditure of the previous year, multiply it by a prescribed ratio, and adjust it at intervals. In plain terms: take what an average local person spent last year and mark it down (national averages; varies by locality)
Note
The subsistence allowance is the last-line safety net and must be applied for in your place of household registration. If the family's home, car, or savings exceed local limits, or your children are able to support you, the application may be denied. Once approved there are further benefits: subsidized resident medical insurance premiums (resident medical insurance, see entry 9), medical assistance for treatment (medical assistance, see entry 10), and legal aid without a means test (legal aid, see entry 3).
Sources (3 references)
State Council (2014, 2019 revision). Interim Measures for Social Assistance (State Council Decree No. 649, Articles 9, 10, and 11; Article 12: "The civil affairs department of the county-level people's government shall pay the minimum-living-guarantee allowance monthly in the amount by which the per-capita income of the household members living together falls below the local minimum-living-guarantee standard"). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5468952.htm; National Bureau of Statistics (2025). Social programs developing for the better, people's wellbeing steadily improving — statistical report on social and livelihood development since the 14th Five-Year Plan. https://www.gov.cn/lianbo/bumen/202509/content_7042627.htm; Ministry of Civil Affairs and three other departments (2024). Guiding Opinions on Further Improving the Determination and Adjustment of Minimum-Living-Guarantee Standards (Minfa [2024] No. 16). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_7007237...

Disability certificate holders: apply for the two disability subsidies

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Disabled people in subsistence-allowance households can receive the living subsidy. Those rated disability grade 1 or 2 who also need long-term care can receive the nursing-care subsidy. The two can be received at once. Provinces set their own standards, which differ widely — ask your subdistrict office for specifics. Bring your second-generation disability certificate and complete it in one visit to the subdistrict or township.

Cost
It costs nothing. Bring your disability certificate and submit one application at the subdistrict or township office.
Benefit
The State Council set up the two subsidies. The first is the living subsidy for disabled people in difficulty; the document's target is "disabled people in subsistence-allowance households; places where conditions allow may gradually expand to low-income disabled people and other disabled people in difficulty" — meaning it first covers disabled people in subsistence-allowance households, and can widen where local finances permit. The second is the nursing-care subsidy for severely disabled people, targeting "severely disabled people rated grade 1 or 2 who need long-term care." The two can be received at the same time
Note
Provincial governments set the standards, which differ greatly by locality — anywhere from a few dozen yuan to several hundred yuan a month. Applications require the second-generation disability certificate. If applying in person is difficult, a family member can do it for you
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2015). Opinions on Fully Establishing the System of Living Subsidies for Disabled People in Difficulty and Nursing-Care Subsidies for Severely Disabled People (Guofa [2015] No. 52). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2015-09/25/content_101...
9

Don't let the 400-yuan-a-year resident medical insurance lapse; hardship households can get it reduced or waived

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Individuals pay from 400 yuan a year, and the budget tops it up with a subsidy of around 700 yuan per head. People in extreme poverty get it fully funded; subsistence-allowance recipients get a fixed amount funded. Lapsing has a price: if you didn't enroll during the centralized window or didn't pay consecutively, there's a 3-month period after you pay when medical bills aren't reimbursed — plus, in principle, 1 extra month for each additional year you missed.

Cost
The individual share is at least 400 yuan per person per year — the national standard for 2024 and 2025, and localities can go higher. Pay during the fixed centralized payment window each year. People in extreme poverty are fully funded: the government pays the whole amount. Subsistence-allowance recipients get fixed-amount funding: the government pays a fixed share.
Benefit
Besides the individual share, the budget adds a per-head top-up. In 2024 it was at least 670 yuan; in 2025 it rose 30 yuan over the previous year, to at least 700 yuan, while the individual payment stayed at no less than 400 yuan (Yibaofa [2025] No. 22, as relayed by provincial documents). The 2026 government work report says it will rise another 24 yuan. For subsistence-allowance recipients and people in extreme poverty, after medical insurance pays its share of qualifying medical expenses, the remainder can be claimed again through medical assistance at no less than 70%. The cost of lapsing is the waiting period: those who didn't enroll in the centralized window or didn't pay consecutively face a fixed 3-month benefit waiting period after paying, during which medical bills aren't reimbursed. Each additional year missed adds 1 more month, in principle (nationwide, from 2025)
Note
The National Healthcare Security Administration's 2025 notice (Yibaofa [2025] No. 22) was not publicly posted on the NHSA website or the central government website. The 700-yuan and 400-yuan figures are consistent across the Hebei and Anhui documents, and the Anhui one states it follows that notice. While you receive unemployment insurance benefits, the unemployment insurance fund pays your employee medical insurance, so don't double-enroll.

10

With a serious illness, first use medical insurance, major-illness insurance, medical assistance, and cross-region filing; don't touch online loans

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

The order is fixed. Before a cross-province hospital stay, file through the "National Healthcare Security Administration" official account so you can settle directly at discharge without fronting the full bill. If you still can't afford your share after reimbursement, apply for medical assistance at the township or subdistrict. Employees have a medical treatment period of 3 to 24 months depending on seniority, during which the company cannot dismiss you. Stay away from online loans and high-interest private lending.

Cost
It costs nothing. The order is fixed; take it step by step. Step 1: before a cross-province hospital stay, file through the "National Cross-Region Medical Treatment Filing" mini-program inside the "National Healthcare Security Administration" WeChat official account. Step 2: settle directly at discharge. Step 3: if your out-of-pocket share after reimbursement is still too heavy, apply for medical assistance at the township government or subdistrict office. Step 4: if you're employed, take sick leave under the medical treatment period — the stretch of time when illness stops your work but you cannot be fired; work injuries go through work-injury insurance. Step 5: if you can't pay your credit card, approach the bank proactively to negotiate installments. Step 6: only if that isn't enough, fundraise on a personal-appeal platform designated by the Ministry of Civil Affairs. The main materials are the diagnosis certificate, itemized bills, and settlement slips; expect 2 to 4 trips. The hard part is running these errands while ill.
Benefit
The state calls basic medical insurance, major-illness insurance, and medical assistance together the "three-tier system," each tier catching what the one above lets fall. Subsistence-allowance recipients and people in extreme poverty get assistance at no less than 70% of qualifying medical expenses. Seriously ill patients who weren't poor before but were impoverished by treatment can apply for further assistance themselves. With cross-province filing done before admission, you settle directly at discharge instead of fronting the full bill and claiming back at your enrollment place. Illness-related work stoppage carries a medical treatment period of 3 to 24 months, set by the length of your working years. During it the company must not terminate the labor contract, and sick pay must not fall below 80% of the local minimum wage. Workers with a work injury have a suspension-of-work-with-pay period — the stretch spent recovering without working — with original wages and benefits paid monthly by the employer, generally no more than 12 months. If credit-card debt exceeds your ability to repay but you're willing to repay, you can negotiate a personalized installment plan with the bank, reorganizing the debt over up to 5 years; once the agreement is signed the bank must stop collection. Online personal-appeal platforms that fundraise on a person's behalf must be designated by the civil affairs department of the State Council. Platforms must verify that appeal information is genuine. Donations can go only to the appealant in person, or to an account the appealant provides (nationwide)
Note
What share medical assistance covers and its annual cap are set by the place where you're insured. The medical treatment period has six tiers, based on your total working years and your years at this employer. Once it expires, the company may lawfully end the contract — know your tier in advance. Emergency rescue patients are also among those who need filing. The NHSA page doesn't say whether emergencies count as automatic filing or can be done retroactively; call your enrollment place to ask. Stay away from online loans and high-interest private lending. Courts protect interest only up to the line of 4 times the one-year LPR (on not borrowing from loan sharks, see entry 15). Amounts beyond that line are unprotected, though the principal is still owed. And you don't have the energy for that kind of court fight from a hospital bed. Acute, severe illness is a different matter: even with no money, call 120; hospitals may not refuse, shirk, or delay treatment, and the emergency fees for that care are paid by the disease emergency relief fund — see section 24, entry 8 (emergencies must be treated first). The original page of Laobufa [1995] No. 309 wouldn't open on the MOHRSS website; the content is taken from a provincial department's reposting.

Public-welfare jobs are positions developed with government funding; the subsidy is benchmarked to the local minimum wage. Government-developed public-welfare jobs give priority to people with employment difficulties. There is also a one-time job-seeking subsidy for college graduates, covering graduates from subsistence-allowance households, zero-employment households, and extreme-poverty status. Job hunt with a system, not just resumes: learn the skills, set targets, ask for help

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: yesBenefit: large

People who received job-search coaching were 2.67 times as likely to find work as those who didn't. What works: learning concrete job-search skills, getting clear on how to present yourself, setting definite targets, taking initiative, and asking people for help. Asking for help, in practice, means having acquaintances refer you internally.

Cost
It costs nothing. Budget 1 to 2 hours a day, for several weeks running. Skip the paid courses and use the free career guidance at public employment service agencies instead. The hard part is keeping it up every day when no one is watching, and reaching out to people for help.
Benefit
This pools 47 controlled studies of job-search coaching. These studies used experimental or quasi-experimental designs, all with comparison groups. The result: the coached group's odds of finding work were 2.67 times those of the uncoached group (OR 2.67, i.e., an odds ratio). The ingredients that work: teaching job-search skills; improving self-presentation (getting yourself across clearly); raising self-efficacy (believing you can do it); encouraging initiative; goal setting; and soliciting social support (asking people for help). Programs that both teach skills and lift motivation work best
Note
Most of these studies were done in Europe and America, as packaged group courses. Applying them in China borrows results measured elsewhere; they were not tested domestically. Soliciting social support, in practice, means having acquaintances introduce and refer you — don't be shy about asking.
Sources (1 reference)

No deposits, no leaving documents as collateral, no 'training loans,' no pyramid schemes, no loan sharks

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Employers may not hold your ID card, charge a deposit, or collect money under another name. If an agency fails to place you in a job, it must refund the fee. Training loans where you pay tuition before starting work, and pyramid schemes that pay on recruitment, are scams officially flagged by name. On loans, courts don't support the portion of interest beyond 4 times the one-year LPR — but the principal is still owed.

Cost
It costs nothing. When you hear "pay first, start work later," "train first, then we'll place you," or "bring in recruits," refuse on the spot. Keep chat logs and transfer records. The hard part: the poorer you are, the more you want to gamble, and saying "no" on the spot isn't easy.
Benefit
Companies may not seize your ID card or other documents, demand that you find a guarantor, or collect your money or property under another name. Violators are ordered to return them and fined 500 to 2,000 yuan per person. Employment agencies likewise may not hold documents or take deposits, and if no job is placed, they must refund the agency fee to you. Using recruitment as bait to get you to pay training fees or take out a loan first is the "recruitment-turned-training" and "training loan" scam flagged by name in a risk alert from MOHRSS and four other departments. Schemes that pay commissions on recruitment and require payment to join are pyramid schemes; participants can be fined up to 2,000 yuan. For private lending, courts do not support the portion of interest beyond 4 times the one-year LPR at the time the contract was signed. This new rule replaced the old system that carved rates into three bands at the 24% and 36% lines (nationwide, from August 2020)
Note
4 times the LPR is the ceiling of interest courts will protect, not "you can borrow and not repay" — the principal is still owed. This judicial interpretation was amended again in December 2020, with articles renumbered; the current text governs. For converting installment and online-loan fees into annualized rates, see section 5, entry 7 (converting interest to annualized rates). The more desperate you are for money, the more easily these schemes target you. First use the legitimate channels earlier in this section: unemployment insurance benefits, labor inspection complaints, legal aid, relief stations, temporary assistance.

Don't panic over gaps in social insurance: pensions count cumulatively, and medical insurance can be made up per the rules

Pensions are counted on cumulative years, not consecutive ones — a gap doesn't reset the clock. Reach retirement age with 15 cumulative years and you draw a monthly pension. What gaps really affect are benefits requiring continuous contributions, like buying a home, hukou settlement, or points systems.

Those released after serving their sentences may not be discriminated against in employment, schooling, or social insurance; those in hardship are helped with placement by the government. The dishonesty blacklist lasts 2 years, and once the money is repaid the court should remove your name within 3 working days. Adults' criminal records are not sealed and must be truthfully reported for military service and employment.

Cost
No handling fees. If released from prison, report to the judicial office or subdistrict of your registered or actual residence and apply for resettlement assistance (government placement and support). If you're on the dishonest judgment-debtor list, repay everything owed, then apply to the enforcement court to have your name removed. Individuals who have paid into social insurance in Shenzhen for 3 full years can apply for personal bankruptcy. Every step requires materials and interviews, plus an observation period of 1 to 3 years. The hard part is retelling your past over and over, and enduring the observation period.
Benefit
People released after serving their sentences enjoy the same rights as other citizens by law and may not be discriminated against in employment, schooling, or social security. The Shenzhen Special Economic Zone Personal Bankruptcy Regulation is currently the only personal bankruptcy law: after bankruptcy is declared and the 3-year observation period is served, unpaid debts can be discharged. Corporate legal persons that can't pay debts as they fall due, and owe more than they own (insolvent), can apply for reorganization, composition, or bankruptcy liquidation, with the debts resolved along with the enterprise (nationwide; personal bankruptcy in Shenzhen only)
Note
Adults' records are not sealed. Article 100 of the Criminal Law requires truthful reporting of prior criminal punishment when applying for military service or jobs. Civil servants, judges, lawyers, teachers, and similar professions, plus political vetting, carry separate statutory restrictions. Before November 1, 2026, the current text of the Prison Law corresponds to Articles 37 and 38; article numbers follow the text in force. The original page for Zhongbanfa [2010] No. 5 couldn't be found on the central government website; it's taken from a district government's reposting. During the personal bankruptcy observation period: no first-class flights, no high consumption, no buying property; 8 categories of debt are not discharged, including damages for intentional personal injury; a discharge obtained through fraud can be revoked. Before major illness strikes, add a one-year medical or critical-illness policy on top of basic insurance, and look hard at the words 'guaranteed renewal'

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Such insurance covers what you pay out of pocket after medical insurance reimbursement, plus the losses from stopping work. Before buying, look for the words "guaranteed renewal": policies without them may be discontinued or repriced next year. Disclose your health status truthfully; concealment means denied claims. Get basic medical insurance first, then consider this one.

Cost
For young people, a one-year expense-reimbursement medical policy costs a few hundred yuan a year. Expense-reimbursement means it reimburses what you actually spent. Critical-illness insurance starts at several thousand yuan a year (author's rough estimate; no official figures). Before applying, truthfully disclose your health status — a one-time half hour.
Benefit
Officially these products split into two kinds. Medical insurance reimburses your actual medical expenses. Disease insurance pays a lump sum at the agreed amount as soon as one of the diseases specified in the contract is diagnosed. Both cover your out-of-pocket share after medical insurance reimbursement, plus the losses from stopping work. Policies of one year or less whose terms don't state guaranteed renewal are short-term health insurance. Over one year, or with guaranteed renewal written in, is long-term health insurance. "Guaranteed renewal" means: at renewal, the company must continue coverage under the original terms and agreed rates. Insurers may not induce the same person to repeatedly buy expense-reimbursement medical policies with identical or similar coverage; with two policies, the same money is still reimbursed only once. Critical-illness disease definitions have an industry-wide standard covering 28 major diseases and 3 minor diseases. Malignant tumors, acute myocardial infarction, and stroke sequelae are the core conditions (nationwide, from 2019 and 2020)
Note
This is graded B because officials provided only definitions and rules, not figures for "how much buying saves you." "Million-yuan medical insurance" is a sales label; under the rules it counts as short-term health insurance. Without "guaranteed renewal" in the terms, it may be discontinued or repriced next year — find those words in the contract before buying. Two expense-reimbursement medical policies can't reimburse the same money twice; don't stack them. Those who buy while already ill and don't disclose it face denied claims. Truthful disclosure has a two-year limit: once the contract has been in force for two years, the insurer can no longer rescind it for non-disclosure and must pay claims. If deliberate non-disclosure is discovered within two years, events before rescission aren't paid and premiums aren't refunded. For which losses are worth insuring, see section 5, entry 39 (losses you can't absorb). Get resident medical insurance (entry 9) first, then consider this one. The disease-definition specification was issued by industry associations under CBIRC guidance; it is not a government document.
Sources (4 references)

Notice on Matters Concerning the Use of the "China Life Insurance Industry Critical Illness Experience Incidence Table (2020)" (Yinbaojianfa [2020] No. 51). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-11/06/content_555...; NPC Standing Committee (2015 revision). Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 16 (truthful disclosure, and no rescission once the contract has been in force for two years). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4...
21

If you truly have nowhere to sleep, 24-hour venues are for one emergency night only; go to a relief station first

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: small

Airport and railway station waiting areas can get you through a night, with toilets and power outlets. But no official data says this is safe. Keep valuables on your person, accept no food or drink from strangers, and avoid isolated corners. Don't sleep at night under bridges, by rivers, or on construction sites. Relief stations provide free food and lodging — go there first.

Cost
Airport and station waiting areas usually cost nothing. Fast-food restaurants and internet cafes require some spending. You won't sleep soundly, and there's a risk of theft. The hard part: not daring to truly sleep all night.
Benefit
You can get through one night; there are toilets and places to charge. No official figures
Note
The safety risks are real. Keep valuables on your person, accept no drinks or food from strangers, and avoid isolated corners. Don't sleep rough at night under bridges, by rivers, or on construction sites. Sleeping rough in extreme weather can be fatal. The relief station in entry 4 provides free food and lodging — go there first. Some venues clear out at midnight; don't clash with security.
Sources
Author's experience; no official documents.
22

Owed wages? First work out who employed you: for unlicensed workshops and labor contractors, go to labor inspection all the same; only for private work for households or individuals go to court

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Unlicensed workshops and shops that owe wages can still be reported to labor inspection and taken to labor arbitration, and the boss personally can be pursued. When a labor contractor subcontracted work on a site owes wages, the general contractor or construction unit pays. Only private work for a household or individual — being a nanny, say — isn't a labor dispute, and you must sue in court.

Cost
It costs nothing. First work out three things: is the other party running a shop, factory, or business; was the work subcontracted down from a company or site; and are you working inside someone's home. Whether the other party has a license can be checked on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publicity System.
Benefit
Article 2 of the Labor Contract Law defines employing units as enterprises, individual economic organizations, private non-enterprise units, and similar organizations — natural persons are not among them. The Supreme People's Court's judicial interpretation on labor disputes lists several disputes that are not labor disputes. One: disputes between a household or individual and domestic service workers. Two: disputes between individual craftsmen and their helpers or apprentices. Three: disputes between rural contracted-operation households and their hires. These go to court as ordinary civil disputes, with a 3-year limitation period. Employing units without a business license are not in this exception. Article 93 of the Labor Contract Law: where an employing unit without lawful business qualifications has received labor already performed, that unit or its investor must pay labor remuneration, severance, and damages. Article 29 of that interpretation: where a worker has a dispute with an employing unit that never obtained a business license, had its license revoked, or continued operating past its term, the unit or its investor is to be listed as a party. Article 33 of the Regulations on Labor Security Supervision: units without a license, or whose license has been lawfully revoked, that nonetheless engage in labor employment are subject to labor security supervision by the labor security administrative department. Where individually contracted operations unlawfully recruit workers and cause them harm, the contracting-out organization and the individual contractor bear joint liability for damages (Labor Contract Law, Article 94). Where a construction unit or general contractor awards or subcontracts work to individuals or units without lawful business qualifications, causing migrant workers' wage arrears, the construction unit or general contractor clears the wages (Regulations on Guaranteeing Wage Payment to Migrant Workers, Article 36) (nationwide)
Note
Judge in this order. First, was the work passed down from a company or site? If so, go after the awarding company or the general contractor. For dedicated wage accounts on sites and the general contractor clearing wages first, see entry 2 (owed wages: complain to labor inspection first). Next, is the other party running a business? Shops, factories, workshops — with or without a license — go through inspection and arbitration, listing the boss personally in arbitration. Only the remainder — private work for households or individuals — goes to court. In court you sue yourself and bear the burden of proof; first instance under the ordinary procedure runs 6 months and up. Attorney fees are not among the litigation costs courts order the losing side to bear — you pay your own lawyer; if you can't afford it, apply for legal aid, see entry 3 (legal aid). With an IOU in hand you can first apply for a payment order; for small amounts use small-claims procedure, see section 8, entry 22 (scammed in secondhand trades; small claims). The limitation period is 3 years, see section 8, entry 19 (claims have deadlines). No route guarantees the money arrives; if the other side has no assets, you win and get nothing.
Sources (7 references)

(reposted in the State Taxation Administration policy and regulations database); Supreme People's Court (2020). Regulations on Labor Security Supervision (State Council Decree No. 423, Article 33). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2004/content_63042.htm; State Council (2019). Regulations on Guaranteeing Wage Payment to Migrant Workers (State Council Decree No. 724, Article 36). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5469641.htm; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 188). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; State Council (2006). Measures on the Payment of Litigation Fees (State Council Decree No. 481, Articles 6 and 29). https://www.gov.cn/ziliao/flfg/2006-12/29/content_483682.htm; NPC Standing Committee (2023 revision).
