8. Don't get yourself implicated: legal and property safety

46 items

This section is counted in money and personal freedom, not converted into years of life. It covers three things: what responsibilities the law assigns you, how much less you may have to pay by following the rules, and what procedural rights you have when something happens. Every article number has been checked against the official original texts. The ordering rule: the ones where a single incident costs the most and that take the least effort go first; the ones that need advance arrangements go in the middle; the ones backed only by experience, with no official document behind them, go last. This section's entries are grouped by topic below; entry numbers are in parentheses. Fraud prevention: demand a payment freeze the moment you discover a scam (item 2), hard anti-fraud rules (item 3), a face on video is not verification (item 4), don't lend out bank cards or SIM cards (item 8), free credit report checks (item 9), scammed in online or second-hand deals (item 22), ask the price before at-home repairs (item 27), don't carry things for strangers (item 29), 'lending your face' for a loan is an AB loan (item 45). Signing, lending money, and debt: read the whole document before signing (item 17), write a clear IOU when lending money (item 18), claims have deadlines (item 19), declare assets truthfully when under enforcement (item 20), being put on the dishonesty list (item 21), don't be a name-only legal representative (item 28), a family member ran up gambling debts (item 44). Conflict and grudges: call the police first when conflict breaks out (item 10), you may fight back against assault you can't escape (item 11), don't go settle scores after a falling-out (item 12), never attack uninvolved people (item 13), thoughts of going down together (item 14), when someone close says no one gets to live well (item 15), the buy-insurance-first-then-act route is blocked (item 38). Dating and marriage: think carefully before delivering large gifts (item 23), pay bride price by transfer (item 24), spell out pre-marital assets (item 25), verify marital status before marrying (item 26), call the police first when facing domestic violence (item 43). Police reports, charges, and evidence: get a lawyer first when summoned (item 5), come forward and tell it clearly (item 6), falsely reported on fabricated facts (item 33), insufficient evidence should mean acquittal (item 34), apply for state compensation (item 35), demand the case-acceptance receipt when reporting (item 39), don't give money to the people handling the case (item 40), record conversations that could turn ugly (item 41), shoot the panorama first on scene (item 42). Online speech and cyberbullying: no insults or rumors online (item 16), switch on protections first when cyberbullied (item 37). Sex and blackmail: no sex when the other person isn't fully conscious (item 31), nude-chat blackmail demands: call the police directly (item 32), victims seeking compensation: don't meet the other side alone (item 36). Driving, dogs, and burglary prevention: don't flee a traffic accident (item 1), don't touch the steering wheel after drinking (item 7), dogs must be leashed (item 30), fit good locks on doors and windows (item 46).

1

In a traffic accident: stop, help the injured, call the police — never flee

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Flee, and the accident is by default counted as entirely your fault. Your license is revoked and you can never take the test again this lifetime. There is a more concrete layer too: collision and third-party liability insurance never pays on hit-and-runs, and several hundred thousand in compensation comes entirely out of your own pocket. Staying to help the injured and call the police costs you an hour or two at most.

Cost
Costs nothing. Stop the car, turn on the hazard lights, help the injured, phone the police — waiting for traffic police takes an hour or two at most. In a minor accident where nobody is hurt and both sides agree on the facts, photograph everything first. Then write down the other party's name, phone number, license plate, driver's license number, insurance certificate number, and the point of impact. Once both parties sign, you may leave the scene first and settle it between yourselves.
Benefit
The party that flees bears full responsibility for the accident. Only if you can prove the other side was also at fault might your share be reduced a little. Fleeing also means your driver's license is revoked, and you can never retake the test in this lifetime. If the accident constitutes the crime of causing a traffic accident, fleeing draws 3 to 7 years; if the flight causes a death, 7 years or more. Insurance won't cover it either: under commercial auto policies, collision coverage and third-party liability coverage never pay when it comes to 'hit-and-run' or 'deliberately destroying, fabricating, or tampering with the scene and destroying evidence' — several hundred thousand in compensation is yours alone to pay (nationwide)
Note
If anyone is hurt, rescue them first, then call the police. If things must be moved to rescue someone, first mark where the vehicles and people originally stood. 'I bumped something, didn't feel it, and drove off' can still be counted as hit-and-run afterwards; when in doubt, call the police. The insurance point cites the model clauses — the insurance industry's uniform template — so what you actually get paid is governed by the policy in your own hands.
Sources (4 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2021). Road Traffic Safety Law (2021 revision, Articles 70 and 101). https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/205308/index.html (reposted by the Beijing Traffic Management Bureau); State Council (2017). Implementation Regulations for the Road Traffic Safety Law (State Council Decree No. 405, 2017 revision, Articles 86 and 92). http://xzfg.moj.gov.cn/front/law/detail?LawID=75; NPC (1997). Criminal Law (Article 133). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml; Insurance Association of China (2020). Model Clauses for Commercial Motor Vehicle Insurance (2020 edition) (Articles 9 and 22). https://www.iachina.cn/art/2020/9/4/art_24_104621.html
2

Scammed? Call 110 or 96110 at once to freeze the payment; don't investigate on your own first

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The short span right after the money leaves your account is the only window there is. In it, the police can urgently stop the payment and freeze it fast, and the banks must cooperate. Once the money has been moved through layer after layer of accounts and scattered, it is basically unrecoverable. So call 110 or 96110 first — don't go checking or asking around on your own first. When 96110 calls you, it's the police trying to dissuade you; pick up.

Cost
Costs nothing. Make one phone call and state clearly the time of the transfer, the amount, and the other side's account number. Keep the transfer screenshots and chat records safe.
Benefit
Public security organs have the authority to run instant queries, emergency payment stops, and rapid freezes on funds involved in a case. Banks and payment institutions must cooperate. Frozen funds are returned to the victim through due procedure. Once the money has been transferred away and dispersed, the odds of recovery drop sharply, so the earlier the stop, the better it works. 96110 is the nationwide unified anti-fraud warning hotline; when it calls, it is the police trying to dissuade you — be sure to answer (nationwide, since December 2022)
Note
Anyone claiming to be the police, prosecutors, or the courts and telling you to move your money to a 'safe account' is a scammer. The law only says to 'establish a payment-stop and freeze system', meaning the banks hold the money. How much can be recovered depends on whether the money is still in the account when you report. The description of the 'National Anti-Fraud Center' app and 96110 is quoted from the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department's page; the original page on the Ministry of Public Security website won't open.
Sources (2 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2022). Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law (Articles 20 and 34). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202209/t20220902_575631.shtml; Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (2023). If 96110 calls, please be sure to answer. http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202303/t20230… (provincial public security organ page)
3

Remember the hard anti-fraud rules: don't trust unexpected callers, don't reveal information, don't click links, verify before transferring — the seven most common scams all fit this shape

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Whoever asks you to transfer money, share your screen, download an unfamiliar app, click a link, or read out a verification code — hang up first, then call back on the official number to verify. Order-brushing rebates, fake investments, online loans, fake customer service, impersonating the police or prosecutors, pig-butchering, and sex-lure tasks — these seven are the most common, and they all want your money first. Spotting them beforehand is far cheaper than chasing the money afterwards.

Cost
Costs nothing. Memorize the 'three don'ts and one more', read through the seven types below, install the 'National Anti-Fraud Center' app, and always answer a call from 96110. Whoever asks you to transfer money, share your screen, download an unfamiliar app, click a link, or read out a verification code — hang up first, then call the official number to verify. The hard part is that the other side often pushes with great urgency; you must withstand that push and hang up first.
Benefit
The law requires the government and the departments concerned to explain the tactics of the various kinds of telecom and online fraud to the public. Public security organs, together with the finance, telecom, and cyberspace authorities, have built an early-warning and dissuasion system; when they spot someone who is about to be scammed, they step in and dissuade them in time. 96110 is precisely this nationwide unified warning-and-dissuasion hotline; answer when it calls. The Ministry of Public Security reported in June 2026 that the 10 most frequent fraud types account for 85% of all telecom fraud cases. Order-brushing rebate fraud is the most frequent, at 25%. Fake online investment fraud causes the largest losses, about 40% of all losses. The Fujian Provincial Public Security Department breaks the recognition signs down type by type. Order-brushing rebates: 'whoever calls on you to make money together probably wants to make money off you' — fail to finish the task list and your principal is not returned. Fake investments: paid shills in the group flaunt their returns, small rebates come first to hook you and then you are pushed to put in more, and withdrawals require 'paying tax.' Online loans: 'a real loan never requires a security deposit or a faked bank-statement record; once you run into that, it is definitely fake.' Fake customer service: they claim your membership will be auto-charged and will hurt your credit, pressing you to transfer money to cancel. Impersonating the police, prosecutors, or courts: 'police, procuratorial, and judicial organs have no such thing as a "safe account"; any "authority" that handles cases or takes statements by phone, QQ, WeChat, or the internet is a scammer.' Pig-butchering: 'do not readily trust a "lover" you have never met in person and have only seen in photos or videos' — there are never video calls or meetings, yet there is always some urgent matter that needs money. Sex-lure tasks: before any meetup you must first 'do tasks,' and the money you hand over keeps growing. Spotting it beforehand is far cheaper than a payment stop afterwards. How much a stop can recover depends on whether the money is still in the account when you report; for how to stop a payment, see item 2 (call 110 or 96110 to demand a payment stop) (nationwide, since December 2022)
Note
Anyone claiming to be the police or prosecutors, customer service, your boss, or platform risk control, asking you to 'cooperate with an investigation,' 'cancel your membership,' 'brush orders for rebates,' or act on 'insider investment tips,' is running the same play. A real loan never requires a deposit, and the police have no 'safe account' — remembering these two lines blocks more than half of the scams. Grade B because this mnemonic is only official publicity messaging; there is no figure for 'how much less you get scammed after memorizing it.' The mnemonic and the seven-type breakdown come from a provincial public security department's page. The MPS's 2026 list of 10 high-frequency fraud types also includes fake e-commerce and logistics customer service, loan-and-credit-record scams, fake online game transactions, online romance, impersonated bosses and acquaintances, and flight change-and-refund scams — the play is the same and it always ends with you transferring money. For an acquaintance asking you in person to 'lend your face' for a loan — you don't transfer money, you take on the debt — see item 45 (lending your face). For the agency-operation scam you can hit while running a business, see section 12, item 24 (agency-run online stores).
Sources (10 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2022). Anti-Telecom and Online Fraud Law (Articles 8, 20, and 34). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202209/t20220902_575631.shtml; Ministry of Public Security (2026). MPS press conference: briefing on the latest situation and features of current telecom and online fraud crime and tips for preventing telecom and online fraud (June 12, 2026): 'These 10 types of cases alone account for 85% of all telecom fraud cases. Among them, order-brushing rebate fraud has the highest incidence, 25% of all telecom fraud cases; fake online investment fraud causes the largest losses, about 40% of all losses in telecom fraud cases'. https://www.mps.gov.cn/n2254536/n2254544/n2254552/n10491781…; Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (2023). If 96110 calls, please be sure to answer. http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202303/t20230… (provincial public security organ page, containing the mnemonic 'don't readily trust callers, don't disclose information, don't click links, verify more before transferring' and the tip 'beware of scam calls beginning with 192'); Fujian Provincial Public Security Department (2023 to 2024). Scam-spotting skills column: order-brushing http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202307/t20230…; investment scams http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202312/t20231…; loans http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202312/t20231…; fake customer service http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202310/t20231…; impersonating police and prosecutors http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202309/t20230…; pig-butchering http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202308/t20230…; sex-lure tasks http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202403/t20240…
4

A face on video or a voice on the phone is not verification; where transfers are involved, hang up first and call back on the old number in your own contacts

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

A face on video, a voice on the phone — neither counts as verification. Whenever money is involved, hang up first, then call back on the old number saved in your own contacts, or ask someone you both know. If they say 'bad signal' or 'I'm in a meeting' and refuse an on-camera video call, treat it as a scam.

Cost
Costs nothing. One extra phone call, a few extra minutes of waiting. Day to day, post fewer full-face videos and long voice messages on public accounts. The hard part is that they often rush you; you must resist transferring on the spot.
Benefit
The MPS cybersecurity bureau offers three methods. The first is motion testing: ask the other person to make one smooth head-turning motion, or to cover their face completely with a palm and pull the hand away fast. The original text says 'current AI technology tends to stutter, blur, or distort when simulating these complex facial occlusions and lighting changes.' The second is listening for voice detail: 'AI-generated voices sometimes lack natural breathing pauses and emotional rises and falls, or carry a slight mechanical quality or abnormal background noise.' The third is verifying through multiple channels. The original calls it 'the most crucial move': 'after hanging up, dial the number the person normally uses and that you know well (do not call back the suspicious incoming number), or check indirectly through a third person you both know.' The mnemonic: 'do not readily trust video or voice; test with motions and verify more.' In law, face-swapping and voice-cloning have long been banned from use in fraud. For face generation, face replacement, synthesized voices, and voice imitation services, platforms must attach a conspicuous label, and no organization or individual may maliciously delete, alter, forge, or conceal it. But it is platforms that follow the rules; scammers will not add the label, so 'no AI label seen' cannot be turned around into evidence that the other person is real. The MPS criminal investigation bureau has publicized a case: a 14-member gang was caught with more than 50,000 synthesized dynamic facial videos and more than 500,000 items of citizens' personal information; the police also seized 60 cloud servers (nationwide; the labeling obligation applies from September 1, 2025)
Note
Call back on the old number saved in your own contacts. Do not call back the number on the incoming call, and do not use a new number they send you in the chat. If they refuse an on-camera video call or the requested motion on grounds of 'bad signal' or 'being in a meeting,' treat it as a scam. Motion testing is only an aid; AI keeps improving, and the only dependable step is the third one — verification. Already sent the money? See item 2 of this section (call 110 at once to stop the payment). For keeping your own face and voice from being harvested, see section 14. Grade B because the authorities give identification methods and case examples, but no figure for 'how much the scam rate drops when you verify this way.' The Ministry of Public Security's website (mps.gov.cn) was again entirely down with 521 errors this time; the cybersecurity bureau and criminal investigation bureau texts are taken from the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department's reposting pages.
Sources (4 references)
MPS Cybersecurity Bureau (2025). Seeing is not believing — beware of new types of AI fraud! http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202509/t20250… (reposted by the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department); Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, and Ministry of Public Security (2022). Provisions on the Administration of Deep Synthesis in Internet Information Services (Articles 6, 16, and 17; effective January 10, 2023). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-12/12/content_573…; Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Ministry of Public Security, and National Radio and Television Administration (2025). Measures for Labeling AI-Generated and Synthesized Content (Article 10; effective September 1, 2025). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-03/14/c_1743654684782215.htm; MPS Criminal Investigation Bureau and CCTV News (2026). Police seize more than 50,000 synthesized dynamic facial videos — who is 'copying' your face? http://gat.fujian.gov.cn/ztzl/fjjffpzxrx/spjq/202603/t20260… (reposted by the Fujian Provincial Public Security Department)
5

Charged or summoned? Get a lawyer first; no private settling, no deleting records

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: a lotTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

From the very first time you are called in for questioning, you may retain a lawyer. When your lawyer requests to see you, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest, and the conversation cannot be monitored. You may refuse to answer questions unrelated to the case.

Cost
Lawyer fees start from a few thousand yuan. Those in financial difficulty can apply to a legal aid institution for a free lawyer. During questioning, answer only questions related to the case and leave the rest to your lawyer. The hard part is staying composed on the spot and not rushing to explain yourself.
Benefit
From the first interrogation onward, or from the moment compulsory measures are taken against you (your personal freedom restricted), you have the right to retain a lawyer. While the case is still in the police's hands at the investigation stage, you may retain only a lawyer — no one other than a lawyer may act as your defender. When the lawyer requests a meeting, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest, and the meeting is not monitored. No one may be forced to prove their own guilt. You have the right to refuse to answer questions unrelated to the case. A summons or a compelled summons lasts at most 12 hours at a time, or at most 24 hours for especially major and complex cases. A summons is a notice to come in for questioning; a compelled summons is being forcibly brought in for questioning. Serial summonses must not be used to hold a person in disguised detention. Fabricating facts to accuse someone falsely, intending to have them criminally pursued, draws up to 3 years; where serious consequences result, 3 to 10 years. If after detention or arrest the case is withdrawn, prosecution is declined, or you are acquitted, you may apply for state compensation, calculated daily at the previous year's national average daily wage of employees (nationwide)
Note
Do not go to the other party privately, and do not go to their family either. Any 'private settlement' can be read as an admission. Chat records, call logs, and travel records are the material that proves your innocence; deleting them means deleting your own evidence. Misremembering, or a report that later proves unfounded, is not the crime of false accusation. This item applies to accused persons regardless of gender. For the three expanded items, see item 33 of this section (holding the fabricator accountable), item 34 (insufficient evidence should mean acquittal, plus petitions and retrials), and item 35 (state compensation for time held, paid by the day).
Sources (3 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 amendment, Articles 34, 35, 39, 52, 119, and 120). https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml; NPC (1997). Criminal Law (Article 243). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml; NPC Standing Committee (2012). State Compensation Law (2012 amendment, Articles 17 and 33). https://www.stats.gov.cn/gk/tjfg/xgfxfg/202503/t20250306_19… (reposted by the National Bureau of Statistics)
6

When something happens, come forward and tell it clearly: voluntary surrender can cut up to 40% off your sentence, and 'outlasting the statute of limitations' is a dead end

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Voluntary surrender can shave up to 40% off the sentence, and for lesser offenses it can mean no punishment at all. Confessing truthfully only after they come knocking still cuts up to 20%. Running and denying earn you none of this. Hoping to hide for a few years and let the case expire doesn't work either: once a case has been opened, the time you spend hiding does not count toward the limitation period.

Cost
Costs nothing. Turn yourself in at a public security organ, or stay where you are, call the police, and tell the whole story truthfully. The hard part is resisting the thought of 'wait a bit longer; maybe no one is investigating.'
Benefit
Article 67 of the Criminal Law: one who voluntarily turns himself in after committing a crime and truthfully confesses the crime has voluntarily surrendered. Such a person may receive lighter or mitigated punishment, and where the crime is minor, punishment may be waived. One who does not surrender but truthfully confesses the crime (candid confession) may receive lighter punishment; where the truthful confession averts especially serious consequences, punishment may be mitigated. The sentencing guidance of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate gives the ranges in black and white. The baseline sentence is the term first worked out from the facts of the case, and the percentages below are all reductions from it. Voluntary surrender cuts up to 40% off the baseline sentence; where the crime is minor, more than 40%, or punishment may be waived by law. Within candid confession: truthful confession of one's crime cuts up to 20%; truthful confession of a similar, more serious offense the judicial organs do not yet know of cuts 10% to 30%; truthful confession that averts especially serious consequences cuts 30% to 50%. Pleading guilty and accepting punishment cuts up to 30%; where voluntary surrender, major candid confession, returning illicit gains and paying restitution, compensating the victim, and the victim's forgiveness all exist, up to 60%; where the crime is minor, more than 60%, or punishment waived by law. Limitation periods run in four tiers by the statutory maximum penalty: 5, 10, 15, and 20 years (Article 87 of the Criminal Law). But Article 88 states plainly: once a procuratorate, public security organ, or state security organ has opened a case for investigation, or a court has accepted the case, evasion of investigation or trial is not subject to any limitation period (nationwide; sentencing ranges effective July 1, 2021)
Note
The beneficiary here is yourself. Voluntary surrender is only a mitigating factor — the conviction still stands, the court decides how much comes off, and the sentencing guidance requires leniency to be applied strictly for serious violent crimes and drug crimes. Traffic accidents follow a separate calculation: staying at the scene, rescuing the injured, and reporting to the public security organ counts as voluntary surrender, but because these are legal duties in the first place, leniency is to be applied strictly; fleeing and then turning yourself in still counts as surrender, only the heavier statutory penalty tier is taken as the baseline before deciding whether and how much to reduce — see item 1 of this section (stop, help the injured, call the police). Getting a lawyer first does not conflict with confessing truthfully; see item 5 of this section (get a lawyer when charged): what your lawyer checks for you is whether the transcript was recorded correctly, not helping you invent a story.

After drinking, don't touch the steering wheel — including e-bikes and 'just moving the car a little'

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Drive after drinking: license suspended 6 months, a fine of 1,000 to 2,000 yuan. A repeat offense brings detention plus revocation. Drunk driving means immediate revocation, no retaking the test for 5 years, plus criminal liability for dangerous driving — a record that affects political vetting and some careers. Insurance won't cover it either: drive after drinking and auto insurance pays nothing. 'Just moving the car a little' still counts as driving.

Cost
A designated-driver service or a taxi costs a few dozen yuan. Before the gathering, agree in advance on who is not drinking today. The hard part is pushing back when you're pressed to drink in the moment.
Benefit
Driving after drinking: license suspended for 6 months and a fine of 1,000 to 2,000 yuan. Repeat offenders: up to 10 days of detention plus license revocation. Drunk driving: license revoked outright, no re-test for 5 years, criminal liability pursued for the crime of dangerous driving, with a sentence of criminal detention plus a fine — criminal detention means short-term custody. Commercial vehicle drivers face heavier penalties: driving after drinking brings 15 days of detention, a 5,000 yuan fine, and a 5-year driving ban; drunk driving brings a 10-year ban, plus a lifetime ban on commercial driving. Those who cause a major accident after drinking or while drunk, constituting a crime, are banned from driving for life. Commercial auto insurance never pays for driving after drinking or taking drugs (nationwide)
Note
Drunk driving is a criminal offense and leaves a record, affecting your own political vetting and some professional qualifications. The line between 'having drunk' and 'drunk' is drawn by blood alcohol content, with the specific threshold set by national standards. This section has not verified that figure — don't estimate by feel which tier you fall into.

8

Lend no one your bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts; being a 'money mule' isn't a part-time job

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Renting out, lending, or selling your bank cards, SIM cards, or payment accounts is itself illegal. The fine is 1 to 10 times the illicit gains, or up to 200,000 yuan if there are no gains; in serious cases, 15 days of detention, plus being entered into your credit record and having account functions restricted. If you knowingly help collect and move money for someone else's crime, that is the crime of assisting information network criminal activities, punishable by up to 3 years.

Cost
Costs nothing. When someone says 'just let your card process a payment, I'll give you a few hundred yuan,' simply refuse.
Benefit
Renting out, lending, buying, or selling phone cards, bank accounts, payment accounts, or internet accounts is itself illegal. Illicit gains are confiscated, plus a fine of 1 to 10 times those gains. With no illicit gains, a fine of up to 200,000 yuan. Serious cases: up to 15 days of detention. You may also be entered into credit records, have account functions restricted, and have non-counter services suspended (everything must then be done in person at the counter). Knowing that someone uses the internet to commit a crime and still providing payment-settlement help — in serious cases this constitutes the crime of assisting information network criminal activities ('assistance' offense), punishable by up to 3 years plus a fine (nationwide)
Note
Saying 'I don't know what he used the card for' doesn't shield you. Investigators infer knowledge from outward circumstances: having taken a cut, obviously abnormal transaction flows — either can count as knowing. If the card was used to receive stolen money, even if you are ultimately not convicted, the account gets frozen and you face discipline yourself. Lending your face or reading out verification codes for someone else's identity check carries the same penalties as this item; see item 45 (lending your face).
Sources (2 references)

Criminal Law Amendment IX (Article 29, i.e., Article 287-2 of the Criminal Law). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180205_364562.shtml
9

Check your own credit report twice a year for free; look for loans and cards you didn't open

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

You can check your own credit report online for free twice a year; it takes ten minutes. Use the People's Bank of China Credit Reference Center's official website or mobile banking — not third-party 'credit check' apps, which are collecting your information. Adverse records stay for 5 years from the day the matter ends, and should be deleted after that. You can raise a dispute, and they must reply to you in writing within 20 days.

Cost
Costs nothing. Check online; it takes ten minutes.
Benefit
The administrative regulation states that 'an individual information subject has the right to obtain their own credit report free of charge twice each year' — you can check yourself twice a year for free. Adverse information is kept 'for 5 years from the date the adverse act or event terminates; beyond 5 years, it shall be deleted.' If you dispute the report, you can raise it; the credit reporting institution or the institution that provided the information must reply to you in writing within 20 days of receiving the dispute
Note
When someone else takes out online loans or opens cards with your stolen ID, you often find out only when a mortgage application is rejected — by then years have passed. The place to check is the People's Bank of China Credit Reference Center's official website, or mobile banking. Do not use third-party 'credit check' apps; those apps are themselves collecting your information. Especially after you have 'lent your face or played witness' for an acquaintance, run a check; see item 45 (lending your face).

In a conflict, call the police and keep your hands off: whoever strikes first almost certainly comes off worse

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Assault someone: 5 to 10 days of detention and a fine of 500 to 1,000 yuan. Group attacks, attacking the elderly, pregnant women, children, or people with disabilities, or repeat offenses: 10 to 15 days of detention and a fine of 1,000 to 2,000 yuan. Injuries assessed as 'minor injury' make it a criminal case, up to 3 years; serious injury draws 3 to 10 years. Two people swinging at each other is not self-defense, and whoever strikes first almost certainly comes off worse. Backing away to somewhere crowded and calling the police works better than fighting back.

Cost
Costs nothing. Retreat to somewhere crowded and call the police, letting the cameras capture the other side's moves. The hard part is holding back the retorts and the shoving.
Benefit
Beating someone or intentional injury: 5 to 10 days of detention plus a fine of 500 to 1,000 yuan. Group attacks, attacking the elderly, pregnant women, children, or people with disabilities, or beating several people at once or repeatedly: 10 to 15 days of detention plus a fine of 1,000 to 2,000 yuan. Group brawling is handled as picking quarrels and provoking trouble — up to 15 days of detention plus a 2,000 yuan fine; picking quarrels means stirring up trouble and making scenes out of nothing. Deliberately injuring another person where a crime is constituted: up to 3 years; causing serious injury: 3 to 10 years. Two people swinging at each other is legally 'mutual affray,' not self-defense. But if the other side struck first with clearly excessive force, or you had already tried hard to get away and they kept hitting, your counterattack will generally be recognized as defense. Only counterattack that goes too far is excessive defense, which requires both at once: clearly exceeding the necessary limits, and causing major harm. Even genuinely excessive defense must receive mitigated punishment or none at all (nationwide; Public Security Administration Punishments Law effective January 1, 2026)
Note
After the 2025 revision of the Public Security Administration Punishments Law the article numbers all changed: beating others moved from Article 43 of the old law to Article 51, so material citing the old numbers is out of date. How 'minor injury' — the kind that turns a beating into a criminal sentence — is assessed is set by forensic standards; this section has not verified them. If the other person is already on the ground or has already run off, the assault has ended; chasing after them to keep hitting is not defense. Carrying a knife, an expandable baton, or a stun gun for self-protection gets you punished if found in an ordinary check; see section 9, item 26 (don't buy a baton or stun gun for self-defense).
Sources (3 references)

11

Against assault you can't escape, fighting back is allowed — but only against the one attacking, and stop when they stop

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: a lotTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

While someone is attacking you or another person, if you step in to stop them and injure them, you bear no criminal liability. If they are in the middle of a violent assault, murder, robbery, rape, or kidnapping, injuring or even killing them is not excessive. But you may only strike the person actively attacking, and you stop when they stop. Even if the final ruling is on your side, you may still first have a case opened against you and spend a few days in custody.

Cost
Lawyer fees start at a few thousand yuan; those in financial difficulty can apply for legal aid. The main cost comes afterwards: you are often first booked for suspected intentional injury, must cooperate with the investigation, and may even be held for a dozen-odd days first. The hard part is keeping your composure through those days.
Benefit
The Criminal Law sets out what counts as justifiable defense. When the state, the public interest, or the personal, property, and other rights of yourself or someone else is under unlawful attack at that moment, stepping in to stop it and injuring the attacker constitutes justifiable defense, with no criminal liability. The same article adds: 'Where justifiable defense clearly exceeds the necessary limits and causes major harm, criminal liability shall be borne, but punishment shall be mitigated or waived.' Another clause: 'Against ongoing assault, murder, robbery, rape, kidnapping, and other violent crimes that gravely endanger personal safety, defensive acts that cause injury or death to the attacker do not constitute excessive defense and carry no criminal liability.' The guiding opinions of the Supreme People's Court, the Supreme People's Procuratorate, and the Ministry of Public Security draw the boundaries more finely. Finding excessive defense requires both 'clearly exceeding the necessary limits' and 'causing major harm'; neither alone suffices. 'Causing major harm' means seriously injuring or killing the attacker; minor and lighter injuries do not count. The attack counts as over only when the attacker has genuinely lost the ability to attack, or has genuinely given up. Defense must be aimed at the attacker personally. Where an unlawful attack is plainly trivial — anyone can see it is only minor — and you stop it outright by means capable of causing serious injury or death, it is not recognized as a defensive act. The procedural cost has official cases. Procuratorate Case No. 47, the Yu Haiming case: on the night of August 27, 2018, the police opened a case for 'intentional injury.' On September 1, the Kunshan public security bureau found justifiable defense under Article 20, paragraph 3, of the Criminal Law and withdrew the case. Procuratorate Case No. 45, the Chen case: a student surrounded and beaten by nine people fought back with a knife, seriously injuring three. The police opened an investigation on suspicion of intentional injury and placed him in criminal detention. The procuratorate found it was justifiable defense and declined to approve arrest; only then did the police release him. Where the police believe arrest is needed after detention, they must submit it to the procuratorate for review and approval within 3 days (the procuratorate decides whether to approve the arrest). Special circumstances allow an extension of 1 to 4 days. Major suspects who committed crimes on the move, repeatedly, or in gangs may have it extended to 30 days. The procuratorate then makes its decision within 7 days (nationwide)
Note
The default move is still what item 10 says: back away and call the police (in a conflict, call the police and keep your hands off). Two people swinging at each other is not defense, and neither is chasing and hitting someone who is down or has run off. Consider fighting back only at the moment you have nowhere left to retreat. Afterwards, three things to do. First, after calling the police, don't leave the scene. Second, secure the surveillance footage and witnesses quickly — the guiding opinions require the police to pull on-site video and audio and interview witnesses first thing. Third, get a lawyer before formal police questioning; see item 5 (get a lawyer when charged). If the case is ultimately withdrawn, not prosecuted, or you are acquitted, the days you were held can be claimed as state compensation by the day; see item 35 (state compensation after detention). Defending someone else is equally lawful. But wading bare-handed into a fight between strangers carries separate risks; see section 13, item 37 (coming upon a group brawl). The main beneficiaries of this item are yourself and your family.
Sources (4 references)

Guiding Opinions on Lawfully Applying the Justifiable Defense System (Fa Fa [2020] No. 31, Articles 5, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 14, and 19). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/251611.html; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2018). Twelfth Batch of Guiding Cases (Procuratorate Case No. 45, the Chen justifiable defense case; Procuratorate Case No. 47, the Yu Haiming justifiable defense case). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/jczdal/201812/t20181219_402920.s…; NPC Standing Committee (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 amendment, Article 91). Full text reposted by the People's Procuratorate of the Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region https://www.nx.jcy.gov.cn/zwsy/qwfb/202011/t20201119_608817…
12

Whoever wrongs you — unpaid wages, wrongful firing, cheated money — go through complaints, arbitration, and lawsuits; don't go settle scores in person

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Take the legal route and the worst case is you don't get the money back. Take revenge and you still don't get the money back — and you pay with your life. The Wuxi case: Xu Moujin, denied his diploma and unhappy with his internship pay, went on a knife attack that killed 8 and wounded 17; he was sentenced to death, and the sentence has been carried out. For unpaid wages, the complaint-and-arbitration route recovered 8.65 billion yuan for 654,000 people nationwide in 2024.

Cost
Costs nothing; complaints and arbitration are both free. It takes a trip or two and a few months of waiting. The hard part is holding off from taking matters into your own hands during those months.
Benefit
The legal route has official numbers. In 2024, labor inspection nationwide investigated and handled 137,000 cases and recovered 8.65 billion yuan in wages for 654,000 people. Another 998 people were convicted of the crime of refusing to pay labor remuneration. For how to complain to labor inspection about unpaid wages and how to apply for labor arbitration, see section 7, item 2. The price list for the revenge route is written in Article 232 of the Criminal Law: 'whoever intentionally kills another shall be sentenced to death, life imprisonment, or fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years; in lesser circumstances, fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 3 but not more than 10 years.' Official case: Xu Moujin failed his exams, did not receive his diploma, and was unhappy with his internship pay. On November 16, 2024, he returned to the Wuxi Institute of Arts and Technology and attacked people with a knife, killing 8 and injuring 17. At first instance he was sentenced to death for intentional homicide and deprivation of political rights for life; the Supreme People's Court approved the sentence, and it was carried out on January 20, 2025. His grievance was with the school and that pay — but the victims were his fellow students, and he never got a cent of that pay (nationwide)
Note
Interns still in school generally don't count as having formed a labor relationship with the employer. If internship pay can't be recovered, the only options are asking the school to step in or suing in court — labor arbitration is not available. If you're owed money for private work done for a household or an individual, that likewise means going to court; see section 7, item 22 (first figure out who actually employs you). For exactly how to complain and arbitrate unpaid wages, see section 7, item 2. For the red lines in debt collection, see section 9, item 15 (collect debts without seizing or confining anyone). The legal route may still fail to recover the money — a closed case doesn't mean the money arrived. Take revenge and you still don't get the money back, and you pay with your life.

No matter the rage, never attack uninvolved people: driving into crowds or attacking in public is convicted as endangering public safety by dangerous means — 3 years minimum, death penalty if someone dies

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Driving into crowds or attacking people in public places is convicted as endangering public safety by dangerous means. Even if you don't injure a single person, it starts at 3 years. With deaths, it's 10 years or more, life, or death. The Zhuhai case: Fan Weiqiu, unhappy with his divorce property split, drove into a crowd exercising at the sports center, killing 35 and injuring 43; he was sentenced to death, and the sentence has been carried out.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is crushing the impulse while you're in a rage.
Benefit
Article 114 of the Criminal Law: 'whoever commits arson, breaches dikes, causes explosions, releases toxic, radioactive, or infectious-disease pathogens and the like, or endangers public safety by other dangerous means, where serious consequences have not yet been caused, shall be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 3 but not more than 10 years.' Even if not one person is hurt, it starts at 3 years. Article 115: causing serious injury or death, or major losses to public or private property, is punishable by fixed-term imprisonment of not less than 10 years, life imprisonment, or death. Official case: Fan Weiqiu, his marriage broken and his life adrift and unhappy with the outcome of the divorce property split, 'resolved to vent his private rage by driving into a crowd.' On the evening of November 11, 2024, he drove into the crowd exercising at the Zhuhai Sports Center, killing 35 and injuring 43. At first instance he was sentenced to death for endangering public safety by dangerous means and deprivation of political rights for life; the Supreme People's Court approved the sentence, and it was carried out on January 20, 2025. The people he struck were runners he had never met (nationwide)
Note
'I don't want to live anyway' earns no discount at sentencing. The Supreme People's Court's 2025 work report puts it this way for such cases: 'for the most heinous offenders who challenge the bottom lines of law and morality, punish firmly, severely, and swiftly according to law.' Even just making the threat is already illegal. Threatening to commit arson, explode bombs, poison, or other acts endangering public safety, in a way that throws public order into confusion, draws 5 to 10 days of detention and a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. Writing threatening letters, or otherwise threatening another person's personal safety, is likewise illegal: up to 5 days of detention, or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan (Public Security Administration Punishments Law effective January 1, 2026). If your thoughts have reached this point, see item 14 (treat thoughts like 'find someone to take along' as an emergency).

Thoughts like 'find someone to take along' or 'we go down together' are an emergency: leave the scene, hand your car keys and knives to someone else, call 12356

Grade BValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

From the moment such a thought appears to the moment of action, the window is short. Of 82 suicide-attempt survivors, 47.6% said no more than 10 minutes passed from the first thought to the act. So the task is not to 'think your way through it' — it is to put one step of distance between yourself and the steering wheel, the knives, the gas valve, and the rope, and ride out those ten minutes. Then call 12356.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is admitting you are not all right right now, and handing the items over to someone else.
Benefit
The window from such thoughts to action is short. In interviews with 82 suicide-attempt survivors within three days of hospital admission, 47.6% said no more than 10 minutes passed from the first thought to the act. A 10-year systematic review (which pooled and combed through a decade of research) holds that the evidence for restricting lethal means keeps strengthening. After painkillers were brought under control, suicides involving them fell 43%. After jump hotspots were fitted with barriers, suicides fell 86% (79% to 91%). Putting one step of distance between yourself and the steering wheel, the knives, the gas valve, and the rope buys exactly those ten minutes. 12356 is the nationwide unified psychological assistance hotline, answering calls no fewer than 18 hours a day (nationwide, from May 1, 2025)
Note
Grade B because both pieces of evidence come from the literature on suicide; there is no direct research applying them to 'the urge to hurt other people.' The Deisenhammer study had only 82 people and was done at a single hospital. When you are in a bad state, do not drive, and do not take shifts in which other people's safety depends on you — hand the shift over first. For thoughts of hurting yourself, see section 1, item 25 (call 12356 when suicidal thoughts arise). For what to do first when you feel low, see section 3, item 18.
Sources (3 references)
Deisenhammer EA et al. (2009). The duration of the suicidal process: how much time is left for intervention between consideration and accomplishment of a suicide attempt? Journal of Clinical Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.4088/JCP.07m03904; Zalsman G et al. (2016). Suicide prevention strategies revisited: 10-year systematic review. Lancet Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(16)30030-X; National Health Commission (2024). 15

If someone close says 'no one gets to live well' or 'I'll take the kids with me,' don't brush it off as venting: close relatives can have them taken straight in for evaluation, and police must act on reports

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

When a family member says 'no one gets to live well' or 'I'll take the kids with me,' close relatives can take them straight to a hospital, and the hospital may not refuse to evaluate them. Where they have already acted, or trouble is clearly imminent, hospitalization does not need their own consent. If you can't tell venting from the real thing, call 12356 to ask first, or report to 110 and have the police come. Covering for them is not helping them.

Cost
Registration and consultation fees run from tens to a few hundred yuan. Accompanying them to the hospital takes half a day to a day. The hard part is talking them into coming with you.
Benefit
Article 28, paragraph 2, of the Mental Health Law states: 'where a person suspected of having a mental disorder harms themselves or endangers others' safety, or where there is a danger of harm to self or to others' safety, their close relatives, their employer, or the local public security organ shall immediately take measures to stop it and take them to a medical institution for diagnosis of the disorder.' The same article provides: 'a medical institution that receives a person suspected of a mental disorder brought in this way may not refuse to diagnose them.' Article 29 requires the hospital to keep such a brought-in person in hospital, immediately assign a licensed psychiatrist to diagnose, and issue its conclusion promptly. Article 30 makes hospital treatment voluntary in principle. But there is one exception: where the diagnosis shows a severe mental disorder and the person 'has already endangered others' safety, or poses a danger to others' safety.' For this category, inpatient treatment shall be imposed and does not require the person's consent. Threatening to hurt someone can itself be reported straight to 110. Writing threatening letters, or otherwise threatening another person's personal safety: up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. Threatening crimes that endanger public safety — arson, explosion, releasing dangerous substances — in a way that throws public order into confusion: 5 to 10 days of detention plus a fine of up to 1,000 yuan (nationwide; Public Security Administration Punishments Law effective January 1, 2026)
Note
On the beneficiary basis, this item counts the spouse, parents, and children living with you. 'No one gets to live well' usually includes you, and the law gives the power to have someone brought in precisely to close relatives — an outsider who wants to intervene cannot; they can only call the police. Use the bring-in only for genuine danger signals: angry words in a quarrel do not count, and you cannot use it to lock a disobedient family member in a hospital. The same law also says: if a further examination or an expert evaluation finds the person does not have a severe mental disorder, the hospital may not keep them in (Article 35). If you cannot tell, call 12356 to ask first, or report to 110 and have the police come. The Germanwings Flight 9525 investigation concluded that the authorities and the employer had no way to take any measure to stop the co-pilot from flying that day. The reason: 'neither he himself nor any other person — doctors, colleagues, or family — had informed them.' All 150 people aboard died: 2 pilots, 4 cabin crew, and 144 passengers.

Online: no insults, no rumors, no forwarding unverified claims; if cyberbullied, preserve evidence before reporting to police

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Publicly insulting someone or spreading rumors and defamation: up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan; for more serious cases, 5 to 10 days. Severe cases constitute the crimes of insult and defamation, up to 3 years. Forwarding doesn't exempt you. The other way around, when you are the one cyberbullied, insult and defamation are in principle crimes you must take to court yourself, so screenshots, screen recordings, and saved links depend on you alone.

Cost
Costs nothing. Think ten extra seconds before posting. When attacked, screenshot and record the screen, save links and account IDs, complain to the platform first, then report to the police. The hard part is not firing back when you're being flamed.
Benefit
Publicly insulting another person or fabricating facts to defame them: up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan; more serious cases, 5 to 10 days. Repeatedly sending insulting or threatening messages, pestering, hounding, and stalking, or secretly filming and spreading someone's private life: punished the same way. Deliberately spreading rumors that throw public order into confusion: 5 to 10 days of detention. Severe cases constitute the crimes of insult and defamation, up to 3 years. For online defamation, where the victim has difficulty collecting evidence, they can ask the court to require the police to assist (nationwide; Public Security Administration Punishments Law effective January 1, 2026)
Note
The two crimes of insult and defamation are in principle 'handled only upon complaint' — you must take them to court yourself. The police generally do not open a case on their own, so the evidence is yours to build. But there are two exceptions. One: 'except where social order and the interests of the state are seriously harmed' — the police may handle those directly (Article 246, paragraph 2, of the Criminal Law). Two: for online defamation where you genuinely have difficulty collecting evidence, the court may require the police to help investigate (paragraph 3 of the same article, added by Criminal Law Amendment IX). Forwarding still carries liability — knowingly passing on something false likewise counts as 'fabricating facts.' For what to do after you are cyberbullied, see item 37 of this section (cyberbullied: secure the evidence first, then choose your route). The article number for insult and defamation moved from Article 42 of the old law to Article 50 of the new one.

17

Read the whole document before signing; never sign on someone's behalf; never sign a blank sheet

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Once signed, it counts — a thumbprint counts exactly like a signature. 'I didn't read it carefully' and 'I thought it was something else' basically won't hold up in court. So spend a few extra minutes reading it start to finish, ask on the spot about anything you don't understand, and photograph it for your records. Never sign for someone else, never sign a blank sheet, and write the purpose clearly on any photocopy of your ID card. Electronic signatures and face-scan confirmations count as signing all the same.

Cost
Costs nothing. A few extra minutes to read contracts, IOUs, guarantee letters, and onboarding paperwork start to finish. Ask on the spot about anything unclear, then photograph it for your records. The hard part is reading it all slowly right in front of the other party.
Benefit
A lawfully formed contract is protected by law and binds both signing parties. Once you sign, you must perform in full as agreed. Article 490 of the Civil Code states that where a contract is made in the form of a contract document, it 'is formed when both parties sign, seal, or press a fingerprint.' Thumbprint, signature, and seal are three parallel methods; with a thumbprint alone the contract is just as formed. 'I didn't read it carefully' and 'I thought it was something else' are very hard to sustain in court. Don't sign, and you won't carry debts and obligations that were never yours (nationwide)
Note
'Never sign for others, never sign a blank sheet, state the purpose on ID copies' are rules of thumb with no single official document behind them. Their purpose is the same: don't let your signature be pieced into a contract that is legally formed and that you will have no choice but to honor. Electronic signatures and face-scan confirmations count as signing all the same. For an acquaintance asking you to lend your face or your signature for a loan, see item 45 (lending your face).
Sources (1 reference)
NPC (2020). Civil Code (Articles 465, 490, and 509). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
18

Write an IOU when lending money; before guaranteeing a loan for someone, ask yourself whether you'd willingly repay it for them

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The IOU must be complete: lender, borrower, amount, interest rate, term, repayment method, and both signatures. Move the money by transfer, never cash — a complete IOU is what makes suing feasible. When guaranteeing for someone, look carefully for the words 'joint liability.' With an ordinary guarantee, the creditor must first sue the borrower and fail to recover through enforcement before it's your turn. Sign a joint-liability guarantee and the creditor can come straight after you.

Cost
Costs nothing. One sheet of paper stating the lender, borrower, amount, interest rate, term, and repayment method, with both signatures. Move the money by transfer so there's a trail — never cash.
Benefit
A loan contract shall be in written form and generally covers the type of loan, the currency, the purpose, the amount, the interest rate, the term, and the repayment method. Only when it is complete can you sue on it. Where a guarantee contract does not specify which form of guarantee applies, or states it unclearly, it counts as an ordinary guarantee. An ordinary guarantor can wait: the creditor must first sue or go to arbitration, then apply to enforce against the borrower's assets, and only if enforcement still comes up short does it fall to you to repay for them. The other way round, once you have signed a 'joint liability guarantee' there is no such protection — the creditor can come straight to you (nationwide)
Note
For money you lend, the court doesn't protect the portion of interest beyond 4 times the LPR; see section 7. Writing the ID number on the IOU and labeling it 'loan' are rules of thumb. Whether the guarantee letter carries the words 'joint liability' decides whether you stand behind the borrower or beside him facing the debt collector — read it carefully before signing. For when they say you'll be the guarantor but the contract you actually sign is the loan itself, see item 45 (the borrower is you, not a guarantor).
Sources (1 reference)
NPC (2020). Civil Code (Articles 668, 681, 686, and 687). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
19

Claims have deadlines: 3 years for civil lawsuits, 1 year for labor arbitration; once past, a single 'you're out of time' from the other side ends it

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The civil litigation limitation period is 3 years, counted from the day you knew your rights were harmed. Past the deadline, the court will not raise it on its own, but one line from the other side in court — 'you're past the time limit' — is enough: the money still exists; you just can't get it back. Meanwhile, one dated demand-for-payment message restarts the 3 years from zero. Labor disputes run on a separate clock: the arbitration time limit is 1 year.

Cost
Costs nothing. Don't chase debts only in your head — leave a trail by WeChat, SMS, email, or registered mail.
Benefit
The Civil Code provides that 'the limitation period for applying to the people's court for protection of civil rights is three years.' It runs 'from the date the right holder knew or should have known that the right was harmed and who the obligor is' — from the day you knew you had been wronged and whom to pursue. The maximum is 20 years from the day the right was harmed. Once the period has run out, 'the obligor may raise the defense of non-performance.' The court will not dig into the time limit on its own, but the moment the other side raises it in court it takes effect — the money still exists; you just can't get it back. Four things interrupt the time limit, and once interrupted the 3 years are counted anew. One: you demand that the person who owes you perform. Two: they agree to perform. Three: you file suit or apply for arbitration. Four: other circumstances with the same effect. Where repayment in installments was agreed, the clock runs from the day the last installment falls due. Four kinds of claims are not subject to the time limit: demands to stop the infringement, remove the obstruction, and eliminate the danger; recovery of your own real estate and of your registered movables; child support, elder support, and spousal support; and other circumstances provided by law. Labor disputes run on a separate clock: the arbitration time limit is 1 year, from the date you knew or should have known your rights were harmed. But 'where a dispute over withheld labor remuneration arises while the labor relationship continues, a worker's application for arbitration is not subject to the arbitration time limit in the first paragraph of this article; however, once the labor relationship has terminated, the application must be made within one year from the date of termination' (nationwide)
Note
This is probably the cheapest thing in the whole book: one dated demand-for-payment message restarts the 3 years; doing nothing can forfeit your right to win the lawsuit. Agreeing in advance that 'I won't invoke the time limit' doesn't count, and the two sides agreeing to lengthen or shorten the 3 years doesn't count either. Conversely, once the period has run out, if the other side still agrees to repay, they can no longer refuse to pay by invoking the time limit. What has already been repaid voluntarily cannot be taken back either. For IOUs and guarantees, see item 18 (IOUs and guarantees). For the enforcement stage, see item 20 (declare assets truthfully when sued or under enforcement). Overtime pay and unused annual-leave pay go through labor arbitration; see section 19, items 1 and 2.
Sources (2 references)
NPC (2020). Civil Code (Articles 188, 189, 192, 193, 195, 196, and 197). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; NPC Standing Committee (2007). Labor Dispute Mediation and Arbitration Law (Article 27). https://rsj.ankang.gov.cn/Content-2150407.html (reposted by the Ankang Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau)

Sued or under enforcement? Declare your assets truthfully and repay what you can; don't move your house or money to relatives, friends, or a company

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Putting the house under a company's name or moving money to relatives and friends is exactly what the crime of refusing to comply with judgments spells out: up to 3 years, or 3 to 7 years in especially serious cases. Relatives, friends, and companies that help hide money or process transfers count as accomplices, and the money is recovered all the same. Refusing to report or falsely reporting assets: individuals can be fined up to 100,000 yuan and detained 15 days. Genuinely having no money is not this crime.

Cost
Costs nothing. Report your assets as the court requires: what you have now, and what you had in the year before the day you received the enforcement notice. Repay what you can first. If you can't, negotiate a settlement and installments with the applicant for enforcement — that's the creditor.
Benefit
Transferring assets is itself a circumstance that constitutes the crime. The NPC Standing Committee has issued an interpretation of Article 313 of the Criminal Law, listing directly as 'having the ability to comply but refusing, with serious circumstances': 'the person subject to enforcement conceals, transfers, or deliberately destroys property, or transfers property gratuitously or at a plainly unreasonably low price, such that the judgment or ruling cannot be enforced.' Hiding money, moving it, deliberately smashing your own belongings, giving them away, or flogging them off cheap so the judgment cannot be enforced — all of it counts. The 2024 interpretation by the two top bodies (the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate) added ten more items. They include disposing of your own property interests through sham settlements and sham transfers, and buying someone else's property at a plainly unreasonably high price or guaranteeing someone else's debt. All are deliberate ways of hollowing out assets that could repay your debts. The crime of refusing to comply draws up to 3 years; in especially serious cases, 3 to 7 years plus a fine. 'Especially serious' covers these situations: obstructing enforcement through sham litigation, sham arbitration, or sham notarization; mobbing and storming an enforcement scene; besieging, detaining, or beating enforcement officers; and driving the applicant for enforcement to suicide or self-harm by refusing to comply. An outsider who is not a party to the case, who knows the situation and still colludes to help hide money or process transfers, is treated as an accomplice (co-conspirator) in the crime. Property disposed of unlawfully shall be recovered by law, or the person ordered to make restitution. Transferring after the defendant receives notice to respond to the suit but before the judgment takes effect counts the same. On the civil side, for gratuitous transfers and transfers at plainly unreasonably low prices, the creditor can ask the court to revoke the transfer. For refusing to report assets or falsely reporting them, the court may impose a fine — up to 100,000 yuan for an individual — and detention of up to 15 days (nationwide; the SPC and SPP interpretation effective from December 2024)
Note
The online tip of 'putting the house under the company as staff housing and transferring all money to relatives' is not a loophole — it is precisely the gratuitous and sham transfers the interpretation names. The relatives, friends, and companies that help you do it count as accomplices, and the property is recovered all the same. Conversely, genuinely having no money is not this crime. Deciding whether you are 'able to pay but refusing to' first deducts the expenses essential for daily life of you and the family you support. Repay part or all before the procuratorate indicts, with minor circumstances, and the case may go unprosecuted; repay before the first-instance judgment and punishment can be lighter or even waived. For what to do once you're on a list or under a consumption restriction, see item 21 (consumption restriction or dishonesty list). For how to recover after fulfilling your obligations, see section 7, item 19 (starting over after the dishonesty list).

Reposted by the Guizhou Provincial Market Regulation Administration: https://amr.guizhou.gov.cn/zwgk/xxgkml/jcxxgk/zcfg/fl/20240…
21

Under a consumption restriction or on the dishonesty list? First find out which provision you were listed under, and seek correction where possible

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

First work out whether you are under a consumption restriction or on the dishonesty list — these are two different things. Only six circumstances allow listing on the dishonesty list, for a term of 2 years. For seven circumstances such as having fully performed, the court must delete within 3 working days. The consumption restriction bans nine categories of spending — even a seat on a G-series high-speed train counts. What is necessary for living or business can be applied for one at a time.

Cost
Costs nothing. Go to the enforcement court and find out under which provision you were listed. Prepare proof that you have repaid or complied with the judgment (performance records), or prepare guarantee materials. The necessary living or business expense must be applied for one at a time. The hard part is making all those trips and filings yourself.
Benefit
Only six circumstances allow listing on the dishonesty list. One: having the ability to perform but refusing to. Two: obstructing or resisting enforcement with fabricated evidence or violence and threats. Three: evading enforcement through sham litigation, sham arbitration, or concealing and transferring assets. Four: violating the asset reporting system. Five: violating the consumption restriction order. Six: refusing without justified reason to perform a settlement agreement. Where sufficient and effective guarantee has been provided, or the sealed, seized, or frozen assets are enough to satisfy the debt, the court must not list under item one (able to perform but refusing). A person subject to enforcement who is a minor must not be listed. The listing term is 2 years. Obstructing or resisting enforcement with violence and threats in serious circumstances, or multiple dishonest acts, allows a 1-to-3-year extension. For seven circumstances — having fully performed, the settlement agreement fully performed, the court ruling enforcement concluded, and the like — the court must delete within 3 working days. Actively performing or proactively correcting the dishonest conduct allows even earlier deletion. A natural person under consumption restriction may not make nine categories of high-end consumption and spending not necessary for life or work. One: airplane travel, soft-sleeper train berths, or ship cabins above second class. Two: high-end spending at star-rated hotels, nightclubs, and golf courses. Three: buying real estate, or building, extending, or upscale-renovating housing. Four: renting upscale office buildings, hotels, or apartments for an office. Five: buying vehicles not needed for business. Six: travel and vacations. Seven: children attending high-fee private schools. Eight: insurance and wealth-management products bought with high premiums. Nine: any seat on a G-series EMU train, or first class or above on other EMU trains. Where one of these is necessary for living or business, you must apply to the court and may do it only once approved. With genuinely effective guarantee, or with the applicant for enforcement's consent, the court can lift the restriction (nationwide)
Note
The consumption restriction means restricting high-end consumption. The provision came out in 2010 and was amended in 2015 by Fa Shi [2015] No. 17, which changed its name to 'Provisions on ... and Related Consumption'; this item follows the amended text now in force. Three changes in 2015 matter. First, the ninth category was added, covering all seats on high-speed trains. Second, the qualifier 'paid for with their assets' was deleted; the original read 'may not commit the following acts of paying expenses with their assets.' Third, where an organization is under consumption restriction, its actual controller is restricted along with it, but private consumption paid with personal money can be applied for at the enforcement court. The dishonesty list and the consumption restriction are two different things; you may be touched by only one of them. Neither equals a stain on your credit record — deletion from the list does not change your credit report; see section 7, item 19 (starting over after the dishonesty list). Whether spouses and children are restricted when spending money they earned themselves is not stated in the current text; if you run into it, ask the enforcement court.

Scammed in online or second-hand deals? Complain to the platform first, then the police, then weigh whether a lawsuit is worth it

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Go to the platform first. Platforms hold deposits and run penalty rules, so they move fastest. Then report to the police: being scammed out of 3,000 yuan or more clears the case-filing threshold for the crime of fraud; below the criminal standard it's handled as a public-security offense, with 5 to 10 days of detention. If you'll sue, online-shopping disputes can be filed in the court of the place of delivery; small amounts go through small-claims procedure, decided within 2 months, with filing possible entirely online.

Cost
Platform complaints and police reports are free. To sue: for amounts in dispute up to 10,000 yuan, the acceptance fee is 50 yuan, halved again for simplified procedure, mediation, or withdrawal. Filing, the hearing, and enforcement each take at least half a day to a day; online filing saves the legwork. Save the order, chat records, transfer records, and shipping labels. The hard part is not giving up halfway through all the back-and-forth.
Benefit
Fraud of 3,000 yuan up to 10,000 yuan or more constitutes the 'relatively large amount' tier of the crime of fraud: up to 3 years, plus a fine or a fine alone, with each province setting local standards within this range. Below the criminal standard, public-security punishment applies: 5 to 10 days of detention, or a fine of up to 2,000 yuan; more serious cases, 10 to 15 days of detention plus a fine of up to 3,000 yuan. On the civil side, online-shopping contract disputes can be filed in the court of the place of delivery — no need to travel to the seller's location. Where the sum in dispute is at or below 50% of the province's previous-year average annual wage of employed persons, small-claims procedure applies. Small claims are final at first instance (effective as soon as decided, no appeal). Decided within 2 months of filing; simplified procedure takes 3 months. Civil litigation can be conducted on online platforms with the same effect as offline (nationwide; Civil Procedure Law from January 2024, Public Security Administration Punishments Law from January 2026)
Note
To work out whether it's worth suing: take your after-tax hourly wage, multiply by the time it will eat up, and add the court's acceptance fee. Count filing, the hearing, and possibly applying for enforcement at half a day to a day each. Compare the total with the sum you want back, then apply a discount — estimate whether, even if you win, the money can actually be enforced. Whether to sue is your call, based on this arithmetic. After the 2025 revision of the Public Security Administration Punishments Law the article numbers all changed: theft and fraud moved from Article 49 of the old law to Article 58. After the 2023 amendment of the Civil Procedure Law, small claims sit in Article 165. Don't copy old materials on either point. 'Platform complaint first' is experience: platforms hold deposits and run penalty rules, so they move fastest. The procuratorate's webpage does not display the document number for Fa Shi [2011] No. 7; the number awaits checking against the SPC's original page.

23

Large gifts in dating and marriage: think carefully before handing anything over — in principle it can't be clawed back afterwards

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Once the money is handed over, in principle you can't get it back. What you've given away can be freely revoked only before it's transferred into their name. After the transfer completes, it can be revoked only in three situations: the recipient gravely infringes you or your close relatives, they fail to support you when obliged to, or they fail to perform the obligations agreed in the gift contract. So think it through before a large transfer — is this a loan or a gift?

Cost
Costs nothing. Before a large transfer, ask yourself: loan, or gift? If it's a loan, write an IOU and put 'loan' in the transfer memo. The hard part is saying the words out loud.
Benefit
What you've given away can be revoked before it's transferred into their name — the law calls this point the transfer of property rights. Once the transfer or title change completes, only three situations allow revocation: the recipient gravely infringes you or your close relatives; they fail to support you when obliged to; or they fail to perform the obligations agreed in the gift contract. Gifts and cash of modest value given at commemorative moments such as festivals and birthdays, as well as everyday spending to express or deepen affection, do not count as bride price and are not returned on separation as if they were (nationwide)
Note
'Special numbers like 520 and 1314 are usually recognized as gifts' is a common saying in practice; this section found no official SPC text for it and does not treat it as settled. A gift that has been notarized at a notary office cannot simply be revoked on a change of heart. Whether a transfer counts as a loan or a gift comes down, in the end, to evidence — one line in the chat records, 'consider this money a loan for now,' is far more useful than arguing about it afterwards.
