24

Pay bride price by bank transfer with a memo and keep the chat records; money taken under the guise of marriage can be reclaimed

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Using marriage to demand property is forbidden by law, and the courts support returning it. You can demand it back if the marriage was never registered, if it was registered but the two of you truly never lived together, or if the pre-marital bride price left the paying side in genuine hardship. Where the marriage is registered and the couple has lived together, it is generally not returned. So send the bride price, the three golds, and the "Mom and Dad" gift by bank transfer with a memo saying what each is for — whoever paid keeps the evidence, and the rule is the same for men and women.

Cost
Costs nothing. Send the bride price, the three golds, and the "Mom and Dad" gift by transfer, with the purpose spelled out in the memo. For anything agreed aloud, keep a written trail in chat records, or have a family member there to confirm it.
Benefit
The law forbids using marriage to demand property. Where one party took property under the cover of a bride price, the courts support the other side's demand for it back. There are three situations in which it can be demanded back: no marriage registration was completed; registration was completed but the couple truly never lived together; or the pre-marital bride price left the paying side in genuine hardship. Where the couple is registered and has lived together, it is generally not returned. But where the time living together was short and the bride price was excessively high, the court will set the proportion to be returned based on how the money was actually spent, whether there was a dowry, whether there was a pregnancy or birth, and whether either side was at fault. Where the couple never registered but lived together, the same proportional approach applies (nationwide, from February 2024)
Note
Whether a bride price counts as "excessively high" depends on per-capita disposable income where the paying side lives and on that family's circumstances; there is no single national figure. How much must be returned is decided by the judge, case by case. The rules are identical for the paying side and the receiving side: whoever paid keeps the evidence.

Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Book of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Article 5). https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html
25

Pre-marital assets are safe; get adding a name to the deed and parental contributions spelled out first

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Property you own before marriage stays yours; it does not become joint property just because the marriage lasts a long time. Spouses may agree in writing that pre-marital and marital property each stays with its own side. One thing to watch: if you agree to add the other person's name to the house, you can still back out before the ownership change is registered — once registered, it is theirs. In a divorce, a spouse who hid money, moved or squandered assets, or fabricated debts may receive a smaller share or none.

Cost
Writing a property agreement yourself costs nothing; notarization is charged separately. When parents put up money, ask them to write a short statement. The whole thing takes a few hours, once. The hard part is opening the money conversation with your family.
Benefit
Pre-marital property is personal property and does not become joint property just because the marriage lasts. Spouses may agree in writing that pre-marital property and income acquired during the marriage belong to each separately, to both jointly, or partly jointly — and that agreement binds both sides. Where parents fund a home purchase before the marriage, it is deemed a gift to their own child unless clearly stated to be for the two of you. Where parents contribute after the marriage, it is handled per the couple's agreement; with no agreement, under joint-property principles. Where the parties agree before or during the marriage to gift one spouse's property to the other or make it jointly owned, the gifting side may revoke before the change of registration is complete; once registered, it belongs to the other. In a divorce, a spouse who hid, transferred, sold off, or squandered joint property, or fabricated debts, may receive a smaller share or none (nationwide)
Note
A property agreement binds husband and wife equally. To hold it up against debts your spouse owes to outsiders, the creditor must know the agreement exists; if they don't, it cannot touch them. The agreement is valid without notarization — notarization just spares you later wrangling over signatures and dates. For how to spell out in writing whether parental money for a home is a loan or a gift, see Section 10, item 11 (parents funding a home purchase).
Sources (2 references)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1063, 1065, 1092). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Book of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Articles 29, 31, 32). https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html
26

Before marrying, verify the other person's marital status; swindling money under the pretense of marriage is prosecuted as fraud

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A bigamous marriage is void. Marrying while already married, or knowingly marrying someone you know is married, carries up to 2 years. Swindling money under the pretense of marriage is prosecuted as fraud: "relatively large" amounts carry up to 3 years, "huge" amounts 3 to 10 years, "especially huge" amounts 10 or more years, or life. Before registering, take a look at the marital status on the other person's ID card and household register.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before registering, look at the marital status on their ID card and household register. For large movements of money or property, keep the transfer records and chat records.
Benefit
A bigamous marriage is void. Committing bigamy while married, or marrying while knowingly aware that the other person is married, carries up to 2 years. Defrauding public or private property in "relatively large" amounts carries up to 3 years plus a fine. "Huge" amounts carry 3 to 10 years. "Especially huge" amounts carry 10 or more years or life, plus a fine or confiscation of property (nationwide)
Note
"Marriage fraud" is not itself a crime name. Whether it can be handled as fraud depends on whether the person intended from the very start to keep the money, made up lies to get it, and whether the police actually opened a case. What counts as "relatively large" is set by judicial interpretation and can be adjusted locally; this section did not verify it. Marriage fraud victimizes both sexes — there are cases of swindled bride price and of swindled dowry alike.
Sources (2 references)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1051). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Articles 258, 266). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml
27

For home repairs, vehicle inspections, or renovations, ask the price before any work starts and watch the whole time

Grade BValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Appliance repair shops must post their fee schedules, hand over repair receipts and invoices, must not fabricate faults, and must not deliberately replace parts that work fine — serious violations draw fines of up to 30,000 yuan. Every business must display prices clearly and may not charge above the listed price. So before any work starts, ask the price and which parts will be replaced; when it's done, ask for the receipt and invoice, and keep the old parts. If you were overcharged, call 12315 first.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before work starts, ask about the fee schedule and which parts will be replaced; photograph the quote or have them send it in writing. When the work is done, get the repair receipt and invoice, and keep the old parts. You'll also stand by watching for an hour or two. The hard part is staying put the whole time and not walking away.
Benefit
Appliance repair businesses must clearly display the fee standards for services and parts, quality specifications, warranty periods, and complaint hotlines. They must give consumers repair service receipts and itemized invoices, filled in truthfully with the work done. They must not invent, exaggerate, or falsify repair items, must not falsely report faulty parts, and must not deliberately replace parts that still perform. Serious violations draw fines of up to 30,000 yuan. Every business must display prices clearly, may not charge above the listed price, and may not collect any fee not posted. Luring customers in with low prices then settling high, and fake discounts, count as price fraud. Businesses must prominently display the items, content, prices, and pricing method of their services, and must not make false or misleading claims (nationwide)
Note
If you're overcharged, call 12315 first; the penalties are imposed by the commerce and market-regulation authorities — you don't have to fight it out in court yourself. Graded B because although the rules are official, there is no number for "how much watching saves you"; it rests mostly on experience. Ask the price, keep the receipts, keep the old parts — do it with everyone, without judging by appearances. The appliance measure covers appliance repair only; for vehicle inspections and renovations, follow the price-posting rules and their implementation regulations. The higher-level Consumer Rights Protection Law also states these two rights: Article 8 says you may require the business to explain the content, specifications, and cost of the service; Article 10 says you may refuse a forced transaction.
Sources (4 references)
Ministry of Commerce (2012). Measures for the Administration of the Appliance Repair Service Industry (MOFCOM Order No. 7 of 2012, Articles 5, 7, 9, 14). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2231695.htm; State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Provisions on Clear Price Marking and the Prohibition of Price Fraud (SAMR Order No. 56, Articles 5, 8, 19). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5699926.htm; State Council (2024). Implementing Regulations of the Consumer Rights Protection Law (State Council Decree No. 778, Articles 9, 10). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202403/content_6940159…; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2013 amendment). Consumer Rights Protection Law (Articles 8, 10): "Consumers have the right, depending on the nature of the goods or services, to require business operators to provide ... information on the content, specifications, and costs of services"; "the right to refuse a business operator's forced transactions." https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf767… (National Laws and Regulations Database)
28

Don't be a 'name-only' legal representative; don't lend your ID card for registering a company

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The law presumes the legal representative is the one actually running the show; "I was just lending my name, I knew nothing" is no defense. If the legal representative causes harm to others while performing duties, the company pays first — and after paying it can come back for the money from you, if you were at fault. Already carrying a name-only post? The Company Law lets you resign, and the company must designate a new legal representative within 30 days.

Cost
Costs nothing. When someone asks you to "just lend your name, you won't have to do anything," refuse.
Benefit
The legal representative is to be a director or manager who actually conducts the company's affairs; the law presumes you are the one in charge. If the legal representative causes harm to others in performing duties, the company pays first, and after paying it may seek recovery from the at-fault legal representative (take the money back from them). Directors and senior managers owe the company duties of loyalty and diligence (faithful to the company, conscientious in their work). Where they cause harm in performing duties and acted intentionally or with gross negligence, they pay out of their own pocket too. "I didn't know" is not, in law, a way out of liability (nationwide, from July 2024)
Note
The Company Law text itself only settles who bears responsibility. The more common consequences of a name-only post: when the company is in court enforcement, the legal representative is restricted from high consumption along with it, and tax and administrative penalties can also reach you. These consequences come from other laws and enforcement rules whose original texts this section did not verify — hence grade B. Already carrying the title? The Company Law lets you resign, and the company must designate a new legal representative within 30 days. For lending your name to a loan, see item 45 (lending your face).
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023). Company Law (2023 revision, Articles 10, 11, 180, 191). https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm
29

Crossing borders: don't carry anything for strangers; don't receive packages of unknown origin

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The Ministry of Foreign Affairs' consular affairs department advises citizens going abroad: do not carry luggage or items for other people, especially prohibited goods or anything you don't really know. If drugs or smuggled goods really are found in your luggage, "I didn't know what was inside" is something you must prove yourself. The same goes for receiving packages for others at home, especially when they ask you to pay first and reimburse you later.

Cost
Costs nothing. Just refuse.
Benefit
The MFA consular affairs department's advice to citizens going abroad is "be sure to avoid carrying luggage or items for others, especially prohibited items or items you know nothing about." The point is to keep you from unknowingly carrying prohibited goods for someone else and taking on the legal responsibility for it. When drugs or smuggled goods are found in your luggage, "I didn't know what was inside" is yours to prove
Note
The official advisory pages of the General Administration of Customs and the Ministry of Public Security on this matter would not open, so this item cites only the MFA consular affairs page. And the original gives principles, not legal provisions — hence grade B. The same applies to receiving domestic packages for others, especially when asked to pay up front and be reimbursed afterwards.
Sources (1 reference)

30

Dogs must be leashed: off-leash incidents carry no-fault liability (you pay whether or not you were careless), and pay in full

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

If your dog hurts someone, in principle you pay whether or not you were at fault. Only by proving the injured person acted deliberately or was grossly negligent can you pay less or nothing. And if you broke the rules by not leashing, the only mitigator left is "the injured party acted deliberately" — going off-leash boards up your only escape. If a banned fierce dog hurts someone, there is no exemption at all.

Cost
A leash costs a few dozen yuan. The hard part is remembering it every single time you go out.
Benefit
If an animal you keep hurts someone, the keeper or whoever was minding it at the time must pay — the law calls it tort liability. Only where the injured person deliberately provoked the animal or was grossly negligent may you pay nothing or less. Where management rules are violated and safety measures not taken — the dog should have been leashed and wasn't — the only mitigator left is "the injured party acted deliberately." Where a prohibited fierce dog hurts someone, no ground for exemption exists
Note
Compensation for a dog bite covers medical costs, lost wages, the rabies vaccine, and immunoglobulin; a single incident often runs past 10,000 yuan. Serious injuries, or injuries to a child, push the number higher. Abandoning the dog doesn't shed responsibility: if an abandoned or escaped animal hurts someone during that period, the original keeper is still on the hook. What to do after a bite: see Section 13.
Sources (1 reference)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code. Full text republished by the Supreme People's Procuratorate. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml Article 1245: "Where a kept animal causes harm to another person, the animal's keeper or manager shall bear tort liability; however, where it can be proven that the harm was caused by the injured party's intent or gross negligence, liability may be waived or reduced." Article 1246: "Where management provisions are violated and safety measures are not taken for the animal, causing harm to another person, the animal's keeper or manager shall bear tort liability; however, where it can be proven that the harm was caused by the injured party's intent, liability may be reduced." Article 1247: "Where a dangerous animal such as a prohibited fierce dog causes harm to another person, the animal's keeper or manager shall bear tort liability." Article 1249: where an abandoned or escaped animal causes harm during that period, the original keeper or manager bears responsibility
31

If they're drunk to the point of semi-consciousness, asleep, or possibly under 14, don't have sex

Grade BValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Someone drunk into unclear consciousness or asleep cannot consent; sex at that point legally counts as rape, with a base sentence of 3 to 10 years. Afterwards you will almost never be able to prove they consented. The only dependable move is not to have sex: when the party breaks up, hand the person to their own friends or family. On determining age, see Section 9, item 18 (under 14).

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is stopping things right then. The hard part is stopping in the moment.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 236: raping a woman by violence, coercion, or other means carries 3 to 10 years' imprisonment. "Other means" is not limited to physical force — when the other person's consciousness is clouded or they are asleep, they cannot consent effectively, and that falls within "other means." Raping a woman in vile circumstances, raping several women, and the like carry 10 or more years' imprisonment, life imprisonment, or the death penalty. The same article provides that sex with a girl under 14 is treated as rape and punished more heavily; on how a girl's age is determined, see Section 9, item 18 (under 14). A public-education article from the Beijing Xicheng District Procuratorate says that sexually assaulting a woman "after drugging or getting her drunk likewise constitutes rape." The key is "whether the victim's true inner will was violated"; whether the victim resisted at the time "is not the crux." Criminal Law Article 237 covers forcible indecency: forcibly committing indecent acts on another person by violence, coercion, or other methods carries up to 5 years' imprisonment or criminal detention (nationwide)
Note
Graded B because the statute says only "other means" and nothing more specific. "Getting her drunk still counts as rape" comes from a procuratorate public-education article, not a judicial interpretation. The rape statute's text speaks only of women. A man violated this way is pursued as forcible indecency — so whichever sex the other person is, hands off. If you are the one victimized, what to do first is in Section 13, item 42 (after a sexual assault). When you yourself drink to blackout, the risk of being accused and the risk of being blackmailed exist at the same time — see item 32 of this section (when they come for money with leverage, call the police).
Sources (3 references)
National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 236). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml; National People's Congress (2020 amendment). Criminal Law (Article 237). https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index… (integrated text republished by the Beijing Traffic Management Bureau); Beijing Xicheng District People's Procuratorate (2018). Why they are no longer silent... https://www.bjjc.gov.cn/c/xicheng/xjjsl/320654084.jhtml
32

After sex or a nude video call, if the other side demands money by threatening to report you, post the photos, or tell your employer: give not a cent, delete not one record, and call the police directly

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Threats like "I'll go to the police" or "I'll send the photos to your employer" to squeeze money out of you are extortion. Give not a cent, delete not one record, and call the police on the spot — pay once and a second demand will follow. If they really do send the photos out, that adds another crime to their own record. Extortion of 2,000 to 5,000 yuan or more carries up to 3 years; 30,000 to 100,000 yuan or more carries 3 to 10 years.

Cost
Costs nothing. Screenshot their account, the chat records, and the payment QR code, and take your phone to the police station. The hard part is resisting the urge to "pay first and make it go away."
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 274: whoever extorts public or private property — where the amount is relatively large or the extortion is repeated — is sentenced to up to three years' imprisonment, criminal detention, or public surveillance, with a fine imposed concurrently or separately. Criminal detention is short-term custody; public surveillance restricts freedom without custody; "with a fine imposed concurrently or separately" means an additional fine, or a fine by itself. A huge amount or other serious circumstances carry three to ten years' imprisonment, plus a fine. An especially huge amount or other especially serious circumstances carry ten or more years' imprisonment, plus a fine. The two high bodies also issued an interpretation: the Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Extortion Cases (Fa Shi [2013] No. 10, effective April 27, 2013). Article 1 of that interpretation sets the three amount tiers. Extorted public or private property valued at 2,000 to 5,000 yuan or more is deemed "relatively large." 30,000 to 100,000 yuan or more is deemed "huge." 300,000 to 500,000 yuan or more is deemed "especially huge." Article 3: extorting three or more times within two years is deemed "repeated extortion" (nationwide). Civil Code Article 1032: no organization or individual may infringe another person's privacy rights by prying, intruding, leaking, or publicizing. Article 1033 forbids disturbing anyone's private peace by telephone, text messages, instant messaging, and the like. So if the other side really does send the photos out, that adds another crime to their own record. The Fujian Provincial Public Security Department's advisory on similar cases puts it this way: "Be sure to preserve the evidence, dial 110 promptly, and never keep transferring money"
Note
The three tiers are set by each province within the ranges the judicial interpretation provides. 2,000 to 5,000 yuan or more counts as "relatively large"; 30,000 to 100,000 yuan or more counts as "huge"; 300,000 to 500,000 yuan or more counts as "especially huge." Which figure applies in your province follows the local standard. Three or more extortions within two years count as "repeated" even if each amount is small. Don't delete the chat records or photos, deactivate the account, or block them and call it done — that deletes your own evidence too; see item 5 of this section (summoned? get a lawyer first; don't delete records). If a case really is opened against you, those same records are the material that proves your side. And don't try to "negotiate payment in installments." Nude-video-call extortion is mostly run by overseas gangs, who screen-record while a trojan reads off your contact list. "Forward it to your family" is a script — the case can still be filed after you report to the police. Being threatened with money over "I'll tell your family you like the same sex" is the same extortion. In Yancheng, Jiangsu, someone lured a man to a meetup through a same-sex dating app and extracted 14,500 yuan this way; after the victim reported, he was prosecuted — he had already been convicted twice before for the same method. Forcing sex with nude photos is prosecuted as rape. In Xiangshan, Zhejiang, someone obtained nude photos of multiple women by deception on a social platform, then threatened to publish them; ten victims were verified. One reported to the police as soon as the threat arrived — the two had never met — and the procuratorate still handled it as attempted rape, finally indicting for rape and forcible indecency. So don't send nude photos to people you know from the internet. Conversely, if you are the victim seeking compensation from the wrongdoer, a high figure is not extortion — see item 36 of this section (a victim seeking compensation). If photos really do end up online, you can notify the platform to delete them. Civil Code Article 1195 gives you the right to notify the platform to delete, block, or disconnect links; the notice must attach preliminary evidence of the infringement and your real identity information. If the platform fails to act on the notice in time, it and the poster jointly compensate for the aggravated portion of the harm.

33

Falsely reported? You can demand accountability: at the public-security level, detention from 5 days; at the criminal level, up to 3 years

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Fabricating facts to falsely accuse and frame someone, aiming to get them criminally prosecuted or administratively punished, is itself illegal. That draws up to 5 days' detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan; graver cases draw 5 to 10 days. The criminal tier is the crime of false accusation and framing, punishable by up to 3 years. But honest mistakes and wrong reports don't count — to hold them accountable you must prove they meant to frame you.

Cost
Costs nothing. Report to the public security authorities and state that the other side fabricated it. The hard part is producing something that shows it was deliberately made up.
Benefit
The Public Security Administration Punishments Law (revised June 27, 2025, effective January 1, 2026), Article 50, covers false accusation. Fabricating facts to falsely accuse and frame another person, in an attempt to have them criminally prosecuted or administratively punished, is punishable: up to 5 days' detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan; where the circumstances are graver, 5 to 10 days' detention, possibly with a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. Criminal Law Article 243 covers the crime of false accusation and framing. Fabricating facts to falsely accuse another person, intending to have them criminally prosecuted, in serious circumstances, carries up to 3 years' imprisonment, criminal detention, or public surveillance; where serious consequences result, 3 to 10 years. State functionaries who commit the crime in the preceding paragraph are punished more heavily — "more heavily" means toward the severe end within the same sentencing tier. Where there was no intent to frame — a mistaken complaint or an inaccurate report — the preceding two paragraphs do not apply. Honest mistakes and wrong reports are not pursued under these two provisions (nationwide)
Note
To hold the other side accountable, proving "I didn't do it" is not enough — you must also prove they "fabricated facts" and "meant to frame you." The latter is far harder to prove, and accountability may not land. There are no publicly available national statistics on false-accusation case filings and handling for this book to check, so no incidence rate is given, nor any gender breakdown. For building evidence and finding remedies after you yourself are accused, see items 34 and 35 of this section (insufficient evidence should mean acquittal; state compensation).
Sources (2 references)

Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 revision, Article 50). https://gaj.beijing.gov.cn/wsgs/2024zcwj/zcfg/202506/t20250… (full text republished by the Beijing Municipal Public Security Bureau); National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 243). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml
34

Insufficient evidence should mean acquittal anyway, and coerced confessions must be excluded; after a verdict there are still petitions and retrials

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

The bar for conviction is written in the Criminal Procedure Law: the evidence that decides the case must be verified as true through statutory procedures, and the evidence of the whole case, taken together, must exclude reasonable doubt. If it can't, the verdict should be not guilty. Confessions extracted under torture and testimony obtained by violence or threats must be excluded and cannot serve as the basis of a verdict. After a judgment takes effect, you, your legal representative, and your close relatives can still petition.

Cost
The procedures themselves cost nothing, but petitions and retrials eat time. You'll usually need a lawyer; fees start in the thousands of yuan. Those in financial hardship can apply for legal aid — see item 5 of this section (accused? get a lawyer first). The hard part is waiting round after round without giving up.
Benefit
Criminal Procedure Law Article 55: for evidence to be reliable and sufficient it must meet these conditions — the evidence that decides the case has been verified as true through statutory procedures, and, taking all the evidence of the case together, reasonable doubt about the facts found has been excluded. Excluding reasonable doubt means that with all the case's evidence combined, no plausible alternative account of the facts may remain. Article 56: confessions of criminal suspects or defendants collected by unlawful means such as torture, and witness testimony or victim statements collected by violence or threats, shall be excluded. Where evidence that should be excluded is discovered during investigation, review for prosecution, or trial, it shall be excluded according to law and may not serve as the basis for prosecution opinions, prosecution decisions, or verdicts. Article 200, item (3): where the evidence is insufficient to find the defendant guilty, a verdict of not guilty shall be rendered on the grounds that the evidence is insufficient and the charged crime cannot be established. Article 252 opens the petition route. Parties, their legal representatives, and close relatives may petition the people's court or the people's procuratorate against a judgment or ruling that has already taken legal effect — but a petition does not stay the execution of the judgment or ruling. Article 253 lists the circumstances in which the people's court shall retry the case (nationwide)
Note
These are the floors the system writes down; outcomes are not guaranteed. This book has no verifiable official figures on acquittal rates or petition-reversal rates in Chinese criminal cases, so no percentages are given and no individual cases are judged. Three things are in your own hands. First, retain a lawyer right after the first interrogation — see item 5 of this section (accused? get a lawyer first). Second, read the interrogation transcript word by word before signing. Third, don't confess to something you didn't do in order to "get out sooner" — pleading guilty and accepting punishment buys leniency only, not exemption from liability. Where the statutory circumstances are met, the court shall retry the case.
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 amendment, Articles 55, 56, 200, 252, 253). https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml
35

Detained and then the case was withdrawn, dropped, or you were acquitted? Apply for state compensation — paid by the day

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

If you were detained or arrested and the case was then withdrawn, dropped, or ended in acquittal, you can apply for state compensation. Days in custody are compensated by the day: 495.94 yuan per day from May 18, 2026 — about 180,000 yuan a year. Serious consequences draw additional mental-distress compensation on top. No compensation for those who offended but escaped prosecution only because the circumstances were minor; none where the limitation period passed, the offender was under the age of responsibility, or you gave a false confession yourself.

Cost
Costs nothing. Submit the compensation application to the authority that made the original detention, arrest, prosecution, or verdict decision.
Benefit
The State Compensation Law, Article 17, lists the situations in which victims have the right to compensation. First, detention: detention measures taken against a citizen in violation of the Criminal Procedure Law, or lawful detention that exceeded the statutory time limit — followed by a decision to withdraw the case, drop prosecution, or a verdict of not guilty terminating criminal liability. Second, arrest: after arrest measures were taken against a citizen, a decision to withdraw the case, drop prosecution, or a verdict of not guilty terminating criminal liability. Third, retrial: a case retried under trial-supervision procedures and the verdict changed to not guilty, where the original sentence was already served. Trial-supervision procedure is the procedure for taking an already effective judgment back up for review. Article 33: for infringement of a citizen's personal freedom, the daily compensation is computed at the state's average daily wage of employees for the previous year. Article 35: where mental harm is caused, the impact shall be eliminated and reputation restored within the scope affected by the infringement, with an apology; where serious consequences result, corresponding mental-distress compensation shall be paid. Article 19 lists six situations where the state does not pay. One: you deliberately gave false confessions or fabricated other evidence of guilt and were detained or convicted as a result. Two: persons not criminally responsible under Criminal Law Articles 17 and 18 were detained — for instance, below the age of criminal responsibility, or a mental patient causing harm while unable to recognize or control their own conduct. Three: persons whom the Criminal Procedure Law says shall not be pursued criminally were detained — this includes cases where the circumstances are minor and the harm slight, not considered a crime; where the limitation period has passed; or where the suspect has died. It also includes minor offenses where the procuratorate decided not to prosecute — the commonly mentioned relative non-prosecution (also called discretionary non-prosecution). Non-prosecution of a juvenile after the probation period of conditional non-prosecution expires, and non-prosecution after reconciliation with the victim, are likewise included. Four: conduct by case handlers unrelated to the exercise of their powers. Five: harm caused by your own deliberate acts such as self-injury or self-harm. Six: other situations provided by law. The two high bodies' 2015 judicial interpretation on criminal compensation, Article 7, reaffirms: the state does not compensate for the detention of persons not criminally responsible or given relative non-prosecution. But where, after prosecution, the court wrongly sentenced someone to criminal detention, fixed-term imprisonment, or life imprisonment and the sentence was served, the portion of custody continuing after the judgment took effect is still compensated. Article 8 of that interpretation: where the case-handling organ refuses compensation on the grounds of "your own false confession" or "your own self-injury or self-harm," the case-handling organ bears the burden of proof. The Supreme People's Procuratorate issued a notice in May 2026. On May 15, 2026, the National Bureau of Statistics announced that the 2025 average annual wage of employees in urban non-private units nationwide was about 129,000 yuan (129,441 yuan). The average daily wage derived from it is 495.94 yuan. From May 18, 2026, procuratorates at all levels, when making state compensation decisions, compute compensation for infringement of personal freedom at 495.94 yuan per day. The previous standard was 475.52 yuan per day, in effect from May 2025 (nationwide)
Note
This daily standard updates each May with the National Bureau of Statistics' announced prior-year average annual wage for urban non-private units. When you use it, look up the current year's figure rather than quoting this item's. When you receive a non-prosecution decision, first read the basis it states. If it says "no criminal facts" or "insufficient evidence," you can apply for compensation. If it says "minor criminal circumstances," or the limitation period has passed, the days in custody in principle cannot be compensated. If you disagree with a relative non-prosecution decision, you may petition the procuratorate within 7 days of receiving the decision. Mental-distress compensation is set by the case-handling organ according to consequences; there is no uniform formula. The organ that should pay is the one that originally decided to hold you (police, procuratorate, or court) — take it up with them first. Unsatisfied with their handling, apply upward under the State Compensation Law's procedures. To see how it works in practice, look at the compensation decision in the Guo Li case under item 36 of this section (a victim seeking compensation). Guo Li was held 1,826 days. Compensation was computed at the standard for the year the decision was made, not the year he was held — the 2016 national average daily wage of 258.89 yuan. The deprivation-of-personal-freedom portion came to about 473,000 yuan (472,733.14 yuan), with mental-distress compensation of about 165,000 yuan (165,450 yuan) on top. His own claim of 88.88 million yuan in mental-distress compensation for ten years was not supported beyond that amount. Know too what cannot be compensated: that decision classified lost wages, bodily-injury damages, property losses, attorney fees, and detention-center living subsidies as outside the scope of state compensation.
Sources (4 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2012 amendment). State Compensation Law (Articles 17, 19, 33, 35). https://www.stats.gov.cn/gk/tjfg/xgfxfg/202503/t20250306_19… (republished by the National Bureau of Statistics); Supreme People's Procuratorate (2026). The Supreme People's Procuratorate announces the latest compensation standard for infringement of citizens' personal freedom. https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202605/t20260519_727675.…; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2015). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Compensation Cases (Fa Shi [2015] No. 24, Articles 7, 8). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/16409.html; National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 amendment, Articles 16, 177, 181, 284, 290). https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml. Article 19 of the State Compensation Law and this interpretation cite the 2012 Criminal Procedure Law numbering (Article 15; Article 173, paragraph 2; Article 273, paragraph 2; Article 279), which after the 2018 amendment corresponds in order to Article 16, Article 177 paragraph 2, Article 284 paragraph 2, and Article 290
36

As a victim seeking compensation, go through 12315, a lawsuit, or a lawyer; don't meet them alone, and never bind 'you pay me' and 'I won't expose you' into one sentence

Grade BValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

As a victim claiming compensation from the wrongdoer, you are on solid legal ground, and a "high ask" does not automatically become extortion. But the price can be enormous: Guo Li was first sentenced to five years for extortion and only cleared at retrial years later. So use channels that leave a trail, don't go alone to a place they designate to talk, and never say "pay me" and "or I go public" as one condition.

Cost
Costs nothing. Go through 12315, sue in court, or have a lawyer raise it. Record the whole of any meeting. The hard part is resisting the urge to sit down with them one-on-one yourself.
Benefit
Official case: after the authorities announced in 2008 that certain batches of "Shien" brand milk powder contained melamine, testing of Guo Li's daughter showed "several punctate strong echoes visible in the central collecting systems of both kidneys." Guo Li repeatedly sought compensation from the seller and the Shien company, and exposed the matter to the media. In June 2009 the two sides reached an agreement: the Shien company would pay 400,000 yuan in compensation, and Guo Li issued a written statement that he would not pursue the matter further and waived his compensation claims. The company then reported it to the police, and the Chao'an County People's Court sentenced Guo Li to five years' imprisonment for extortion. The Guangdong Provincial People's Procuratorate made a retrial recommendation, holding that "the existing evidence is insufficient to establish that Guo Li subjectively intended illegal appropriation." As the child's statutory guardian, Guo Li "had the right to claim compensation from the milk powder manufacturer, and his claim had a legal basis." The recommendation also stated that "consumers have the right to expose and criticize, through mass media, conduct that harms their lawful rights and interests." On April 7, 2017, the Guangdong High People's Court declared Guo Li not guilty at retrial, on the grounds that "the original trial's finding that Guo Li, with the purpose of illegal appropriation, used threats and coercion to extort property was unclear in fact and insufficient in evidence, and the nature of Guo Li's conduct did not exceed the bounds of a civil dispute." Guo Li was held from July 23, 2009 to July 22, 2014 — 1,826 days (Guangdong, verdict reversed at the 2017 retrial)
Note
Graded B because this is a single case, not a rate you can generalize. It shows two things at once: claiming compensation is itself lawful, and you can still be treated by the police as a case to open and investigate. The lowest-risk route is to hand the claim to a lawyer or sue in court directly, and not meet the other side alone yourself. Be especially careful when they invite you to "talk it out in person" where they live — police reports and case filings usually happen in the other side's home turf. Once a settlement is signed, follow it; raising a new, larger claim afterwards is what is most easily read as "blackmail." For what to do once a case is opened, see items 5, 34, and 35 of this section (get a lawyer first; insufficient evidence should mean acquittal; state compensation). For when the other side demands money while holding leverage over you, see item 32 of this section (they demand money with police reports and photos).
Sources (2 references)
Guangdong Provincial People's Procuratorate (2017). The provincial procuratorate's retrial recommendation reversed the Guo Li case to not guilty. http://www.gd.jcy.gov.cn/jcyw2/201704/t20170411_1975029.shtml (Guangdong Provincial People's Procuratorate official website); Guangdong High People's Court Compensation Committee (2018). State compensation case in which Guo Li applied on grounds of retrial acquittal against the Chaozhou Intermediate People's Court of Guangdong Province ([2018] Yue Wei Pei No. 11). https://www.gdcourts.gov.cn/caipanwenshuxuandeng/caipanwens…
37

Cyberbullied? First switch on protections and preserve evidence, then pick among platform complaint, court injunction, and police report

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

On the spot, do three things: switch on the platform's protection settings, save the content with the one-tap evidence tool, and report it through the quick-report entry. After that you can apply to court for an injunction to make them stop first. You can also sue yourself; if evidence is hard to collect, you can ask the police to assist. Where the consequences are especially severe and the impact vile, the procuratorate prosecutes — you don't have to prove it yourself.

Cost
Costs nothing. On the spot it takes ten-odd minutes to set protections and save evidence. If it gets to applying for an injunction or a private prosecution, you'll be running to court and may need a lawyer. The hard part is saving evidence while being flamed instead of flaming back.
Benefit
Fa Fa [2023] No. 14, Article 15, covers the injunction. Where the right holder has evidence that the actor is committing or is about to commit an unlawful act infringing their personality rights, and failing to stop it promptly will cause irreparable harm to their lawful interests, the people's court may, on an application under Civil Code Article 997, issue a personality-rights infringement injunction — a court order ordering the other side to stop first. Article 11 of that document covers evidence collection. In private prosecution cases, "where the victim has genuine difficulty providing evidence, they may ask the public security organs to assist." The police shall promptly identify the actor and collect evidence materials on how the content spread and its impact. Network service providers shall provide the necessary technical support. "Where evidence has been collected with the assistance of the public security organs and the acceptance conditions for a private prosecution case are met, the people's court shall decide to open the case." Where it cannot be collected, the public security organs shall explain in writing. A private prosecution case is one the victim must bring to court personally. Article 12 of that document lists five situations to be found "seriously endangering social order" under Criminal Law Article 246, paragraph 2. One: causing the victim or their close relatives mental breakdown, suicide, or other grave consequences, with vile social impact. Two: arbitrarily targeting ordinary members of the public, with the information spreading on a large scale and drawing large volumes of vulgar, malicious comments, with vile social impact. Three: insulting or defaming multiple people, or repeatedly spreading such content, with vile social impact. Four: organizing or directing people to spread it in volume across multiple platforms, with vile social impact. Five: others. Article 4 of that document: organizing "human-flesh searches" (doxxing) — unlawfully collecting and publishing citizens' personal information to unspecified members of the public — where the circumstances are serious, is convicted and punished as the crime of infringing citizens' personal information. The Provisions on the Governance of Cyberbullying Information, Article 23, require platforms to offer these protection options: you can block strangers or specific users; you can limit who can see your posts; you can forbid reposts or comments; you can receive private messages only from friends, or reject all private messages. Article 25 requires a one-tap evidence-preservation function. Article 26 requires a prominently placed quick complaint and report entry. Article 15 requires platforms that discover suspected crimes to report them to the public security organs promptly
Note
The order runs by "fast and cheap" first: the platform is fastest and costs least — preserve evidence first, report first. Court is slowest and most expensive; decide last whether to go that far. On all three routes you carry the process costs yourself. For the injunction you apply to the court yourself. Private prosecution means filing at court and gathering the evidence yourself. To have the procuratorate take over and switch to public prosecution, you must hit one of the five situations listed in Article 12 of Fa Fa [2023] No. 14; fall short and you can only sue yourself. Two things not to do. One: don't trade insults — insulting back makes you the one punished under item 16 of this section (online: no insults, no rumors). Two: don't delete the content in your own account — that's evidence. When you can't take any more, call 12356 — see Section 1, item 25. To have the platform delete your personal information, see Section 14, item 8. For being filmed and posted online after helping a stranger, see [docs/When to stop and help a stranger in trouble.md](../docs/遇到陌生人出事该不该停.md).
Sources (3 references)
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, and Ministry of Public Security (2023). Guiding Opinions on Punishing Cyberbullying Crimes and Violations According to Law (Fa Fa [2023] No. 14, Articles 4, 11, 12, 15). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/412992.html; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 997). Full text republished by the Supreme People's Procuratorate https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Culture and Tourism, and National Radio and Television Administration (2024). Provisions on the Governance of Cyberbullying Information (Articles 15, 23, 25, 26; effective August 1, 2024). State Council Gazette https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11526/202408/content_…

The 'buy insurance on them first, then act' route is legally blocked end to end: you get none of the money, and intentional homicide plus insurance fraud are punished cumulatively

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

All four doors are shut. Taking out death-contingent insurance on a family member behind their back makes the contract void. If the policyholder deliberately causes the insured's death, the insurer pays nothing. Whoever deliberately kills the decedent forfeits the right to inherit. The Criminal Law lists this insurance fraud as its own item, punished cumulatively with intentional homicide — up to the death penalty. You get not a cent of the money.

Cost
Costs nothing.
Benefit
Insurance Law Article 34: a contract that makes death the condition for paying insurance benefits is void unless the insured consented to it and acknowledged the insured amount. The insured is the person being covered. Parents insuring their minor children are not subject to this restriction. Article 39: when the policyholder designates a beneficiary, the insured's consent is required. The policyholder is the one who pays the premiums; the beneficiary is the one who collects after an incident. Article 43 covers deliberate harm. Where the policyholder deliberately causes the insured's death, disability, or illness, the insurer bears no obligation to pay benefits; where the policyholder has paid premiums for two full years or more, the cash value is refunded to the other right holders. Where a beneficiary deliberately causes the insured's death, disability, or illness, or deliberately attempts to kill the insured, that beneficiary forfeits the right to benefit. Article 27, paragraph 2: where the policyholder or the insured deliberately creates the insured event, the insurer may rescind the contract and bears no liability to compensate or pay; except as provided in Article 43, premiums are not refunded. Civil Code Article 1125: whoever deliberately kills the decedent forfeits the right to inherit. Criminal Law Article 198, paragraph 1, item 5, lists "the policyholder or beneficiary deliberately causing the insured's death, disability, or illness to defraud insurance money" as insurance fraud. Relatively large amounts carry up to 5 years, plus a fine of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. Huge amounts carry 5 to 10 years. Especially huge amounts carry 10 or more years. Paragraph 2: where such conduct also constitutes another crime, punishment follows the rules on cumulative punishment for multiple crimes — several crimes counted together in one sentence. Article 232: intentional homicide carries the death penalty, life imprisonment, or 10 or more years' imprisonment. The case is the Zhang Mousong case in Xuancheng, Anhui. In the early hours of July 18, 2016, he drove his car into a pond and his wife drowned. Less than half a month before, he had taken out 4 policies on her, 1 million yuan each. He was arrested on July 25. The court, punishing cumulatively for intentional homicide and insurance fraud, sentenced him to death with a two-year reprieve, plus a 50,000 yuan fine
Note
This item's beneficiary is you yourself; what it avoids is the death penalty or life imprisonment. The case's casualties and verdict are taken from the procuratorate's published typical-case text; the main text adds no details beyond what that record covers. Insurance fraud that doesn't involve loss of life — staged accidents, inflated losses — is also a crime, accomplices who help fake testimony included; see Section 9, item 21 (staging accidents and inflating losses for claims). Buying insurance for your family is normal in itself; what to guard against is the thought "get the insurance, then act." Urges to harm a family member are treated as an emergency — see items 14 and 15 of this section (when the urge surfaces on its own; when someone close voices it)
Sources (4 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015 amendment). Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, Articles 27, 34, 39, 43. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4…; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, Article 1125. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (consolidated text as amended by Amendment XI), Articles 198 and 232. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181796a636a0179822a19…; Legal Daily, republished by the Anhui Provincial People's Procuratorate (2020-01-13). Wife-killing insurance fraud unravels into a case within a case (an Anhui Provincial People's Procuratorate typical case of civil false-litigation supervision). http://www.ah.jcy.gov.cn/jczt/jjslhyqkjc/mtjj/202001/t20200…

When reporting a case, get the case-acceptance receipt on the spot; if no case is filed, demand written notice: apply for reconsideration within 7 days and for review within a further 7; the procuratorate can order the police to open a case

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

When you report a case, get the case-acceptance receipt on the spot — it's the only proof you ever reported. If the police decide not to open a case, they must give you a written notice of non-filing. If you disagree, apply for reconsideration within 7 days; still disagree, apply for review within a further 7 days. You can also go to the procuratorate and ask it to supervise the police into opening the case.

Cost
Costs nothing. Ask one extra question on the spot and get the case-acceptance receipt in hand. Then chase progress against the dates above. The hard part is asking, again and again.
Benefit
The Provisions on Procedures for Public Security Organs Handling Criminal Cases (as amended by MPS Order No. 159), Article 171, covers the case-acceptance receipt. The text reads: "When accepting a case, public security organs shall prepare a case-acceptance registration form and a case-acceptance receipt, and shall hand the receipt to the person who seized and delivered the offender, the person reporting the case, the complainant, or the informant." Article 174: "Cases accepted, or crime clues discovered, shall be reviewed promptly by the public security organs." Article 178 covers whether to file. After review of an accepted case, where criminal facts requiring criminal liability are believed to exist and the matter falls within its jurisdiction, the case is filed upon approval by the responsible official of a public security organ at or above county level. A refusal to file still earns you a piece of paper: "For cases with a complainant, where a decision is made not to file, the public security organ shall prepare a written notice of non-filing and deliver it to the complainant within three days." Article 179 covers what to do if you disagree. The text reads: "A complainant who disagrees with a non-filing decision may apply for reconsideration to the public security organ that made the decision within seven days of receiving the notice of non-filing; the public security organ shall decide within thirty days of receiving the reconsideration application." It continues: "A complainant who disagrees with the reconsideration decision may apply for review to the public security organ at the next higher level within seven days of receiving the reconsideration decision; the next higher organ shall decide within thirty days of receiving the review application. Where a higher public security organ revokes a non-filing decision, the lower organ shall execute it." For major or complex cases, the reconsideration and review time limits may be extended, but "by no more than thirty days, with written notice to the applicant." Criminal Procedure Law Article 112: where criminal facts requiring criminal liability are believed to exist, the case shall be filed; where not filed, "the reasons for not filing shall be communicated to the complainant. If the complainant disagrees, they may apply for reconsideration." Article 113: "Where a victim believes the public security organ failed to open a case for a matter that should be investigated, and raises it with the people's procuratorate, the procuratorate shall require the public security organ to explain why no case was opened. Where the procuratorate finds the reasons untenable, it shall notify the public security organ to open a case, and upon receiving the notice the public security organ shall open the case." The Provisions on Procedures for Public Security Organs Handling Administrative Cases, Article 61, carries the same requirement. Cases within the unit's jurisdiction "shall be investigated and handled immediately, with a case-acceptance registration form and case-acceptance receipt prepared and the receipt handed to the person reporting the case, the complainant, the informant, or the person who seized and delivered the offender." The time limit for handling public security cases "shall not exceed 30 days from acceptance; for major or complex cases, it may be extended by 30 days with approval of the public security organ at the next higher level," and time spent on forensic appraisal is not counted in the handling limit. The Regulations on Public Security Organs' Supervision by Inspection, Article 9, covers complaining about the police. The text reads: "For violations or breaches of discipline by public security organs and their people's police that the public complains of while occurring, inspection bodies shall dispatch officers promptly, dispose of the matter on scene according to regulations, and feed the outcome back to the complainant in good time" (nationwide)
Note
The beneficiary is you. Reporting doesn't guarantee action, but whether they act and how fast both have explicit standards and deadlines. Remember three moves in order. (1) Get the case-acceptance receipt on the spot and note the case number and accepting unit. (2) If the deadline passes with no result, chase progress against the limits above — ask "which stage is the case at," not "why is nobody helping me." (3) When the notice of non-filing arrives, read the reasons first: reconsideration within 7 days, then review within a further 7, and in parallel you can raise case-filing supervision with the people's procuratorate — the three routes don't conflict. Public security cases are things like fights and petty theft. The handling limit runs from the day of acceptance, no more than 30 days; major or complex cases can be extended another 30 days with approval from the next higher public security organ. Time spent on appraisal doesn't count. For rude treatment at the front desk, complain through the inspection-supervision channel; the case itself still proceeds through the filing process. Found property and neighbor disputes were never criminal cases in the first place; the police handle them as administrative cases or through mediation, sometimes only logging them — don't read that as "nobody cares about my report." For the payment-freeze process after a scam, see item 2 of this section (call 110 at once to freeze the payment). For cyberbullying, see item 37 of this section (cyberbullied? preserve evidence first, then pick your route)
Sources (5 references)
National People's Congress (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 amendment, Articles 112, 113). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d1b81…; Ministry of Public Security (2020). Decision on Amending the Provisions on Procedures for Public Security Organs Handling Criminal Cases (MPS Order No. 159), with the amended full text. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2020/content_5549884.htm; Ministry of Public Security (2013/2019 amendments). Provisions on Procedures for Public Security Organs Handling Administrative Cases (MPS Order No. 125, as amended by Decision No. 149). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2013/content_2321117.htm, http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/31/content_5428…; State Council (2011). Regulations on Public Security Organs' Supervision by Inspection (State Council Decree No. 603, Article 9). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2011-09/08/content_613…

Don't give money or gift cards to investigators or enforcers: bribery convicts you too, and bribing supervisory, enforcement, or judicial personnel draws heavier punishment

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

"Spending a little to smooth things over" is a distinct crime in the Criminal Law, and the one caught isn't only the person taking the money. Giving bribes carries up to 3 years. Serious circumstances carry 3 to 10 years, especially serious 10 or more or life. Bribing supervisory, administrative-enforcement, or judicial personnel is an expressly aggravated tier. Money given because you were extorted, without obtaining improper benefits, is not bribery.

Cost
Costs nothing. Just don't do it.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 389 defines bribery: "Whoever gives money or property to a state functionary for the purpose of obtaining improper benefits commits the crime of bribery." The same article adds: "In economic dealings, giving property to state functionaries in violation of state regulations, where the amount is relatively large, or giving state functionaries rebates or handling fees of various names in violation of state regulations, is punished as bribery." It also keeps one exception: "Giving property to a state functionary because of extortion, without obtaining improper benefits, is not bribery." Sentencing is in Criminal Law Article 390 (as amended by Amendment XII, effective March 1, 2024). The text reads: "Whoever commits the crime of bribery is sentenced to up to three years' imprisonment or criminal detention, plus a fine; where improper benefits were sought through bribery in serious circumstances, or major losses were caused to state interests, the sentence is three to ten years' imprisonment, plus a fine; where the circumstances are especially serious, or especially major losses were caused to state interests, the sentence is ten or more years' imprisonment or life imprisonment, plus a fine or confiscation of property." There are seven aggravating circumstances that draw heavier sentences: "(1) bribing repeatedly or bribing multiple people; (2) a state functionary giving bribes; (3) bribing in connection with major national projects; (4) bribing to obtain appointment, promotion, or transfer of posts or ranks; (5) bribing supervisory, administrative-enforcement, or judicial personnel; (6) bribing and committing unlawful or criminal acts in fields such as ecology and environment, finance, work safety, food and drugs, disaster prevention and relief, social security, education, or health care; (7) using illegal gains to bribe." The final paragraph leaves a door for coming forward: "Where the briber voluntarily confesses the bribery before being prosecuted, punishment may be lighter or reduced; where the crime is minor, or the confession played a key role in breaking open or solving major cases, or there is major meritorious service, punishment may be reduced or waived" (nationwide)
Note
The beneficiary is you. Don't count on a bribe buying exemption from punishment. The other side has colleagues, ledgers, cameras, and inspectors; what you hand over becomes evidence against them when they're investigated — and evidence of your own crime — and this category of bribery sits squarely in the expressly aggravated tier. If the other side really does solicit a favor, go through the channels in item 39 (report the case and get the acceptance receipt on the spot): keep the receipt and the paperwork, and raise it with the inspection body or the discipline-inspection and supervision authorities. The exemption in Criminal Law Article 389 paragraph 3 requires "being extorted and obtaining no improper benefit" — once you use the opening to get something you couldn't otherwise have gotten, that condition fails. Red envelopes in hospitals follow a different set of rules — see Section 24, item 11
Sources (2 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China (consolidated text as amended by Amendment XI), Article 389. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181796a636a0179822a19…; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2023). Criminal Law Amendment XII of the People's Republic of China (item 5, amending Criminal Law Article 390; effective March 1, 2024). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081818c3ce31f018cb6a6bc…
41

For calls and meetings that could turn ugly, just record: a conversation you take part in needs no consent from the other side

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Loans, debts, compensation, refunds, labor disputes: everything said clearly on the phone but nothing left behind means months later each side tells a different story. A conversation you take part in can be recorded, and not telling the other side in advance doesn't by itself disqualify it as evidence. What you can't do is wiretap, pry into others' privacy, sneak into someone's home to record, or threaten someone into talking.

Cost
Costs nothing. Turn on call recording or a recording app on your phone. Record start to finish, keep the original file afterwards, and don't edit or overwrite it.
Benefit
The Civil Procedure Law, Article 66, lists audio-visual materials and electronic data as forms of evidence. The Supreme People's Court's interpretation of the Civil Procedure Law, Article 106, excludes only evidence obtained by three methods: seriously infringing others' lawful rights and interests, violating prohibitive provisions of law, or seriously offending public order and good morals. "Not telling the other side first" is not among the three. The SPC's evidence provisions, Article 15: to use a recording or video as evidence, submit the original carrier storing it — say, the original phone. Article 90: audio-visual materials or electronic data with doubtful points cannot alone establish facts. A judge's article republished on the SPC's official website says the same: recordings must be lawfully obtained, true in content, unedited, and relevant to the case (nationwide)
Note
The beneficiaries are you and your family. In the recording, try to make the people, events, amounts, and dates line up. Don't just ask "when will you pay me back" — ask naturally, "That 50,000 yuan you borrowed last year — when are you planning to repay it?" Give the recording to the court, the arbitration commission, or the police; don't post it online — publicizing what someone said can drag you into privacy and reputation disputes, see item 16 of this section (online: no insults, no rumors). Having a recording doesn't mean winning; the court will still weigh it against other evidence for whether it's genuine and relevant. Recording only settles whether you can prove it; whether to actually sue and how long that takes are separate calculations. For what to save before leaving a job, see Section 19, item 8 (before you resign, save your pay slips and attendance records first). This item rests on civil procedure rules; how evidence is used in criminal and administrative cases is governed separately.

When something happens on scene, shoot the panorama first, then positions relative to each other, then damage and injuries; never delete the originals

Grade CValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

A close-up of one scratch on the car or one object on the ground tells nobody, days later, where it originally was. Shoot a panorama first, taking in the intersection, the door plates, the cars, the people, and the surroundings; then shoot how things sit relative to each other; details last. If something or a car must be moved, shoot first if you can. Keep the original photos and videos on your phone — don't settle for the single copy that passed through a chat app.

Cost
Costs nothing. Shoot continuously on your phone for tens of seconds to a few minutes. Keep yourself safe first, and don't delay rescuing people or handling the situation.
Benefit
The Civil Procedure Law, Article 66, lists physical evidence, audio-visual materials, and electronic data as forms of evidence. The SPC's evidence provisions, Article 14, classify images, audio, and video as electronic data. Article 15 requires submitting the original of electronic data; a video used as evidence must be submitted on its original carrier. Photos and video preserve a scene state that is about to change, and can later be cross-checked against the police report, repair records, medical records, and witness accounts. The "panorama, positions, details" order is accumulated practice, not a rule of law (nationwide)
Note
The beneficiaries are you and your family. Graded C because shooting order is just experience; the law only says photos and video can serve as evidence and originals must be submitted. If someone is injured, there's a fire, a gas leak, or any other danger, rescue people and get clear first — don't let photographing get in the way. What to do at a traffic accident scene: see item 1 of this section (in a traffic accident: stop, help the injured, call the police).

Suffering domestic violence? Call the police first for a response record, then apply to court for a personal safety protection order — no divorce needed, and it's free

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Of women killed worldwide, more than a third are killed by a partner, often the endpoint of long-term domestic violence. Among equally abused women, those who have been strangled are more than 7 times likelier to later be killed than those never strangled. So call the police when you're beaten, then apply to court for a protection order. The court generally must answer within 72 hours.

Cost
Costs nothing. Applying for a personal safety protection order involves no court fee and no bond. What it costs is time — reporting to police, getting injuries documented, writing the application. The hardest part is saying it about your own family.
Benefit
First, the risk. Pooling data from 66 countries (a systematic review): among cases of women killed, 38.6% were killed by an intimate partner; for men, 6.3%. The authors note that such killings are often the last step in long-term abuse. Another study compared 506 homicides and attempted homicides with 427 abused women in whom no such outcome occurred. Those previously strangled by a partner had 6.70 times the odds of an attempted homicide (OR 6.70, 95% CI 3.91–11.49), and 7.48 times the odds of being killed (OR 7.48, 95% CI 4.53–12.35). Now the law. Victims and their close relatives can report to the police. The public security organs must respond promptly, stop the violence, investigate and collect evidence, and help with medical care and injury documentation. For minor cases, the police may issue the other side a written warning. Where you suffer domestic violence or face its real and present danger, you can apply to the court for a personal safety protection order. The court must rule within 72 hours of accepting the application, or within 24 hours in urgent situations. The order can forbid the other side from violence, forbid them from harassing, stalking, or contacting you and your close relatives, and order them to move out of your home. An order lasts at most 6 months, and you can apply to extend before it expires. Applying does not require divorce. The court may issue one where domestic violence is "fairly likely" to exist. If the other side violates the order, the court may fine them up to 1,000 yuan or detain them up to 15 days; where a crime is made out, it is handled as the crime of refusing to comply with judgments or rulings. Habitual insults, threats, stalking, and harassment, as well as withholding warmth or food, also count as domestic violence.
Note
The beneficiaries are mainly you and your family. The homicide figures are foreign data; China has no published statistics on the same basis. Evidence accumulates: police response records, written warnings, injury assessments, medical records, written pledges from the other side, chat records, and recordings all count. On recordings see item 41 of this section (recording). A protection order needs no lawyer and usually comes through within days. Divorce or compensation is a separate lawsuit — first-instance ordinary procedure starts at 6 months, and you pay your own attorney fees. Domestic violence victims can seek legal aid, and the court may defer, reduce, or waive court fees. A protection order is not a guarantee of physical safety — with danger right in front of you, call 110 first. Where a victim is coerced or intimidated and cannot apply herself, close relatives, the public security organs, the Women's Federation, the residents' committee, or the village committee may apply on her behalf. If the victim is a friend or colleague, you can go with them to the police or the hospital. Seeing someone being beaten inside a stranger's home, calling 110 is enough. Don't wade in to pull them apart — the reasons are in item 10 of this section (in a conflict, call the police first).
