10. Whether dating and marriage are worth it

20 items

This section breaks "whether marriage is worth it" into separate ledgers — money, time, health, legal risk, and relationship quality — and tallies each one on its own. Every ledger uses only figures with traceable sources, limited to official statistics or meta-analyses (which pool the data from many studies and recompute it). No moral judgments here, and no conclusions drawn for you. The health ledgers are counted in mortality risk, the time ledgers in minutes per day, and the legal ones in what the statutes actually say. These three ways of counting are not converted into one another. For the ledger method, a fill-in checklist, and common pitfalls, see [docs/Whether marriage is worth it](../docs/结婚划不划算.md). The entries in this section are grouped by theme below, with entry numbers in parentheses. Finding partners and dating: meet more people (item 1), stop after a clear rejection (item 2), read interest from behavior (item 3), take turns answering questions from light to deep (item 5), long distance is no worse than same city (item 6). Whether the relationship is good: go by how you feel in the relationship (item 4), argue issues not persons (item 17), go to couples therapy together (item 20). The marriage ledgers: check the registration data first (item 7), discount health benefits as observational data (item 8), count time as unpaid labor (item 9), count the exit costs (item 15), book "marrying for the elders" as a separate ledger (item 16). Getting the certificate and premarital checkups: registration takes only an ID (item 13), have a premarital checkup (item 14). Money and debt: for money, learn the legal defaults first (item 10), state in writing whether parental home funding is a loan or a gift (item 11), large loans taken out by one spouse (item 12). Same-sex couples and sexual orientation: same-sex couples should set up guardianship by agreement and wills (item 18), don't marry while hiding your sexual orientation (item 19).

1

Meet more people rather than fixating on one: whether two people click can't be predicted before meeting

Grade AValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

In two speed-dating studies, people filled out more than 100 mate-choice survey questions before meeting. The surveys could work out who tends to like others easily and who is generally popular — but not whether these two specific people would spark. Whether two people are compatible only shows up in person. So meeting a few more people pays off better than betting everything on one.

Cost
Costs nothing. Spend the time meeting a few more people instead of ruminating over the same one. The hard part is resisting the urge to fixate.
Benefit
In two speed-dating studies, participants first filled out more than 100 self-report scales about mate choice (questionnaires you score yourself on) before meeting. The researchers used random-forest models (an algorithm for finding patterns). For "how easily a person tends to like others in general," the questionnaires could explain 4%–18% of the variance — variance is the differences between people, and the questionnaires accounted for only a small slice of it. They could also work out "how popular a person is in general," explaining 7%–27%. But "whether these two specific people would spark" could not be predicted — no combination of pre-event traits and preferences predicted it. The same researchers had run an earlier speed-dating experiment. Before the event, participants stated their ideal-partner preferences, such as valuing looks versus economic prospects. Those preferences did not predict their interest in any specific person at the event
Note
The two studies only show that it can't be computed before meeting — not that effort is useless. Compatibility only reveals itself in person, so spending the time to meet several people and genuinely go out with each beats betting everything on one. The study subjects were all European and American college students. China's dating scene is different; discount before applying this to yourself
Sources (2 references)
Joel S, Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2017). Is romantic desire predictable? Machine learning applied to initial romantic attraction. Psychological Science, 28(10), 1478-1489. https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797617714580; Eastwick PW, Finkel EJ (2008). Sex differences in mate preferences revisited: do people know what they initially desire in a romantic partner? Journal of Personality and Social Psychology, 94(2), 245-264. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.94.2.245
2

Stop after a clear rejection; keeping after them is a public-order violation, not 'sincerity'

Grade AValue: FairBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

If the other person has clearly said no and you keep messaging them or keep waiting around for them, that is a public-order violation as of January 2026. Penalties: up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan; in more serious cases, 5 to 10 days of detention. The police can also order you not to contact the person, and violating that order means another 5 to 10 days of detention.

Cost
Costs nothing, and no time. The hard part is holding back: no more messages, no more waiting around.
Benefit
The Public Security Administration Punishments Law, effective January 1, 2026, makes pestering and stalking a separate offense. The provision reads: "repeatedly sending obscene, insulting, or threatening messages, or disturbing, pestering, or stalking others in ways that interfere with their normal life." Such conduct draws up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. In more serious cases, 5 to 10 days of detention, possibly with a fine of up to 1,000 yuan on top. The provision adds one more layer: with the approval of a responsible official of the public security organ, the offender may be ordered to have no contact with the victim for a specified period. Violating the no-contact order draws another 5 to 10 days of detention
Note
"Persisting to the end will move them" has zero research support, but detention and no-contact orders are written in black and white. The record left behind also affects civil-service exams, public-institution hiring, political vetting, and professional licensing in some occupations. The line between pursuing someone and harassing them is not drawn by how you feel; it is drawn by whether they have clearly said no
Sources (1 reference)
NPC Standing Committee (2025 revision). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (Article 50, Paragraph 1, Item 5; Paragraph 2). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml (republished by the Supreme People's Procuratorate)
3

Read interest from behavior, not 'signals': who initiates, who plans, who follows up

Grade BValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Researchers had 52 pairs of strangers chat for about ten minutes, then judge whether the other person was flirting. "They were not flirting" was judged fairly accurately; "they were flirting" was much harder to spot. Swapping in 261 people judging video clips gave the same result. So don't read expressions and tone — read behavior: who initiates, who arranges the next meeting, whether they follow up when you stop pushing.

Cost
Costs nothing and little time. The hard part is changing the habit: stop decoding expressions and tone, and start recording facts.
Benefit
Two studies measured how accurately people detect flirting. The first had 52 pairs of previously unacquainted men and women talk one-on-one for 10 to 12 minutes. Afterwards each reported whether they had flirted, and whether they thought the other had. The result: "interactions without flirting were judged more accurately, while interactions with flirting were judged worse." The second used 26 one-minute video clips, judged by 261 observers, with the same conclusion. People can fairly reliably tell that "the other person is not flirting," but struggle to tell that "the other person is flirting"
Note
Disputed. Another line of research argues that men don't overestimate women's sexual intent — rather, women underreport their own intent on questionnaires. Who judges more accurately remains unresolved. But both camps agree on one thing: inferring someone's mind from subtle cues like expressions and tone has very low accuracy. Visible behavior is far more reliable: whether they initiate, whether they arrange the next meeting, whether they follow up even when you stop pushing
Sources (2 references)
Hall JA, Xing C, Brooks S (2015). Accurately detecting flirting: error management theory, the traditional sexual script, and flirting base rate. Communication Research, 42(7), 939-958. https://doi.org/10.1177/0093650214534972; Perilloux C, Kurzban R (2015). Do men overperceive women's sexual interest? Psychological Science, 26(1), 70-77. https://doi.org/10.1177/0956797614555727 (the dissenting source)
4

Judge the relationship mainly by how you feel in it, not by the other person's credentials

Grade AValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

What says the most about how good a relationship is, is how you feel in it — not the other person's credentials: whether you feel they are committed, whether you feel appreciated, how much you fight. Your own feelings are two to four times more predictive than your partner's reports. But whether the relationship will get better or worse from here is something no questionnaire can basically predict.

Cost
Costs nothing and little time. The hard part is switching perspective: put away the partner checklist and watch how the relationship actually goes.
Benefit
A machine-learning analysis of 29 labs and 43 longitudinal couple datasets — longitudinal meaning the same couples were tracked over time. The items that best predicted relationship quality all came from the participants' own feelings about the relationship: perceived partner commitment, perceived appreciation, sexual satisfaction, perceived partner satisfaction, and conflict. Among the individual-difference items, the strongest were life satisfaction, negative emotion, depression, avoidant attachment, and anxious attachment. At the start of the studies, the relationship items explained at most 45% of the variance. Variance here is the difference in relationship quality between couples; 45% is the share these items could account for. By the end of the studies, at most 18%. And the self-reported items were two to four times more predictive than the partner-reported ones. Adding individual differences and the partner's reports on top of one's own self-reported relationship feelings added no predictive power at all
Note
The same study also found that whether a relationship got better or worse over the study period was essentially unpredictable from any set of self-report measures in the questionnaires. So to judge how the relationship is doing right now, asking your own feelings beats checking the other person's credentials — but don't expect to predict where it goes. For the ledger connecting relationship quality to physical health, see item 17 of this section (treating the relationship as a health account).
Sources (1 reference)
Joel S, Eastwick PW, Allison CJ, et al. (2020). Machine learning uncovers the most robust self-report predictors of relationship quality across 43 longitudinal couples studies. Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, 117(32), 19061-19071. https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.1917036117
5

To build closeness, take turns answering questions from light to deep; don't memorize scripts

Grade BValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Two strangers took turns answering 36 questions from light to deep; after 45 minutes they were far closer than pairs who just small-talked for the same length of time. What worked was taking turns telling the truth, one layer deeper each round — not clever lines. This only shows momentary closeness; it doesn't mean it will grow into a long-term relationship.

Cost
Costs nothing. Takes 45 minutes.
Benefit
Previously unacquainted pairs were matched up and took turns answering three sets of progressively deeper questions, 36 in all — from "who would you most want at a dinner" all the way to "when did you last cry in front of another person." Closeness after 45 minutes was significantly higher than a control group that small-talked for the same length of time. It was also higher than the college students' average rating of their closest real-life relationship in the same study
Note
The experiment was run once, on college students, and measured only short-term closeness — not whether it develops into a long-term relationship. The closeness came from two people taking turns opening up about their real selves, one layer deeper each round; not from scripts, routines, or one-sided performance. So in conversation you can "share something true and ask a question just as deep," alternating both ways
Sources (1 reference)
Aron A, Melinat E, Aron EN, Vallone RD, Bator RJ (1997). The experimental generation of interpersonal closeness: a procedure and some preliminary findings. Personality and Social Psychology Bulletin, 23(4), 363-377. https://doi.org/10.1177/0146167297234003
6

Long distance is no worse than same city; the real hurdle is the first three months after you move in together

Grade BValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: a lotTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Long-distance couples are actually more stable while apart, because seeing each other rarely makes it easy to idealize the other person. The real hurdle comes after moving in together. In the tracking data, about half of long-distance couples made it to the same-city stage; the other half ended while still apart. Of the half that reunited, one third broke up within 3 months.

Cost
Travel costs, plus time on the road both ways. Fewer meetings than same-city couples. The hard part is bearing the separation long term.
Benefit
Two studies reached the same conclusion. Long-distance relationships were more stable than same-city ones while apart. The reason: in long-distance relationships the degree of idealizing the partner — the study measured idealized distortion, romantic love, relationship recall, and perceived agreement — was markedly higher. And the longer between meetings, the rosier the picture. But that stability only holds while the couple is still apart; once they become same-city, long-distance couples break up more easily. The study tracking the move from long distance to same city gave these proportions: about half of long-distance couples reached the moving-in-together stage; the other half ended while apart. Of the half that reunited, one third broke up within 3 months of reuniting. The longer the gaps between meetings and the stronger the idealization while apart, the less stable after reunion
Note
The subjects were American college students in dating relationships, not marriages, and the studies are older — don't apply the absolute percentages directly. Another study surveyed 717 long-distance and 425 same-city people. Quality differed very little between the two types; how good a relationship is depends mainly on the two individuals and the relationship itself. So when deciding whether to go long distance, don't use "long distance always falls apart" as a reason. What to prepare for in advance is the months after reunion, when autonomy shrinks, mutual knowledge grows, and conflict and jealousy rise
Sources (3 references)
Stafford L, Merolla AJ, Castle JD (2006). When long-distance dating partners become geographically close. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 23(6), 901-919. https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407506070472; Stafford L, Merolla AJ (2007). Idealization, reunions, and stability in long-distance dating relationships. Journal of Social and Personal Relationships, 24(1), 37-54. https://doi.org/10.1177/0265407507072578; Dargie E et al. (2015). Journal of Sex & Marital Therapy, 41(2), 181-202. https://doi.org/10.1080/0092623X.2013.864367 (the long-distance study in the note)
7

Check the registration data before listening to your elders: what do the marriage and divorce rates actually count?

Grade AValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

In 2024, China registered 6.106 million marriages, down about 20% from the previous year, and 3.513 million divorces. The claim online that "over half of marriages end in divorce" comes from dividing these two numbers — about 57.5%. But the divorcing couples and the marrying couples are not the same people, so it cannot be read as "half of marriages end in divorce." The bulletin's marriage rate of 4.3‰ and divorce rate of 2.5‰ are computed against the whole national population.

Cost
Costs nothing. Read the marriage-registration section of the Ministry of Civil Affairs' annual bulletin — a few minutes.
Benefit
In 2024, 6.106 million couples registered marriage nationwide, down 20.5% from the previous year; the marriage rate was 4.3‰. The same year, 3.513 million couples completed divorce proceedings: 2.622 million registered divorces with civil-affairs departments and 891,000 divorce judgments and mediations by courts; the divorce rate was 2.5‰. The bulletin notes: marriage (divorce) rate = number of couples marrying (divorcing) in the year / average total population for the year × 1000‰. This is a "crude rate" — the denominator is the whole population, not the married population
Note
The common online claim of "a divorce rate above 50%" divides the number of couples divorcing in a year by the number marrying that year: 351.3 / 610.6 ≈ 57.5%. That's the "divorce-to-marriage ratio." The two numbers are not the same cohort, and the bulletin contains no such indicator, so it cannot be read as "half of marriages end in divorce." To compute "the probability that a given marriage eventually ends in divorce," you would have to follow one marrying cohort over time — no such official data was found for this section
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of Civil Affairs (2025). 2024 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Civil Affairs (Section V(2)1: marriage registration services, Note 5), web and PDF versions. https://www.mca.gov.cn/n1288/n1294/n1554/c16620049999800061… and https://www.mca.gov.cn/gdnps/n2445/n2451/n2458/n2681/c16620…
8

Count the health benefits in, but discount them as observational data

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Married people's probability of dying over the same period was about 12% lower than unmarried people's; people who had never married had about 24% higher than married people's. But that is two things occurring together, not marriage doing the work. People who are healthier, better paid, and more socially connected to begin with are both more likely to marry and more likely to live long. These figures come mostly from Europe and America; treat them as an order-of-magnitude reference for China at most.

Cost
Costs nothing and no time. Just remember one thing: these numbers say death rates are lower among married people — two things occurring together, not marriage extending your life.
Benefit
A meta-analysis in older adults pooled and recomputed multiple studies: 53 comparisons, over 250,000 people. All-cause mortality RR 0.88 for married versus unmarried, 95% CI 0.85–0.91 (RR is the risk ratio, CI the confidence range) — about 12% lower probability of dying over the same period. Within the same analysis: widowed 1.11, divorced or separated 1.16, never-married 1.11 — about 11%, 16%, and 11% higher respectively. No difference between men and women. The most conservative estimate was RR 0.94, only about 6% lower. Another meta-analysis compared unmarried (never married) with married, using 95 publications and over 500 million people. Result: HR 1.24 (1.19–1.30) — about 24% higher probability of dying over the same period. And the older the age, the smaller the gap. A third meta-analysis split by sex, 21 studies, over 7.89 million people: for both men and women, being unmarried co-occurred with all-cause, cancer, and cardiovascular death. For men the gaps in cardiovascular and all-cause death were larger. Unmarried men versus unmarried women: 31% more stroke deaths and 9% more all-cause deaths
Note
The dispute: married people are a pre-selected group — healthier, better paid, more socially connected people are both more likely to marry and more likely to live long. All three meta-analyses used observational data from existing populations, just tracked records, with no randomized groups. The authors themselves noted publication bias or methodological limits. Roelfs also found that the more rigorous the study, the smaller the estimated gap. These figures are mostly European and American populations; treat them as an order-of-magnitude reference for China
Sources (3 references)
Manzoli L, et al. (2007). Marital status and mortality in the elderly: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Soc Sci Med 64:77–94. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2006.08.031; Roelfs DJ, et al. (2011). The rising relative risk of mortality for singles: meta-analysis and meta-regression. Am J Epidemiol 174(4):379–389. https://doi.org/10.1093/aje/kwr111; Wang Y, et al. (2020). Sex differences in the association between marital status and the risk of cardiovascular, cancer, and all-cause mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of 7,881,040 individuals. Glob Health Res Policy 5:4. https://doi.org/10.1186/s41256-020-00133-8
9

Tally the time ledger as 'unpaid labor'; settle who does what before you get the certificate

Grade AValue: HighBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

In the national time-use survey, unpaid work such as housework and caring for family averaged 1 hour 52 minutes a day for men and 3 hours 29 minutes for women. The survey has no breakdown by marital status, so there is no official figure for "how much more housework after marriage" — treat this gender gap as an upper-bound reference. The division of labor can be negotiated into something entirely different before you get the certificate.

Cost
Costs nothing. Spend an hour or two before the wedding working unpaid chores — housework, care for elders and children, whose career yields — into an explicit division of labor, then execute it. The hard part is laying it all out on the table instead of putting it off.
Benefit
The 2024 national time-use survey. Unpaid labor means unpaid work such as housework and caring for family. Among those who did such work on the survey day, the daily average was 2 hours 45 minutes — 1 hour 52 minutes for men, 3 hours 29 minutes for women. The share of people who did such work on a given day was 67.5% for men and 83.9% for women. Housework averaged 1 hour 17 minutes a day among all residents, or 1 hour 59 minutes counting only those who did it — 28 minutes less than in 2018. Caring for family averaged 30 minutes a day, or 1 hour 46 minutes counting only those who did it. The 2018 figures: housework 45 minutes for men, 2 hours 6 minutes for women; caring for children 17 minutes for men, 53 minutes for women
Note
Both surveys group only by sex, urban/rural, and age — not by marital status. So there is no official number for "how much more housework after marriage"; the gender gap can only serve as an upper-bound reference. The figures are national averages — the division of labor between the two of you can be negotiated into something completely different
Sources (3 references)
National Bureau of Statistics (2024). Bulletins No. 2 and No. 3 of the Third National Time Use Survey. https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957216.html and https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202410/t20241031_1957215.html; National Bureau of Statistics (2019). 2018 National Time Use Survey Bulletin. https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202302/t20230203_1900224.html
10

For money, learn the legal defaults first, then decide whether to put agreements in writing

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Without a written agreement, the law defaults to both spouses jointly owning wages and bonuses earned during the marriage, business and investment income, and inherited or gifted property. Only premarital property, and property that a will or gift contract explicitly gives to one side, stays individual. The two of you can agree in writing that everything stays separate — once signed, it binds. The spouse who carried more of the childcare and eldercare can claim compensation at divorce.

Cost
Costs nothing. Read the property provisions in the Civil Code's marriage and family book. If needed, the two of you sign a written property agreement — the law only requires it be in writing; notarization is not required. The hard part is talking money openly in advance.
Benefit
The default rules absent a separate agreement: wages, bonuses, and labor remuneration earned during the marriage; income from production, business operation, and investment; intellectual-property income; and inherited or gifted property are jointly owned by the couple (Article 1062). Premarital property, compensation for personal injury, property that a will or gift contract explicitly assigns to one spouse only, and items for one spouse's exclusive daily use are individual property (Article 1063). The couple may agree in writing that premarital and marital property belongs to each separately, jointly, or partly separately and partly jointly; such an agreement is legally binding on both (Article 1065). The spouse who bore more of the obligations for raising children, caring for elders, or assisting the other's work has the right to request compensation at divorce (Article 1088)
Note
There are no official statistics on bride price, weddings, or the marital home, so this entry gives no figures. How much the Article 1088 compensation is: first the two of you negotiate; failing that, the court decides — there is no fixed formula. A written property agreement works both ways: useful for the higher earner, and just as useful for the one doing more of the unpaid housework and care
Sources (2 references)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (in force January 1, 2021; Articles 1062, 1063, 1065, 1088). National Laws and Regulations Database https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?title=%E4%B8%AD%E5%8D%8E%E4%B…; full text republished in the Supreme People's Court Gazette http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6…
11

When parents fund a home purchase, state in writing at the time of transfer whether it's a loan or a gift

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

When parents fund a home purchase before marriage, it defaults to a gift to their own child only. Money contributed after marriage with no agreement counts as joint marital property. From February 2025, when one spouse's parents fully fund a post-marriage purchase without stating it is for their own child only, the court can award the house to the funding side's child at divorce, then decide whether the other spouse gets compensation. If it's meant as a loan, write that down the same day, signed by both sides.

Cost
Costs nothing. On the day of the transfer, write a one-page statement saying whether the money is a gift and to whom, or a loan to whom, signed by the funding parents and the child. If it's a loan, have both spouses sign, and put the same wording in the transfer memo.
Benefit
Where parents fund a home purchase for the couple before marriage, it is deemed a gift to their own child alone — unless the parents explicitly said it was a gift to both. Contributions after marriage follow any agreement; with no agreement or an unclear one, they are handled under joint-marital-property principles. From February 1, 2025 there is one more rule: when one spouse's parents fully fund a purchase during the marriage and the gift contract does not state it is only for their own child, the court may, at divorce, award the house to the funding parent's child. After awarding it, the court weighs several factors to decide whether the other spouse gets compensation and how much: the state of shared life and whether they had children together, fault in the divorce, the size of contributions to the family, and the home's market price at divorce. When one parent contributes part, or both sets of parents contribute, the award is based on the source and proportion of the contributions, with reasonable compensation (nationwide)
Note
Writing it down clearly helps both sides. Funding parents no longer have to hope a retroactive IOU saves their contribution at divorce. After Interpretation (II) took effect, who paid is itself the basis for dividing the house — whose name is on the deed no longer decides ownership. And the side receiving the money doesn't have to wait for divorce to learn what it counts as. If it's a loan, actually treat it as one: both agree it's a loan, set repayment terms, state it in the transfer, and keep repayment records where needed. Miss any piece and you'll be explaining it in court
Sources (3 references)
Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Book of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Article 29). https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/282071.html; Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation (II) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Book of the Civil Code (Fa Shi [2025] No. 1, Article 8). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/452771.html; NPC (2020). Civil Code (Article 1062, Paragraph 1, Item 4). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
12

Money a spouse borrows in large amounts doesn't automatically become your debt if you never signed or ratified it

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Money your spouse borrows behind your back does not automatically become your debt, as long as it clearly exceeds daily household expenses and you neither signed nor ratified it afterwards. The creditor has to prove themselves that the money went to shared living or a joint business. But if money like a home purchase really became a house you live in together or co-own, the other side can usually prove that much.

Cost
Costs nothing. Don't sign "co-borrower" or "guarantor" on your spouse's IOUs or guarantee documents. And don't write things like "we will pay this back" in chats — it could be taken as ratifying the debt after the fact. The hard part is not taking the bait when creditors press you.
Benefit
Debts count as joint marital debts in these situations: first, signed by both spouses; second, ratified afterwards by one spouse — meaning the debt was acknowledged after the fact and both own up to it; third, borrowed by one spouse in their own name for everyday family needs during the marriage. Money borrowed by one spouse in their own name that clearly exceeds everyday family expenses is not a joint marital debt. The exception: the creditor (the one seeking repayment) can prove the money went to the couple's shared life or joint production and business operations, or that both acknowledged the debt. A home purchase clearly exceeds everyday family needs, and the burden of proof lies with the party claiming the debt — the creditor must produce the evidence. But if the money really became a home the couple live in together or co-own, creditors can often prove the "used for the couple's shared life" part. So the more useful step is item 11 (state in writing whether parental funding is a loan or a gift) (nationwide, since 2021)
Note
If your spouse's parents suddenly produce a loan agreement signed only by your spouse during property division at divorce, look at it in two steps. Step one: did the loan actually happen? If you say the money was never delivered and your account holds together, the court weighs several things together: the loan amount, how the money was delivered, both sides' financial capacity, usual transaction practices, whether property changed accordingly, and what witnesses say. If the other side has only a transfer record, they still must prove the loan exists. Step two, once the loan is established, whether it is a joint debt. For general rules on IOUs and guarantees, see section 8, item 18
Sources (2 references)
NPC (2020). Civil Code (Article 1064). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; Supreme People's Court (2020, second revision). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Private Lending Cases (Articles 15 and 16). http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/94b6623974526df7d2430a3… (Supreme People's Court Gazette)
13

Marriage registration takes only an ID plus a signed declaration — no household register, no fee, certificate issued on the spot

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

From May 2025, getting the certificate takes two things: your ID card and a signed declaration. The declaration states that you have no existing spouse and are not related to the other person by direct-line blood or within three generations of collateral blood. No household register needed, and no going back to either person's registered hometown. Registration costs nothing, and qualified couples get the certificate on the spot.

Cost
Costs nothing. Both must appear in person. Usually done in a few tens of minutes.
Benefit
The new Marriage Registration Regulations, effective May 10, 2025, changed what mainland residents must submit to marry. The provision says only two items are needed: "(1) the person's resident identity card; (2) a signed declaration that the person has no spouse and has neither direct-line blood kinship nor collateral blood kinship within three generations with the other party." The household register is no longer a required document. The registration authority is "the civil affairs department of the county-level people's government, or the township (town) people's government designated on the principle of convenience by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or directly administered municipality." The old regulation's restriction of "going to either party's place of permanent household registration" has been removed. The regulations also state that "marriage registration authorities may not charge fees for marriage registration," and that "parties meeting the conditions for marriage shall be registered on the spot and issued a marriage certificate"
Note
The registration authority refuses only four situations: under the legal marriage age; not fully voluntary on both sides; one or both already married; the two are direct-line blood kin or collateral blood kin within three generations. The only possible charges are peripheral services like photos and photocopies. Registration itself costs nothing — refuse and report any "processing fee" or "expedited fee." For the 30-day cooling-off period in divorce registration, see the exit-costs entry in this section
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2025). Marriage Registration Regulations (State Council Decree No. 804, Articles 2, 6, 8, 10). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017752…
14

Have a premarital checkup, and any major illness must be honestly disclosed before registration

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If someone has a major illness and doesn't honestly disclose it before registration, the other spouse can ask a court to annul the marriage. The request must be filed within one year of learning of it. The checkup itself has not been a prerequisite for the certificate since 2003 — it's voluntary. Cost depends on local policy; it takes half a day.

Cost
Free or discounted for people of appropriate age in most areas; out of pocket it's only a few hundred yuan. Takes half a day.
Benefit
The legal consequence of concealment is clear. The new Marriage Registration Regulations provide: "a party with a major illness shall honestly inform the other party before marriage registration; failing to do so, the other party may petition the people's court to annul the marriage under Article 1053 of the Civil Code." The state treats the premarital checkup as the first gate for birth-defect prevention. Current targets: "premarital medical examination rates and pre-pregnancy eugenics health check coverage of target populations to stay above 70% and 80% respectively." The document also calls for "placing premarital checkup institutions near marriage registration venues for public convenience," and promotes "one-stop services combining marriage registration, premarital medical examination, and fertility guidance." The Civil Code provides that a party with a major illness shall disclose it honestly before marriage registration; failing that, the other party may petition the people's court to annul the marriage. An annulment petition must be filed within one year of knowing, or when the party should have known, of the ground for annulment
Note
Since 2003 the premarital checkup has not been a required step before the certificate — it's voluntary. But the provision on "having a major illness and not disclosing it" does give the other spouse the right to petition the court to annul the marriage, within one year of learning of it. There is no national rule making checkups free. A 2020 notice from the National Health Commission and four other departments only "actively encourages localities to implement free premarital checkups as feasible." So whether it's free, and what it covers, is set locally — ask your local maternal and child health institution or the one-stop window at the marriage registration office.
Sources (4 references)
NPC (2020). Civil Code (Article 1053). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; State Council (2025). Marriage Registration Regulations (State Council Decree No. 804, Article 12). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202504/content_7017752…; General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Plan for Improving Birth Defect Prevention and Treatment Capacity (2023–2027) (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Fa [2023] No. 9). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202308/content_6900320…; National Health Commission and four other departments (2020). Notice on Strengthening Premarital Health Care (Guo Wei Fu You Han [2020] No. 205): "actively encourages localities to implement free premarital checkups as feasible." https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-05/22/content_551…
15

Count the exit costs: divorce by agreement has a 30-day cooling-off period; litigated divorce has statutory conditions

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Divorce by agreement isn't done at signing. Within 30 days of filing the application, either party can withdraw it. After the period expires, both must appear in person within another 30 days to collect the divorce certificate — failing to go counts as withdrawal. If the other side won't agree, your only route is to sue. The court mediates first; only with grounds like domestic violence, bigamy, or two full years of separation, and only if mediation fails, does it grant the divorce.

Cost
Costs nothing. Spend some time before marriage reading up: if you ever need out, how long it takes and what procedure applies. The hard part is contemplating a split before you're even married.
Benefit
Divorce by agreement requires a written divorce agreement and applying in person at the marriage registration authority (Article 1076). Within 30 days of the authority receiving the application, either party may withdraw. Within 30 days after that period, both must apply in person for the divorce certificate; not applying is deemed withdrawal (Article 1077). When one side refuses, the route is litigation, and the court must mediate first. Where there is bigamy or cohabitation with another person, domestic violence or maltreatment and desertion, habitual gambling or drug use unchanged despite repeated education, or two full years of separation due to broken affection, divorce shall be granted if mediation fails. If a first petition is denied and separation then lasts another full year, a renewed petition shall be granted (Article 1079). Of China's 3.513 million divorces in 2024, 891,000 went through court judgments or mediation
Note
The cooling-off period applies only to divorce by agreement. Litigated divorce has no cooling-off period but takes longer. Court fees and lawyer fees vary by region; this entry gives no figures. High exit costs don't mean you shouldn't marry — but you should know them before you do
Sources (2 references)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 1076, 1077, 1079). http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/7f184078694d811fb3314f6…; Ministry of Civil Affairs (2020). Notice on Implementing the Marriage Registration Provisions of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Min Fa [2020] No. 116). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-12/04/content_556…; Ministry of Civil Affairs (2025). 2024 Statistical Bulletin on the Development of Civil Affairs. Same reference as item 7 (what the marriage and divorce rates actually count)
16

Book 'marrying for the elders' as a separate ledger; don't blend it into your own

Grade CValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The elders' gains — peace of mind, face, no more nagging — are real. But they don't automatically become your health benefits or relationship quality. Meanwhile the time ledger, the money ledger, and the exit costs are borne entirely by you. Split the page into two columns — which gains go to you, which to the elders — and whether this ledger is worth it becomes obvious at a glance.

Cost
Costs nothing. Two columns on paper. One column: which gains from this marriage are yours — the earlier entries in this section can compute that. The other: which gains belong to the elders — peace of mind, face, the nagging stops. The hard part is leaving the elders' column separate instead of merging it into your own.
Benefit
The elders' gains are real. But they don't automatically convert into your health benefits (item 8) or relationship quality (item 4 — judge the relationship by how you feel in it). Meanwhile the time ledger (item 9), the money ledger (items 10 to 12), and the exit costs (item 15) are all borne by the couple themselves. Once the books are separate, whether "marrying as a task assignment" is good value is something you can see for yourself
Note
The elders' column can also count as a heavy one; how to weigh it is your call. For the fill-in checklist, see [docs/Whether marriage is worth it](../docs/结婚划不划算.md)
Sources
Author's experience; a methodological suggestion. For the data, see the earlier entries in this section
17

Treat the state of the relationship as a health account: argue issues, not persons — no insults, no sarcasm

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: small

Couples in good marriages are somewhat healthier, with somewhat lower death risk. The association is modest — about the size of the diet-to-health association. In one experiment, couples who stayed hostile throughout arguments healed experiment-induced small wounds at only about 60% the speed of calmer couples.

Cost
Costs nothing. In a fight, stick to the issue at hand: no insults, no sarcasm, no dredging up old grievances. The hard part is watching your mouth while angry.
Benefit
A meta-analysis pooling 126 studies and over 72,000 people. Higher marital quality tracked better health, with correlation coefficients r between .07 and .21. (A correlation of 0 means no relationship; 1 means perfectly in sync.) The correlation with lower death risk was r = .11; smaller cardiovascular reactions during conflict, r = -.13. The authors note these effects are all small — about the size of the association between health habits like diet and health. In another crossover experiment, 42 healthy couples were each hospitalized twice for 24 hours — once for mutually supportive discussions, once to discuss a disagreement. After the conflict sessions, experiment-induced blister wounds healed more slowly. Couples who showed more hostility in both sessions healed at only 60% the speed of low-hostility couples. The morning after a fight, their blood inflammatory markers (IL-6, tumor necrosis factor) also rose more.
Note
Why Grade B: the pooled studies mostly just tracked records, with no control groups, so one can't tell whether a bad relationship makes people sick or poor health worsens the relationship. In some studies the association persisted after adjusting for age and income. Robles's paper also states that some results show publication bias. Studies that explicitly compared men and women largely found no difference. This section found no pooled analysis directly comparing mortality in "bad marriages" versus "not marrying," so "a bad marriage harms you more than staying single" remains an inference. The wound experiment had only 42 couples. "Argue issues, not persons — no insults, no sarcasm" is the author's extrapolation from the experiments' "hostile behavior"; no study has compared it directly. If fights are fierce and won't change, go to couples therapy together — see item 20 of this section (couples therapy). If fights turn physical, or involve long-term verbal abuse and threats, that is no longer a communication problem — it's domestic violence; see section 8, item 43 (domestic violence). To think through whether to leave, see the exit costs in item 15 of this section (exit costs).
Sources (2 references)
Robles TF, Slatcher RB, Trombello JM, McGinn MM (2014). Marital quality and health: a meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0031859; Kiecolt-Glaser JK et al. (2005). Hostile marital interactions, proinflammatory cytokine production, and wound healing. Archives of General Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1001/archpsyc.62.12.1377
18

Same-sex couples, while you're both clear-headed, set up powers of attorney, guardianship by agreement, and wills: legally you are not next of kin — without them you have no right to sign or inherit

Grade AValue: FairBasis: FreedomMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Legally, next of kin means spouse, parents, children, siblings — a partner doesn't count. Without documents prepared in advance, when one partner falls seriously ill, the other cannot make decisions for them; when one partner dies, the other inherits nothing. Three documents cover three stages: power of attorney while alive, guardianship by agreement after capacity is lost, and a will for after death.

Cost
Guardianship by agreement and wills go through a notary office; notary fees vary by region, starting around a few hundred yuan. A handwritten will costs nothing. Budget one or two half-days. The hard part is sitting down together to talk about illness and death.
Benefit
Article 1045 of the Civil Code lists next of kin as spouse, parents, children, siblings, grandparents, maternal grandparents, grandchildren, and maternal grandchildren. Under Article 1127, statutory heirs are first spouse, children, and parents, then siblings and grandparents. A partner appears in neither list. Article 1219 governs surgery and special examinations or treatments: where informing the patient is impossible or inadvisable, medical staff must inform the patient's "next of kin" and obtain consent. Three routes can close the gap. First, Article 33 lets an adult agree in advance, in writing, with "other individuals willing to serve as guardian"; once the person loses or partially loses civil capacity, that person becomes guardian — and the guardian is the statutory agent. Second, Article 165 provides that a written power of attorney must state the agent's name, the matters entrusted, the scope of authority, and the period, signed or sealed by the principal. The moment the principal dies, the authorization ends. Third, Article 1133 allows a will leaving personal property to individuals outside the statutory heirs. An article by the Yichang Justice Bureau published on the Hubei Provincial Justice Department's website states that same-sex partners can notarize a guardianship-by-agreement protocol, designating each other as future guardian (nationwide)
Note
A partner receiving assets under a will is a "legatee," not an heir. Within 60 days of learning of the bequest, they must explicitly accept it; silence counts as renunciation. Neither the partner nor people with an interest in the estate can serve as will witnesses. Where several wills exist, the last one prevails — see section 17, item 2 (a later will overrides an earlier one). Whether a guardianship-by-agreement guardian can sign surgical consent forms directly varies by hospital; ask your usual hospital in advance. If family members reject these documents, it goes to court: first-instance ordinary procedure runs from 6 months, and you pay your own lawyer. So notarize the documents where possible. For jointly bought homes and jointly saved money, write a separate written agreement reflecting actual contributions. For how to set up guardianship by agreement, see section 17, item 1 (designating a future guardian in writing). The beneficiaries are you and your partner.
Sources (2 references)
NPC (2020). Civil Code (Articles 23, 33, 165, 173, 1045, 1124, 1127, 1133–1140, 1142, 1219). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5… (National Laws and Regulations Database); Yichang Justice Bureau (2021). Notarized guardianship by agreement: a notarial road to the rainbow. "Practice Highlights" column, Hubei Provincial Justice Department website. https://sft.hubei.gov.cn/fbjd/sjhc/202101/t20210108_3208602…
19

Don't marry while hiding your sexual orientation, and don't treat a marriage of convenience as an easy fix: legally it's a real marriage, and the only exit is divorce

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

A marriage entered into while hiding your sexual orientation is not void under the law, nor can it be annulled — the only exit is divorce. A marriage of convenience is a real marriage too: money earned and debts owed after it count as marital. The deceived spouse can seek a larger property share and damages for emotional harm at divorce, but whether courts will support that is unsettled.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is withstanding family pressure to marry — which may last many years.
Benefit
Article 1051 of the Civil Code limits void marriages to three situations: bigamy, a prohibited degree of kinship, and being under the legal marriage age. Articles 1052 and 1053 limit voidable marriages to two: marriage under duress, and concealing a major illness before marriage. Article 17 of Interpretation (I) on the Marriage and Family Book provides that courts reject claims to have a marriage declared void on grounds other than these three. So the only exit is divorce. A registered marriage of convenience is a legal marriage. Article 1062: wages, bonuses, and labor remuneration earned during the marriage are joint marital property. Article 1064: debts signed by both, or borrowed by one for everyday family needs, are joint marital debts. Divorce damages fall under Article 1091, limited to bigamy, cohabitation with another, domestic violence, maltreatment or desertion of family members, and "other major faults." Interpretation (I), Article 2, restricts "cohabitation with another" to cohabitation with a "person of the opposite sex outside the marriage." So a same-sex affair can only be argued as an "other major fault." Damages include emotional-harm compensation; the deceived spouse must raise it in the divorce petition — if the court denies the divorce, damages are not supported. Since the Civil Code took effect, no public court decisions of this kind were found. Under the old law, a 2013 article on the Jiangsu High People's Court's website discussed a case where a wife sued for divorce because her husband concealed his homosexuality. The article set out two views. One held that homosexuality was not among the statutory faults of the time, so neither a larger property share nor emotional damages should be supported. The author endorsed the other: treat the deceived spouse as the "no-fault party," favor her in property division, and award emotional solatium (nationwide)
Note
The larger-property-share and emotional-damages point rests on a single analysis article that doesn't say how the case ended, so whether you'd get them depends on the specific court. The Civil Code adds "other major faults" beyond the old law, giving the deceived spouse an argument to make. The statutory provisions themselves are Grade A. Where both parties to a marriage of convenience have same-sex partners, those partnerships enjoy no protection under marriage law — write property arrangements down separately; see item 18 of this section (same-sex couples set up guardianship by agreement and wills). Divorce from a marriage of convenience goes through the same 30-day cooling-off period or a lawsuit; see item 15 of this section (divorce by agreement has a 30-day cooling-off period). If the divorce agreement waives damages, a later suit won't be supported. The primary beneficiary is the spouse who would have been deceived; secondarily, yourself: once the concealment is discovered, divorce, property division, and child custody all land at once.
Sources (3 references)
NPC (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1051–1054, 1062, 1064, 1079, 1087, 1091). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5… (National Laws and Regulations Database); Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on the Application of the Marriage and Family Book of the Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Fa Shi [2020] No. 22, Articles 2, 17, 86–90). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80808177e75f880178006736…; Zhu Laikuan, Wang Hongjuan (2013). Can damages be claimed for a divorce caused by homosexuality? Jiangsu Courts website. http://www.jsfy.gov.cn/article/26621.html
20

Stuck in repeated fights and cold wars? Go to couples therapy together: waiting rarely fixes it

Grade AValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: a lotTime: moderateWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Couples stuck in a rut who completed couples therapy together were markedly more satisfied with the relationship — about 70% improved. Couples who just sat on a waiting list barely changed. But the effect fades: by year 5, about half were still clearly improved, while about a quarter had separated or divorced.

Cost
Costs money. Charged per session; it varies by region and provider, so this entry gives no figures. In the studies it was generally once a week, and one trial ran about 8 months in total. The hard part: both partners have to go, and see it through.
Benefit
A 2020 meta-analysis pooled 58 studies and 2,092 couples. After couples therapy, the pre-post change in relationship satisfaction was g = 1.12 (confidence range 0.92–1.31), which the authors call a large effect. (g is an effect size; see the README glossary.) Couples assigned to a waiting list over the same period: g = 0.12 (−0.04 to 0.29), no significant improvement. The worse the relationship at the start, the more it improved. A 2012 review reported that couples therapy helps 70% of the couples treated. Another randomized trial recruited 134 couples with long-standing, severe discord and ran two behavioral couples therapies for about 8 months. At the end, satisfaction changes were d = 0.90 and 0.71. At year 5, 50.0% and 45.9% of the couples respectively still showed clear improvement — what the authors call "clinically significant improvement." At the same time, 25.7% and 27.9% had already separated or divorced
Note
The dispute is how long the effects last. In another meta-analysis restricted to randomized trials, g was 0.60 at the end of treatment and 0.44 six months later. At 12 months only behavioral couples therapy had data: g = 0.06 — almost nothing kept. Another review pooling 20 meta-analyses said clinically meaningful improvement appears in 40% to 50% of people. "70% improved" and "40–50% clearly improved" use different standards; don't mix them. The year-5 trial had no no-treatment control, so it can't say whether divorce became more or less common. The 2020 meta-analysis covered only heterosexual couples, and no Chinese randomized trials were found for this entry — discount before applying it to yourself. Where to go in China: the Mental Health Law requires psychotherapy to be delivered in medical institutions, and counselors may not practice psychotherapy. Ask the psychiatry or psychology department of a hospital whether they offer couples therapy. For private providers outside hospitals, first check their credentials and training. Don't do joint therapy when there is domestic violence. The 2016 meta-analysis states its conclusions apply only to mild-to-moderate cases where both partners are violent over conflict; violence characterized by control or severe harm is excluded. Practitioners also worry about retaliation after sessions. If you've been hit, see section 8, item 43 first (domestic violence). For how to talk during fights, see item 17 of this section (argue issues, not persons); for whether to leave, see item 15 (exit costs). The beneficiaries are you and your spouse.
Sources (7 references)
Roddy MK, Walsh LM, Rothman K, Hatch SG, Doss BD (2020). Meta-analysis of couple therapy: effects across outcomes, designs, timeframes, and other moderators. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 88(7), 583-596. https://doi.org/10.1037/ccp0000514; Lebow JL, Chambers AL, Christensen A, Johnson SM (2012). Research on the treatment of couple distress. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 38(1), 145-168. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-0606.2011.00249.x; Christensen A, Atkins DC, Baucom B, Yi J (2010). Marital status and satisfaction five years following a randomized clinical trial comparing traditional versus integrative behavioral couple therapy. Journal of Consulting and Clinical Psychology, 78(2), 225-235. https://doi.org/10.1037/a0018132; Rathgeber M, Bürkner PC, Schiller EM, Holling H (2019). The efficacy of emotionally focused couples therapy and behavioral couples therapy: a meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 45(3), 447-463. https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12336 (the dissenting source); Shadish WR, Baldwin SA (2003). Meta-analysis of MFT interventions. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 29(4), 547-570. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1752-0606.2003.tb01694.x (the dissenting source); Karakurt G, Whiting K, van Esch C, Bolen SD, Calabrese JR (2016). Couples therapy for intimate partner violence: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Marital and Family Therapy, 42(4), 567-583. https://doi.org/10.1111/jmft.12178; NPC Standing Committee (2018 revision). Mental Health Law (Articles 23 and 51). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf744… (National Laws and Regulations Database)

11. Red lines programmers and tech workers can easily cross

19 items

This section's ledger covers personal freedom and money; the payback is "not getting locked up" and "not paying damages." People who write code and build tech often treat the things below as "purely technical issues," but they map onto specific crimes in the Criminal Law, or specific sums owed in civil liability. Each entry gives the article numbers of the statutes, plus cases published on the official websites of the Supreme People's Procuratorate and the Supreme People's Court. Criminal Law citations use the consolidated text "as amended by Criminal Law Amendment XI," republished by the Beijing Traffic Management Bureau. Entries are ordered from high to low by "how easily tech workers assume it's harmless × how heavy the consequences." Item 1 is the general one: how to judge before acting, and what to do first if something goes wrong.

1

Before acting, ask three questions: whose interests are harmed, how able are they to pursue you, how much evidence do I leave; the moment someone comes after you, get a criminal defense lawyer

Grade CValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Before acting, ask one question: will the vendor, the platform, or the company report it to the police? Server logs, payment records, group-chat records — investigators can pull them all. If you really are criminally detained, the decision on formal arrest comes within at most 37 days. You can hire a lawyer from the very first interrogation, and those 37 days are when a criminal defense lawyer does the most good.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before acting, swap "can it be done technically" for a different question: will the vendor, the platform, or the company report it? The hard part is resisting the thought "nobody cares about something this small" — because server logs, payment records, and group-chat records all get pulled by default in an investigation
Benefit
Any unit or individual who discovers criminal facts has the right to report them. Where the handling authority finds criminal facts exist, it must open a case. After criminal detention, the police must submit a request for arrest approval (apply to the procuratorate for formal arrest) within 3 days; extendable by 1 to 4 days in special circumstances, and up to 30 days for itinerant offending (committing crimes across places, one after another). The procuratorate then takes 7 days to decide. In total, whether to arrest is decided within at most 37 days. From the first interrogation onward — or from the imposition of compulsory measures (detention, arrest, and the like) — you may retain a lawyer. While the case is still in the police investigation stage, only a lawyer may be retained. When a lawyer requests a meeting, the detention center must arrange it within 48 hours at the latest. If the likely sentence is a lighter penalty such as public surveillance or criminal detention, or only supplementary penalties without a principal one, you can be released on bail pending trial: post a bond or provide a guarantor, and wait at home while the case proceeds. Bail runs at most 12 months (nationwide)
Note
These 37 days count from detention to the procuratorate's decision on whether to approve arrest — they are not a cap on how long you can be held. After arrest approval, the detention period during investigation continues from there. For a competent lawyer, these 37 days are also the most useful window: meet the client, submit an opinion to the procuratorate that arrest should not be approved, and apply for release on bail. Waiting until after indictment to find a lawyer is too late. Every other entry in this section is about the same question: does the other side have a reason to report it?
Sources (1 reference)
NPC (2018). Criminal Procedure Law (2018 revision, Articles 34, 39, 67, 79, 91, 110, 112). https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/201810/t20181027_396818.shtml
2

Don't make or sell game cheats and helpers — including AI aids that 'only read the screen, never touch memory' — or modified builds that add features to software like WeChat

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Selling a cheat 20 times, or making 5,000 yuan from it, is enough for up to 3 years — 3 to 7 years in especially serious cases. One person built wallhack and aimbot cheats, sold over 80,000 yuan's worth in 3 months, and got 1 year suspended for 1 year plus a 5,000 yuan fine. Others took a game's server program to run private servers and collected over 20 million yuan in top-ups — the heaviest sentence was 4 years, with fines up to 10 million yuan.

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is giving up income from such gigs and "little tools." The hard part: the money comes fast, and you can't see who would come after you
Benefit
Providing programs or tools specially used to intrude into or illegally control computer systems: up to 3 years in serious cases, with a fine imposed alongside or instead — "alongside" means fined at the same time as the sentence, "instead" means fined alone. Especially serious cases: 3 to 7 years with a fine. The threshold for "serious circumstances" is providing the tools 20 or more times, or illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more — illegal gains are what you made from it. Deliberately circumventing or destroying rights holders' technical protection measures can also constitute the crime of copyright infringement: up to 3 years, or 3 to 10 years in serious cases. Official cases: Wang and others made and sold cheats that read and modified game memory for wallhacks and aimbots, selling over 80,000 yuan's worth in 3 months and profiting over 30,000. Sentence: 1 year suspended for 1 year, fined 5,000 yuan — suspension means the 1-year sentence is deferred; stay out of trouble for the year and you won't serve it. Xiang and others sold the "TZ" series of cheats with sales over 200,000 yuan; Xiang got 3 years suspended for 3 years and a 20,000 yuan fine. Liu and others obtained a game's server program, changed parameters, and ran private servers, collecting over 20 million yuan in top-ups: sentences from 4 years down to 2 years 6 months, with fines from 10 million down to 1.3 million yuan. And it's not just games. A Shanghai company made flashing packages that added dozens of features to WeChat on phones — auto-forwarding, auto-liking, bulk messaging — and sold 2,381 phones as "marketing phones." In 2019 the Shanghai Xuhui court convicted the company of copyright infringement, fined it 500,000 yuan, and gave the person in charge 1 year 6 months suspended for 1 year 6 months (nationwide)
Note
Published cheat cases all involve reading and writing game memory and bypassing anti-cheat. No official precedent yet for helpers that "only take screenshots, only simulate key presses." But the ticket-grabbing case in item 3 shows that never touching memory — just sending requests — can still support a conviction for illegally obtaining data. Whether it's ultimately a crime, and under which crime, is decided by the handling authorities based on the materials the vendor submits when reporting — not by the author. Twenty sales is enough for "serious circumstances"; that's a very small quantity.
Sources (5 references)
NPC (2020). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases Involving Endangering the Security of Computer Information Systems (Article 3). https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html (republished by the Shenzhen Public Security Bureau); Supreme People's Procuratorate (2026). Shanghai Jing'an: severely punishing the production and sale of game cheats and the related gray industry to protect a clean cyberspace. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202608/t20260825_735480.shtml; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2021). 2020 typical cases of procuratorial intellectual property protection (Case 5). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/xwfbh/wsfbt/202104/t20210425_516…; National Copyright Administration (2020). Shanghai's ten typical copyright cases of 2019 released (by the Shanghai Copyright Bureau; Case 8: Shanghai Yugong Network Technology Co., Ltd. and others' copyright infringement case). https://www.ncac.gov.cn/xxfb/ywxx/202004/t20200430_47269.html
3

Don't write or sell ticket-grabbing, flash-sale, order-brushing, or promo-farming scripts — even 'just automating button clicks'

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Scripts that never touch memory or crack anything — they just fire requests faster than a human — still get convicted: 5,000 yuan earned or 10,000 yuan of losses to the other side is enough. One person used bought 12306 accounts to grab over 200 tickets for others and made over 20,000 yuan: 1 year 6 months suspended for 1 year 6 months, fined 5,000 yuan. A seller of ticket-grabbing software in an online shop paid 20,000 yuan in unfair-competition damages.

Cost
Costs nothing and takes no time
Benefit
Intruding into a computer information system, or using other technical means to obtain the data inside: up to 3 years in serious cases, with a fine imposed alongside or instead; 3 to 7 years in especially serious cases. The "serious circumstances" threshold is illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more, or losses caused of 10,000 yuan or more. Official cases: one person used a cheat tool to bulk-import bought 12306 accounts and submit ticket requests intensively across multiple threads. He grabbed over 200 train tickets for others and profited over 20,000 yuan. The court convicted him of illegally obtaining computer information system data: 1 year 6 months suspended for 1 year 6 months, fined 5,000 yuan. Zheng sold ticket-grabbing software targeting a ticketing app in an online store, was found to have committed unfair competition, and paid 20,000 yuan (nationwide)
Note
The ticket-grabbing scripts never touched memory or cracked anything — just "faster than a human" — yet were convicted under Criminal Law Article 285. Paid ticket-grabbing and selling scripts both count as profit-making. No official case found for one-time personal use.
Sources (4 references)
NPC (2020). Criminal Law (as amended by Criminal Law Amendment XI, Article 285, Paragraph 2). https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index…; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases Involving Endangering the Security of Computer Information Systems (Article 1). https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2026). Shanghai Jing'an: investigating a case of profiting from bulk train-ticket grabbing with cheat software. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/dfjcdt/202607/t20260707_731426.s…; Supreme People's Court (2025). 2024 typical intellectual property cases of the people's courts (Case 7, ticket-grabbing software unfair competition case). https://enipc.court.gov.cn/zh-cn/news/view-4205.html
4

Crawlers: only public pages that need no login; don't bypass anti-crawler measures, don't touch personal data, and don't sell what you scrape

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Data that takes a login, a token, or signature-cracking to get counts as bypassing protections: up to 3 years, or 3 to 7 years in serious cases. Personal information is worse still. Fifty items of location, communications, credit, or property data already count as "serious circumstances." So do 500 items of accommodation, health, or transaction data, 5,000 items of other data, or 5,000 yuan earned.

Cost
Costs nothing. A crawler is a program that automatically flips through web pages and grabs the data on them. Before crawling, glance at the robots file and the API authorization terms — the robots file is the one a site puts in its root directory listing which pages must not be scraped. Data that needs a login, a token (a temporary access credential), or signature-cracking: don't scrape it. The hard part: technically the data is one grab away, and restraint is entirely on you
Benefit
Bypassing protections to take data from a system carries the same sentencing as item 3 (ticket-grabbing, flash-sale, and order-brushing scripts): up to 3 years, or 3 to 7 years. Illegally obtaining, selling, or providing citizens' personal information counts as "serious circumstances" upon any of: 50 or more items of location-trajectory, communication-content, credit, or property information; 500 or more items of accommodation, communication records, health, or transaction information; 5,000 or more items of other personal information; or illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more. Serious circumstances: up to 3 years, with a fine imposed alongside or instead; especially serious: 3 to 7 years. Official cases: developer Li disguised a phone-album-stealing function as a "beauty check" app, harvesting 1,751 face photos, and also resold data-breach dumps — 3 years suspended for 3 years. (A "social-worker database" is a database pooling personal information leaked from many places.) A tech company used crawlers to take a food-delivery platform's shop and order data, causing losses of over 40,000 yuan, and was prosecuted for illegally obtaining computer information system data (nationwide)
Note
The 2017 judicial interpretation provides that "giving lawfully collected information to others without the person's consent" also counts as "providing." Exporting a user table to an external partner at work falls under the same sentence. 5,000 items is just one small table's worth.
Sources (4 references)
NPC (2020).
