Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases of Infringing Citizens' Personal Information (Articles 3, 4, 5). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/201705/t20170509_190088.…; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2022). Typical cases of procuratorial organs punishing crimes of infringing citizens' personal information according to law (Case 2). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/xwfbh/wsfbt/202212/t20221207_594…; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Typical cases of procuratorial organs punishing crimes against enterprise data security according to law and serving and safeguarding enterprise innovation and development (Case 1). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202501/t20250124_680670.…
5

Don't take development gigs for gambling, fraud, or porn apps; don't set up payment channels or get accounts unbanned for 'clients'

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Take one of these high-priced, vaguely specified gigs and you're a co-conspirator of the gambling ring. Running a gambling venue draws up to 5 years — 5 to 10 years in serious cases — heavier than the 3-year cap for merely helping. At one esports betting app, the 28 coders got 1 year to 3 years 6 months. Unbanning QQ accounts for a fraud ring: 1 year 6 months and a 20,000 yuan fine.

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is turning down outsourcing that pays well but can't be clearly specified. The hard part: the money offered is often a big cut above normal gigs
Benefit
Knowingly helping someone exploit the internet for crime — technical support, payment settlement, and the like — up to 3 years in serious cases, with a fine imposed alongside or instead. Where it also constitutes another crime, the heavier one applies. Running a gambling venue: up to 5 years with a fine; 5 to 10 years in serious cases. Official cases: the Zhangsheng Group developed gambling games and "packaged sites for export," collecting site-setup and reporting fees. Nearly 7 billion yuan involved. Zhangsheng got 9 years 9 months and a 50 million yuan fine. The 79 people responsible for outsourced development, including Wang Qiang, got from 6 months to 9 years 9 months. Chen Dong and others developed and ran an esports betting app, with the tech team writing code in Hainan: 28 people convicted of running a gambling venue, sentences ranging from 1 year to 3 years 6 months, plus fines. Zhang opened a studio unbanning blocked QQ accounts for fraud rings: 1 year 6 months and a 20,000 yuan fine (nationwide)
Note
"Knowing" doesn't require the client to spell out the use. Quotes clearly above market rate, features that are top-ups, withdrawals, and betting odds, a client who won't say what it's for — all used in an investigation to infer that you knew. Tech staff developing gambling apps are handled as accomplices to running a gambling venue, not capped at the 3-year tier of the aiding-cybercrime offense. (The "aiding offense" is short for the crime of assisting information network criminal activities.)
Sources (4 references)
NPC (2020). Criminal Law (as amended by Criminal Law Amendment XI, Article 287-2; Article 303, Paragraph 2). https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index…; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2023). Building and selling gambling websites, nearly 7 billion yuan involved. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202307/t20230711_621248.shtml; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2022). Shanghai Minhang: handling a new type of online gambling venue case. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202208/t20220805_569952.shtml; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Typical cases of punishing crimes of assisting information network criminal activities and related crimes according to law (Case 1). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202507/t20250728_702377.…
6

When leaving a job, hand over all accounts and access; no deleting databases, no backdoors, no locking systems with password changes — even if the company owes you money

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The company gave you the account and password — that doesn't mean you may keep using them after leaving. Logging in counts as illegal control: up to 3 years. Deleting data so systems stop running: up to 5 years, and 5 or more if the consequences are especially serious. One laid-off senior engineer logged into company servers with the old admin account and deleted data and logs, causing over 120,000 yuan in losses: 3 years suspended for 5 years and a 30,000 yuan fine.

Cost
Costs nothing. If the company owes you wages, get them back through labor arbitration — don't take matters into your own hands (labor arbitration: section 7). The hard part is keeping your hands off the systems while angry
Benefit
Illegally controlling a computer information system: up to 3 years in serious cases, with a fine imposed alongside or instead; 3 to 7 years in especially serious cases. Deleting or modifying system functions or data so systems can't run normally: up to 5 years where the consequences are serious, 5 or more where especially serious. Official cases: after being laid off, senior IT engineer Lü logged into the company's shared server with the old admin account. He changed the password and deleted data and logs, causing losses of over 120,000 yuan. Sentence: 3 years suspended for 5 years, fined 30,000 yuan. Bai, an employee of a software company, deliberately planted faulty code in an upgrade program, leaving client systems unable to log in — losses of over 40,000 yuan; prosecuted for sabotaging computer information systems (nationwide)
Note
Company-issued accounts don't remain yours after you leave. Logging in with the old account counts as "illegal control." Losses are measured by data-recovery costs; tens of thousands of yuan is enough to open a case.
Sources (3 references)
NPC (2020). Criminal Law (as amended by Criminal Law Amendment XI, Article 285, Paragraph 2; Article 286). https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index…; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2024). Typical cases of procuratorial organs "punishing cybercrimes according to law and supporting comprehensive cyberspace governance" (Case 6). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202402/t20240223_644505.…; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Typical cases of procuratorial organs punishing crimes against enterprise data security according to law and serving and safeguarding enterprise innovation and development (Case 7). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202501/t20250124_680670.…
7

When leaving, take no source code, client lists, or technical documents; don't upload them to personal cloud drives or reuse them at your next job

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Code you wrote yourself is still the company's copyright; client lists count as trade secrets. Taking them is taking the company's property. One ex-employee took security-screening system source code to a new company: 5 years and a 500,000 yuan fine personally, and the new company was fined 4 million yuan. Someone exploited a system vulnerability to download over 33,000 design files: 1 year 10 months. The company can also sue you separately for damages.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before leaving, purge company materials from your personal computer and cloud drive. The hard part: some files are ones you wrote line by line, and it hurts to let go
Benefit
Breaching confidentiality obligations to disclose or use trade secrets: up to 3 years in serious cases, with a fine imposed alongside or instead; especially serious: 3 to 10 years with a fine. The Anti-Unfair Competition Law also lists two acts as infringement: obtaining trade secrets by "electronic intrusion" (breaking into systems by technical means), and instigating or helping others breach confidentiality. Official cases: departing employees including Sun took security-screening system source code and core algorithms into a new company's products — Sun got 5 years and a 500,000 yuan fine; the new company was fined 4 million yuan. Tian exploited a system vulnerability to download over 33,000 design files: 1 year 10 months and a 100,000 yuan fine. Engineer Yang stored an app module's source code on personal computers and the cloud and built a similar app after job-hopping: prosecuted for infringing trade secrets (nationwide)
Note
Code you wrote yourself is still the company's copyright — see item 13 (code written with company resources belongs to the company). Taking it is taking the company's property. Client lists are business information and likewise trade secrets. On top of criminal sentences, the company can file a separate civil claim.
Sources (5 references)

Anti-Unfair Competition Law (2025 revision, Article 10). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699862.shtml; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Typical cases of procuratorial intellectual property protection (Case 7). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202504/t20250423_693691.…; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2020). 2019 typical cases of procuratorial intellectual property protection (Case 16). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202004/t20200425_459623.…; Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Typical cases of procuratorial organs punishing crimes against enterprise data security according to law and serving and safeguarding enterprise innovation and development (Case 5). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbh/202501/t20250124_680670.…
8

Don't run your own programs on other people's computers, servers, or cameras; don't mine cryptocurrency on company machines

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Controlling other people's computers, servers, or cameras without permission: 20 devices is enough for up to 3 years, and 3 to 7 in especially serious cases. Below the criminal threshold, you still face up to 5 days of detention and possibly a 50,000-to-500,000 yuan fine. Anyone with a criminal punishment is barred for life from key posts in cybersecurity management and network operations.

Cost
Costs nothing and takes no time
Benefit
Illegally controlling computer information systems: up to 3 years in serious cases, with a fine imposed alongside or instead; 3 to 7 years in especially serious cases. Illegally controlling 20 or more devices is "serious circumstances." Below the criminal threshold, police confiscate illegal gains, detain up to 5 days, and may fine 50,000 to 500,000 yuan; in more serious cases 5 to 15 days of detention and possibly 100,000 to 1 million yuan. Those with a public-order punishment are barred for 5 years, and those with a criminal punishment for life, from key posts in cybersecurity management and network operations. Official cases: Li bought IPs of network cameras and used software to control 105 cameras to spy on private life: 3 years suspended for 5 years, fined 20,000 yuan. Wu and others implanted trojans into phone motherboards, controlling over 3.3 million phones to relay verification codes: sentences from 2 to 4 years 6 months (nationwide)
Note
No published SPP or SPC case was found for mining on company servers; this entry is written from the statute on controlling other people's systems without permission. The "lifetime bar from key posts" is a consequence the Cybersecurity Law attaches beyond fines and sentences — for tech workers, heavier than the fine.

9

Don't test other people's systems without written authorization; 'good intentions' and 'reporting it afterwards' are not defenses

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Conviction turns on authorization and how much you took — not on your intentions. Obtaining 500 sets of ordinary credentials, or making 5,000 yuan, or causing 10,000 yuan in losses, is enough for up to 3 years. Exporting a user table offhand to prove a vulnerability often blows past 500 sets in one go. Even with credentials in hand, using them beyond the authorized scope counts as intrusion.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before joining a vendor's SRC or a crowdtest, get the document stating the authorized scope, target list, and testing window. (An SRC is a vendor's own security emergency response center for receiving externally reported vulnerabilities.) Stop once you've verified the vulnerability exists. The hard part is giving up the "let me just try it" moment
Benefit
Ordinary companies' and individuals' systems fall outside the fields of state affairs, national defense, and cutting-edge science and technology. Intruding into such systems, or using other technical means to obtain data stored, processed, or transmitted inside: up to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment or criminal detention in serious cases, with a fine imposed alongside or instead. Especially serious: 3 to 7 years with a fine. The "serious circumstances" standards: obtaining 10 or more sets of identity-authentication information (credentials like account-password pairs) for online financial services such as payment settlement, securities trading, and futures trading; 500 or more sets of other identity-authentication information; illegally controlling 20 or more computer information systems; or illegal gains of 5,000 yuan or more, or economic losses of 10,000 yuan or more. Five times or more of any of these figures is "especially serious." Official case: Procuratorial Example No. 36 established one sentence: "using accounts and passwords to log into a computer information system beyond the authorized scope constitutes intrusion into a computer information system." That is, even holding the credentials legitimately, using them beyond the authorization is itself intrusion. In that case three people used accounts, passwords, and tokens from their work to log into the company's internal systems remotely, downloaded data outside their job scope, and sold it online — illegal gains of 37,000 yuan. They were sentenced to 4 years, 3 years 9 months, and 4 years respectively, each fined 40,000 yuan (nationwide)
Note
Procuratorial Example No. 36 was itself a data-selling-for-profit case. It's cited only for the sentence "logging in beyond the authorized scope counts as intrusion" — not to say good-faith testing gets the same sentence. Neither your intentions nor reporting it afterwards can erase the offense; they can only affect how heavy the sentence is and whether you're prosecuted. A vendor thanking you and then reporting you are not contradictory — thanks is not authorization. In 2016, a white hat submitted a vulnerability in the Jiayuan dating site to a third-party vulnerability platform; Jiayuan then reported him to the police and he was detained. Jiayuan told reporters it reported the matter because data had been taken, and at the time didn't know the person taking it was the one who submitted the vulnerability. Only media coverage exists for this case — no verdict, no official notice, no official word on the outcome. No good-faith-testing case verifiable word-for-word was found on the SPC or SPP websites either, so this entry is graded on the statutes and punishment standards alone. If you must test, use the vendor's public SRC or a commissioned assessment with written authorization, with scope, targets, and time window all in the document. Prove the vulnerability with minimal evidence; don't bulk-export data. Even below the criminal threshold you face public-order punishment and a bar from the profession — fine amounts and durations as in item 8 (don't run your own programs on other people's machines). For what to do after finding a vulnerability, see item 10 (report vulnerabilities through the proper channels).
Sources (6 references)
NPC (2020). Criminal Law (as amended by Criminal Law Amendment XI, Article 285, Paragraphs 1 and 2). https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index…; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2011). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases Involving Endangering the Security of Computer Information Systems (Article 1). https://ga.sz.gov.cn/ZWGK/ZCFG/ZCJD/content/post_1304363.html (republished by the Shenzhen Public Security Bureau); Supreme People's Procuratorate (2017). Ninth batch of guiding cases (Procuratorial Example No. 36: the case of Wei Menglong, Gong Xu, and Xue Dongdong illegally obtaining computer information system data). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/jczdal/201710/t20171017_202593.s…; CNR (2016-06-29). White hat detained after publishing a vulnerability; Jiayuan denies "phishing" him into it (reporter Zhao Ke, intern reporter Liu Xiangxi). https://m.cnr.cn/news/yctt/20160629/t20160629_522531823.html (web archive https://web.archive.org/web/20261005043859/https://m.cnr.cn…)
10

Report vulnerabilities through the proper channels; before they're patched, publish no details, release no exploit tools, send nothing abroad

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Individuals are covered by the Regulations on the Security Management of Network Product Vulnerabilities too. Until the vendor has a fix, you may not disclose the vulnerability — nor details of vulnerabilities in systems in active use. You may not release programs and tools specifically for exploiting the vulnerability, and any disclosure must say alongside it how to fix it. Undisclosed vulnerabilities must not be handed to overseas organizations or individuals other than the vendor.

Cost
Costs nothing. Report the vulnerability to the product provider, or to an official platform. Until the vendor fixes it: no details, no proof-of-concept code
Benefit
The regulations cover three kinds of actors: network product providers and network operators within China, and organizations or individuals engaged in discovering, collecting, and publishing vulnerabilities. No organization or individual may use vulnerabilities to endanger network security, or illegally collect, sell, or publish vulnerability information. Publishing vulnerability information publicly must follow five rules. First, no publishing before the product provider has offered remediation measures. Second, no publishing details of vulnerabilities in networks, information systems, and equipment that network operators have in use. Third, no deliberately exaggerating harm and risk, and no using vulnerability information for malicious hype or fraud. Fourth, no releasing or providing programs and tools specifically for exploiting vulnerabilities to endanger network security. Fifth, remediation or mitigation measures must be published alongside. In addition, undisclosed vulnerability information must not be provided to overseas organizations or individuals other than the product provider. The regulations encourage reporting to four official platforms: the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's cybersecurity threat and vulnerability information sharing platform; the vulnerability platform of the National Network and Information Security Information Notification Center; the vulnerability platform of the National Computer Network Emergency Response Technical Treatment and Coordination Center; and the China Information Security Evaluation Center's vulnerability database. Collecting or publishing vulnerability information in violation is handled by MIIT and the Ministry of Public Security within their respective duties; where it fits the Cybersecurity Law, penalties follow that law. Publishing system vulnerabilities and other cybersecurity information publicly must follow national rules; violators are ordered to correct and warned, with fines of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan; refusing to correct or serious circumstances bring fines of 100,000 to 1 million yuan. Authorities may also order suspension of the relevant business, rectification and shutdown, closing the website or application, revoking the relevant business license, or revoking the business license. Directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible personnel face fines of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan (nationwide)
Note
The regulations explicitly put individuals among the governed — "I'm just a hobbyist" is not an exception. Submitting holes in domestic systems to overseas bug-bounty platforms lands squarely on the "undisclosed vulnerabilities must not be provided abroad" clause. Whether you're entitled to test at all, see item 9 (don't test other people's systems without written authorization) — keep that separate from what to do once you have a vulnerability. Even lawfully discovered vulnerabilities can be punished over how they were published; for vulnerabilities found without authorization, both the testing and the publishing are problems. Among reporting channels, the MIIT platform and CNCERT are the most used. The regulations don't specially address "the vendor was notified but won't fix" — in practice, keep records of the negotiation and reporting process and report to an official platform in parallel.
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, Cyberspace Administration of China, and Ministry of Public Security (2021). Regulations on the Security Management of Network Product Vulnerabilities (Gong Xin Bu Lian Wang An [2021] No. 66, Articles 2, 4, 9, 10, 14; effective September 1, 2021). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5641351.htm; NPC Standing Committee (2025). Cybersecurity Law (2025 revision, effective January 1, 2026, Articles 28 and 65; in the 2016 text Articles 26 and 62 — Article 14 of the regulations cites the 2016 numbering). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm
11

Don't sell censorship-circumvention tools or VPN accounts, and don't set up such nodes for others

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Build your own route out of the country, or use an international channel other than the state public channel, and police can order you to stop connecting, warn you, fine you up to 15,000 yuan, and confiscate illegal gains. Run it as a business and it can be handled as illegal business operation: up to 5 years in serious cases. This entry is about selling and running nodes. For personal use, punishment tops out at a warning plus a fine.

Cost
Costs nothing and takes no time
Benefit
Direct international networking must use the international entry-exit channel provided by the state public telecom network. No unit or individual may build or use other channels: neither your own route out of the country nor someone else's. Violations: police order an end to networking, issue a warning, may fine up to 15,000 yuan, and confiscate illegal gains. Run it as a business and the handling authorities can treat it as the crime of illegal business operation. Serious cases: up to 5 years, with a fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal gains imposed alongside or instead. Especially serious: 5 or more years (nationwide)
Note
When this section was written, no published censorship-circumvention precedents were found on the SPC or SPP websites, and local handling varies widely — hence Grade B. For personal use, the heaviest punishment is the warning plus fine written in Article 14 of the interim provisions.
Sources (2 references)
State Council (1997). Interim Provisions on the Administration of International Networking of Computer Information Networks (Articles 6 and 14). https://nyncw.cq.gov.cn/wsdw/zz/zhfb/wlyxxaq/202406/t202406… (republished by the Chongqing Agriculture and Rural Affairs Committee); NPC (2020). Criminal Law (as amended by Criminal Law Amendment XI, Article 225, Item 4). https://jtgl.beijing.gov.cn/jgj/jgxx/flfg/fl/11033925/index…
12

Signed a non-compete? If the company doesn't pay monthly compensation after you leave, press it in writing; after 3 months unpaid you may terminate it; if your role never touched trade secrets, you can ask to have the clause declared invalid

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

A non-compete means you may not work for competitors for a period after leaving — at most 2 years — and the company must pay monthly compensation. With no agreed amount, it's 30% of your average wage over the 12 months before departure, and no lower than the local minimum wage. If the company's own fault leaves it unpaid for 3 months, you can ask to terminate it. From 2025, workers in roles that never touched trade secrets can ask to have the clause declared invalid.

Cost
Costs nothing. When leaving, keep the original non-compete agreement, plus evidence that the company didn't pay monthly
Benefit
Non-competes can bind only senior executives, senior technical personnel, and others with confidentiality obligations. The term is at most 2 years, and the company must pay monthly compensation throughout it. With no agreed amount: 30% of the average wage over the 12 months before departure, and no lower than the local minimum wage. If nonpayment for 3 months is the company's own fault, the worker can ask to terminate the non-compete. If the company terminates it, it owes 3 extra months of compensation. From 2025, workers who never knew of or touched trade secrets in their role can ask to have the clause declared invalid; to the extent the agreed scope exceeds the secrets they actually knew, that part is void. Official case: a pharmaceutical company sued its former chief technology officer Zheng for 7.1 million yuan in penalty damages. The court found his new employer's products not substitutable with the old company's and that the non-compete scope should be limited to the secrets he actually knew — the claim was dismissed in full (nationwide)
Note
Conversely, if the agreement is valid and the company paid monthly, going to a competitor anyway means paying the agreed penalty — and you may still be required to observe the rest of the non-compete period. A non-compete agreed while still employed binds even without extra separate pay.
Sources (4 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2012). Labor Contract Law (2012 revision, Articles 23 and 24). https://yjglj.fushun.gov.cn/008/20260622/d846d3c2-df3d-4c4c… (republished by the Fushun Emergency Management Bureau); Supreme People's Court (2020). Interpretation (I) on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (Articles 36–40). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/282121.html; Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation (II) on Issues Concerning the Application of Law in the Trial of Labor Dispute Cases (Fa Shi [2025] No. 12, Articles 13–15). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/472691.html; Supreme People's Court (2025). Typical labor dispute cases (Case 4). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/472681.html
13

Code written on work time or with company resources belongs to the company; build your own open-source projects on your own time and devices, and keep company code out

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Software written mainly on company equipment, intranet, or business data, with the company bearing responsibility, belongs to the company by copyright — you keep only authorship credit, and the same goes where the contract says so. Written after hours but on a company computer or with business data, it may still count as the company's. Inventions made with company resources belong to the company by patent too.

Cost
Costs nothing. When hired, read the intellectual-property clauses of the employment contract carefully. The hard part: personal projects and company work often share one machine — keep them apart
Benefit
Works created to complete one's unit's work tasks are "works of employment" (things made while doing the job). In the general case, copyright stays with the author; the unit may use it on a priority basis within its business scope, and for 2 years the author may not license third parties to use it the same way. Two categories differ: works like engineering designs and software created mainly with the unit's material and technical conditions and with the unit bearing responsibility; and works the contract assigns to the unit. For these two, authors keep only authorship credit. The unit's material and technical conditions means the company's equipment, intranet, business data, and the like. Inventions completed in the course of the unit's tasks, or mainly with the unit's material and technical conditions, are service inventions: the right to apply for the patent and the granted patent both belong to the unit (nationwide)
Note
Software is written directly into the "copyright belongs to the unit" category; programmers almost never fall into the "author keeps copyright, unit gets 2-year priority use" tier. For "written after hours," using a company computer, the intranet, or company business data can still get it counted as mainly made with the unit's equipment and materials. To keep personal projects clean: use your own machine, don't touch company repos, and don't overlap with company business.
Sources (2 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2020). Copyright Law (2020 revision, Article 18). http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796…; NPC Standing Committee (2020). Patent Law (2020 revision, Article 6). http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308800…
14

Building a product on GPL and other open-source code: open-source as the license requires or change licenses; don't assume 'nobody will notice'

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Copyright infringement is compensated by the other side's losses or your gains — up to 1 to 5 times for willful infringement in serious circumstances. One company hired a competitor's former employees and produced substantially similar software, arguing the plaintiff's software used GPLv2 and should have been open-sourced. The Supreme People's Court held that whether the other side open-sourced its code doesn't affect its copyright — and still ordered the infringement stopped, with 500,000 yuan in damages.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before using someone's open-source code, look at its license (the conditions of use the author states). The GPL family requires products using it to open their source too — that conflicts with selling closed source, and if it conflicts, switch. The hard part: giving up a library you've gotten comfortable with
Benefit
Copyright infringement is compensated by the rights holder's actual losses, or by what the infringer made. Where neither can be computed, it is set by reference to what a normal license purchase would cost. Willful infringement in serious circumstances can draw 1 to 5 times in damages. Where the public interest is harmed, illegal gains may also be confiscated and fines imposed. Official case: (2021) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 51. The defendant hired the plaintiff's former employees and developed gateway software substantially similar to the plaintiff's. The defense argued the plaintiff's software was based on GPLv2 and should have been open-sourced. The Supreme People's Court held that "whether a developer itself violated the GPLv2 and whether it holds software copyright are two independent questions," and ordered the infringement stopped, with 500,000 yuan in damages (nationwide)
Note
The case shows that "the other side used GPL code" is not a reason you may copy it. Conversely, GPL authors suing closed-source commercial users already have effective judgments in China; this section didn't find the originals on the SPC website, so they're not cited. Grade B because open-source license compliance is governed only by general contract and copyright-law provisions — there is no dedicated statute.
Sources (2 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2020). Copyright Law (2020 revision, Articles 53 and 54). http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202011/t20201119_308796…; Supreme People's Court Intellectual Property Court (2022). Copyright infringement case involving "open-source software" ((2021) Zui Gao Fa Zhi Min Zhong No. 51). https://ipc.court.gov.cn/zh-cn/news/view-3042.html
15

For apps, collect only the personal information the service requires; get guardian consent for under-14s; write the privacy policy clearly

Grade BValue: FairBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Collect only the information the service requires; under-14s need guardian consent. Violators are first ordered to correct, and the app may be suspended. Refusing to correct: fines up to 1 million yuan, with responsible persons fined 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. Serious cases: up to 50 million yuan or 5% of last year's revenue, with responsible persons fined 100,000 to 1 million yuan — and those who write the code or build the product can count as responsible persons.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before launch, cross-check the app's requested permission list against the privacy policy and drop any permission you can do without. The hard part: the product side always wants to keep a bit more data that "might come in handy later"
Benefit
Processing personal information requires a clear and reasonable purpose directly related to it, and the manner with the least impact on individuals' rights. Processing requires the individual's consent, or a statutory basis. Under 14: parental or guardian consent is mandatory. Violations: regulators order correction, warn, confiscate illegal gains, and order noncompliant apps to suspend or terminate service. Refusing to correct: fines up to 1 million yuan, and 10,000 to 100,000 yuan for directly responsible supervisors and other directly responsible personnel. Serious circumstances: fines up to 50 million yuan, or up to 5% of the previous year's revenue. Responsible personnel fined 100,000 to 1 million yuan. Such people may also be barred for a period from serving as directors, supervisors, or senior executives of relevant companies. For selling or providing personal information amounting to a crime, see item 4 (nationwide)
Note
In practice, "directly responsible personnel" often lands on the people who write the code and build the product. MIIT regularly names and delists noncompliant apps; this section couldn't verify which specific notice, so none is cited.
Sources (1 reference)
NPC Standing Committee (2021). Personal Information Protection Law (Articles 6, 13, 31, 66). http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088…
16

Complete ICP filing before a website or app goes live, and keep logs for at least 6 months under classified-protection requirements

Grade AValue: FairBasis: FreedomMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Filing is free and takes a few weeks through your cloud provider; domestic servers without filing get shut down. Filing is supposed to be free — charging for it draws fines of 100,000 to 1 million yuan. Logs must be kept a full 6 months; refusing to correct, or actual consequences, draws 10,000 to 100,000 yuan fines.

Cost
Filing is free; through a cloud provider it takes a few weeks. Classified-protection assessments are charged by level. (Classified protection, "Dengbao," is the state's graded set of security-management requirements based on how important the system is; small sites generally don't need an assessment)
Benefit
Commercial internet information services operate under a license; non-commercial ones under a filing. Neither may operate without the license or filing. Unfiled sites are ordered to correct by the telecom authority; refusing, they're ordered to shut down. Operating unlicensed: confiscation of illegal gains plus fines of 3 to 5 times those gains, or 100,000 to 1 million yuan. Not displaying the filing number on the site's home page: 5,000 to 50,000 yuan. Network operators must, under the classified protection system ("Dengbao"), establish security-management systems, guard against attacks, keep network logs at least 6 months, and classify, back up, and encrypt data. Failing that: ordered to correct and warned. Refusing to correct, or where consequences occur: 10,000 to 100,000 yuan, with supervisors fined 5,000 to 50,000 yuan (nationwide)
Note
Without filing, a domestic server's domain won't resolve at all. For how to file, the fine for not displaying the number, and how to check a provider's credentials, see section 26, item 4 (servers in China require filing). Two common traps: filing as individual non-commercial while actually charging fees; and switching domains or entities without updating the filing. Keeping logs 6 months is both a duty and self-protection — when something happens, they prove it wasn't you.
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2011). Measures for the Administration of Internet Information Services (2011 revision, Articles 4, 19, 22). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1860864.htm; NPC Standing Committee (2025). Cybersecurity Law (2025 revision, effective January 1, 2026, Articles 23 and 61; in the 2016 text Articles 21 and 59). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm
17

Before offering generative AI services to the public, run the required security assessment and algorithm filing, and label AI-generated content

Grade BValue: FairBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Generative AI services facing the public that can influence opinion or mobilize people need a security assessment and algorithm filing before launch, plus change and deregistration filings if modified or shut down. Generated images and videos must be labeled. Small tools for your own use, not open to the public, don't trigger any of this. Violations are punished under the Cybersecurity Law and other laws.

Cost
Costs nothing, but goes through the cyberspace administration's process and takes time. Personal small tools simply don't trigger this as long as they're not open to the public
Benefit
Providers of generative AI services with opinion-shaping or social-mobilization capacity must conduct a security assessment per state rules, complete algorithm filing under the algorithm-recommendation management rules, and handle subsequent change and deregistration procedures. Opinion-shaping or social-mobilization capacity means being able to influence public views, or to organize and mobilize people. Providers must label generated content such as images and videos. The measures took effect August 15, 2023 (nationwide)
Note
The measures themselves specify no penalties; for violations you fall back on the Cybersecurity Law, the Data Security Law, and the Personal Information Protection Law — hence Grade B. Civil cases over AI-generated content infringing copyright or portrait rights weren't verified on the SPC website, so none are cited. For relay stations reselling overseas large-model APIs at low prices, see item 19 of this section (AI relay stations).
Sources (1 reference)
Cyberspace Administration of China and six other departments (2023). Interim Measures for the Administration of Generative Artificial Intelligence Services (Articles 12 and 17). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891752…
18

Don't make or distribute tools that auto-skip or block other apps' ads — even free and offline, they can be judged unfair competition

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Build software that skips or blocks other apps' ads for users, and you can be sued for unfair competition. Free of charge can still count — the law's "business operators" include individuals providing services. One browser blocked Mango TV's pre-roll ads by default and paid 800,000 yuan. An app letting users skip Mango TV's splash ads outright paid 80,000 yuan in losses.

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is giving up a very popular little tool. The hard part: you feel you made no money — you just clicked "skip" for the user
Benefit
The law provides that business operators may not use technical means to obstruct or sabotage the normal operation of network products or services lawfully provided by other operators. Operators here means natural persons, legal persons, and unincorporated organizations providing goods or services. Causing damage: compensate by the other side's actual losses, or by what you gained from it, plus their reasonable costs of stopping the infringement. Market regulators may also fine 100,000 to 1 million yuan — 1 to 5 million in serious cases. Official cases: the 720 browser's built-in feature blocked Mango TV's pre-roll and pause ads by default. The first instance dismissed Mango TV's suit; on appeal the Guangzhou Intellectual Property Court reversed, found unfair competition, and awarded 800,000 yuan in economic losses and reasonable costs. In 2021 the Supreme People's Court listed it as a typical case. The "Lanjingling" app let users skip Mango TV's splash ads outright: the first instance ordered it to stop, paying 80,000 yuan in economic losses and 10,000 in reasonable costs. In April 2024 the Beijing Intellectual Property Court upheld it on appeal, holding that it actually blocked the splash ads rather than just clicking "skip" for users (nationwide)
Note
Both judgments applied the pre-revision text. After the 2025 revision the provision moved to Article 13, adding data, algorithms, and platform rules. The appellate court said it ruled on blocking — users clicking "skip" themselves are unaffected. In August 2023, the free Android ad-skipping tool "Litiaotiao" received a lawyer's letter from Tencent, saying it blocked Tencent Browser's ads, constituted unfair competition, and demanded delisting within 48 hours. The developer said it was nonprofit in nature; reports said it only took occasional tips — but it still announced indefinite suspension, and several similar tools shut down too. Only media coverage exists; no suit, no verdict. An individual developer getting a lawyer's letter either stops or pays a lawyer out of pocket to fight: first-instance ordinary procedure runs from 6 months, and lawyer fees generally come from your own pocket. No case found of a purely personal script being pursued. For selling ticket-grabbing software and paying unfair-competition damages, see item 3 of this section (ticket-grabbing and flash-sale scripts). The beneficiary is you.
Sources (6 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2025 revision). Anti-Unfair Competition Law (Articles 2, 13, 22, 29). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181971552b40197b1016e…; Supreme People's Court (2021). Typical antitrust and anti-unfair-competition cases of the people's courts (Case 5: the "720 Browser" unfair competition dispute, (2018) Yue 73 Min Zhong No. 1022). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/324491.html; Beijing Political-Legal Network (2024-04-18). Mango TV v. "Lanjingling" unfair competition case won on appeal (source: Jing Fa Wang Shi). https://www.bj148.org/sa1/ajbb/202404/t20240418_1664299.html; Caijing app (2023-09-10). App blocks splash ads: Tencent sends a lawyer's letter demanding delisting — is that reasonable? (Caijing E-Law, Fan Rui). https://www.mycaijing.com/article/detail/500930?source_id=40 (web archive https://web.archive.org/web/20261005041658/https://www.myca…)
19

Don't run 'AI relay stations' reselling overseas large-model APIs at low prices: a station operator in Shanghai has already been criminally detained

Grade CValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

An AI relay station is a website reselling overseas large-model API access at low prices. One Shanghai station operator was criminally detained for 37 days over it; after release on bail he said himself a conviction was certain, and has already made restitution. The Ministry of State Security has also issued a warning that many relay stations lack operating qualifications and secretly send user data abroad.

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is giving up a low-barrier side business with respectable turnover. To do model aggregation for real, take the straight road: get a business license and use officially authorized models — that costs real money and time
Benefit
In June 2026 the Ministry of State Security issued a risk advisory. It said AI relay stations are a proxy layer sitting between users and model vendors' official services. Some relay stations lack operating qualifications. Some, without compliant data-export qualifications and without the statutory security-assessment process, transmit user-entered data to overseas servers. Some even let users bypass network-access, official-authorization, and cross-border-transfer restrictions. In June 2026 China Newsweek reported a case. In May 2026, a Shanghai relay-station operator posted a shutdown statement in a tech community. He said he had been criminally detained for 37 days by Shanghai police for illegally obtaining large-model API access, and was now on bail pending trial. He said "a conviction is certain sooner or later," had already made restitution and returned gains, and still owed a fine. The report said such stations bulk-register or buy subscription accounts for overseas large models, set up servers abroad as springboards, and resell cheaply to domestic users (nationwide / Shanghai)
Note
This case rests on media reports and the person's own account — no verdict, no police notice, no official word on the charge. The specific charges and sentences circulating online come from lawyer articles and are not cited here. So we can't say "running a relay station is necessarily a crime" — only that someone has already been criminally detained for it. For legitimate model aggregation, charging fees requires a business license — see section 26, item 2 (fee-charging websites need a license). Offering generative AI to the public requires filing — see item 17 of this section (generative AI security assessment). Sending user data abroad has statutory conditions — see section 26, item 10 (user data leaving the country). Users of relay stations face their own risks — see section 14, item 10 (AI relay stations). The beneficiary is you.
Sources (4 references)
Ministry of State Security (2026). "AI relay stations": guard against the risks. https://www.szzg.gov.cn/2026/xwzx/szkx/202606/t20260608_533… (republished from the Ministry of State Security's WeChat account on the Digital China Summit website); China Newsweek (2026-06-22). AI relay stations face a cleanup "storm" (reporter Meng Qian). https://www.chinanews.com/cj/2026/06-22/10644787.shtml (web archive https://web.archive.org/web/20261005042903/https://www.chin…)

12. Startups and business: don't lose the family fortune

24 items

This section counts only money and legal liability; nothing is converted into lifespan. When you open a shop or a company, at which step do your own money, your family's money, and your spouse's money all get lost together? What does the law say, and can you fence it off in advance? The entries that most easily burn through the family fortune — and are easiest to avoid — come first. So entries about signing things come early, and methods that require doing things yourself come later. Entries written from experience alone, with no literature behind them, are marked Grade C. This section's entries are grouped by theme below; entry numbers are in parentheses. Don't stake the family fortune before opening: start a business only with money you can afford to lose (entry 1), don't sign personal guarantees on company loans (entry 2), pick the right entity before opening (entry 3), don't be a nominee shareholder (entry 4), check the MOFCOM filing before buying a franchise (entry 5), ask hard questions before paying anyone to run your online shop (entry 24). Registration and licenses: settle the name and business scope before registering (entry 6), don't open before the license comes through (entry 7). Food: find your tier before entering the food business (entry 8), labels on prepackaged food (entry 9), ordinary food may not claim to cure disease (entry 10), the criminal line in food (entry 11). Taxes and invoices: file a zero return on time even with no income (entry 12), invoice only real transactions (entry 13), anyone claiming the tax bureau is pressing you to pay is a scammer (entry 14). Contracts and hiring: write 'forfeitable deposit', not 'refundable advance', when taking money (entry 15), sign the contract within the first month of hiring (entry 16), pay wages per contract and law (entry 17), follow procedures on the job (entry 22). Products and sourcing: sell before you build (entry 18), run the sample through a mass-production checklist (entry 19), keep invoices and supplier details for every batch (entry 20), artwork must be your own or licensed (entry 21). Exit: when you lose money, exit by procedure (entry 23).

1

Start up only with money you can afford to lose; don't touch the family savings and don't borrow to open

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Money an individually-owned business owes is repaid from the money and property in your own name. If it can't be determined whether the whole family ran it together, it's repaid from the family's assets. Starting a company isn't full protection either: when the company can't repay its debts, the capital you promised to contribute at the start but whose payment deadline hasn't arrived can be demanded from you early. So decide how much to put in by this rule: even if all of it is lost, you can still pay the mortgage and cover medical bills.

Cost
It costs nothing. Before you start, set yourself a number: even if this money is lost entirely, it doesn't affect your mortgage payments, your children, or your medical care. Don't invest beyond that number. Family money and borrowed money don't count toward it. The hard part is resisting the urge to add more when the business seems to be picking up.
Benefit
Losing isn't just losing the money. Debts of an individually-owned business: if you ran the business alone, it's repaid from the money and property in your own name (borne from personal assets). If the family ran it together, or it's unclear who did, it's repaid from the family's money and property (borne from family assets). A debt signed by both spouses is joint debt, repaid by the two of them together. A debt one spouse ratifies afterward counts too. Money borrowed in one spouse's name: as long as the creditor can prove it went into the business the couple ran together, both spouses repay it all the same. Companies have their own rule: when a company can't repay maturing debts, creditors can demand that a shareholder pay in early the capital he or she subscribed in the registered capital but whose payment deadline hasn't arrived (subscribed capital) (nationwide)
Note
"Affordable to lose" means: if this money is lost entirely, you still don't have to sell your house or borrow from relatives to plug the hole. As for how many businesses survive and how long they last on average, no verifiable official figures could be found this round on the National Bureau of Statistics or SAMR websites. So the text gives no numbers, only the legal consequences — hence Grade B.
Sources (2 references)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 56 and 1,064). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; NPC Standing Committee (2023). Company Law (2023 revision, Articles 47 and 54). https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm
2

Don't sign personal guarantees for company loans — spouses above all shouldn't sign

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

What you sign is a "joint-liability guarantee": if the company can't pay, the creditor can skip the company and come straight after you. Only a "general guarantee" forces the creditor to sue the company first, and only the shortfall after the company's assets are sold reaches you. If your spouse signs too, both spouses' assets go in together, and the "limited" in limited company stops protecting you personally.

Cost
It costs nothing. When a bank, supplier, or landlord asks you to sign a "shareholder's personal joint-liability guarantee" or a "spouse's signature", pause first. Signing that page means personally giving up the protection that "company debts don't reach the individual" (waiving limited liability). Don't sign if you can avoid it. If you must sign, sign only a "general guarantee" and write in the maximum amount you'll guarantee. The hard part is holding firm when they keep saying "no signature, no loan".
Benefit
That sentence on the guarantee means: "if the borrower doesn't repay, you will." Written as a "joint-liability guarantee", the creditor can skip the company and come directly to you. Written as a "general guarantee", the creditor must first sue the company or go to arbitration, then have the court compulsorily sell the company's assets to cover the debt. Only the shortfall after the sale falls to you. A debt signed by both spouses is joint debt repaid by the two of them; a debt one spouse ratifies afterward counts too. When the spouse signs, the whole family's assets go in together (nationwide, since 2021)
Note
Banks lending to small and micro businesses almost always require a shareholder's personal joint-liability guarantee. You can still take the loan — just understand exactly what that page signs away before signing, and keep the guaranteed amount under the "affordable to lose" figure from entry 1 (start up only with money you can afford to lose). For general rules on IOUs and guarantees, see section 8, entry 18.
Sources (1 reference)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 681, 687, 688, and 1,064). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
3

Choose the right entity before opening: sole proprietors and partners are liable to the last cent; only limited companies are 'limited'

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Sole proprietors and general partners are liable to the last cent: however much is owed, that's how much they repay. Shareholders of a limited company are liable only up to the amount they subscribed at registration. But what you subscribe, you must actually pay in within 5 years: write 1 million and you may owe 1 million. If you mix the company's accounts with your own, the "limited" fails too.

Cost
Registration is done online on the local government services portal, a few hours each time. After opening a limited company there's monthly bookkeeping and tax filing — a permanent overhead: doing it yourself costs time, hiring a bookkeeper costs money, and prices vary by region.
Benefit
Debts of an individually-owned business are repaid from personal money and property, or from the family's. Partners in a general partnership bear unlimited joint liability for the partnership's debts: however much is owed gets repaid, and it isn't over until it's all repaid. A creditor can also single out just one partner and demand the whole amount. A limited partnership is different: its limited partners are liable only up to what they subscribed (limited to the subscribed capital). Shareholders of a limited liability company are likewise liable only up to their subscribed capital (limited to the subscribed capital amount). But "limited" fails in three situations. First, the subscribed capital must be paid in full within 5 years of incorporation; when the company can't repay maturing debts, creditors can demand early payment. Second, capital paid in and then withdrawn (capital withdrawal) must be returned. Third, using the company as a shell to dodge debts. A company with only one shareholder that can't prove the company's money is separate from the owner's falls under this third case too. Under the last two, you personally join in repaying the company's debts (joint liability) (nationwide, since July 2024)
Note
"Limited" presumes a clean line between company and private money: don't mix company and personal accounts, don't pay household expenses from company money, and keep complete records. Don't fill in a big registered capital just to look good. Whatever you subscribe, you must actually pay in within 5 years. Fill in 1 million and that's 1 million of potential debt.
Sources (3 references)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 56). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; NPC Standing Committee (2006). Partnership Enterprise Law (2006 revision, Article 2). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2006/content_413955.htm; NPC Standing Committee (2023). Company Law (2023 revision, Articles 4, 23, 47, 53, and 54). https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm
4

Don't be a nominee shareholder; don't hold equity on someone else's behalf

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

If your name is on the register, you are the shareholder in law. The capital you subscribed must be paid in on time; fail, and you both pay it up and compensate the company's losses. If other shareholders never actually paid in their capital when the company was founded, you answer for the shortfall along with them. Someone else runs the business; the debt lands in your name.

Cost
It costs nothing. If anyone asks to "borrow your ID card to list you as a shareholder" or to "park the shares in your name for now", refuse flat out.
Benefit
A shareholder on the register is the shareholder in law. Within the deadline set in the articles of association, you must pay in every cent of the capital you subscribed (pay subscribed capital in full). If you miss the deadline, you pay it up and compensate the company's losses besides. If a shareholder never actually paid in when the company was founded, the other founding shareholders jointly cover that shortfall (joint liability). When the company can't repay maturing debts, creditors can demand early payment of capital not yet due. The person actually running the business isn't on the register; the debt is in your name (nationwide, since July 2024)
Note
Between the nominee shareholder and the real investor, a nominee-holding agreement stands unless it falls under statutory grounds for invalidity. But for the real investor to have their name substituted in, a majority of the other shareholders must consent. If the nominee sells or pledges the equity, the court applies the bona fide acquisition rules of the Civil Code. If the buyer was unaware, paid a reasonable price, and completed registration, the real investor can't get the equity back — only claim damages from the nominee. A draft of a new interpretation (for public comment) came out in September 2025; once finalized and effective it will repeal the present one in its entirety, so the 2020 revision — still in force as of September 2026 — governs. On the risks of being a nominee legal representative, see section 8, entry 28.
Sources (3 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2023). Company Law (2023 revision, Articles 47, 49, 50, and 54). https://www.gov.cn/yaowen/liebiao/202312/content_6923395.htm; Supreme People's Court (2020 revision). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (III) (Fa Shi [2011] No. 3, amended in 2014 by Fa Shi [2014] No. 2 and in 2020 by Fa Shi [2020] No. 18, Articles 24 and 25): "Where no ground for invalidity prescribed by law exists, the people's court shall find the contract valid"; "Where the actual investor requests the company to change the shareholder registration without the consent of a majority of the other shareholders... the people's court shall not support the request"; "Where a nominee shareholder's disposal of the equity causes loss to the actual investor, and the actual investor requests compensation from the nominee shareholder, the people's court shall support the request". https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181799def980179ac07a9… (National Laws and Regulations Database); Supreme People's Court (2025). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of the Company Law of the People's Republic of China (draft for public comment), Article 90. https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/477881.html
5

Before buying a franchise, check the MOFCOM filing, obtain written disclosure, and write a 'cooling-off period' into the contract

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

By rule, the brand must first have opened 2 directly-operated stores of its own and run them for a full year, and must file with the commerce authorities within 15 days of signing. Before you sign, it must give you written disclosure on 12 items, including the franchise fees, how the deposit is refunded, and whether existing stores make money. No filing on record, unwilling to hand over the materials, or contract shown only after you pay — walk away.

Cost
It costs nothing. Check the Ministry of Commerce's "Commercial Franchise Information Management System" website to see whether the brand has filed. Then require the other side to give you, before signing, the written disclosure of what it must disclose, together with the contract text. A few hours of work.
Benefit
The regulation requires the brand (the "franchisor" in the regulation) to have at least 2 directly-owned, directly-operated stores, open for more than 1 year. Counting from the day the first franchise contract is signed, it must file with the competent commerce department within 15 days. Not filing: a fine of 10,000 to 50,000 yuan. Still not filing past the deadline: a fine of 50,000 to 100,000 yuan, plus a public announcement. Before signing, it must hand you written disclosure covering 12 items. These include which kinds of franchise fees it charges and how much each is, under what conditions the deposit is refunded, how many franchise stores currently exist and how their business is doing. Plus summaries of audit reports for the past 2 years and lawsuits and arbitrations from the past 5 years. The contract must also state that for a period after signing, the franchisee can unilaterally walk away (unilateral rescission). If the brand conceals facts or gives false information, the franchisee may terminate the contract (nationwide, since May 2007)
Note
No filing on record, no disclosure documents, or contract shown only after payment — walk away. The "cooling-off period" is those days after signing when you can still unilaterally walk away. The number of days is set by the contract; the regulation only says "a certain period", so demand at signing that the days be written in. For the brand's disclosed "average sales, gross profit, and net profit of existing franchise stores", press for where the numbers come from — the measures require the brand to state its sources. For schemes that avoid the word "franchise" and charge only "shop management" or "store-opening training" service fees, see entry 24 (shop-management services and opening courses).
Sources (3 references)
State Council (2007). Regulation on the Administration of Commercial Franchise Operations (State Council Decree No. 485, Articles 7, 8, 12, 22, 23, and 25). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_417…; Ministry of Commerce (2012). Measures for the Administration of Information Disclosure in Commercial Franchise Operations (MOFCOM Order No. 2 of 2012, Articles 5 and 9). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2012/content_2177025.htm; Ministry of Commerce. Commercial Franchise Information Management System. https://txjy.syggs.mofcom.gov.cn/
6

Before registering, settle the name, premises, business scope, and registered capital; with complete paperwork you can get the license on the spot

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Registration itself is free — the registration fee was abolished in 2015. Only five items must be submitted: the application form, proof of identity or qualification, premises documents, the articles of association or partnership agreement (sole proprietors don't need this), plus anything else the regulations specifically require. With complete paperwork the license is issued on the spot; if it can't be issued on the spot, it's done within 3 working days. Whatever you're charged is usually an agent's errand fee.

Cost
The registration step costs nothing. The registration fee for enterprises and individually-owned businesses was abolished from January 1, 2015. Do it yourself on the local government services portal, or at the government service hall — a few hours each time. Getting the official seal carved, hiring a bookkeeper, or renting a registered address (address hosting) are market services you buy, not government fees.
Benefit
The regulation fixes the required documents at five items. "(1) The application form." "(2) The applicant's qualification documents and the natural person's identity proof." "(3) Documents relating to the domicile or main place of business." "(4) The articles of association of a company, non-company enterprise legal person, or farmers' professional cooperative (union), or the partnership agreement of a partnership enterprise." "(5) Other documents required by laws, administrative regulations, and the market regulation department of the State Council." In plain words: an application form; something proving who you are, or that you're qualified to do this; something proving the shop or office is yours to use; the articles of association or partnership agreement; plus anything else the regulations specifically require. A company also files appointment documents and identity proofs for the legal representative, directors, supervisors, and senior officers. A sole proprietor doesn't file articles of association. The name is "declared by the applicant on their own responsibility under the law" — you choose it and file it yourself. Registered capital "adopts the subscription registration system": you write down what you promise to contribute; nothing has to be paid on the spot. Business scope is picked from categories published by the registration authority. With complete documents in correct form, the application "is confirmed and registered on the spot." If it can't be done on the spot, it's done "within 3 working days"; complex cases get 3 more working days. "The issue date on the business license is the establishment date of the market entity": the day printed on the license is the day the company or shop came into being (nationwide, since March 2022)
Note
Registration itself is free; whatever you're charged is mostly an agent's errand fee. Seal-carving prices are set by the market. The General Office of the State Council has expressly "prohibited designating particular seal-makers to make official seals", so if someone says "you must carve your seal at the designated place", you needn't accept it. The registered capital figure doesn't affect appearances; it only sets the cap on your liability, and it must be paid in within 5 years — see entry 3 of this section (choose the right entity before opening). If the business scope includes licensed items, you can't open until the license is issued — see entry 7 of this section (trades that need permits).
Sources (3 references)
State Council (2021). Regulation on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (State Council Decree No. 746, Articles 10, 13, 14, 16, 19, and 21). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5636139.htm ; SAMR (2022). Implementation Rules for the Regulation on the Administration of Market Entity Registration (SAMR Order No. 52 of 2022, Articles 12, 25, and 26). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-03/02/content_567… ; Ministry of Finance and National Development and Reform Commission (2014). Notice on Cancelling, Suspending, and Exempting a Batch of Administrative and Institutional Fees (Cai Shui [2014] No. 101, Annex 1). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2014-12/23/content_5023513.htm
7

In trades that need permits, don't open until the permit is in hand

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Open without a permit and the lightest outcome is an order to shut down, confiscation of what you earned, and a fine of up to 10,000 yuan. If you deal in goods subject to monopoly or exclusive sale, or run securities, futures, insurance, or payment settlement businesses, serious cases constitute the crime of illegal business operation, with a base sentence of up to 5 years. Renovating before applying, or "trial operating" before the permit arrives, are the most common missteps.

Cost
It costs nothing. Before opening, find out whether the business you want to run needs a license. Catering and selling food require a food business license. Only selling prepackaged food made by others needs no license, just a filing. Open for business only after the permit is issued.
Benefit
Doing business without the required license is investigated and punished by the department designated in laws and regulations. Operating without a license where the law specifies no penalty: ordered to stop, illegal gains confiscated, plus a fine of up to 10,000 yuan. There's a heavier tier. Dealing without permission in goods subject to monopoly, exclusive sale, or restricted trading under laws and regulations. Running securities, futures, insurance, or payment settlement businesses without approval. In these two situations, serious cases constitute the crime of illegal business operation: up to 5 years of fixed-term imprisonment or criminal detention (short-term custody), plus a fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal gains. Especially serious cases: over 5 years (nationwide)
Note
Licensing conditions for finance, healthcare, and private tutoring each have their own dedicated laws; this entry verifies only the general enforcement rules and the criminal provisions. Bubble-tea shops and snack shops count as catering services and need a food business license. Renovating before applying, or trial-operating before the permit arrives, are common pitfalls. For the tiers of the food trade and whether selling fresh meat and vegetables needs a license, see entry 8 (find your tier in the food business first).
Sources (3 references)
State Council (2017). Measures on Investigating and Punishing Unlicensed and Unregistered Business Operations (State Council Decree No. 684, Articles 5, 6, and 13). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-08/23/content_521…; SAMR (2023). Measures for the Administration of Food Business Licensing and Filing (SAMR Order No. 78 of 2023, Article 4). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10606/202307/content_…; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 225). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml
8

In the food business, first find which tier you're in: production and catering need licenses; selling only prepackaged food needs only filing; fresh meat and vegetables need no permit

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If you make things yourself to sell — a snack shop, braised foods, baking, homemade pickles — you need a license. Only selling prepackaged food made by others needs no license; just file with the market regulation department at or above the county level. Selling fresh meat and vegetables needs no permit. Work without one and the minimum fine is 50,000 to 100,000 yuan — more than the capital behind most small businesses.

Cost
The license itself is free. But your premises and facilities must meet standards, and the on-site inspection plus permit processing takes a few weeks. Meat sellers must also keep quarantine certificates and meat quality inspection certificates for every batch.
Benefit
Food Safety Law: food businesses need a license first. Producing food, selling food, and catering all require a license under the law. "However, selling edible agricultural products or only prepackaged food requires no license. Those selling only prepackaged food shall file with the food safety regulation department of the local people's government at or above the county level." Edible agricultural products means unprocessed things like fresh meat and vegetables. Prepackaged food is food made by others and sold in its packaging. "The specific management measures for small food production and processing workshops and food vendors are set by provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the central government" — those two categories follow each province's own rules. Running a food business without a license: the illegal gains, the food, and the tools, equipment, and ingredients are confiscated in full. If the total value of the goods at sale prices (goods value) is under 10,000 yuan, an additional fine of 50,000 to 100,000 yuan. If the goods value is 10,000 yuan or more, a fine of 10 to 20 times the goods value. Pig Slaughter Regulation: pigs may only be slaughtered at state-designated slaughterhouses, with official centralized quarantine. "Except for rural households slaughtering for their own consumption, which are exempt from designated slaughter, no unit or individual may engage in pig slaughter without designation." "Pig products produced or sold by units and individuals engaged in selling pig products or producing and processing meat foods, and by catering operators and collective dining facilities, must be pig products from designated pig slaughterhouses that have passed quarantine and meat quality inspection." So the pork you sell or use must come from a designated slaughterhouse and pass both checks. Slaughtering pigs privately outside a designated slaughterhouse: ordered to shut down; the pigs, the slaughter tools and equipment, and the illegal gains are confiscated together; the fine matches the unlicensed-food tier above. Animal Epidemic Prevention Law: animal products sold or transported must travel with quarantine certificates and quarantine marks. Without them: ordered to correct, plus a fine of up to one times the goods value of comparable compliant goods. Judicial interpretation: where food made or sold by small workshops or food vendors fails food safety standards, courts shall support buyers' claims for ten-times compensation (punitive damages — the extra amount beyond the refund) (nationwide)
Note
Thresholds for small workshops, small caterers, and food vendors are set by each province; this entry gives no specific numbers. Visit your province's market regulation website and search "regulation on small food workshops, small caterers, and food vendors" for the local version. Selling homemade food online doesn't save you a license because it's "online" — if it needs a license, it needs one. Beyond licensing, this section's general rules also apply: entity and registration, see entry 6 (settle the name, premises, scope, and capital before registering); whether other trades need permits, see entry 7 (trades that need permits). For how much buyers can claim, see section 5, entry 31 (ten-times compensation for food).
Sources (4 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2025, third amendment). Food Safety Law (Articles 35, 36, and 122). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=7b5a76d0461745a08d3f964916…; State Council (2021). Regulation on the Administration of Pig Slaughter (State Council Decree No. 742, Articles 2, 23, and 31). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/22/content_562…; NPC Standing Committee (2021 revision). Animal Epidemic Prevention Law (Articles 51 and 100). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080817703add2017737395a…; Supreme People's Court (2024). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases of Punitive Damages in Food and Drug Disputes (Fa Shi [2024] No. 9, Article 4). http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/bf531a70471f10d377788f2…
9

Bag it and sell it, and it's prepackaged food: the label must carry production date, shelf life, and ingredient list — not one missing

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Food sold in packaging is prepackaged food in law: the package must carry a label, and nine items must be marked, production date and shelf life included. Bulk food must also show the name, dates, and the seller's name and address. Missing required items: goods value under 10,000 yuan means a 5,000 to 50,000 yuan fine; at 10,000 yuan or more, 5 to 10 times the value.

Cost
Labels run from a few cents to a few dimes each. Every batch needs correct dates and ingredients filled in — it takes some time.
Benefit
Food Safety Law: prepackaged food (food sold in packaging) must have a label on the package. The label must state the name, specifications, net content, and production date; the ingredients or ingredient list; the producer's name, address, and contact details; and the shelf life. Also the product standard code, storage conditions, the standard generic names of any food additives used, and the production license number. Anything else required by laws, regulations, or food safety standards must be labeled too. Bulk food is the unpackaged, weighed-to-order kind. Selling bulk food: the container and outer packaging must also show the food's name, the production date or production batch number, the shelf life, and the producer's or seller's name, address, and contact details. Making or selling prepackaged food without a label, or with a label or instructions that violate this law: illegal gains and food confiscated. If the goods value is under 10,000 yuan, an additional fine of 5,000 to 50,000 yuan. If the goods value is 10,000 yuan or more, a fine of 5 to 10 times the goods value. Serious cases: ordered to halt production and business until the license is revoked. A label or instructions with only minor flaws (defects) that neither affect food safety nor mislead consumers: ordered to correct first; a fine of up to 2,000 yuan only if they refuse. The new General Standard for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods, numbered GB 7718-2025, was issued on March 16, 2025 and takes effect on March 16, 2027, with a two-year transition in between. It requires an independent area on the package showing the production date and the end date of the shelf life together. The dates must use high-contrast, easily readable fonts and colors, arranged in year-month-day order (nationwide)
Note
Label problems come in two kinds, and both fines and compensation follow the split. One is minor flaws — typos, non-standard font sizes — that neither affect food safety nor mislead anyone. For these the market regulator only orders a correction, with a fine of up to 2,000 yuan on refusal, and buyers can't claim ten-times compensation. The other is missing required items, like a missing production date or shelf life. The judicial interpretation says explicitly this is not a minor flaw: the fine is set by goods value — 5,000 to 50,000 yuan under 10,000 yuan of value, 5 to 10 times the value at 10,000 yuan or more. And buyers can separately claim ten times the food's price as compensation, with a floor of 1,000 yuan (see section 5, entry 31, ten-times compensation for food). For GB 7718-2025's item-by-item requirements, this entry verified only the dates and display rules given in the announcement and official interpretations; the standard's own text governs the specifics.
Sources (4 references)
