Announcement on Issuing 50 Food Safety National Standards, Including the General Standard for the Labeling of Prepackaged Foods (GB 7718-2025), and 9 Amendment Sheets (Announcement No. 2 of 2025). https://jkw.lasa.gov.cn/wswyh/wjzl/202504/a90766908ef24869a… (full text of the announcement reposted by the Lhasa Municipal Health Commission); Supreme People's Court (2024). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Cases of Punitive Damages in Food and Drug Disputes (Fa Shi [2024] No. 9, Articles 6 and 8). http://gongbao.court.gov.cn/Details/bf531a70471f10d377788f2… (the split between label flaws and missing mandatory items); Beijing Municipal Administration for Market Regulation (2026). Can't find the production date? Food labels are in for a change! Key points of the new rules you must know. https://scjgj.beijing.gov.cn/zwxx/scjgdt/202605/t20260507_4… (effective dates, transition period, and the new date-display requirements)
10

Ordinary food may never claim to cure disease: labels, manuals, ads, and livestream scripts all count

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Ordinary food's labels, instructions, and ads may never claim to prevent or cure disease. Apart from ads for medical care, drugs, and medical devices, no other ad may claim to cure disease or use words that sound like medicine. The fine is 1 to 3 times the advertising cost; if the cost can't be determined, 100,000 to 200,000 yuan. Serious cases can add revocation of the business license.

Cost
It costs nothing. Go through your slogans, product detail pages, and livestream scripts. The hard part is resisting phrases like "lowers the three highs (blood pressure, blood sugar, blood lipids)" or "cures constipation".
Benefit
Food Safety Law: "Labels and instructions for food and food additives must not contain false content and must not involve disease prevention or treatment. Producers and sellers are responsible for the content of the labels and instructions they provide." "Food advertising content shall be true and lawful, must not contain false content, and must not involve disease prevention or treatment. Food producers and sellers are responsible for the truthfulness and legality of their food advertising." In plain terms: packaging, instructions, and ads may never claim to prevent or cure disease, and the seller answers for whatever is written. Exaggerating or deceiving consumers about food in ads is fined under the Advertising Law. The Advertising Law has its own ban: "Apart from ads for medical care, drugs, and medical devices, all other advertising is barred from involving disease treatment functions and from using medical terms, or terms easily confused with drugs or medical devices." So no ad outside those three categories may claim to cure disease, or use words that sound like medicine or medical devices. Violating this: the ad is ordered stopped. The party that placed the ad (the advertiser) must also publicly clarify and undo the impact where the ad ran. Then a fine of 1 to 3 times the advertising cost. If the advertising cost can't be determined, or was reported clearly too low: a fine of 100,000 to 200,000 yuan. Serious cases: 3 to 5 times the advertising cost, or 200,000 to 1,000,000 yuan, plus possible revocation of the business license — an end to the business altogether (nationwide)
Note
"Health functions" are also off-limits for ordinary food. A health food's allowed health-function claims come only from the national catalog, and the product must be registered or filed — ordinary food never goes through that process. For how buyers can spot these scripts, see section 6, entry 10 (don't spend big on health supplements to fix your body). Beyond packaging and ads, product detail pages, livestream scripts, and social-media copy all count as advertising content — once published, the record exists.
Sources (2 references)

Food has a criminal threshold: selling diseased meat or substandard goods is already a crime; adulterating with toxic or harmful substances means 5 years minimum, regardless of amount

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The previous entries fine money; this one imprisons people. Selling meat from diseased or dead animals, meat that failed inspection, or goods with pesticide residues, veterinary drug residues, or heavy metals severely above limits is already a crime as long as it "could" cause serious food poisoning — no one actually needs to get sick. Up to 3 years. Mixing toxic or harmful non-food ingredients into food starts at a tier of up to 5 years, no matter how much you sold.

Cost
It costs nothing. Follow the entry-8 playbook (find your tier in the food business first): keep quarantine certificates and purchase receipts, and put in the ingredient list only things whose approval numbers can be looked up.
Benefit
Criminal Law Article 143 covers this tier: food you make or sell fails food safety standards. As long as it "is sufficient to cause serious food poisoning or other serious foodborne illness", it's a crime. Up to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment or criminal detention (short-term custody), plus a fine. Causing serious harm to health, or other serious circumstances: 3 to 7 years plus a fine. Especially serious consequences: over 7 years up to life imprisonment, plus a fine or confiscation of all property. Article 144: mixing toxic or harmful non-food ingredients into food you make or sell, or knowingly selling food so adulterated: up to 5 years of fixed-term imprisonment plus a fine. Serious harm to health or other serious circumstances: 5 to 10 years plus a fine. Causing death, or other especially serious circumstances: punished under Article 141 (over 10 years, life, or death). The Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate issued a joint interpretation (the "Two Supremes" interpretation). It lists the situations that count as "sufficient to cause serious food poisoning or other serious foodborne illness". One: "containing pathogenic microorganisms, pesticide residues, veterinary drug residues, biological toxins, heavy metals, or other contaminants severely exceeding standard limits". Two: "being meat or meat products of livestock, poultry, beasts, or aquatic animals that died of disease, died of unknown cause, or failed inspection and quarantine". Three: "being goods the state expressly bans from production or sale for disease control or other special needs". Four: "being formula foods for special medical purposes, or staple and supplementary foods for infants and young children, whose nutrients severely fail food safety standards". Additives overdosed or misapplied, to the point of causing the above consequences, are convicted under Article 143 as well. What counts as a "toxic or harmful non-food ingredient" isn't up to you. One category is substances laws and regulations forbid adding to food. Another is substances on lists published by the relevant departments of the State Council, such as banned pesticides and drugs barred from use on food animals. One more situation also counts as "other serious circumstances" under Article 144: producing or selling 100,000 yuan to under 200,000 yuan worth. The location being in or around primary or secondary school campuses, childcare facilities, or elderly-care institutions. The buyers being minors or the elderly. Slaughtering and selling pigs in a private, self-built slaughterhouse outside the designated slaughterhouses, in serious cases, is punished as illegal business operation. Doing 100,000 yuan or more in business, or making 50,000 yuan or more in gains, counts as "serious circumstances" (nationwide)
Note
The line between this and the previous three entries: whether food safety itself is breached. Operating unlicensed, missing label items, and hyping cures cost money. Selling diseased meat, substandard goods, misusing additives, or mixing in non-food ingredients goes to criminal procedure. The easiest defense is still the entry-8 playbook (find your tier in the food business first). Source meat only from designated slaughterhouses. Keep quarantine certificates and meat quality inspection certificates for every batch. Use only ingredients whose approval numbers can be looked up. So-called "cheap clearance meat" and "trimmings from who knows where" cause the most trouble. The original Supreme People's Court Gazette page returned a 502 this round, so two provincial official reposts are cited, checked word-for-word against each other.
Sources (3 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2020 amendment). Criminal Law (Articles 141, 143, and 144). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181796a636a0179822a19… (National Laws and Regulations Database); Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2021). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases Endangering Food Safety (Fa Shi [2021] No. 24, Articles 1, 2, 5, 7, 9, 17, and 18, effective January 1, 2022). https://scjg.hebei.gov.cn/info/79117 (full text reposted by the Hebei Provincial Administration for Market Regulation), https://sft.ln.gov.cn/sft/ywgz/zfflgw/xzys/2525860BD0F843EF… (full text reposted by the Liaoning Provincial Department of Justice; the two texts checked word-for-word identical)
12

Getting the license starts your filing duty: even with no income, file a zero return on time (submit the all-zeros form)

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

With a license comes the duty to file taxes on time. Even having earned nothing, you still file — just fill the form with all zeros. Not filing: a fine of up to 2,000 yuan first; serious cases, 2,000 to 10,000 yuan. Failing to file any tax for three consecutive months gets you automatically flagged as an abnormal taxpayer, and you can't issue invoices anymore.

Cost
It costs nothing. File monthly or quarterly yourself on the e-tax bureau — a few minutes each time. Hiring a bookkeeper is a separate market expense. If you have employees, you must also complete social insurance registration within 30 days of establishment. The hard part is remembering to file on time in months with no business.
Benefit
"Taxpayers with no tax payable within the filing period shall still complete tax filing as required": no tax is due this period, but the form must still be filed. Not filing on time: "the tax authority shall order correction within a time limit and may impose a fine of up to 2,000 yuan; in serious cases, a fine of 2,000 to 10,000 yuan." Not filing and underpaying tax: the tax is recovered, the daily-accruing late-payment surcharge must be paid on top, plus a fine "of 50 percent to 5 times the underpaid tax". The surcharge accrues at 0.05 percent per day. "Taxpayers failing to file any tax for three consecutive months are automatically designated abnormal taxpayers by the tax administration system, which suspends their invoice ledger and invoice use." Three months of nothing filed and the system flags you itself: no invoices can be obtained or issued. It clears automatically after you file the back returns and accept the penalty. Employers "shall, within 30 days of establishment... apply to the local social insurance agency for social insurance registration" (nationwide)
Note
After "multi-license-in-one" reform there's no separate tax registration. Log into the e-tax bureau with the unified social credit code on your business license, confirm your registration details, and declare which taxes you'll pay. Individually-owned businesses and sole proprietorship enterprises pay individual income tax on business income: first pay an installment "within 15 days after the end of the month or quarter", then "complete the annual settlement before March 31 of the year following the income" (a full-year reckoning — overpayments refunded, shortfalls made up). No business yet doesn't mean no filing; a zero return is still a filing. Ignore it for three months and you become an abnormal taxpayer with invoices suspended — and you can't use the simple deregistration procedure either; see entry 23 of this section (exit by procedure when you lose money).

13

Invoicing follows real transactions only; as a small-scale taxpayer, use your full tax-free quota

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

If you're a small-scale taxpayer filing the simplified way, sales under 100,000 yuan a month or 300,000 yuan a quarter are VAT-free. What would have been taxed at 3% is also cut to 1% over the same period. The reverse: "getting invoices from others to offset costs" is false invoicing — the starting tier is up to 3 years, plus a fine of 20,000 to 200,000 yuan.

Cost
It costs nothing. Don't buy invoices, don't sell invoices, and don't "run others' money through your books" with invoices. Invoice and file for the business that actually happened.
Benefit
The small scale that files the simplified way is called a small-scale taxpayer. The law reads: "where sales fall below the threshold, VAT is exempt." That line is the threshold. From January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2027, the threshold is 100,000 yuan per month, 300,000 yuan per quarter, and 1,000 yuan per transaction or per day — below the line, no VAT. Over the same period, what would have been 3% is reduced to 1%, except for selling or renting out real estate and transferring land-use rights. The reverse: issuing VAT special invoices with no real transaction behind them, or other invoices usable to offset tax, means up to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment or criminal detention, plus a fine of 20,000 to 200,000 yuan. Issuing for others, issuing for yourself, having others issue for you, or brokering it for others — all count. Larger tax amounts involved: 3 to 10 years. Huge amounts: over 10 years or life imprisonment (nationwide)
Note
The VAT Law takes effect January 1, 2026. The two earlier small-scale taxpayer relief announcements — No. 19 of 2023 and No. 1 of 2023 — cease to apply or are repealed accordingly. The monetary thresholds didn't change, but the basis did; this entry has been updated to the new document. The Criminal Law page is the 1997 version; Article 205's sentencing tiers were later adjusted by amendments, so this entry states only the tiers verified and left unaltered. The exemption is VAT only — income tax is separate. "Getting invoices from others to offset costs" is false invoicing, not tax saving.
Sources (3 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2024). Value-Added Tax Law (effective January 1, 2026, Article 23). https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100009/c5237365/content.…; Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration (2026). Announcement on the Connection of VAT Preferential Policies after the VAT Law Takes Effect (Announcement No. 10 of 2026 of the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration, Articles 1, 2, and 6). https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c102416/c5247434/content.…; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 205). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml
14

Anyone claiming to be the tax bureau pressing you to pay or file is a scammer; handle taxes only through the e-tax bureau or 12366

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The tax authorities will never phone asking for your bank card password, payment password, or SMS verification codes, nor give you an account to transfer taxes into. Genuine on-site inspectors must show an inspection notice and an inspection certificate. Get one of these calls: hang up first, then call 12366 to verify. Money already transferred: call 110 or 96110 immediately to freeze the payment.

Cost
It costs nothing. Calls or texts about a "tax spot check", an "abnormal account", or "fines if you don't file", or a stranger adding you as a friend: hang up first, don't reply. Then call 12366, or the landline of the competent tax authority, to verify.
Benefit
The tax administration's warning, verbatim: "Tax authorities will not ask through WeChat mini-programs, phone calls, or text messages for bank card passwords, payment passwords, account balances, or SMS verification codes related to bank card payments and receipts." "Some criminals impersonate tax officers to approach taxpayers under the names of 'assisted tax filing', 'tax-benefit handling', 'policy coaching', and the like." To verify, call "the 12366 tax and payment service hotline or the landline of the competent tax authority." Genuine on-site audits (inspection) "must present the inspection notice and the inspection certificate." "Taxes may only be paid through the e-tax bureau or at the tax service hall; tax authorities will not provide designated accounts." There's also a rule for intermediaries that handle taxes for others: "extorting taxpayers or withholding agents in the name of tax authorities or tax personnel" draws fines by severity. Swindling taxpayers and tax-withholding units under the banner of the tax bureau and its officers is exactly this situation. Impersonating state functionaries to deceive: 10 to 15 days of detention, plus possible fines of up to 1,000 yuan. Where conduct meets both the fraud offense and the impersonation-swindling offense, "convict and punish under the provision with the heavier penalty" (whichever article carries the heavier punishment governs) (nationwide)
Note
These scams specifically target newly registered individually-owned businesses and small companies. The script: "our system shows you haven't filed; handle it today or be fined" — then they steer you to their own official account or mini-program and charge a few hundred yuan a pop. That filing itself is free and takes minutes to do yourself. Hiring a market bookkeeping firm isn't illegal, but it isn't a government body and won't press you in the tax bureau's name. Already paid or transferred: call 110 or 96110 immediately to freeze the payment — see section 8, entry 2 (freezing payments after being scammed).

When collecting money, contract a forfeitable deposit, not a refundable advance; spell out the penalty amount; and vet credit terms like a lender

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Only when the contract says "forfeitable deposit" does the double rule apply: if you breach, you can't get the money back; if the other side breaches, they owe you double. Any part above 20% of the contract value doesn't count. Written as a "refundable advance", none of this exists in law. Extending credit terms means lending your own money for nothing; if the other side goes under, it's a bad debt.

Cost
It costs nothing. Write "forfeitable deposit" in the contract, at no more than 20% of the total contract value. Collect money before shipping. Before agreeing to goods-first-payment-later (credit terms), vet the other side first.
Benefit
A deposit counts only once the money actually reaches the other side (formed upon actual delivery). If the paying party breaches, the money is forfeit. If the receiving party breaches, they must return the original amount and pay an equal amount on top (double return). Any part exceeding 20% of the total contract value (the value of the main contract) doesn't count as deposit. A stipulated penalty wildly above or below the actual loss can be adjusted down or up by the court on a party's request. Where both a penalty clause and a deposit are written into the contract, on an actual breach you must choose one — you can't take both (nationwide, since 2021)
Note
The "refundable advance" gets none of the deposit rules in the Civil Code; it's generally treated as a mere prepayment. This is the standard practice reading; this section did not verify case law. Credit terms mean lending your money to the other side interest-free; if they collapse, it's a bad debt. Before extending credit, check the other side's record on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publication System — see whether it has been sued.
Sources (1 reference)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 585, 586, 587, and 588). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
16

Sign a written contract within the first month of hiring and complete social insurance registration within 30 days

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: a lotTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

An employee who has worked a full month with no written contract signed earns double wages from the second month on, counted up to the one-year mark. Social insurance must be registered within 30 days of hiring; skip it and the fine is 1 to 3 times the contributions due. In law there is no such thing as "the employee voluntarily waives social insurance".

Cost
The employer's share of social insurance keeps being paid, at rates that vary by region. The contract itself costs nothing — just use your local human resources and social security bureau's contract template.
Benefit
An employee who has worked more than a month but less than a year with no written contract earns double wages each month. Counting from the first day of work, complete social insurance registration for them within 30 days. If not: correction ordered first. Past the deadline: a fine of 1 to 3 times the contributions due, plus 500 to 3,000 yuan for the person in charge of handling it. Social insurance paid late or not in full: from the day it fell into arrears, a surcharge of 0.05 percent per day accrues (late-payment surcharge). Still unpaid past the deadline: another fine of 1 to 3 times the arrears. The employer must declare on its own and pay in full on time. Only statutory causes beyond one's control, like natural disasters, permit late or reduced payment. There is no "voluntary waiver by the employee" (nationwide)
Note
Double wages run from the second month until the one-year mark — the longer you drag, the more it costs. If an employee without a contract or social insurance has a workplace injury, or goes to arbitration after leaving, back payments plus fines plus compensation usually dwarf what you saved.
Sources (2 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2007). Labor Contract Law (Articles 10 and 82). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm; NPC Standing Committee (2010). Social Insurance Law (2018 amendment, Articles 58, 60, 84, and 86). https://www.mohrss.gov.cn/xxgk2020/fdzdgknr/zcfg/fl/202011/…
17

Pay wages per contract and law; put raises, loans, and bonuses in writing

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Pay wages in full and on time per contract and law. If you fall behind, the employee can go straight to court for a payment order. Raises, bonuses, and advances settled by word of mouth: in a real dispute, whoever can't produce evidence loses. Lending an employee your own money requires a written IOU stating the amount, interest, and repayment date.

Cost
It costs nothing. Write wages clearly into the contract. Raises, bonuses, advances, loans — everything gets a signed piece of paper. No verbal promises. And don't pay company wages out of your own pocket. The hard part is holding to this rule when it's someone you know asking.
Benefit
What a labor contract must state includes how wages are paid and how social insurance is contributed. The employer must pay wages timely and in full per the contract and state rules. Dragging on payment: the employee can apply directly to court for a payment order (a court-issued demand for payment). A boss lending an employee their own money is a loan contract: except where two natural persons agree otherwise, it must be written, stating how much was borrowed, how interest is calculated, and when and how repayment happens. A bonus promised verbally has nothing on paper; in a real dispute, whoever can't produce evidence loses (nationwide)
Note
It's not about refusing to help — help must go through the system too. Once out-of-system favors become custom, stopping them breeds disputes. Mixing private loans with company accounts means that when the company loses, the bad debt lands on you. The statutes were verified; the advice itself is experience — hence Grade C.
Sources (2 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2007). Labor Contract Law (Articles 17 and 30). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 469 and 668). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
18

Sell before you build: validate demand with presales and small orders, then fund production

Grade BValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Researchers tracked 116 Italian startups for about a year: founders who formed a hypothesis and then tested it against market feedback ran better businesses, were more willing to switch direction in time, and were no more likely to quit early. So if nobody will prepay and nobody will place a small order, don't believe "build it and they will come".

Cost
A few dozen to a few hundred yuan for a sample or a landing page. Then find a few dozen real customers and get them to prepay or place small orders. This is a few weeks slower than just starting production. The hard part is resisting building the product first.
Benefit
A randomized controlled trial tracked 116 Italian startups for about a year. In an RCT, subjects are randomly split into two groups, only one gets the training, and the two groups' outcomes are compared. The result: trained founders who made decisions by "form a hypothesis first, then test it rigorously against market feedback" performed better, were more likely to turn to other plans in time, and were not more likely to give up early. The authors' explanation: the approach reduces the odds of pumping more money into projects that look promising but won't work (false-positive projects) (Italy, published 2020)
Note
It's a single study with a small sample, done in Italy — hence Grade B. The title, source, and abstract were checked against Crossref and Semantic Scholar; the effect numbers in the full text were not verified for this section. Operationally: if nobody will prepay and nobody will place a small order, don't believe "build it and they will buy".
Sources (1 reference)
Camuffo A, Cordova A, Gambardella A, Spina C (2020). A Scientific Approach to Entrepreneurial Decision Making: Evidence from a Randomized Control Trial. Management Science 66(2):564-586. https://doi.org/10.1287/mnsc.2018.3249
19

Once the sample is made, run it through a mass-production checklist before talking about starting production

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

The difference between one sample and a thousand units is where the money is tied up. Yield decides the true cost. Minimum order quantities and payment terms decide how much you must front. Inventory decides when the money comes back. If the product is on the compulsory certification catalog, it can't leave the factory or be sold without certification and the certification mark.

Cost
A few hundred yuan for one small-batch trial run. Then a few hours to nail down these items: yield (how many of 100 units are sellable), the supplier's minimum order quantity and payment terms, how much cash inventory ties up, packaging and logistics, certification and licensing, trademarks. The hard part is resisting skipping this step and starting production directly.
Benefit
The difference between one sample and a thousand units is where the money is tied up. Yield decides the true cost — yield is the share of a finished batch that is compliant and sellable. How little the supplier will sell per order (minimum order quantity) and how long after shipping until you're paid (payment terms) — these two decide how much you must front. Inventory decides when the money comes back. Products listed in the compulsory product certification catalog must pass certification and bear the certification mark before leaving the factory or being sold. Leaving the factory or selling without certification is punished under the Regulation on Certification and Accreditation. Catering and selling food require a food business license (nationwide)
Note
The checklist itself is a rule-of-thumb method; the statutes were verified against original texts. Before production, search CNIPA's trademark lookup system for similar registrations, then apply for your own trademark. For the red lines on using others' trademarks and artwork, see entries 20 and 21 (keep invoices and supplier details; artwork must be your own or licensed). The compulsory certification catalog follows the latest version published by SAMR.

Measures for the Administration of Food Business Licensing and Filing (SAMR Order No. 78 of 2023, Article 4). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10606/202307/content_…
20

For every batch you buy, keep the invoices and the supplier's details; refuse goods priced clearly below market: when an employee sources fakes, it's the boss who gets sentenced

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Selling fakes: 30,000 yuan in gains or 50,000 yuan in sales is enough for a criminal sentence of up to 3 years. Goods sitting unsold in the warehouse count too. "I didn't know it was fake" isn't yours to declare: buying clearly below market with no good reason gets you ruled "knowing". Keep purchase contracts, invoices, payment records, and supplier details — that's the only route out of paying damages.

Cost
It costs nothing. For every batch keep these items: the purchase contract, invoices, payment records, and the supplier's business license and authorization documents. Then set an internal rule: whoever sources the goods signs for them, and anything priced clearly below market is refused across the board. The hard part is passing up cheap goods that look so profitable.
Benefit
Knowingly selling goods bearing counterfeit registered trademarks: illegal gains of 30,000 yuan, or sales of 50,000 yuan, reach the threshold for a criminal sentence. Up to 3 years plus a fine, or a fine alone. Ten times those figures: 3 to 10 years plus a fine. Unsold stock counts too: goods value at three times or more of the sales threshold is likewise a crime. "Knowing" doesn't require your confession. The Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate's 2025 judicial interpretation lists five situations that directly establish knowledge, unless you can produce evidence proving you truly didn't know. One: knowing the registered trademark on the goods was altered, switched, or covered. Two: forging or altering the trademark holder's authorization documents, or knowing those documents were forged or altered. Three: having been criminally or administratively punished for selling counterfeit goods, then selling the same kind again. Four: buying or selling at prices clearly below market without justification. Five: after being discovered by administrative or judicial authorities, moving or destroying infringing goods, accounting vouchers, and other evidence, or providing false proof. Where a company commits this offense, "the unit is fined, and the directly responsible managers and other directly liable personnel" are punished under the same article — the company pays a fine, and the decision-makers and handlers are sentenced under the same article. So when the employee sourced the goods, it's still the person who signed off who gets fined and sentenced. The reverse: the Trademark Law leaves one exit — a seller who genuinely didn't know the goods infringed a registered trademark "bears no liability for damages if they can prove the goods were lawfully obtained and identify the supplier." Whether you escape damages depends entirely on having invoices and supplier details; without them, this route is closed (nationwide; judicial interpretation effective April 26, 2025)
Note
Cosmetics, liquor, mother-and-baby products, electronics, and clothing are the categories where these cases cluster. The common thread: the same item has a huge price spread. "Channel goods", "factory overruns", "duty-free from overseas" — none of these sayings replaces paperwork. Beyond the criminal sentence there's an administrative layer: once infringement is established, the infringing goods and tools are confiscated, and with illegal business volume of 50,000 yuan or more, a fine of up to 5 times can be added. If you've already bought the goods and then find they're wrong: stop selling immediately, seal the stock, and contact the brand owner or the market regulator. Don't keep selling — and whatever you do, don't destroy the goods or the accounts. Destroying evidence lands you squarely in the fifth situation of the "presumed to know it was fake" list above. On using other people's artwork, see entry 21 (artwork must be your own or licensed). There's a scam aimed precisely at this rule: someone comes to you offering pens or other small goods for free — display them in your shop, sell them, and split the money. Days later a "customer" buys one, evidence is gathered on the spot, and an infringement claim follows. With goods given free, all three conditions for escaping damages happen to be missing: no purchase contract or payment records, no real supplier you can name, and a price that's plainly abnormal. "Lawfully obtained and supplier identified" gets you nowhere. So: unsolicited doorstep deliveries with no paperwork, leaving only a WeChat handle — never put them on the shelf. If you really want to sell on consignment, sign a written consignment contract, keep copies of the other side's ID card and business license, and write in who owns the goods and who bears infringement liability.
Sources (4 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2020). Criminal Law Amendment (XI) (items 17 and 24, i.e., Criminal Law Articles 214 and 220). https://www.spp.gov.cn/zdgz/202012/t20201227_503682.shtml; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2025). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases Involving Infringement of Intellectual Property Rights (Fa Shi [2025] No. 5, effective April 26, 2025). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/202504/t20250424_693977.…; NPC Standing Committee (2019). 21

Artwork on products, packaging, tags, and promo images must be your own or licensed; changing a color or adding an icon doesn't count as 'changed'

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Recoloring someone's image, swapping the background, or adding your own icon is still using their work without permission. Copying others' artworks for profit: 30,000 yuan in gains, 50,000 yuan in business volume, or 500 copies printed constitutes the crime of copyright infringement — up to 3 years. On the trademark side, "similar enough to cause confusion" is itself infringement.

Cost
Licensed stock images start at a few dozen yuan each. Original design work runs a few hundred to a few thousand yuan. For every image used on a product, keep a copy of the license certificate and the purchase record. The hard part is not grabbing images from a casual web search.
Benefit
Copyright Law lists "using a work by adaptation, translation, annotation, or other means without the copyright holder's permission" as infringement alongside direct copying. So recoloring the original image, swapping the background, or adding your own icon is still unauthorized use of someone's work. The criminal threshold is here: for profit, printing and selling (reproducing and distributing) an artwork without the copyright holder's permission. Three numbers trigger the crime. Illegal gains of 30,000 yuan. Or business volume of 50,000 yuan (illegal business amount). Or a total of 500 copies (sheets) printed. Any one of the three constitutes the crime of copyright infringement. Up to 3 years plus a fine, or a fine alone. Ten times any threshold: 3 to 10 years. Merely selling infringing copies someone else printed: gains of 50,000 yuan or more, or sales of 100,000 yuan or more, means up to 5 years for selling infringing copies. Trademarks work the same: using a trademark similar to a registered trademark on the same goods, or an identical or similar trademark on similar goods, "where confusion is likely" is itself within infringement. "Similarity" is an expressly written infringing situation in the statute — a small tweak still infringes (nationwide; judicial interpretation effective April 26, 2025)
Note
Three common missteps. One: printing cartoon characters or celebrity photos from a web search onto clothes, mugs, or phone cases. Two: fonts — most commercial fonts need separate licensing; a free preview isn't a free commercial license. Three: design drafts made for clients with unlicensed assets baked in — liability still falls on the seller. For an easy life, use stock libraries with commercial licenses and save the license pages. Or have the designer state in the contract where the assets came from and the scope of the license, with the designer on the hook if things go wrong. Beyond criminal sentences there are civil damages and administrative fines: harming the public interest allows confiscation of illegal gains plus a fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal business volume. For trademark checks before production, see entry 19 (run the sample through a mass-production checklist). Conversely, if your own images get used, these same rules are your recourse. For the criminal line on uploading others' comics and TV shows, running ads and charging membership fees, see section 9, entry 24 (fan-translated comics and re-uploaded shows).
Sources (4 references)

Trademark Law (2019 amendment, Article 57, item 2; after the 2026 revision, Article 72, item 2). https://www.cnipa.gov.cn/art/2019/7/30/art_95_28179.html
22

Follow the procedures on the job; for goodwill beyond the procedures, first think through who bears the responsibility

Grade BValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Take nurses as the example: the regulation states that a nurse who finds a patient in critical condition must immediately notify the physician, and who finds a medical order violating the rules must raise it with the ordering physician. Other jobs are the same: first find where your procedures draw the "must report" line. The law doesn't ask anyone to stand by while someone dies: voluntary emergency aid that accidentally injures the person carries no liability for damages.

Cost
It costs nothing. Work by the rules, the physician's orders, and the process. Don't make decisions beyond your own authority. Before helping, ask yourself one question: if something goes wrong, who's responsible? The hard part is holding firm in the moment against a "just bend the rules this once" request.
Benefit
Using nurses as the example, the regulation's written duty boundaries are these. On finding a patient in critical condition, notify the physician immediately. In emergencies, to rescue a dying patient, necessary emergency care may be given first. On finding a medical order violates laws or rules, or clinical and technical norms, raise it with the physician and, where necessary, report to the department head. The Civil Code adds: one who voluntarily gives emergency aid and accidentally injures the person being rescued bears no liability for damages (no civil liability) (nationwide)
Note
Within the post, follow the procedures; emergency rescue is protected by law. For everything else, first sort out whose authority and whose responsibility it is — don't substitute private goodwill for an institutional decision. The Nurses Regulation was amended in 2020 by State Council Decree No. 726, touching only the registration articles; Article 17 was untouched word for word. The provisions of the Physicians Law on practicing per clinical norms could not be opened in original text this round, so they are not cited.
Sources (3 references)
State Council (2008). Nurses Regulation (State Council Decree No. 517, Article 17). http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6169…; State Council (2020). Nurses Regulation (2020 revision, Article 17). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081777d07c50177b8ed29… (National Laws and Regulations Database); National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 184). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
23

When it loses money, exit by procedure: deregister the simple way if you can, go bankrupt if insolvent — don't just leave it there

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

No debts owed, no unpaid wages, taxes, or social insurance: all investors sign a commitment; after 20 days of public notice with no objection, simple deregistration goes through. A sole proprietor needs no public notice — 10 days with no objection and it's deregistered directly. Can't repay debts? File for bankruptcy. Leave it unattended: two years without annual reports and unreachable, the license is revoked, and the responsible legal representative can't serve as one again for 3 years.

Cost
Simple deregistration is doable yourself: post it on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publication System for 20 days. With debts still outstanding, first settle the accounts — collect what's owed to you, pay what you owe. That step is liquidation. Bankruptcy means applying to court and takes months. The hard part is facing it after losses instead of putting it off forever.
Benefit
Nothing owed by you or to you, or all of it settled. No unpaid wages, no unpaid social insurance, no unpaid taxes. A written commitment from all investors. Meet these, post the 20-day public notice with no objection raised, and simple deregistration is available. A sole proprietor needs no notice: no objection from the relevant department within 10 days and it's deregistered directly. A company that can't repay maturing debts and owes more than it holds (insolvent) may apply to court for reorganization, composition, or bankruptcy liquidation. One already dissolved without liquidation and owing more than it has: the person responsible for liquidation should apply for bankruptcy liquidation. The consequences of leaving it alone are these: failing to publish the annual report on time lands you on the abnormal-operations list. Two consecutive years without annual reports, listed on the abnormal-operations list without correcting it, and unreachable at the registered address: business license revoked. Having served as legal representative of a company whose license was revoked and bearing personal responsibility for it: barred from serving as a company's legal representative, director, supervisor, or senior officer for 3 years from the revocation. And if you're already on the abnormal-operations list, even simple deregistration is off the table (nationwide)
Note
The Interim Regulation on the Disclosure of Enterprise Information was revised in 2024 by State Council Decree No. 777, effective May 1, and hasn't changed since. The old Article 17 — "three years on the abnormal-operations list means the seriously-lawbreaking-enterprises list" — has been deleted. Today's seriously-lawbreaking-and-untrustworthy list covers enterprises falsifying annual reports in serious cases. Much of what's online still quotes the old version; don't copy it. Personal bankruptcy (individually-owned businesses included) is piloted only in a few regions; this section couldn't verify the original texts, so it isn't covered.

24

Before paying for shop-management services, opening courses, or 'no-inventory' models, ask what extra charges come later and where the sales will come from

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

These scams take a small payment first, then keep you adding money with "package upgrades", goods-payment advances, and "unfreezing fees". The orders and earnings in the backend may be fabricated — try withdrawing and you can't. Fake-order boosting is itself illegal, and shop-management firms caught doing it get fined.

Cost
It costs nothing. Before paying, get three things: a written contract, the other side's full company name, and the refund conditions. Pay only the company named in the contract, never a personal account. The hard part is not paying on the spot when they flash screenshots of "students earning 10,000-plus a month".
Benefit
The Guangdong High People's Court tried a shop-management scam. Jiang, Xu, and others, 55 people in all, opened several companies in Guangzhou, Nanning, and Hangzhou. The court found they "knew full well they had neither the ability nor the technical conditions for e-commerce shop management". Still, under the banner of managing Taobao shops, they duped 7,711 victims into buying and upgrading "service packages", cheating them of over 52.994 million yuan in total. The two ringleaders were sentenced to 14 years and 13 years 6 months respectively for fraud. The court said the scam was engineered "airtight" and that "multiple victims were cheated again and again". The Jiangsu Provincial Department of Public Security in 2025 broke the "no-inventory" cross-border e-commerce scam into four steps. Step one: posts on social platforms saying "zero experience needed" and "no stock required". Step two: they add you as an "operations coach" and get you to download a designated platform. Step three: your new shop quickly gets its first order. They have you pay the goods' cost price upfront, saying the buyer's payment is frozen in the platform and released after delivery. Then the backend fabricates floods of orders while you keep adding money. Step four: when you try to withdraw, it's "account abnormal" or "system maintenance" — pay another unfreezing fee and handling charges. The Ms. Zhang in the case put in over 900,000 yuan in installments; three days later the website wouldn't open. On the fake-order side: a shop-management firm organized fake group-buy deals for merchants to game rankings. The market regulator fined it 100,000 yuan, the platform forfeited its 50,000-yuan deposit, and the court upheld the forfeiture. The Supreme People's Court listed it among 2026's typical cases, in its words: "fake transactions and order-brushing are behaviors expressly prohibited by law". SAMR published another case in 2025: a company selling "one-click store migration" and "one-click dropshipping" software that scraped other platforms' product listings was fined 530,000 yuan. SAMR warned operators "not to engage in 'store-stealing migration', 'no-inventory operations', and the like". The way out is in the Civil Code: a contract you were tricked into signing by fraud can be rescinded by a court or arbitration institution. Apply within 1 year of the day you learned of the fraud. Once rescinded, money the other side obtained thereby must be returned (nationwide)
Note
See "zero experience needed", "no stock required", "low input, high returns", or "guaranteed profits"? Stop first. Asked to front goods payments into their designated platform? Stop first. Before paying, check the other side's license and penalty records on the National Enterprise Credit Information Publication System. Write the service content and the refund terms into the contract. Keep all chats, the contract, and transfer screenshots. Money already transferred: call 110 or 96110 immediately to freeze the payment — see section 8, entry 2 (freezing payments after being scammed). If the other side actually did the work and it was merely poor, it's mostly a contract dispute: negotiate, complain, or sue. Rescinding the contract means litigation — first-instance ordinary procedure starts at 6 months, you pay your own lawyer, and by the time judgment lands the other side may long be gone. Anyone collecting money under a franchise banner: check the filing first, per entry 5 (check the MOFCOM filing before buying a franchise). The main beneficiary is you.
Sources (5 references)

Prevention alert: 'no-inventory' cross-border e-commerce — watch out for fraud! https://gat.jiangsu.gov.cn/art/2025/2/13/art_89956_11491354…; Supreme People's Court (2026). SPC releases typical cases on regulating platform operations and protecting consumers' lawful rights and interests (Case 3: dispute over a service contract between a shop-management operator and a platform). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/507691.html; SAMR (2025). SAMR publishes five typical cases of online unfair competition (Case 1). https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2025/art_0d043840ec9445a6…; National People's Congress (2020). 13. Emergencies: what to do first

44 items

This section lays out what to do first, what to do next, and what not to do. The first-aid and wilderness entries are measured in deaths from specific causes and survival rates. The entries on threats and scams are measured in money and personal freedom. The two kinds of numbers are not interchangeable. Entries are ordered from high to low by "how common the situation is × how many lives doing it right versus wrong saves." These entries are written first of all for yourself, your spouse, and your immediate family. 79.2% of cardiac arrests happen at home — the person you are most likely to save is a family member. Friends and colleagues come second. Strangers benefit too, but this tier carries the lowest value, and you risk being extorted or dragged into a lawsuit. That is why these entries put self-protection steps and liability exemptions up front. This section only covers actions taken within minutes. Spotting a scam, or handling a blackmailer who demands money with leverage over you, is measured in days and belongs elsewhere. For hard anti-fraud rules and the seven most common scams, see Section 8, item 3 (Anti-fraud hard rules). For someone demanding money over private photos or nude-chat recordings, see Section 8, item 32 (When the other side blackmails you for money). If the money has already been transferred, call 110 or 96110 immediately to request a payment stop — see Section 8, item 2 (Stopping the payment). This section's entries are grouped by theme below; item numbers are in parentheses. CPR and choking: someone collapsed and not breathing (item 1), an elderly person who fell — don't rush to lift them (item 2), someone choking and unable to speak (item 26), an infant choking and unable to cry (item 43), infant CPR (item 44). Sudden medical emergencies: sudden facial droop or one-sided weakness (item 3), violent dizziness and unsteadiness (item 4), one eye suddenly going dark (item 5), one eye aching and pressurized (item 6), crushing chest pain (item 7), tearing pain (item 8), the worst headache of your life (item 9), an older person becoming sluggish after a head bump (item 10), one leg suddenly swelling (item 11), anaphylactic shock (item 15), someone convulsing (item 16), a diabetic suddenly shaking (item 17). Trauma and burns: heavy bleeding — press the wound first (item 12), dog or cat bites (item 13), cooling a burn with water (item 14), an object embedded in the body — don't pull it out (item 40), suspected fracture — don't move it (item 41). Poisoning, fire, and accidents: electrocution — cut the power first (item 18), the CO alarm sounds (item 19), swallowing cleaner, pesticide, or medication (item 20), chemicals splashed on the body (item 21), dizziness and no sweating in high heat (item 22), lightly salted water for heatstroke (item 23), crawling low in a fire (item 24), seeing someone drowning (item 25), in an earthquake, read the building first (item 30). Wilderness: lost in uninhabited terrain — stay where you are (item 27), shivering and slurred speech mean hypothermia (item 28), snakebite — no cutting, no sucking (item 29), meeting bears, wild boars, or feral dogs (item 31), thunderstorms in the open (item 32), ascending to altitude slowly (item 33), an embedded tick (item 34), boiling wilderness water before drinking (item 35). Confrontation and after a rescue: a stranger demands money in the wild (item 36), stumbling on a group brawl (item 37), injured or out of pocket from rescuing someone (item 39). Sexual assault and HIV exposure: possible HIV exposure (item 38), after sexual assault (item 42).

1

Someone collapses and isn't breathing: start hard chest compressions immediately, and have a bystander call 120 and fetch an AED

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The person you press on will most likely be your own family: 79.2% of cardiac arrests happen at home. With someone doing compressions, the share who survive to hospital discharge rises from 3.9% to 16.1%. No response, no breathing — just start pressing. The spot is the center of the chest, on the line between the nipples. Stack your hands and press hard, 2 times per second, without stopping. Have a second person call 120 and fetch an AED, and don't take your hands off.

Cost
Free. A Red Cross or hospital CPR course takes half a day to a day, and one round of training holds up for years. You can do it untrained too: stack your hands on the center of the chest, on the line between the nipples, press down hard about 2 times per second, and don't stop.
Benefit
Pooled across 79 studies and 142,740 people (a meta-analysis): of people whose heart stops outside a hospital (out-of-hospital cardiac arrest), only 7.6% in total survive to discharge. When a bystander does CPR, survival to discharge rises from 3.9% to 16.1%. A bystander witnesses the collapse in 53% of cases, but only 32% actually get bystander compressions. China's BASIC-OHCA registry recorded 38,227 emergency-response cases; in 30,282 of them (79.2%) the cardiac arrest happened at home. Within that group, the bystander compression rate was 20.3% and survival to discharge 1.2%. The order is: compressions first, then have the second person call and fetch the AED. Once the machine is on, follow its voice prompts
Note
Infants under 1 need a different technique that includes rescue breaths — see item 44 in this section (Infant CPR). Don't start by pinching the philtrum, don't go hunting for family members, don't start filming. And don't hold back out of fear of cracking ribs. Article 184 of the Civil Code states it plainly: if you voluntarily perform emergency aid and injure the person you helped, you bear no civil liability.
Sources (3 references)
Sasson C et al. (2010). Predictors of survival from out-of-hospital cardiac arrest: a systematic review and meta-analysis. Circulation: Cardiovascular Quality and Outcomes. https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCOUTCOMES.109.889576 ; Zheng J et al. (2023). Incidence, process of care, and outcomes of out-of-hospital cardiac arrest in China: a prospective study of the BASIC-OHCA registry. The Lancet Public Health. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(23)00173-1 ; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Article 184). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
2

An elderly person falls or someone collapses: crouch down, speak to them, and call 120; don't rush to lift them. With strangers, walking away is also legal — but if you stop, don't move the person yourself

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The main audience for this one is your own elderly relatives and people close to you. Check breathing first; if there is none, start chest compressions per item 1 (hard chest compressions). Even with breathing, don't pick the person up: they may have had the stroke or the faint before the fall, and forcing them upright can make things worse. Crouch down and speak to them; ask whether they remember how they fell. Anyone with lower-back pain or signs of a fracture is not to be moved — call 120 on the spot.

Cost
Free. Crouching down to ask a question and making a call takes a few minutes. The hard part is holding back the reflex to reach out and lift. With strangers there is an extra ledger: calling 120 leaves your number behind, you may get called back, and you may be asked to give a statement. If the family really comes after you, a lawsuit takes months at minimum — and even if you win in the end, the lawyer's fees come out of your own pocket.
Benefit
The Health Ministry's Technical Guidelines for Fall Intervention in the Elderly states two sentences outright. One: "Falls are the leading cause of injury death among people over 65 in China." The other: "When you find an elderly person who has fallen, do not rush to lift them up — handle it according to the situation." If they are not fully conscious, call an ambulance immediately. If vomiting, turn the head to one side and clear the mouth and nose. If breathing and heartbeat have stopped, start chest compressions at once. "If moving is necessary, keep it steady and lay them flat as much as possible." If they are conscious, first ask whether they have any memory of the fall: "if they cannot recall it, it may have been a faint or a cerebrovascular event." With severe headache, a drooping mouth, slurred speech, or weakness in the hands and feet: "lifting an elderly person up immediately can worsen cerebral hemorrhage or cerebral ischemia and aggravate the condition." With signs of a fracture, back or lower-back pain, or incontinence: "without the relevant professional knowledge, do not move them at will." In all of these cases, call an ambulance immediately. If the person wants to stand up on their own, you may help them rise slowly: "have them sit or lie down, rest, and observe, and only leave once you have confirmed they are fine." As for the fear of being extorted, here is what the law says. Article 90 of the Supreme People's Court's Interpretation on the Application of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China contains two sentences. The first: "A party must provide evidence to prove the facts on which their claims are based..." The second: "If, before judgment is rendered, a party fails to provide evidence, or the evidence is insufficient to prove their factual claims, the party bearing the burden of proof suffers the adverse consequences." Article 1198 of the Civil Code reads: "Where the operator or manager of a business venue or public venue — hotels, shopping malls, banks, stations, airports, sports venues, entertainment venues, and the like — or the organizer of a mass activity fails to fulfill its duty of safety protection and causes harm to others, it shall bear tort liability." Article 184 of the Civil Code: "Where a person voluntarily performing emergency aid causes harm to the person being helped, the rescuer bears no civil liability." The Supreme People's Court published one telling case: a pharmacy operator performed CPR on someone in cardiac arrest and broke the person's ribs. The person spent 18 days in the hospital and claimed a little over 9,000 yuan in damages. The court ruled that the rescuer bore no civil liability
Note
It is graded B because the guidelines only say how to handle things; there is no "how many fewer deaths if you follow this" number. Article 184 exempts harm caused in the course of the rescue, provided you acted voluntarily and in an emergency. It does not cover things like "taking it upon yourself to stuff the person into your own car and drive them to a hospital" — waiting for the 120 ambulance is the safer call. After calling 120, don't hang up; do what the dispatcher on the line tells you. This decision framework is written first for your own elderly relatives and people you know. For a stranger on the street, walking away is legal and also the simplest option: the law doesn't require you to rescue anyone. If you do stop, tally what it costs you, layer by layer: time, leaving your number, being tracked down by the family, being sued, the dispute following you to your workplace, being filmed and spread online. See [docs/Should you stop when a stranger has an accident](../docs/遇到陌生人出事该不该停.md) for the full picture. If you truly decide to stop, the one thing you must do is not move the person yourself, and the reason is medical: forcing them upright can worsen a brain hemorrhage or a spinal injury. One exception: if you run the place, manage it, or organized the activity, walking away could leave you liable. Article 1198 of the Civil Code imposes a duty of safety protection that makes you responsible for the safety of people on the premises. For fall prevention itself, see Section 1, item 13 (Training balance and leg strength). For delayed symptoms after an elderly head bump, see item 10 in this section. For money after being injured in a rescue, see item 39 in this section. For documenting and reporting online harassment, see Section 8, item 16.
