14. Account and information security

10 items

Basis: money and personal information. When someone else logs into your account, the first thing you lose is money. They will then use your account to scam the people in your contacts. Your identity, in effect, is taken as well.

1

Turn on two-factor for email, payment, and social accounts; prefer phone pop-up confirmation, with SMS codes as the fallback

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Two-factor means that when you log in, on top of your password you confirm once more that it is really you. With the method where a pop-up appears on your phone and you tap to confirm, more than nine in ten phishing account takeovers are blocked. With the old method of answering questions like "where did you last log in" or "what is your backup email", only about one in ten phishing takeovers is stopped.

Cost
Costs nothing. Set up once per account; done in two or three minutes.
Benefit
Google analyzed 350,000 real account takeover attempts (also called account hijacking). One type relies on device-based verification, such as a pop-up on your phone that you tap to confirm, or plugging in a security key. This type blocked "over 94% of hijacking attempts that originated in phishing, and 100% of automated hijacking attempts". Phishing means tricking you into typing your password on a fake website; automated means machines mass-trying leaked passwords. The other type relies on answering questions, such as where you last logged in and what your backup email is. That type "blocked as little as 10% of phishing hijacks and 73% of automated hijacks"
Note
The same study also found that this kind of verification sometimes locks out the legitimate user. 52% of real users failed to get in on the first try, though 97% eventually did. Turn this on for your email first, because most other accounts recover their passwords through email. Verification codes are for your use only — what you take on when you read out codes or show your face for someone else, see Section 8, item 45 (reading out verification codes)
Sources (1 reference)
Doerfler P, Thomas K, Marincenko M, et al. (2019). Evaluating Login Challenges as a Defense Against Account Takeover. The World Wide Web Conference (WWW '19). https://doi.org/10.1145/3308558.3313481
2

Your email gets its own password, never repeated on any website

Grade CValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Passwords stolen from other websites get used to log straight into your email. Once someone is inside your email, every account that can recover its password through that email goes down with it. So your email password should be one of a kind, never used anywhere else.

Cost
Costs nothing. Store it in a password manager and you don't have to memorize it. The hard part is breaking the old habit of using one password everywhere.
Benefit
Taking leaked account-password pairs from other sites and trying them one by one is called credential stuffing — the laziest form of attack — and your email gets tried this way too. Once someone is inside your email, every account that recovers its password through it is lost at once. The advice of the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency: a different strong password for every account, at least 16 characters, kept in a password manager
Note
If you can't remember them, use your browser's built-in password manager. It remembers each site's password for you, which beats reusing one password everywhere by a wide margin. Don't store passwords in WeChat favorites or your notes app
Sources (1 reference)
US CISA. Use Strong Passwords. https://www.cisa.gov/secure-our-world/use-strong-passwords
3

Set a lock-screen passcode on the phone and a PIN on the SIM

Grade CValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The SIM is the small card inside your phone, and SMS verification codes arrive through it. If your phone is lost, whoever finds it can pull the card out, slip it into another phone to receive your codes, and reset your accounts one by one. Put a PIN on the card: when it moves to another phone, that PIN must be entered first thing at power-on, and this route is cut off.

Cost
Costs nothing. Set the lock-screen passcode and the SIM PIN once each and you're done.
Benefit
After a phone is lost, the fastest route for the finder is to put the SIM into another phone and receive your SMS verification codes. With the codes, they can reset your accounts one by one. With a PIN on the SIM, it demands the password at power-on in any other phone, and the finder can't use it to receive your codes
Note
The PIN is set under "SIM card lock" in your phone's settings. The factory default is usually 1234 or 0000. Enter it wrong three times in a row and you'll need the PUK code from your carrier to unlock it. So once you set the PIN, write it down on paper first
Sources
Author's experience; no direct literature
4

Phone lost? Do this in order: suspend the SIM, lock it remotely, change passwords, report to police, freeze bank cards

Grade CValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Order matters more than speed. Step one, suspend the SIM, and the lifeline of verification codes is cut. Next, lock the phone remotely, then change your email and payment passwords from a computer, then report to the police and get the record, and finally freeze bank cards as needed. If the phone isn't on you, you can suspend the SIM by calling your carrier's customer service from someone else's phone.

Cost
Costs nothing. The whole sequence takes a dozen or so minutes.
Benefit
Order matters more than speed. Step one, suspend the SIM, and no one else can receive your verification codes. Step two, lock the phone remotely and wipe its contents. Step three, from a computer, change your email and payment passwords. Step four, report to the police and get the record. Finally, freeze bank cards as needed. The US Federal Communications Commission's advice is the same: lock it remotely even if you think it's merely lost. If it was stolen, report to the police right away with the model and the IMEI number (the phone's identity number), and tell your carrier immediately
Note
Write down the customer service numbers of the three carriers in advance: China Mobile 10086, China Unicom 10010, China Telecom 10000. Also note which city your phone number was registered in — customer service will ask. You can call customer service from someone else's phone to suspend the SIM just the same
Sources (1 reference)
US FCC. Protect Your Smart Device. https://www.fcc.gov/consumers/guides/protect-your-mobile-de…; the order of steps is the author's experience; for replacing an ID card see Section 7, and for loans taken out in your name see the credit-record item in Section 8
5

Card fraud: report and freeze first, then police, then demand the bank compensate — proving 'it was you who spent it' is the bank's burden

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

When your card is defrauded, you don't have to prove "it wasn't me who spent it". It's the reverse: the bank must produce evidence that you made the transaction yourself in person, and if it can't, it pays you. The precondition is that you report and freeze the moment you discover it. Drag your feet on the freeze, and any losses that pile up afterward are on you.

Cost
Costs nothing. The moment something looks wrong on your card, report it lost or freeze it immediately. Keep the police report, the loss-report record, and the transaction notices the bank sent you. If the card is still in your possession, make a small balance inquiry or deposit/withdrawal nearby to leave a record proving the real card was in your hands at the time. The hard part is holding back from arguing with customer service first — freeze first.
Benefit
The Supreme People's Court's rules separate out "who must produce the evidence". If you claim counterfeit-card fraud or online fraud, you present evidence first. Counterfeit-card fraud means someone copied your card and spent with the copy. All of these can serve as proof: legally effective legal instruments, where the real card was at the time of the bank-card transaction, and where the transaction took place. Also account transaction details, transaction notices, police reports, loss reports, and so on. Conversely, when the card-issuing bank or a non-bank payment institution (third-party payment) claims the transaction was made by the cardholder in person or with their authorization, it is up to them to produce the evidence. If, after you notify the bank, it fails to verify in time, or fails to provide or preserve transaction receipts and surveillance footage in time so the evidence cannot be obtained, the bank bears the consequences of the missing evidence. Once the finding stands: as a debit-card (savings card) holder, you can demand the issuing bank pay you the stolen deposits with interest, plus compensation for your losses. As a credit card holder, you can demand the return of the deducted overdraft principal and interest and penalty charges, plus compensation; if the bank turns around and demands you repay that overdraft, the court will not support it. You can also demand the issuing bank promptly remove the corresponding adverse credit records (nationwide, effective May 25, 2021)
Note
There are two situations where you bear liability yourself. One: you failed to properly safeguard your bank card, password, or verification codes and are yourself at fault (the original text reads "at fault for failing to fulfill the duty of proper safekeeping"), and you bear losses in proportion to your fault. So never tell anyone your password, and never forward verification codes to anyone (see item 1: for two-factor, prefer phone pop-up confirmation). Two: you didn't report the loss in time and let the losses keep growing; the extra portion is on you. So the first step is always report-and-freeze; don't start by arguing with customer service. Third-party payment institutions are covered by the same rules. Where their promotional materials promise "advance compensation" in specific, definite terms, you can hold them to it and demand they pay first. If you were tricked into transferring the money out yourself, that follows a different track — see Section 8, item 2 (the moment you discover the scam, call 110 or 96110 immediately and demand a payment stop).
Sources (1 reference)
Supreme People's Court (2021). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Bank Card Civil Dispute Cases (Articles 4, 5, 7, 14, and 15). https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/304771.html
6

Review each account's logged-in devices and authorized apps every so often; clear out the ones you don't use

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

"Logged-in devices" are the phones and computers that can still use your account right now. Account thieves often lie low for a while before they strike. When a device you don't recognize shows up in the list, or software you stopped using long ago is still connected to your account, log out of everything and change your password on the spot.

Cost
Costs nothing. A few minutes each time you look. The hard part is that no one reminds you — you have to remember to check yourself.
Benefit
Account takeovers often don't happen on the spot; the intruder lies low first. The logged-in devices list in your account records the phones and computers that can still use it. The authorized-apps list records other companies' software you permitted to sign in with this account. Unfamiliar devices and long-abandoned third-party software in these lists are the easiest traces to spot
Note
WeChat, Alipay, email, Apple, and Android accounts all have this entry point. When you find a device you don't recognize, tap "log out everywhere" and then change your password
Sources
Author's experience; no direct literature
7

Don't click 'agree to all' just to use an app: they cannot refuse you service for declining to share non-essential data

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

When an app asks for your information, if it isn't something providing that service requires, it cannot shut you out for declining to share. What it may collect is limited to what it actually needs. A map asking for your location is necessary; a flashlight asking for your contacts is not.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is resisting the tap on "agree to all".
Benefit
The law spells out two things. First, products or services may not be refused on the grounds that a person did not consent or withdrew consent, unless processing the information is necessary to provide the service. Second, collection must be limited to the minimum scope needed to achieve the processing purpose — only what will actually be used may be collected
Note
The test is whether the information is necessary for providing the service. A map needing your location is necessary; a flashlight needing your contacts is not. After installing an app, go to the app permissions page in your phone's settings and switch off the non-essential permissions. When you actually need the feature, choose "allow this time only".
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Personal Information Protection Law. National People's Congress website. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088…: Article 6, "The collection of personal information must be limited to the minimum scope necessary to achieve the processing purpose; excessive collection of personal information is not allowed"; Article 16, "A personal information processor must not refuse to provide products or services on the grounds that the individual does not consent to the processing of their personal information or withdraws consent, except where processing the personal information is necessary to provide the product or service"; Article 15, "Where personal information is processed on the basis of an individual's consent, the individual has the right to withdraw that consent. The personal information processor must provide a convenient way to withdraw consent"
8

You may view, copy, correct, and delete your personal information — and sue if refused

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

You have the right to require companies to let you view, copy, correct, and delete your own information. When the service shuts down, the retention period expires, or you withdraw consent, the company is supposed to delete on its own. If it refuses, it must state its reasons; if it won't act, you can take it straight to court. Cancelling an account and deleting information are two different things — after cancelling, you must separately request deletion.

Cost
Costs nothing. Only when they drag their feet do you need to complain or sue. A real lawsuit takes months at minimum, and you pay the lawyer yourself, so complaining first is the better deal. The hard part is having to chase them again and again while they stall.
Benefit
There are several situations in which a company should delete on its own initiative: the service has shut down, the agreed retention period has expired, you withdrew consent, the original purpose of collection has been fulfilled, and so on. If it hasn't deleted, you can demand that it does. If it refuses to let you exercise these rights, it must state its reasons. You can sue directly in the people's court
Note
Cancelling an account and deleting personal information are two separate things; after cancelling, you must separately request deletion. Before switching phones or selling an old one, sign out of and unbind all accounts on the old phone first, then factory-reset it. The law gives you the right to deletion after the fact; it cannot pull back what has already leaked.
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Personal Information Protection Law. National People's Congress website. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088…: Article 45, "An individual has the right to access and copy their personal information from a personal information processor... Where an individual requests access to or copying of their personal information, the personal information processor shall provide it in a timely manner"; Article 46, the right to correction and supplementation; Article 47 lists five situations requiring proactive deletion, including "(1) the processing purpose has been achieved, cannot be achieved, or is no longer necessary for achieving the processing purpose", "(2) the personal information processor has ceased to offer the product or service, or the retention period has expired", "(3) the individual has withdrawn consent", and "where the personal information processor has not deleted the information, the individual has the right to request deletion"; Article 50, "A personal information processor shall establish a convenient mechanism for accepting and handling individuals' requests to exercise their rights. Where a request to exercise rights is refused, reasons shall be given" and "an individual may file a lawsuit with the people's court in accordance with law"
9

You don't have to accept facial recognition: where alternatives exist they can't offer face-only, and if you refuse they must give you another way

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

As long as another way exists to accomplish the same thing, they cannot make face scanning your only option. If you refuse facial recognition, they must offer an alternative — a card, a password, your ID — and they may not pressure you with "then we can't process this". In hotel guest rooms, public bathhouses, changing rooms, and restrooms, no one may install facial recognition equipment at all.

Cost
Costs nothing. When asked to scan your face, ask "is there another way to verify?" If they say no, demand one. The hard part is speaking up face to face.
Benefit
The Measures for Security Management of Facial Recognition Technology state: "Where other non-facial-recognition methods exist to achieve the same purpose or meet the same business requirement, facial recognition technology must not be used as the sole verification method. Where an individual does not consent to identity verification through facial information, other reasonable and convenient methods shall be provided." The Measures also state: "No organization or individual may mislead, deceive, or coerce an individual into accepting facial recognition for identity verification on grounds such as processing business or improving service quality." Processing facial information on the basis of your consent requires "separate consent given voluntarily and explicitly with full knowledge": you are asked about this one matter on its own, and it is your separate nod that counts. You have the right to withdraw consent, and the processor must provide a convenient way to withdraw. Processing the facial information of a minor under fourteen requires the consent of parents or other guardians. Facial recognition equipment installed in public places "must be necessary for maintaining public safety", with prominent warning signs posted. Inside the private spaces of public places — hotel guest rooms, public bathhouses, public changing rooms, public restrooms — no organization or individual may install it. Facial information must be stored within the facial recognition device itself and must not be transmitted over the internet. Two exceptions: where laws or administrative regulations provide otherwise, or where separate consent has been obtained (nationwide, effective June 1, 2025)
Note
The most common encounters are residential gate systems, rental platforms, gyms, and hotels asking you to register your face. When they say "the system only supports face scanning", read them the Measures' original words: "Where other non-facial-recognition methods exist to achieve the same purpose or meet the same business requirement, facial recognition technology must not be used as the sole verification method." Then demand they provide an alternative such as a card, a password, or an ID. If they still refuse, report it to the local cyberspace administration. Where the state has separate rules for face-based identity verification — some finance and government-service scenarios, for example — follow those rules. The biggest difference between your face and a password is that a face cannot be changed once it leaks, which is why it deserves more caution than a password. Organizations storing facial information on 100,000 or more people must file with the cyberspace administration at or above the provincial level within 30 working days — a question worth asking to gauge how legitimate they are. For the rights to access, correct, and delete your personal information, see item 8. Someone borrowing your face to take out a loan of their own is a different matter — see Section 8, item 45 (lending your face to someone).
Sources (1 reference)
Cyberspace Administration of China, Ministry of Public Security (2025). Measures for Security Management of Facial Recognition Technology (Order No. 19, Articles 10, 12, and 13, effective June 1, 2025). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-03/21/c_1744174262156096.htm
10

Never hand code, keys, or private data to 'AI relay stations' of unknown provenance — above all when letting AI execute commands automatically

Grade BValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

A relay station sits between you and the model providers: everything you send and every response you get back, it can see and alter. One study tested more than 400 relay stations: 9 injected malicious code into responses, and 17 tampered with the cloud-service keys the researchers had planted on purpose. If you let AI execute commands automatically, a single altered command is enough for your computer to be taken over.

Cost
Official direct access usually costs more than a relay station, and topping up is less convenient. The hard part is that relays are cheap, and one entry point can reach several model providers
Benefit
The Ministry of State Security issued a risk warning in June 2026. Some relay stations keep user-submitted data on their servers; some quietly siphon it off and resell it to other large model providers for training. Some hide backdoors, planting malicious code on user devices, stealing account keys and cloud credentials, even installing remote-control programs. The warning advises using official direct connections and properly licensed platforms, and avoiding platforms of unknown origin, without operating qualifications, or without security guarantees. If you must use one, desensitize personal privacy and project materials first, manage keys carefully, and rotate them regularly. On abnormal charges, unexplained account bans, or data anomalies: stop using it immediately, change your keys, run a virus scan, and preserve evidence. In 2026 researchers at the University of California, Santa Barbara and other institutions ran a measurement study. They bought 28 paid relay stations from Taobao, Xianyu, and overseas online stores, and collected 400 free ones from public communities. The result: 1 paid and 8 free ones injected malicious code into returned tool calls. Tool calls are the commands AI has your computer execute, such as installing a software package. Another 2 struck selectively — the paper's example was targeting only fully automated sessions. 17 had used the Amazon Web Services keys the researchers had planted deliberately. 1 drained money from a researcher's Ethereum wallet; the wallet held very little, and the loss was under 50 US dollars. The alteration the paper demonstrated is subtle: swapping requests in the install command for the near-identical spelling reqeusts — impossible to catch at a glance (nationwide)
Note
It is graded B because there is only one study, and a preprint at that — the version made public before formal publication. Most of the tested relays were free; only 28 were paid, so no "what share of relay stations are bad" figure can be computed. Some media reported the theft as 500,000 US dollars; the paper itself says under 50 dollars. The benefit is rated medium based on consequences: the losses from stolen keys versus stolen code differ enormously, and the study offers no dollar figure to plug in. If you have already used a relay of unknown provenance, go to the model providers, revoke and regenerate the keys you used, and swap the cloud-service and code-repository keys as well. While traffic goes through a relay, don't let AI execute commands fully automatically — read each command before letting it through. Running a relay station carries criminal risk — see Section 11, item 19 (AI relay stations). The beneficiary is you.
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of State Security (2026). "AI relay stations": guard against the risks. https://www.szzg.gov.cn/2026/xwzx/szkx/202606/t20260608_533… (reposted on the Digital China Summit's official website from the Ministry of State Security's WeChat account); Liu H, Shou C, Wen H, Chen Y, Fang RJ, Feng Y. (2026). Your Agent Is Mine: Measuring Malicious Intermediary Attacks on the LLM Supply Chain. arXiv:2604.08407. https://arxiv.org/abs/2604.08407

15. Renting and buying a home

9 items

Basis: money. In renting, the easiest places to lose money are the deposit and the agent. In buying, the costliest things are the loan interest — and what the seller knows that you don't.

1

The deposit amount, refund deadline, and deduction conditions must be written into the contract

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

How much the deposit is, when it is refunded, and under what conditions it can be deducted — all of it goes into the contract before you sign. Deduction reasons not written into the contract cannot be used against your deposit when you move out.

Cost
Costs nothing. Ten extra minutes at signing. The hard part is raising it in front of the landlord
Benefit
The administrative regulation is explicit: "Where a lessor collects a deposit, the housing lease contract shall stipulate the deposit amount, the refund time, and the circumstances for deducting the deposit. Except as stipulated in the housing lease contract, the lessor may not deduct the deposit without proper reason." Three things go into the contract: how much deposit is collected, when it is refunded, and under what circumstances it can be deducted. Reasons not written into the contract cannot be used to take your money
Note
On move-out day, take photos and video together with the landlord. Photograph the readings of the water, electricity, and gas meters, and the walls and floors as well. If your deposit is deducted without cause, complain first to the housing rental administration. For small amounts, use small-claims litigation — see Section 8
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2025). Housing Rental Regulation (State Council Decree No. 812, effective September 15, 2025) (Article 10). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032956…
2

Utilities cut, locks changed, or threats to force you out: call the police and preserve evidence first — regulations forbid forcing you out this way

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

A landlord cannot cut your water and power, change the locks, or show up with threats to force you to break the lease or move out — the regulations expressly forbid it. If it happens, call the police first. The police response record is your evidence when you later claim damages. Do not fight it out with them yourself.

Cost
Costs nothing. One phone call to the police, done on the spot
Benefit
The administrative regulation is explicit: "A lessor may not use violence, threats, or other unlawful means to force the lessee to terminate the housing lease contract or vacate the rented housing." Vacate means making you move out. When this happens, call the police first and preserve the evidence. Do not fight back with your own hands
Note
Calling the police is about getting a response record on file; it becomes your evidence when you later claim damages. Also notify the housing rental administration
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2025). Housing Rental Regulation (State Council Decree No. 812, effective September 15, 2025) (Article 12). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032956…
3

Agents may not collect or pass on rent and deposits; pay the landlord directly

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

By regulation, rent and deposits may not be collected or paid through the agent — the money goes straight to the landlord. Every pass through the agent's hands is one more chance for it to abscond with the funds. If it really runs, you have paid rent for nothing and the landlord will still evict you. Before paying, check that the payee is the name on the title deed.

Cost
Costs nothing. Checking the payee before paying takes a few minutes. The hard part is resisting the agent's pitch to send the money to them
Benefit
The administrative regulation lists "collecting or paying housing rent and deposits on behalf of others" as prohibited conduct for real estate brokerage agencies: the agent may not collect your rent and deposit on the landlord's behalf. Every pass through the agent's hands is one more chance for it to abscond with the funds
Note
Before paying, check that the payee is the name on the title deed. If it isn't the owner, get clarity and keep a written authorization on file. An agent may only charge the brokerage fee for making the match
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2025). Housing Rental Regulation (State Council Decree No. 812, effective September 15, 2025) (Article 25). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032956…
4

Before renting long-term apartment housing, check its supervised escrow account; don't pay a year up front to save money

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Pay a year up front and the discount you get is that small. If the company collapses, your deposit and the remaining dozen-odd months of rent vanish together. Tied into a rent loan it is worse: the operator vanishes, and you are still repaying the loan month by month. Before signing, check whether it has published a supervised escrow account for rental funds.

Cost
Costs nothing. One check takes a dozen or so minutes
Benefit
The administrative regulation requires housing rental enterprises that operate by subletting to "establish a supervised housing rental funds account and publish it to the public". Operating by subletting means the company leases whole units from landlords and re-rents them to you. The small discount from paying a year up front does not offset the risk that the company absconds and your deposit and remaining rent vanish together. Sign a rent loan at the same time and the risk is greater still
Note
At signing, look carefully for any tied loan. If an installment app paid the operator a year's money up front while you repay it in monthly installments, then when the operator vanishes you keep repaying. Do not sign this kind of contract
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2025). Housing Rental Regulation (State Council Decree No. 812, effective September 15, 2025) (Article 19). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032956…
5

If the place is sold during your lease, the lease still holds — you don't have to move

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If the home is sold during your lease, your lease remains valid. The new owner must let you stay to the end of the term under the original contract. No moving, no renegotiating the price. The precondition is that you live there lawfully — keep the contract, the transfer records, and proof of when you moved in.

Cost
Costs nothing
Benefit
The Civil Code has a provision known as "sale does not break the lease". The article's original words: a change of ownership of the leased property during the lease term does not affect the validity of the lease contract. Meaning: if the home changes hands mid-lease, the signed lease still holds. The new owner must let you stay to the end of the term under the original contract
Note
The precondition is that you have lawfully moved in — the statute's wording is lawful possession and use. Keep the contract, the transfer records, and the evidence of your move-in date safe
Sources (1 reference)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 725). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
6

Before signing, check the title deed and mortgage status; run all payments through bank transfers with the purpose noted

Grade CValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The two most common ways to lose everything: rent paid to someone who is not the owner, and a house long since mortgaged to the bank that later gets seized. Before signing, check ownership and mortgage status once at the real estate registration center. Run all money through bank transfers with the note "rent for such-and-such house, such-and-such month" — in a dispute, that is direct evidence.

Cost
Costs nothing. One check takes half an hour
Benefit
The two most common ways to lose everything: rent paid to someone who is not the owner, and a house long since mortgaged to the bank that later gets seized. Note the transfer "rent for such-and-such house, such-and-such month" — in a dispute, that is direct evidence
Note
Ownership information can be checked at the local real estate registration center. At signing, have the landlord there in person; if they cannot come, get a power of attorney. If a sublessor is re-renting to you, you need the original landlord's written consent
Sources
Author's experience; no direct literature. The same logic of preserving evidence and noting transfer purposes runs through the two items in Section 8 on betrothal gifts and IOUs
7

For second-hand homes where the agent collects the purchase money, it must go through the agent's dedicated escrow account at a bank

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The purchase money runs from hundreds of thousands to millions of yuan — the largest single sum in this book. Where the agent collects it, the rules require it to go through the dedicated account the agency opened at a bank, never a WeChat transfer to some agent personally. Also: two agencies working one deal may charge only one commission, and loan or title-transfer handling must be under a separate contract with the fees disclosed in advance.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is holding out for the dedicated account — you may have to argue with the agency a little more
Benefit
The rules are explicit: where it is agreed that a real estate brokerage agency collects and pays transaction funds, the funds must be transferred through the dedicated client transaction settlement funds account it has opened at a bank. Meaning: the purchase money goes into a supervised dedicated account — not the agency's own account, and not some individual agent's personal account
Note
The purchase money runs from hundreds of thousands to millions of yuan — the largest single sum in this book — so never WeChat it to an individual agent. Two more common overcharges. First, where two agencies jointly handle one deal, only one commission may be charged. Second, loan handling and title-transfer handling are separate services: they require a separate contract with the fees disclosed in advance. Run all payments through transfers with the purpose noted — see item 6 (checking the title deed and mortgage status before signing).
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2011). Measures for the Administration of Real Estate Brokerage (Order No. 8, amended by Order No. 29 of 2016), Article 24: "Where the parties to a real estate transaction agree that the brokerage agency collects and pays transaction funds, the funds must be transferred through the dedicated client transaction settlement funds account the agency has opened at a bank." Article 18, "Real estate brokerage services operate under a published-price system... brokerage service items, service content, and fee standards must be posted in a prominent place in the business premises"; Article 19, "Where two or more real estate brokerage agencies cooperate on the same real estate brokerage business, commission may be charged for that one business only, and no additional fees may be imposed on the client"; Article 17, on loan handling, real estate registration handling, and other services, "the service content, fee standards, and other particulars shall be explained to the client, and a separate contract shall be signed after the client agrees". http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1918920.htm
8

Don't rent partitioned units: the smallest lawful rental unit is a room as originally designed; kitchens, bathrooms, and balconies may not be lived in

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

By regulation, the smallest rental unit is the room as originally designed. Kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and underground storage rooms may not be lived in. If such a unit gets busted, you may be the one who has to move. Also, during the lease the landlord cannot raise the rent just by saying so.

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is that on the same budget you either live farther out or in a smaller place
Benefit
The rules are explicit: the smallest rental unit is a room as originally designed, and one room may not be partitioned into several and rented out separately. Per-capita rented floor area may not fall below the local minimum standard. Kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and underground storage rooms may not be rented out for people to live in. During the lease term, the lessor also may not unilaterally and arbitrarily raise the rent
Note
When an illegal partition gets busted, it is the tenant who moves, and the deposit and rent already paid are usually unrecoverable. Safety is worse too: partition walls often block escape routes, and a crowd in one unit shares a single electrical circuit. Three things to check at a viewing: whether the wall was built later, whether the room has a window, and whether the wiring can carry that many people's load.
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development (2010). Measures for the Administration of Commodity Housing Leasing (Order No. 6), Article 8: "When renting out housing, the room as originally designed shall be the smallest rental unit, and per-capita rented floor area shall not fall below the minimum standard set by the local people's government. Kitchens, bathrooms, balconies, and underground storage rooms may not be rented out for people to live in." Article 9: "The lessor shall perform the repair obligations agreed in the contract and ensure the safety of the house and indoor facilities... During the housing lease contract term, the lessor may not unilaterally and arbitrarily raise the rent level." http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1845070.htm
9

Urban hukou holders who want to live in the countryside: rent rural houses only; don't buy homestead land or houses on it

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Urban hukou holders cannot buy homestead land, farmers' houses, or "small-property-rights homes" in the countryside — state documents expressly forbid it. Even if villagers say "a written contract is all you need", it doesn't work: the money leaves your hands and the house never becomes yours. To live in the countryside long-term, sign a lease — at most 20 years per term, renewed at expiry.

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is that the house is not yours, each lease term is at most 20 years, and at expiry you renegotiate with the landlord
Benefit
The General Office of the State Council's document is explicit: "Urban residents may not purchase homestead land, farmers' houses, or 'small-property-rights homes' in rural areas." The same document also provides that after a farmer sells or rents out their housing, any further homestead application will not be approved. The 2019 document from the Central Rural Work Leading Group Office and the Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs said it again: "Urban residents are strictly forbidden to purchase homestead land in rural areas." The same document lays out the legal path: urban residents may rent rural houses to live in or operate, lease contract terms may not exceed twenty years, and at expiry the two parties may agree anew
Note
Homestead land is what a village allocates to its own villagers for building houses, and it goes only to village members. When renting a rural house, sign a written contract with the farming household that spells out the term, the rent, whether renovation or remodeling is allowed, and how renovation costs are settled at expiry. The documents cap the term at 20 years, so don't sign "50-year lease" or "70-year lease" contracts, and never prepay years of rent in one lump sum. The documents also ban using homestead land in the countryside to build villa compounds and private clubs — don't put money into a "joint build" with villagers.
Sources (2 references)
General Office of the State Council (2007). Notice on Strictly Implementing the Laws and Policies Concerning Rural Collective Construction Land (Guobanfa [2007] No. 71). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_239…; Central Rural Work Leading Group Office, Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (2019). Notice on Further Strengthening the Management of Rural Homestead Land (Zhongnongfa [2019] No. 11), Parts 5 and 6. https://www.moa.gov.cn/govpublic/NCJJTZ/201909/t20190920_63…

16. Living with a chronic illness

9 items

Basis: all-cause mortality and money. After a chronic illness is diagnosed there are often decades of life left; this section is about how to manage those decades.

1

Take the full course as prescribed; don't quit just because you feel better

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

People who take their medication in full as the doctor prescribed are only about half as likely to die over the same period as people who take it on and off. Take that number with a discount. Even people who diligently take placebo (fake pills) have lower mortality, which means part of the benefit comes from "people who can stick to medication were already more health-conscious". But the harm of stopping is certain — especially for blood-pressure drugs, anticoagulants, and anti-rejection drugs.

Cost
Costs nothing — it actually saves the money you would later spend treating complications. Daily medication takes a few minutes at most; the hard part is taking it every single day without fail.
Benefit
21 studies, 46,847 people pooled (a meta-analysis): compared with people who take medication on and off, those who take it in full as prescribed are about 44% less likely to die over the same period. Raw value: odds ratio 0.56, 95% CI 0.50–0.63 (the credible range). Looking only at treatments of proven efficacy: about 45% lower (0.55, 0.49–0.62)
Note
Contested. This is the number in this book most in need of a discount. In the same pooled analysis, people who diligently took even the placebo (fake pills) had lower mortality too (0.56, 0.43–0.74). That means a considerable part of the benefit comes from "people who can stick to medication were already more health-conscious". The authors call this mixed-in factor the healthy-adherer effect. But the harm of stopping the drug itself is clear — especially for blood-pressure drugs, anticoagulants, and anti-rejection drugs
Sources (1 reference)
Simpson SH, Eurich DT, Majumdar SR, et al. (2006). A meta-analysis of the association between adherence to drug therapy and mortality. BMJ, 333(7557), 15. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.38875.675486.55
2

Get the outpatient chronic/special disease designation first, then the cross-region filing; hypertension, diabetes, radio- and chemotherapy, dialysis, and anti-rejection treatment can then settle directly away from home

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

For five conditions — hypertension, diabetes, outpatient radio- and chemotherapy for malignant tumors, dialysis for uremia, and anti-rejection treatment after organ transplant — outpatient visits away from home can bill medical insurance directly. No more fronting the money yourself and going back to your insurance locale for reimbursement. But you must first get the outpatient chronic/special disease designation in your insurance locale, then complete the cross-region medical care filing. Only with both in place does it work.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before departure, complete the cross-region filing once in the medical insurance app — all doable on your phone.
Benefit
The National Healthcare Security Administration's document says this has been achieved. The original words: "basically achieved county-level availability of direct cross-province settlement of outpatient chronic/special disease costs for 5 conditions: hypertension, diabetes, outpatient radio- and chemotherapy for malignant tumors, dialysis for uremia, and anti-rejection treatment after organ transplant." "County-level availability" means it can be done at the county level. The document also adds 5 more conditions on top of these 5
Note
The precondition is that both things get done: first the outpatient chronic/special disease designation in your insurance locale, then the cross-region medical care filing. How far the 5 newly added conditions have rolled out varies by region — go by what your local medical insurance department publishes
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the National Healthcare Security Administration, General Office of the Ministry of Finance (2024). Notice on Steadily and Orderly Expanding the Scope of Outpatient Chronic/Special Disease Conditions Eligible for Direct Cross-Province Settlement (Yibaibanfa [2024] No. 19). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202409/content_6974467…
3

Do follow-ups at the intervals the doctor sets, and record every reading in the same notebook

Grade CValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Chronic disease is judged by change over time, not by any single reading. Record the date, the values, and the medications and doses you were on at the time in the same notebook. When you switch hospitals, bring it out — no need to redo the tests and pay for them all over again.

Cost
Each round of tests runs tens to hundreds of yuan. A hospital trip plus waiting for results takes some time. The hard part is that it recurs every so often, and it is easy to keep putting it off.
Benefit
With chronic disease what matters is how the values change over time; any single reading is not enough. Recording in one place has another benefit: when you switch hospitals you don't repeat the tests, or the spending
Note
Record at least four things each time: the date, the test values, the medications you were taking, and their doses. Photographing lab slips with your phone works too, but keep everything in one place — not scattered here and there
Sources
Author's experience; no direct literature
4

Don't suspend proper treatment to try folk remedies or supplements

Grade CValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

The harm of stopping medication is certain; the benefits of folk remedies and supplements are not. That is trading a certain loss for an uncertain gain. If you want to try a supplement, tell your attending doctor first. Some supplements affect blood levels of anticoagulants and anti-rejection drugs.

Cost
Costs nothing — it saves the money you would have spent on supplements. Takes no time. The hard part is holding firm when people keep urging you to try things.
Benefit
The harm of stopping medication is certain; the benefit of folk remedies is not. For the common ineffective categories, Section 6 of this book lists a batch
Note
If you want to try a supplement, tell your attending doctor first. Some supplements interact with prescription drugs — affecting blood levels of anticoagulants and anti-rejection drugs, for example
Sources
Author's experience; no direct literature; for the relevant evidence see Section 6
5

For a stable chronic condition, a community hospital can dispense up to 12 weeks of medication at a time

Grade AValue: HighBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If your condition is stable and your medications unchanged, a community health center can dispense a full 12 weeks of medication at once. That saves the half-day each month spent trekking to a big hospital and queuing to register. Within the same insurance locale, the reimbursement rate at a primary-level hospital is usually about ten percentage points higher than at the next tier up.

Cost
Costs nothing. Ask at the community health center whether a long-term prescription is possible — it is a one-sentence question.
Benefit
No more monthly round trips to a big hospital to queue for prescriptions. Within the same insurance locale (also called the pooling region), the reimbursement rate at primary-level hospitals is, in principle, about 10 percentage points higher than at the next tier up
Note
"Meeting the conditions" is the doctor's call — generally people whose diagnosis is clear and whose medication regimen is stable. Same drug, same prescription; what you save is the half-day monthly trip and the registration fee. If the primary level doesn't stock your drug, ask whether there is a drug-shortage registry and delivery service. The same document also requires tier-3 hospitals to gradually trim routine outpatient visits for these chronic conditions, with routine clinics by the same specialists moved into the community. Keep treating the big hospital as a prescription pickup point, and appointments will only get harder to get.
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Building of a Tiered Diagnosis and Treatment System. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031…: "For chronic disease patients who meet the conditions, primary-level medical and health institutions may issue a long-term prescription of no more than 12 weeks of medication per visit."; the same document, "in principle, inpatient reimbursement rates of medical and health institutions within a pooling region are staggered by a gap of roughly 10 percentage points per tier", and it requires higher-level hospitals to open outpatient clinics at the primary level for common and chronic conditions such as hypertension, diabetes, and chronic obstructive pulmonary disease; the same document, "tier-3 hospitals shall focus on acute, critical, and complex cases, strengthen referral, consultation, and inpatient services, and gradually reduce routine follow-up visits for common conditions and routine outpatient visits for chronic conditions with clear diagnoses and stable conditions", "and extend specialist-team routine outpatient clinics to primary-level medical and health institutions"
6

Before signing with a community family doctor, ask what's covered by insurance and what's out of pocket

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The basic service package you sign up for is covered by medical insurance as regulated. Personalized service packages are paid entirely out of pocket. When someone pitches an "upgrade package", first ask whether it is the basic package or a personalized one, whether it has been filed, and what it costs a year.

Cost
Costs nothing. One extra question before signing — a minute's work.
Benefit
The basic service package is paid for by medical insurance as regulated. Personalized service packages are paid entirely by the individual, and such packages must also be filed with the county-level health department
Note
The value of signing up lies in having someone following your condition long-term, not in how many items get bundled. When someone pitches an "upgrade package", ask three things first: basic package or personalized package, filed or not, and how much a year.
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Building of a Tiered Diagnosis and Treatment System. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031…: "Strengthen the policy linkage between primary outpatient payment and contracted services: the basic service package is covered by medical insurance payment as regulated; personalized service packages are filed by the signing primary-level medical and health institution with the county-level health department according to procedure, and the costs are paid by the individual."
7

Once diagnosed with diabetes, get a retinal exam, then follow-up at the doctor's intervals; check your feet once a year

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

By the time diabetes damages your retinas or your feet, there is almost no sensation — right up until you can't see or the flesh starts to rot. Found early, it is still treatable. With type 2 diabetes, get a dilated retinal exam at diagnosis; with type 1, start 5 years after onset. If one or two exams come back clear and your blood sugar is on target, you can stretch to every one or two years. Feet: once a year.

Cost
A dilated retinal exam runs tens to hundreds of yuan. The foot exam is usually included in the outpatient visit, at no extra charge. The hard part is remembering to go while your eyes and feet feel perfectly fine.
Benefit
Diabetes damage to the retina is called retinopathy; damage to the foot, diabetic foot. Neither gives much warning before it goes wrong. Found early, there is still treatment. Wait until you can't see or the foot starts to rot, and it is too late
Note
Type 2 gets examined at diagnosis; type 1 doesn't start until 5 years after onset. The difference: with type 2, blood sugar has often been quietly high for years already. If one or two exams show nothing and blood sugar is on target, you can stretch to every 1 to 2 years. If sensation in your feet has dulled, look at the soles of your feet yourself every day — a mirror works too.
Sources (1 reference)
American Diabetes Association (2026). Standards of Care in Diabetes—2026, Chapter 12: Retinopathy, Neuropathy, and Foot Care. Diabetes Care: "People with type 2 diabetes should have an initial dilated and comprehensive eye examination by an ophthalmologist or optometrist at the time of the diabetes diagnosis." "Adults with type 1 diabetes should have an initial dilated and comprehensive eye examination by an ophthalmologist or optometrist 5 years after the onset of diabetes." "If there is no evidence of retinopathy from one or more annual eye exams and glycemic indicators are within the goal range, then screening every 1–2 years may be considered." "Perform a comprehensive foot evaluation at least annually to identify risk factors for ulcers and amputations." https://doi.org/10.2337/dc26-S012
8

After kidney stones, drink 2.5–3 liters of water a day and keep salt under 6 grams

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Of people with a first calcium stone who do nothing, about one in four grows another within five years. Of those who drink enough water every day, only about one in ten recurs within five years — cut by more than half. The UK guideline's numbers: 2.5 to 3 liters of water a day, and salt no more than 6 grams.

Cost
Costs nothing. Turn steady sipping into a habit. On heavy-sweat days drink more still; the hard part is remembering every single day.
Benefit
A 5-year randomized controlled trial with two groups, covering 199 patients with a first calcium stone of no identifiable cause (also called idiopathic calcium stones). One group drank at least 2 liters of water a day; the other received no intervention at all. Recurrences over 5 years: 12/99 (12.1%) in the water group vs 27/100 (27.0%) in the no-intervention group, P=0.008. The smaller the P value, the less the difference between the two groups looks like chance. Average interval to recurrence: 38.7±13.2 months vs 25.1±16.4 months, P=0.016. Baseline 24-hour urine volume: stone patients measured markedly lower than people without stones — men 1,057±238 mL vs 1,401±562 mL (P<0.0001), women 990±230 mL vs 1,239±440 mL (P<0.001). NICE guideline NG118, recommendation 1.8.1, advises adults to drink 2.5 to 3 liters of water a day, and children and adolescents 1 to 2 liters depending on age. Add fresh lemon juice to the water, skip carbonated drinks, and keep adult salt intake at no more than 6 grams a day
Note
Recurrence cut by roughly 55% at no cost — by this book's ranking rules, the best-value item in this section. What you watch is 24-hour urine volume, with a target above 2 to 2.5 liters — not how much you drink. Heavy sweaters and people who work in high heat need to drink even more. That trial covered first-episode idiopathic calcium stone patients. Stones come in more than one composition: uric acid stones, infection stones, and cystine stones each have their own playbook. If you have recurred, a stone-composition analysis and a 24-hour urine test are worth doing before deciding whether to add medication. Don't cut out calcium to prevent stones — see Section 6, item 21. Severe flank or abdominal cramping during an episode means a trip to the hospital; you don't flush a stone out by drinking more water. Painless blood in the urine calls for a different set of tests — see Section 1, item 27
Sources (2 references)
Borghi L, Meschi T, Amato F, Briganti A, Novarini A, Giannini A (1996). Urinary volume, water and recurrences in idiopathic calcium nephrolithiasis: a 5-year randomized prospective study. The Journal of Urology, 155(3), 839-843. https://doi.org/10.1016/s0022-5347(01)66321-3; National Institute for Health and Care Excellence (2019). Renal and ureteric stones: assessment and management. NICE guideline NG118, recommendation 1.8.1. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/ng118/chapter/Recommendations
9

Once diagnosed with gout, take urate-lowering medication long-term and keep blood uric acid below 360 µmol/L for good

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Gout calls for long-term urate-lowering medication to press uric acid below 360 µmol/L — not just painkillers when it hurts. Among patients whose doses a nurse adjusted based on lab results, 95% hit target after two years, against 30% under usual care. Even at target, you don't stop. Diet restrictions alone won't get you to that line, and quitting alcohol lowers it by only 1.6 mg/dL.

Cost
Allopurinol runs a few to a few dozen yuan a month. Early on, test blood uric acid every few weeks to adjust the dose; once stable, every few months. For the first 3 to 6 months you also take a flare-prevention drug alongside. The hard part is staying on it when nothing hurts.
Benefit
A randomized controlled trial with two groups: 517 adults who had flared within the previous 12 months. One group was nurse-led — patients were taught clearly what the disease is, and urate was titrated to target by the numbers. The other carried on with their GP as usual. Share with blood uric acid down to <360 µmol/L (6 mg/dL) at 2 years: 95% vs 30%. The odds of reaching target were 3.18 times the usual-care group's (RR 3.18, 95% CI 2.42–4.18 — the credible range for that number), P<0.0001. The secondary outcomes at year 2 — flare frequency, tophi, quality of life — were also all better than usual care. Each additional quality-adjusted life year (a year of life weighted for its quality) cost £5,066. The same trial also ran a follow-up study: questionnaires went to 438 people, with 82% returned. Both groups self-reported their flares over the past 12 months. The target group's median was 0 flares (the middle half fell between 0 and 0). The usual-care group: 1 (0–3), P<0.001. The range in parentheses is called the interquartile range. The share still taking urate-lowering medication was 1.19 times that of the usual-care group (adjusted RR 1.19, 1.09–1.30). The American College of Rheumatology's 2020 gout guideline strongly recommends starting urate-lowering therapy for three kinds of people: those with tophi under the skin, those whose imaging shows gout gnawing defects into bone, and those who flare ≥2 times a year. The method: keep monitoring blood uric acid and titrate the dose by the results until target, goal <6 mg/dL. Allopurinol is the first choice, including for people with stage 3 or worse chronic kidney disease, at a starting dose ≤100 mg/day. When starting, an anti-inflammatory prophylactic is given alongside, taken for at least 3 to 6 months. The same guideline also cites a case series: patients who stopped the drug after long-term good control, with blood uric acid still holding at <7 mg/dL after stopping. Among them, only 13% (27/211) went five years of follow-up without a single flare. On diet: people who limit or quit alcohol run blood uric acid 1.6 mg/dL lower than those who don't; one serving of beer raises it by 0.16 mg/dL. Healthy diet, the Mediterranean diet, and the DASH diet do even less. There is disagreement over the first-choice urate-lowering drug. The American College of Rheumatology guideline strongly recommends allopurinol as first choice — effective at adequate doses, well tolerated, safe, and cheap. It conditionally suggests that people on febuxostat with a cardiovascular history, or a new cardiovascular event, switch if another drug is available. That recommendation is consistent with the FDA's boxed warning on febuxostat. One basis is the CARES trial: 6,190 gout patients with cardiovascular disease randomized to febuxostat or allopurinol. All-cause mortality risk in the febuxostat group was 1.22 times that of the allopurinol group (HR 1.22, 95% CI 1.01–1.47 — about 22% higher). Cardiovascular death was 1.34 times (1.03–1.73 — about 34% higher). Europe's FAST trial came out differently. It enrolled 6,128 patients over 60 with cardiovascular risk factors, and febuxostat showed no more major cardiovascular events than allopurinol (HR 0.85, 0.70–1.03). Deaths: 7.2% on febuxostat vs 8.6% on allopurinol. For people taking uricosuric drugs (which push uric acid out through the kidneys), the American College of Rheumatology conditionally recommends against alkalinizing the urine: no evidence it works, and the certainty of the evidence is very low. It does instruct that these people be told to drink more water; those with known kidney stones or stage 3 or worse chronic kidney disease should not use this drug class
Note
Contested: which drug to lower urate differs across national guidelines. The US guideline prefers allopurinol and has people with cardiovascular disease switch off febuxostat if they can, but the European FAST trial saw no added danger from febuxostat. Benzbromarone is also available in China; it is a uricosuric. The Chinese Medical Association's guidelines (2019 edition and 2024 update) give their own recommendations on drug choice and urine alkalinization. On whether to add sodium bicarbonate to alkalinize the urine while taking benzbromarone, the US guideline finds no evidence; follow your own doctor's advice, and don't skip the extra water. If you are Han Chinese, it is worth testing for HLA-B*5801 before starting allopurinol. It is an inherited gene type involved in immune response; test once and the result holds for life. Carriers make up 7.4% of Han Chinese, Korean, and Thai people, against only 0.7% of white and Hispanic people. After taking allopurinol, Asian and Black patients run three times the risk of allopurinol hypersensitivity syndrome that white patients do; in severe cases the skin peels off in large sheets, and it can be fatal. The American College of Rheumatology's 2020 gout guideline suggests that for these two groups, testing before starting the drug may be considered. Lowering urate at the outset actually makes flares more likely to be triggered, which is why the guideline explicitly requires an anti-inflammatory prophylactic for the first 3 to 6 months. "It hurt more after I started the urate-lowering drug, so I stopped" is the most common way this fails. What you do when it hurts is add the anti-inflammatory as prescribed — not stop the urate-lowering drug. Target values are written differently by different bodies: <6 mg/dL is roughly 360 µmol/L, and Chinese lab reports mostly use µmol/L. High uric acid found on a checkup with never a single flare is a different matter — see Section 6, item 19. For sugary drinks and alcohol, see Section 2, items 7 and 19 (no sugary drinks; drink little or no alcohol)
Sources (6 references)
Doherty M, Jenkins W, Richardson H, et al. (2018). Efficacy and cost-effectiveness of nurse-led care involving education and engagement of patients and a treat-to-target urate-lowering strategy versus usual care for gout: a randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 392(10156), 1403-1412. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(18)32158-5; Abhishek A, Jenkins W, La-Crette J, Fernandes G, Doherty M (2020). Nurse-led care is preferred over GP-led care of gout and improves gout outcomes: results of Nottingham Gout Treatment Trial follow-up study. Rheumatology, 59(3), 575-579. https://doi.org/10.1093/rheumatology/kez333; FitzGerald JD, Dalbeth N, Mikuls T, et al. (2020). 2020 American College of Rheumatology Guideline for the Management of Gout. Arthritis Care & Research, 72(6), 744-760. https://doi.org/10.1002/acr.24180; White WB, Saag KG, Becker MA, et al.; CARES Investigators (2018). Cardiovascular Safety of Febuxostat or Allopurinol in Patients with Gout. New England Journal of Medicine, 378(13), 1200-1210. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1710895; Mackenzie IS, Ford I, Nuki G, et al.; FAST Study Group (2020). Long-term cardiovascular safety of febuxostat compared with allopurinol in patients with gout (FAST): a multicentre, prospective, randomised, open-label, non-inferiority trial. Lancet, 396(10264), 1745-1757. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(20)32234-0; Chinese Society of Endocrinology (2020). Chinese guideline for the management of hyperuricemia and gout (2019). Chinese Journal of Endocrinology and Metabolism, 36(1), 1-13. https://doi.org/10.3760/cma.j.issn.1000-6699.2020.01.001

17. When there are elderly at home

9 items

Basis: money and personal freedom. With elderly at home, most of the trouble is not a shortage of money but failing to get the words said and the papers signed in advance. The last two items cover pressure sores from long-term bed rest and cataract surgery; they are tallied on mortality and are not compared with the other items in this section.

1

While the elder is still lucid, designate their future guardian in writing

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

While the elder's mind is still clear, spend a few hundred yuan at a notary office on a written document naming who will be their guardian down the road. Without that document, once the elder can no longer make their own decisions, a court decides who signs on their behalf and who manages their money. If the family disagrees, it drags on even longer.

Cost
One visit to a notary office, a few hundred yuan. One conversation with the elder settles it. The hard part is raising it: you have to say to their face that a day may come when they cannot manage their own affairs
Benefit
The Civil Code provides that an adult of sound mind who can make their own decisions (in legal terms, "an adult with full capacity for civil conduct") may arrange in advance, with another party, who will be their guardian. That party can be a close relative or any other individual or organization willing to serve. Once agreed, the guardian must be "determined in writing". When the elder can no longer make decisions, or can make only some of them (in legal terms, "loses or partially loses capacity for civil conduct"), the person named in the document takes over. Without it, who signs and who manages the money is settled through court appointment
Note
This document is called guardianship by agreement: you name in advance the person you choose. That person stands ahead of the default statutory order of guardians. Elders living alone, with children far away, or in complicated family situations need it all the more. Notarization at a notary office is recommended
Sources (1 reference)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 33). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
2

Make the will; remember a later will overrides an earlier one, and notarized wills no longer take priority

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The law recognizes six forms of will, but a mistake in form voids the whole document — the most common way a will fails. The handwritten kind must be written out by the testator personally, from start to finish, signed, and dated with the year, month, and day. If several wills conflict, the latest one governs. Since 2021, a notarized will no longer automatically takes precedence.

Cost
Handwriting a will yourself costs nothing. Notarization at a notary office runs a few hundred to over a thousand yuan. The hard part is raising it: you have to talk with the family about what happens after death
Benefit
The Civil Code recognizes six forms of will: handwritten by the testator, written down at their dictation, printed, recorded in audio or video, oral, and notarized. Each has its own formalities that must be met (in legal terms, "formal requisites"). If several wills conflict, the latest one prevails. Since 2021, the notarized one no longer automatically takes precedence
Note
A handwritten will must be written out by the testator personally, from start to finish, signed, and dated with the year, month, and day. A printed will requires two or more witnesses. The testator and the witnesses must sign every page and write the date in full. Heirs, anyone named in the will to receive property, and their close relatives may not serve as witnesses. A defect in form voids the entire will — the most common way a will fails
Sources (1 reference)
National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1134 to 1142). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml
3

Keep the elder's money in a separate account, with a two-person confirmation rule for large spending

Grade CValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Scams that get elders to buy supplements, collectibles, or wealth products all run the same play: spend a few months building trust, then take everything in one sweep. Agree beforehand on one rule — any spending above a set amount gets mentioned to a named person first. That pushes the moment of handing over the money back past the most impulsive stretch.

Cost
Costs nothing. One family discussion to set an amount. The hard part is how to raise it without making the elder feel you are guarding against them
Benefit
Scams targeting elders with supplements, collectibles, and wealth products all work by spending months accumulating trust and then harvesting it in one sweep. Agree in advance that "any spending above a set amount gets mentioned to a named person first". That delays the decision to hand over the money past the most impulsive stretch
Note
Do not frame it as "we're afraid you'll be scammed". Framing it as "the family's money is tracked in one ledger" goes down easier. And do not put all of the elder's money into the children's keeping — that invites a different kind of dispute
Sources
Author's experience; no direct references. For general anti-fraud rules see Sections 8 and 13
4

Equip the elder with a line they can always say: 'I need to go home and discuss it with my family'

Grade CValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Sales pitches and scams run on in-the-moment pressure that makes people too embarrassed to refuse on the spot. Rehearse one line with the elder in advance: "I need to go home and discuss it with my family." They can say it at any time and save face on the spot. That works better than reasoning with them after the fact.

Cost
Costs nothing. One conversation with the elder, a few minutes
Benefit
Sales pitches and scams both rely on pressure in the moment. Agreeing in advance on the line "I need to go home and discuss it with my family" gives the elder a face-saving way out. More effective than reasoning after the fact
Note
Use it together with Item 3 (a separate account for the elder's money). While you're at it, do the fall-proofing at home too; see Section 1. The line gives the elder a face-saving out so they don't have to push back hard on the spot — it is not for guarding against them. When salespeople close in, the hardest thing is saying no in front of a roomful of people — harder than judging what's true
Sources
Author's experience; no direct references
5

Any 'invest in retirement' scheme that wants money up front is untouchable: cards, beds, senior apartments, resort stays, senior products — all the same illegal fundraising

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Every retirement scheme that takes money up front and promises returns is the same scam: membership cards, beds, senior apartments, resort-style retirement stays, conferences selling senior products. Under the rules, if this money is lost, you bear the loss yourself. One scheme collected 136 million yuan by pre-selling retirement-apartment beds and burned more than 2,100 people. The only step you can block is the handover of money.

Cost
Costs nothing. Read the schemes below to the elder once; a few minutes. From then on, refuse outright: no lectures, no site visits, no leaving a phone number. The hard part: if the elder has already gone a few times and gotten friendly with people, they are hard to talk out of it
Benefit
The Ministry of Civil Affairs lists five forms; recognizing the scheme is more reliable than judging the people. First, in the name of an elderly care service institution: no real operation, a rented venue for the occasion, and a claimed cooperation agreement with a care institution as "proof" of legitimacy. Second, in the name of providing "elderly care services": selling "VIP cards", "membership cards", and "prepaid cards", collecting "elderly care service fees" in advance, with promised services clearly exceeding their own bed capacity. Third, in the name of investing in "retirement projects". Common versions: buying shares in wellness and retirement bases, selling nonexistent senior apartments, plus long-term rental of care beds and "time bank" mutual-aid retirement. The hooks are sales with principal repayment, sale-and-leaseback, and agreed buybacks. Fourth, in the name of selling "senior products": product buybacks, consignment sales, consumption rebates, free health checks, gifts, conference marketing, wellness lectures, and free expert clinics. Fifth, in the name of "resort-style retirement": cheap or free tours, stored-value rebates, and points-based retirement. The money cannot be recovered; the regulation says so in writing. Article 25 of the Regulations on the Prevention and Disposal of Illegal Fundraising provides that "losses from participating in illegal fundraising are borne by the participants themselves" — money lost is written off. In officially reported cases, Dai Mouping and others illegally raised 136 million yuan in the name of pre-selling retirement-apartment beds, victimizing more than 2,100 people; Dai Mouping was sentenced to 15 years for fundraising fraud plus a 400,000-yuan fine. Cao Mouming committed fundraising fraud of 13.207 billion yuan in the name of investing in the elderly care industry, involving more than 110,000 people; he was sentenced to life imprisonment, deprivation of political rights for life, and confiscation of all personal property. Supplement conference sales are prosecuted as fraud. Ni Mourong used free banquets, gifts, and chauffeured rides to pull elders into sales lectures. Lecturers fabricated anti-cancer and cancer-fighting claims with "fake personas, fake cases, and inflated discounting". Elders were tricked into buying "dihydroquercetin" at dozens of times its cost price. Sales totaled over 620,000 yuan. Ni Mourong was sentenced to 10 years and 3 months plus a 120,000-yuan fine (nationwide; the regulation took effect May 1, 2021)
Note
Judge not by "this outfit looks legit" but by "did they ask for money up front, did they promise returns". Care institutions are supposed to sell services; the moment the pitch turns to investment, rebates, or getting your principal back, don't believe it. Being taken to lectures, tours, or free clinics is not itself illegal and is hard to stop. What you can block is the handover of money — use it together with the two-person confirmation rule in Item 3. If money has already been paid, immediately demand a payment stop by calling 110 or 96110 per Section 8, Item 2, and report to the local lead department for handling illegal fundraising. House-for-pension is a different route; see Item 6 (reverse-mortgage pension insurance for the elderly).
