6

Beyond the insurer's reverse-mortgage pension product, touch no 'house-for-pension' schemes, and never mortgage the house to buy wealth products

Grade BValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

There is exactly one legitimate house-for-pension arrangement: the insurer's reverse-mortgage pension insurance for the elderly, still in a pilot. The version sold door to door has nothing to do with it; it tricks elders into mortgaging the house, then steers the borrowed money into the wealth products it recommends. Some people never even knew their house was mortgaged — and ended up losing the house while still carrying the loan.

Cost
Costs nothing. Never hand the property deed to anyone who shows up pitching "house-for-pension". Have the children read any mortgage, guarantee, or loan agreement before signing. The hard part: the visitors are often warm and make many trips, and the elder feels awkward turning them away
Benefit
The CBIRC Consumer Protection Bureau spelled out the real one and the fake ones. There is exactly one legitimate house-for-pension arrangement, called "reverse-mortgage pension insurance for the elderly". An elder with full legal ownership of the home mortgages the property to an insurance company. They keep living in it, using it, and collecting rent on it. Selling or otherwise disposing of it requires the mortgagee's (the insurer's) consent. The elder receives a pension on the agreed terms until death. The product is still in a pilot phase and uptake is low. The "house-for-pension" pitched by fraudsters is "entirely unrelated" to the state's pilot reverse-mortgage pension insurance; it is "a propaganda device that borrows national policy to build momentum for illegal fundraising". The play is to trick elders into mortgaging the property, then put the borrowed money into the wealth products the fraudster recommends — "often a 'repay the old with the new' Ponzi scheme". The warning's own words on the aftermath: "some participants did not even know their property had been mortgaged and ultimately lost the house while still carrying the loan". The alert also draws a line for judging yields, quoting: "if a wealth product promises returns above 6%, treat it with suspicion; above 8% is very dangerous; above 10%, be prepared to lose your entire principal — 'guaranteed high returns' is financial fraud". The same alert also demands "great care at the contract-signing stage; never sign a blank contract" (nationwide, June 2021)
Note
Grade B because these claims come from a regulator's risk alert and experience-based judgment, not research data. The 6%, 8%, and 10% lines are consumer reference points from the regulator, not legal standards. The CBIRC has since been merged into the National Financial Regulatory Administration; the original posting is no longer reachable, and what is cited here is a provincial financial regulator's republication. Losing money on wealth products is the lesser problem: once the house is mortgaged the elder still owes a loan, and the loss far exceeds the principal. For general rules on signing and blank contracts, see Section 8, Item 17; for stopping payments after being scammed, Section 8, Item 2.
Sources (2 references)
CBIRC Consumer Rights Protection Bureau (2021). Risk Alert on Guarding Against 'Invest-in-Retirement' and 'House-for-Pension' Financial Fraud (No. 3 of 2021). https://dfjrjgj.hunan.gov.cn/dfjrjgj/yhlj/202106/t20210608_… (republished by the Hunan Provincial Local Financial Supervision and Administration Bureau); Ministry of Civil Affairs and China Banking and Insurance Regulatory Commission (2021). Risk Alert on Illegal Fundraising in the Elderly Care Sector (fourth form: illegal fundraising in the name of declaring "house-for-pension"). https://www.mca.gov.cn/n152/n164/c36171/content.html
7

With an elder long bedridden or severely disabled, apply to the medical insurance authority where they're enrolled for long-term care insurance; it is not only for the elderly

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Long-term care insurance helps pay for hired care. If someone in the family is severely disabled for more than six months, apply to the medical insurance authority where they are enrolled. You don't front the care costs: about 70% is reimbursed for those enrolled as employees, about 50% for those enrolled as urban and rural residents; bed fees and meal fees are not covered. There is no age threshold — a young person with severe disability can apply too.

Cost
File one application with the medical insurance authority where the person is enrolled. Then one disability-level assessment. If they pass on the first assessment, the assessment fee is covered by the fund — you don't pay out of pocket
Benefit
Qualifying long-term care service costs have no deductible. A deductible means paying a threshold out of pocket before reimbursement starts; here there is none. Enrolled under the employer-employee policy, the fund reimburses about 70%. Enrolled under the non-employed urban and rural resident policy, about 50%. The most that can be reimbursed in a year (the annual payment cap) does not exceed 50% of the previous year's per-capita disposable income of urban and rural residents in the local pooling area
Note
The disability must be "long-lasting (generally more than 6 months)"; a few weeks in the hospital does not reach the threshold. There is also a 6-month waiting period before benefits start. Costs that are not care — bed fees, meal fees — are not paid by long-term care insurance, and neither are medical costs that belong to medical insurance. Those already receiving the work-injury living-care allowance do not get both. This money and the care subsidy within the two subsidies for people with disabilities are two separate processes and two separate payments; they do not conflict — see Section 7, Item 8 (the two subsidies). Care at home and in the community gets favorable reimbursement rates, so an institution is not the only option. The program rolls out in batches across localities, and disability assessment standards differ. First call 12393 or the medical insurance handling agency where the person is enrolled to ask whether it has started locally and how to book an assessment. If the assessment fails, don't give up — reapply once the disability worsens.
Sources (2 references)
National Healthcare Security Administration and seven other departments (2026). Notice on Issuing the Implementation Plan for Accelerating the Establishment of the Long-Term Care Insurance System. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202603/content_7063915…: covered persons are "disabled persons who have enrolled and paid premiums as required, whose disabled state has lasted long term (generally more than 6 months), and whose disability has been confirmed by assessment upon application"; "at the system's start-up stage, coverage targets the severely disabled"; "benefits have no deductible. For qualifying long-term care service costs, those enrolled under the non-employed urban and rural resident policy are paid by the fund at about 50%; those enrolled under the employer-employee policy at about 70%, and retirees receive employer-employee benefits"; "the annual fund payment cap for insured persons does not exceed 50% of the pooling area's previous-year per-capita disposable income of urban and rural residents"; "the fixed waiting period for benefits is in principle set at 6 months". See also the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council, Opinions on Accelerating the Establishment of the Long-Term Care Insurance System. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12666/202604/content_…
8

With someone long bedridden, treat pressure sores as public enemy number one: get an alternating-pressure air mattress, turn them at set intervals, and check the bony prominences once a day

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: littleTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Elders who already have pressure sores before hip-fracture surgery are about 20% more likely to die within 30 days. Switching to an electric air mattress cuts new pressure sores by about 60%. Turning on schedule, done properly, cuts them by about 70%. Don't let anyone lie face down for long stretches. Check the sacrum-tailbone, heels, hips, and shoulders and back once a day; if you find a red mark that doesn't fade when pressed, get a nurse or doctor that same day.

Cost
A home electric alternating-pressure air mattress starts at a few hundred yuan. One turn takes only minutes. The hard part is turning every two to three hours without pause, nights included — one person can't carry it alone
Benefit
19,520 hip-fracture surgery patients (US NSQIP, 2016 to 2019). Those with pressure sores before surgery died within 30 days at a higher rate. The association held after adjusting for other factors (OR 1.2, a 21% increase in the odds, P=0.004). They also had more other problems: deep vein thrombosis (OR 1.59), pneumonia (OR 1.39), unplanned readmission (OR 1.43), plus 0.4 more days in hospital on average. 324 hospitalized elders (average age 86) followed for a median of 18 months. Pressure sores predicted long-term mortality on their own (HR 1.500, 95% CI 1.059 to 2.126, P=0.020). "On their own" means it predicts even after other factors are ruled out. 65 randomized trials pooled (network meta-analysis), comparing powered active air-flow support surfaces with standard hospital mattresses (standard hospital support surfaces). Powered active air-flow surfaces are the electric air mattress category. Users had lower pressure sore incidence (RR 0.42, 95% CI 0.29 to 0.63, moderate certainty). Powered hybrid air-flow surfaces: RR 0.22 (0.07 to 0.66). A Cochrane review of 11 trials and 4,462 people (2026 update). Turning every 2 hours versus every 4 hours: the difference is unclear (RR 1.05, 95% CI 0.79 to 1.39, very low certainty). Comparisons between other turning intervals were equally very uncertain. In a trial of 1,226 ICU patients, wearable sensors giving real-time reminders and visual alerts made the 2-hour turning schedule actually happen; pressure sore incidence was lower than with usual care (RR 0.28, 95% CI 0.10 to 0.75, moderate certainty). In a 116-person trial, the prone (face-down) group had higher pressure sore incidence than the supine (face-up) group (RR 4.55, 95% CI 2.31 to 8.98)
Note
Three reasons for the B. First, the two mortality studies only show "people with pressure sores fared worse later"; that does not mean "preventing pressure sores lowers mortality". Second, the turning-interval randomized trials rest on shaky conclusions. Third, the air-mattress evidence is firmer, but the studies compared hospital-bed mattresses, so extending it to home mattresses is an extrapolation. Daily checks of the sacrum-tailbone, heels, hips, and shoulders and back for "a red mark that doesn't fade when pressed" are standard nursing practice with no separate citation. For care services reimbursable under long-term care insurance, see Item 7 of this section. A suddenly swollen leg should be handled as deep vein thrombosis — see Section 13, Item 11. For the stretch of long-term bed rest after a fall or serious injury, see Section 1, Item 34
Sources (4 references)

PLoS ONE, 13(2), e0192707. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0192707; Latimer SL, Chaboyer WP, Probst S, et al. (2026). Repositioning for pressure injury prevention in adults. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 6, CD009958. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD009958.pub4
9

When the elder's cataracts impede seeing the road, get an eye evaluation for surgery; with both eyes affected, don't delay the second too long

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: a lotTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

For women over 70, first-eye cataract surgery done promptly cut the number of falls over a year by about 34%, and fewer people fractured bones. But the number who fell at least once did not drop. For the second eye, surgery showed no clear difference in falls. Elders who had surgery had about 16% fewer hip fractures within a year.

Cost
First accompany the elder to ophthalmology for one examination; the doctor judges whether surgery is warranted. One eye, one operation; many hospitals do it as day surgery and the patient goes home the same day. With cataracts in both eyes, it's done in two operations. Out-of-pocket cost depends on which intraocular lens (artificial lens) is chosen and how local medical insurance reimburses — ask clearly before surgery.
Benefit
A randomized trial enrolled 306 women over 70 with cataracts. Half had first-eye surgery within about 4 weeks; the other half waited the usual 12 months. Over a year, the prompt-surgery group fell about 34% fewer times. The raw value was a rate ratio of falls of 0.66, 95% CI 0.45 to 0.96. People who fell at least once: 49% in the surgery group versus 45% in the waiting group — no reduction. People who fell more than twice: 18% in the surgery group versus 25% in the waiting group. 4 people in the surgery group fractured a bone (3%) versus 12 in the waiting group (8%). The Cochrane review included this trial and concluded that first-eye surgery in women reduced the number of falls, while second-eye surgery did not. The second-eye randomized trial enrolled 239 women over 70. The surgery group's fall rate was 32% lower, but the difference could be chance (rate ratio 0.68, 95% CI 0.39 to 1.19). In a 5% sample of US Medicare, there were 1,113,640 cataract patients over 65 (2002 to 2009). This study was observational tracking only, with no comparison groups. Those who had surgery had about 16% lower odds of hip fracture within a year (OR 0.84, 95% CI 0.81 to 0.87). The absolute difference was 0.20 percentage points, about 2 fewer cases per 1,000 people
Note
Controversy: pooling the two randomized trials, the number of people who fell did not clearly decrease (OR 0.81, 95% CI 0.55 to 1.17). In Western Australia's whole-population hospital records, in the year after first-eye surgery, hospitalizations for fall injuries actually rose 27%. In the stretch between the two operations, such hospitalizations ran 2.14 times the preoperative rate. Before-and-after comparisons like these cannot separate the surgery's effect from the effect of people getting older. In another Australian cohort study, falls dropped the most after second-eye surgery — so with cataracts in both eyes, don't delay the second too long. In the stretch between the two operations, take extra care walking and on stairs. The Cochrane review also included one trial of helping elders manage vision problems; falls went up about 57%. Surgery is about seeing clearly; fewer falls also depend on Section 1, Item 13 (balance and leg strength). For whether bones can take a fall, see Section 1, Item 39 (bone density testing) and Section 1, Item 40 (treat osteoporosis once it's found). The national eye health plan states that sight-restoring cataract surgery is now widely available at the county level; a big-city hospital is not required. The beneficiaries here are mostly your parents and grandparents.

18. Is Raising a Kid Cost-Effective?

6 items

This section runs two ledgers, money and time. As with the marriage math in Section 10, it only breaks the accounts down for you; it does not draw the conclusion for you. If you are already pregnant and need to work through the process step by step, see Section 27.

1

Count what you can claim first: the national childcare subsidy is 3,600 yuan per child per year, paid up to age 3

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

If your child was born after January 1, 2025 and is not yet 3, you can claim this money. One of the parents applies where the child's household registration is. 3,600 yuan per child per year, paid all the way to age 3. It is not subject to individual income tax, and it does not count into your family's income when applying for aid such as the minimum living allowance.

Cost
Costs nothing. Apply where the child's household registration is; one trip and it's done
Benefit
The plan issued by the General Office of the CPC Central Committee and the General Office of the State Council provides: infants and toddlers born on or after January 1, 2025 who are under 3 receive "3,600 yuan per child per year". One of the child's parents or another guardian claims it. The subsidy is "exempt from individual income tax". When aid such as the minimum living allowance is assessed, it "is not counted into family or individual income"
Note
This is the national floor. Some provinces and cities have their own local subsidies that can be stacked on top of this one. Over three years it adds up to 10,800 yuan — a small slice of the cost of raising a child, so don't make it your basis for whether to have one
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the CPC Central Committee and General Office of the State Council (2025). Implementation Plan for the Childcare Subsidy System. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_12206/202508/content_…
2

Maternity leave is 98 days; the maternity allowance comes from the maternity insurance fund, based on your employer's average monthly employee wage of the previous year

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Childbirth brings at least 98 days of maternity leave, 15 of which may be taken before the birth. Difficult labor adds 15 days; each additional baby adds 15 more. The money paid over this period is the maternity allowance, paid by the maternity insurance fund. If your employer never enrolled you in maternity insurance, the employer pays it itself.

Cost
Costs nothing. The employer files the claim; you don't have to go anywhere
Benefit
The length of maternity leave is set by the State Council: "Female employees are entitled to 98 days of maternity leave, of which 15 days may be taken before the birth; for difficult labor, 15 days are added; for multiple births, 15 days are added for each additional infant." The money paid during leave is the maternity allowance. Those enrolled in maternity insurance are paid "by the maternity insurance fund at the standard of the employer's average monthly employee wage of the previous year". Those not enrolled are paid by the employer at your pre-leave wage standard
Note
98 days is the national minimum. Provincial population and family planning regulations generally add 60 or more days of reward leave on top, typically 158 days and up. Who pays the wages during the reward leave differs from province to province
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2012). Special Provisions on the Labor Protection of Female Employees (State Council Decree No. 619, Articles 7 and 8). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-05/07/content_658…
3

Know this rule: no pay cuts or dismissal for pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

During pregnancy, childbirth, and breastfeeding, cutting your pay or firing you is illegal, with fines of 1,000 to 5,000 yuan per person. While your child is under one, you get 1 hour a day for breastfeeding, and the employer cannot schedule you for overtime or night shifts. For how to claim compensation, see Section 19.

Cost
Costs nothing
Benefit
The State Council provides: "An employer may not, on account of an employee's pregnancy, childbirth, or breastfeeding, reduce her wages, dismiss her, or terminate her labor or employment contract." Over these three periods the employer cannot cut your pay, and cannot dismiss you or end your contract. While breastfeeding an infant under 1, you get 1 hour a day of nursing time. The employer also may not extend your working hours or assign night shifts. Violations draw a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 yuan per person
Note
If you are actually dismissed unlawfully, the claims route is in Section 19. The key evidence is written notices of reassignment or pay cuts and chat logs — keep both safe
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2012). Special Provisions on the Labor Protection of Female Employees (State Council Decree No. 619, Articles 5, 9, and 13). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-05/07/content_658…
4

Do the time math by 'whose time gets used up', not by 'how hard it feels'

Grade CValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Convert the daily hours of childcare and the number of night wakings into time. Multiply by the hourly wage of whoever does that work. The resulting number is usually far larger than the formula-and-diapers bill. So it's best to settle the division of labor before the child is born.

Cost
Costs no money; it costs time. Before age 3, a child occupies essentially the whole day. The hard part is that it's like this every day — you can't grit your teeth for a few days and be through it
Benefit
Convert daily childcare hours and night wakings into hours, then multiply by the hourly wage of whoever does the work. The number usually dwarfs the formula-and-diapers bill. Childcare, cooking, and getting up at night go unpaid, but book them into the cost all the same. The method is the same one Section 10 uses for housework. Settle the division of labor first; then decide whether to have a child
Note
The numbers need not be precise. What helps is two people talking through the division of labor over the same sheet before the birth, so they don't fight after it
Sources
Author's experience; no direct references. For the method, see Section 10
5

Split the money math into three stages: ages 0 to 3, compulsory education, and everything after

Grade CValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: a lotTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

From 0 to 3, the money mainly goes to how the child is cared for: by yourself, by the grandparents, or by hired help. From primary school through junior high, it mainly goes to housing and extracurriculars. After that, it mainly goes to the track of school admissions. The three stages spend money in completely different ways; mixing them only produces one scary total.

Cost
There is no fixed figure; it varies enormously by city and by care arrangement. The hard part is sitting down and splitting the three stages into separate accounts instead of plucking a number by feel
Benefit
From 0 to 3 the biggest item is the care arrangement: yourself, the grandparents, or hired help. During compulsory education (primary through junior high) it is housing and extracurricular spending. After that it is the path through school admissions. Where the money goes differs completely across the three stages; blend them together and you get nothing but a scary total
Note
First count in the money you can certainly get — the childcare subsidy, the maternity allowance, medical insurance reimbursements — then see how much is still missing. Don't decide based on the internet's "it takes however many hundred thousand to raise a child"; those numbers come with no clear method, and you can't tell what they counted or left out
Sources
Author's experience; no direct references
6

A child for your parents, a child for the marriage, a child for your old age — keep a separate ledger for each

Grade CValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

That others want you to have a child can count as one factor you weigh. But the time and the money go on your own ledger. "Raise children to secure your old age" deserves its own entry, because it bets on another person's finances and willingness twenty years out. Write down the consequences of not having one too, and compare the two sides.

Cost
Costs no money; it costs one serious conversation. The hard part is saying it plainly rather than talking around it
Benefit
Same approach as Section 10. Others' expectations can count as one factor you weigh. But the costs go on your own ledger, not on theirs. "Raising children to secure your old age" especially needs its own entry, because what it assumes is another person's finances and willingness twenty years out
Note
Write down "the consequences of not having a child" as well, and set it next to "the consequences of having one" for comparison
Sources
Author's experience; no direct references. For the same kind of analysis, see Section 10

19. Employment, Departure, and Work Injuries

18 items

This section is about money: how it is calculated, how contracts are signed, how deadlines run. The first three items cover money you should receive while still on the job; the next six cover leaving; the seven after that cover occupational disease and work injuries. Work-injury money runs an order of magnitude above layoff pay, and its deadlines are harder. Damage from occupational disease cannot be bought back. Three more items close the section: what to do about being bullied at work, how to get your separation certificate, and how income tax on severance is figured.

1

Overtime pay runs at 1.5x, 2x, or 3x; if it isn't paid, complain to the labor inspection authority — late payment adds another 50% to 100%

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Weekday overtime pays 1.5 times your wage. Weekend overtime with no compensatory time off pays 2 times. Working on statutory holidays like New Year's Day, Spring Festival, Labor Day, or National Day pays 3 times, and compensatory time off cannot replace it. If the company won't pay, complain to the labor inspection authority. If it still doesn't pay after being ordered to pay within a deadline, the employer owes an additional 50% to 100% of the arrears.

Cost
Costs nothing. As a habit, save your clock-in records, schedules, and overtime approval forms, and screenshot the boss's work assignments in the work group chat. The hard part is remembering to do it every month.
Benefit
The law's normal working hours are no more than 8 hours a day and no more than 44 hours a week on average. Weekday overtime generally may not exceed 1 hour a day. Where special reasons require more, no more than 3 hours a day, and no more than 36 hours in a month in total. Overtime pay has three tiers. Weekday extended hours: no less than 150% of wages. Working on a rest day with no compensatory rest arranged: no less than 200%. Working on a statutory holiday: no less than 300%. For the statutory-holiday tier, the statute offers no "pay compensatory time off instead" option. If an employer schedules overtime and won't pay for it, the labor administration department orders it to pay in full within a time limit. Past the deadline, it is ordered to pay the worker an additional damages amount of 50% to 100% of the sum owed, on top of the arrears (nationwide)
Note
Keep rest days and statutory holidays separate. Statutory holidays are only the few legally designated days a year — New Year's Day, Spring Festival, Labor Day, National Day, and the like. Days strung into long breaks by schedule swaps count as rest days, paid at 200%. "Company policy requires overtime approval" and "I stayed voluntarily" do not let the company off the hook, but they make your evidence harder — so keep the assignment and approval records. To adopt the two special hours arrangements — comprehensive working hours or flexible working hours — a company needs prior approval from the labor administration department; it cannot decide on its own. For the limitation period on disputes, see Section 8, Item 19.
Sources (2 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Labor Law (second amendment of 2018, Articles 36, 41, 43, and 44). https://www.samr.gov.cn/zw/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/bgt/art/2023/art… (carried by the State Administration for Market Regulation); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law (Article 85, item 3). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
2

Annual leave is 5, 10, or 15 days by total years worked; days you couldn't take convert to cash at 300% of your daily wage

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

With 1 to 10 total years of service across all employers, you get 5 days of annual leave a year. At 10 years it's 10 days; at 20 years, 15 days. Job changes still count toward the total. If the employer can't arrange the leave and you agree not to take it, those days pay 3 times your daily wage. Sign the "voluntary waiver of annual leave" form and you're left with normal pay only.

Cost
Costs nothing. Add up your years across all employers; social insurance payment records are the proof. The hard part: refusing to sign the "voluntary waiver of annual leave" form when the company slides it over.
Benefit
After 12 months of continuous work you have annual leave. The days are set by cumulative working time — years at all employers added together. 1 to 10 years: 5 days; 10 to 20 years: 10 days; 20 years: 15 days. Statutory holidays and rest days do not count against annual leave. If the employer genuinely cannot arrange the leave for work reasons and you personally agree to forgo it, the untaken days are paid "annual leave wages at 300% of the employee's daily wage income". That 300% already includes the normal day's pay you'd get for working, so what actually lands in your hands extra is 200%. Daily wage = your own monthly wage ÷ 21.75. Monthly wage is the average over the 12 months before payment, computed after excluding overtime pay. If you joined this employer in the current year, it is prorated over the calendar days remaining at that employer. On departure it is prorated by how much of the year you worked and settled up; extra leave already taken is not clawed back. An employer that neither arranges the leave nor pays is ordered to correct within a time limit. Past the deadline, it must pay an additional damages amount equal to the annual leave wages on top of them (nationwide, effective January 1, 2008)
Note
Cumulative working time adds up across employers; if you've changed jobs, don't go by your current employer's tenure. Only if the employee "forfeits the leave for personal reasons and does so in writing" may the employer pay normal wages only — so don't sign the "voluntary waiver of annual leave" form. With 20 or more days of personal leave in the year for which the employer doesn't dock your pay, you get no annual leave that year. Neither do you if sick leave exceeds the corresponding months: under 10 years of service, 2 months; 10 to 20 years, 3 months; over 20 years, 4 months. Family visit leave, marriage and bereavement leave, maternity leave, and the work-injury suspension-of-work-with-pay period do not count into annual leave.
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2007). Regulations on Paid Annual Leave for Employees (State Council Decree No. 514, Articles 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2008/content_859865.htm; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2008). Implementation Measures for Paid Annual Leave for Enterprise Employees (MHRSS Decree No. 1, Articles 3, 4, 5, 10, 11, 12, and 15). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2009/content_1265995.htm
3

Probation has legal caps, pay can't drop below 80%, and it can only be agreed once

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Contracts under 1 year: probation of at most 1 month. 1 to 3 years: at most 2 months. Over 3 years: at most 6 months. The same company may put you on probation only once — a second probation after confirmation via a transfer is illegal. Probation pay cannot fall below the lowest bracket for the same position or 80% of the contract wage, and never below the local minimum wage.

Cost
Costs nothing. Spend a few minutes before signing checking the contract's term against the probation length.
Benefit
Contracts of 3 months to under 1 year: probation may not exceed 1 month. 1 year to under 3 years: not over 2 months. 3 years or more, plus open-ended contracts with no end date: not over 6 months. Contracts sized to completing one task, or shorter than 3 months in total, may not include probation at all. "The same employer and the same worker may agree on probation only once" — one company, one person, one probation. If a contract states only a probation period, that probation is void and the stated term is the labor contract term. Probation pay "may not be lower than the lowest wage bracket for the same position at the employer or 80% of the wage agreed in the labor contract, and may not be lower than the minimum wage where the employer is located". If probation was agreed beyond the legal cap and the person actually worked, the employer owes extra compensation for the overage at your post-probation monthly wage. During probation the employer may terminate the contract only on the situations the law lists, and must explain its reasons to the worker (nationwide)
Note
The three most common violations. One: a 1-year contract with a 3-month probation. Two: a second probation after confirmation via a transfer. Three: "no social insurance during probation" — the social insurance obligation starts on your first day of work and has nothing to do with probation; the employer-side duties are in Section 12, Item 16. Being fired during probation doesn't mean you get nothing; it depends on whether the employer's reason is one of the kinds the law allows for dismissal. Unlawful termination pays 2N per Item 6.
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law (Articles 19, 20, 21, and 83). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
4

If you're laid off, first work out your N: one month's wage per full year, and half a month for less than six months

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Severance when you're laid off works like this: one month's wage per full year; half a year to a full year counts as a year; under half a year gets half a month's wage. The monthly wage here is your 12-month average before departure, with bonuses, allowances, and subsidies all included. Wages above 3 times the local previous-year monthly average wage are capped at 3 times, and the counted years max out at 12.

Cost
Costs nothing. One run with a calculator, ten minutes.
Benefit
The economic compensation defined in the Labor Contract Law — the money the employer owes you when you're laid off, commonly called N — works like this: "for each full year, pay one month's wage... six months or more but less than a year counts as one year; for less than six months, pay the worker half a month's wage". If the monthly wage exceeds 3 times the local previous-year average monthly employee wage, it is capped at 3 times, and service years count only up to 12
Note
Monthly wage means the average wage over the 12 months before the contract ends. Bonuses, allowances, and subsidies all count — not just base pay. This is where companies lowball most often. For whether this money is taxed, see Item 18 of this section (tax on severance)
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2008) (Article 47). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
5

If the company fires you without 30 days' notice, it owes you one extra month's pay

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If the company dismisses you because you can't do the job after illness, can't do the work, or circumstances have fundamentally changed, and it didn't give 30 days' written notice, it owes one extra month's wage beyond N — the well-known N+1. In negotiations, list that month separately; don't let the company fold it into N.

Cost
Costs nothing.
Benefit
Under the Labor Contract Law, an employer terminating under this article has two options. One: "notify the worker in writing 30 days in advance". The other: "terminate the contract after paying the worker one additional month's wage". If it wants you out immediately, it must pay the extra month. That extra month is commonly called payment in lieu of notice — a separate sum outside N. It is computed on your previous month's wage, while N uses the average wage of the 12 months before departure; the two bases differ
Note
The extra month appears only in the three situations of Article 40 of the Labor Contract Law: after illness or non-work-related injury, unable after the medical period to do the original job or any reassigned one; incompetent at the job and still incompetent after training or reassignment; or a major change in the objective circumstances underlying the contract with no agreement reached on changes. No other situations carry the extra month: economic layoffs (Article 41) only require the company to explain the situation to the union or all staff 30 days ahead; termination by mutual agreement at the company's proposal is N; dismissal for your own serious misconduct earns nothing; unlawful termination is 2N. For the three Article 40 cases, keep N and the 1 separate in negotiations — don't let the company fold the extra month into N
Sources (2 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2008) (Articles 36, 39, 40, 41, 46, 47, and 87). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm; State Council (2008). Implementation Regulations of the Labor Contract Law (State Council Decree No. 535), Article 20: "Where an employer, under Article 40 of the Labor Contract Law, chooses to terminate the contract by paying the worker one additional month's wage, that additional wage shall be set at the standard of the worker's previous month's wage." http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2008/content_1107604.htm
6

If the company terminates you unlawfully, compensation is twice the standard severance amount

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

If the company's termination is unlawful, damages are double the standard severance — the well-known 2N. Whether it is unlawful depends on the specifics. Ask legal aid or a lawyer first; then decide whether to negotiate with the company or go to arbitration.

Cost
Costs nothing. Arbitration takes months. The hard part is staying with it the whole way and not giving up halfway.
Benefit
The Labor Contract Law provides that where an employer terminates or ends a labor contract in violation of this law, it "shall pay the worker damages at twice the economic compensation standard set in Article 47". The method: compute one round of severance under the economic compensation standard, then double it
Note
This is the well-known 2N. What counts as unlawful termination depends on the specifics. Consult legal aid or a lawyer first, then decide between negotiating and arbitration; the routes are in Section 7
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2008) (Article 87). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
7

Don't sign 'resigning voluntarily for personal reasons' — sign it and your N is gone

Grade BValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Sign a paper admitting "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" and you usually forfeit both severance and unemployment insurance. Leaving of your own accord is not among the situations that earn compensation anyway — unless the company owes wages or skipped social insurance. You don't have to sign that day; sleep on it.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is withstanding the pressure to sign on the spot.
Benefit
The Labor Contract Law confines economic compensation to the categories it lists. A worker who leaves of their own accord is not among them — unless it is over statutory faults like unpaid wages or unpaid social insurance. Sign "voluntary resignation" and severance and unemployment insurance usually both evaporate
Note
The company's usual line: "sign first to keep the process moving; the compensation comes separately." Then it goes into the agreement on the spot, or you don't sign. Not signing that day carries no legal consequence; sleep on it
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law of the People's Republic of China (effective January 1, 2008) (Articles 38 and 46). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm
8

Before you leave, save your payslips, attendance records, labor contract, social insurance records, and chat logs

Grade CValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Once you hand back the computer and accounts, your payslips, attendance records, contract, social insurance records, and chat logs are gone for good. In arbitration, your wage level and whether you worked overtime still come down to the materials in your own hands. What you save is your own employment records; do not walk off with the company's source code or client lists.

Cost
Costs nothing. Half an hour to save the materials. The hard part is remembering to do it before you go.
Benefit
Once the computer and accounts are handed back, these materials are gone for good. Arbitration's burden of proof tilts toward the employer somewhat, but your wage level and whether there was overtime still rest on the evidence in your own hands
Note
What you save is your own employment material. Don't casually take the company's source code, client lists, or technical documents; the risks of taking them are in Section 11. When you go, also demand a separation certificate from the employer — see Item 17 of this section (separation certificate)
Sources
Author's experience; no direct references. For rights-enforcement routes, see Section 7
9

Before taking a post with dust, noise, or chemicals, check whether the contract names the hazards; the three occupational health checks are arranged and paid for by the employer

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

When signing, the employer must truthfully write into the contract what occupational hazards the post involves, how to protect against them, and what benefits apply. If it hid them from you, you can refuse the work and it cannot fire you for that. The three occupational health checks — before starting, during the job, and at departure — are arranged and paid for by the employer. Without a pre-departure exam, the employer cannot end your contract.

Cost
Costs nothing. When signing, read the "occupational hazard disclosure" part clause by clause. Get a copy of every health check report to keep. The hard part is asking face to face and walking out with the materials in hand.
Benefit
The Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases provides that when signing a labor contract, the employer must clearly state four things: what occupational hazards the work may produce, what consequences may follow, how to protect against them, and what benefits apply. The statute's words: "truthfully inform the worker and state it in the labor contract; concealment or deception is prohibited." If you are later reassigned to hazardous work the contract never disclosed, the employer must inform you truthfully again and negotiate contract changes with you. If it fails to, "the worker has the right to refuse work involving occupational hazards, and the employer may not terminate the labor contract for that reason". The health checks total three: before starting, during employment, and at departure. "Occupational health check costs are borne by the employer"; the employer pays, and the results must be given to you in writing. Without a pre-start check, the employer may not assign someone to work with occupational hazards. Nor may it assign people medically unsuited to such work (those with occupational contraindications) to those contraindicated jobs. Anyone found to have health damage related to the work must be moved out of the original post and properly resettled. "A labor contract may not be terminated or ended with a worker who has not had the pre-departure occupational health check". On departure you "have the right to request a copy of your own occupational health surveillance file, which the employer shall truthfully and gratuitously provide, signed and sealed on the copy". The employer must give you a truthful copy of this file free of charge, stamped and signed (nationwide)
Note
Three questions at the interview gauge how legit the outfit is: does the post involve occupational hazards, will they be written into the contract, and who pays for the pre-start health check. If they can't answer or say "just start first and we'll see", weigh the risk yourself. The pre-departure check is the most easily overlooked: without it the employer cannot terminate or end your contract. It is also key material for a future occupational disease diagnosis — the file copy likewise; get them in hand before you leave. Occupational disease itself runs through the work-injury track; benefits start at Item 11.
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases (2018 amendment, Articles 33, 35, and 36). https://www.beijing.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengcefagui/qtwj/201711… (republished by the Beijing Municipal People's Government)
10

Damage from dust, noise, and chemical toxins is irreversible: the employer must provide protective gear, and you can refuse work with no protective measures in place

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Pneumoconiosis, noise-induced hearing loss, and chemical eye burns are all statutory occupational diseases; once the lungs or hearing are damaged, they don't come back. You have the right to know the post's hazards, and the right to demand protective installations and gear from the employer. You can refuse work with no protection in place. Any pay cut or dismissal over that doesn't count.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is wearing particulate respirators, earplugs, and goggles the whole time, and refusing unprotected work — at the price of being called fussy by coworkers.
Benefit
From August 1, 2025, statutory occupational diseases number 135 kinds in 12 categories, including 4 open clauses. Category one is occupational pneumoconioses: silicosis, coal workers' pneumoconiosis, graphite pneumoconiosis, carbon black pneumoconiosis, asbestosis, and talc pneumoconiosis, plus cement pneumoconiosis, mica pneumoconiosis, potter's pneumoconiosis, aluminum pneumoconiosis, welders' pneumoconiosis, and foundry workers' pneumoconiosis, with one open clause. Occupational diseases of the ear, nose, throat, and mouth include noise-induced deafness and blast deafness. Occupational eye diseases include chemical eye burns and photoelectric ophthalmia. All this damage is irreversible; no treatment repairs the lungs or the hearing. The law gives four rights you can invoke on the spot. One: to know what occupational hazards exist in the workplace, what consequences they may cause, and what protective measures should be taken. Two: to demand that the employer provide qualified protective installations and personal protective equipment and improve working conditions. Three: to criticize, report, and file charges over violations of occupational disease prevention laws and regulations and over practices that endanger life and health. Four: "to refuse unlawful directives and orders to perform operations with no occupational disease protective measures" — non-compliant orders and unprotected work, you can decline. And "any reduction of a worker's wages, benefits, or other treatment, or termination of the labor contract, because the worker lawfully exercised these rights, is void". Pay cuts, benefit cuts, or dismissal for using these rights don't count (nationwide)
Note
Pick the right mask: only particulate respirators stop dust; ordinary gauze masks and disposable surgical masks don't. If the employer won't issue earplugs for noisy posts, buy your own — a few yuan a pair; lost hearing doesn't come back. "Two years, save up enough, and out" doesn't work with pneumoconiosis. Silicosis can appear years after dust exposure ends, and it keeps worsening. That makes the pre-departure check all the more important (see Item 9: the three occupational health checks are arranged and paid for by the employer). The new catalogue also added two categories. One is occupational musculoskeletal diseases — carpal tunnel syndrome, limited to manufacturing workers who repetitively use their wrists or exert force for long periods. The other is occupational mental and behavioral disorders — post-traumatic stress disorder, limited to police officers, medical and health workers, firefighting and rescue personnel, and other emergency responders deployed in emergency incidents. For on-the-spot handling of chemical splashes, see Section 13, Item 21.
Sources (3 references)
National Health Commission, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, National Disease Control and Prevention Administration, and All-China Federation of Trade Unions (2024). Classification and Catalogue of Occupational Diseases (effective August 1, 2025). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202412/content_6992843…; for the new catalogue's count of 12 categories and 135 kinds, see National Health Commission (2024). New Catalogue Adjusts Occupational Diseases to 12 Categories and 135 Kinds. https://www.gov.cn/lianbo/bumen/202412/content_6992838.htm; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Law on the Prevention and Control of Occupational Diseases (Article 39). https://www.beijing.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengcefagui/qtwj/201711… (republished by the Beijing Municipal People's Government)
11

Injured at work or hit on your commute: the first step is a work-injury determination — if the employer won't file, file it yourself

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Injured on the job counts as a work injury. Hit on the commute with the main responsibility not yours also counts. But without a work-injury determination, the medical bills, the wages paid through recovery, and the disability subsidy all vanish. The employer should file within 30 days. If it doesn't, you, your family, or the union can file with the social insurance administration yourself within one year.

Cost
Costs nothing but a trip to the social insurance administration. Bring three things: the work-injury determination application form, proof of the labor relationship, and the medical diagnosis certificate.
Benefit
Without a work-injury determination, the medical bills, the wages paid through recovery (the suspension-of-work-with-pay period), and the disability subsidy all vanish. If the employer files more than 30 days late, the work-injury benefit costs for that stretch come out of the employer's own pocket
Note
Take the 1 year seriously; don't dawdle. But time lost for reasons not your own does not count inside it: force majeure, restricted personal freedom, the employer's fault, imperfect registration systems at the social insurance authority, or seeking arbitration or going to court to confirm the labor relationship. So if the employer stalls past the deadline, file anyway and bring evidence of its stalling. If the social insurance authority won't accept the case, or you dispute the determination, you can seek administrative reconsideration or sue directly. If the employer says it isn't a work injury, the employer carries the burden of proof. But keep your own materials too: photos from the day of the accident, coworkers' contact details, medical records, attendance records. Article 16 of the Regulations lists three situations that don't count: intentional crime, drunkenness or drug use, self-harm or suicide. Article 15 adds "deemed work injuries": sudden illness at work and on the job leading to death, or death within 48 hours despite emergency treatment.
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2010 revision). Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance (State Council Decree No. 586). Article 14 lists seven situations "to be recognized as work injuries", including "(6) traffic accidents, or urban rail transit, passenger ferry, or train accidents, on the commute for which the employee bears no primary responsibility"; Article 17: "the employer shall file the work-injury determination application with the social insurance administration of the pooling area within 30 days of the accident or of the occupational disease diagnosis"; "if the employer fails to file as required by the preceding paragraph, the injured employee, their close relatives, or the trade union may file directly with the social insurance administration of the pooling area where the employer is located within 1 year"; "where the employer fails to submit the work-injury determination application within the time limit in the first paragraph of this Article, the costs of work-injury benefits and the like arising during that period are borne by that employer"; Article 19: "where the employee or their close relatives hold it a work injury and the employer does not, the employer bears the burden of proof"; Article 20: "the work-injury determination shall be made within 60 days of accepting the application"; Article 55: against "a decision not to accept the work-injury determination application" or "the work-injury determination conclusion", one "may seek administrative reconsideration according to law, or bring an administrative lawsuit before the people's court". https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm; Supreme People's Court (2014). Provisions on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Administrative Cases Involving Work-Related Injury Insurance (Fa Shi [2014] No. 9), Article 7: "where the application deadline is exceeded for reasons not the employee's or their close relatives' own, the lost time does not count within the application period"; the listed situations are "(1) force majeure; (2) restricted personal freedom; (3) the employer's fault; (4) imperfect registration systems at the social insurance administration; (5) the party seeking arbitration or civil litigation over whether a labor relationship exists". https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/6775.html
12

Don't believe 'it only counts if you make it to your desk': if you suddenly feel unwell, call 120 first — don't rush to clock in

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Rushing to the office while acutely ill earns you no extra money. Deemed work-injury status requires falling ill during working hours and at the work post — falling ill on the way, before reaching the post, was never covered. And treatment past 48 hours disqualifies it too. The minutes you burn trying to fit the conditions trade away your own odds of survival.

Cost
Costs nothing.
Benefit
Deemed work-injury status requires dying of sudden illness "during working hours and at the work post", or dying within 48 hours despite emergency treatment. Delaying care to fit those two conditions stakes your chance of survival, and the compensation you trade for it is not guaranteed to be paid
Note
Both conditions must hold at once: during working hours, and at the work post. Falling ill en route, before reaching the post, doesn't qualify. Falling ill on the job and then being taken home or to hospital, dying within 48 hours despite treatment, still may qualify. What counts is where you were when it struck, not where you died. Short videos frame this as "hold out until you reach the office and there's money" — exactly backwards. What changes the outcome is whether those first minutes after falling ill end at a hospital. Also, 48 hours is a hard line: rescue past 48 hours disqualifies.
Sources (1 reference)
Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, Article 15, paragraph 1, item (1): sudden illness "during working hours and at the work post" resulting in death, or death within 48 hours despite emergency treatment, is deemed a work injury; Article 14, item (6), lists as work injuries only commute accidents "involving traffic accidents, or urban rail transit, passenger ferry, or train accidents, for which the employee bears no primary responsibility"; sudden illness en route is not among them. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm
13

If your employer never paid into work-injury insurance, you still get the same benefits, paid in full by the employer at the same standard

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

No work-injury insurance on file? Your benefits are identical — only the payer changes: the employer pays in full, item for item at the same standard, missing nothing. Non-enrollment adds penalties for the employer: an order to make up the payments, a daily late fee of 0.05%, and on top a fine of 1 to 3 times the arrears. "We never bought work-injury insurance, so we can't pay you" is a lie.

Cost
Costs nothing. If the employer denies it, that means arbitration or even a lawsuit, months at minimum. The hard part is staying with it through those months.
Benefit
The Regulations state it plainly: where an employer never enrolled employees in work-injury insurance and an employee suffers a work injury, that employer pays the money under the items and standards the Regulations set. Which payments are due and how much each is are exactly the same as for insured workers; only the payer changes to the employer itself
Note
"We never bought work-injury insurance for you, so we can't compensate you" is the most common lie in these cases. Non-enrollment only adds penalties for the employer; your benefits don't shrink.
Sources (1 reference)
Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, Article 62, paragraph 2: "where an employee of an employer required to enroll in work-injury insurance under these Regulations but not enrolled suffers a work injury, that employer pays the costs under the work-injury benefit items and standards set by these Regulations." Same article, paragraph 1: an order to enroll and make up payments within a time limit, "a daily late fee of 0.05% from the day the arrears began; continued non-payment draws a fine of 1 to 3 times the amount owed". https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm
14

Once your condition stabilizes, get a labor capacity assessment; the disability grade converts directly into money

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Once the injury stabilizes, get the labor capacity assessment; the grade converts directly into money. The one-time disability subsidy is computed on your own wage: grade 5, 18 months; grade 6, 16 months; grade 7, 13 months; grade 8, 11 months; grade 9, 9 months; grade 10, 7 months. Don't sign any "one-time final settlement" agreement before the assessment result is out.

Cost
Costs nothing. One pass through the labor capacity assessment process, with some waiting on either end.
Benefit
The one-time disability subsidy converts the disability grade into months of your own wage, paid in one lump sum. Grade 5, 18 months; grade 6, 16 months; grade 7, 13 months of your own wage. Grade 8, 11 months; grade 9, 9 months; grade 10, 7 months of your own wage
Note
Grades 5 and 6 keep the labor relationship — you remain this employer's employee and draw a monthly disability allowance. For grades 7 to 10, when the contract expires or you propose to end it, two more payments apply: the one-time work-injury medical subsidy from the fund and the one-time disability employment subsidy from the employer, in amounts the province sets. Don't sign a "one-time final settlement" agreement before the assessment result is out.
Sources (1 reference)
Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, Article 21: "where disability remains and labor capacity is affected after the injury has relatively stabilized with treatment, a labor capacity assessment shall be conducted"; Article 22: "labor dysfunction is graded on ten disability levels, the heaviest being grade 1 and the lightest grade 10"; Article 36, grade 5 and 6 benefits (one-time disability subsidy of 18/16 months' own wage; monthly disability allowance of 70%/60% of own wage); Article 37, grades 7 to 10 benefits (13/11/9/7 months' own wage). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm
15

Keep straight the three payments for a death at work: the funeral allowance, the dependent-relatives pension, and the one-time death-at-work benefit

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A death at work means three payments; don't negotiate only one of them. The funeral allowance is 6 months of the local previous-year average monthly employee wage. The dependent-relatives pension is paid monthly on the deceased's own wage: 40% a month for a spouse, 30% for each other relative. The one-time death-at-work benefit is 20 times the previous year's national per-capita disposable income of urban residents — one figure for the whole country.

Cost
Costs nothing but one set of paperwork.
Benefit
Death at work pays three sums. First, the funeral allowance: 6 months of the previous-year average monthly employee wage in the enrollment (pooling) area. Second, the dependent-relatives pension, paid monthly on the deceased's own wage: 40% a month for a spouse, 30% for each other relative. Third, the one-time death-at-work benefit: 20 times the previous year's national per-capita disposable income of urban residents — one national figure, no regional variation. For a death at work in 2026, this payment is about 1.13 million yuan (1,130,040 yuan). The arithmetic: the previous year's national per-capita disposable income of urban residents, 56,502 yuan, times 20.
Note
The one-time death-at-work benefit is nationally uniform, updated each year with the National Bureau of Statistics' published data. In settlement talks, don't accept "our local standard is lower here".
Sources (2 references)
Regulations on Work-Related Injury Insurance, Article 39: "(1) The funeral allowance is 6 months of the pooling area's previous-year average monthly employee wage. (2) The dependent-relatives pension goes, at a set proportion of the employee's own wage, to relatives who depended mainly on the deceased employee and cannot work. The standards: 40% monthly for a spouse, 30% monthly for each other relative, with an extra 10% monthly for each elderly widower or widow or orphan on top of these standards... (3) The one-time death-at-work benefit is 20 times the previous year's national per-capita disposable income of urban residents." https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm; National Bureau of Statistics (2026). Residents' Income and Consumption Expenditure in 2025. https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfbhjd/202601/t20260119_196232…
16

If you're long bullied, insulted, or obstructed at work, don't tough it out: document everything first, then complain, call the police, or seek arbitration depending on the nature of it

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

People bullied at work run about 60% higher risks of heart disease and stroke later, and the more bullying, the higher the risk. Bullied people are about twice as likely to develop suicidal thoughts within a few years. Being berated and ground down is not something to simply endure.

Cost
Costs nothing, but takes time to document: dates, who was present, the other side's exact words; keep original screenshots and emails. Arbitration or a lawsuit takes months. Changing jobs costs the most; whether to go is your own arithmetic.
Benefit
On health: three Swedish and Danish cohorts pooled, 79,201 workers aged 18 to 65, all free of cardiovascular disease at the start, followed 12.4 years on average. 9% said they had been bullied at work in the past year. The bullied had about 59% higher risk of cardiovascular disease (coronary heart disease and cerebrovascular disease) (HR 1.59, 95% CI 1.28–1.98). Those who had faced workplace violence ran about 25% higher (HR 1.25, 1.12–1.40). For both, the more exposure, the higher the risk. A nationally random-sampled Norwegian panel followed 1,846 workers with measurements every two to three years, three waves in all. The bullied were about 2 times as likely to develop suicidal thoughts later (OR 2.05, 95% CI 1.08–3.89). The reverse did not hold: people who first had suicidal thoughts were not more likely to be bullied later. Legally, China has no statute dedicated to "workplace bullying"; you match the specific conduct to specific laws. An employer that insults, corporally punishes, beats, or unlawfully searches or detains workers faces administrative penalties, pays damages for harm done, and bears criminal liability where a crime is constituted. If the employer uses violence or threats to force you to work, you can terminate the contract immediately without prior notice and still collect economic compensation. The employer must take measures to prevent and stop sexual harassment committed through official position or hierarchical relationships. Victims can demand the harasser bear civil liability. Labor arbitration concludes within 45 days of acceptance, extendable at most 15 more days for complex cases.
Note
Why B: the health numbers come from observational tracking, not controlled experiments, and "being bullied" is self-reported. Four steps you can take first. Step one, start recording today; on recording, see Section 8, Item 41 (recording). Step two, raise it in writing through internal channels, leaving a record of having done so. Step three, if you are beaten, confined, or publicly humiliated, call the police. Step four, if you're being forced out over unpaid wages or unpaid social insurance, follow Item 7 of this section (don't sign 'voluntary resignation') and Item 8 (save evidence before leaving). For how severance is computed, see Item 4 of this section (work out your N first). Plain cold-shouldering, exclusion, and obstruction mostly match no specific statute; the realistic paths are internal complaints, reassignment, and changing jobs. Arbitration runs at most 60 days from acceptance; a first-instance lawsuit takes 6 months and up, with lawyer's fees on you. If you're at the end of your rope, call 12356 first — see Section 1, Item 25 (12356). Don't quit at the first affront; the cost of changing jobs is your own arithmetic.
Sources (6 references)
Xu T et al. (2019). Workplace bullying and workplace violence as risk factors for cardiovascular disease: a multi-cohort study. European Heart Journal. https://doi.org/10.1093/eurheartj/ehy683; Nielsen MB, Nielsen GH, Notelaers G, Einarsen S (2015). Workplace Bullying and Suicidal Ideation: A 3-Wave Longitudinal Norwegian Study. American Journal of Public Health. https://doi.org/10.2105/AJPH.2015.302855; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Labor Contract Law (Article 38, paragraph 2; Article 46; Article 88). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_711013.htm; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Article 1010). Full text republished by the Supreme People's Procuratorate https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202006/t20200602_463888.shtml; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2022 revision). Law on the Protection of Women's Rights and Interests (Article 25). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181841257210184281512…; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Law on Mediation and Arbitration of Labor Disputes (Article 43). Full text republished by the Ankang Municipal Human Resources and Social Security Bureau https://rsj.ankang.gov.cn/Content-2150407.html
17

When you leave, get a separation certificate from the employer stating your contract term, departure date, position, and years of service

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Whether you're fired, the contract expires, or you resign, the employer must hand you a separation certificate when you leave and transfer your file and social insurance within 15 days. The certificate must state the contract term, departure date, position, and years there. You need it for unemployment registration. If the employer refuses, the labor authority orders it to comply — and it must compensate you for losses it causes.

Cost
Costs nothing. Ask in person before you go, or send a written message asking — leaving a record of the request. The hard part is making the ask after relations have soured. If the employer stalls, complain or seek arbitration; a few dozen days to a few months all told.
Benefit
The Labor Contract Law requires the employer to issue a certificate upon terminating or ending the labor contract. The statute doesn't care who initiated — an expired contract not renewed, your own resignation, or dismissal are all covered. The employer must also complete the transfer of your file and social insurance relationship within 15 days. The implementation regulations require the certificate to state four things: the labor contract term, the date of termination or ending, the position, and years of service with the employer. The Unemployment Insurance Regulations require the jobless worker to take this employer-issued certificate promptly to the social insurance handling agency for unemployment registration. Unemployment benefits start from the day of registration. If the employer won't issue the written certificate, the labor administration department orders it to comply. If it causes you damage, the employer must pay. The law also provides that a new employer who hires someone still under contract with a previous employer, causing losses to that employer, bears joint liability for compensation. The separation certificate is your written proof that the contract with the previous employer has ended (nationwide)
Note
The statute does not tie issuing the certificate to the handover of work; what waits for the handover to finish is the economic compensation. If the employer stalls, send a written message and ask again. Still nothing, call 12333 or complain to the labor inspection office of the human resources and social security bureau. Complaints are free, investigated within 60 working days of filing, extendable 30 more working days for complex cases. To make the employer pay for losses, go to labor arbitration — also free, applied for within 1 year. Arbitration concludes within 45 days of acceptance, extendable at most 15 more. You must prove the losses yourself — for instance, unemployment registration delayed or a new employer's rejection because the certificate was missing. Appeal the award to the court; first-instance ordinary procedure starts at 6 months. The court's filing fee for labor disputes is 10 yuan per case; lawyer's fees sit outside the litigation costs and come from your own pocket. The four items the regulations require do not include the reason for leaving. If the certificate says "voluntary resignation for personal reasons" and that isn't the truth, object on the spot — the reasons are in Item 7 of this section (don't sign 'voluntary resignation'). For claiming unemployment benefits, see Section 7, Item 1 (unemployment insurance).
Sources (6 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2012 amendment). Labor Contract Law (Articles 50, 89, and 91). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf74d…; State Council (2008). Implementation Regulations of the Labor Contract Law (State Council Decree No. 535, Article 24). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f3cbb3c016f40927c…; State Council (1999). Unemployment Insurance Regulations (State Council Decree No. 258, Article 16). https://xzfg.moj.gov.cn/front/law/detail?LawID=517; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Law on Mediation and Arbitration of Labor Disputes (Articles 2, 27, 43, and 53). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf64f…; State Council (2004). Regulations on Labor Security Supervision (State Council Decree No. 423, Article 17). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2004/content_63042.htm; State Council (2006). Measures on the Payment of Litigation Costs (State Council Decree No. 481, Articles 6, 13, and 29). https://www.gov.cn/ziliao/flfg/2006-12/29/content_483682.htm
18

When you get severance, check the income tax first: it's tax-free up to 3 times the local average employee wage of the previous year; the excess is taxed separately, not folded into that year's salary

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A one-time payment for ending the labor contract is income-tax-free up to 3 times the local previous-year average employee wage. The excess is taxed separately, not merged with that year's salary. If the employer folded the whole sum into one month's salary and withheld tax on it, ask the employer first, then call 12366 for the tax bureau.

Cost
Costs nothing. Look up the local previous-year average employee wage, then spend a few minutes checking how the employer withheld the tax. The Individual Income Tax app shows the filing details of every income entry.
Benefit
A document from the Ministry of Finance and the State Taxation Administration provides that one-time compensation income from ending a labor relationship with an employer — including severance pay, living subsidies, and other subsidies — is exempt from individual income tax up to 3 times the local previous-year average employee wage. The part above 3 times is not merged into the year's comprehensive income; it is taxed separately on the comprehensive income rate table. On that table, the portion up to 36,000 yuan a year is taxed at 3%, the portion from 36,000 to 144,000 yuan at 10%, rising by brackets up to 45%. Example: with a local previous-year average employee wage of 100,000 yuan, 3 times is 300,000 yuan. On a 360,000-yuan severance, only the excess 60,000 yuan is taxed — 3,480 yuan. The same 360,000 yuan taxed as one lump on that table would come to 58,080 yuan. This rule has run since January 1, 2019, with no expiry date written (nationwide)
Note
In the same document, the annual one-time bonus item carries a deadline, since extended to December 31, 2027. The termination-of-labor-relationship compensation item has no written deadline and does not follow the bonus item. The document names only severance pay, living subsidies, and other subsidies; it does not separately name payment in lieu of notice or damages for unlawful termination. If you're unsure whether those two count, call 12366 and ask the local tax bureau. Which figure counts as "the local previous-year average employee wage" is likewise up to the local tax bureau. For computing the compensation itself, see Item 4 of this section (work out your N first), Item 5 (no 30 days' notice), and Item 6 (damages for unlawful termination). One-time subsidies for early retirement or internal retirement follow a different method and don't use this rule.
Sources (3 references)
Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration (2018). Notice on the Transition of Relevant Preferential Policies after the Amendment of the Individual Income Tax Law (Cai Shui [2018] No. 164, Article 5, item (1), Articles 8 and 9). https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c102416/c5202364/content.… (State Taxation Administration policy and regulations database); Ministry of Finance and State Taxation Administration (2023). Announcement on Extending the Individual Income Tax Policy for Annual One-Time Bonuses (No. 30 of 2023). https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c102416/c5211524/content.… (State Taxation Administration policy and regulations database); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018 amendment). Individual Income Tax Law (Articles 3 and 9, Individual Income Tax Rate Table 1). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf724…

20. Caring for a Newborn

13 items

Basis: infant mortality and money. This section includes only things that bear on whether your child survives or how much you have to spend — and only those where the difference is large enough and the evidence is solid. Soothing techniques and day-to-day childcare how-tos are not this book's business. For what to handle before the birth and on discharge day, see Section 27.

1

Baby sleeps on their back, on a firm surface, in your room but not your bed, with nothing soft in the crib

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Lay your baby down to sleep face up, on a firm surface. You share the same room, but not the same bed. No pillows, blankets, bumpers, stuffed animals, or head-shaping pillows in the crib. Inclined cradles and infant seats are for sitting, not for sleeping. In the United States alone, about 3,500 infants die in their sleep every year.

Cost
Costs nothing. You may need to swap in a firm mattress, a few hundred yuan. The hard part is holding your ground against older relatives and sticking with it
Benefit
About 3,500 infants die each year in the US from sleep-related causes. That includes sudden infant death syndrome, unknown causes, and accidental suffocation in bed. The American Academy of Pediatrics' safe sleep environment is "on the back; on a firm, non-inclined sleep surface; room-sharing without bed-sharing; avoiding soft bedding and overheating." Several other things also lower the risk: breastfeeding, keeping the baby away from nicotine and alcohol, timely vaccination, and using a pacifier
Note
"Nothing soft in the crib" means no pillows, blankets, bumpers, stuffed animals, or head-shaping pillows at all — not even nursing pillows, which look perfectly safe. Inclined cradles and infant seats are not places to sleep. Within this section, this one makes the biggest difference and takes the most pressure from older relatives
Sources (1 reference)
Moon RY, Carlin RF, Hand I, Task Force on Sudden Infant Death Syndrome and the Committee on Fetus and Newborn (2022). Sleep-Related Infant Deaths: Updated 2022 Recommendations for Reducing Infant Deaths in the Sleep Environment. Pediatrics, 150(1), e2022057990. https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2022-057990
2

Get the first hepatitis B vaccine dose within 24 hours of birth

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The first hepatitis B vaccine dose must be given within 24 hours of birth. About 95% of people infected with hepatitis B in infancy or early childhood go on to chronic hepatitis; those infected as adults almost always clear it on their own. So the earlier this shot, the more it protects. If the mother is hepatitis B surface antigen positive, the baby also gets hepatitis B immunoglobulin at the same time.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hepatitis B vaccine is part of the national immunization program, so it is free. It is given at the hospital on the day of birth — no extra trip
Benefit
The WHO's position: "all infants should receive the hepatitis B vaccine as soon as possible after birth (within 24 hours)." The reason: "infection in infancy and early childhood leads to chronic hepatitis in about 95% of cases." Infected as adults, the vast majority recover on their own (they get better without treatment)
Note
