If the mother's hepatitis B surface antigen is positive, the baby also needs a shot of hepatitis B immunoglobulin at birth. Get this sorted out during prenatal care — don't wait until after the delivery to ask. For the screening the mother herself needs, see Section 1
Sources (1 reference)
World Health Organization. Hepatitis B fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/hepatitis-b
3

Complete every vaccine in the national immunization program — it's free throughout; if you miss one, only the missed doses get made up

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Vaccines in the national immunization program are free the whole way through; vaccination units may not charge for them. Daycare and school enrollment both require checking the vaccination certificate, so missed doses get caught and made up. If you fall behind, only the unfinished doses are completed — you don't start over, and you can switch manufacturers midway. Eczema, hives, allergic rhinitis, and asthma are all fine to vaccinate as long as the condition is stable — and so is newborn jaundice.

Cost
Costs nothing. The law states that "vaccination units may not charge any fee for administering immunization program vaccines." You'll make several clinic trips by month of age. Keep the vaccination certificate safe; don't lose it
Benefit
At daycare and school enrollment, childcare institutions and schools must check the vaccination certificate. A child found not to have received the scheduled immunization program vaccines is reported to the vaccination unit, which then works with the guardians to get the catch-up done. So missed vaccines can't be shelved — they will be caught at enrollment. The schedule now in force is the 2026 edition. The HPV (human papillomavirus) vaccine has been added to the national immunization program. The DTaP vaccine's starting age moved from 3 months to 2 months, 5 doses in all — at 2, 4, 6, and 18 months, and again at age 6. Children of the right ages in Tibet, Qinghai, Xinjiang, and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps also get the Japanese encephalitis vaccine routinely from March 2026. Several vaccines can be given the same day: all current national immunization program vaccines may be given simultaneously per the immunization schedule or catch-up principles. Two or more injectable vaccines go in different sites, and "mixing two or more vaccines into the same syringe is strictly forbidden." If not given the same day, two or more injectable live attenuated vaccines must be at least 28 days apart. There is no required interval between inactivated vaccines, oral live attenuated vaccines, and other vaccines. For children under 18, the catch-up principle is to catch up as early as possible: "only the unfinished doses need to be completed; there is no need to restart the whole series," and you can continue the same vaccine from a different manufacturer (nationwide, 2026-edition schedule)
Note
The most common misconception is "my child has a weak constitution, let's hold off." The official position: a so-called "allergic constitution," allergies in the family, or a child's past food or drug allergies are none of them reasons not to vaccinate. Atopic dermatitis (eczema), hives, allergic rhinitis, and bronchial asthma are all fine to vaccinate when the condition is stable. Being on antihistamines, or on inhaled steroids, is also fine. Physiological newborn jaundice and breast-milk jaundice are also fine. The only true contraindications are two: a past acute severe allergic reaction to the same vaccine, or a severe allergy to a known component of it. Children with immune deficiencies, or on chemotherapy, radiotherapy, or immunosuppressants, need to be assessed one by one — explain the situation at the vaccination clinic before deciding. For the first hepatitis B dose, see item 2. Self-paid non-program vaccines charge separately for the vaccine and the administration service; that has nothing to do with the free vaccines covered here.
Sources (2 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2019). Vaccine Administration Law (Articles 48 and 49). http://ynswsjkw.yn.gov.cn/html/2019/faguiguizhangxin_0731/6… (reposted by the Yunnan Provincial Health Commission); National Disease Control and Prevention Administration & National Health Commission (2026). Q&A on the "National Immunization Program Vaccine Childhood Immunization Schedule and Instructions (2026 edition)". https://www.ndcpa.gov.cn/jbkzzx/c100013/common/content/cont…
4

For the first 6 months, breastfeed only — not even water; from 6 months, add solids and keep breastfeeding

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Start nursing within the first hour after birth. For the first 6 months, breastfeed only — not even water. From 6 months, add solids with iron-rich animal foods every day, and keep breastfeeding to age 2 or beyond. If your milk falls short or you can't nurse, use formula and don't beat yourself up. What you feed affects your child's safety far less than how they're laid down to sleep.

Cost
Costs nothing — it saves the formula money. What it costs is time; nursing takes up a good chunk of every day. The hard part is keeping it going without interruption for the first 6 months
Benefit
The WHO recommends "beginning breastfeeding within the first hour after birth." For the first 6 months, "exclusive breastfeeding — no other food or liquids of any kind, including water." Then "from 6 months of age, begin safe and adequate complementary foods while continuing breastfeeding up to 2 years or beyond." The National Health Commission's service guidelines likewise promote exclusive breastfeeding from 0 to 6 months, and require that from 6 months on, "complementary foods each day must include iron-rich animal foods"
Note
If your milk is short or your body won't allow nursing, use formula. The gap between breastfeeding and formula is far smaller than the one on safe sleep. How often to add solids: 1 to 2 times a day at 6 to 8 months, 2 to 3 times a day at 9 to 12 months. What the child eats each day should cover at least 4 of the 7 food groups. If your child has severe eczema or an egg allergy, whether to steer clear of peanuts is covered in item 12 of this section (don't avoid peanuts).
Sources (2 references)
World Health Organization. Breastfeeding. https://www.who.int/health-topics/breastfeeding; General Office of the National Health Commission (2024). Service guidelines for nutrition and feeding assessment of infants and young children (trial) (NHC General Office document [2024] No. 452). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202502/content_7002872…
5

Mix formula with water at 70 ℃ or above, let it cool before feeding, and throw out what's left

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Powdered formula is not sterile and can carry a bacterium called Cronobacter sakazakii. When newborns are infected, reported fatality rates run between 40% and 80%. When mixing, pour the hot water into the bottle first, let it cool to about 73.8 ℃, then add the powder. The formula is still above 70 ℃ at that point — hot enough to cut this bacterium to less than one hundred-thousandth of its original count. Let the bottle cool before feeding, and throw out whatever's left.

Cost
Costs nothing. Wait a few extra minutes each time for the bottle to cool. The hard part is waiting for the water temperature to come down even while the baby is crying hungry
Benefit
Powdered formula is not sterile and can carry Cronobacter sakazakii. Reported fatality in infected newborns is 40% to 80%. Experimental work shows: pour hot water into the bottle first, let it drop to about 73.8 ℃, then add the powder — in the vast majority of cases the formula stays above 70 ℃. That cuts this bacterium by more than 5 log cycles, to under one hundred-thousandth of the original count
Note
The 70 ℃ threshold comes from public-health guidance. In Beary et al.'s words: "public health guidelines for caregivers of high-risk infants recommend reconstituting powdered infant formula with water heated to at least 70 ℃ (158 ℉) to inactivate microorganisms." Premature babies, low-weight babies, and babies under 2 months are at the highest risk. Don't mix formula with water that has sat in an insulated cup all day. And don't leave a prepared bottle standing at room temperature to feed at the next meal
Sources (3 references)
Beary MA, Daly SE, Baker J, Snyder AB (2025). Assessing Hot Water Reconstitution Instructions and Labeling of Powdered Infant Formula to Ensure Cronobacter spp. Reduction. Journal of Food Protection, 88(9), 100571. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jfp.2025.100571; Sima WG, Legesse T, Girma S, et al. (2025). Emerging microbial risks: Cronobacter sakazakii in powdered infant formula for infants under six months of age in Ethiopia. BMC Microbiology, 26, 307. https://doi.org/10.1186/s12866-025-04380-y; World Health Organization & FAO (2007). Safe preparation, storage and handling of powdered infant formula: guidelines. https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/9789241595414
6

No honey before age 1

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

No honey for a child under 1. Honey water, honey stirred into solids, pastries containing honey — all of it counts. Honey can carry the bacteria that cause botulism. An adult's gut flora keeps it in check; an infant's cannot. Homemade pickles and fermented foods are the same story.

Cost
Costs nothing
Benefit
The US CDC's advice is "do not feed honey to children under 1 year of age," because "honey can contain the bacteria that cause botulism." Adult gut flora can hold down these spores (the bacteria's dormant state); an infant's cannot
Note
What can't be given includes honey water, honey-mixed solids, and pastries containing honey. By the same logic, don't give babies homemade pickles or fermented foods either
Sources (1 reference)
US CDC. Preventing Botulism. https://www.cdc.gov/botulism/prevention/index.html
7

The vitamin K shot at birth is a must

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Newborns store very little vitamin K, and without a supplement they can bleed — the late-onset kind is often bleeding in the brain. Where the shot isn't routine, 478 out of every 100,000 newborns suffer this kind of bleeding. With the shot, that is estimated to drop by more than 78%. Legitimate hospitals in China give it routinely; if you deliver at home or at an unregulated facility, ask proactively whether it was given.

Cost
0 to a few dozen yuan. This is usually already included in the hospital delivery bill — no separate payment
Benefit
Newborns store very little vitamin K. Without supplementation, vitamin K deficiency bleeding can occur; the late form often shows up as intracranial hemorrhage (bleeding in the brain). The Belgian consensus recommends "a single intramuscular dose of 1 or 2 mg of vitamin K at birth." In regions without systematic prophylaxis, the incidence of vitamin K deficiency bleeding is 478 per 100,000 — a figure from 42,000 newborns in Tashkent. The authors estimate that prophylaxis would cut the incidence by "more than 78.5%"
Note
Deliver at a legitimate hospital in China and the shot is given routinely — nothing to arrange yourself. Deliver at home or at an unregulated facility and you must go confirm it. Oral dosing works less well than the shot, and the shot here means an injection into the muscle
Sources (2 references)
Fiesack S, Smits A, Rayyan M, et al. (2021). Nutrients, 13(11), 4109. https://doi.org/10.3390/nu13114109; Tursunov D, Yoshida Y, Yrysov K, et al. (2018). Nagoya Journal of Medical Science, 80(1), 11. https://doi.org/10.18999/nagjms.80.1.11
8

A baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38 ℃ goes straight to the hospital — no watching and waiting at home

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A baby under 3 months with a temperature of 38 ℃ goes straight to the hospital. Don't observe at home, and don't give fever medicine first and wait it out. At this age, even a serious bacterial infection can show up as nothing but a fever. So "seems in decent spirits" is no reason to wait at home. For babies less than 8 days old, even the guidelines don't cover them — go immediately.

Cost
A few hundred yuan for registration plus tests
Benefit
The American Academy of Pediatrics has a dedicated guideline for well-appearing full-term infants 8 to 60 days old. It defines fever as "temperature ≥38.0 ℃" and splits the babies into three bands — 8 to 21 days, 22 to 28 days, 29 to 60 days — each with its own management pathway. Infants under 8 days old are not even within the guideline's scope, which means at that stage you should seek care immediately
Note
At this age, a serious bacterial infection can present as nothing but fever. So "seems fine" cannot serve as a reason to watch and wait at home. And don't give fever medicine yourself, then wait to see
Sources (1 reference)
Pantell RH, Roberts KB, Adams WG, et al. (2021). Evaluation and Management of Well-Appearing Febrile Infants 8 to 60 Days Old. Pediatrics, 148(2), e2021052228. https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2021-052228
9

Never shake a baby, no matter how exhausted or angry you are

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

A baby's head is big and the neck has no strength. Hard shaking bleeds the brain and the eyes, can kill the child, and can leave lifelong disability. Gentle rocking to settle a baby to sleep doesn't count; the danger is uncontrolled violent shaking. When you're about to lose it, put the baby back in the crib and walk away for a few minutes — letting them cry for a while is safer than holding and shaking.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is stopping your hands when you are exhausted and furious
Benefit
Babies have proportionally large heads and weak neck muscles. Violent shaking causes intracranial hemorrhage and retinal hemorrhage (bleeding in the brain and the eyes), and can kill or leave permanent disability. Gentle rocking to settle a baby doesn't count; the danger is losing control and shaking hard. Medicine calls these injuries from shaking or impact "abusive head trauma." It is the leading cause of death from head trauma in children under 2. In the US, from 1999 to 2014, it killed nearly 2,250 children under 5
Note
At the moment you're truly about to lose control, put the baby in the crib and walk away for a few minutes. Letting them cry for a while is much safer than shaking them in your arms. Those parenting alone, or chronically short on sleep, need this the most. For handling your own emotions, see Section 3
Sources (2 references)
Spies EL, Klevens J (2016). Fatal Abusive Head Trauma Among Children Aged <5 Years — United States, 1999–2014. MMWR 65(20):505-509. https://doi.org/10.15585/mmwr.mm6520a1; Choudhary AK et al. (2018). Consensus statement on abusive head trauma in infants and young children. Pediatric Radiology 48(8):1048-1065. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00247-018-4149-1
10

For diapers, judge by three things, not the brand: the fit, how often you change them, and whether the brand has ever failed a spot check

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

No official body has ever ranked "which brand is best." The only things you can check are two: the market-regulation authority's product-quality spot-check notices, and the regulators' investigations of specific incidents. Expensive doesn't mean safe; imported doesn't mean compliant. Buy a small pack and trial it for a week — watch for diaper rash and red marks — then stock up if it fits.

Cost
Anywhere from 200–300 to over 1,000 yuan a month, depending on the tier you buy
Benefit
No official body has published a "best brand" ranking, so this book makes no brand recommendations. The only verifiable information comes in two kinds. One is the State Administration for Market Regulation's product-quality spot-check notices. The other is regulators' investigations of specific incidents. After the June 2026 "formamide in baby diapers" issue drew attention, the State Administration for Market Regulation led a joint investigation team to verify it
Note
When the joint team was formed, officials said only that "relevant information will be released in due course." TODO (to verify: the investigation's conclusion. As of September 30, 2026, no diaper findings could be found on the SAMR website or in recent national supervision spot-check notices). How to actually buy: expensive doesn't mean safe, and imported doesn't mean compliant. Buy a small pack and trial it for a week — watch for diaper rash and red marks — then stock up if it fits. Diaper rash is mostly caused by infrequent changes and poor ventilation; its link to the brand is smaller than you'd think. For how to look up spot-check notices, see Section 5
Sources (2 references)
State Administration for Market Regulation (2026-06-22). SAMR leads a joint investigation team to verify the "formamide in baby diapers" issue: "Regarding the 'formamide in baby diapers' issue reported by the media, the State Administration for Market Regulation, the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, the National Health Commission, and the National Disease Control and Prevention Administration take it seriously, have formed a joint investigation team to verify the formamide issue in baby diapers, and will handle it in accordance with laws and regulations. Relevant information will be released in due course.". https://www.samr.gov.cn/xw/zj/art/2026/art_78c0425db7604b27…; Reposted on the Chinese government web portal. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202606/content_7072931.htm
11

For big items, go in order: borrow, buy secondhand, buy new — don't kit out everything at once

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Strollers, cribs, swaddles, and toys all get used for a short time, and secondhand ones abound. Borrow first; if you can't borrow, buy secondhand; only then buy new — that usually saves 1,000 yuan or more. Don't buy car seats or mattresses secondhand: damage from a crash is invisible to the eye. For big money like postpartum care centers and early-education classes, cool off for 24 hours before deciding.

Cost
No extra cost; the savings usually run into thousands of yuan. The hard part is resisting the urge to buy everything in one go
Benefit
Strollers, cribs, swaddles, and toys are all used briefly, and secondhand supply far outstrips demand. The only two things that can't be skimped on — and shouldn't be bought secondhand — are the car seat and the mattress. Structural damage to a car seat after a crash is invisible to the naked eye
Note
Postpartum care centers, early-education classes, and baby swimming pools — this book neither recommends nor condemns them. But they are all large optional expenses, so apply the 24-hour cooling-off period from Section 5
Sources
Author's experience; no direct references. For car-seat evidence, see Section 1; for impulse spending, see Section 5
12

If your child has severe eczema or an egg allergy, don't avoid peanuts — introduce them early under a doctor's guidance, but never feed whole peanuts

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

For infants with severe eczema or egg allergy, regularly eating peanuts from 4 to 11 months on: by age 5, only 1.9% were peanut-allergic, versus 13.7% among those who avoided peanuts completely. For children whose skin-prick test already showed a slight reaction, it was 10.6% among the eaters versus 35.3% among the avoiders. See a doctor before introducing. And never feed whole peanuts — they can block the airway.

Cost
A jar of peanut butter is a few dozen yuan. Feeding several times a week takes no extra effort. Before starting, take the child to a doctor once for an evaluation.
Benefit
The UK LEAP randomized trial. 640 infants enrolled, on the condition of severe eczema, egg allergy, or both, at 4 to 11 months of age at enrollment. Randomized into two groups — one regularly eating peanut products, one avoiding them completely — with peanut allergy rates checked at 60 months of age. Among the 530 who were skin-prick negative at enrollment, 13.7% of the avoidance group became allergic versus 1.9% of the eaters (P<0.001). Among the 98 who were weakly positive at enrollment, 35.3% in the avoidance group versus 10.6% in the eaters (P=0.004). Serious adverse events did not differ between the two groups.
Note
The only acceptable forms are thinned peanut butter or peanut powder stirred into solids — never whole peanuts. The health commission's core feeding messages are explicit: "Whole peanuts, nuts, jelly, and similar foods are easily inhaled into the windpipe and cause choking; infants and young children should avoid them." For what to do about choking, see Section 13, item 26 (someone choking and unable to speak). This applies only to high-risk children: those with severe eczema, or already allergic to eggs. See a doctor for an evaluation before introducing; don't trial it at home on your own. In the LEAP trial, every child got a skin-prick test before enrollment, and children with a test reaction larger than 4 mm were excluded from the trial and not fed peanut. The evidence for ordinary children is far weaker. In another trial of 1,162 ordinary breastfed infants, by group assignment, food allergy was 5.6% in the early-introduction group versus 7.1% in the usual-care group — not significant (P=0.32); it was significant only among the children who actually followed through (2.4% versus 7.3%). That way of slicing the data tends to inflate the effect, and the authors themselves said the group-assignment analysis failed to prove efficacy — though it did show early introduction is safe. China's official feeding documents currently take no position on whether allergenic foods should be introduced early or avoided, so this item rests on the international trial evidence. Timing matters too: LEAP started from 4 months, while in China solids begin at 6 months — see item 4 of this section (first 6 months, breast only). For when and how to start with a high-risk child, follow the doctor.
Sources (3 references)
Du Toit G, Roberts G, Sayre PH, et al. (2015). Randomized trial of peanut consumption in infants at risk for peanut allergy. New England Journal of Medicine, 372(9), 803-813. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1414850; General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Core health-education messages on infant and young child feeding. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-08/01/content_553…; Perkin MR et al. (2016). Randomized Trial of Introduction of Allergenic Foods in Breast-Fed Infants. New England Journal of Medicine, 374(18), 1733-1743. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1514210 (the EAT trial of ordinary infants, mentioned in the note)
13

Watch for jaundice warning signs in a newborn: yellow within 24 hours of birth, getting more yellow, can't be woken and won't feed, or pale stools — go to the hospital that day

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

More than 80% of newborns go a bit yellow, and most clear up on their own. Yellow within the first 24 hours of birth, or getting more yellow, sleepier than usual and hard to wake, not feeding, or body gone floppy or stiff — go to the hospital that day. Pale, whitish stools can mean biliary atresia and also need checking fast. Bilirubin that climbs too high damages the brain and can leave lifelong disability.

Cost
A few hundred yuan at most for registration plus a bilirubin test. If phototherapy is needed, it's usually about two days in the hospital. The hard part is making the trip even when the baby looks fine
Benefit
The American Academy of Pediatrics' 2022 guideline says "more than 80% of newborns will have some degree of jaundice." Bilirubin that climbs too high causes acute bilirubin encephalopathy and kernicterus. The guideline calls kernicterus "permanent, disabling neurologic disease." Its signs include dyskinetic cerebral palsy with involuntary writhing of the hands and feet, inability to look upward, poor enamel development of the baby teeth, and hearing damage. The guideline lists "jaundice appearing within the first 24 hours after birth" as a risk factor for progressing to severe jaundice. The UK's National Health Service (NHS) advice for parents comes in two tiers. The first tier means calling emergency services or going straight to the ER. This tier: the baby is jaundiced and also sleepier than usual or hard to wake, won't feed, is floppy or stiff, or has jerking movements. A baby jaundiced before 24 hours of age also counts in this tier. The second tier means getting a doctor's appointment as soon as possible. This tier: past 24 hours of age, jaundice not improving or getting worse, dark yellow or brown urine, or stools the color of pale cream. Globally, an estimated 480,000 newborns in 2010 had Rh hemolytic disease (caused by mother–baby blood type incompatibility) or extremely severe hyperbilirubinemia. Of these children, 24% died and 13% developed kernicterus. Among kernicterus survivors, more than 83% were left with one or more impairments. Pale stools can mean biliary atresia, a disease whose outlook is clearly better if the Kasai operation is done within 60 days. From 2004, Taiwan printed a stool color card into every newborn's child health handbook. The share receiving surgery within 60 days rose from 60% in 2004 to 74.3% in 2005. In another Taiwan nationwide study, after the color card's introduction, mortality among children with biliary atresia fell from 26.2% to 15.9%. These are before-and-after comparisons, not randomized trials
Note
Phototherapy (light therapy) uses special light on the baby's skin to convert bilirubin into a form the body can easily excrete. Don't substitute sunbathing at home: the American Academy of Pediatrics says sunlight is very hard to deliver both safely and without sunburn, so it does not recommend it as treatment. Don't give extra water or glucose water to flush out jaundice either — the guideline explicitly advises against that too. Judging the depth of yellow by eye cannot estimate how high the bilirubin is. The UK NICE guideline says not to rely on visual assessment alone; if in doubt, go get one measurement. Babies born before 38 weeks, those whose older siblings needed phototherapy, and those not getting enough breast milk jaundice more heavily. Follow-up follows the national basic public health service standards: within 1 week of discharge, health workers make a home visit. At 28 to 30 days after birth, a follow-up at the community health service center or township health center. Jaundice is checked both times. If the doctor scheduled a separate bilirubin recheck at discharge, go at the appointed time. If a full-term baby is still jaundiced past 14 days — past 21 days for preterm — the NICE guideline calls for a conjugated bilirubin measurement and a check of whether the stools are pale. Jaundice itself is no reason to delay vaccination — see item 3 of this section (vaccines). For newborn screening, see Section 27, item 13 (heel-prick screening).
Sources (7 references)
Kemper AR, Newman TB, Slaughter JL, et al. (2022). Clinical Practice Guideline Revision: Management of Hyperbilirubinemia in the Newborn Infant 35 or More Weeks of Gestation. Pediatrics, 150(3), e2022058859. https://doi.org/10.1542/peds.2022-058859; NHS. Jaundice in babies (reviewed 2026-03-24). https://www.nhs.uk/conditions/jaundice-newborn/; NICE (2010, revised 2023). Jaundice in newborn babies under 28 days (CG98), 1.2.6 and 1.7.1. https://www.nice.org.uk/guidance/cg98/chapter/Recommendations; Bhutani VK, Zipursky A, Blencowe H, et al. (2013). Neonatal hyperbilirubinemia and Rhesus disease of the newborn: incidence and impairment estimates for 2010 at regional and global levels. Pediatric Research, 74(Suppl 1), 86-100. https://doi.org/10.1038/pr.2013.208; Hsiao CH, Chang MH, Chen HL, et al. (2008). Universal screening for biliary atresia using an infant stool color card in Taiwan. Hepatology, 47(4), 1233-1240. https://doi.org/10.1002/hep.22182; Lee M, Chen SC, Yang HY, et al. (2016). Infant Stool Color Card Screening Helps Reduce the Hospitalization Rate and Mortality of Biliary Atresia: A 14-Year Nationwide Cohort Study in Taiwan. Medicine, 95(12), e3166. https://doi.org/10.1097/MD.0000000000003166; National Health and Family Planning Commission (2017). National Basic Public Health Service Standards (3rd edition), standards for health management of children aged 0–6. https://www.nhc.gov.cn/ewebeditor/uploadfile/2017/04/201704…

21. Going Abroad, Travel, and Safety Overseas

11 items

This section tallies money and personal freedom, and a few items also touch personal safety. Once abroad, what governs you is the law of the country you're in, not China's. There is a clear line on how far Chinese embassies and consulates can help you.

1

Before departure, check the foreign ministry's travel advisories once; anywhere marked 'do not travel' — don't go

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The foreign ministry sorts overseas safety risks into four levels; the highest is called "do not travel." From September 15, 2026, avoiding high-risk countries and regions is written into administrative regulation. When you apply for documents or clear exit control, staff will also remind you — and where necessary talk you out of going. Skim that page before departure; it takes minutes.

Cost
Costs nothing. Open the China Consular Service Network and skim it; a few minutes and you're done.
Benefit
The foreign ministry publishes overseas safety advisories openly by risk level. From low to high there are roughly four tiers: "take note of safety," "heighten safety precautions," "exercise caution when traveling," "do not travel." The new rules effective September 15, 2026 write the individual's duty into administrative regulation. The original text: "Chinese citizens shall heed overseas safety advisories and travel-destination safety risk warnings, and avoid traveling to and staying in high-risk countries or regions." The new rules also require the immigration administration (the departments handling entry-exit documents and border inspection) to remind people heading to high-risk areas when they apply for documents or clear exit inspection. That provision's original text: "Chinese citizens preparing to travel to countries or regions at the highest risk level, or where incidents seriously endangering personal safety occur at sudden high frequency, shall be dissuaded from going where necessary"
Note
Advisories change with the situation, so this book does not copy the list — check that page yourself once before you travel. As of September 7, 2026, the column still carried these "do not travel"-type advisories: Eswatini (2026-08-25), Palestine (2023-10-10), Sudan (2023-04-17). Four more: Afghanistan (2023-02-17), Syria (2023-01-04), Peru (2022-12-29), Somalia (2022-11-24). There are also dedicated advisories for northern Myanmar and for certain provinces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo. Travel agencies owe you disclosure too. Before joining a tour, you can require the operator to state the destination's risks in writing
Sources (3 references)
State Council (2026). Provisions on the Administration of Exit and Entry (State Council Decree No. 841). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173… (Article 2); State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761… (Articles 19 and 21); Department of Consular Affairs, Ministry of Foreign Affairs. Safety advisories. https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmzhw/lsbh/aqtx/
2

Save the 12308 hotline and the local embassy or consulate's consular-protection numbers in your phone, and keep a paper copy in your wallet — don't wait for trouble to look them up

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

There is one number to call when things go wrong: 12308 if you're in China, +86-10-12308 if you're abroad. Since it opened, the hotline has taken more than 3 million calls. Over the same period, the foreign ministry and missions overseas handled more than 500,000 consular-protection cases.

Cost
Costs nothing. Save two numbers and copy them out once; a few minutes.
Benefit
The foreign ministry runs a global emergency hotline for consular protection and services, staffed 24 hours a day. From inside China dial 12308. From abroad dial +86-10-12308, or +86-10-65612308. Since opening in 2014, this hotline has answered more than 3 million calls in total. Over the same period, the foreign ministry and missions overseas handled more than 500,000 consular-protection cases of all kinds
Note
The embassy or consulate in the country itself also has a consular-protection number, usually faster than the main line. Look it up by country on the China Consular Service Network before departure and save it alongside the main number. If your phone is lost or dead, the saved numbers are useless. So also copy them out by hand and put them in your wallet, or write the numbers out for a family member
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Chinese Embassy and Consulates in Myanmar (2023). Consular advisory on the current security situation in northern Myanmar. https://cs.mfa.gov.cn/zggmzhw/lsbh/aqtx/202311/t20231109_11…; State Council Information Office (2023). State Council policy briefing on consular protection and assistance. https://www.gov.cn/xinwen/2023zccfh/11/index.htm
3

Know what consular protection can and can't do: it can arrange visits, it can't get you out, and you pay your own costs

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If you're detained abroad, what the embassy or consulate can do: verify the situation with local authorities, demand you be handled fairly under the law, come see you, and observe the hearings. It cannot overturn your sentence, and it cannot take you away. Lodging, transport, and medical costs advanced by others are still yours to pay in the end. So sort out your money and insurance before going abroad — don't make "the state will bail me out" your plan.

Cost
Costs nothing. Spend a few minutes reading this line clearly.
Benefit
When you're detained, the embassy or consulate can do several things. Verify the situation with the relevant authorities of the host country and demand lawful, fair handling. The regulation's original text: "to visit or contact the person under the laws of the host country and the international treaties concluded or jointly acceded to by China and the host country, learn their relevant needs, and require the host country's relevant departments to grant that Chinese citizen humanitarian treatment and fair treatment." In plain terms: under local law and the treaties the two countries have signed, they can visit you, stay in contact, ask what you need, and demand that you be treated by humanitarian and fair standards. At trial the embassy or consulate may observe the proceedings and may demand that your litigation rights be protected. If you're injured or caught in a disaster, it can press local authorities for emergency assistance and help your family handle the aftermath. But on costs the regulation is just as clear: "Where a Chinese citizen, legal person, or unincorporated organization receives goods and services such as food, lodging, transport, or medical care provided by a third party in the course of consular protection and assistance, they shall pay the costs they themselves should bear." Whatever others front for you — lodging, transport, medical — is still yours to pay
Note
The embassy or consulate will not pay your fines, will not pay your medical bills, will not buy your plane ticket, and cannot change the host country's court conclusion. What it can give you is information on local lawyers, interpreters, medical providers, and funeral homes, plus help contacting relatives and friends and finding channels of relief. So prepare your own money and insurance before going abroad; don't make "the state will cover it" your plan
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761… (Articles 9, 10, 14, and 26)
4

Buy insurance that covers overseas medical care and medical evacuation, not just flight delay

Grade CValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Medical care abroad comes out of your own pocket. Domestic insurance basically doesn't reimburse it, and the embassy or consulate won't front the money either. What really wrecks a family isn't the clinic bill — it's hospitalization after a serious injury, plus getting the person home, which takes a charter flight or a medical escort. When buying travel insurance, look mainly at two coverage limits: overseas medical expenses, and emergency medical evacuation and repatriation.

Cost
A short-term overseas travel policy runs a few dozen to a few hundred yuan.
Benefit
Medical care abroad is on you. Domestic insurance basically doesn't reimburse it overseas. Consular protection doesn't advance the money either (see item 3 — what consular protection can and can't do; the basis is Article 26 of the regulations). What actually breaks a family isn't outpatient fees; it's hospitalization after major injury and medical transport. Moving someone from a hospital abroad back home requires a charter flight or medical escort — among the most expensive out-of-pocket items there are. The US CDC's words: emergency transport of a patient from a remote area to a high-quality hospital could otherwise cost more than $100,000. When buying insurance, check two limits first. One, the overseas medical expenses limit. Two, the emergency medical evacuation and repatriation limit — how much it pays at most to transfer you after an incident or fly you home
Note
The $100,000 figure is a floor statement, not a cost range. No official or industry statistics on public cost ranges were found, so this book doesn't give a specific range. Before buying, confirm three things. First, whether the country you're going to is within coverage. Second, whether high-risk activities like diving, skiing, or riding motorcycles are excluded. Third, whether claims settle directly between the insurer and the hospital, or you pay up front and claim reimbursement back home. Buy it even for visa-free destinations
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761… (Article 26); US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Travelers' Health: Travel Insurance: "Medical evacuation insurance covers emergency transportation from a remote area to a high-quality hospital, which could otherwise cost more than $100,000.". https://wwwnc.cdc.gov/travel/page/insurance; the rest is author's experience, no direct references
5

Treat every 'high-paying job overseas' as a scam; people tricked into online-fraud work can face exit restrictions even after returning

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

A monthly salary absurdly out of line, no questions about education or experience, no formal contract, an assembly point in a border city first, and they keep your passport for you. Take a job like that and neither you nor your passport are in your own hands. Fake documents at exit control get you stopped without clearance. And if you took part in illegal or criminal activity abroad, you can be barred from leaving for 6 months to 3 years even after returning.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is turning down, with your own hands, a job that looks great.
Benefit
The official characterization of these cases is direct. In recent years there have been people "duped into going abroad or leaving illegally under fabricated pretexts to engage in cross-border gambling, telecom and online fraud, and other illegal activities, gravely endangering people's lives and property." Meaning: tricked into going, or sneaking out on a made-up story, then put to work on gambling and telecom fraud. The new rules tighten both ends. At the exit end: "the stated grounds for applications to exit or enter, or to stay or reside, shall be true and lawful." Submit fake materials or false statements, and the immigration administration has the power to refuse to issue documents and refuse to let you exit. At the return end: "A Chinese citizen who engages in illegal or criminal activities abroad, endangering national security and interests, may be … barred from exiting for 6 months to 3 years from the date of return." The same 6-month-to-3-year bar applies to those administratively detained for obtaining documents by fraud or for illegal exit or entry
Note
The identifying features are basically fixed: pay far above the same role elsewhere, no education or experience required, no formal contract, an assembly point in a border city first, and the agent handles your visa and keeps your passport. There is already a dedicated consular advisory for northern Myanmar. Go, and your personal freedom and your passport are both out of your hands — you can't leave even if you want to
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2026). Provisions on the Administration of Exit and Entry (State Council Decree No. 841). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173… (Articles 3 and 4); Ministry of Justice, Ministry of Public Security & National Immigration Administration (2026). Answers to reporters' questions on the State Council's Provisions on the Administration of Exit and Entry. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202608/content_7077270.htm
6

Overseas cash withdrawals can't exceed 100,000 yuan a year — and that's all your cards combined

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The overseas cash-withdrawal quota isn't one per card. All the bank cards in your name (supplementary cards included) count together: 100,000 yuan per calendar year. Hit the cap, and you can't withdraw abroad for the rest of the year or the next. Only withdrawals stop — card purchases are unaffected and don't touch your annual $50,000 quota for buying foreign exchange.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before departure, estimate how much cash the trip needs; put the rest on cards. The hard part is changing the habit — when a card works, don't withdraw cash.
Benefit
The basis is the State Administration of Foreign Exchange's Notice on Regulating Large Overseas Cash Withdrawals with Bank Cards (Huifa [2017] No. 29, effective January 1, 2018). Article 1: "When an individual withdraws cash abroad with a domestic bank card, the total across the bank cards in the person's own name (supplementary cards included) may not exceed the equivalent of 100,000 yuan per calendar year. Those exceeding the annual quota will be suspended from withdrawing cash abroad with domestic bank cards for the current year and the following year." Paragraph 2 of the same article: "Individuals may not evade, or assist in evading, overseas cash-withdrawal management by borrowing another person's bank card or lending out their own." Article 2: the foreign exchange authority sends the suspension list to card-issuing banks daily, and issuing banks must, no later than 17:00 Beijing time that day, suspend anyone on the list from withdrawing cash abroad with that bank's cards. Article 3: those placed on the suspension list can take their valid ID to a branch of the foreign exchange authority to check their overseas withdrawal details. Article 4: the per-card, per-day cap for foreign-currency cards is adjusted from the equivalent of 1,000 US dollars to the equivalent of 10,000 yuan; RMB cards remain at no more than the equivalent of 10,000 yuan per card per day. Article 6: card-issuing banks, domestic RMB card clearing organizations, and individuals that violate the notice are punished under the relevant provisions of the Foreign Exchange Administration Regulations of the People's Republic of China. The foreign exchange authority's press Q&A clarified several more points. The notice doesn't affect card purchases abroad. Food, lodging, transport, and shopping on tourism, business, and study trips are current-account transactions, all payable by bank card. These purchases also don't use up the individual's annual $50,000 convenience quota for buying foreign exchange. The annual quota is computed by the foreign exchange authority from data aggregated across card-issuing financial institutions; because real-time control would slow transaction response, "the foreign exchange authority uses delayed control" (it doesn't block on the spot). Separately, statistics show 81% of domestic card cash withdrawals abroad in 2016 were below 30,000 yuan (nationwide)
Note
The quota runs by calendar year and starts accumulating fresh on January 1. Only overseas withdrawals stop; card purchases are unaffected. If you genuinely need large cash abroad, buy foreign exchange first under the Individual Foreign Exchange Administration Measures, then carry foreign banknotes out of the country. Withdrawals have two more pitfalls, spelled out on UnionPay International's "overseas ATM withdrawals" page. One: dual-branded cards, at some ATMs in some countries, can't select the UnionPay channel to withdraw. Two: some overseas ATMs display an extra fee (surcharge) on screen, collected by the local acquiring institution — "nothing to do with UnionPay." The same page also notes that "because credit-card withdrawals incur overdraft interest, cardholders are advised to use a UnionPay debit card for withdrawals abroad." For a lost, swallowed, or fraudulently charged card, see Section 14, item 5 (card stolen: report the loss and freeze it first, then call the police)
Sources (3 references)
State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2017). Notice on Regulating Large Overseas Cash Withdrawals with Bank Cards (Huifa [2017] No. 29, Articles 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7, effective January 1, 2018). https://www.safe.gov.cn/safe/2017/1230/21873.html; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2017). SAFE official answers to reporters' questions on regulating large overseas cash withdrawals with bank cards. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2017-12/31/content_5251958.htm; UnionPay International. Overseas ATM withdrawals. https://m.unionpayintl.com/wap/cn/serviceCenter/cardUsingIn…
7

Photograph your passport, visa, and ID and store a copy in the cloud; if lost, report to the police first, then apply for a travel document

Grade CValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If your passport is lost, the embassy or consulate can issue you a travel document for getting home. The precondition is proving who you are. With photos of the data page and visa pages and your entry-exit records in hand, reissuance is far faster. You also have to report to the local police first and get a report receipt — exit checks and insurance claims both accept that piece of paper. Phones tend to be lost along with passports, so don't store the photos only on your phone.

Cost
Costs nothing. Take a few photos before departure.
Benefit
With a lost passport, the embassy or consulate abroad can issue you a travel document for the trip home — but you must first prove your identity. Clear photos of the passport data page and visa pages, plus entry-exit records, make a big difference in reissuance speed. At the same time, you must report to the local police first and get a report receipt. In many countries, both exit checks and insurance claims require this document. Your way in to the embassy or consulate is the two consular-protection numbers you saved under item 2
Note
How to store: after photographing, put the copies in two different places — one in cloud storage, one sent to a family member. Also print one paper copy and keep it apart from the originals. Photograph bank cards and prescriptions for your regular medications too. Phones and passports are usually lost together, so storing only on the phone is as good as not storing. If the cloud login needs a verification code sent to the phone, losing the phone can lock you out. Before departure, test the login once on another device and confirm you can open it without that phone. Document photos are sensitive information; an encrypted storage method is safer. But with an encrypted method, forget the password and no one can open it — so the copy sent to family is not optional.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761… (Article 16); author's experience, no direct references
8

Before driving abroad, confirm the destination recognizes a Chinese license; 'international driving permits' sold online are mostly worthless paper

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The "international driving permit" arranged online doesn't hold up for mainland China. That booklet is a translation recognized mutually among the parties to the 1949 Geneva convention, and mainland China is not among the 103 contracting parties. So no matter who arranges it for you domestically, it has no legal effect. Whether you can drive on a Chinese license depends on the destination's own rules; don't drive until you've confirmed.

Cost
Costs nothing. Check the destination's rules once before departure.
Benefit
The so-called "international driving permit" (IDP) is a translation mutually recognized among states party to the 1949 Convention on Road Traffic. The convention was concluded in Geneva on September 19, 1949 and entered into force on March 26, 1952. It currently has 103 contracting parties (signatory countries and regions). Mainland China is not on that list. So China does not issue this kind of international driving permit. Any agency "arranging an international driving permit" domestically produces something with no legal effect. Whether you can drive on a Chinese license depends on the destination country or region's own rules: some accept a Chinese license plus a notarized translation, some require exchanging for a local license, and some don't recognize it at all
Note
In most countries, driving without a valid license is a criminal offense or draws a heavy penalty. And after a crash the insurer will most likely deny the claim — that's the real cost. Two ways to check: find the destination country's "notes for Chinese citizens" on the China Consular Service Network, or get a written confirmation directly from the rental company. Hong Kong, Macao, and Taiwan, and some countries, have separate arrangements
Sources (1 reference)
United Nations Treaty Collection. Convention on Road Traffic, Geneva, 19 September 1949 — status of treaties. https://treaties.un.org/pages/ViewDetailsV.aspx?src=TREATY&…
9

Before using an agency for visas, study abroad, or immigration, ask whether it's registered with the immigration administration

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

From September 15, 2026, agencies handling visas, study abroad, and immigration must register with the immigration administration. "Guaranteed pass," "guaranteed visa," "we'll do the materials for you" — these lines are themselves on the explicitly banned list. Fill in your own form wrong and at worst this application is refused. Get caught using fake materials and ruled to have committed fraud, and the stain stays in your entry-exit records for years after.

Cost
Costs nothing. Ask one extra question about whether it's registered, and keep the written materials.
Benefit
In 2018, the market-entry license for private entry-exit agencies was abolished (no approval needed to open one). Agency numbers then grew fast, and problems appeared: "unclear headcount of agencies, some agencies handling business in violation of laws and regulations, harming the lawful rights and interests of people exiting and entering" — officially, even the number of agencies couldn't be counted. From September 15, 2026, such agencies switch to registration-based management. An agency must file with the local immigration administration within 15 days of establishment; those already operating must register within 90 days of the effective date. Explicitly banned conduct has these classes. One: "publishing false information, or soliciting clients through exaggerated or misleading publicity." Two: "providing or assisting to provide false materials, or assisting others to handle visas, stay or residence documents, passports, and other exit-entry documents or procedures in violation of regulations." Three: "disclosing, selling, or illegally providing … personal privacy or personal information." Four: "organizing or assisting others in cross-border illegal or criminal activities." Overseas enterprises and organizations may not provide such intermediary services within China
Note
An agency that keeps saying "guaranteed pass," "guaranteed visa," "we'll do the materials for you" is doing what is explicitly banned in the first place. Once it's found out, the stain lands on your visa record. Problems with your own application at most mean a refusal this time. Being ruled to have committed fraud with fake materials is far heavier. Policy consultation and information lookup not done for profit don't count as intermediary services
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2026). Provisions on the Administration of Exit and Entry (State Council Decree No. 841). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173… (Articles 7, 8, 10, 12, and 13)
10

Don't issue invitation letters for strangers, and don't let anyone use your name for entry-exit procedures

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Issue an invitation letter or application materials for someone else and the content turns out false — the issuer is the one fined. Individuals fined 5,000 to 10,000 yuan, with any illicit gains confiscated along with it. Organizations fined 10,000 to 50,000, and the people who handled it fined another 5,000 to 10,000. One favor, and the bill lands on you.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is turning down a favor to someone's face.
Benefit
Whoever issues an invitation letter is responsible for whether the content is true. The original text: "Where an individual issues false invitation letters or other application materials for another person's application to exit or enter, or to stay or reside, the immigration administration imposes a fine of 5,000 yuan up to 10,000 yuan; where there are illicit gains, the illicit gains are confiscated." An organization issuing false materials is fined 10,000 yuan up to 50,000 yuan. At the same time, the directly responsible supervisors and other directly liable personnel (the leaders in charge and the people who handled it) are fined another 5,000 yuan up to 10,000 yuan
Note
This is the same class of risk as Section 8's "don't carry things for strangers": materials issued in your name, consequences landing on you. Where public employees or military personnel seek to obtain foreign nationality or overseas residence through an agency in violation of regulations, the agency must not handle it — and must report it to the supervisory authorities
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2026). Provisions on the Administration of Exit and Entry (State Council Decree No. 841). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202607/content_7077173… (Articles 3 and 11)
11

Before leaving the country, send your itinerary, lodging, and travel companions to a family member, and agree on how often you'll check in

Grade CValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If you go missing abroad, your family can turn to the embassy or consulate for help; it will tell them how to report to the local police, and once a case is filed it will press for action. The precondition: someone at home knows where you should be and when you should make contact. Send flight numbers, lodging addresses, companions' phone numbers, and an agreed contact interval to one family member — that's enough.

Cost
Costs nothing. One message before departure.
Benefit
When a Chinese citizen goes missing abroad, relatives can seek help from the diplomatic mission there. The regulation's original text: "the diplomatic mission abroad shall provide the means of reporting to the local police and other information for obtaining assistance." Once the local police file a case, the embassy or consulate will press them to handle it promptly. Whether any of this assistance can even be started depends on someone at home knowing where you were supposed to be and when you were supposed to make contact
Note
Four things written clearly are enough: flight numbers, lodging addresses, companions' names and phone numbers, and the agreed contact frequency. If you're headed somewhere with poor signal or poor public order, also spell out how long without news should trigger a police report. All of the assistance procedures above can only begin once family knows your itinerary
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2023). Regulations on Consular Protection and Assistance (State Council Decree No. 763). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6891761… (Article 13); author's experience, no direct references

22. How to Unwind: Entertainment Venues and Stress Relief

10 items

The first half covers which entertainment-venue money is wasted and where the emergency exits are; the basis is money and personal freedom. The second half covers how to decompress; the basis is energy and all-cause mortality. The numbers in the two halves are not converted against each other. Section 3 already covered what to do first when your mood sinks; this section gives more concrete methods.

1

Before entering a KTV, bar, or escape room, spot the emergency exits; if they're locked or blocked, go somewhere else

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

By regulation, entertainment venues must keep evacuation routes and emergency exits clear while open. No sealing them off, no locking them, no objects blocking the way, and no covering the signs. Internet cafés likewise may not seal doors or lock windows. Failing this is illegal, and you can report it. Rooms in the basement, only one exit, corridors piled with clutter — pick another place.

Cost
Costs nothing. Look up for 10 seconds when you walk in.
Benefit
These are the operator's statutory duties. Failing them is illegal, and you can report it. The regulation's original text: "While open for business, entertainment venues shall ensure evacuation routes and emergency exits are unobstructed; they may not seal off or lock evacuation routes and emergency exits, and may not place fences or other obstacles impeding evacuation on evacuation routes and emergency exits." The regulation also requires venues to "install clearly visible directional signs on evacuation routes and emergency exits; the signs may not be blocked or covered." Internet cafés are bound the same way: they are required that "while open for business, doors, windows, evacuation routes, and emergency exits may not be sealed off or locked," and "open-flame lighting and smoking are prohibited"
Note
Any one of the following — pick another place: rooms in the basement, only one exit, corridors piled with clutter, unlit exit signs. When these venues catch fire there is heavy smoke, narrow corridors, dense crowds — and most people have been drinking. The time left to you to escape is counted in seconds. Under the regulation, the reporting hotline should be printed on the warning signs inside the venue
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2006). Regulations on the Administration of Entertainment Venues (State Council Decree No. 458, Articles 20 and 21). http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297…; State Council (2002). Regulations on the Administration of Internet Service Business Venues (State Council Decree No. 363, Article 21). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61788.htm
2

Ask for the price list before ordering; entertainment venues must post prices — no 'play first, settle later'

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

By regulation, entertainment venues must clearly mark prices for services and goods, and must proactively show you the price list. So-called "astronomical drink bills" almost all happen where no price list was ever seen and the bill was settled afterward on a verbal quote. Ask for the list when you enter the room and photograph it. After ordering, ask for a confirmed itemized list. Dispute at checkout, call 12315 on the spot.

Cost
Costs nothing. Open your mouth and ask for the list once. The hard part is asking about prices in front of everyone — it can feel awkward.
Benefit
The regulation's original text: "In providing entertainment services and selling goods, entertainment venues shall clearly mark prices and present a price list to consumers; they may not coerce or deceive consumers into accepting services or buying goods." Violations of price laws and regulations are punished by the relevant departments under the law. The vast majority of "astronomical drink bill" disputes happen in exactly this setting: no price list was shown, and the bill was settled afterward on a verbal quote
Note
How to do it: ask for a price list when you enter the room — paper or electronic both fine — and photograph it as soon as you get it. After ordering, ask for a confirmed itemized list. "Signature cocktails" and fruit platters the server recommends: ask the price first, order second. If checkout is disputed, call 12315 right there. Don't pay first and seek redress after — once you've paid, proving your case gets much harder
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2006). Regulations on the Administration of Entertainment Venues (State Council Decree No. 458, Articles 29 and 53). http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297…
3

If anyone in the venue passes you 'something', leave at once — harboring or supplying drugs isn't 'helping a friend'

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Entertainment venues may not traffic in drugs, may not supply them, and may not let people use them on the premises; violators get 3 to 6 months of suspended operation for rectification, and in serious cases the license is revoked. Using drugs yourself brings a public-security punishment. Letting someone "use a little" in your booked room or your lodging is harboring others to take drugs — a criminal offense. Someone pulls out an unknown powder, pill, or vape pod and offers you a try — walk out on the spot.

Cost
Costs nothing. Stand up and walk out. The hard part is leaving in front of the whole table.
Benefit
The regulation explicitly bans entertainment venues from "trafficking in or providing drugs, or organizing, coercing, instigating, luring, deceiving, or harboring others to take or inject drugs." Staff likewise may not use drugs and may not provide the conditions for customers to do any of the above. Violators have illegal gains and illegal property confiscated by the public security authorities and are ordered to suspend business for rectification for 3 to 6 months. In serious cases, the entertainment business license is revoked. The regulation also requires venues to hang anti-drug, anti-gambling, and anti-prostitution warning signs in prominent positions in the lobby, boxes, and private rooms, with the reporting hotline noted
Note
The moment anyone produces an unknown powder, pill, or vape pod and asks you to "try it," leave on the spot — don't stay for the spectacle. The risk you personally carry is heavier than the venue's. Using drugs yourself is itself punishable under public security administration. And "letting a friend use some here," in your booked room or your own lodging, constitutes harboring others to take drugs — a criminal offense
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2006). Regulations on the Administration of Entertainment Venues (State Council Decree No. 458, Articles 14, 30, and 42). http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_6297…
4

Don't take candy or snacks from strangers, don't drink anything that left your sight, and don't accept a vape pod handed to you

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Today's drugs don't look like drugs. Vapes laced with synthetic cannabinoids — the "head-spinning" kind — look nearly identical to ordinary vapes, and people pass them around to try in bars, KTVs, and hotels. Tricking someone into vaping brings 10 to 15 days of detention and a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 yuan, and the person duped into vaping also gets 10 to 15 days of detention. If a drink ever left your sight, get a new one.

Cost
Costs nothing. Refuse anything handed over. If your own glass left your sight, get a new one.
Benefit
Today's drugs don't look like drugs. Synthetic cannabinoids have been controlled as an entire class since July 1, 2021 — the whole family is regulated as drugs. People blend them into vape oil to make "head-spinning" vapes. In a case reported by the Supreme People's Procuratorate, the case handlers described this oil as able to "take on various colors and various flavors through added food coloring," and "essentially identical in appearance to an ordinary vape." Sellers peddled it to friends and acquaintances in bars, KTVs, and hotels, inducing others to vape. In the report, minors made up nearly 40% of the users in that locality's vaping cases that year. Etomidate was added to the Schedule II psychotropic drugs catalog on October 1, 2023. Tricking someone into using is itself an offense: luring, instigating, deceiving, or coercing others to take or inject drugs brings 10 to 15 days of detention plus a fine of 1,000 to 5,000 yuan. Where it constitutes a crime: up to 3 years; serious circumstances 3 to 7 years; coercion 3 to 10 years; offenses against minors punished more heavily. The consequences also fall on the person duped: taking or injecting drugs brings 10 to 15 days of detention and possibly a fine of up to 3,000 yuan. Minor circumstances bring up to 5 days of detention or a fine of up to 1,000 yuan. There may also be a simultaneous order barring entry to entertainment venues for 6 months to 1 year. Those addicted are ordered into 3 years of community-based rehabilitation. Refusing community rehabilitation, or using again during it, brings 2 years of compulsory isolation rehabilitation, extendable by up to 1 more year (nationwide, Public Security Administration Punishments Law, from January 2026)
Note
Not just entertainment venues — school gates, friend gatherings, long-distance buses are the same. Whether it's candy, a drink, or a vape pod being handed over, it's all the same. Drugging is often followed by robbery, sexual assault, and extortion; there are no published official statistics on that part, so it's a judgment from experience. Replace any drink that has left your sight — far less hassle than pursuing it afterward. For what to do when someone in the venue produces an unknown powder, pill, or vape pod, see item 3 of this section. For carrying things for others, see Section 8, item 29.
Sources (5 references)
Supreme People's Procuratorate (2021). Wujiang District, Suzhou, Jiangsu: case prosecutors unmask new drugs dressed up in trendy garb. https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/zdgz/202110/t20211011_531831.shtml; National Medical Products Administration, Ministry of Public Security & National Health Commission (2023). Announcement on adjusting the catalogs of narcotic drugs and psychotropic drugs (No. 120 of 2023). https://yjj.sh.gov.cn/qtgzwj/20230911/3b612c94e35b4b63abba3… (reposted by the Shanghai Municipal Medical Products Administration; the original page at nmpa.gov.cn returned HTTP 412 from this machine); Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2025). Public Security Administration Punishments Law (2025 revision, Articles 84 and 85). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202506/t20250627_699863.shtml; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 353). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2007). Anti-Drug Law (Articles 33, 38, and 47). http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/post_2520706.html (reposted by the Guangdong Provincial People's Government)
5

For script-murder games and escape rooms, skip ones housed in residential buildings or below the second basement level

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The five departments' 2022 notice states it plainly: script-entertainment venues may not open inside residential buildings, or below the first basement level. These venues are dark, chopped into partitions, full of flammable props — and the door often takes a puzzle to open. Once a fire starts, they're much harder to escape than an ordinary shop. Check the address and floor on the reviews page before you book; non-compliant, pick another.

Cost
Costs nothing. Ask which floor it's on before you book.
Benefit
The five departments' dedicated 2022 notice is specific: "script-entertainment venues may not be located in residential buildings, below the first basement level of a building (the first basement level itself not included), and the like." The notice also requires venues to meet the work safety law and the fire protection law, to "routinely carry out fire-risk self-awareness, self-inspection, and self-correction, and improve their ability to organize evacuation and escape and to fight incipient fires in emergencies." The same notice also requires age-appropriate labels on scripts. Where the scenes are unsuitable for minors, minors may not be admitted. Outside statutory holidays, rest days, and winter and summer vacations, script-entertainment activities may not be provided to minors
Note
These venues' traits: darkness, many partitions, flammable props, and doors that often need a "puzzle" solved before they open. Once a fire starts, escaping is harder than from an ordinary shop. The reviews page shows the floor before you book, and shows whether it's a residential building. Non-compliant — just pick another
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Culture and Tourism, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Housing and Urban-Rural Development, Ministry of Emergency Management & State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Notice on strengthening the administration of script-entertainment venues. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-06/27/content_569…
6

When your mood sinks, go walk or run — the antidepressant effect size (how big the effect is) scales with intensity

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: yesBenefit: large

When your mood is low, brisk walking or jogging shows the clearest improvement. Next come yoga, strength training, and tai chi/qigong, with little separating them. The higher you set the intensity, the better the effect; strength training and yoga are the easiest to keep up. The evidence here is on the weak side; what's certain is that moving beats not moving — pick the kind you can stick with.

Cost
Costs nothing. About half an hour a session. The hard part: when your mood is worst is exactly when you least want to move, so you have to push yourself.
Benefit
This pools 218 randomized two-arm controlled trials. It covers 495 arms and 14,170 participants meeting clinical criteria for major depression. The statistics let the exercises be compared against each other (a Bayesian network meta-analysis). The comparators were usual care and placebo pills (active controls). Effect size is Hedges' g; the further negative, the more symptoms improve. Brisk walking or jogging −0.62 (95% credible interval −0.80 to −0.45, meaning the true value most likely falls in that range). Yoga −0.55 (−0.73 to −0.36). Strength training −0.49 (−0.69 to −0.29). Mixed aerobic −0.43 (−0.61 to −0.24). Tai chi or qigong −0.42 (−0.65 to −0.21). The paper says "the effects of exercise scale with the intensity prescribed": the higher the intensity, the better the effect. Strength training and yoga had the best acceptability — the easiest to keep up
Note
Contested. The authors themselves state that of the 218 studies, only 1 was clean enough not to be skewed by its design. On the standard grading, brisk walking/jogging rates only "low" confidence and the rest "very low." Exercise also can't be hidden from participants: people know they're exercising, so they feel likelier to be better, and that expectation can't be stripped out. The direction of the conclusion still holds: moving beats not moving, don't set the intensity too low, and pick what you can sustain. This expands Section 3's "when your mood sinks, move first," and cannot replace proper treatment after a diagnosis
Sources (1 reference)
Noetel M, Sanders T, Gallardo-Gómez D, et al. (2024). Effect of exercise for depression: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials. BMJ, 384, e075847. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj-2023-075847
7

When anxiety disrupts your life, a mindfulness-based stress reduction course works as well as common anti-anxiety medication

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: large

For people diagnosed with an anxiety disorder, an 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course improved symptoms almost as much as taking the anti-anxiety drug escitalopram. Nearly 80% of those on the medication had at least one adverse reaction, and some dropped out over it. About 15% of the course-takers had one; nobody dropped out. It has to be the standardized 8-week course — just any meditation app doesn't count.

Cost
Signing up for the course costs some money. It runs 8 weeks, one class a week, plus daily practice at home. The hard part is practicing every single day for 8 straight weeks.
Benefit
This was a trial at 3 urban academic medical centers in the US, testing whether the course falls short of medication (a non-inferiority randomized controlled trial). 276 adults with diagnosed anxiety disorders were randomized 1:1 into two halves. One group took the 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction course. The other took escitalopram (flexible 10 to 20 mg dosing). 208 people completed the full course. At the end, scored on the clinicians' anxiety severity rating (Clinical Global Impressions severity scale), the mindfulness group improved by 1.35 points and the medication group by 1.43. The difference between groups was −0.07 (95% CI −0.38 to 0.23, meaning the true gap most likely falls in that range; P=0.65, meaning this gap is indistinguishable from no difference). The interval's lower bound did not cross the pre-set "not meaningfully worse" line (non-inferiority margin −0.495). Side effects differed sharply: 78.6% of the medication group had at least one trial-related adverse reaction, and 10 people dropped out because of it. In the mindfulness group it was 15.4%, and nobody dropped out
Note
The trial used the standardized 8-week mindfulness-based stress reduction (MBSR) program; just any meditation app cannot be equated with it. It applies to people who already meet the diagnostic criteria for an anxiety disorder — if you should see a doctor, still see one. If worry about drug side effects has kept you from treatment, this is an option backed by evidence of comparable strength
Sources (1 reference)
Hoge EA, Bui E, Mete M, Dutton MA, Baker AW, Simon NM (2023). Mindfulness-based stress reduction vs escitalopram for the treatment of adults with anxiety disorders: a randomized clinical trial. JAMA Psychiatry, 80(1), 13-21. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2022.3679
8

To recover on the spot, spend 5 minutes on 'cyclic sighing': a two-stage inhale, then a drawn-out exhale

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Do 5 minutes of breathing practice a day for a month, and both mood improvement and the slowing of breathing beat mindfulness meditation of the same duration. Of the breathing methods, "cyclic sighing," which stretches out the exhale, worked best. The method: inhale through the nose, top it up with a small second sip of air to fill the lungs fully, then let it all out slowly through the mouth. This is one trial, with outcomes self-reported by the participants — but it costs nothing.

Cost
Costs nothing. 5 minutes a day.
Benefit
This was a randomized controlled trial done at home, comparing three 5-minute-a-day breathing exercises with mindfulness meditation of the same duration over 1 month. The three breathing methods: cyclic sighing (emphasizing a lengthened exhale), box breathing (equal inhale, hold, exhale), and cyclic hyperventilation with holds (long inhale, short exhale). Pooling the data from every person and every session (mixed-effects models), the breathing practices all beat mindfulness meditation — especially cyclic sighing, built around the exhale. It was better both on mood improvement (P<0.05, meaning this difference doesn't look like chance) and on reduced breathing rate (P<0.05)
Note
The method: inhale through the nose, add a brief second sip of air to fill the lungs fully, then let the breath out slowly and long through the mouth; repeat for 5 minutes. There is only this one trial, done at home, with outcomes self-reported on questionnaires and a modest number of participants. The effect is only slightly better than meditation — it doesn't solve your problems. But it costs nothing, takes 5 minutes, and can be done anywhere, which makes it good value
Sources (1 reference)
Balban MY, Neri E, Kogon MM, et al. (2023). Brief structured respiration practices enhance mood and reduce physiological arousal. Cell Reports Medicine, 4(1), 100895. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.xcrm.2022.100895
9

Treat regular time with people as a health expense — don't reach out only when you feel bad

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

People who rarely mix with others are about 30% more likely to die over the same period. Those who feel lonely, about a quarter more likely; those who live alone, about 30% more; the effect is clearer in people under 65. All of these come from observational follow-up — and it may also be that people in worse health are more likely to live alone.

Cost
Costs a little money, plus the time of actually meeting. The hard part is reaching out even when your mood is fine.
Benefit
This pools 70 studies that recorded people's situation first and then followed them over time (a meta-analysis): 3.4 million participants, followed 7 years on average. Social isolation, loneliness, and living alone are each associated with higher mortality. After subtracting confounders like age and health status, the weighted average odds ratios are: social isolation 1.29, loneliness 1.26, living alone 1.32.
