Converted, the probability of dying over the same period is about 30% higher, about a quarter higher, and about 30% higher respectively. The three effect sizes are similar, and all are larger in people under 65 than in older adults
Note
Contested. These are associations observed by following populations, not controlled trials with assigned groups — who causes whom can't be separated. People in worse health to begin with are more likely to live alone and socialize less. The authors treat social relationships as a health factor on the same scale as smoking and obesity, but no randomized trial has shown that "adding social contact lowers mortality." This item doesn't conflict with Section 3's "cut the relationships that drain you": that one prunes the relationships draining you; this one protects the handful that restore your energy
Sources (1 reference)
Holt-Lunstad J, Smith TB, Baker M, Harris T, Stephenson D (2015). Loneliness and social isolation as risk factors for mortality: a meta-analytic review. Perspectives on Psychological Science, 10(2), 227-237. https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691614568352
10

If you live near green space, use it — walking, strolling, or just sitting all count

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

The better the greenery within 500 meters of your home, the lower your probability of dying over the same period — about 4% lower per 0.1 increase in the vegetation index. What's measured is the greenery around your home, not how often you go to parks. In leafier areas, the residents tend to be wealthier and the air is better too. So don't read it as "going to the park extends life"; just weigh nearby green space when choosing where to live.

Cost
Costs nothing. It happens along the way.
Benefit
This pools 9 studies that followed populations for years (a meta-analysis of cohort studies), covering 7 countries and 8.32 million people. It looks at the greenness within 500 meters of home, measured with the normalized difference vegetation index (NDVI — a number that condenses how green the ground is). Per 0.1 increase in greenness, the pooled hazard ratio for all-cause mortality is 0.96 (95% CI 0.94–0.97): about 4% lower probability of dying over the same period, with the true value most likely between 3% and 6% lower. Seven of the 9 studies found lower mortality with better greenery, and the difference doesn't look like chance. The other 2 found no association
Note
Contested. The studies' results scatter widely (I²=95% — the higher this number, the less they agree with one another). And it measures the greenness around the residence, unrelated to how often you visit parks. People living in greener areas are often also wealthier, breathe better air, and exercise more, and these can't be separated from the greenery to say which is doing the work. Don't read it as "going to the park extends life"; the usable part is weighing green space when choosing where to live, at zero cost. On the NDVI scale, bare ground and concrete sit near 0, and dense vegetation near 1. So "0.1" is roughly the difference between moving from a bare block to a block lined with rows of street trees
Sources (1 reference)
Rojas-Rueda D, Nieuwenhuijsen MJ, Gascon M, Perez-Leon D, Mudu P (2019). Green spaces and mortality: a systematic review and meta-analysis of cohort studies. The Lancet Planetary Health, 3(11), e469-e477. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2542-5196(19)30215-3

23. Which Skills Are Worth Learning

23 items

This section runs the numbers on money and time; item 2 additionally runs them on mortality. The first six items answer one question: whether to keep studying. Item 1 first covers which stretch of options the law strikes out, item 2 runs the numbers on schooling and lifespan, and item 3 shows where the whole country's education levels sit. Item 4 covers what aid exists when you can't afford school, item 5 covers the roads left if you miss the cutoff for academic high school, and item 6 turns "study or work" into a problem and gives a do-it-yourself way to calculate it. The next seven items answer another question: once you've decided to learn something, how to choose. China's wage statistics broken down by occupation are hard to verify item by item through public official channels. So this section only covers things with traceable sources: roughly how much wages rise per extra year of school (also called the rate of return to education), how to verify whether a certificate is legitimate, where training subsidies come from, and which dimension to look at when picking a skill so you're less likely to be displaced. For what a specific trade earns per month, this book gives no figures. Items 14 to 19 answer a third question: once you've settled what to learn, how to learn it in a way that saves time. These six items count time only; no conversion to money. Items 20 to 23 answer a fourth question: for those already doing professional and technical work — where to apply for a professional title, how the exam works, which pitfalls to avoid, and what a title is worth. This section's items are grouped by topic below; item numbers are in parentheses. Whether to keep studying: under 16 you can't take a job (item 1), whether school pays goes into the mortality math (item 2), the national education mix (item 3), run the policy numbers when school seems unaffordable (item 4), paths if you miss academic high school (item 5), turning "study or work" into a calculation (item 6). What to learn and how to pick: the return to an extra year of education (item 7), check the occupational qualification catalog before paying for a certificate (item 8), use government-subsidized channels for training (item 9), pick skills that need hands-on work and on-the-spot judgment (item 10), check whether the skill has graded assessment (item 11), check the local shortage-occupation list (item 12), choose short-cycle programs that lead straight to a job (item 13). How to learn in less time: finish by closing the book and testing yourself (item 14), spread the time over several days (item 15), don't treat highlighting as a main method (item 16), mix question types when practicing (item 17), don't pick methods by visual/auditory type (item 18), quiz yourself on what you must memorize (item 19). Professional titles: find the application channel (item 20), junior and intermediate accounting titles go by unified exam (item 21), don't use agencies to obtain titles (item 22), a title doesn't mean a raise (item 23).

1

Under 16, 'going to work' isn't an option: an employer who hires you is fined 5,000 yuan a month — anyone willing to hire you is running illegal labor

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: freeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

People finish junior high at 15 to 16 — right on this line. Under 16, hiring you is illegal, with a 5,000 yuan fine per child worker per month. So anyone willing to take you on knows it's illegal and does it anyway. If something really happens, the medical bills and compensation can only be pursued from that employer; if it stiffs you or disappears, no one backstops it.

Cost
Free. Spend a minute working out how old you are.
Benefit
Compulsory Education Law, Article 11: 'all children who have reached the age of six shall be enrolled in school by their parents or other legal guardians to receive and complete compulsory education'. Article 14: 'employers are prohibited from hiring school-age children and adolescents who should be receiving compulsory education'. Article 58: those who, without justifiable reason, fail to send school-age children or adolescents to school as this law requires are, by the local township people's government or the education administrative department of the county-level people's government, 'given criticism and education and ordered to correct within a time limit'. Regulations on the Prohibition of Using Child Labor, Article 2: state organs, social organizations, enterprises and public institutions, private non-enterprise units, and individually owned businesses 'may not hire any minor under the age of 16'. Article 6: penalties are imposed 'at the rate of a 5,000 yuan fine per child worker per month', rising to 10,000 yuan per person per month if not corrected in time. Article 7: those who broker a child into employment are 'fined 5,000 yuan per person brokered'. Article 10: when a child worker falls ill or is injured, the employer 'shall take responsibility for sending the child to a medical institution for treatment and bear all medical and living expenses during treatment', plus a one-time compensation payment if the child is disabled or killed. Article 13 leaves a single exception: with the consent of parents or other guardians, arts and sports units may hire professional performers and athletes under 16 (nationwide)
Note
The beneficiary is you. Working after 16 is legal. But the jobs willing to take a 16-year-old with no credentials are exactly the category in item 10 of this section (picking automation-resistant skills): fixed routines, the easiest for machines to displace. The overtime pay, annual leave, and work-injury benefits covered in section 19 all presuppose a legal employment relationship and evidence. Illegal work has neither, so that money is out of reach
Sources (2 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Compulsory Education Law (second amendment, 2018, Articles 11, 14, 58). http://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_sjzl/sjzl_zcfg/zcfg_jyfl/202110/t… (published by the Ministry of Education); State Council (2002). Regulations on the Prohibition of Using Child Labor (State Council Decree No. 364, Articles 2, 6, 7, 10, 13). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2002/content_61798.htm
2

Put 'is school worth it' into the mortality math too: each additional year of education cuts adult mortality risk by about 1.9%

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: small

Each extra year of schooling goes with an adult death risk about 1.9% lower on average. The effect is clearest at ages 18 to 49 — about 2.9% lower per extra year — and only 0.8% lower past 70. People who can keep studying tend to start out better off; how much of this is schooling itself is impossible to separate.

Cost
Free. What it costs is the time and energy of those extra school years; the tuition side is covered in item 4 of this section (vocational school tuition and grants). The hard part is staying in school without dropping out midway.
Benefit
A systematic review and meta-analysis that gathered all prior studies and pooled them. The search ran from January 1980 to May 2023 and finally included 603 studies, 70 sites in 59 countries, and 10,355 observations. Education and adult mortality (deaths from all causes combined) follow a dose-response relationship (the more schooling, the lower the risk). Each additional year of education lowers mortality risk by 1.9% on average (95% uncertainty interval 1.8–2.0, meaning the true value most likely falls in that range). For ages 18 to 49, each extra year means 2.9% (2.8–3.0). Past 70, 0.8% (0.6–1.0). No visible difference between men and women. No visible difference by country development level (sociodemographic index) either
Note
Contested. The authors themselves reported publication bias (p<0.0001), meaning studies with flattering results get published more easily. Results also vary widely across studies. Everything included is observational tracking, not trials that assign people to groups. Years of schooling are tangled up with family circumstances, region, and occupation; how much of the 1.9% comes from schooling itself versus "people who can stay in school started out better off" — studies of this type can't separate. The reverse path can't be separated either: people who were sick or had mental-health problems in childhood are more likely to drop out and also more likely to die early, which makes schooling look better than it is. So the evidence strongly supports "more schooling and longer life move in the same direction", but it does not mean "go study and you'll extend your life by 1.9%". The benefit is rated small: readers are usually facing another three or four years of school, and at 1.9% a year that sums to under 10% — small by this book's thresholds. The beneficiary is you
Sources (1 reference)
IHME-CHAIN Collaborators (2024). Effects of education on adult mortality: a global systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Public Health, 9(3), e155-e165. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2468-2667(23)00306-7
3

Before judging whether degrees have depreciated, look at the national education mix: only 15,467 in every 100,000 people have a college education

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The 2020 census: nationwide, only 15,467 in every 100,000 people went as far as junior college or above — about 15%. People with junior high education number 34,507, the largest group. Those 15 and older average just 9.91 years of schooling, barely past junior high graduation. So a junior high education in China isn't "enough" — it's the most common level there is.

Cost
Free. Just look at the numbers below.
Benefit
The seventh national census has a standard reference time of November 1, 2020. Of the national population, 218,360,767 people have college education (junior college or above). Senior high (including vocational secondary school): 213,005,258. Junior high: 487,163,489. Primary school: 349,658,828. Compared with the sixth census in 2010, per 100,000 people those with college education rose from 8,930 to 15,467. Senior high rose from 14,032 to 15,088. Junior high fell from 38,788 to 34,507. Primary school fell from 26,779 to 24,767. Average years of schooling for those 15 and older rose from 9.08 to 9.91. The illiteracy rate fell from 4.08% to 2.67%
Note
These numbers only show how scarce each education level is in the population. Whether school pays off for one specific person is something to calculate yourself, using the method in item 6 of this section (how to weigh study against work). Also note: the census counts the entire national population, elderly and children included. Among young people the share reaching college is far higher than this figure, so comparing it against your own age group overstates your edge. Conversely, using it to rebut "school is useless" is fair, because the denominator is exactly the whole labor force competing with you for jobs. The beneficiary is you
Sources (1 reference)
National Bureau of Statistics; Leading Group Office of the State Council for the Seventh National Population Census (2021). Communiqué of the Seventh National Population Census (No. 6) — education of the population. https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/tjgb/rkpcgb/qgrkpcgb/202302/t20…
4

Before saying school is 'unaffordable', run the numbers on policy: vocational high school tuition is mostly free, the grant is 2,300 yuan, and student loans go up to 20,000 yuan a year

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In public secondary vocational schools, rural students, urban students in agriculture-related majors, and students from families with financial difficulties already pay no tuition. Grants for vocational and academic high schools are 2,300 yuan a year from spring 2025. In college, the grant is 3,700 yuan a year, and student loans can be borrowed up to 20,000 yuan a year. If money is short you can defer, or find another way; it rarely comes to having to drop out and work right now.

Cost
Free. Before the term starts, ask the school's student aid office once and submit your paperwork once.
Benefit
Free tuition at secondary vocational schools is policy since the fall term of 2012. The original text: 'tuition is waived for all rural (including county and town) students, urban students in agriculture-related majors, and students from families with financial difficulties, among full-time formally enrolled first-, second-, and third-year students at public secondary vocational schools (except students in related performing-arts majors)'. Student aid policies were adjusted in 2024. The national grant for undergraduate and vocational-college students rose from 3,300 yuan per student per year to 3,700 yuan. The national endeavor scholarship rose from 5,000 to 6,000 yuan. Both take effect from the fall term of 2024 (the endeavor scholarship from 2024). The national grants for secondary vocational schools and for academic high schools both rose from 2,000 yuan per student per year to 2,300 yuan, effective from the spring term of 2025. National student loans were also adjusted, from the fall term of 2024. For undergraduate and vocational-college students, 'the loan application cap per person per year rises from no more than 16,000 yuan to no more than 20,000 yuan'; for graduate students, 'from no more than 20,000 yuan to no more than 25,000 yuan'. The interest rate is the loan prime rate (LPR) of the same term and tier minus 70 basis points (0.7 percentage points lower) (nationwide)
Note
The beneficiaries are you and your children. Who exactly the tuition waivers cover and how many tiers the grants have are set by each province. Private schools are subsidized at the local public-school standard for the same kind of major, and you still pay the difference, so check your local documents before enrolling. A student loan is a loan, not a grant — you repay it after graduation. But it splits "can't pay tuition right now" from "is school worth it these years", so don't treat being short of money as the conclusion. Section 7 covered training subsidies and temporary assistance during unemployment; if your family's income has truly stopped, apply for those first
Sources (3 references)
Ministry of Finance, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2012). Opinions on Expanding the Scope of the Tuition-Free Policy for Secondary Vocational Education and Further Improving the National Grant System (Caijiao [2012] No. 376). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2013/content_2332779.htm; heads of the relevant departments of the Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, and Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2024). Q&A with reporters on adjusting student aid policies. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202410/content_6983672.htm; Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Education, People's Bank of China, National Financial Regulatory Administration (2024). Notice on Adjusting and Improving National Student Loan Policies (Caijiao [2024] No. 188). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202411/content_6984812…
5

Not getting into academic high school isn't a dead end: vocational schools offer integrated through-track admission and separate exams, and skilled-job hiring can lower its education requirements

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The 2022 Vocational Education Law states it plainly: vocational education and general education are equally important in status. Secondary vocational schools can run through-track admission with higher vocational colleges, which must also set aside enrollment quotas or hold separate exams specifically for vocational school graduates. Employers may not set hurdles against you for being a vocational school graduate. Missing the score for academic high school means switching tracks, not stopping at a junior high education.

Cost
Free. Before filing your high school entrance exam preferences, check your province's vocational education admissions platform once.
Benefit
Vocational Education Law (effective May 1, 2022), Article 3: 'vocational education is a type of education with the same important status as general education'. Article 37: secondary vocational schools 'may, in accordance with relevant state regulations, implement through-track admission and training with higher vocational school education in relevant majors'. Higher vocational schools 'may, in accordance with relevant state regulations, admit students through assessment combining cultural knowledge and vocational skills'. Education administrative departments at the provincial level and above must establish a unified vocational education admissions platform that aggregates and publishes schools, programs, and enrollment information and provides lookup and application services. Article 53: 'vocational school students enjoy equal opportunities with same-level general school students in further education, employment, career development, and other respects'. Higher vocational schools and regular higher education institutions providing vocational education 'shall set a corresponding proportion in their enrollment plans or adopt separate examination methods to specifically recruit vocational school graduates'. 'Employers may not set application, hiring, or employment conditions that obstruct vocational school graduates' equal employment and fair competition.' In public recruitment by public institutions, positions with vocational skill level requirements 'may appropriately lower their education requirements' (nationwide)
Note
The beneficiaries are you and your children. These are legally mandated channels, not guaranteed admission. Which majors through-track training covers, what share separate enrollment reserves, and which subjects the vocational college entrance exam tests are all set by each province. Before filing preferences you must check your own province's vocational admissions platform and enrollment plan for that year; don't extrapolate from another province's experience. When picking a vocational major, run it through the dimensions in item 10 of this section (picking automation-resistant skills): majors that require being on site in non-standard environments are harder to displace. Pick a school by whether it's in your province's vocational enrollment plan that year. Then verify its certificate with the three steps in item 8 (checking whether a certificate is in the catalog). Turn down any recruitment pitch promising "guaranteed job placement" or "guaranteed pass"
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2022). Vocational Education Law (2022 revision, Articles 3, 37, 53). http://www.moe.gov.cn/jyb_sjzl/sjzl_zcfg/zcfg_jyfl/202204/t… (published by the Ministry of Education)
6

Turn 'study or work' into a calculation: three years of early wages weighed against decades of annual income difference

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Lay both options out on paper and compare. Working early gets you three years of wages from low-barrier jobs — once only. Staying in school buys the extra slice you earn every year afterward, multiplied by the thirty or forty years remaining. In urban China, each extra year of schooling meant income 4.0% (1988) to 10.2% (2001) higher on average. The data is old — read it as a rough magnitude.

Cost
Free. Sit down and run the numbers once, about half an hour.
Benefit
This is an estimate for urban China, 1988 to 2001. How much income rises per extra year of schooling is called the rate of return to education. The paper's wording: 'a substantial rise from 4.0% per year of education in 1988 to 10.2% in 2001'. Most of the increase came after 1992. It reflects a growing college wage premium — the extra slice that people who reached college earn over those who didn't. This is the local Chinese magnitude available for converting "one more year of school" into an annual income difference. For the global average, see item 7 of this section (the global average return to an extra year of education)
Note
Before calculating, subtract the tuition waivers and grants from item 4 of this section (vocational tuition and grants), and fold in the mortality math from item 2 (education and mortality) as well. The data ends in 2001 and covers only urban areas — it can't be used directly as today's number. The same goes for the 9% global average in item 7 of this section. Run honestly, the conclusion varies person to person. With high tuition, a major that doesn't match available jobs, and many years of schooling, the math may genuinely not pay off — but that only shows this specific program isn't worth it, not that schooling is useless. A few more things the formula can't capture: legal education thresholds (see item 5 of this section, through-track admission and separate exams); displacement resistance (see item 10, picking automation-resistant skills); and whether you can switch industries. The beneficiary is you
Sources (1 reference)
Zhang J, Zhao Y, Park A, Song X (2005). Economic returns to schooling in urban China, 1988 to 2001. Journal of Comparative Economics, 33(4), 730-752. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jce.2005.05.008
7

Start from the baseline: each extra year of education brings an average global private return (the part landing in your own income) of about 9% a year

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

On the worldwide average, each extra year of schooling means personal income about 9% higher, and women's returns are consistently higher than men's. This number is about formal schooling; don't apply it directly to a course you sign up for. Use it as a ruler: if a course costs you 30,000 yuan and half a year, ask whether the income change it brings is worth a year of formal schooling.

Cost
Free. Memorize this number and use it as the yardstick for every "learn something" plan.
Benefit
A review covering 1950 to 2014, 139 countries, and 1,120 estimates computes: 'the global average private return to one more year of education is 9% a year'. The private return is the part landing in your own income: one more year of school, income about 9% higher on average. The private return to higher education is rising. The social return to education (the part accruing to society as a whole rather than the individual) remains high. Women's average returns to education are consistently higher than men's
Note
This is the global average for "one more year of school", not the payoff of "taking a course", and it's not a China-specific figure — only an order-of-magnitude reference. Its use is as a yardstick for every training plan: if a course costs you 30,000 yuan and half a year, ask whether it can deliver an income change equivalent to a year of formal schooling. Also note: global averages mask enormous differences across fields and countries
Sources (2 references)
Psacharopoulos G, Patrinos HA (2018). Returns to investment in education: a decennial review of the global literature. Education Economics, 26(5), 445-458. https://doi.org/10.1080/09645292.2018.1484426; World Bank Policy Research Working Paper 8402. https://doi.org/10.1596/1813-9450-8402
8

Before paying for a certificate, check it's in the national occupational qualification catalog or on the list of assessment bodies filed with the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Some organizations run sloppy courses, charge wildly, and hand out certificates under the banner of "new occupations" and "skill levels"; some even impersonate authoritative bodies — the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security has run dedicated crackdowns on this. Before signing up, check three things: is this occupation in the national occupational qualification catalog, is the issuing body an assessment organization filed with the human resources and social security authorities, and can the certificate number be found on the official platform. If it can't be found, the registration fee is money down the drain.

Cost
Free. One lookup, ten-odd minutes.
Benefit
The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security ran a nationwide rectification for this. The problems named in the document: 'some organizations and units casually hold training, assessment, and certificate-issuing activities in the name of new-occupation qualifications and vocational skill levels, charging arbitrary fees and issuing certificates indiscriminately; some organizations and units make false or exaggerated claims, or even organize training, assessment, and certificate issuance in the name of authoritative institutions'. Measures included joint enforcement with the cyberspace, public security, and market regulation authorities to 'severely crack down on fake appraisal bodies and on assessment and certificate-issuing activities by bodies impersonating those filed with human resources and social security departments'. Non-compliant promotion on websites and new media is shut down under the law. The document also calls for 'guiding the public to learn the channels and methods for verifying certificates and to judge whether a certificate is lawful, compliant, and worth anything'
Note
Verify in this order. First, is the occupation in the National Occupational Qualification Catalog — if it isn't in the catalog, it isn't a national occupational qualification. Second, is the issuing body an assessment organization filed with the human resources and social security authorities. Finally, on the official skill-talent assessment certificate lookup platform, check whether the certificate number can be found. If it can't be found, don't register, period. Certificates with words like "international", "senior", or "registered" in the name, or promising a "guaranteed pass" or "rent it out for income", carry the highest risk
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2022). Notice on Launching the Special Rectification of 'Knock-off Certificates' in the Technical and Skills Category. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-03/18/content_567…
9

For training, use government-subsidized channels first — don't jump straight into self-funded commercial courses

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

From 2025 through the end of 2027, the state plans to run subsidized training for over 30 million person-times. The money comes from multiple sources: employment subsidy funds, the unemployment insurance fund, enterprise employee education funds, and more. The scarcer the trade and the higher the training cost, the higher the subsidy. If you're employed, ask your employer first; everyone else, check your local human resources and social security bureau's subsidy catalog before deciding what to learn.

Cost
Free, or sharply discounted. The training itself takes time. The hard part is resisting the impulse to sign up and self-fund before checking the subsidy catalog first.
Benefit
The national scale is explicit: from 2025 to the end of 2027, 'carry out subsidized training for over 30 million person-times, focused on high-end and cutting-edge industries, sectors in urgent need, key employment groups, and other priorities'. Funding sources are bundled into one package: employment subsidy funds, the unemployment insurance fund, industry development funds, east-west collaboration funds, enterprise employee education funds, and more. Subsidy levels are set by how urgently an occupation (job type) is needed and by training cost, and differ across trades. Enterprises are also required to 'set aside and use employee education funds in full as required, ensuring over 60% goes to frontline employee education and training'
Note
How to claim and how much are set by each province. The entry point is the "vocational training subsidy catalog" on your local human resources and social security bureau's website, plus the public training bases. Section 7 covered vocational training subsidies during unemployment (one person can claim them at most 3 times) and social insurance subsidies. Employed people should first ask about their employer's employee education fund. Checking the subsidy catalog before choosing what to learn saves far more money than choosing first and hunting for a subsidy afterward
Sources (1 reference)
Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection of the State Council (2025). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out the Campaign for Large-Scale Vocational Skills Improvement Training. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222…
10

When picking a skill, favor ones that need hands-on work and on-the-spot judgment — those are hardest for automation to displace

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

One US estimate put about 47% of jobs at high risk of being taken over by computers; later estimates done task by task put the share far lower. Machines struggle with three things: manual dexterity, coming up with new ideas, and dealing with people. So work that requires being on site, in non-standard environments, with on-the-spot judgment is harder to displace, while fixed-routine, mostly information-processing jobs carry the highest risk.

Cost
Free. Before choosing, run the work you want to learn through this dimension.
Benefit
Each of 702 US occupations was rated for "how likely is this work to be handed to a computer" (a computerisability probability assessment); about 47% of employment fell in the high-risk band. What decides the risk in the model are three bottlenecks machines can't yet get past, which the authors call "engineering bottlenecks". First, perception and manipulation, including finger dexterity, hand dexterity, and working in cramped spaces and awkward postures. Second, creative intelligence (the ability to come up with new things). Third, social intelligence (the ability to deal with people). So work in non-standard environments that takes manual skill and on-the-spot judgment has consistently lower displacement probability — not an accident of a few occupations. Fixed-routine, information-processing-centered jobs carry the highest risk
Note
Contested. This began as a 2013 working paper that was never formally published, and it scored whole occupations for whether machines could take them over. Later research broke the estimate down to individual tasks and got much lower high-risk shares. It also doesn't say in which year this happens. When using it, don't fixate on the 47% figure; look at the three bottlenecks it identifies. On-site installation, repair, and care work resist displacement better than pure clerical work — that's why. So when "learning a skill", favor the kind that requires being on site and facing non-standard environments
Sources (1 reference)
Frey CB, Osborne MA (2017). The future of employment: how susceptible are jobs to computerisation? Technological Forecasting and Social Change, 114, 254-280. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.techfore.2016.08.019
11

Before learning, confirm the skill has a graded assessment and whether the grade can be turned into money

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The state is rolling out the "new eight-level worker" system, requiring companies to tie post wages to skill levels, and standout workers can be certified at a level directly, regardless of years of service or seniority. This is the policy direction; practice varies widely by region and employer. Only skills with a national occupational standard and a grading ladder can later offer level-based raises — check before you learn.

Cost
Free. One lookup is enough.
Benefit
The state is rolling out the "new eight-level worker" vocational skill grading system. The document explicitly requires linking grades to pay, in the words 'strengthen the skill-oriented pay distribution system... guide enterprises to adopt pay schemes that tie post wages to both post value and skill level'. Localities must 'increase the intensity and frequency of evaluation and appointment at senior-worker level and above'. Eligible enterprises can run skill-level assessments for their own workers. For standout workers, they 'may set aside conditions such as years of service, grade, and seniority, and directly certify the corresponding vocational skill level'
Note
This is a policy direction, not wages already delivered; how far it's implemented varies greatly by region and employer. The actionable part: when choosing a skill, check whether it has a corresponding national occupational standard and a grading ladder — only skills with a ladder can later offer level-based raises. A "skill" with no grading and no industry entry barrier leaves you to hustle for work on your own after finishing
Sources (2 references)
Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection of the State Council (2025). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out the Campaign for Large-Scale Vocational Skills Improvement Training. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222…; Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2021). Implementation Plan for the 'Skills China Action'. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/06/content_562…
12

Don't take 'they say it pays well online' as proof of demand — check the local shortage-occupation list and subsidy catalog

Grade CValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

How large a training subsidy each locality offers for a trade is set by how urgently it's needed and training costs, so subsidy levels reveal whether the trade is short of hands locally. "This trade makes X a month" claims online are mostly job-board asking prices or personal anecdotes. What you see is mostly the people who made money, and it never counts hours, commuting, occupational illness, or slow and busy seasons.

Cost
Free. Look up two local documents.
Benefit
Subsidy levels are themselves the official pricing of "which trades are short of people". The policy requires 'improving the differentiated subsidy mechanism determined by how urgently an occupation (job type) is needed, training costs, and other factors', and localities use it to set the scope of their subsidized vocational training programs. So how much subsidy levels for the same trade differ between cities directly reflects how scarce it is locally
Note
Official wage statistics by occupation only go down to five broad job classes, not specific trades. The National Bureau of Statistics' 2025 figures: average annual wage at above-designated-size enterprises was about 106,000 yuan (exactly 106,080 yuan). Middle-level and above managers about 210,000 yuan (exactly 210,016 yuan), professional and technical staff about 155,000 yuan (exactly 155,491 yuan), clerical staff 94,936 yuan, production and manufacturing staff 80,739 yuan, and social production and living services staff 79,857 yuan. The Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security's "100 occupations most short of workers" ranking is available on the China Employment website; the latest edition stops at the fourth quarter of 2022, compiled from recruitment and job-seeking data of public employment service agencies in 102 cities nationwide. The "this trade makes X a month" claims circulating online almost all come from job-board asking prices or personal anecdotes. What reaches you is mostly the people who made money, and none of it counts hours, commuting, occupational illness, or slow and busy seasons. For real demand, check the subsidy catalog on your local human resources and social security bureau's website, then the job-demand rankings of the public employment service agencies. Finally, go to actual worksites, factories, and shops and ask the people working there
Sources (3 references)
Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection of the State Council (2025). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out the Campaign for Large-Scale Vocational Skills Improvement Training. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222…; National Bureau of Statistics (2026). Average annual wages of employed persons in urban units, 2025: 'the average annual wage of employed persons in above-designated-size enterprises was 106,080 yuan, of which middle-level and above managers earned 210,016 yuan, professional and technical personnel 155,491 yuan, clerical and related personnel 94,936 yuan, social production and living services personnel 79,857 yuan, and production, manufacturing and related personnel 80,739 yuan'. https://www.stats.gov.cn/sj/zxfb/202605/t20260515_1963707.html; Employment Training Technical Guidance Center of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2023). For the same money and time, choose short-cycle programs that lead straight to a job

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Policy encourages "quick, short, sharp" training that leads to a job fast, plus vocational colleges' micro-majors. Pick a program by one criterion: after finishing, is there a specific job you could send a resume to. Programs running a year or more that still require "gaining more experience" after completion cost far more time than the sticker price shows. Write the exit condition before starting: if by this point you still haven't found work, stop.

Cost
Short-course tuition to pay, not much money. It takes a stretch of time. The hard part is stopping at the agreed condition when you're midway through and nothing has paid off yet.
Benefit
Policy speaks the same language: supporting "private training providers in running market-oriented, high-quality vocational skills training programs and 'quick, short, sharp' vocational skills training programs that lead to employment within a short time". It also pushes vocational colleges to "focus on the knowledge and skills the job market urgently needs... and open micro-majors and vocational capability training courses"
Note
The test is one: after finishing, is there a specific job to send a resume to. Programs that run a year or more and still require "gaining more experience" after completion cost far more in reality than the sticker price. The exit condition from section 4 applies here too: write it down before you start — "stop if I've reached this point and still found no work"
Sources (1 reference)
Leading Group for Employment Promotion and Labor Protection of the State Council (2025). Guiding Opinions on Carrying Out the Campaign for Large-Scale Vocational Skills Improvement Training. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202507/content_7032222…
14

When you finish studying, close the book and test yourself first — don't go back and reread

Grade AValue: HighBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Rereading what you just read feels familiar but doesn't stick. Closing the book and testing yourself once works clearly better; classrooms that added quizzes saw medium-sized grade gains. In the ranking of ten common study methods, self-testing sits in the top tier. After finishing a section, write out the key points from memory first, then flip back and check.

Cost
Free, and total time doesn't increase. Take the time you'd have spent rereading and use it to write from memory or do problems with the book closed. The hard part: self-testing exposes on the spot what you haven't learned, and it feels worse than rereading.
Benefit
A meta-analysis of 222 independent studies and 48,478 students: classroom quizzing raises students' academic performance, with a medium effect size (g = 0.499). The effect size depends on several conditions: what method the comparison group used, whether the quiz format matched the final exam, whether the material was matched, whether corrective feedback was given, how many times the test was repeated, where and when it was administered, how long the intervention ran, and what experimental design was used. Another review that evaluated ten common learning methods one by one rated "practice testing" and "distributed practice" in the top tier (high utility), because they work for learners of different ages and abilities and have been validated across multiple assessment formats and real educational settings.
Note
Self-testing is about forcing retrieval from memory, not grading. Method: after finishing a section, close the book and write out the key points first, then flip back and check. Corrective feedback improves results, so after checking your answers, look closely at where you went wrong. The benefit is rated "large" based on the effect size and tier rankings. Both pieces of evidence measured grades, not hours saved, so the time-savings thresholds weren't applied. Self-testing and item 15 (spreading the same time over several days) are the two top-rated methods in the same review — use them together.
Sources (2 references)
Yang C, Luo L, Vadillo MA, Yu R, Shanks DR (2021). Testing (quizzing) boosts classroom learning: A systematic and meta-analytic review. Psychological Bulletin, 147(4), 399–435. https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000309; Dunlosky J, Rawson KA, Marsh EJ, Nathan MJ, Willingham DT (2013). Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 14(1), 4–58. https://doi.org/10.1177/1529100612453266
15

Spread the same study time over several days — don't cram it all into one go

Grade AValue: HighBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The same study time spread over several days beats one single session for retention. All 317 experiments on this point agree. And there's a practical rule: the longer ahead you need to remember, the longer the review gap should be. Exam tomorrow — review today. Exam in a month — go over it every few days.

Cost
Free, and total time unchanged. Only the schedule changes: the same 3 hours split into three days of 1 hour each. The hard part is starting several days ahead, not leaving it to the last night.
Benefit
A meta-analysis aggregating 184 articles, 317 experiments, and 839 assessments of distributed-practice effects. It compared two things: learning in one stretch versus in separate sessions (the spacing effect), and shorter versus longer gaps (the lag effect). The conclusion: the review gap and "how far ahead you need to remember" jointly determine retention on the final test — the longer the retention target, the longer the review gap that yields the best retention. Another review that evaluated ten common learning methods one by one rated distributed practice in the top tier (high utility).
Note
Works best stacked with item 14 (closed-book self-testing): spread the self-testing itself over several days. The materials in Cepeda's meta-analysis were mostly word-list memorization; no universal number of days is given for the optimal gap with complex material. "The farther the exam, the longer the gap" is the rule the paper gives, without a concrete schedule. A cram session the night before helps on the day — the problem is it fades fast.
Sources (2 references)
Cepeda NJ, Pashler H, Vul E, Wixted JT, Rohrer D (2006). Distributed practice in verbal recall tasks: A review and quantitative synthesis. Psychological Bulletin, 132(3), 354–380. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.132.3.354; Dunlosky J, Rawson KA, Marsh EJ, Nathan MJ, Willingham DT (2013). Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 14(1), 4–58. https://doi.org/10.1177/1529100612453266
16

Don't rely on highlighting, rereading, or summarizing as your main study methods

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Highlighting and rereading are what students use most, yet in the ranking of ten common study methods both sit in the lowest tier. Summarizing, the keyword mnemonic, and imagery for the text are also in the lowest tier. They aren't entirely useless — the conditions where they work are just too narrow, and the same time spent on self-testing buys more.

Cost
Free — it actually saves time. The hard part is that these are the easiest to do and give the strongest sense of "I'm studying".
Benefit
A review of ten common learning methods rated them on whether 'the effects generalize across learning conditions, student characteristics, materials, and assessment formats'. Top tier: practice testing and distributed practice. Middle tier: elaborative interrogation, self-explanation, interleaved practice. Bottom tier, five methods: summarization, highlighting (or underlining), the keyword mnemonic, imagery for the text, and rereading. The review states: most students report rereading and highlighting, but these two do not reliably raise grades and should be replaced with other methods — for instance, substituting practice testing for rereading.
Note
Underlining is fine for "marking which parts to self-test later"; the problem is treating the underlining itself as studying. The review also notes the lowest tier doesn't mean zero — the conditions where they work are narrow, and more research is needed. Replacements: item 14 (closed-book self-testing) and item 15 (spreading the same time over several days).
Sources (1 reference)
Dunlosky J, Rawson KA, Marsh EJ, Nathan MJ, Willingham DT (2013). Improving Students' Learning With Effective Learning Techniques: Promising Directions From Cognitive and Educational Psychology. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 14(1), 4–58. https://doi.org/10.1177/1529100612453266
17

Mix question types as you practice — don't grind twenty of the same kind in a row

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Doing a long run of one problem type goes smoothly on the spot, but afterward you may not be able to tell which method to use. Shuffling several types together works better long term — a medium-sized effect. But the trick is picky about material: it works best for pictures and classification, smaller for math, and for vocabulary, blocked practice is actually better.

Cost
Free. Change the workbook from type-by-type order to shuffled order. The hard part: mixing types lowers your in-the-moment accuracy, which feels like regression.
Benefit
A multilevel meta-analysis of 59 studies, 238 effect sizes, and 158 samples. The overall effect of interleaved versus blocked practice is medium (Hedges' g = 0.42). By material: paintings are best (g = 0.67), other visual materials also good; math tasks show smaller effects (g = 0.34); expository texts and taste materials show no significant overall effect; for vocabulary, blocked practice is actually better (g = −0.39). Regression analysis shows: the more similar the categories, the less similar items within a category, and the more complex the material, the bigger interleaving's advantage.
Note
The review cited in item 16 (don't rely on highlighting as a main method) rated interleaved practice middle tier because the research base was still thin at the time. Putting the two together, the use case is: material that requires "recognizing which type this is and which method applies" — practice interleaved, like math problem types, clinical cases, applying legal provisions; material that requires rote memorization — practice in blocks, like vocabulary and term definitions.
Sources (1 reference)
Brunmair M, Richter T (2019). Similarity matters: A meta-analysis of interleaved learning and its moderators. Psychological Bulletin, 145(11), 1029–1052. https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000209
18

Don't pick study methods based on 'I'm a visual learner, he's an auditory one'

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Many believe everyone has their own learning style — visual, auditory — and that teaching to the style is what makes learning work. Rigorous tests of this are rare; almost none support it, and a few found results in exactly the opposite direction. People do have preferences, but there's no evidence that teaching to them improves learning — so don't pay for a style assessment.

Cost
Free. Simply stop choosing materials and courses by this classification, and stop paying for style assessments.
Benefit
A review commissioned to assess the learning-styles evidence points out: to prove "teaching to learning styles" works, students must first be grouped by style, then randomly assigned within each group to different teaching methods, and finally tested with the same instrument. The valid criterion is a specific interaction: the method most effective for one style is not the most effective for another. The review's conclusion: almost no such interaction was found; the learning-styles literature is vast, but studies using adequate experimental designs are extremely rare, and several of those found results directly opposite to the "matching hypothesis". The authors conclude the existing evidence is insufficient to support using learning-style assessments in educational practice.
Note
The review also notes this doesn't mean every version of learning-styles theory has been tested and refuted — many were never tested at all. What to avoid: paying for style assessments, and picking training courses by style. The standards for picking training are in item 9 (use government-subsidized channels first) and item 13 (choose short-cycle programs that lead straight to a job).
Sources (1 reference)
Pashler H, McDaniel M, Rohrer D, Bjork R (2008). Learning Styles: Concepts and Evidence. Psychological Science in the Public Interest, 9(3), 105–119. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1539-6053.2009.01038.x
19

For what you must memorize, test yourself with questions shaped like future use — don't just recite it once verbatim and call it done

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Closed-book self-testing pays off beyond the exact items you memorized. Across 192 comparisons and over 10,000 people pooled, it also works for questions with changed formats and for applied and reasoning problems — a small-to-medium effect. But two cases almost never transfer: swapping the question and answer around, and material seen only in the book, never tested.

Cost
Free, and barely any extra time. Only the practice changes: swap "recite it verbatim once" for "quiz yourself in the form it will be used". The hard part is thinking through how you'll actually use this material.
Benefit
A meta-analysis pooling over 40 years of research: 67 published and unpublished articles, 122 experiments, 192 transfer effect sizes, 10,382 people in total. Compared with a "study it again but don't test" control, learning from practice testing does transfer to other contexts, effect size d = 0.40 (95% CI 0.31 to 0.50). The strongest transfer cases: testing with a changed question format, applied and reasoning problems, medical-diagnosis-type questions, and cue words with similar meaning. The weakest: swapping stimulus and response, material seen during initial learning but never tested, and worked-example problems. Among moderators, whether the response format matched between practice and test, whether retrieval practice with detailed feedback was done, and whether the initial test was answered correctly all strongly influence whether positive transfer appears. The authors also corrected for publication bias two ways: the moderator effect sizes were barely affected, but the intercept estimate was clearly pushed down — when none of the conditions above hold, positive transfer often doesn't appear
Note
"Memorizing" usually blends two different things: going over the material again (rereading, highlighting) and actively recalling with the book closed. The first kind ranks lowest in the review that ranked ten methods; for the ranking itself see item 16 (don't rely on highlighting, rereading, or summarizing as main methods). What to do is the second: active closed-book recall — specifics in item 14 (closed-book self-testing) — and spread over several days, see item 15 (spread over days). The method: first work out how it will be used — picking it out on an exam paper, or judging it on the spot — then quiz yourself in that form. Testing in the swapped direction is also worth doing: this meta-analysis found transfer weakest in the swapped direction, so both directions need practice.
Sources (1 reference)
Pan SC, Rickard TC (2018). Transfer of test-enhanced learning: meta-analytic review and synthesis. Psychological Bulletin, 144(7), 710-756. https://doi.org/10.1037/bul0000151
20

Before applying for a professional title, work out which series and which level you fall under, then find the application channel matching your employer's type

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

Nationwide, titles are organized into 27 series, each divided into junior, intermediate, and senior levels. You generally move up one level at a time. Employed people go through their employer, which reviews and publicizes the application before passing it up. In private companies, you can go to a title application service point, or apply through a talent agency or an industry association. Freelancers apply to the evaluation run by the local human resources and social security department.

Cost
Free. Look up your province's application notice for the year once, about half an hour.
Benefit
There are 27 title series nationwide, such as economics, engineering, health, and publishing. Titles have three tiers: senior, intermediate, and junior. Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Decree No. 40 applies to enterprises, public institutions, social organizations, and individual economic organizations, and to freelancers as well. Applicants generally apply level by level. Your employer must review the materials and publicize them within the unit for no fewer than 5 working days. Private-enterprise employees and freelancers can have personnel agencies and the like review, publicize, and recommend on their behalf. Localities must set up title application service points in science parks, high-tech zones, and similar places, and may also accept applications through talent agencies, industry and commerce associations, and academic societies. Eligible freelancers join the evaluation organized by the local human resources and social security department on a territorial basis. For materials that can be verified online, you may not be asked for extra paper certificates. If materials are incomplete, the evaluator must tell you everything that's missing in one go. Private-company employees generally apply where their labor relationship is based. Those posted elsewhere continuously for a full year may apply at the place of posting. Retirees cannot apply. Public-institution staff with a demerit or heavier sanction cannot apply while the disciplinary period lasts (nationwide)
Note
There's no single national list of required materials. Each series and each province issues an application notice yearly, containing the document checklist, application window, and performance criteria. So step one is finding that year's notice on your provincial human resources and social security department's website. Papers are no longer required across the board: the 2016 reform opinions require not treating publications as a hard threshold for application-oriented talent, and set no unified requirement for title foreign-language or computer exams. Skilled workers have a route too: eligible high-skill talent may take part in the engineering-series title evaluation. Civil servants cannot take part in title evaluation.

Opinions on Deepening the Reform of the Professional Title System. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5163445.htm: 'publications are not to be a restrictive condition in the evaluation of application-oriented talent' 'no unified requirement is imposed for title foreign-language and computer application ability exams' 'eligible high-skill talent may take part in the engineering-series title evaluation for professional and technical talent' 'civil servants may not take part in the professional title evaluation for professional and technical talent'
21

Junior and intermediate titles like accounting come through the national unified exam — check your education and work years before registering

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: small

In some series, junior and intermediate titles are earned by exam: pass, and you hold the title — no separate evaluation. Accounting is one: assistant accountant needs senior high school or above; accountant needs a bachelor's with 4 full years in accounting, or a junior college diploma with 5. Those who already hold certain occupational qualifications may also count directly as holding the corresponding title.

Cost
Registration fees paid at each province's standard. Exam prep takes several months of spare time.
Benefit
The 2016 reform opinions provide that for professions where junior and intermediate titles run on national unified exams, the corresponding evaluation or certification is no longer conducted. In fields where titles and occupational qualifications are closely tied, obtaining the qualification is recognized as holding the corresponding title, and can also serve as the condition for applying to the next title level up. Take accounting as the example. Assistant accountant and accountant run on the national unified exam. Senior accountant combines exam and evaluation; full senior is generally evaluation only. Registration requirements: assistant accountant — senior high school graduation or above, including vocational secondary school, vocational high school, and technical school. Accountant — a doctoral degree; or a master's degree with 1 full year in accounting; or a second bachelor's degree or graduate-program diploma with 2 full years; or a bachelor's degree with 4 full years; or a junior college diploma with 5 full years. Those with a professional master's or doctoral degree in accounting are exempt from the Financial Management subject in the accountant exam (nationwide)
Note
Whether your series is exam-based, evaluation-based, or a mix depends on that series' "Guiding Opinions on Deepening the Reform of the XX Professional Title System". These were issued series by series by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the competent industry departments, and are searchable in the policy document library on the Chinese government website. For registration dates and exam subjects, go by that year's exam announcement. Civil servants may sit the accounting exam but cannot take part in accounting title evaluation.

(2024). Notice on the Connection between Accounting Professional Degrees and Accounting Professional and Technical Qualifications. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202405/content_6952602…

No agency-obtained titles, no ghostwritten papers, no faked materials: if confirmed, the title is revoked and you're flagged in the integrity records for 3 years

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Titles obtained with fake materials, ghostwritten papers, or plagiarized work are revoked once confirmed. The dishonesty record lasts 3 years and goes into the national credit platform. If the commitment letter signed at application proves untrue, no new applications for 3 years. The human resources and social security authorities also run dedicated crackdowns on agencies' false advertising, fake evaluations, and counterfeit certificates.

Cost
Free. The hard part is resisting the "pay and pass, guaranteed" ads.
Benefit
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Decree No. 40 provides that anyone who obtains a title by submitting false materials, plagiarizing others' work and academic results, or other improper means has the title revoked. It is also entered into the title evaluation integrity archive, incorporated into the national credit information sharing platform, with a record period of 3 years. The 2024 supervision measures name several applicant violations: false promises and fabricated information, paper fraud and ghostwriting, faked performance records, and pulling strings. At application you sign a personal commitment letter; if it proves untrue, you may not apply again for 3 years. The human resources and social security authorities work with public security, cyberspace, and market regulation agencies to investigate agencies' fake websites, false advertising, contract traps, fake evaluations, and counterfeit certificates. Serious cases suspected of crimes are transferred to the relevant authorities (nationwide)
Note
One way to tell real from fake: a title from proper evaluation can be found on the national title evaluation information lookup platform. Entries are the 12333 website, the 12333 mobile app, and the ministry's official website. Titles from evaluation committees that never filed for the record don't show up in this system. So anyone promising a "guaranteed pass", "no need to take part yourself", or "works even if it can't be looked up" can basically be judged suspect. The beneficiary is mainly you; the benefit is rated on "avoiding title revocation and a 3-year dishonesty record".

Interim Measures for Supervising Professional Title Evaluation. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202408/content_6969436…: Articles 5, 15, 17, 27; General Office of the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security (2022). Notice on Further Improving Professional Title Evaluation Work. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-12/24/content_573…: 'the results of title evaluation committees that have not filed for the record are not incorporated into the national title evaluation information lookup and verification system'; Xinhua News Agency (2024). Title evaluation enters peak season: how do you check the information, and what has changed? https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202410/content_6978917.htm: 'you can log in through multiple channels, including the www.12333.gov.cn website, the mobile 12333 app, the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security portal, and the "Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security" official WeChat account'
23

A title doesn't automatically mean a raise: first ask whether your employer fills posts by quota, or grants titles without necessarily appointing you to one

Grade BValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

A title is the basis for hiring, appraisal, and promotion, but winning the title and being appointed to the post are two different things. Public institutions generally evaluate within their post quotas, and with the title in hand you can mostly be appointed. Units without post management can separate evaluation from appointment: with the title, the employer still may not give you the matching post and pay. After changing employers or cities, the title may need to be re-evaluated or reconfirmed.

Cost
Free. Ask your employer's HR department once.
Benefit
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Decree No. 40, Article 2: title evaluation results are an important basis for hiring, appraisal, promotion, and related decisions for professional and technical talent. The 2016 reform opinions provide that public institutions under full post management generally conduct title evaluation within their post structure ratios. Units without post management, broadly applicable series, and emerging occupations may separate evaluation from appointment. When professional and technical talent move across regions or employers, titles are re-evaluated or confirmed according to administrative authority, except where the state provides otherwise (nationwide)
Note
The evidence is graded B because the documents only cover how evaluation links to appointment; there's no nationwide figure for "how much of a raise a title brings". The actionable part: at public institutions and state-owned enterprises, ask HR first about the unit's post vacancies and appointment rules. At private companies, ask the boss first whether the certificate counts and whether it adds pay.
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security Decree No. 40 (2019). Interim Provisions on the Administration of Professional Title Evaluation. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2019/content_5437137.htm: Articles 2, 29; General Office of the CPC Central Committee; General Office of the State Council (2016). Opinions on Deepening the Reform of the Professional Title System. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5163445.htm: 'for public institutions under full post management whose professional and technical talent's academic and technical levels are closely tied to post duties, title evaluation should generally be conducted within the post structure ratios. For units without post management, and for title series that are broadly applicable and spread across all kinds of organizations and emerging occupations, evaluation and appointment may be separated.'

24. Medical Care: How to Spend Less and Avoid Detours

12 items

Basis: money and time. This section covers how to navigate medical care itself: which hospital to go to first, how to get referred up the ladder, and where the savings come from. It also covers how the emergency-room queue works, and which assessments and certificates to pursue after a serious injury has been treated. For benefits you can claim, see Section 7. For long-term management of chronic illness, see Section 16. For what to do first at the scene of an emergency, see Section 13. This section is based mainly on the Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Diagnosis and Treatment System, issued by the General Office of the State Council in April 2026. Tiered diagnosis and treatment means deciding which level of hospital to go to first by how serious the condition is. This document ties "going to the grassroots level" directly to "saving money." But progress on the ground differs by locality; the main text states the national-level rules. For your own pooling region, go by what your local medical insurance and health authorities say. A pooling region is where your medical insurance is enrolled — usually a city.

1

For common illnesses, start at the community clinic and get referred up level by level — your inpatient deductible carries on from where it left off

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Go to the community clinic first, and let it refer you up to a big hospital for inpatient care — the money you pay upfront counts only once. Check yourself straight into a tertiary hospital and only later transfer back to a community facility to recover, and you may pay that money twice. For those transferred down from a big hospital to a community facility to continue their stay, the same illness won't be charged a fresh deductible within that episode either.

Cost
Costs nothing. You have to make one trip to the community clinic first. The hard part is resisting the urge to book a specialist appointment directly.
Benefit
For insured patients referred up level by level through primary care, the inpatient deductible at the higher-level hospital can be counted on a continuing basis. The deductible is the portion you pay yourself at each admission — only once you've paid enough does insurance start reimbursing. Counting on a continuing basis means the two hospitals together count as one deductible; you don't pay it a second time. For inpatients transferred down from a higher-level hospital back to primary care, no new deductible is set within the same illness episode.
Note
Check yourself straight into a tertiary hospital and then transfer back to primary care to recover, and that money may come out of your pocket twice; go through a proper referral and it counts once. Referral rules are set separately by each province, each city, and each medical consortium, so ask the community clinic before you go. Don't go to a big hospital just to refill prescriptions for a chronic condition in its stable phase: general outpatient services like these will be gradually phased out at big hospitals, and a community clinic can prescribe up to 12 weeks of medication at once — see Section 16, item 5 (a community clinic can prescribe up to 12 weeks of medication at once).
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Diagnosis and Treatment System. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031…: "For insured patients referred up level by level through primary-level medical institutions within a pooling region, the inpatient deductible at the higher-level hospital may be counted on a continuing basis; for inpatients transferred down from a higher-level hospital to primary-level medical institutions, no new inpatient deductible is set within the same illness episode."
2

Within the same pooling region (where your insurance is enrolled), the lower the hospital tier, the higher the reimbursement rate — a gap of about 10 percentage points

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

For the same hospital bill, the lower the hospital's tier, the more gets reimbursed. Localities are required to widen the gaps between tiers — roughly ten percentage points per step up. For example, on a 10,000-yuan hospital bill, if reimbursement falls from 80% to 70%, your out-of-pocket share goes from 2,000 yuan to 3,000 yuan. Newly added medical insurance funds also tilt toward the grassroots level.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is resisting the urge to run to a big hospital.
Benefit
The document requires localities to widen the gap in inpatient reimbursement levels across different tiers of medical institutions, in principle by about 10 percentage points per level. At that gap, each step up to a higher-tier hospital for the same bill means paying out of pocket roughly 10% more of the reimbursable amount. For example, on a 10,000-yuan reimbursable hospital bill, if the reimbursement rate falls from 80% to 70%, what you pay goes from 2,000 yuan to 3,000 yuan. The extra 1,000 yuan is one-tenth of the total bill, but 50% more than what you paid before. Actual rates differ by locality, and deductibles and annual caps change the difference too; this is only an illustration based on the document's 10 percentage points. Annual new medical insurance funds also tilt toward the grassroots level.
Note
For the same hospital bill, the gap between what you pay at a primary facility and at a tertiary hospital can run to several thousand yuan. Don't go up the ladder for an illness that can be fully handled at the primary level — not every illness needs to be seen at a community clinic.
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Diagnosis and Treatment System. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031…: "Localities should, in light of local conditions, appropriately widen the gap in inpatient reimbursement levels for insured persons across different tiers of medical institutions; in principle, within a pooling region the inpatient reimbursement rates of medical institutions are to be staggered by about 10 percentage points per level." "Where conditions permit, localities may, guided by tiered diagnosis and treatment, appropriately widen the gap in outpatient reimbursement levels for insured persons across different tiers of medical institutions."
3

To get into a big hospital, use primary-care referral or the hospital's referral center — never appointment scalpers

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Big hospitals must set aside a share of appointments and beds specifically for people referred up from primary care. Hospitals must also set up a referral center, or designate a fixed department to handle referrals, with full coverage by 2027. Failing to snag an appointment doesn't mean there's no way in. Besides costing more, a scalper's appointment may land you in the wrong department.

Cost
Costs nothing. It adds one extra referral step to handle.
Benefit
The lead hospital of a close-knit medical consortium must reserve a certain proportion of appointment slots and beds for primary-level institutions and promptly take in patients referred up through primary care. A close-knit medical consortium is a group of several hospitals and community health institutions bound together to work as one. So patients referred up from the community have their own appointments and beds, and don't squeeze in with the crowd fighting for slots in the lobby. Medical institutions must set up a referral center or designate a fixed department, with full coverage by 2027.
Note
Reserved appointment slots are set aside specifically for referred patients; if you can't get an appointment, you can go the referral route. Besides being expensive, scalpers may land you in the wrong department. If you can't find the referral center, call the hospital's service line and ask.
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Diagnosis and Treatment System. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031…: "The lead hospital must reserve a certain proportion of appointment slots and beds for primary-level medical institutions and promptly take in patients referred up through primary care." "Medical institutions must strengthen unified management of referral services, set up a referral center or designate a fixed department to handle patient referral services, and achieve full coverage by 2027."
4

Before going out of province for care, ask locally first; in principle the necessity must be assessed by an associate chief physician or above

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Whether you should go elsewhere for care is, in principle, assessed by a doctor of associate chief physician rank or above at a secondary or tertiary hospital. How much is reimbursed for a temporary out-of-town visit differs from what a same-tier hospital in your enrollment place would pay; the details follow local rules. One question asked locally before you leave beats discovering after you've arrived that nothing will be reimbursed.

Cost
Costs nothing. Ask one extra question before setting out.
Benefit
The necessity of crossing pooling regions or crossing provinces for care is, in principle, assessed by staff holding the title of associate chief physician or above at secondary or tertiary hospitals. Crossing pooling regions means stepping outside the place where your medical insurance is enrolled. Whether you go elsewhere for treatment is for a doctor senior enough to decide. The reimbursement level for people temporarily going out of province for treatment keeps a reasonable difference from that of same-tier institutions in the enrollment place. Treated for the same illness away from home, the money that comes back will be a chunk less than at home.
Note
"Temporary out-of-town treatment" and "long-term residence elsewhere" are two different filings, with different reimbursement levels. For how to file and which categories of illness allow direct settlement, see Section 16. Don't rush off elsewhere first and only then start thinking about reimbursement.
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the State Council (2026). Several Measures on Accelerating the Construction of a Tiered Diagnosis and Treatment System. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065031…: "In principle, the necessity of a patient crossing pooling regions or provinces for care is assessed by staff holding the title of associate chief physician or above at secondary or tertiary hospitals."
