"Management and services for direct settlement of cross-region medical care are to be further strengthened, with the reimbursement level for people temporarily going out of province keeping a reasonable difference from the reimbursement level of same-tier medical institutions in the enrollment place."
5

After every visit, keep your own copies of medical records, test reports, and imaging

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Viewing and copying your own medical records is a right the law gives you. Outpatient records, inpatient records, lab slips, imaging, surgery and anesthesia records, pathology materials, and itemized bills can all be copied. The hospital has a dedicated window that handles this and may charge only the cost of copying. Changing hospitals, getting another doctor to take a second look, claiming on commercial insurance, actually having a dispute — all of it rests on this stack of paper.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hospital may charge a copying fee as prescribed, and the fee schedule must be public. The hard part is remembering to get a copy after every single visit.
Benefit
The regulations expressly list viewing and copying medical records as a patient's right. The scope covers outpatient records, inpatient records, lab slips, medical imaging, surgery and anesthesia records, pathology materials, medical expenses, and all other records. Changing hospitals, getting a second doctor to take another look, claiming on commercial insurance, actually having a dispute — all of it rests on these.
Note
There's a dedicated window for copying; you don't need to plead with the doctors. For the list of what to copy, simply read out Article 16 of the Regulation on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes. First: outpatient records, inpatient records, temperature charts, physician order sheets, lab slips, and imaging materials. Then: surgery and anesthesia records, pathology materials, nursing records, and itemized medical bills. Once you have them, keep them in a folder in chronological order. The most important items inside are the discharge summary, the surgery record, the pathology report, and the key images. For a chronic illness, log every round of test results in the same notebook — see Section 16.
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2018). Regulation on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes (State Council Decree No. 701), Article 16: "Patients have the right to view and copy all of their records, including outpatient records, inpatient records, temperature charts, physician order sheets, lab slips (test reports), medical imaging materials, consent forms for special examinations, consent forms for surgery, surgery and anesthesia records, pathology materials, nursing records, medical expenses, and other records designated as part of the medical record by the health authority under the State Council." "Where a patient requests copies of medical records, the medical institution shall provide copying services and affix a certification seal to the copied records... it may charge a copying fee, and the fee schedule shall be public." "Where a patient has died, the patient's close relatives may view and copy the medical records in accordance with this Regulation." Article 15: "No organization or individual may tamper with, forge, conceal, destroy, or seize medical records." https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-08/31/content_531…; National Health and Family Planning Commission and State Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (2013). Provisions on Medical Record Management in Medical Institutions (2013 edition): medical institutions "shall designate a department or dedicated (or concurrent) staff to handle applications for copying medical records"; copying is carried out with the applicant present and a certification seal is affixed. http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2014/content_2600084.htm
6

If you have doubts about your care, demand the records be sealed on the spot — both sides present, an inventory drawn up, one copy each

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

If you have doubts about your treatment, you can demand that the medical records be sealed. Sealing requires both the medical side and the patient side to be present, with an inventory drawn up, signed and stamped, one copy each. If the records aren't finished yet, the completed portion is sealed first. If you suspect a problem with an IV drip, a blood transfusion, an injection, or medication, the bag of fluid, the drug, and the infusion set must be sealed together with them.

Cost
Costs nothing. Submit the sealing request to the hospital and wait for both sides to be present to complete the formalities. The hard part is saying the words out loud in front of the doctors.
Benefit
The regulation provides that "where a medical dispute requires sealing or unsealing of medical records, it shall be carried out with the medical and patient sides both present." What is sealed may be the originals or copies, kept in the custody of the medical institution. Where records are not yet complete and need sealing, the completed portion is sealed first, and the rest sealed once finished. The medical institution shall draw up a sealing inventory of the sealed records, signed or stamped by both sides, one copy each. Where an adverse outcome is suspected to have been caused by IV infusion, blood transfusion, injection, or medication, both sides shall jointly seal and unseal the physical items on site. Where testing is needed, both sides shall jointly entrust a qualified testing institution. If the two sides cannot jointly entrust one, the health authority of the county-level people's government where the medical institution is located designates one. Where a blood transfusion is suspected of causing an adverse outcome and the blood needs sealing, the medical institution shall notify the blood station to send staff to the scene. There is also one hard constraint: "No organization or individual may tamper with, forge, conceal, destroy, or seize medical records." After sealing, if the dispute has been resolved, or three years pass without a renewed request to resolve it, the medical institution may unseal on its own (nationwide, effective October 1, 2018).
Note
Sealing and copying are two different things. Copying is what you should do routinely — see item 5 (keep your own copies of medical records and imaging). Sealing fixes the evidence in place when a dispute arises, guarding against additions and alterations made after the fact. If you suspect a problem with an IV, a transfusion, or medication, seal the bag of fluid, the drug, and the infusion set along with the records — don't let anyone take them away and throw them out. Medical institutions must publicize, in a prominent place, the channels, procedures, and contact information for resolving medical disputes, and set up a unified complaint-management department. When something goes wrong, go to that department first — don't argue with the doctor on duty.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2018). Regulation on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes (State Council Decree No. 701, Articles 15, 24, and 25). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-08/31/content_531…
7

For acute, serious conditions go straight to the ER triage desk, not the registration window

Grade AValue: HighBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The ER doesn't run on first come, first served — patients are sorted into four levels by severity. The sorting happens at the triage desk at the ER entrance, not the registration window. Skip triage and you have no level in the system; no matter how badly you're hurt, you can only shuffle along with the queue. When you arrive, report the most dangerous thing first: heavy bleeding, can't breathe, not lucid, something impaled in the body, crushing chest pain.

Cost
Costs nothing. Walk a few extra steps inside the door to find the triage desk. State the most life-threatening symptom in one sentence.
Benefit
The National Health Commission's 2024 edition of emergency medicine quality-control indicators requires ER triage to "sort patients into four levels by criticality." "Level I is for critically ill patients, who need treatment immediately." "Level II is for acute and severe patients, for whom assessment and treatment often proceed at the same time." "Level III is for acute patients, who need diagnosis and treatment within a short time." "Level IV is for non-urgent or sub-acute patients, who are seen in order in the general treatment area." Triage means that on entering the ER, a dedicated staffer first assesses how serious the condition is and sets the order of care. Beijing's implementation standard gives the response requirements for each level. Level 1: "assess and treat immediately; take the patient into a resuscitation room or resuscitation bay." Level 2: "monitor vital signs immediately; treatment within 10 minutes; take the patient into a resuscitation bay." Level 3: "treated ahead of Level 4 patients; the patient waits in the general treatment area; if the wait exceeds 30 minutes, re-assessment is required." Level 4: "seen in order; unless the condition changes, the wait is longer; if the wait exceeds 4 hours, the patient may be re-assessed." Triage must "uphold the principle that the critically and urgently ill are seen first," and a pre-examination triage area must be set up in a prominent position at the ER entrance (the four-level standard is national; the response times follow Beijing's standard).
Note
The four-level sort is uniform nationwide. How long each level waits is set by each province and city; Beijing's is a version you can check word for word. Leveling looks at indicators and symptoms — heart rate, blood pressure, blood oxygen — not at how much pain you feel. Level 1's hard criteria include the following. First, a heart rate above 180 bpm or below 40 bpm. Second, systolic pressure below 70 mmHg — systolic is the higher number in a blood pressure reading. Third, blood oxygen below 80%. Fourth, shock, a confirmed heart attack, or acute altered consciousness. If you think triage rated you too low, spell out your most dangerous symptom and say it again. If your condition changes while you wait, go straight back to the triage desk to be re-assessed. When it's truly critical, calling 120 is faster than getting there yourself: the pre-hospital medics will assign a level under the same standard and notify the hospital in advance to prepare for your arrival (see Section 13).
Sources (2 references)
General Office of the National Health Commission (2024). Notice on Issuing the Medical Quality Control Indicators for Six Specialties Including Emergency Medicine (2024 edition) (Guo Wei Ban Yi Zheng Han [2024] No. 150), Annex 1, Indicator 4, "implementation rate of graded emergency triage." https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202405/content_6951260…; Beijing Municipal Health Commission (2019). Beijing Work Plan on Strengthening Pre-examination Triage by Severity in Emergency Care, with the annexed Beijing Hospital Emergency Pre-examination Triage Severity Standard (Trial): "uphold the principle that the critically and urgently ill are seen first. Based on the severity of the patient's condition, and following the principles of from severe to mild and from rapidly changing to relatively stable, arrange the order of care sensibly." "Set up the emergency pre-examination triage area in a prominent position at the ER entrance." http://wjw.beijing.gov.cn/zwgk_20040/ylws/201912/t20191216_…
8

No money, no ID, can't say who you are — the ER must still treat you first

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The state has a disease emergency relief fund that pays specifically for the emergency care of two kinds of people: those whose identity can't be established, and those who can't pay. Hospitals may not refuse or delay emergency rescue, and emergency centers may not refuse to dispatch an ambulance over money. So don't tough it out at home because you have no money, and don't skip calling an ambulance for fear of the bill. This fund covers only emergency care; any later hospitalization still goes through medical insurance and medical assistance.

Cost
Costs nothing.
Benefit
The disease emergency relief system covers "patients within China who suffer an acute, severe, or critical illness or injury and need emergency care but whose identity is unclear or who are unable to pay the corresponding fees." The fund pays two kinds of expenses: "emergency care costs incurred for patients whose identity cannot be established" and "emergency care costs owed by patients whose identity is clear but who are unable to pay." The document also states that "medical institutions at every level and of every type, and their staff, must rescue patients with acute, severe, or critical illness or injury promptly and effectively, and may not refuse, pass off, or delay treatment on any pretext." Pre-hospital emergency care is also regulated: the national pre-hospital emergency call number is 120. Emergency centers (stations) "may not refuse, pass off, or delay pre-hospital emergency medical services for reasons of command and dispatch," nor "may they refuse or delay pre-hospital emergency medical services over fees." Transport follows "the principles of nearest, most urgent, meeting professional needs, and giving due regard to the patient's wishes" (nationwide, since 2013).
Note
The fund pays only the "emergency care costs" portion, and treatment comes first — afterward the medical institution applies to the fund, so you don't have to go claim the money at a window. Those with medical insurance still go through insurance first as usual. Application procedures and limits differ by province. In the transport principles, "nearest" and "most urgent" rank ahead of "the patient's wishes," so the ambulance won't necessarily take you to the hospital you name; in critical cases, the nearest facility that can handle it prevails. If your remaining out-of-pocket share is still too heavy, go through medical assistance — see Section 7, item 10 (medical assistance).
Sources (2 references)
General Office of the State Council (2013). Guiding Opinions on Establishing the Disease Emergency Relief System (Guo Ban Fa [2013] No. 15). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2013-03/01/content_606…; National Health and Family Planning Commission (2014). Measures for the Administration of Pre-hospital Medical Emergency Care (Commission Decree No. 3, Articles 13, 22, 23, and 25). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2014/content_2580977.htm
9

Get disability assessed only after treatment ends; too early, and your grade comes out lower

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

How much compensation you get depends mainly on the disability grade, and the grade depends on how much functional impairment remains after treatment is finished. The standard states the assessment must be done after treatment has concluded, or after the clinical outcome has stabilized. Go get assessed while the bone hasn't healed or the plate hasn't been removed, and what gets assessed is how you look at that moment — you'd be grading yourself down. An ordinary fracture that has healed without impairing function doesn't qualify at all.

Cost
The assessment fee runs from a few hundred to 2,000 yuan, generally advanced first by whoever applies. You must wait until treatment ends or the clinical outcome stabilizes — usually three to six months after the injury, sometimes longer. The hard part is wanting to lock it down before the injury has fully healed; you have to hold back.
Benefit
The Grading of Disability Caused by Human Body Injuries stipulates that the timing of assessment "should be after treatment of the primary injury and its genuinely related complications has concluded, or after the clinical treatment outcome has stabilized." The standard "divides disability from bodily injury into 10 grades, from Grade 1 (100% disability rate) to Grade 10 (10% disability rate), with each grade differing by 10%." The judgment basis is "structural damage to human tissues and organs, functional impairment, and the degree of dependence on medical care and nursing, with due consideration of the effects of the disability on social interaction and psychological factors." Among the 10 grades, the provisions related to fractures include the following. First, "a compression fracture of one vertebral body (compression reaching one-third) or a comminuted fracture." Second, "fractures of the pelvis at two or more sites, or comminuted fractures, with malunion." Third, "loss of 25% or more of function in any major joint of the limbs (except the ankle)." Disabilities of the same site and nature must not be counted twice. Where two or more sites are disabling, the grade for each shall be stated separately (nationwide, effective January 1, 2017).
Note
The three assessment systems are not interchangeable — don't mix them up. For injuries from an assault, traffic accidents, and other personal injury, go through the judicial-appraisal Grading of Disability Caused by Human Body Injuries, which is used to calculate disability compensation (see Section 9). Work injuries go through labor capacity appraisal, which uses a different set of ten disability grades and governs work-injury benefits (see Section 19). To enjoy policy benefits for persons with disabilities, you must separately obtain a disability certificate (see item 10, disability certificate). Before the assessment, get your medical records, surgery records, and follow-up imaging ready (see item 5, keep your own copies of medical records and imaging); missing imaging is the most common reason grades get pushed down. When this injury is entangled with a pre-existing condition, the assessment opinion must also state how much of the disability outcome this injury accounts for. That line directly affects how much you're paid.
Sources (1 reference)
Supreme People's Court, Supreme People's Procuratorate, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of State Security, and Ministry of Justice (2016). Announcement on Issuing the Grading of Disability Caused by Human Body Injuries (issued April 18, 2016; effective January 1, 2017), Articles 4.2, 4.4, 4.5, 5.10.6, and 6.2 of the standard. https://www.moj.gov.cn/pub/sfbgw/zwxxgk/fdzdgknr/fdzdgknrtz…
10

If treatment leaves real functional impairment, apply for a disability certificate at the county-level disabled persons' federation where your household is registered

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The disability certificate is the gateway to benefits for persons with disabilities, not a proof of injury. There are seven categories — vision, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, psychiatric, and multiple — each with grades one to four. The process is: apply, have the application accepted, get assessed at a designated institution, public notice, review and approval, certificate issued; it's valid for ten years and renewed free at expiry. If you don't qualify, you don't qualify — this is not something a well-connected acquaintance can get done.

Cost
The certificate itself carries no fee. Assessment and photo costs are, in principle, borne by the applicant; those in hardship can apply for a reduction or waiver. Bring your ID card, household registration booklet, and 3 two-inch photos on a white background to the county-level disabled persons' federation where your household is registered. If you pass the assessment, there's a 5-working-day public notice in the village (community), and the federation completes its review within 10 working days. The hard part is making these trips and waiting it out.
Benefit
The disability certificate "is the legal credential for identifying persons with disabilities and their disability category and grade, and an important basis for persons with disabilities to lawfully enjoy preferential policies of the state and local governments." The assessment standard is the national standard Classification and Grading of Disabilities (GB/T 26341-2010). Certification is voluntary to apply for and administered by the place of registration. All seven categories — vision, hearing, speech, physical, intellectual, psychiatric, and multiple — can apply, with disability grades one to four. County-level federations handle applications and issuance, based on assessment conclusions from hospitals or professional institutions designated by the province. Where the assessment conclusion meets the standard, there's a five-working-day public notice in the village (community), and the county-level federation "completes its review within ten working days." "No fee is charged for issuing a disability certificate." Assessment and photo costs "are, in principle, borne by the applicant personally; localities with the means may subsidize them from local finances, and for applicants in special hardship the relevant departments should be coordinated to grant a reduction or waiver." The certificate is valid for ten years and renewed free at expiry. If the disability category or grade changes, you can apply for re-assessment. If you dispute the assessment conclusion, you can apply within ten working days to the prefecture-level federation for re-assessment. If you still dispute it, the provincial disability assessment expert committee makes the final conclusion (nationwide, effective January 1, 2018).
Note
Do the math before deciding whether to apply. The certificate itself pays nothing directly. What it unlocks is the two subsidies for persons with disabilities: those with disabilities in minimum-livelihood (dibao) families receive the living subsidy, and those in grades one or two who need long-term care receive the nursing subsidy — see Section 7, item 8 (the two subsidies). The certificate also unlocks local benefits for rehabilitation, assistive devices, taxes and fees, employment, and transport. These standards vary widely by province; check the local federation's website first, then decide whether the trip is worth it. It, the judicial-appraisal disability grade, and the work-injury labor capacity appraisal are three separate systems that don't substitute for one another (see item 9, get disability assessed only after treatment ends). The certificate is for the holder's use only and may not be lent out. Those whose disability no longer meets the standard have the certificate canceled, and cannot reapply for one year after cancellation. For multiple disabilities, the grade is set by the most severe category.
Sources (1 reference)
China Disabled Persons' Federation and National Health and Family Planning Commission (2017). Measures for the Administration of Disability Certificates of the People's Republic of China (issued May 27, 2017; effective January 1, 2018; Articles 2, 3, 5, 7, 9, 17, 19, 22, and 25). https://www.bdpf.org.cn/cms68/web1459/subject/n1/n1459/n150…
11

Thank the doctor who saved you with a letter, a banner, or a satisfaction rating — not a red envelope: the rules ban money and gifts, not gratitude

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Money up front buys no priority; appointment slots, beds, scarce medicines, and surgery scheduling are all banned from being traded for favors. If afterward you want to thank the doctor who saved your life, you may — but don't send cigarettes, liquor, or a red envelope; accepting would put him in violation. Three ways to thank him that actually land on him: fill in a satisfaction rating conscientiously, write a thank-you letter naming him or present a silk banner, and come back for follow-up as instructed.

Cost
Costs nothing. Writing a thank-you letter, or filling in one satisfaction survey, takes ten-odd minutes.
Benefit
The Nine Rules on Integrity in Practice for Staff of Medical Institutions (Guo Wei Yi Fa [2021] No. 41), item 7: "Maintain order in diagnosis and treatment; do not undermine fairness in seeking care. Uphold the principle of equality and jointly build a fair environment for seeking care. It is strictly forbidden to use medical resources such as appointment slots, beds, and scarce medicines and consumables, or care arrangements such as tests and surgery, to take favors or profit at the public's expense." Item 8: "Build harmonious relations together; do not accept 'red envelopes' from patients or their families. Abide by medical ethics and practice strict self-discipline." The same item also states it is "strictly forbidden to solicit or accept gifts, cash gifts, consumption cards, negotiable securities, equity, other financial products, or other property from patients and their relatives and friends." Dinners and entertainment paid for by the patient's side are the same: "it is strictly forbidden to take part in banquets or in travel, fitness, entertainment, or other activities that they arrange, organize, or pay for." The document also requires medical institutions to fulfill their primary responsibility, carry out inspections, and "resolutely investigate and punish violations." Satisfaction ratings have been written into the performance assessment of tertiary public hospitals. The basis is the Opinions of the General Office of the State Council on Strengthening the Performance Assessment of Tertiary Public Hospitals (Guo Ban Fa [2019] No. 4). The document says: "The performance assessment indicator system for tertiary public hospitals consists of indicators in four areas: medical quality, operational efficiency, sustainable development, and satisfaction evaluation." It further states: "Hospital satisfaction consists of two parts: patient satisfaction and medical staff satisfaction..." It goes on to say that "patients' sense of gain and medical staff motivation are to be measured through satisfaction evaluations by outpatients, inpatients, and medical staff." The evaluations also have a nationwide unified platform: "The state establishes a management system for public hospital satisfaction..." The timetable: "By the end of March 2019, all tertiary public hospitals nationwide are to be brought into the National Health Commission's satisfaction survey platform. Localities are to use the NHC satisfaction survey platform and incorporate the survey results into the performance assessment of tertiary public hospitals." Hospitals must also handle complaints. The basis is Article 2 of the Measures for the Administration of Complaints in Medical Institutions (National Health Commission Decree No. 3, effective 2019). Complaint management refers to patients "submitting opinions, suggestions, or complaint requests" regarding medical services, medical management, medical quality and safety, and the like. The hospital is responsible for investigating, handling, and giving feedback. "Medical institutions of grade two or above shall set up a physician-patient relations office or designate a department (hereinafter collectively the complaint management department) to take charge of complaint management uniformly." The complaint management department's duties include "receiving complaints uniformly, investigating and verifying complaint matters, proposing handling opinions, and answering patients promptly." Medical institutions "shall encourage staff to proactively collect patients' opinions and suggestions on medical services, medical quality and safety, and other matters" (nationwide).
Note
The beneficiary is you, and also the person who saved you. Wanting to thank someone after an all-night rescue is only human; you may thank them — only the form needs to change. Red envelopes and cigarettes-and-liquor shift the risk onto the other person; thank-you letters, silk banners, and satisfaction ratings are the ways the system recognizes. If you've already given something and it's refused, don't take it as "too little" or "putting on airs" — that's what he's required to do by the rules. Also keep two things apart: giving a doctor a red envelope is a matter of professional discipline and hospital rules, while giving money or goods to case-handling or law-enforcement officers is the crime of bribery under criminal law — the two are not the same order of magnitude; for the latter, see Section 8, item 40. Hospitals generally accept thank-you letters and banners, but that "it goes into personal and department records" is word of mouth, with no document behind it. What has a documented basis is that satisfaction survey results are incorporated into the performance assessment of tertiary public hospitals. If you have doubts about the care itself, demand the records be sealed on the spot (see this section's item 6, sealing medical records) and keep the records and imaging on file (item 5, keep your own copies of medical records and imaging).
Sources (3 references)
National Health Commission, National Healthcare Security Administration, and National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (2021). Notice on Issuing the Nine Rules on Integrity in Practice for Staff of Medical Institutions (Guo Wei Yi Fa [2021] No. 41). Gazette of the State Council http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5678098.htm; General Office of the State Council (2019). Opinions on Strengthening the Performance Assessment of Tertiary Public Hospitals (Guo Ban Fa [2019] No. 4). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-01/30/content_536…; National Health Commission (2019). Measures for the Administration of Complaints in Medical Institutions (Commission Decree No. 3). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-10/08/content_543…
12

Before getting dental implants, ask exactly what the package price includes; prefer providers that have committed to the price-governance program, and don't trust low-price ads

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

After dental implants underwent centralized price cuts in 2023, the total cost of a routine single implant fell from an average of 15,000 yuan to 6,000-7,000 yuan. At tertiary public hospitals the service fee per implant is in principle capped at 4,500 yuan, with the implant body and the crown counted separately. Implants, dentures, and orthodontics are not covered by medical insurance; treatments like fillings and extractions are generally covered everywhere.

Cost
Costs nothing. Before dental work, check the provider list once on the National Healthcare Security Administration's official WeChat account and get the prices clear in person — ten-odd minutes.
Benefit
A January 2024 announcement by the National Healthcare Security Administration says the cost of a routine single implant consists of three parts. First, the medical service fee, charged as a package. The package covers "the consultation fees for the entire implant process, biochemical and imaging test fees, the implant placement fee, the crown placement fee, and the scan-design-modeling fee; it does not include extraction, periodontal scaling, root canal treatment, bone grafting, or soft-tissue grafting." "At tertiary public hospitals everywhere, the medical service charge for a single routine implant is in principle capped at 4,500 yuan"; economically developed regions may loosen this by at most 20% under the 2022 special governance notice. Second, the implant body: nationwide centralized procurement in January 2023, with "winning prices ranging from 548 yuan to 1,855 yuan, at an average of over 900 yuan." The lead agency, the Sichuan Provincial Healthcare Security Administration, announced that high-priced imported brands fell from a procurement median of 5,000 yuan to about 1,850 yuan, and the highest-volume brands from about 1,500 yuan to about 770 yuan. Third, the crown, with "prices ranging from 100 yuan to 656 yuan, at an average of over 300 yuan." At its second-half 2023 press conference, the NHSA said local governance measures were all fully in place by the end of April and early May, and "the total cost of a dental implant fell from an average of 15,000 yuan to around 6,000-7,000 yuan." Does insurance cover it: a 1999 document from the Ministry of Labor and Social Security and other departments listed "dentures" (false teeth) and "non-functional cosmetic and orthopedic surgery" as not payable by basic medical insurance. In its 2019 reply to a CPPCC proposal, the NHSA said "cosmetic diagnostic and treatment items (including restoration of missing teeth, orthodontics, and the like) are not included in the payment scope of the medical insurance fund. But for dental treatment items, there is no exclusion at the national level, and localities have generally included them in insurance payment" (nationwide, as of October 2026).
Note
The 4,500-yuan line only governs public hospitals. Private providers set their own prices, but the special governance notice requires them not to induce patients with false or misleading "subsidies" or "low prices." The low price in an ad is often just the implant body alone; extraction, bone grafting, and other items outside the package are where the markups live, so before signing, get an itemized list with each item's price. The list of providers that have committed to the price-governance program is published by the NHSA on its official WeChat account. A missing tooth or two doesn't have to be replaced with an implant; fixed and removable dentures are also restoration options, and their prices haven't moved with the cuts — ask your doctor which suits you. Whether the employee medical insurance individual account can pay for implants has no unified national answer; ask your local insurance department; for how the individual account can be used for family members, see Section 5, item 13 (family mutual aid). For why missing teeth should be replaced, see Section 2, item 10 (replace missing teeth promptly). Benefit is rated medium: the price cuts came from policy; what the reader can save at this step is mainly the markups beyond the package and the part charged by high-priced providers — a few thousand yuan per implant.
Sources (6 references)
National Healthcare Security Administration (2024). Announcement on Publishing the "List of Medical Institutions Committed to Participating in Dental Implant Price Governance" and Other Information (January 12, 2024). https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2024/1/12/art_109_11954.html; National Healthcare Security Administration (2022). Notice on Launching Special Governance of Dental Implant Medical Service Charges and Consumable Prices (Yi Bao Fa [2022] No. 27, Articles 4 and 6). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-09/08/content_570…; National Healthcare Security Administration (2023). The NHSA Holds Its Regular Press Conference for the Second Half of 2023 (September 22, 2023). https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2023/9/22/art_14_11321.html; Sichuan Provincial Healthcare Security Administration (2023). Proposed Winning Results of the Centralized Volume-Based Procurement of Dental Implant Systems (January 11, 2023). https://ylbzj.sc.gov.cn/scsybj/nc020100/2023/1/11/ac5565c7e…; Ministry of Labor and Social Security et al. (1999). Notice on Issuing Opinions on the Administration of Diagnostic and Treatment Items, the Scope of Medical Service Facilities, and Payment Standards under Basic Medical Insurance for Urban Employees (Lao She Bu Fa [1999] No. 22, Annex 1). https://policy.mofcom.gov.cn/claw/clawContent.shtml?id=39317; National Healthcare Security Administration (2019). Reply Letter on Proposal No. 4043 of the Second Session of the 13th National Committee of the CPPCC. https://www.nhsa.gov.cn/art/2019/12/3/art_26_2096.html

25. What to Handle After Someone Dies

10 items

Basis: money. This section covers only how to handle the paperwork and how to get the money: what to do first when someone has just died, and which charges have a published list to check against. It also covers which account balances can be withdrawn, and which matters close relatives have the right to handle. The first five items follow the order events unfold: the scene, the death certificate, the body and cremation, what to do if you dispute the cause of death, and canceling the household registration. The remaining items are ordered by value for the effort. For arrangements an elder should make while alive — voluntary guardianship, wills, accounts — see Section 17. For the three work-related death benefits, see Section 19. The funeral part of this section is based on the new version of the Funeral Management Regulation, effective March 30, 2026. How much the funeral subsidy and survivor benefits under pension insurance pay is set separately by the human resources and social security authorities. No original text that could be checked word for word was obtained this time, so the main text does not quote specific amounts.

1

If someone dies at home or elsewhere, first tell normal death from abnormal: for accidents, unknown causes, or anyone living alone found dead, call the police immediately and don't touch the body or the scene

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Accidental deaths, deaths of unknown cause, and people who lived alone and are found long after — for these, only the police can issue the death certificate. If the scene has been disturbed, the facts can't be established, and the certificate can't be issued either. Without that piece of paper, everything downstream — cremation, canceling the household registration, insurance claims — grinds to a halt. If you can't tell which case it is, call 110 first. Once the police have investigated on scene, they'll still issue the certificate.

Cost
Costs nothing. One phone call does it.
Benefit
Article 8, paragraph 2 of the Household Registration Regulation: "Where a citizen dies in an accident or of unknown cause, the head of the household and the person who discovered the death shall immediately report to the local public security police station or the township people's committee." In other words: if there was an accident, or you don't know how the person died, the head of household and whoever found the body must report to the police station or township government right away. Article 23 of the Funeral Management Regulation: "Where a natural person dies a normal death, the medical and health institution shall promptly issue a death certificate. For the deceased in abnormal-death cases (or incidents) handled by the public security organs according to law who were not treated by a medical institution, the public security organs issue the death certificate." In other words: for a normal death from illness, the medical institution that treated the person issues the death certificate. For the kind that involved no hospital treatment and falls to the police, the police issue it. For abnormal deaths, only the police can issue the death certificate. If the scene has been disturbed, the facts can't be established and the certificate can't be issued either. Cremation, canceling the household registration, and insurance claims all hinge on this one piece of paper.
Note
Someone bedridden with long illness who dies at home counts as a normal death. The certificate can be issued by the institution that treated them in life, or by the community health service center or township health center serving the neighborhood. For who issues the death certificate — whoever treated, issues — see item 2 (death certificate). If you can't tell which case it is, treat it as abnormal: call 110 first, and once the police have investigated on scene, they can still issue the certificate. If you tidy up the scene first and only then report, no one can help you. Do not move the body yourself, wash or redress them, or take away pill bottles and notes.
Sources (2 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (1958). Regulation of the People's Republic of China on Household Registration (Article 8). http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/mpost_2531969.html (posted on the Guangdong Provincial People's Government portal website); State Council (2026). Funeral Management Regulation (State Council Decree No. 824, effective March 30, 2026, Article 23). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169…
2

The death certificate unlocks everything that follows: whoever provided treatment issues it; for a normal death at home, go to the community health service, which signs it within one day

Grade AValue: HighBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If the person died in a hospital, the one that handled treatment issues the death certificate. For a normal death at home, go to the community health service institution or township health center for the neighborhood. When the cause of death is clear, it's issued within one day. Canceling the household registration, cremation, withdrawing the housing provident fund, claiming social insurance benefits, insurance claims, handling inheritance — every one of them requires it. Once you have it, make several extra copies first.

Cost
Costs nothing.
Benefit
The Administrative Standard for Registration of Population Death Information (Trial) says: for deaths within a medical and health institution, it is "issued by the medical and health institution responsible for treatment" — if the person died in a hospital or health center, go to the one that handled treatment. For normal deaths at home or in other places, it is "issued by the community health service institution or township (street) health center of the jurisdiction" — go to the community health service center, township, or street health center for the neighborhood. Where public security or judicial organs determine the death to be abnormal, the public security and judicial departments handle it under current rules and procedures. The 2026 notice from five departments says the Death Certificate's "paper version and electronic credential have the same legal force" — the electronic version works the same as paper. For normal deaths with a clear cause, it must be issued within one day of the death. If the certificate is lost, you can apply to the original issuing institution for one reissue. If the basic information is wrong, you can apply with supporting materials for one reissuance.
Note
Canceling the household registration, cremation, withdrawing the housing provident fund, claiming social insurance benefits, insurance claims, handling inheritance — every one needs it. Once you have it, make several extra copies, and apply for the electronic credential too if one can be issued. There's only one chance at a reissue, so don't lose the original. If the name or ID number is wrong, fix it on the spot; if you only discover it at the inheritance stage, you'll redo the queue at every single window.
Sources (2 references)
General Office of the National Health and Family Planning Commission (2014). Administrative Standard for Registration of Population Death Information (Trial) (Guo Wei Ban Gui Hua Fa [2014] No. 68, Article 9). https://mzj.sz.gov.cn/szmz/pc/zwgk/jcxxgk/zcfg/byfw/content… (forwarded by the Shenzhen Municipal Civil Affairs Bureau); National Health Commission, Ministry of Public Security, Ministry of Civil Affairs, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine, and National Disease Control and Prevention Administration (2026). Notice on Strengthening the Registration of Resident Death Medical Certificate Information and the Management of Electronic Credentials (Guo Wei Gui Hua Fa [2026] No. 5). https://wjw.fujian.gov.cn/xxgk/fgwj/gjwj/202602/t20260228_7… (forwarded by the Fujian Provincial Health Commission)
3

Body transport, storage, and cremation go only through a funeral home; hospital morgues don't handle funerals, and storage generally can't exceed 3 days

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Transport, storage, embalming, cosmetic restoration, and cremation can only be done by a funeral home. A hospital morgue doesn't handle funerals; at most it lets the body sit temporarily. Funeral home storage generally can't exceed 3 days; to keep the body longer you must file for an extension. Cremation requires the death certificate and the cremation confirmation form. The cremation certificate issued afterward is still needed for inheritance and insurance claims.

Cost
Costs nothing.
Benefit
Article 25 of the Funeral Management Regulation: "Body transport, body storage, embalming, cosmetic restoration, and cremation services are provided exclusively by funeral homes." No one else can do these things. Article 24: "The morgue of a medical and health institution may not be outsourced and may not conduct funeral services, but may provide convenience services for the temporary holding of a body." A hospital morgue can only hold the body temporarily; it cannot stage a funeral. Article 27: "A funeral home generally stores a body for no more than 3 days; where extended storage is needed, the bereaved family or the party transferring the body shall complete extension procedures at the funeral home." To keep the body a few more days, file for the extension at the funeral home. Article 28: "A funeral home shall cremate a body upon presentation of the death certificate and the cremation confirmation form, and shall issue a cremation certificate." Both documents are indispensable; after cremation you'll be given a cremation certificate. Article 29: "In areas where cremation is practiced, the body shall be cremated at a funeral home on site or nearby" — find a funeral home near where the person died and cremate there.
Note
The "one-stop" outfits that converge on you after a hospital death are usually not the funeral home's people. Transport itself is a basic item with a set price — see item 6 (the basic items list). Keep the cremation certificate safe; it's needed for inheritance, insurance, and moving the ashes. Whether the locality practices cremation or burial is delineated by the provincial government. The funeral customs of ethnic minorities are protected by Article 9 of the regulation. Those who bury when cremation is required, or who bury or build graves outside cemeteries and ecological burial areas, will be ordered by the civil affairs department to correct within a time limit (to put it right by the deadline).
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2026). Funeral Management Regulation (State Council Decree No. 824, effective March 30, 2026, Articles 8, 9, 24, 25, 27, 28, and 29). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169…
4

If you dispute the cause of death, request an autopsy within 48 hours and have the medical records sealed at the same time

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

If you have doubts about the cause of death, request an autopsy within 48 hours of the death. If the hospital can freeze-store the body, it can be extended to 7 days. An autopsy also requires the signed consent of close relatives. If they don't sign, or the deadline is allowed to lapse, responsibility for the cause of death going unestablished falls on the party that delayed. When requesting the autopsy, also demand that the medical records be sealed. Once the body is cremated, an autopsy is forever impossible.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is remembering to ask at that moment.
Benefit
The autopsy deadline is in Article 26 of the Regulation on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes. The original text: "Where a patient has died and the medical and patient sides dispute the cause of death, an autopsy shall be performed within 48 hours of the patient's death; where the body can be freeze-stored, this may be extended to 7 days." So to establish the cause of death, the autopsy must be done within 48 hours of the death, extended to at most 7 days if the hospital can freeze the body. The same article states: "An autopsy requires the consent and signature of the deceased's close relatives; refusal to sign is deemed the close relatives' non-consent to the autopsy." If the family doesn't sign, it counts as refusal. It further states: "Where refusal to consent to an autopsy or delay causes the prescribed time to be exceeded, affecting determination of the cause of death, responsibility lies with the party that refused or delayed." Whoever refuses or misses the deadline bears the responsibility if the cause of death can't be established afterward. Article 24: sealing and unsealing medical records "shall be carried out with the medical and patient sides both present." Sealing and unsealing the records requires both you and the hospital to be there.
Note
After the deadline, saying "I suspected something was wrong from the start" shifts responsibility onto the party that delayed. Once the body is cremated, an autopsy is never possible again, so this must be settled before contacting the funeral home. For how to seal medical records, see Section 24.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2018). Regulation on the Prevention and Handling of Medical Disputes (State Council Decree No. 701, Articles 24 and 26). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/content/2018-08/31/content_53180…
5

Canceling the household registration has statutory deadlines: before burial in cities, within one month in the countryside

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

In cities, cancel the registration before burial; in the countryside, within one month. Take the death certificate and the household registration booklet to the police station. Drag it out, and inheritance transfers, benefit claims, and insurance refunds all stall on the household status.

Cost
Costs nothing. Take the death certificate and the household registration booklet and make one trip to the police station.
Benefit
Article 8, paragraph 1 of the Household Registration Regulation: "When a citizen dies, in cities before burial and in the countryside within one month, the head of household, a relative, the person supporting them, or a neighbor shall report the death to the household registration authority and cancel the registration. If a citizen dies at their place of temporary residence, the household registration authority there notifies the household registration authority of the permanent residence to cancel the registration." In other words: in cities it's done before burial, in the countryside within a month. The head of household, relatives, the supporting person, or a neighbor can all go to the household registration authority (the police station) to report the death and cancel the registration. If the person died while temporarily residing elsewhere, the police station there notifies the station where the household is registered to cancel it.
Note
With the registration still on the books, inheritance transfers, benefit claims, and insurance refunds all stall — those windows all check household status. If the pension keeps being paid, that's fraudulent claiming, and it will have to be paid back sooner or later. While at the police station, also ask how to stop the social insurance and medical insurance benefits and how to apply for the funeral subsidy. For those sums, see item 9 (housing provident fund balance, social insurance benefits).
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (1958). Regulation of the People's Republic of China on Household Registration (Article 8). http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/mpost_2531969.html (posted on the Guangdong Provincial People's Government portal website)
6

Funeral services divide into basic and non-basic items; basic items have a published list with fees set by law

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Body transport, storage, farewell ceremony, cremation, ash storage, and ecological burial are all on the national basic items list. Niche interment provided by public institutions is on it too. The prices of these items are set by rule. Beyond the list, no additional items may be created to charge for. Before you set out, get clear on which items count as basic and what the local standard is, then discuss the rest.

Cost
Costs nothing. Spend a few minutes on the list before setting out.
Benefit
Body transport, body storage, farewell ceremony, body cremation, ash storage, and ecological burial are all on the national basic items list. Niche interment provided by government-run funeral service institutions is on the list too. The fee standards for these items are set by law, the prices fixed by rule — not left to the funeral home's discretion. The non-basic items list is determined by civil affairs departments at the level of cities divided into districts and above (prefecture-level cities and up).
Note
Provinces, autonomous regions, and directly administered municipalities may add items on top of the national list. First get clear on which items are basic and what the local fee standard is, then discuss the rest. Items on the list are priced firmly by rule; off-list ones are optional. Keep the two categories straight — only then does the overcharged part become something you can contest. Wanting a dignified send-off for a loved one is not wrong; I won't urge you to skimp — where the money goes is your call.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2026). Funeral Management Regulation (State Council Decree No. 824, revised and adopted at the 72nd executive meeting of the State Council on November 14, 2025, "effective March 30, 2026"). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169… Article 5: "Funeral services are divided into basic and non-basic items, with fee policies formulated by the development and reform and finance departments under the State Council together with the civil affairs and other departments under the State Council." "The state formulates a list of basic funeral service items, incorporating body transport, body storage, farewell ceremony, body cremation, ash storage, ecological burial, and niche interment provided by government-run funeral service institutions within the list's scope"; Article 50: "Funeral services are subject to list-based management with dynamic adjustment; establishing items or charging fees outside the list is prohibited."
7

If you run into forced bundles, markups above listed prices, or one service split into several charges, write it down and complain

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

All of these are price violations named by the regulation: not posting a price list, adding charges beyond the listed price, bundling funeral goods into forced sales, and forcing you to accept another business's paid services. Splitting one item into several charges also counts as a disguised price increase. On the spot, ask for the price list first, and keep the receipts and chat records. Complaining afterward is still in time. For pricing, go to market regulation; for funeral services, go to civil affairs.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is still being willing to press the point at that moment.
Benefit
The regulation lists five categories of price violations; four are described here. Not posting a price list, or collecting more than the listed price, constitutes failure to clearly mark prices or adding charges beyond the listed price. Withholding one service unless you buy another constitutes forced sale through bundling or attaching unreasonable conditions. Forcing another business's paid services on you constitutes forced or disguisedly forced acceptance of third-party paid services. Charging extra under a different name constitutes disguisedly raising fee standards. It also prohibits "disguised fee increases through splitting items or expanding the scope of charges." Splitting one service into several separately billed items, or widening the scope of what gets billed, are both on the prohibited list.
Note
Investigating price violations belongs to the market regulation authorities; funeral services themselves belong to civil affairs. Ask for a price list on the spot, keep the receipts and chat records, and complaining afterward is still in time.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2026). Funeral Management Regulation (State Council Decree No. 824, revised and adopted at the 72nd executive meeting of the State Council on November 14, 2025, "effective March 30, 2026"). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169… Article 42: "Funeral service institutions may not, in violation of relevant provisions, set up fee items on their own initiative, or disguisedly raise fee standards by splitting items, expanding the scope of charges, and the like." The price violations listed in Article 43 include "(1) failing to clearly mark prices as required, or adding charges beyond the listed price or collecting unlisted fees"; "(3) forcing or disguisedly forcing the sale of funeral goods and the provision of funeral-related services for fees through bundling, attaching unreasonable conditions or unreasonable restrictions, and the like"; "(4) forcing or disguisedly forcing the bereaved family to accept third-party paid services, or repeatedly charging fees through related service outlets"; Article 51 requires civil affairs departments to establish an information-sharing and oversight mechanism with the government service convenience hotline: "problems with funeral services reported by bereaved families shall be handled promptly together with the relevant departments, and the outcome communicated to the family."
8

Intermediaries for funeral agency, supply purchasing, and ceremony planning must register with the county-level civil affairs department

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Intermediaries for funeral agency, goods purchasing on your behalf, ceremony planning and officiating, and information consulting must file with the county-level civil affairs department. Unregistered ones aren't in the civil affairs department's funeral service information system. Whether you can look this up yourself varies by locality; the safest is to phone the county-level civil affairs department and ask. Those who use tricks to overcharge or traffic in the deceased's information will be dealt with according to law.

Cost
Costs nothing. Ask one question: filed or not filed.
Benefit
Unregistered intermediaries are not in the funeral service information system administered by civil affairs. Those who charge fees improperly by deception, induce lavish spending, force services on people, or traffic in the deceased's information will be dealt with according to law, flagged in the system, and made public for all to see.
Note
"Trafficking in the deceased's information" is the most common trap in this trade. If a stream of sales calls arrives right after you finish the paperwork, the information was probably resold. Online memorial platforms are regulated the same way. Article 45 of the regulation forbids them from inducing consumption and from handling the deceased's information unlawfully.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2026). Funeral Management Regulation (State Council Decree No. 824, revised and adopted at the 72nd executive meeting of the State Council on November 14, 2025, "effective March 30, 2026"). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202601/content_7054169… Article 41: "Apart from funeral service institutions, organizations and individuals engaged in funeral-related service activities such as funeral service agency, goods purchasing on behalf, ceremony planning and officiating, and information consulting shall file with the civil affairs department of the county-level people's government." "Those whose conduct harms the rights and interests of bereaved families — improperly charging fees by deception or other means, inducing lavish arrangements, forcing acceptance of services, or trafficking in the deceased's information — shall be dealt with according to law, flagged in the funeral service information system, and made public."
9

Go claim the money scattered in different places one by one: housing provident fund balance, social insurance benefits, work-injury benefits

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The housing provident fund balance can be withdrawn by heirs; it isn't in a bank account, so it's the easiest to miss. What remains in the pension insurance individual account can be inherited too. For a death from illness, the family separately receives a funeral subsidy and a survivor's pension of 3 to 24 months. For a work-related death, there are the three work-injury payments besides.

Cost
Costs nothing, but takes several windows. Before going, get the death certificate and proof of kinship ready.
Benefit
The housing provident fund account balance (what remains in his provident fund account) can be withdrawn by heirs and legatees. A legatee is the person named in the will to receive things. For a work-related death there are three further payments: the funeral subsidy, pensions for dependent relatives, and the one-time death-at-work compensation. What remains in the pension insurance individual account is expressly inheritable under the Social Insurance Law. For a person in employee pension insurance who dies of illness or from non-work causes, the family can also receive a funeral subsidy and a survivor's pension, together called survivor benefits. For enterprise employees the standard is one nationwide formula. The funeral subsidy is 2 times the previous year's monthly per-capita disposable income of urban residents in the province. The survivor's pension uses that monthly income as the base and pays 3 to 24 months by contribution years: under 5 years, 3 months; 5 to 10 years, 6 months; 10 to 15 years, 9 months; above 15 years, 1 more month per extra year, up to 24 months. For those already retired, 1 month is deducted per year of pension received, with a minimum of 9 months.
Note
The provident fund sum is the most often forgotten, because it isn't in a bank account and doesn't automatically enter the estate split. What remains in the pension individual account and survivor benefits are calculated and paid separately, but both are handled at the social insurance service windows of the enrollment place. Required materials differ by locality. With under 5 years of contributions, total survivor benefits don't exceed what the person paid in. This formula comes from the enterprise employee pension measures; for survivor benefits under government/institution and urban-rural resident pension insurance, ask at the window. For the formal requirements of wills and inheritance, see Section 17.
Sources (5 references)
State Council (2026). Regulation on the Administration of Housing Provident Funds (amended by State Council Decree No. 844, effective September 20, 2026), final paragraph of Article 24. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2026/issue_12946/202608/content_…: "Where an employee dies or is declared dead, the employee's heirs and legatees may withdraw the stored balance in the employee's housing provident fund account; where there is neither an heir nor a legatee, the stored balance in the employee's housing provident fund account goes into the housing provident fund's value-added income."; for the three benefits under Article 39 of the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance, see Section 19. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018 revision). Social Insurance Law (Articles 14 and 17): "Where an individual dies, the individual account balance may be inherited" and "Where a person participating in basic pension insurance dies of illness or from non-work causes, their survivors may receive a funeral subsidy and a survivor's pension." https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f210989… (National Database of Laws and Regulations); Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and Ministry of Finance (2021). Interim Measures on Survivor Benefits under Basic Pension Insurance for Enterprise Employees (Ren She Bu Fa [2021] No. 18, effective September 1, 2021, Articles 4 and 5); the original was not published online, and the provisions were verified against the verbatim quotations in the administrative reconsideration decision of the Huadu District People's Government of Guangzhou (Hua Du Fu Xing Fu [2022] No. 226): "the funeral subsidy standard is calculated as 2 times the previous year's monthly per-capita disposable income of urban residents in the province where the insured person died..." "with contribution years under 5, the number of months paid is 3... with contribution years above 30, calculated as 30, with the number of months paid capped at 24." https://www.huadu.gov.cn/xxgk/xzfy/content/post_8672730.html; Fujian Provincial Department of Human Resources and Social Security. Frequently asked questions: "for each year of basic pension received, 1 month is deducted, with the number of months paid no lower than 9" and "where cumulative contribution years are under 5, the survivor benefits (including the funeral subsidy and the survivor's pension) may not exceed the sum of the person's individual contributions." http://rst.fujian.gov.cn/wz/cjwt/czzgly/202311/t20231113_62…
10

Close relatives can request to view, copy, correct, or delete the deceased's account data and personal information

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

After a person dies, close relatives, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, can ask the platform to view, copy, correct, or delete the deceased's personal information. If the platform refuses, it must state its reasons. You can also sue in court. There is one exception: if the deceased made other arrangements while alive — say, designating an account heir or leaving clear wishes — their arrangements govern.

Cost
Costs nothing. You only need to complain or sue if the platform doesn't cooperate.
Benefit
The law states plainly: where a natural person has died, close relatives may, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, exercise rights such as viewing, copying, correcting, and deleting over the deceased's relevant personal information. Close relatives can ask the platform to bring out the person's information to view, copy it, fix errors, and delete it.
Note
The statute contains a line, "except where the deceased made other arrangements while alive" — where an account heir was designated or clear wishes were left, what they left governs. So while a person is still of sound mind, it's worth writing down where the accounts and passwords go — see Section 17. Deleting an account and deleting personal information are two different things — see Section 14.
Sources (1 reference)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2021). Personal Information Protection Law. National People's Congress website. http://www.npc.gov.cn/npc/c2/c30834/202108/t20210820_313088… Article 49: "Where a natural person has died, their close relatives may, for their own lawful and legitimate interests, exercise the rights of viewing, copying, correcting, and deletion provided in this chapter over the deceased's relevant personal information, except where the deceased made other arrangements while alive."; Article 50: "Personal information handlers shall establish convenient mechanisms for accepting and handling individuals' requests to exercise their rights. Where a request by an individual to exercise rights is refused, reasons shall be given" and "Individuals may file suit with the people's court according to law."

26. Building a Website or Platform: Licenses, Filing, and Servers

11 items

You want to build a website or an app. This section answers four things: what kind of business it counts as in the eyes of the law, which license you need, where to put the server, and who is responsible for what users post and the money they pay. The basis here is personal freedom and money. The items are ordered as follows: first the ones that can land you in prison, then the ones that require a license before you start, then what a platform has to do every day, and the last item is experience in choosing a server — that one can only offer judgment, not numbers. If you are a salaried technical employee, see Section 11 for the red lines. How to register a company and file taxes is covered in Section 12 and not repeated here. For a comparison table of the various licenses and a decision table for choosing a server, see [docs/Which licenses a platform needs](../docs/做平台要办哪些证.md).

1

A platform shouldn't collect money itself and pass it to sellers — route payments through a licensed payment institution that settles directly

Grade AValue: HighBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noBenefit: large

If the buyer's money lands in your account first and you then pass it on to the seller, you are doing payment business. That business requires approval from the People's Bank of China and a genuine 100 million yuan of capital. Do it without approval and you get shut down, the money you made is confiscated, and there are fines — separate ones for the boss and the people who handled it. In serious cases, prison. There is exactly one safe approach: the money never enters your account.

Cost
Costs nothing. It takes some time to integrate a licensed payment institution's product. A licensed payment institution is a company that has obtained a payment license from the central bank. Use its split-settlement or escrow features so the buyer's money settles directly to the seller and never enters the platform's own account
Benefit
The regulations define payment business as "transferring monetary funds according to electronic payment instructions submitted by the payee or the payer." In plain terms: moving money for other people on their instructions. To run this business, you "shall obtain approval from the People's Bank of China and a payment business permit." Minimum registered capital is 100 million yuan, and it must be paid-in monetary capital — that 100 million yuan has to genuinely land in the company's account. "Whoever, without legal approval, establishes a non-bank payment institution without authorization, or engages in payment business directly or in disguised form, shall be banned by the People's Bank of China in accordance with the law, and illegal gains shall be confiscated." Do this without approval and you are shut down outright, with the money you made taken away. If illegal gains reach 500,000 yuan or more, an additional fine of 1 to 5 times the illegal gains. With no illegal gains, or gains under 500,000 yuan, a fine of 500,000 to 2 million yuan. The legal representative and the directly responsible people face separate fines of 100,000 to 500,000 yuan. The criminal law also counts "illegally engaging in fund payment and settlement business" as illegal business operation: in serious cases up to 5 years in prison, in especially serious cases more than 5 years. What counts as "serious" is drawn in the interpretation issued by the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate. The line is: illegal business volume above 5 million yuan, or illegal gains above 100,000 yuan (nationwide, effective May 2024)
Note
Design the money flow so it never enters your account — that is the only safe approach. The market calls this collect-and-forward model "second clearing," but the term appears in no official document. The implementation rules use the phrase "engaging in payment business in disguised form," meaning moving money on users' instructions without approval. The Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate interpretation lists only three scenarios: cashing out with fabricated transactions, cashing out through corporate accounts, and cashing out with checks. It does not name platform collect-and-forward, so you cannot say platform collect-and-forward "necessarily constitutes a crime"
Sources (4 references)
State Council (2023). Regulation on the Supervision and Administration of Non-Bank Payment Institutions (State Council Decree No. 768, Articles 2, 6, 8, 27, 47). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11086/202401/content_… ; People's Bank of China (2024). Implementation Rules for the Regulation on the Supervision and Administration of Non-Bank Payment Institutions (PBOC Decree [2024] No. 4, Article 68). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11546/202408/content_… ; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 225, Item 3). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml ; Supreme People's Court and Supreme People's Procuratorate (2019). Interpretation on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases of Illegally Engaging in Fund Payment and Settlement Business and Illegal Foreign Exchange Trading (Articles 1, 3, 4). https://www.spp.gov.cn/xwfbh/wsfbt/201901/t20190131_407161.…
2

Most fee-charging websites need a license; if you only sell your own goods and don't host other sellers, you don't; matching third-party trades calls for a different license; free sites just need ICP filing

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: a lotTime: a lotWillpower: noBenefit: large

Websites that charge users mostly need a value-added telecom business operating license first, and an individual cannot get one. If you only sell goods on your own website or app and don't let other sellers open shops, you don't need it. Nor do you if you only run a WeChat or Alipay mini program or an online store. Charge money and open a site when the license was required but not obtained, and your revenue is confiscated on top of fines; in serious cases the site is shut down.

Cost
ICP filing is free. The value-added telecom business operating license costs money; it governs "whether a website that charges users may operate." To apply for it you first need a company. Operating within a single province: registered capital of at least 1 million yuan. Operating across provinces: at least 10 million yuan. Review period 60 days; the license is valid for 5 years
Benefit
The regulation's exact words: "The State implements a licensing system for commercial internet information services and a filing system for non-commercial internet information services. Those who have not obtained a license or completed the filing procedures may not engage in internet information services." If you charge, get the license first; if you don't charge, file first; with neither, you cannot open the site. What counts as commercial? The regulation says: "providing information or web page production and other such services to internet users for compensation over the internet." Simply put: charging users. The trade-matching category is called online data processing and transaction processing business, known in the industry as EDI. The regulation defines it as "providing users with online data processing and transaction/transaction-processing services over public telecom networks or the internet, using various data and transaction-processing application platforms connected to public telecom networks or the internet," and it "includes transaction processing business, electronic data interchange business, and network/electronic device data processing business." That is: a website processing data online for users, or matching and processing transactions between buyers and sellers. Operating without the license, or beyond its scope, means confiscation of illegal gains plus a fine of 3 to 5 times those gains. Operating beyond scope means you hold the license but do things outside what it covers. With no illegal gains, or gains under 50,000 yuan, a fine of 100,000 to 1 million yuan. In serious cases, the site is ordered closed (nationwide). Charging money does not automatically mean you need the license. A Q&A issued by the Guangdong Communications Administration in October 2025 says that, per the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology's requirements, the following three situations do not require this license. First, a company "directly selling its own or other enterprises' goods or services in a self-operated manner" on its own website or app, with no other organization or individual opening shops on it. Second, a company only publishing its own information on its own website or app, not providing a platform for others to post. Third, a company doing business only through mini programs, official accounts, video accounts, or online stores on platforms like WeChat and Alipay, "with no other independently operated platform." Conversely, as soon as you let others open shops, or let users post information on your site, you fall outside those three
Note
Whether what you're building falls into the EDI category, check for yourself against the definitions in the Telecommunications Business Classification Catalogue. No official sentence anywhere explicitly says "e-commerce platforms with trade matching and payment handling must obtain an EDI license." MIIT's service guide only says to "apply for the corresponding telecom business operating license according to the business classification." So whether you need it, you can only judge for yourself against the definitions. One more thing: an individual cannot get this license; the applicant must be a lawfully established company. The three self-operated exemptions come from the Guangdong Communications Administration's Q&A, which states it follows MIIT requirements, but no similar public text was found from other provinces. If unsure, call your local communications administration first. The Q&A also reminds you that you don't need an intermediary to apply — submit materials only through MIIT's "Telecom Business Market Comprehensive Management Information System," and the government charges no fees
Sources (5 references)
Guangdong Communications Administration (2025). Frequently Asked Questions on Obtaining a Value-Added Telecom Business Operating License (October 17, 2025, Item 1). https://gdca.miit.gov.cn/bsfw/bszn/jyxk/tzgg/art/2025/art_6… ; State Council (2000). Measures for the Administration of Internet Information Services (State Council Decree No. 292, second revised December 6, 2024, Articles 3, 4, 7, 19). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1860864.htm ; State Council (2024). Decision on Amending and Repealing Certain Administrative Regulations (State Council Decree No. 797, Item 18). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_11786/202501/content_… ; State Council (2000). Telecommunications Regulations (second revised 2016, Articles 7, 9, 13, 69). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2016/content_5139478.htm ; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2017). Measures for the Administration of Telecommunications Business Operating Licenses (MIIT Decree No. 42, Articles 6, 9, 11, 14). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5240090.htm
3

Live streaming needs a network culture business license; the audiovisual program license is one private firms essentially can't obtain

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: a lotTime: a lotWillpower: noBenefit: large

To run livestreams or game commentary you need a Network Culture Business License issued by the provincial culture department. The license's business scope must explicitly include online performance. Results come within 20 days of acceptance; the license lasts 3 years. You must keep broadcast videos yourself for a full 60 days.
