Open for business without the license and you get ordered to stop, warned, and fined up to 30,000 yuan; keep going and you land on a blacklist.

Cost
The Network Culture Business License, colloquially the "wangwen" license, governs "whether you can make money from online performances such as livestreams and game commentary." It is approved by the provincial culture administration, with results within 20 days of acceptance, valid 3 years, renew starting 30 days before expiry. The audiovisual program license governs "whether you can broadcast programs online," and it requires the applicant to be a wholly state-owned or state-controlled entity
Benefit
Entities doing online performance must get the license first. The regulation's exact words: they "shall, in accordance with the Interim Provisions on the Administration of Internet Culture, apply to the provincial culture administration for a Network Culture Business License, and the license's business scope shall explicitly include online performance." Playing games for an audience, with commentary, is managed the same way — the regulation says such activities are "administered with reference to these measures." All online performance video materials must "be kept for no less than 60 days" — you keep the broadcast videos yourself for a full 60 days. Running commercial internet cultural activities without approval: ordered to stop, given a warning, and fined up to 30,000 yuan. Those who keep going after being ordered to stop are placed on the culture market blacklist. Broadcasting programs online requires a different license: you "shall obtain an Information Network Transmission of Audiovisual Programs License." The applicant must "have legal-person status and be a wholly state-owned or state-controlled entity" — state-funded or state-controlled units only; private companies essentially cannot get it. Doing it without that license: a warning, an order to correct, plus possible fines up to 30,000 yuan. In serious cases, punished under the Broadcasting and Television Administration Regulations (nationwide)
Note
Which business pairs with which license is laid out most clearly in the seven-department document. Platforms making money from livestreams need the network culture license plus ICP filing — ICP filing is the registration procedure a website completes with MIIT. Broadcasting programs online requires the audiovisual program license, or completed registration. Publishing news requires an Internet News Information Service License. One more thing: the version of the Interim Provisions on the Administration of Internet Culture reposted on the central government website in 2025 is the unrevised 2011 text; for citations, go by the Ministry of Culture and Tourism's current version
Sources (4 references)
Ministry of Culture (2016). Measures for the Administration of Online Performance Business Operations (Wen Shi Fa [2016] No. 33, Articles 2, 4, 6, 13, 20). https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/scgl/202012/t20201206_9181… ; Ministry of Culture (2011). Interim Provisions on the Administration of Internet Culture (Ministry of Culture Decree No. 51, revised 2017 by Decree No. 57, Articles 7, 8, 9, 16, 21, 28). https://zwgk.mct.gov.cn/zfxxgkml/zcfg/bmgz/202012/t20201204… ; State Administration of Radio and Television and Ministry of Information Industry (2007). Provisions on the Administration of Internet Audiovisual Program Services (Decree No. 56, revised 2015, Articles 2, 7, 8, 24). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/2022-08/23/content_5722664.htm ; Cyberspace Administration of China and six other departments (2021). Guiding Opinions on Strengthening the Standardized Management of Online Livestreaming (Guo Xin Ban Fa Wen [2021] No. 3, Item 9). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-02/10/content_558…
4

Servers inside the country require ICP filing, and your access provider must hold a value-added telecom license in its own name

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noBenefit: medium

With servers inside the country, you must complete ICP filing before the site goes live. Filing is free, submitted through the provider along with the server, usually taking a few days to a few weeks. No filing: ordered to correct within a time limit and fined 10,000 yuan; refuse and the site is closed. Not displaying the filing number on the homepage means a separate fine of 5,000 to 50,000 yuan.

Cost
Filing is free. It is submitted through the provider together with the server and usually takes a few days to a few weeks. Checking whether a provider is properly licensed takes ten minutes
Benefit
The regulation's exact words: "Without filing, no non-commercial internet information services may be provided within the People's Republic of China." Even a site that doesn't charge users must file first as long as it is hosted inside the country. No filing: ordered to correct within a time limit and fined 10,000 yuan. Refuse to correct, and the site is closed. The provider that connects your server to the internet is regulated too: it "may not provide internet access services to organizations or individuals engaged in non-commercial internet information services without filing." The same goes for the provider that collects money for you. The regulation says such providers "may not provide access, fee collection on behalf of others, or similar services to organizations or individuals that have not lawfully obtained an operating license or completed non-commercial internet information service filing." Meaning: legitimate providers may not serve sites with neither a license nor a filing. Also, server colocation and cloud hosting are called internet data center business in the regulations, and broadband access is internet access service business — both require licenses themselves, so the provider must hold one first. Not displaying the filing number on the site's homepage: ordered to correct, plus a fine of 5,000 to 50,000 yuan (nationwide)
Note
Before negotiating prices, check whether the provider has a license. Verify licenses at MIIT's Telecom Business Market Comprehensive Management Information System, tsm.miit.gov.cn, searching by full company name or license number. Check website filings at beian.miit.gov.cn. With an unlicensed "data center," when something goes wrong you won't even know whom to appeal to. Putting the machine abroad does indeed bypass filing. But with users inside the country and money inside the country, none of the obligations written in items 5 through 10 of this section go away, and you add a layer of data-export costs
Sources (3 references)
Ministry of Information Industry (2005). Measures for the Administration of Non-Commercial Internet Information Service Filing (MII Decree No. 33, revised 2024 by MIIT Decree No. 68, Articles 5, 13, 18, 22). https://www.miit.gov.cn/gyhxxhb/jgsj/cyzcyfgs/bmgz/xxtxl/ar… ; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2017). Measures for the Administration of Telecommunications Business Operating Licenses (MIIT Decree No. 42, Articles 20, 24). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2017/content_5240090.htm ; Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (2015). Telecommunications Business Classification Catalogue (2015 edition, B11, B14, B21, B25). https://www.miit.gov.cn/zwgk/zcwj/wjfb/tg/art/2020/art_e984…
5

Let users sell on your platform, and you must verify and register them, report the information, and keep records for three years

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: someBenefit: large

Let others sell on your platform and you must first verify each seller's identity, address, contact details, and licenses, then register them and build files. Once the files exist, re-verify at least every six months. Who the sellers are gets reported to market regulation; tax information gets reported to the tax authorities every quarter. Product and transaction records are kept three years. Miss any one item: ordered to correct first, then fined 20,000 to 100,000 yuan.

Cost
Costs nothing. You need seller qualification checks in your backend plus a registration archive. Tax-related information reported once a quarter, transaction data kept three years. The hard part is that it is ongoing work, not something you do once and are done with
Benefit
The law has a paragraph of requirements for platforms. Exact words: platforms "shall require operators applying to enter the platform to sell goods or provide services to submit true information such as identity, address, contact details, and administrative licenses; shall verify and register it, establish a registration archive, and verify and update it periodically." Before a seller enters, they submit identity, address, contact details, and whatever licenses they need. You verify it, register and archive it, and re-verify at intervals afterward. How long is "periodic"? A departmental rule is more specific: "at least once every six months." You must also report the identity information of on-platform operators to the market regulation department. And to the tax side: "in accordance with tax collection and administration laws and administrative regulations, report the identity information of on-platform operators and tax-related information to the tax authorities." So who the sellers are goes to market regulation, and sellers' identities and tax situation go to the tax authorities. Product and service information and transaction information must "be kept for no less than three years from the date the transaction is completed" — from the day a deal is done, the data stays at least three years. Fail any item above: ordered to correct within a time limit. Miss the deadline: fined 20,000 to 100,000 yuan. Serious cases: ordered to suspend business for rectification, plus a fine of 100,000 to 500,000 yuan. Tax information must be reported "within the month following the end of the quarter" — in the month right after each quarter ends. Late reporting carries the same penalties (nationwide)
Note
Sellers themselves must also register as market entities. The law lists categories that don't need to: "individuals selling self-produced agricultural and sideline products or household handicraft products; individuals using their own skills to provide convenient services that lawfully require no license, and occasional small-value transactions." "Occasional small-value" has a concrete number: Article 8 of the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions sets it at 100,000 yuan in annual transaction volume. Two more things the platform must do: label registered and unregistered sellers as such, and never delete consumer reviews
Sources (4 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2018). E-Commerce Law (Articles 10, 27, 28, 31, 80). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf8af… ; State Administration for Market Regulation (2021). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Transactions (SAMR Decree No. 37, Articles 8, 24, 25, 31). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2021/content_5602020.htm ; State Council (2025). Provisions on the Reporting of Tax-Related Information by Internet Platform Enterprises (State Council Decree No. 810, Articles 2, 3, 4, 10). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_12146/202507/content_… ; State Taxation Administration (2025). Announcement on Matters Concerning Internet Platform Enterprises' Reporting of Tax-Related Information (STA Announcement 2025 No. 15). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202506/content_7029727…
6

User-posted content is your responsibility: moderation mechanisms, a reporting channel, and immediate takedown and reporting when something illegal turns up

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: littleTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: large

What users post is the platform's responsibility when things go wrong. Build the whole system: registration, post moderation, comment moderation, daily patrols, and incident handling. Put a reporting entrance somewhere prominent on the page. See illegal information: immediately stop its spread, keep records, and report to the competent authority. Don't, and the fine is 50,000 to 500,000 yuan — more in serious cases.

Cost
You pay people to moderate — the platform's biggest long-term expense. The reporting entrance and the record of every enforcement action must leave a trail. The hard part is that someone has to watch it every single day; skip a day and something can go wrong
Benefit
The regulation says platforms "shall fulfill their primary responsibility for information content management" — what users post is the platform's own job to govern. Specifically, it must "improve systems for user registration, account management, information publication review, comment review, page and interface ecosystem management, real-time patrols, emergency response, and the handling of online rumors and black-industry-chain information." From registration, posting, and comments to daily patrols and incident handling, every link needs written rules. It must also "set up a convenient complaint and reporting entrance in a prominent position" — the report button goes where users can see it and reach it at a glance. On discovering illegal information, the platform "shall immediately take disposal measures in accordance with the law, preserve relevant records, and report to the competent authorities." The Cybersecurity Law is more specific. Exact words: "Upon discovering information prohibited from publication or transmission by laws or administrative regulations, [the network operator] shall immediately stop transmitting that information, take disposal measures such as deletion to prevent its spread, preserve relevant records, and report to the competent authorities." Failure: ordered to correct, given a warning, circulated as a notification, plus possible fines of 50,000 to 500,000 yuan. Refusal to correct, or serious cases: 500,000 to 2 million yuan, plus possible orders to suspend business for rectification, close the website or app, or revoke licenses or the business registration. The directly responsible people face separate fines of 50,000 to 200,000 yuan (nationwide)
Note
You don't have to invent moderation rules — copy them. The nine categories of prohibited content are laid out clearly in Article 15 of the Measures for the Administration of Internet Information Services. Livestreaming adds three things: "establish a livestream content review platform," be able to cut off a live broadcast at any moment — the statute calls it "immediate blocking" — and keep livestream content and logs for 60 days. Online performance video materials likewise, no less than 60 days
Sources (3 references)
Cyberspace Administration of China (2019). Provisions on the Governance of the Online Information Content Ecosystem (CAC Decree No. 5, Articles 8, 9, 10, 16, 37). http://www.cac.gov.cn/2019-12/20/c_1578375159509309.htm ; NPC Standing Committee (2025). Cybersecurity Law (amended 2025, effective January 1, 2026, Articles 49, 69). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm ; State Council (2000). Measures for the Administration of Internet Information Services (Articles 15, 16, 23). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1860864.htm
7

Offer information publishing or instant messaging, and you must require users to provide real identity information

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noBenefit: medium

If your site lets people post, or chat, you must ask for their real identity information when they activate the service. Those who won't provide it cannot use it. The approach: store real names in the backend, let users pick whatever nickname shows on the page, and verify with a phone number. Skip real-name verification: ordered to correct first. Refuse, and the fine is 50,000 to 500,000 yuan, with the site possibly shut down.

Cost
You need to integrate a real-name verification channel; these charge per check. Design the product on the "real name in the backend, voluntary on the front end" principle: real names stored in the backend, nickname displayed on the page
Benefit
The law's exact words: "When network operators provide users with network access or domain name registration services, handle subscription procedures for landlines or mobile phones, or provide users with information publishing, instant messaging, and similar services, they shall require users to provide real identity information when signing agreements or confirming service provision. Users who do not provide real identity information may not be provided the relevant services." Not asking for real names, or letting users keep using the service after they failed to provide real identity: ordered to correct. Refusal to correct, or serious cases: fined 50,000 to 500,000 yuan, plus possible orders to suspend the relevant business, suspend operations for rectification, close the website or app, or revoke licenses or the business registration. The directly responsible people face separate fines of 10,000 to 100,000 yuan. Livestreaming services follow the "real name in the backend, voluntary on the front end" principle, conducting "real identity verification based on mobile phone numbers and similar means." Meaning: the platform stores users' real names in the backend, users choose their own displayed nicknames, and verification relies on phone numbers and the like. Livestream commerce is stricter: "real identity verification based on ID document information, unified social credit codes, and the like." A unified social credit code is the string of digits on the business license (nationwide)
Note
The article numbers have moved. The Cybersecurity Law was amended in 2025, effective January 1, 2026. The real-name article moved from Article 24 to Article 26, and the penalty provision from Article 61 to Article 64. The wording is unchanged. If your materials still cite the old article numbers, update them
Sources (3 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2025). Cybersecurity Law (amended 2025, effective January 1, 2026, Articles 26, 64; Articles 24 and 61 in the 2016 text). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2025-12/29/c_1768735112911946.htm ; Cyberspace Administration of China (2016). Provisions on the Administration of Internet Livestreaming Services (Articles 12, 16). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2016-11/04/c_1119847629.htm ; Cyberspace Administration of China and six other departments (2021). Measures for the Administration of Livestream Marketing (Trial) (Guo Xin Ban Fa Wen [2021] No. 5, Article 8). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-04/23/content_560…
8

No livestreaming accounts for anyone under 16, with tips handled in age-based tiers

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noBenefit: medium

People under 16 cannot register a livestreaming account with you. Those 16 or older need identity verification plus consent from parents or other guardians. Tipping comes in three tiers: under 8 cannot tip at all; 8 to 16 needs guardian consent; over 16 needs guardian consent or verified proof of income. If a child tips behind a guardian's back, the guardian can demand the money back, and the court will order a refund.

Cost
Costs nothing. Add one step at each of two points — registration and payment: first determine age, then confirm guardian consent was given
Benefit
The law's exact words: "Providers of internet livestreaming services may not provide account registration services for livestream publishers to minors under the age of 16; when providing such registration to minors aged 16 or over, they shall verify their identity information and obtain the consent of their parents or other guardians." The regulation also requires you to "establish a dynamic verification mechanism for the real identity information of livestream publishers" — you must be able to re-check a broadcaster's identity at any time. It also requires you to "reasonably limit the single-purchase and same-day cumulative spending amounts of minors of different age groups using their services" — per-transaction and per-day spending caps set by age. Tipping now comes in three tiers: "Tipping services may not be provided to minors under the age of 8. Providing tipping to minors aged 8 to 16 requires guardian consent. Providing tipping to minors over 16 requires guardian consent or verification of income proof materials." One more provision: when a person with limited civil capacity tips without guardian consent, the court shall support the guardian's claim, and the money can be recovered. A person with limited civil capacity is a minor who, in law, cannot yet make all decisions independently (nationwide)
Note
If a refund dispute actually arises, handle it in the direction most favorable to the minor. The official line here has changed. The 2022 four-department opinion and the 2020 notice from the radio and television regulator both said minors were barred from tipping entirely. The April 2026 notice switched to tiers at 8 and 16, but did not state that the two earlier documents were repealed, and officials have not said how the two fit together. So the statement "minors are flatly banned from tipping" is no longer accurate
Sources (4 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2020). Law on the Protection of Minors (Articles 74, 76). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2020-10/22/c_1604928959588622.htm ; State Council (2023). Regulations on the Protection of Minors Online (State Council Decree No. 766, Articles 31, 44). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10806/202311/content_… ; General Secretariat of the Office of the Central Cyberspace Affairs Commission (2026). Notice on Strengthening the Standardized Management of Livestream Tipping (Item 7). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2026-04/13/c_1777815804150225.htm ; Supreme People's Court (2020). Guiding Opinions (II) on Lawfully and Properly Adjudicating Civil Cases Involving the COVID-19 Epidemic (Fa Fa [2020] No. 17, Article 9). https://www.court.gov.cn/fabu/xiangqing/230181.html
9

Deal with infringement notices promptly; if nothing follows within 15 days after the counter-statement is forwarded, put the content back up

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noBenefit: medium

When someone sends an infringement notice with preliminary evidence attached, promptly delete, block, or disconnect the item, and forward the notice to the seller. Drag your feet and you owe the seller compensation for the additional losses, jointly. If the seller contests, forward the counter-statement to the claimant and wait 15 days. If the claimant neither files a complaint nor sues, put the content back up.

Cost
Costs nothing. Build a fixed process: receive the notice, forward it to the seller, take in the seller's counter-statement, publish the outcome. Keep records at every step
Benefit
A rights holder "has the right to notify the e-commerce platform operator to take necessary measures such as deletion, blocking, disconnection of links, and termination of transactions and services. The notice shall include preliminary evidence of the infringement." A rights holder is the owner of rights like trademarks, copyrights, and patents. A bare sentence doesn't count — preliminary evidence must be attached. On receiving the notice, the platform "shall promptly take the necessary measures and forward the notice to the on-platform operator; failing to take necessary measures promptly, it bears joint liability with the on-platform operator for the enlarged portion of the harm." Drag your feet and you owe the seller, jointly, for the additional losses. After the seller's counter-statement, the platform "shall promptly terminate the measures taken if, within fifteen days after the counter-statement reaches the intellectual property rights holder, no notice of a complaint or lawsuit from the rights holder has been received." Meaning: forward the seller's counter-statement to the rights holder and wait 15 days. No complaint, no lawsuit — restore what was deleted or delisted. A platform that knows, or should know, of an infringement and does nothing bears joint liability with the infringer. The intellectual property authority can also order you to correct within a time limit; miss the deadline and the fine is 50,000 to 500,000 yuan, rising to 500,000 to 2 million yuan in serious cases. Conversely, "anyone who sends a false notice in bad faith, causing losses to an on-platform operator, bears double compensatory liability" (nationwide)
Note
If you are not an e-commerce platform, just an ordinary website, the Civil Code's notice-and-takedown rules apply instead. The difference is how long you wait after the other side's counter-statement: the E-Commerce Law gives a definite 15 days, the Civil Code only says "a reasonable period." Also, publicly posting the notices you receive, the sellers' counter-statements, and your outcomes is an explicit requirement of Article 44 of the E-Commerce Law. If the platform itself organizes pirated uploads, or knows of infringement and leaves it up, the "delete upon notice" rule does not protect it — see Section 9, item 24 (fan-translated comics, reuploaded films and TV shows)
Sources (2 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2018). E-Commerce Law (Articles 42, 43, 44, 45, 84). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf8af… ; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code (Articles 1195, 1196, 1197). https://www.court.gov.cn/zixun/xiangqing/233181.html
10

Don't casually move user data abroad; data exports carry statutory conditions and headcount thresholds

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noBenefit: medium

Sending domestic users' information to a machine outside the country counts as a data export. A server located abroad does not mean the data hasn't been exported. To export, you must go through one of four routes: a security assessment organized by the cyberspace authority, certification by a professional body, signing a standard contract, or another arrangement the law provides. You must also tell users who abroad receives the information and what it will be used for, and ask them about this specifically, once.

Cost
Costs nothing. The simplest route is keeping user data inside the country. If it genuinely must be sent abroad, use the standard contract or get certification
Benefit
Handing domestic users' information to a foreign company, or storing it on a machine abroad, is legally called providing personal information abroad, and it "must satisfy" one of four conditions. One: pass a security assessment organized by the cyberspace authority. Two: complete personal information protection certification through a professional body. Three: sign a standard contract drawn up by the cyberspace authority with the foreign recipient. Four: other conditions provided by laws and administrative regulations. At the same time you must tell users the following: the foreign recipient's name, contact details, processing purpose, processing methods, the types of personal information, and how they can exercise their rights. And you must "obtain the individual's separate consent" — ask the user about this specifically, once. The concrete thresholds are tiered by cumulative headcount. Ordinary companies are called, in the regulation, data processors other than critical information infrastructure operators. For them there is an exemption line, in the original words: "having cumulatively provided personal information (excluding sensitive personal information) on fewer than 100,000 individuals abroad since January 1 of the current year." Below that line, all three — assessment filing, standard contract, certification — are waived. From 100,000 to under 1 million individuals: you must sign a standard contract or obtain certification. 1 million or more, or sensitive personal information of 10,000 or more individuals: you must file for a security assessment (nationwide, effective March 2024)
Note
A server abroad does not mean "the data hasn't been exported." A user registers inside the country and you send their information to a machine abroad — that is an export. One category doesn't need any of the three routes — security assessment, certification, standard contract: cross-border shopping, cross-border delivery, booking flights and hotels — transfers "truly necessary for concluding or performing a contract to which the individual is a party." Also note how the headcount is counted: cumulatively "since January 1 of the current year," not twelve months back from today
Sources (3 references)
NPC Standing Committee (2021). Personal Information Protection Law (Articles 38, 39, 40). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/202108/t20210820_527244.shtml ; Cyberspace Administration of China (2024). Provisions on Promoting and Regulating Cross-Border Data Flows (CAC Decree No. 16, Articles 3, 4, 5, 7, 8). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11366/202405/content_… ; Cyberspace Administration of China (2022). Measures for the Security Assessment of Data Exports (CAC Decree No. 11, Article 4). https://www.cac.gov.cn/2022-07/07/c_1658811536396503.htm
11

Choosing a server: first ask if you can tolerate its downtime, then whether anyone maintains it, and only then compare prices

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noBenefit: medium

The difference between the three tiers isn't price — it's what you have in hand the day something breaks. The big providers have a filing channel, public credentials, outage announcements, compensation clauses, and someone you can reach. Small providers cost half as much, but when they oversell, vanish, or get cut off by their upstream, you don't even know whom to call. For a static site with no user data, a VPS costing a few dozen yuan a month is plenty.

Cost
Cloud hosting from mainstream providers: several hundred to several thousand yuan a month. VPS from small providers: from a few dozen yuan a month. A VPS is a small virtual server. Dedicated server colocation starts at several thousand yuan a year, and you buy the hardware yourself
Benefit
The difference between the three tiers isn't price — it's what you have in hand the day something breaks. Mainstream cloud providers have a filing channel, publicly verifiable credentials, outage announcements, compensation clauses in the contract, and someone you can reach when problems arise. Small providers can be half the price, but when they oversell, vanish, or get cut off by their upstream, you have no one to appeal to — so before negotiating prices, check in the MIIT system whether they hold a value-added telecom business operating license. Dedicated server colocation only pays off when two conditions both hold: bandwidth or hardware costs are clearly cheaper, and you have your own people doing operations. How to choose: for a static site with no user data, the cheapest VPS is enough. With user registration and transactions, pick cloud hosting that scales elastically and supports snapshot backups, and keep backups in at least two places
Note
The above is a judgment from experience, with no literature evidence. The only thing that can truly be checked is the provider's license. If you want to save money, save it on specs and bandwidth — never on credentials
Sources
Author's experience; no direct literature. For the statutory requirements on provider credentials and filing, see item 4 of this section; for the 6-month log retention and classified protection obligations, see Section 11, item 16

27. Pregnancy and Childbirth: From a Positive Test to Discharge and Paperwork

16 items

The first half of this section reckons in mortality risk for the pregnant woman and the fetus. The second half reckons in money and errand time. The two accounts are not converted into each other. The content only covers "what to do when." Things with no hard evidence, or only a small effect — pregnancy nutrition, prenatal education — are not covered here. For maternity benefits, maternity leave, and the money side of raising a child, see Section 18; for caring for the baby after birth, see Section 20; for emergencies, see Section 13. The World Health Organization's figures: in 2023, roughly 260,000 women worldwide died from pregnancy and childbirth. About 75% of them died from these five causes: major postpartum hemorrhage, infections, hypertensive disorders of pregnancy (a group of diseases involving raised blood pressure after conception, including preeclampsia and eclampsia), complications during delivery, and unsafe abortion. WHO also says, "Most maternal deaths are preventable, as the health-care solutions to prevent or manage complications are well known." The most powerful items in this section are the ones that intercept these problems in advance.

1

Start 0.4 mg of folic acid daily when trying to conceive, and keep taking it through the first 3 months of pregnancy

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Taking one folic acid tablet daily around conception cuts the chance of a neural tube defect by about 70%. Neural tube defects are birth defects like anencephaly and spina bifida. For someone who has already had a child with one, the chance of it happening again drops to roughly one third of the original.

Cost
A few dozen yuan a bottle. Rural women pay nothing — the national free folic acid supplementation program supplies it. One tablet a day; the hard part is remembering every single day
Benefit
A Cochrane systematic review pooled 5 trials and 6,708 deliveries and rated the evidence high quality. Daily folic acid around conception cuts the risk of a fetal neural tube defect to RR 0.31 (95% CI 0.17 to 0.58, the credible range) — a reduction of about 70%. For those who have already had a child with a neural tube defect, the risk of it happening again is RR 0.34 (95% CI 0.18 to 0.64) — down to about one third of the original. By population subgroup, 0.4 mg and higher doses show no difference in effect. Folic acid alone versus multivitamins shows no difference either
Note
The key is "start before pregnancy." The fetal neural tube closes within 28 days of conception. By the time a test tells you you're pregnant, most of that window has already passed. So if you plan to have a child, start 3 months ahead. In the same pooled research, folic acid showed no clear effect on cleft lip or palate, congenital heart disease, or miscarriage — don't count on it for anything else
Sources (1 reference)
De-Regil LM, Peña-Rosas JP, Fernández-Gaxiola AC, Rayco-Solon P (2015). Effects and safety of periconceptional oral folate supplementation for preventing birth defects. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (12), CD007950. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD007950.pub3
2

Before week 13, open your Maternal and Child Health Handbook at the community health center and use up the free prenatal checkup quota

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noBenefit: medium

At least five prenatal checkups during pregnancy, plus a postpartum home visit and the 42-day postpartum checkup — the state pays for these. To claim them, open a Maternal and Child Health Handbook at your community health center before week 13 of pregnancy. Skip that, and you miss these free visits entirely.

Cost
Free — this falls under the national basic public health service program. It takes a few trips scheduled by gestational week
Benefit
The National Basic Public Health Service Specifications (Third Edition) include maternal health management services. Pregnant women who are residents of the service area can receive them: 1 first-trimester health check, 2 in the second trimester, 2 in the third trimester, 1 postpartum home visit, and 1 health check at 42 days postpartum. Go open the handbook before week 13, and have the first prenatal checkup at the same time. The two second-trimester visits fall at weeks 16-20 and 21-24; the two third-trimester visits at weeks 28-36 and 37-40. Local public service lists also include a full set of lab tests at the first visit and postpartum depression screening
Note
These 5 visits are the free floor, not the full set of prenatal care. Hospitals add ultrasounds, glucose tests, and fetal heart monitoring as needed — those you pay for yourself. The earlier you open the handbook, the earlier your pregnancy risk grading gets done. Risk grading means classifying pregnant women by risk level; only once a high-risk case is flagged can she be referred early to a hospital equipped to handle her. If you live in a different district, open the handbook where you actually live — no need to go back to your registered residence
Sources (2 references)
National Health and Family Planning Commission (2017). National Basic Public Health Service Specifications (Third Edition). https://www.nhc.gov.cn/ewebeditor/uploadfile/2017/04/201704…; Jingjiang Municipal People's Government. National Basic Public Health Service Program — Maternal Health Management Services (published local service list). https://www.jingjiang.gov.cn/xxgk/zdlyxxgk/wsjk/art/2023/ar…
3

At the first prenatal visit, get the three tests done — HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B; free intervention is available even if positive

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: large

At your first prenatal visit, get all three tested — HIV, syphilis, hepatitis B — without paying yourself. Even a positive result is not a dead end. The state supplies the drugs and the protocol free of charge to block the disease's path from mother to child; it's called prevention of mother-to-child transmission.

Cost
Free — the program for preventing mother-to-child transmission provides free testing
Benefit
Mother-to-child transmission means the disease passing from mother to child. The Working Specifications for Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of HIV, Syphilis, and Hepatitis B (2020 Edition) set requirements. In early pregnancy or at the first prenatal checkup, the hospital must provide the relevant information and "offer appropriate, standardized free testing" — you don't pay for these three tests. Post-test counseling or referral is then provided based on the results. A positive result is not a dead end. Article 44 of the Regulation on AIDS Prevention and Treatment requires providing pregnant women infected with HIV "free treatment and counseling for preventing mother-to-child transmission of HIV." Article 43 requires blocking services (keeping the disease from passing to the child), treatment, postpartum home visits, infant follow-up, and testing. If the mother is hepatitis B surface antigen positive, the newborn gets the hepatitis B vaccine and hepatitis B immunoglobulin at birth (see Section 20, item 2)
Note
The earlier these three are tested, the more useful, because blocking and treatment both take time. Article 3 of the Regulation on AIDS Prevention and Treatment also states that "no organization or individual may discriminate against people living with HIV, AIDS patients, and their families" — marriage, employment, medical care, and schooling are legal rights protected by law. For everyday prevention and testing, see Section 1. For post-exposure prophylaxis after a high-risk exposure, see Section 13
Sources (2 references)
General Office of the National Health Commission (2020). Working Specifications for Prevention of Mother-to-Child Transmission of HIV, Syphilis, and Hepatitis B (2020 Edition). https://wjw.xinjiang.gov.cn/hfpc/zhgl6/202012/08b7de496f0b4… (reposted by the Health Commission of Xinjiang Uyghur Autonomous Region); State Council (2006). Regulation on AIDS Prevention and Treatment (Articles 43, 44). https://wjw.beijing.gov.cn/zwgk_20040/zcwj2022/flfg/202304/… (reposted by the Beijing Municipal Health Commission)
4

No cigarettes and no alcohol at all during pregnancy, and no one smokes indoors at home either

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Smoking during pregnancy raises the odds of preterm birth, a baby born too small, and cleft lip or palate. The risk of abnormal bleeding during pregnancy and delivery literally doubles. The risk of sudden infant death is higher too. If family members smoke indoors, it counts just the same. Whenever you quit, it's still not too late.

Cost
Costs nothing — you even save the cigarette and alcohol money. The hard part is getting everyone in the household to quit along with you
Benefit
Per the US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention: smoking during pregnancy means the baby "could be born too small even at full term" and "could be born too early." It "doubles the risk of abnormal bleeding during pregnancy and delivery." It raises the risk of birth defects such as cleft lip and cleft palate. It also "damages the fetus's developing lungs and brain, and the damage can last through childhood." Infants born to mothers who smoked during pregnancy, and infants exposed to smoke after birth, face a higher risk of sudden infant death syndrome. The official advice: "The best thing is to quit before you get pregnant, but if you're already pregnant, quitting still helps" — "it's never too late to quit"
Note
When someone else smokes indoors, the secondhand smoke a pregnant woman breathes counts against the fetus just the same. So no one living with her smokes indoors either. Alcohol is the same: no amount of drinking is known to be safe, so the simplest rule during pregnancy is not a single drink. For the adult's own ledger on tobacco and alcohol, see Section 2
Sources (1 reference)
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Smoking During Pregnancy. https://www.cdc.gov/tobacco/campaign/tips/diseases/pregnanc…
5

With high-risk factors for preeclampsia, start one low-dose aspirin a day after week 12 of pregnancy

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disease of pregnancy. You count as high-risk if you had it in a previous pregnancy, are carrying multiples, have chronic hypertension, had diabetes before pregnancy, or have kidney disease or an autoimmune condition. High-risk women who take one low-dose aspirin daily from week 12 cut preeclampsia by about 15%, preterm birth by about 20%, and death of the baby around the time of delivery by about 20%. Everyone else: don't take it on your own.

Cost
A few dozen yuan. One tablet a day, continued until delivery. The hard part is never missing a day
Benefit
The US Preventive Services Task Force gives a Grade B recommendation: for those at high risk of preeclampsia, start low-dose aspirin (81 mg/day) after week 12 of pregnancy as prevention. Preeclampsia is a hypertensive disorder of pregnancy. Pooling multiple studies, the results are as follows; the 95% CI is the credible range. Preeclampsia RR 0.85 (95% CI 0.75 to 0.95, 16 studies) — about 15% lower. Preterm birth RR 0.80 (95% CI 0.67 to 0.95, 13 studies) — about 20% lower. Perinatal death RR 0.79 (95% CI 0.66 to 0.96, 11 studies) — about 21% lower; perinatal death means death in the period around delivery. Small-for-gestational-age/intrauterine growth restriction RR 0.82 (95% CI 0.68 to 0.99, 16 studies) — about 18% lower; that is, the fetus grows smaller than others at the same gestational week
Note
High-risk means: preeclampsia in a previous pregnancy, twins or multiples, chronic hypertension. Also type 1 or type 2 diabetes before pregnancy, kidney disease, and autoimmune conditions such as systemic lupus erythematosus or antiphospholipid syndrome. If you're not in one of these categories, don't take it on your own. This drug requires a doctor's prescription — lay out your medical history clearly at a prenatal visit and let the doctor judge. What's sold in China is mostly 100 mg enteric-coated tablets; take it as prescribed
Sources (1 reference)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2021). Aspirin Use to Prevent Preeclampsia and Related Morbidity and Mortality: Preventive Medication. https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recomm…
6

At week 24 or later, do the gestational diabetes screening — don't skip it over the sugary drink

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

Gestational diabetes is high blood sugar that appears only once pregnancy has begun. After week 24, half a morning — one sugary drink and a few blood draws — finds it. Leave it unchecked and unmanaged, and the risks of an oversized baby, difficult labor, a C-section, preeclampsia, and newborn low blood sugar all climb.

Cost
A few dozen to just over a hundred yuan. Go on an empty stomach, a few blood draws, half a morning gone
Benefit
The US Preventive Services Task Force gives a Grade B recommendation: for pregnant women without symptoms (feeling nothing wrong themselves), screen for gestational diabetes at week 24 or later. Gestational diabetes is high blood sugar that appears only once pregnancy has begun. If you screen only once, put that one at week 24 or later. On whether screening before week 24 is a good idea, the Task Force's conclusion is that existing evidence is insufficient to judge benefits and harms (Grade I). Left unmanaged, gestational diabetes raises the risks of: macrosomia (an oversized fetus), difficult labor, cesarean delivery, preeclampsia, and newborn hypoglycemia
Note
Of those diagnosed, most can control blood sugar with diet adjustments and exercise alone; only a minority need insulin injections. Don't skip this test because you're afraid a positive result means injections. After the birth, blood sugar needs rechecking: women who have had gestational diabetes face a clearly higher risk of type 2 diabetes later
Sources (1 reference)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2021). Gestational Diabetes: Screening. https://www.uspreventiveservicestaskforce.org/uspstf/recomm…
7

Memorize this 'go to the hospital now' list — it applies during pregnancy and for a year after birth

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: large

If any one of these appears, go to the hospital that day — don't wait a night at home. A headache that won't go away or keeps getting worse, vision changes, fever of 38 °C. Severe swelling of hands or face, trouble breathing, chest pain or a racing heart. Severe abdominal pain that won't ease, fetal movements that stop or clearly decrease, vaginal bleeding or fluid leaking. One arm or leg swollen and painful, thoughts of harming yourself or the baby. It all counts for a year after birth too.

Cost
Costs nothing. Five minutes to memorize — ideally make sure the people you live with know it too
Benefit
The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention lists these urgent maternal warning signs: a headache that won't go away or keeps getting worse, dizziness or fainting, vision changes, a temperature of 38 °C or higher; severe swelling of the hands or face, thoughts of harming yourself or the baby, trouble breathing, chest pain or a too-fast heartbeat; severe nausea and vomiting, severe belly pain that won't ease, the baby's movements stopping or clearly decreasing during pregnancy; vaginal bleeding or fluid leaking during pregnancy, vaginal bleeding or abnormal discharge after birth; severe swelling, redness, or pain in one arm or leg. All of these can happen within a year after delivery — it is not "all clear once the first month is over"
Note
The point of this list is to separate "push through it" from "leave right now." A headache plus blurry vision plus upper abdominal pain points to preeclampsia (the hypertensive disease of pregnancy). One swollen, painful calf points to deep vein thrombosis (see Section 13). Postpartum hemorrhage, per the World Health Organization, can kill a healthy woman within hours. Any one item: go straight to the hospital — don't first wait a night at home
Sources (2 references)
Centers for Disease Control and Prevention. Hear Her — Urgent Maternal Warning Signs. https://www.cdc.gov/hearher/maternal-warning-signs/index.html; World Health Organization. Maternal mortality fact sheet. https://www.who.int/news-room/fact-sheets/detail/maternal-m…
8

If your water breaks, lie flat where you are, prop your hips up, call 120 — no walking around, no showering

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: large

When your water breaks, you don't slowly pack up and head out. The right move is to lie down where you are, prop your hips up, and call 120. Standing and walking drains the amniotic fluid faster, and the umbilical cord can be swept down with it. That is an emergency that can cost the baby's life.

Cost
Costs nothing
Benefit
The Beijing Municipal Health Commission's instructions: once you notice your water has broken, "lie down flat right away to keep the amniotic fluid from flowing out," "do not walk around," and "call 120 immediately." While waiting for the ambulance, let family know to bring the bag and meet you at the hospital. Guidance from medical institutions explains why: standing lets amniotic fluid drain faster, and the baby's umbilical cord can slip down with it — called cord prolapse, an emergency that endangers the fetus. So lie down, prop your hips up; lying on the left side works
Note
The three signs labor is near are regular contractions, bloody show, and water breaking. With the first two you can pack calmly; water breaking is the only one that means "lie down and call for help on the spot." Showering, squatting on the toilet, or driving yourself after your water breaks are all classic mistakes. Note the time it happened and the color of the fluid, and tell the doctor. Yellow-green fluid, or flecks of meconium in it, signals fetal distress (the baby is short of oxygen in the womb). If regular contractions, clearly decreased fetal movement, or fever with chills are also present, stress to the doctor that this is an emergency
Sources (2 references)
Beijing Municipal Health Commission. Weekly first-aid topic: what should an expectant mother do when her water breaks early? https://wjw.beijing.gov.cn/bmfw_20143/jkzs/jzjj/202001/t202…; Beijing Shunyi Maternal and Child Health Hospital. What to do if your water breaks at home in late pregnancy? https://www.bch-syfy.cn/Html/News/Articles/9453.html
9

If you want an epidural, say so — it doesn't raise the risk of cesarean

Grade AValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

An epidural is one anesthetic injection in the lower back that takes the edge off labor pain. It works better than other pain relief and does not make a C-section more likely. "Epidurals leave your back hurting for a lifetime" has no basis either. It now has its own billing item, so hospitals are more willing to provide it.

Cost
A few hundred to just over a thousand yuan, varying by region. Ask the hospital and the anesthesiology department in advance whether they can do it. The hard part is that you have to raise it yourself
Benefit
A Cochrane systematic review concluded: epidural analgesia is more effective than non-epidural methods at reducing labor pain and improving mothers' satisfaction with pain relief. "Going pain-free" uses epidural analgesia. The same review states, "epidural analgesia has no effect on the risk of cesarean or long-term backache." The previously observed increase in instrumental deliveries (using instruments to deliver the baby) no longer appears in studies after 2005. From 2024, the National Healthcare Security Administration's pricing catalog for obstetric medical services created separate billing items for "labor analgesia," "doula-supported delivery," and "family-accompanied delivery." The reason was precisely that the lack of an independent price item had dampened hospitals' willingness to provide labor analgesia
Note
The two most widespread claims — "an epidural means lifelong back pain" and "an epidural means a difficult labor ending under the knife" — both lack any basis. Cochrane pooled epidural analgesia against other pain-relief methods and concluded it has no effect on cesarean risk or long-term backache. The real side effects are: low blood pressure, fever, weak legs, trouble urinating, plus longer first and second stages of labor and a higher chance of needing oxytocin. Whether to have one is your call, but don't give it up over rumors. Whether it's available also depends on the hospital having anesthesiologists on site 24 hours — ask clearly during a prenatal visit
Sources (2 references)
Anim-Somuah M, Smyth RMD, Cyna AM, Cuthbert A (2018). Epidural versus non-epidural or no analgesia for pain management in labour. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, (5), CD000331. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000331.pub4; National Healthcare Security Administration (2024). Restructuring obstetric service price items to help build a birth-friendly society. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202406/content_6957553.htm
10

Don't ask for a cesarean without a medical indication, and don't schedule surgery to pick an auspicious date

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Per the World Health Organization, once a region's cesarean rate passes 10%, maternal and newborn deaths stop declining. If a C-section is indicated, absolutely have it. Cutting for an auspicious date or out of fear of pain just buys you a major abdominal surgery for nothing.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is standing up to the family's arguments
Benefit
The World Health Organization's 2015 statement: as a population's cesarean rate rises to about 10%, maternal and newborn deaths fall. Beyond 10%, there is no evidence that mortality improves further. WHO also emphasizes that every effort should be made to provide cesarean sections to women in need — not to hit any particular rate
Note
When it is genuinely medically needed, a cesarean is life-saving surgery — have it, don't try to gut it out. What to avoid is surgery with no medical need: fear of pain, picking an auspicious hour, gaming the child's school-entry age. A cesarean is major abdominal surgery with slower recovery, and it raises the risks of placenta previa, placenta accreta, and uterine rupture in the next pregnancy. That directly affects whether you want a second child
Sources (1 reference)
World Health Organization (2015). WHO Statement on Caesarean Section Rates (WHO/RHR/15.02). https://www.who.int/publications/i/item/WHO-RHR-15.02
11

Before getting pregnant, confirm your maternity insurance status; an unemployed spouse can also claim childbirth medical expenses

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

When your employer pays maternity insurance, both the medical costs of childbirth and the allowance during maternity leave come from that fund. If your spouse has no job, the medical expenses side can still be claimed. Whether enough contribution months have accrued, and whether giving birth in another city requires pre-filing — ask in advance; none of it can be fixed after the fact.

Cost
Costs nothing. One call to the social insurance or medical insurance hotline
Benefit
Article 54 of the Social Insurance Law: where the employer has paid maternity insurance premiums, its employees enjoy maternity insurance benefits. An employee's spouse without a job receives childbirth medical expense benefits per state regulations, funded from the maternity insurance fund. In plain terms: with employer-paid maternity insurance, the employee enjoys the benefits, and the medical costs of childbirth for the employee's unemployed spouse also come from this fund. Maternity insurance benefits have two parts: one is childbirth medical expenses — the medical costs of the birth itself; the other is the maternity allowance — the money paid to you during maternity leave. Article 56 lists the three situations that earn the maternity allowance: maternity leave for a female employee giving birth, leave for family-planning surgery, and other situations specified by laws and regulations. The maternity allowance "is paid based on the employer's average monthly wage of its employees in the previous year" — it is reckoned on your unit's average monthly employee wage last year, not on your own salary
Note
Two things to confirm in advance, because neither can be fixed afterward. One: whether your consecutive contribution months are enough — every locality sets a minimum, and below it you get no benefits. Two: if you'll give birth somewhere other than where the insurance is enrolled, whether you need to pre-file for an out-of-town birth — without it you may have to front the money yourself and claim reimbursement manually afterward, or get nothing back. For maternity leave days and how the allowance is calculated, see Section 18, item 2
Sources (1 reference)
NPC Standing Committee (2010). Social Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China (Articles 54, 56). https://guangdong.chinatax.gov.cn/gdsw/qysw_gkwj/2020-02/12… (reposted by the Guangdong Provincial Tax Service, State Taxation Administration)
12

Get the Medical Certificate of Birth done before discharge — decide the name early and don't get the characters wrong

Grade AValue: HighBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

This certificate is the prerequisite for household registration, insurance enrollment, and schooling — and only the delivering institution can issue it the first time. Going back for it after discharge means a separate process and extra documents. As for the name, first confirm its characters can be typed in the household registration system.

Cost
Free. Done in passing while handling the discharge paperwork
Benefit
Article 23 of the Maternal and Infant Health Care Law: medical care institutions and personnel engaged in home delivery shall issue the uniformly produced Medical Certificate of Birth for newborns in accordance with the regulations of the health administration department under the State Council. This certificate is the prerequisite for everything downstream: household registration, insurance enrollment, a health insurance card, kindergarten and school enrollment all require it. And first issuance can only be done by the delivering institution. Reapplying after discharge means a separate process and additional supporting documents
Note
Before filling it in, check the parents' names, ID numbers, and the child's name character by character. The name's characters must be typeable in the household registration system; rare characters cause endless hassle later. Changing a name, or the certificate, both go through reissue or replacement — far more trouble than checking on the spot. Once you have it, store it safely on its own — as important as the household registration booklet and the ID cards
Sources (1 reference)
NPC Standing Committee (1994, amended 2017). Maternal and Infant Health Care Law of the People's Republic of China (Article 23). https://www.gov.cn/guoqing/2021-10/29/content_5647619.htm
13

Don't decline the newborn heel-prick screen or the hearing screen

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: large

One heel-prick blood sample and one hearing test can detect hypothyroidism, phenylketonuria, and hearing loss while the baby looks completely normal. By the time symptoms show, the intellectual damage can no longer be undone.

Cost
Free in most areas, or a few dozen yuan. Some extended panels you pay for yourself. One heel prick after the baby is born
Benefit
Article 3 of the Measures for the Administration of Newborn Disease Screening: "The national newborn disease screening panel includes congenital hypothyroidism, phenylketonuria, and other hereditary metabolic diseases of newborns, as well as hearing impairment." These diseases share one feature: early on there is no visible abnormality at all, and by the time symptoms are obvious, the intellectual damage is irreversible. But early detection with early intervention works very well — thyroid hormone supplementation, special formula, hearing aids, or cochlear implants. Article 10 provides that when a screening result is positive, the institution shall promptly notify the guardians to seek diagnostic testing
Note
Article 11 of the Measures requires that before screening, guardians be truthfully told the items, the conditions, the methods, the sensitivity (how much it detects), and the costs, and sign their consent. So you will be handed an informed-consent form. Read it before signing: which are the nationally specified conditions, and which are self-paid add-ons. A positive initial screen is not a diagnosis; the overwhelming majority are ruled out on one retest — don't fall apart at this step. If the initial hearing screen is failed, go for the rescreen as notified; don't decide for yourself that "the kid can hear, so never mind"
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Health (2009). Measures for the Administration of Newborn Disease Screening (MOH Decree No. 64, Articles 3, 10, 11). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2009/content_1371363.htm
14

Once you have the birth certificate, enroll the baby in resident medical insurance — don't wait until the household registration is done

Grade AValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

With the birth certificate in hand you can enroll the baby online — no need to wait for household registration. Once enrolled, the hospitalization costs at discharge can be claimed on the spot. Newborn hospitalization isn't cheap; the difference between insured and uninsured is huge.

Cost
One annual resident medical insurance premium, a few hundred yuan
Benefit
The central government portal's 2024 position: "Newborns can enroll online using just the Medical Certificate of Birth" — no need to complete household registration first. "After discharge, newborns can directly claim reimbursement of medical costs." The old way was household registration first, then enrollment, with hospitalization costs paid fully out of pocket and claimed back afterward. Average processing time for enrollment and payment was also cut from 28.7 working days at the start of the year to 6.4 working days
Note
Preterm birth, jaundice treated under blue light, newborn pneumonia — these are common reasons newborns are hospitalized, easily topping 10,000 yuan, and insured versus uninsured makes a big difference. Localities differ on "within how many days of birth the baby must enroll for coverage to start from the day of birth." For the exact rule, go by what the local medical insurance department says. The easiest move is to call 12393 before discharge and ask
Sources (1 reference)
Chinese Government Portal (2024). State Council policy briefing on improving the long-term mechanism for basic medical insurance enrollment. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/202409/content_6973567.htm
15

Register the birth at the local police station within one month of the baby's birth

Grade AValue: FairBasis: freedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: small

The law allows one month — not "whenever you get around to it." Household registration gates everything downstream: vaccinations, kindergarten, school, and the ID card. The longer you drag it out, the more documents you'll owe.

Cost
Free. One trip to the police station's household registration window
Benefit
Article 7 of the Household Registration Regulations: "Within one month of an infant's birth, the head of the household, a relative, the person raising the infant, or a neighbor shall declare the birth registration to the household registration authority where the infant habitually resides." That is a deadline set by law, not a suggestion. Household registration is the prerequisite for: vaccinations, kindergarten, school, and the ID card. The longer you delay, the more supplementary documents you'll need
Note
Bring all of these: the Medical Certificate of Birth, both parents' ID cards and household registration booklet, and the marriage certificate. Registering under the father or under the mother is your choice, but the two places' policies differ — school district and insurance enrollment location are both affected. Decide before you go; changing it later is a hassle. Children born outside marriage can likewise be registered
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (1958). Household Registration Regulations of the People's Republic of China (Article 7). http://www.gd.gov.cn/zwgk/wjk/zcfgk/content/post_2531969.html (reposted by the People's Government of Guangdong Province)
16

Don't skip the 42-day postpartum checkup — it doubles as postpartum depression screening

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

This checkup is free and includes a complete blood count, a routine vaginal discharge test, and one postpartum depression screen. Serious problems can arise any time within a year after birth — don't assume you're safe once the first month is over.

Cost
Free, part of basic public health services. Takes half a day. The hard part: fresh out of the first month, you don't feel like moving
Benefit
Under the maternal health management services of the National Basic Public Health Service Specifications (Third Edition), postpartum there is 1 home visit and 1 health check at 42 days. Per the published local service list, this visit includes lab work (complete blood count, routine vaginal discharge) and 1 postpartum depression screen. Serious complications can occur any time within a year after birth. On the "go to the hospital now" list in item 7, "thoughts of harming yourself or the baby," "vaginal bleeding or abnormal discharge after birth," and "severe swelling and pain in one limb" all fall within the postpartum period
Note
Postpartum depression is not being dramatic, and a family member's "cheer up" will not fix it. There are dedicated screening questionnaires, there is treatment, and recovery is possible. For handling suicidal thoughts, see Section 1. For the legal way out when a baby truly cannot be raised, see Section 9, item 20. This checkup also looks at how the wound is healing, how the uterus is recovering, and how the pelvic floor is doing. Contraception is discussed at this visit too: no period after birth does not mean no pregnancy
Sources (2 references)
National Health and Family Planning Commission (2017). National Basic Public Health Service Specifications (Third Edition). https://www.nhc.gov.cn/ewebeditor/uploadfile/2017/04/201704…; Jingjiang Municipal People's Government. National Basic Public Health Service Program — Maternal Health Management Services (published local service list). https://www.jingjiang.gov.cn/xxgk/zdlyxxgk/wsjk/art/2023/ar…

28. Don't Wreck Your Body for Your Looks

9 items

This section is about the things people do to their body in order to change how it looks: starving themselves, taking pills, getting injections, going under the knife. These decisions are usually made after comparing yourself with others, yet the cost lands entirely on you, and a substantial share of the damage cannot be undone. This section passes no judgment on what anyone wants to turn themselves into — that is each person's own business. For the same goal, you can go to someone who offers 'a prescription, qualifications, and follow-up visits', or you can go the route of 'online shopping, beauty salons, upping the dose yourself'; this section only compares how much the risks differ between the two. The accounting mainly looks at what actually happens to the body — blindness, hospitalization, death. The two medical-cosmetology items also touch on criminal liability for unlicensed medical practice.

1

Don't control weight with crash diets, fasting, or vomiting on purpose; if you want to lose, lose on the exercise side of the ledger

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

People with anorexia nervosa are about 5.9 times as likely to die as their peers — 5.1 deaths per 1,000 people followed for a year, and one in five of those deaths is suicide. The gateway to it is dieting: in a three-year follow-up of students at 44 secondary schools, severely dieting girls were 18 times as likely to develop an eating disorder as non-dieters. If you want to control your weight, exercise more; don't eat so little that you go hungry.

Cost
Costs nothing. You actually save the money you would have spent on weight-loss products.
Benefit
Pooled from 36 studies. The anorexia nervosa group was followed for a cumulative 166,642 person-years (the number of years each person was followed, added up). Their standardized mortality ratio was 5.86, meaning a probability of death about 5.9 times that of their peers. That is 5.1 deaths per 1,000 person-years — 5.1 deaths among 1,000 people followed for a year. About 1/5 of the deaths were suicide. For bulimia the standardized mortality ratio was 1.93, and for other eating disorders 1.92 — each about 1.9 times their peers. Another study was done at 44 secondary schools in Victoria, Australia, following 14–15-year-olds for 3 years, with 6 waves of surveys of the same students over the three years. New eating disorders among girls ran at 21.8 per 1,000 person-years — 21.8 new cases for every 1,000 girls followed for a year. Severely dieting girls had 18 times the risk of developing one as non-dieters, and moderate dieters 5 times. After adjusting for prior dieting and psychiatric symptoms — subtracting out the effects of 'having dieted before' and 'already having psychiatric symptoms' — BMI (a measure of fatness or thinness computed as weight divided by height squared), exercise, and sex no longer predicted new eating disorders. The authors' conclusion: 'controlling weight in adolescents through exercise rather than food restriction appears to carry a lower risk of eating disorders.'
Note
'Severe dieting' here means keeping what you eat far below what your body needs over the long run — not skipping a meal or giving up late-night snacks. If you are already making yourself vomit, blaming yourself after bingeing, or weighing yourself over and over and unable to stop, see a psychiatrist or the clinical psychology department of a general hospital. This is an illness with standard treatments; it is not a matter of willpower. For the relationship between BMI and mortality, see Section 2, item 32; that item is about long-term weight ranges, not weight-loss methods.
Sources (2 references)
Arcelus J et al. (2011). Mortality rates in patients with anorexia nervosa and other eating disorders. A meta-analysis of 36 studies. Arch Gen Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1001/archgenpsychiatry.2011.74; Patton GC et al. (1999). Onset of adolescent eating disorders: population based cohort study over 3 years. BMJ. https://doi.org/10.1136/bmj.318.7186.765
2

Before injections, thread implants, or surgery, check two things: whether the facility's license includes 'medical cosmetology', and whether the person operating is a qualified attending physician in charge

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Anything involving needles, scalpels, or medical devices that breaks the skin or enters the body counts as medical care. It can only be done at a facility whose license lists 'medical cosmetology', and the person operating must be a registered licensed physician. Doing it in a beauty salon, a studio, or a hotel room is practicing medicine without a license. The person operating can get up to 3 years for serious cases, 3 to 10 years for injuring someone, and over 10 years if someone dies.

Cost
Costs nothing. Checking these two credentials takes only a few minutes. The facility should hang its Medical Institution Practice License in the lobby. A doctor's credentials can be verified through the health authority's licensed-physician lookup.
Benefit
Article 2 of the Administrative Measures for Medical Cosmetology Services defines medical cosmetology. The original text: 'the repair and reshaping of a person's appearance and the form of various parts of the body using surgery, drugs, medical devices, and other traumatic or invasive medical techniques.' Put plainly: anything that breaks the skin, inserts a needle, or enters the body counts as medical care. Articles 8 and 24 require first obtaining the Medical Institution Practice License and having the medical cosmetology specialty approved by the registration authority before offering such services. If the license does not list 'medical cosmetology', it cannot be done. Article 11 requires the attending physician in charge (the doctor doing the procedure) to hold a licensed-physician qualification and be registered. Cosmetic surgery requires more than 6 years of relevant clinical experience, cosmetic dentistry more than 5 years, and cosmetic traditional Chinese medicine and cosmetic dermatology more than 3 years each. Article 20 requires written disclosure of the indications, contraindications (which situations are suitable and which are not), medical risks, and precautions before the procedure, and signed consent. Article 336 of the Criminal Law governs unlicensed medical practice — someone without a physician's practicing qualification giving injections, performing surgery, or treating patients. In serious cases: up to 3 years of fixed-term imprisonment, criminal detention, or public surveillance, with a fine imposed or imposed alone. Where it seriously harms the patient's health: 3 to 10 years of fixed-term imprisonment plus a fine. Where it causes the patient's death: 10 or more years of fixed-term imprisonment plus a fine.
Note
Article 16 of the same Measures also provides that medical cosmetology procedures may only be performed inside cosmetic medical institutions, or at hospitals and clinics that have a medical cosmetology department. So injections at your home or procedures done privately in a studio fail on the location alone. Article 20 states that minors — people not yet able to decide such matters for themselves — must have guardian consent, with a parent's signature, for medical cosmetology. Facials, massage, and manicures are non-medical beauty services and are not governed by these rules. But the moment a needle or a scalpel is involved, it counts as medical cosmetology.
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of Health (2002). Administrative Measures for Medical Cosmetology Services (MoH Order No. 19; Articles 2, 8, 11, 16, 20, 24). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2003/content_62198.htm; National People's Congress (1997). Criminal Law (Article 336). https://www.spp.gov.cn/spp/fl/201802/t20180206_364975.shtml
3

For facial fillers, avoid the nose bridge, between the brows, and the forehead — and never cut corners with unlicensed injections

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Among people blinded by filler injections, more than half had the injection in the nose, followed by the area between the brows, the forehead, and the smile lines; over 80% involved hyaluronic acid. Only 20% of those blinded fully recovered their vision, a bit over 10% partially recovered, and nearly 20% also suffered brain damage. No rescue method currently works reliably, so the only option is to avoid these sites in advance.

Cost
Costs nothing. Just choose a different injection site, or skip the procedure.
Benefit
A pooled count of cases reported in journals worldwide. From January 2015 to September 2018 there were 48 new cases of partial or complete vision loss after filler injection. The site with the most incidents was the nose, at 56.3%. Next came the glabella (between the brows) at 27.1%, the forehead at 18.8%, and the nasolabial fold (the smile line) at 14.6%. In 81.3% of cases the filler was hyaluronic acid. 43.8% had skin changes. 18.8% had central nervous system complications (something went wrong in the brain). 10 cases (20.8%) fully recovered vision, 8 (16.7%) partially recovered, and the rest did not. The authors' conclusion: management differed widely across providers, and no treatment has been proven to work consistently.
Note
These figures are a case-by-case count of what journals have reported. They contain only the number of people harmed, not the total number of injections, so you cannot calculate 'the probability of going blind from one shot' — only which sites cause the most incidents and that the damage is mostly irreversible afterwards. That is also why the evidence is graded B. The risk-lowering practices at proper facilities are already routine: map out the blood vessels under the injection site first, use a blunt cannula instead of a sharp needle, inject small amounts while withdrawing, and have hyaluronidase ready beforehand. Every one of these requires a trained doctor doing the procedure — which is also the reason not to use unlicensed channels. Before any procedure, run the checks in item 2 of this section (facility license and attending physician).
Sources (1 reference)
Beleznay K et al. (2019). Update on Avoiding and Treating Blindness From Fillers: A Recent Review of the World Literature. Aesthet Surg J. https://doi.org/10.1093/asj/sjz053
4

Don't buy weight-loss pills, diet coffee, slimming candies, or enzyme plums that promise 'fast slimming'

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The adulterant most often detected in these products is sibutramine — once a weight-loss drug, pulled from the market in China in 2010. Overweight people with heart disease or diabetes who took it for over three years had roughly 30% more non-fatal heart attacks and about 36% more strokes. The extra weight lost was only 1.7 kg. By the time a spot test catches it, you have already swallowed it.

Cost
Costs nothing; you save the money you would have spent on these products. The hard part is accepting that there is no such thing as 'dropping a few kilos in a week'.
Benefit
The SCOUT trial enrolled 9,804 people, all over 55, overweight or obese, and with cardiovascular disease or type 2 diabetes. They were randomly assigned to take the drug or not, and treated for an average of 3.4 years. The primary endpoint was a pre-specified list of bad events: non-fatal heart attack, non-fatal stroke, resuscitation after cardiac arrest, and cardiovascular death. The rate of these events was 11.4% vs 10.0%. HR 1.16 (95% CI 1.03–1.31, P=0.02) — the chance of an event was about 16% higher for those on the drug. The true value likely falls between 3% and 31% higher. Non-fatal heart attack: 4.1% vs 3.2%, HR 1.28 (1.04–1.57), about 30% higher. Non-fatal stroke: 2.6% vs 1.9%, HR 1.36 (1.04–1.77), about 36% higher. Cardiovascular death and all-cause death (death from any cause combined) were not increased. After randomization, the sibutramine group lost an average of 1.7 kg more. Based on its safety assessment, the former State Food and Drug Administration concluded that 'the risks of the weight-loss treatment outweigh the benefits', and in October 2010 notified an end to the production, sale, and use of sibutramine preparations and their active ingredient. Both sibutramine and phenolphthalein are banned additives in food, health food included.
Note
SCOUT enrolled high-risk people who already had heart disease or diabetes. The trial did not prove that healthy young people come to harm the same way. But precisely because you cannot tell who is high-risk, the regulator simply pulled it from the market. Another ingredient commonly snuck in is phenolphthalein, originally a laxative; taken long-term in quantity it disrupts the body's electrolytes and can trigger arrhythmias.
