How to judge: legitimate weight-loss drugs are prescription drugs with an approval number you can look up at pharmacies and hospitals. Anything sold under the banner of 'coffee', 'candy', 'plums', or 'meal replacement' that also promises a drop of a few kilos a week should, by definition, have no drug effect — if it does have an effect, something has been added. The original of SFDA Office Document [2010] No. 432 is on the national drug regulator's website, but the page kept returning a 412 error on this machine, so a provincial regulator's page restating it is cited instead. The two phrases 'risks outweigh the benefits' and 'production, sale, and use stopped in October 2010' can be verified verbatim there.
Sources (2 references)
James WPT et al. (2010). Effect of sibutramine on cardiovascular outcomes in overweight and obese subjects. NEJM. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1003114; Tianjin Municipal Commission of Market Regulation. Guard against the illegal addition of 'sibutramine hydrochloride' and 'phenolphthalein' in some foods. https://scjg.tj.gov.cn/tjsscjdglwyh_52651/hdpt/cjwtyxfts/20…
5

Don't use anabolic steroids ('muscle-building shots', 'oral pills') to gain muscle

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Men who tested positive for doping at gyms had 3 times the mortality risk of their peers and more than double the annual number of hospital visits. Acne, enlarged male breasts, and erectile dysfunction each hit at least 1 in 10 users. These drugs are prescription-only in China; any channel that can sell them to you is already breaking the law.

Cost
Costs nothing, and saves the drug money. The hard part is accepting that muscle grows slowly.
Benefit
A Danish register study matched each user with controls of the same age. The users were 545 men who tested positive for androgenic steroids in gym doping tests between 2006-01-03 and 2018-03-01, matched with 5,450 controls. A second analysis repeated the comparison with 644 men who refused testing and 6,440 controls. Results: users died at 3 times the rate of controls, HR 3.0 (95% CI 1.3–7.0), with the true multiple likely between 1.3 and 7. The median number of hospitalizations or clinic visits per year was 0.81 vs 0.36 (P<0.0001). The median is the value with half the people above it and half below. This P value means the difference is almost certainly not chance. Acne, enlarged male breasts, and erectile dysfunction each affected more than 10% of users — at least 1 in 10 — all clearly higher than controls (P<0.0001). The replication cohort showed the same. Article 7 of the Anti-Doping Regulations: the state strictly manages the prohibited substances listed in the doping catalogue, and no unit or individual may illegally produce, sell, or import or export them. The same regulations place anabolic agents and peptide hormones under prescription-drug management — buyable only with a doctor's prescription; 'anabolic agents' is the term the regulations use for this class of drugs.
Note
Caveat: this is a study that tracked a group of people and observed outcomes, not a randomized trial. Users may simply be bigger risk-takers in other ways too, so the 3-fold figure cannot be pinned entirely on the drugs. The true multiple could be as low as 1.3 or as high as 7.0 — a wide range. But 'acne, enlarged male breasts, and erectile dysfunction each affecting more than one in ten users' is a side effect visible to the eye, less susceptible to that bias. In the regulations these drugs are written as 'anabolic agents'; that is the phrase to watch for. Ordinary protein powder and creatine are not covered by this item. The trap is products 'claiming especially fast muscle gains' that may contain hidden ingredients. Use the same test as for weight-loss products (item 4 — don't buy weight-loss drugs that promise fast slimming): legitimate drugs are prescription-only with a checkable approval number. Anything sold as a 'muscle-gainer powder' or a 'supplement' that promises visible results in weeks — if it truly works, something has been added.
Sources (2 references)
Horwitz H et al. (2019). Health consequences of androgenic anabolic steroid use. J Intern Med. https://doi.org/10.1111/joim.12850; State Council (2004). Anti-Doping Regulations (State Council Order No. 398; Articles 7 and 9). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2004/content_63129.htm
6

If you need weight-loss medication, get a prescription at a hospital — don't buy from online shops that ship without one

Grade BValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Prescription drugs must be sold against a prescription, and selling them online requires a genuine prescription and real-name verification. A shop that does no consultation, asks for no prescription, and ships as soon as you order is either not selling what it claims, or is violating the rules. If something goes wrong, no one answers for your dosage and contraindications. A few dozen yuan for one outpatient visit buys you a doctor to clear this hurdle for you.

Cost
One outpatient registration plus the trip there and back: a few dozen yuan and half a day.
Benefit
The Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Drug Trading and Use Quality require drug retailers to observe the prescription-drug/over-the-counter classification system — the system that splits drugs into two classes, one buyable only with a doctor's prescription and one buyable freely. Pharmacies must sell prescription drugs against a prescription as required, and keep prescriptions on file for no less than five years. When the pharmacist or other pharmaceutical professional is not on duty, a notice must be posted, and no prescription drug may be sold without their review. Prescription drugs may not be sold on open shelves — they cannot sit on a rack for customers to grab themselves. Article 9 of the Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Drug Sales: anyone selling prescription drugs to individuals online must ensure the prescription is genuine and reliable and implement real-name registration. Article 10 requires prominently displayed risk warnings under every drug's display page. Before the prescription passes review, the package insert must not be shown and no purchasing service may be offered — until the prescription has been vetted, the page should not even offer a buy button. Article 8: drugs under special state control may not be sold online. These include vaccines, blood products, narcotic drugs, psychotropic drugs, medically toxic drugs, radioactive drugs, and drug-type precursor chemicals.
Note
The legal texts can be verified verbatim, but no one has quantified how much less goes wrong when you take medication by prescription rather than buying it yourself, so this is graded B for 'hard to quantify'. The steroids and sex hormones in items 5 and 7 of this section follow the same rules. If you truly reach the point of needing medication to lose weight, a doctor will first look at your BMI, whether you have other conditions, and whether there are reasons you cannot take the drugs, then decide whether to prescribe and which one. That judgment is not something you can buy.
Sources (2 references)
State Administration for Market Regulation (2023). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Drug Trading and Use Quality (SAMR Order No. 84). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2023/issue_10846/202311/content_…; State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Drug Sales (SAMR Order No. 58; Articles 8 through 10). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5717002.htm
7

Use sex-hormone medications only with a doctor's prescription and regular follow-ups — never buy online or increase the dose on your own

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

This item does not debate whether to use them, only how. Transgender women taking estrogen develop blood clots in their veins noticeably more often than their peers: about 4 extra cases per 1,000 people over two years, about 17 extra over eight years. That risk needs regular follow-ups to watch over it; buy the drugs online and adjust your own dose, and no one is checking for you.

Cost
Regular appointments plus blood-test follow-ups: a few hundred yuan a year, taking up a few half-days.
Benefit
The researchers followed a cohort through the electronic records of the Kaiser Permanente health system: 2,842 transgender women and 2,118 transgender men, followed an average of 4.0 and 3.6 years. Each person was matched on birth year, race, clinic site, and enrollment date with roughly 10 times as many cisgender controls — 48,686 cisgender men and 48,775 cisgender women in total. Transgender women had more venous thromboembolism (blood clots forming in a vessel and blocking it) than controls. Versus cisgender men: 4.1 cases per 1,000 people at 2 years (95% CI 1.6–6.7), and 16.7 at 8 years (6.4–27.5). In headcounts: 4.1 extra cases per 1,000 people over two years, 16.7 extra over eight. Versus cisgender women the two figures were 3.4 (1.1–5.6) and 13.7 (4.1–22.7). Ischemic stroke (the blockage type of stroke) and myocardial infarction were broadly similar across groups overall. But among transgender women who began hormone therapy during the follow-up period, the differences in venous thrombosis and ischemic stroke were more pronounced. The evidence for transgender men was insufficient to draw conclusions. The authors' conclusion: 'these results may suggest a need for long-term vigilance for the vascular side effects of estrogen in transgender hormone therapy.'
Note
The researchers themselves spelled out this study's weakness: they could not see how many people bought drugs outside the health system, so the line between 'on hormones' and 'not on hormones' was never clean to begin with — one more reason to keep use inside proper follow-up. The study only looked at whether blood vessels came to harm; it does not answer whether hormone therapy should be used or what its benefits are — that is a separate body of evidence. The same applies wherever sex hormones are used, including contraceptives, menopausal hormone therapy, and testosterone replacement. Anyone who buys online, adjusts doses according to internet posts, and never gets clot, liver, or kidney markers checked carries risk in exactly the 'no one is watching' stretch, regardless of why they take the hormones. The legitimate route in China is the endocrinology department or the relevant specialty of a proper medical facility, for assessment, prescription, and follow-up.
Sources (2 references)
Getahun D et al. (2018). Cross-sex Hormones and Acute Cardiovascular Events in Transgender Persons: A Cohort Study. Ann Intern Med. https://doi.org/10.7326/M17-2785; State Administration for Market Regulation (2022). Measures for the Supervision and Administration of Online Drug Sales (SAMR Order No. 58; Article 9). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2022/content_5717002.htm
8

If 'feeling ugly' has reached the level of constant mirror-checking and constant urges to fix something, get a body-image assessment before discussing surgery

Grade BValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

About 15% of people seeking plastic surgery have body dysmorphic disorder — magnifying a flaw others can barely see until it disrupts their life. Among those seeking cosmetic treatment in dermatology it is about 13%; in both settings more than 70% are women. Such people finish one area and then fixate on the next; surgery does not solve it. Book one appointment to find out whether this is you, before deciding whether to have surgery.

Cost
One appointment in psychiatry or clinical psychology: a few dozen yuan. The hard part is making that visit before booking surgery.
Benefit
33 studies were systematically assembled and pooled. Among plastic surgery attendees, the prevalence of body dysmorphic disorder (a flaw others can barely see, magnified until it disrupts life) was 15.04%, with individual studies ranging from 2.21% to 56.67%. In headcounts: about 15 in every 100 people seeking plastic surgery qualify, ranging from 2 to 57 across individual studies. Their average age was 34.54±12.41 years (the second number is the spread around it), and 74.38% were women. Among dermatology attendees it was 12.65%, with individual studies ranging from 4.52% to 35.16%, average age 27.79±9.03 years, 76.09% women. The authors recommend that plastic surgeons and dermatologists proactively assess for it, identify the high-risk individuals, and arrange for several departments to manage them together.
Note
The proportions measured by individual studies range enormously, from 2.21% all the way to 56.67%, because the questionnaires and the populations surveyed all differ. So the only safe reading is 'this proportion is not low and is worth screening for once' — do not treat 15.04% as an exact figure, which is also why this is graded B. The vast majority of people seeking cosmetic procedures have no psychological problem. This item targets the small group for whom it is 'repetitive, persistent, and already affecting work and social life'; surgery does not fix their problem. Signs to look for: spending long stretches of the day checking or covering up one body part, avoiding social contact or photos because of it, and moving on to fixate on the next area once one is done.
Sources (1 reference)
Ribeiro RVE (2017). Prevalence of Body Dysmorphic Disorder in Plastic Surgery and Dermatology Patients: A Systematic Review with Meta-Analysis. Aesthetic Plast Surg. https://doi.org/10.1007/s00266-017-0869-0
9

For teeth straightening, see an orthodontically qualified doctor for in-person checks and regular visits — don't buy aligners online and wear them at home

Grade CValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: small

Clear aligners are Class II medical devices in China, and their instructions require wearing them under the guidance of a doctor qualified in orthodontics, with regular follow-up visits. The US drug regulator says it has never approved aligners sold directly to individuals without a dentist's prescription. Without in-person checks, you risk a misaligned bite, teeth moving to the wrong places, pain, even tooth loss.

Cost
More than buying online: registration and follow-up fees, plus a trip to the clinic every so often. The hard part is that treatment often runs one to two years, and you have to keep up the visits.
Benefit
The Center for Medical Device Evaluation of China's national drug regulator said in its 2022 Guiding Principles for the Registration Review of Clear Aligners that these aligners are 'Class II' devices. It requires the instructions to state that 'wearing during treatment must be under the guidance of a physician professionally qualified in orthodontics', and to include 'requirements on eating, tooth-brushing, and regular follow-up visits'. Product names 'should not contain vacuous, hypothetical conceptual names such as "invisible"'. The US Food and Drug Administration (FDA) puts it this way: 'The FDA has not authorized clear aligners that are sold directly to consumers without a prescription and supervision by a dentist or orthodontist' — meaning it has not approved a single clear aligner sold directly to individuals without a dentist's prescription and supervision. The FDA also says: 'In-person examination by a dentist or orthodontist can help lower the risks of uneven bite, unintended tooth movement, pain, and tooth loss' — an in-person dental examination lowers the risks of a misaligned bite, shifted teeth, pain, and tooth loss. Once you start wearing them, only regular in-person visits can confirm the teeth are moving safely and on plan. Both are regulatory documents; neither gives a rate of incidents.
Note
The benefit is rated small because no incident rate could be found; the judgment rests on consequences alone. No risk advisory from China's drug or health authorities specifically about 'buying aligners online and wearing them at home' could be located, so this item leans mainly on the registration requirements and the FDA's statements. Orthodontics is medical care. For cosmetic-type dental straightening, the facility's license must include the corresponding specialty and the doctor doing the work must hold the qualifications — see item 2 of this section (facility license, attending physician) for how to check. A 2023 oral-health notice from four departments also named unlicensed facilities and the hiring of non-medical staff to treat teeth as conduct to be severely punished. Orthodontics is not covered by medical insurance — see Section 24, item 12 (ask for an all-in price before getting a dental implant).
Sources (3 references)
Center for Medical Device Evaluation, National Medical Products Administration (2022). Guiding Principles for the Registration Review of Clear Aligners (No. 41 of 2022). https://www.cmde.org.cn/flfg/zdyz/zdyzwbk/20230103095116100…; General Office of the National Health Commission et al. (2023). Notice on Further Advancing Oral Healthcare Services and Their Support and Management (Guo Wei Ban Yi Zheng Fa [2023] No. 11; Article 5). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202309/content_6903786…; U.S. Food and Drug Administration (2026). Clear Dental Aligners (page updated September 9, 2026). https://www.fda.gov/medical-devices/dental-devices/clear-de…

29. After a Major Blow

13 items

A loved one dies, you are told you have a serious illness, you lose your job, your marriage ends. These events share one feature in the research: it is not just mood that suffers, but the body. The highest-risk stretch is concentrated in the first few weeks to the first year. This section does not cover how to 'move on'; it covers which things in that stretch must have someone watching over them, which decisions must be pushed back, and when to book a doctor's appointment. Most items here count probabilities of death. The four items about spending and benefits count money: don't pay for grief counseling straight away (item 9), call 12356 and book a psychological outpatient clinic (item 11), push irreversible big decisions to later (item 12), and don't use death as a way to repay debts (item 13). The two kinds of numbers are not interchangeable. If you have no family and no friends to turn to, see item 6 for how to make 'find someone to watch over you' concrete. For the paperwork, the body, and the money to claim at the time of a loved one's death, see Section 25. For guardianship and wills for elderly people while they are alive, see Section 17. For what you can claim when unemployed, see Section 7. For exercise and light when feeling low, see Sections 3 and 22. When having suicidal thoughts, call 12356 first — see Section 1, item 25; the time scale of such urges, Section 1, item 32; the aftereffects for those rescued, Section 1, item 33. None of these are repeated here.

1

In the first days after a loved one passes, don't stay alone; if you have heart disease, hypertension, or diabetes, keep taking your medication, and call 120 for crushing chest pain

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In the first day after a loved one's death, the probability of a heart attack is 21.1 times the usual level, falling day by day afterwards. For people aged 60 to 89, heart attack or stroke roughly doubles within 30 days of a partner's death, then falls back after a month. If you already have cardiovascular disease, do not stop your medication during these days. Crushing chest pain, struggling to breathe, or weakness on one side of the body — call 120 immediately.

Cost
Costs nothing. Don't stay alone during these days, and keep taking your medication as usual.
Benefit
1,985 acute heart attack patients, comparing different time windows before and after the event within the same person. Of them, 270 (13.6%) had lost someone significant in the 6 months before onset, and 19 had lost someone within the 1 day before the heart attack. Within 24 hours after a significant person's death, the rate of acute heart attack was 21.1 times higher (95% CI 13.1–34.1; the true multiple is likely between 13 and 34). It declined day by day thereafter. In headcounts: among people with a 10-year heart attack risk of 5%, 1 extra case for every 1,394 people newly bereaved; at 20% risk, 1 extra case for every 320. Another study in the UK compared 30,447 people aged 60 to 89 who had lost a spouse with 83,588 controls of otherwise similar profile. Within 30 days of widowhood, heart attack or stroke occurred in 50 on the bereaved side (0.16%) versus 67 on the control side (0.08%). IRR 2.20 (1.52–3.15) — the probability of an event was about 2.2 times that of the controls. Heart attack: 2.14 (1.20–3.81), about 2.1 times. Stroke: 2.40 (1.22–4.71), about 2.4 times. The elevation weakened after 30 days. The first 90 days also covered two other conditions: non-heart-attack acute coronary syndrome (an acute problem with the heart's blood supply that falls short of a heart attack), IRR 2.20 (1.12–4.29), and pulmonary embolism (a clot blocking a vessel in the lungs), IRR 2.37 (1.18–4.75).
Note
Hand the pill box to someone else to manage; don't rely on your own memory. Don't drive long distances during these days. Don't drink to get through it — the accounting for alcohol is in Section 2. How to recognize a heart attack or stroke and how to call for a ride: Section 13. Both are retrospective population-data studies and cannot separate how many people were going to fall ill anyway. But the two point in the same direction over the same time window. If there is no one to hand the pill box to and you are bound to be alone in the house these days, see item 6 of this section.
Sources (2 references)
Mostofsky E, et al. (2012). Risk of acute myocardial infarction after the death of a significant person in one's life: the Determinants of Myocardial Infarction Onset Study. Circulation. https://doi.org/10.1161/CIRCULATIONAHA.111.061770; Carey IM, et al. (2014). Increased risk of acute cardiovascular events after partner bereavement: a matched cohort study. JAMA Internal Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamainternmed.2013.14558
2

In the week you're told a serious diagnosis, don't collect the report alone, and put off decisions beyond treatment

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

In the first week after a cancer diagnosis, the probability of suicide is 12.6 times that of people without the diagnosis, and the probability of dying from cardiovascular disease is 5.6 times. By the end of the first year, suicide risk falls to 3.1 times — the harder the cancer is to treat, the more pronounced. So bring someone with you on the day you collect the report, and don't be alone at home. Resigning, selling the house — leave such things for the next clinic visit.

Cost
Costs nothing. Find someone to accompany you to collect the report. Push the big decisions beyond treatment back a few days.
Benefit
Sweden's national registers tracked over 6.07 million people (6,073,240) from 1991 to 2006. Compared with people without a cancer diagnosis, the relative risk of suicide in the first week after diagnosis was 12.6 (95% CI 8.6–17.8) — about 12.6 times, with the true multiple likely between 8.6 and 17.8. The incidence that week was 2.50 per 1,000 person-years, i.e. 2.5 cases among 1,000 people followed for a year. By the first year it fell to 3.1 (2.7–3.5; 0.60 per 1,000 person-years), about 3.1 times. Cardiovascular death in the first week: 5.6 (5.2–5.9; 116.80 per 1,000 person-years), about 5.6 times. The first 4 weeks: 3.3 (3.1–3.4; 65.81 per 1,000 person-years). The elevation falls back quickly within the first year after diagnosis. The harder the cancer is to treat and the lower the odds of survival, the sharper the rise. Comparing the same patients across different time windows gives the same conclusion.
Note
These are data for cancer patients; for other serious diagnoses there is no comparably strong source. The number of people actually harmed is small: a first-week suicide rate of 2.50 per 1,000 person-years, i.e. 2.5 cases among 1,000 people followed for a year. The point of writing it out is not to frighten but to show that in the first days after learning the news, someone should be at your side. For long-term management, reimbursement, and follow-ups after diagnosis, see Sections 16 and 24. If you cannot find anyone to go with you, see item 6 of this section (substitute 'that person' with neighbors and community lists).
Sources (1 reference)
Fang F, et al. (2012). Suicide and cardiovascular death after a cancer diagnosis. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1110307
3

After losing your job, first lock in a routine, your medical insurance, and a job-search rhythm — don't stay home all day

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

People who lose their jobs are about 60% more likely to die afterwards than people in work; the effect is clearer for men and for the not-yet-old, and highest in the first ten years. Strip out the effects of smoking and drinking and the increase shrinks by about a quarter — the part you can control yourself. First, register as unemployed and claim unemployment insurance; while you receive it, your medical insurance is paid on your behalf by the unemployment insurance fund.

Cost
Costs nothing. First register as unemployed and claim unemployment insurance, then put the job search on a fixed schedule. The hard part is getting up on time when no one is pushing you.
Benefit
Pooled: 42 studies, 235 death risk estimates, over 20 million people. After equalizing for age and other conditions, the average HR for death from all causes combined among the unemployed was 1.63 — about 60% higher than people in work. Higher for men than for women. The effect was pronounced for people in the early and middle stages of their careers, smaller in the late stage. Risk was highest in the first 10 years of follow-up and declined thereafter. In the subset of studies that also counted health behaviors such as smoking and drinking, the average HR was 24% lower — the calculated increase shrank by about a quarter.
Note
This is a retrospective population-data study and cannot untangle the direction of cause: people in worse health to begin with are also more likely to lose jobs. But 'the effect is 24% lower once the lifestyle component is adjusted away' points to something you can work on. For what you can claim while unemployed, where to claim it, and how to keep social insurance going, see Section 7. For how much compensation you are owed when dismissed and why not to sign a 'voluntary resignation', see Section 19.
Sources (1 reference)
Roelfs DJ, et al. (2011). Losing life and livelihood: a systematic review and meta-analysis of unemployment and all-cause mortality. Social Science & Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.socscimed.2011.01.005
4

If a loved one died by suicide, accident, or violence, don't expect to tough it out — actively seek professional help

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

People whose spouse died by suicide are about 80% (men) and 70% (women) more likely than the general population to be diagnosed with a mental disorder within five years. Compared with people whose spouse died of other causes, they are also 70% to 100% more likely. The suicide-bereaved more often feel shunned by others and feel shame. That is precisely the reason to go find people rather than wait to get better on your own.

Cost
Calling 12356 costs nothing. To see a doctor, a psychological outpatient visit costs the same as an ordinary appointment. The hard part is opening up and asking for help yourself.
Benefit
Denmark's national registers tracked 6.7 million adults from 1980 to 2014, totaling over 136 million person-years (everyone's follow-up years added together). For people widowed by a spouse's suicide, the risk of a newly diagnosed mental disorder within 5 years versus the general population: IRR 1.8 for men (95% CI 1.6–2.0), about 80% higher. Women: 1.7 (1.6–1.8), about 70% higher. Compared with people widowed by other causes of death: IRR 1.7 for men (1.5–1.9) and 2.0 for women (1.9–2.2) — 70% to 100% higher. This group also had higher rates of suicidal behavior, death, and needing municipal assistance. Physical illnesses such as liver cirrhosis and sleep disorders were likewise elevated. A separate review organized 57 studies one by one, without pooling numbers. Bereavement by suicide is associated with the following four things. First, raised suicide risk in partners. Second, raised risk of psychiatric admission for parents after a child's suicide. Third, raised suicide risk for mothers after an adult child's suicide. Fourth, raised depression risk for children after a parent's suicide. Compared with people bereaved by other violent deaths, the suicide-bereaved more often report being shunned by others and feeling shame.
Note
Sudden, violent death means accidents, homicide, and disasters. After such deaths, the rates of post-traumatic stress disorder, depression, and stuck grief are all higher than after deaths from illness, and recovery is slower. For what to do when you have suicidal thoughts yourself, see Section 1, item 25.
Sources (3 references)
Erlangsen A, et al. (2017). Association Between Spousal Suicide and Mental, Physical, and Social Health Outcomes: A Longitudinal and Nationwide Register-Based Study. JAMA Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapsychiatry.2017.0226; Pitman A, et al. (2014). Effects of suicide bereavement on mental health and suicide risk. The Lancet Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2215-0366(14)70224-X; Kristensen P et al. (2012). Bereavement and mental health after sudden and violent losses: a review. Psychiatry. https://doi.org/10.1521/psyc.2012.75.1.76 (the review cited in the Note)
5

In the first six months of widowhood, hand meals, sleep, chronic-disease medication, and checkups to one fixed person to watch over

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

In the first six months of widowhood, the probability of dying in the same period is about 40% higher than for the non-bereaved; after six months it falls to about 15% higher. For men it is about 23% higher; for women the increase is small enough that it may be mere chance. This gap is not something you can think your way past. What should be done is to put the medication, the meals, and the checkups in the hands of one specific person, rather than expecting yourself to remember.

Cost
Costs nothing. Find one specific person — a child, a sibling, or a friend — and have them visit or call on a regular schedule. The hard part is opening your mouth and entrusting this to someone.
Benefit
Pooled: 15 studies that registered people first and then followed them forward, 2,263,888 people in total. Death RR within 6 months of widowhood: 1.41 (95% CI 1.26–1.57) — the probability of dying in the same period was about 40% higher than for the non-bereaved. After 6 months: 1.14 (1.10–1.18), down to about 15% higher. Men: RR 1.23 (1.18–1.28), about 23% higher. Women: 1.04 (1.00–1.08, not statistically significant — this small gap may be chance). No clear difference between those under 65 and those 65 and over. Another analysis pooled 123 papers, 1,377 risk estimates, and over 500 million people. After adjusting away differences in conditions, HR 1.23 (1.19–1.28) — about 23% higher overall, again higher for men than for women. Men: 1.27 (1.19–1.35), 27% higher. Women: 1.15 (1.08–1.22), 15% higher.
Note
This is a retrospective population-data study; other factors get mixed in and cannot be fully removed. Couples' lifestyles and illnesses are similar to begin with. But the pattern 'the first six months are much worse than afterwards' holds in two independent pooled analyses alike, and deserves to be treated as a care window. Men are at higher risk and also ask for help less often. For households with a widowed elder, sort out accounts, guardianship, and wills together per Section 17. If no such person can be found (living alone, having lost an only child, children no longer around), hand this to the community and your phone — see item 6 of this section.
Sources (2 references)
Moon JR, et al. (2011). Widowhood and mortality: a meta-analysis. PLoS ONE. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0023465; Shor E, et al. (2012). Widowhood and mortality: a meta-analysis and meta-regression. Demography. https://doi.org/10.1007/s13524-012-0096-x
6

With no family and no friends, swap 'the one person who checks on you' for three things: a neighbor who can enter your home, a community visiting list, and emergency contacts in your phone

Grade BValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

With no family and no friends, two things need looking after: that someone notices you if something happens, and that you take your medication and eat on time day to day. The medication and meals are on you — write lists, set alarms, don't rely on memory. Being noticed rests on three things: leave a spare key with a neighbor, ask the residents' committee whether you can get on the caring-visit list, and set up emergency contacts in your phone and keep it powered on.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is speaking up first — telling a neighbor and the residents' committee, 'I live alone, and something just happened in my family.'
Benefit
44,573 outpatients, all at risk of or with a history of atherothrombosis (the kind of disease where plaque grows in the vessels and clots easily block them). Doctors from multiple countries registered them into REACH, an international project, for follow-up; enrollment ran from December 2003 to December 2004, with 4 years of follow-up. Of them, 8,594 (19%) lived alone. Over 4 years, death from all causes combined was 14.1% among those living alone versus 11.1% among those living with others. Cardiovascular death: 8.6% versus 6.8%. Both log-rank P<0.01 — the differences are unlikely to be chance. The gap differed by age band (interaction P=0.03). Ages 45 to 65: death for living alone versus living with others was 7.7% versus 5.7%. After adjusting for other conditions, HR 1.24 (95% CI 1.01–1.51), about 24% higher. Ages 66 to 80: 13.2% versus 12.3%, HR 1.12 (1.01–1.26), about 10% higher. Over 80: 24.6% versus 28.4%, HR 0.92 (0.79–1.06) — no elevation, if anything the reverse. A 2022 opinion from ten departments including the Ministry of Civil Affairs requires caring-visit services to be provided. The recipients are older people who live alone, are empty-nest, left behind, disabled, severely disabled, or in special family-planning households. The service format is 'regular home visits, phone and video calls, and remote monitoring'. Townships (subdistricts) carry out surveys with the assistance of village (residents') committees, gather basic information and 'willingness to receive caring-visit services', and fold this into grassroots grid-based management — that is, districts are assigned to dedicated people to watch over. By the end of 2025, 'ensure the monthly visiting rate for older people in special difficulty reaches 100%', and 'for disabled older people in special difficulty, no fewer than one caring visit per month'. The document also encourages households to install smart call systems, smart electricity and water meters, health monitoring products, and elder-care monitoring devices, so that 'once monitoring detects an anomaly, it can issue a timely warning and simultaneously send notifications to emergency contacts'. Service personnel who discover an emergency 'should immediately help dial the emergency assistance number'.
Note
The three things, in practice. One: give a spare key or a temporary door-lock code to a neighbor or the property management, and say, 'I'm on my own these days.' You don't need a friendship, only someone who knows you are inside. Two: go to the community residents' committee, explain that you live alone, and ask whether you can get on the caring-visit list. Among older people, those living alone, empty-nest, or who have lost an only child are officially designated service recipients; while you're there, ask whether the local area offers free installations like smart call buttons or smart water meters. Three: set up emergency contacts and a medical first-aid card in your phone, and for these days don't mute it or power it off. Two reasons for the B grade. First, the link between living alone and mortality comes from retrospective population-data studies; the reverse explanation — 'people in worse health and worse circumstances are more likely to live alone' — cannot be removed, and the source itself says the result needs confirmation. Second, the caring-visit document only covers older people. Those under 60 have no corresponding dedicated system. What you can count on is one line in that document, requiring grid workers and social workers to 'promptly identify psychological-crisis risks such as family upheaval, unemployment, and dropping out of school' (see item 11 of this section, call 12356 for someone to talk to). For why 'someone else in the house' is worth so much, see Section 13, item 1 (chest compressions). Of cardiac arrests outside hospital, 79.2% happen at home. When someone nearby does compressions, 16.1% survive to discharge; with no one, only 3.9%. No one in the house means falling into the low tier. Two more things you can do in passing. Arranging a funeral itself means running between the funeral home, community health services, the police, and the housing fund — several windows (see Section 25). Schedule it as one fixed outing per day, and your outings for these days are already arranged. The hotline can be called again and again — it is not a one-call-only thing (see item 11 of this section, call 12356 for someone to talk to). 'Living alone' is also a long-term risk factor in itself. The odds ratio for death among people living alone is 1.32, about 30% higher — see Section 22, item 9 (treat regular meetings with people as a health expense). But this item only covers the days at hand; the long-term accounting is done separately.
Sources (2 references)
Udell JA, et al. (2012). Living alone and cardiovascular risk in outpatients at risk of or with atherothrombosis. Archives of Internal Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1001/archinternmed.2012.2782; Ministry of Civil Affairs and nine other departments (2022). Guiding Opinions on Providing Caring-Visit Services for Older People in Special Difficulty (Min Fa [2022] No. 73). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2022-10/13/content_571…
7

When a parent dies, tell the child the truth, let them join the farewell, and don't send them elsewhere to 'change the scenery'

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Children who lose a father or mother before 18 are about 50% more likely to die by early adulthood than children who haven't. When the parent died by accident or suicide the increase is about 80%; by illness, about 30%. What a family can do: tell the child the truth, let them take part in the farewell, don't interrupt their schooling, and don't send them to relatives' homes for a change of scenery.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is that you are grieving too, and still have to explain things clearly to the child.
Benefit
All people born in Denmark 1968 to 2008 and Sweden 1973 to 2006 were included, plus an 89.3% sample of those born in Finland 1987 to 2007. Over 7.3 million in total, of whom 189,094 lost a parent before 18. Death from all causes combined among these children was 50% higher than among those who had not lost a parent (mortality rate ratio 1.50, 95% CI 1.43–1.58, about 1.5 times). When the parent died of non-natural causes such as accident or suicide: 1.84 (1.71–2.00), about 80% higher. When the parent died of natural causes such as illness: 1.33 (1.24–1.41), about 30% higher. It was highest when the child's cause of death fell in the same category as the parent's.
Note
When telling the child, don't invent 'they went away on a long trip'; put the guardianship and care arrangements in writing. The B grade is not because the numbers are weak. This is a follow-up study of the entire population of three countries, and the numbers alone would merit an A. The B comes from the gap between this number and the specific practices of 'how to tell the child, whether to join the farewell', where there is no direct trial evidence. The authors also state plainly that data on the parent–child relationship and the child's lifestyle after bereavement are both missing. The elevation contains both an inborn component and the long-term impact the loss itself leaves. For appointing a guardian and arranging property, see Section 17. For the child's support and schooling, see Section 18.
Sources (1 reference)
Li J, et al. (2014). Mortality after parental death in childhood: a nationwide cohort study from three Nordic countries. PLoS Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1001679
8

If grief is still stuck in place after six months and life is unlivable, book a psychiatry or clinical psychology appointment

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

About one in every ten bereaved adults gets stuck: for more than six months, still yearning so persistently that you can't eat, can't work, can't look after your children; numbness; the feeling that life is meaningless. This is not a lack of strength. It has diagnostic criteria, and it has a dedicated treatment. The targeted treatment works for 51%; ordinary psychotherapy for 28%, and it takes effect faster too.

Cost
Registration fee plus treatment fees. This kind of therapy runs in courses — in the trial, 16 sessions over an average of 19 weeks. The hard part is walking out and booking the appointment yourself.
Benefit
Pooled: 14 studies of adults whose loved one did not die by violence and who were not themselves in psychiatric care. Prevalence of prolonged grief disorder: 9.8% (95% CI 6.8–14.0) — about 10 in every 100 bereaved adults. The older the age, the higher the proportion. Another study tested how accurate these diagnostic criteria are: it recruited 291 bereaved people and interviewed them three times, at 0–6, 6–12, and 12–24 months after the loss. The core feature of the diagnosis is intense yearning for the deceased. It must be accompanied by at least five of these nine items. The first five are emotional numbness, shock, feeling that life is meaningless, difficulty trusting others, and bitterness over the loss. The last four are difficulty accepting it, confusion about who you are supposed to be, avoidance of reality, and inability to carry on with life. These features must appear every day, or be severe enough to make normal functioning impossible. And they must still be present at least 6 months after the loved one's death, affecting daily life. There is also a trial in which 95 people were randomized into two groups for 16 sessions of therapy over an average of 19 weeks. Therapy targeted at complicated grief worked for 51%. Ordinary interpersonal psychotherapy: 28% (P=0.02 — the difference is unlikely to be chance). The former also took effect faster. Number needed to treat: 4.3 — on average, one additional person improves for every 4.3 treated.
Note
Don't fixate on counting the months yourself. The real test is 'it is affecting eating, sleeping, work, or caring for your children' — if that fits, book the appointment. The departments are called psychiatry, psychology, or clinical psychology; public psychiatric specialty hospitals all have them. This diagnosis is called complicated grief in some sources, and prolonged grief disorder in others. Different criteria also set different required durations — some say 6 months, some 12. The 9.8% figure comes from 14 studies with considerable variation in method, and the authors caution that it may not carry over to other populations.
Sources (3 references)
Lundorff M, et al. (2017). Prevalence of prolonged grief disorder in adult bereavement: A systematic review and meta-analysis. Journal of Affective Disorders. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.jad.2017.01.030; Prigerson HG, et al. (2009). Prolonged grief disorder: Psychometric validation of criteria proposed for DSM-V and ICD-11. PLoS Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pmed.1000121; Shear MK, et al. (2005). Treatment of complicated grief: a randomized controlled trial. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.293.21.2601
9

Don't pay for grief counseling straight away; first check whether your grief is genuinely stuck (the symptoms in item 8)

Grade AValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Offering counseling to every bereaved person brings small benefit that fades after a while, because most people would recover on their own anyway. But for those who are already clearly failing to adjust, therapy is as effective as it is for other psychological problems. So first check yourself against item 8 (grief stuck — go to psychiatry), and spend the money only if it matches.

Cost
Costs nothing — it saves you a counseling fee instead.
Benefit
Pooled: 61 controlled studies. Universal psychological intervention for the bereaved shows small benefit right at the end of treatment, and after a delay no benefit can be detected. Interventions that enrolled only bereaved people 'already clearly failing to adjust' worked as well as psychotherapy for other psychological problems. Studies without prior screening fared poorly, because the group that received no intervention would have recovered on its own over time anyway. A separate pooling of 14 randomized trials: therapy for people already in trouble was clearly better than control both at the end of treatment and at later follow-up, with the effect still growing after a delay. Universal preventive intervention for people not yet in trouble did not work. Another study followed 205 people from before widowhood all the way to 6 and 18 months after. It distinguished five trajectories: common grief, chronic grief, chronic depression, improvement during bereavement, and resilience (holding up). Resilience was the most common trajectory; common grief was comparatively rare.
Note
This means 'not everyone needs it', not 'no one should do it'. The high-risk bereaved of item 4 (loved one died by suicide, accident, or homicide) and the already-stuck of item 8 (grief stuck — go to psychiatry) are exactly the people for whom doing it is supported by evidence. A Lancet review reaches the same conclusion: grief is not an illness, and most people do not need professional intervention. The effort should go to the high-risk, and to those who have already developed complicated grief, post-bereavement depression, and stress disorders.
Sources (4 references)
Currier JM, et al. (2008). The effectiveness of psychotherapeutic interventions for bereaved persons: a comprehensive quantitative review. Psychological Bulletin. https://doi.org/10.1037/0033-2909.134.5.648; Wittouck C, et al. (2011). The prevention and treatment of complicated grief: a meta-analysis. Clinical Psychology Review. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.cpr.2010.09.005; Bonanno GA, et al. (2002). Resilience to loss and chronic grief: a prospective study from preloss to 18-months postloss. Journal of Personality and Social Psychology. https://doi.org/10.1037/0022-3514.83.5.1150; Stroebe M et al. (2007). Health outcomes of bereavement. Lancet. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(07)61816-9 (the review cited in the Note)
10

After separation or divorce, don't let your medical insurance lapse and don't prop yourself up with alcohol

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Separated or divorced people are clearly more likely to die early than the still-married, with bigger increases for men and younger people. This is not necessarily caused by divorce — people who divorce may already differ in health and income. Two things you can control yourself: don't let medical insurance or checkups lapse, and don't lean on tobacco and alcohol.

Cost
Costs nothing. Renew the insurance, stop the drinking. The hard part is that during this stretch it is easy to prop yourself up with alcohol.
Benefit
Pooled: 32 studies that registered people first and then followed them forward, covering over 6.5 million people, 160,000 deaths, over 755,000 divorces, and 11 countries. Compared with the still-married, separated or divorced adults had a clearly elevated risk of early death. Men and younger people rose more sharply than women and older people. The authors discussed four possible pathways. One, social selection: people whose health or circumstances already differ are more likely to end up divorced. Two, interrupted resources: income and protections cut off. Three, changed health behaviors: worse drinking, smoking, and daily routines. Four, chronic psychological stress (long-term strain).
Note
The source only reported a 'clearly elevated' risk and subgroup contrasts, without quotable multiples, so no specific figures are given here. The benefit is rated medium on the logic of 'direction known, no decrease to which a threshold can be applied'. For property, debts, and bride price in divorce, see Sections 8 and 10. For child custody arrangements, see Section 18.
Sources (1 reference)
Sbarra DA, et al. (2011). Divorce and Death: A Meta-Analysis and Research Agenda for Clinical, Social, and Health Psychology. Perspectives on Psychological Science. https://doi.org/10.1177/1745691611414724
11

For someone to talk to, call 12356; minors and teenagers call 12355; to see a doctor, book a psychological outpatient clinic

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If you want someone to talk to, call 12356 — the national psychological assistance hotline, free. Minors and teenagers have a separate line, the 12355 youth service platform. To see a doctor, book a psychological outpatient visit in psychiatry, psychology, or clinical psychology. Family upheaval, unemployment, and a child out of school are things community grid workers and social workers are supposed to notice on their own.

Cost
Costs nothing. Both hotlines are free. A psychological outpatient visit registers at ordinary outpatient rates.
Benefit
The 2026 plan by the National Health Commission and 24 other departments requires improving the operating system of the 12356 psychological assistance hotline: keeping it running steadily and raising the connection rate. It requires promoting the establishment of provincial 12356 information platforms. It requires strengthening coordination mechanisms with the 110 and other service hotlines. It also requires building up and making good use of the 12355 youth service platform, in coordination with 12356. The targets for 2030 are three. First, more than 80% of administrative villages and urban communities set up counseling rooms or social work stations and provide psychological services. Second, public psychiatric specialty hospitals at all levels and at least 1 hospital in every county (district) provide psychological outpatient services. Third, every province builds a provincial 12356 psychological assistance platform. Psychological crisis intervention and assistance teams are made up of psychiatrists, psychotherapy technicians, psychological counselors, social work professionals, and volunteers. The plan also requires three groups of people to stay alert and detect problems early in normal times. These three groups are grid workers (community staff responsible by district), social work professionals, and volunteers. They are to promptly identify psychological-crisis risks such as family upheaval, unemployment, and dropping out of school (nationwide; issued March 2026).
Note
Grade B because the village and community counseling rooms and the county-level psychological outpatient clinics are goals for 2030, not something every place has today. 12356 and 12355, on the other hand, can be called today. For when 12356 opened and how many hours a day it answers, see Section 1, item 25. Psychological counseling and psychotherapy are not the same thing. Making a diagnosis and prescribing medication must be done by a psychiatrist, and therapy must be done at a qualified medical institution. The paid-by-the-hour 'healing' and 'spiritual counseling' on the market are not part of this system.
Sources (1 reference)
National Health Commission and 24 other departments (2026). Notice on Issuing the Implementation Plan for Improving the Social Psychological Service System and Crisis Intervention Mechanism (Guo Wei Yi Zheng Fa [2026] No. 8). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065035…
12

For the first three months after a major upheaval, push every irreversible big decision to later

Grade CValue: FairBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Your judgment about all sorts of 'opportunities' is at its worst during this stretch. People who claim they can contact the deceased, claim they can get your money back, urge you to quit your job and start over somewhere else, or pull you into a business partnership — they will all come calling. Anything worth more than a month's income, or very costly to undo, gets pushed back three months, no exceptions. First tell it to someone with no stake in the matter, and don't decide on the spot that day.

Cost
Costs nothing — you are only postponing decisions, and may miss certain opportunities because of it. The hard part is that at the time it feels like opportunity won't wait.
Benefit
It avoids irreversible property decisions made in the stretch right after a blow, when judgment is at its worst. Such things include selling the house, quitting the job, investing a death benefit or compensation payout in one go, rushing into remarriage, and guaranteeing someone's loan. These decisions usually run from tens of thousands of yuan up to the scale of a whole apartment, so the benefit is rated medium. Official documents likewise list 'family upheaval, unemployment, and dropping out of school' as psychological-crisis risks that communities should proactively screen for — the state you are in during this stretch is already treated as one that needs an outside hand.
Note
If you have no such uninvolved person around, call 12356 and tell it once (see item 11 of this section, call 12356 for someone to talk to), or write it down yourself and reread it three days later. 'Three months' is a line the author drew; no literature supports that specific duration, so this is graded C. For common scams targeting the bereaved and the elderly, see Section 17 (retirement investment, housing-for-pension schemes) and Section 6 (fortune-telling). For the traps in loan guarantees and IOUs, see Section 8. A few sums of money you should actively go claim, which are not in the 'push to later' category: your housing fund balance, social insurance benefits, and the three work-death payments — see Sections 25 and 19.
Sources (1 reference)
Author's experience; no direct literature. For 'family upheaval, unemployment, and dropping out of school' as psychological-crisis risks, see National Health Commission and 24 other departments (2026). Implementation Plan for Improving the Social Psychological Service System and Crisis Intervention Mechanism (Guo Wei Yi Zheng Fa [2026] No. 8). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202604/content_7065035…
13

Don't use death as a way to repay debts: life insurance won't pay out within the first two years, work-injury status won't be recognized, and debts still come off the estate first

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

If you die by suicide within two years of a life insurance contract, it does not pay out — only the small refundable amount in the policy is returned. Work-injury status is not recognized either, so not one cent of the three work-death payments comes through. The debts you owe are deducted from the estate you leave behind, and your family receives only what remains. They also bear the health toll described in item 4 of this section (bereavement by suicide or violent death).

Cost
Costs nothing — just doing this arithmetic clearly.
Benefit
Article 44 of the Insurance Law governs contracts that pay a benefit on the insured's death. Counting from the date the contract was formed or its effect was restored, if the insured dies by suicide within two years, the insurer bears no liability to pay the insurance benefit. The exception is where the insured lacked civil capacity at the time of suicide — someone legally unable to answer for their own actions. In that case the insurer refunds the policy's cash value as agreed in the contract — that is, only the small refundable part of the policy, not the sum insured. Life insurance sums insured usually run in the hundreds of thousands of yuan, so the benefit is rated large. Article 16, paragraph 3 of the Work Injury Insurance Regulations provides: self-harm or suicide must not be recognized as a work injury or treated as one. The three work-death payments under Article 39 are thereby all lost. One, the funeral allowance, paid as 6 months of the local average monthly wage of employees from the previous year. Two, the dependent relatives' pension. Three, the one-time work-death payment, set at 20 times the previous year's national per-capita disposable income of urban residents. Article 1159 of the Civil Code provides: when an estate is divided, the taxes and debts the deceased was legally obliged to pay shall be settled first — that is, the estate pays the taxes and debts first, and only the remainder is divided. Article 1161 provides: heirs pay debts only up to the actual value of the estate they inherit — that is, they repay out of what they inherited without putting in their own money, and those who renounce the inheritance may bear no liability for repayment.
Note
Here only the money side of the ledger is being counted. The other items in this section and in Section 1 are about not reaching this point at all. Article 44 of the Insurance Law covers only the first two years; it is written out to state the provisions in full, not to provide a timetable. The family's health toll: item 4 of this section (those whose spouse died by suicide face a 70–80% higher risk of a newly diagnosed mental disorder within 5 years). What to do when the thoughts arise: Section 1, items 25 and 32; the aftereffects for those rescued: Section 1, item 33. The standards for the three work-death payments: Section 19, item 15. The concrete procedures for the estate and debts: Section 25, item 9 (go claim the housing fund and social insurance benefits one by one).
Sources (3 references)
Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2015 amendment). Insurance Law of the People's Republic of China, Article 44. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf7c4…; State Council (2010 revision). Work Injury Insurance Regulations (State Council Order No. 586), Articles 16 and 39. https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2011/content_1778064.htm; National People's Congress (2020). Civil Code of the People's Republic of China, Articles 1159 and 1161. https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…

30. School-Age Children

18 items

Section 20 covers the year right after a child is born. Section 18 works out how much money and how much time raising a child takes. The decade or more in between, ages 3 to 18, is written up in this section. The card on managing screen time by age starts from age 0, because the official brackets are simply 0–3, 3–6, and primary/secondary school; splitting it up would only make it harder to use. What this section answers: when "don't fall behind in school" and "the body" collide, which things cannot wait. These things have time windows; once a window is missed, the loss cannot be undone. Whether schoolwork really should be that much of a grind is not discussed here — only the windows and the numbers are given. The first eight cards, card 12 (cycloplegic refraction), card 13 (pit-and-fissure sealants), and cards 15 through 18 count death, and damage that truly lands on body and mind. Among them, cards 16 and 17 cover how to manage a child at home: no hitting, no yelling, and a parenting course that teaches concrete techniques. Card 18 says don't send your child to a locked-down internet-addiction school. Card 9 (don't buy products claiming to "cure myopia") is counted in money. Card 10 (the written rules on sleep, homework, PE, and rankings), card 11 (leave of absence with enrollment held), and card 14 (a child who games a lot) are counted in time. Drowning, traffic, helmets, and the HPV vaccine are in Section 1. Infants and toddlers are in Section 20. Children being scammed and in-game top-ups are in Section 5. Red lines minors should not cross on their own are in Section 9. How to recognize an emergency and call an ambulance is in Section 13. Children after a parent's death are in Section 29. None of these are repeated here.

1

If your child reports sudden severe pain that keeps getting worse, go to the hospital now — don't let them hold out until school ends

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: large

Some illnesses are counted in hours. Sudden, severe pain on one side of the scrotum in a boy is testicular torsion — the cord of blood vessels attached to the testicle has twisted and the blood supply is cut off. Treated within 6 hours, the testicle is saved 97.2% of the time. Drag it out to 19 to 24 hours, and only 42.5% survive. This kind of pain cannot wait until the end of the school day, and it cannot wait until exams are over.

Cost
Costs nothing. Take half a day off and take your child to the emergency department.
Benefit
Thirty case series covering 2,116 testicular torsion patients were systematically gathered and read together. Of these, 1,283 cases were tabulated in 6-hour bands. Counting from the moment the pain began, the testicle survival rate was 97.2% at 0 to 6 hours. 79.3% at 7 to 12 hours. 61.3% at 13 to 18 hours. 42.5% at 19 to 24 hours. 24.4% at 25 to 48 hours. 7.4% beyond 48 hours. Pooled into larger bands: 90.4% within 12 hours, 54.0% at 13 to 24 hours, 18.1% beyond 24 hours. The authors' conclusion is that the salvageable window can be longer than the commonly cited 6 to 8 hours. So even if the pain has already lasted a long time, still go get it treated — don't skip it on the grounds that "it's too late anyway"
Note
Say one thing to boys ahead of time: if you ever get sudden, severe pain down there, speak up right away — there is no need to be embarrassed. Testicular torsion mostly strikes adolescent boys, and many endure it in silence because they cannot bring themselves to mention it. Other conditions also counted in hours: acute appendicitis (perforates if dragged out), diabetic ketoacidosis, and meningitis. For each of these, this section has not verified hour by hour how much worse things get with each hour of delay. Their shared warning signs: sudden onset, steadily worsening, and unlike any previous episode. How to recognize an emergency and call an ambulance: Section 13.
Sources (1 reference)
Mellick LB, et al. (2019). A Systematic Review of Testicle Survival Time After a Torsion Event. Pediatric Emergency Care. https://doi.org/10.1097/PEC.0000000000001287
2

Don't put off needed treatment until 'after the exams'; some windows follow bone age, not the exam calendar

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Scoliosis is a sideways curve of the spine. A brace is a rigid vest worn over the body to hold the spine in place. Worn while the bones are still growing, it kept 75% of children from curving to the point of needing surgery; among those only observed, not braced, just 42%. The window for wearing it follows bone maturity, not the senior-high and college entrance exams — by the time exams are over, surgery is often the only option.

Cost
Costs nothing; the only decision is whether to act sooner or later. Time off and follow-up visits take time, and the cost of the treatment itself is counted separately. The hard part: the brace must be worn at least 18 hours a day, and the child has to put up with it constantly.
Benefit
A trial run by multiple hospitals together enrolled 242 adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis who met the criteria for bracing. Of these, 116 were assigned by lottery; 126 chose for themselves whether to wear the brace. Success and failure were defined in advance: progression past 50 degrees counted as treatment failure, and still being under that threshold when the bones finished growing counted as success. Analysis was by original assignment, regardless of whether the brace was actually worn enough afterward. Success rate: 75% in the randomized bracing group vs 42% in the randomized observation group (OR 4.11, 95% CI 1.85–9.16) — about 4 times the chance of success compared with observation alone. Pooling the lottery-assigned and self-chosen groups: 72% vs 48% (OR 1.93, 1.08–3.46 after leveling out the two groups' pre-existing differences — still about 1.9 times). The more hours the brace was worn each day, the higher the success rate (P<0.001; this relationship is unlikely to be chance). The trial was stopped early because the brace clearly worked
Note
Scoliosis is the example here because it has a lottery-based trial, a clear time window, and happens to be one of the priority items in student physicals (see card 7). In the same family: strabismus, amblyopia, dental caries, and elective surgery such as congenital heart disease that can be scheduled. The common thread: the later they are done, the worse the result or the higher the price. Ask a specialist about the specific window. If missing class is the worry, students in compulsory education can take a leave of absence, up to 1 year, with enrollment held — see card 11.
Sources (1 reference)
Weinstein SL, et al. (2013). Effects of bracing in adolescents with idiopathic scoliosis. New England Journal of Medicine. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa1307337
3

If your child is bullied, report it to the school that day and demand written handling; for beatings, money extortion, or rumor-spreading, call the police directly

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Children bullied by peers are about 2.2 times as likely to have suicidal thoughts as those who aren't bullied, and about 2.6 times as likely to have attempted suicide. A school that receives a report must investigate immediately; once conduct is determined to be bullying, discipline must follow, and serious cases may not be covered up — they must be reported to the police. So report it that same day, demand the formal determination process, and get a written record.

Cost
Costs nothing. Go to the homeroom teacher, and also to the school's student bullying governance body. To report to the police, dial 110. The hard part is withstanding pleas like "don't blow this up."
Benefit
34 studies covering 284,375 children and adolescents were pooled. Peer victimization was associated with suicidal ideation, OR 2.23 (95% CI 2.10–2.37) — about 2.2 times the likelihood of such thoughts compared with the unbullied. Another 9 studies with 70,102 people linked being bullied to suicide attempts, OR 2.55 (1.95–3.34), about 2.6 times. Results held regardless of sex, age, or study quality. The association between cyberbullying and suicidal ideation was stronger than for offline bullying. Article 21 of the Regulations on the Protection of Minors in Schools lists five categories of conduct: beating, kicking, slapping, biting, shoving, and pulling; verbal abuse, mockery, and giving insulting nicknames; snatching, extorting, or deliberately damaging property; maliciously excluding and isolating; and fabricating facts to defame someone or spreading rumors online. The same article provides that where the side with the advantage in age, physical strength, or numbers deliberately or maliciously does these things, causing personal injury, property loss, or psychological harm, it may be determined to be bullying. Article 22 requires school staff who notice abnormal emotions or physical injuries in students to promptly look into them and report. Article 23 requires the school, upon receiving a report, to investigate immediately, refer it to the bullying governance body for determination and handling, and notify parents to take part. Where bullying is confirmed, educational discipline or disciplinary punishment must be imposed. Serious bullying that violates public-security administration or is suspected of being criminal must not be concealed; it should be promptly reported to the public security organs and the education administrative department (nationwide, effective September 1, 2021)
Note
Unexplained injuries on the child, a sudden refusal to go to school, belongings repeatedly going missing — start by asking about those Article 22 signals. This pooled analysis only tracks what happens, without comparison groups, so it cannot prove that bullying alone causes suicide, but the direction and the size of the risk are clear. The Plan for Strengthening the Comprehensive Governance of Bullying Among Primary and Secondary School Students additionally requires a strict distinction between bullying and rough play between students. So the school is obliged to make a determination; it cannot be waved off with "kids were just fooling around."
Sources (2 references)
van Geel M, et al. (2014). Relationship between peer victimization, cyberbullying, and suicide in children and adolescents: a meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2013.4143; Ministry of Education (2021). Regulations on the Protection of Minors in Schools (MOE Order No. 50, Articles 21, 22, and 23). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-06/02/content_561…
4

Give your child 2 full hours outdoors every day — the only myopia-prevention method currently backed by randomized trials

Grade AValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: large

Adding a 40-minute outdoor class every day for first graders cut new myopia over three years from about 40% to about 30%. The National Health Commission's prescribed dose is no less than 2 hours outdoors in daylight every day, or 14 hours a week in total. Overcast days count; standing outside during breaks counts too.

Cost
Costs nothing. But time must be set aside every day, most of it squeezed out of homework and online classes. The hard part is doing it every single day — it's not something you do a few times and finish.
Benefit
First graders at 12 primary schools in Guangzhou, randomized by school (intervention schools 952 children, control schools 951; mean age 6.6). The intervention added one 40-minute outdoor activity class on every school day, and parents were encouraged to take children out more after school. New myopia over 3 years: 30.4% in the intervention group — 259 of 853 eligible children — versus 39.5% in the control group, 287 of 726. Difference between groups: -9.1 percentage points (95% CI -14.1 to -4.1, P<0.001); the true gap is roughly 4 to 14 percentage points. Prescription progression over 3 years (change in spherical equivalent): -1.42 D vs -1.59 D, a difference of 0.17 D (P=0.04) — the intervention group progressed slightly less. D is the unit prescriptions are measured in. Growth in axial length (the eye's front-to-back length) showed no detectable difference between groups (P=0.07). The Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents requires children and adolescents to spend no less than 2 hours outdoors in daylight every day, or 14 hours cumulative per week. It notes that outdoor activity is protective even on overcast days, and says to avoid the hot, intensely sunny hours after midday
Note
This trial ran only 3 years, and the children all started at age 6. The 9.1-percentage-point gap between the groups can only keep some children from becoming nearsighted; it guarantees no one that outcome. The same Ten Core Messages adds several practices. For reading and writing: "one foot, one fist, one inch" — eyes about a foot (33 cm) from the page, chest a fist from the desk edge, fingers an inch (3 cm) from the pen tip. After 20 minutes of close-up eye use, look into the distance for at least 20 seconds. For primary and secondary students, non-study screen use: no more than 15 minutes at a time, no more than 1 hour a day in total. "Being outdoors" and "having PE class" are not the same thing — standing outside during breaks counts.
Sources (2 references)
He M, et al. (2015). Effect of Time Spent Outdoors at School on the Development of Myopia Among Children in China: A Randomized Clinical Trial. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2015.10803; General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2023] No. 278). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284…
5

No screens at ages 0 to 3, as little as possible at 3 to 6, and no more than 1 hour a day of non-study screen time for primary and secondary students

Grade BValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

The National Health Commission says no screens at ages 0 to 3, avoid them as much as possible at 3 to 6, and for primary and secondary students no more than 15 minutes at a time and 1 hour a day of non-study use. The rationale is that long stretches of close-up eye work bring myopia on earlier. The evidence tying screens to myopia isn't that solid; what has actually been tested and shown to work is 2 hours outdoors a day.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is taking the screen out of the child's hands — and the parents watching less themselves in front of the kids.
Benefit
Article 4 of the Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents reads verbatim: "Infants and toddlers aged 0–3 do not use phones, tablets, computers, or other video-screen electronic products; children aged 3–6 should avoid contact with and use of phones, tablets, computers, and other video-screen electronic products as much as possible; for primary and secondary students, non-study use of electronic screens should not exceed 15 minutes at a time, and daily cumulative use should not exceed 1 hour." The same article states: "Long close-range use of electronic video-screen products readily depletes children's hyperopia reserve and is a major reason myopia starts early and is so common among children and adolescents." The 2018 implementation plan from the Ministry of Education and seven other departments gives parents the same instructions, adding "the younger the age, the shorter the continuous use of electronic products should be." The research evidence is much weaker: a systematic review covered 33 studies, 11 of which entered the pooled analysis, with subjects from 3 months to 33 years old. Counting only phones and tablets, the odds ratio for myopia was 1.26 (95% CI 1.00 to 1.60, I²=77%). Including computers: 1.77 (1.28 to 2.45, I²=87%). The authors' conclusion only goes as far as "possibly associated," and notes that not one of the 33 studies had reliable screen-time measurement
Note
Grade B because what the authorities give is a set of age brackets, not numbers measured in trials. The lower bound of the studies' odds ratio sits right at 1.00, and the authors dare claim only "possibly associated." So treat this as a house rule that is easy to enforce — not as "no screens means no myopia." The option with real lottery-trial backing is card 4 (2 hours outdoors). Preschoolers need eye checks too: the same document says children at ages 1–3, 4–6, and after 7 should all have periodic refractive screening to see how much hyperopia reserve remains; for the method, see card 12 (cycloplegic refraction). Screen time and children's language skills have also been meta-analyzed: 42 studies, 18,905 people — the longer the screen time, the weaker the language skills (r=−0.14, 95% CI −0.18 to −0.10). But co-viewing, and watching programs with educational content, were positively associated (r=0.16 and 0.13). This is association, not causation; it only shows that replacing conversation with your child with a screen is a bad trade.
Sources (4 references)
General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2023] No. 278). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284… ; Ministry of Education and seven other departments (2018). Implementation Plan for the Comprehensive Prevention and Control of Myopia Among Children and Adolescents (Jiao Ti Yi [2018] No. 3). http://www.moe.gov.cn/srcsite/A17/moe_943/s3285/201808/t201… ; Foreman J, Salim AT, Praveen A, et al. (2021). Association between digital smart device use and myopia: a systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet Digital Health, 3(12), e806-e818. https://doi.org/10.1016/S2589-7500(21)00135-7 ; Madigan S, McArthur BA, Anhorn C, Eirich R, Christakis DA (2020). Associations between screen use and child language skills: a systematic review and meta-analysis. JAMA Pediatrics, 174(7), 665-675. https://doi.org/10.1001/jamapediatrics.2020.0327
6

Treat myopia as damage that stays: the higher the prescription, the more retinal detachment, macular disease, and glaucoma later in life

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: large

Myopia doesn't go away on its own, and the prescription never comes back down. Nor is it just a matter of "wearing glasses." Compared with people who aren't nearsighted, the odds of myopic macular degeneration are more than ten times higher with mild myopia, and several hundred times higher above 600 degrees (−6.00 D). For retinal detachment: about 3 times higher with mild myopia, about 13 times higher above 600 degrees. So the earlier a child becomes nearsighted and the faster the prescription climbs, the bigger the risks to carry later.

Cost
Costs nothing. Nothing to do in itself — the things to do are in cards 4 and 5 (2 hours outdoors, managing screen time by age).
Benefit
A systematic review and meta-analysis pooled studies published up to June 2019, splitting myopia into three bands by prescription: mild (−0.5 to −3.00 D), moderate (−3.00 to −6.00 D), and high (≤−6.00 D, above 600 degrees). Compared with people without myopia, the odds ratios for myopic macular degeneration were, in order, 13.57 (95% CI 6.18 to 29.79), 72.74 (33.18 to 159.48), and 845.08 (230.05 to 3104.34). For retinal detachment: 3.15 (1.92 to 5.17), 8.74 (7.28 to 10.50), 12.62 (6.65 to 23.94). For posterior subcapsular cataract: 1.56 (1.32 to 1.84), 2.55 (1.98 to 3.28), 4.55 (2.66 to 7.75). For open-angle glaucoma: 1.59 (1.33 to 1.91) for mild myopia, and 2.92 (1.89 to 4.52) for moderate and high combined. For visual impairment appearing after age 60, the odds ratios across the three bands were 1.71 (1.07 to 2.74), 5.54 (3.12 to 9.85), and 87.63 (34.50 to 222.58).
