The Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents says the same: above 600 degrees is high myopia, and in this group the incidence of blinding eye diseases — cataract, open-angle glaucoma, myopic macular degeneration, retinal detachment, myopic optic neuropathy, and the like — is clearly higher than in other groups, and "myopia can be prevented and controlled, but not reversed"
Note
Everything pooled here is observational, and the odds ratios are unusually large. The confidence range for high myopia and macular degeneration runs from 230 to 3104, which means the underlying studies differ greatly — read these numbers as orders of magnitude, not precise values. Most of these complications only show up in middle or old age. Myopia itself is not a disability; the vast majority of people see normally once corrected with glasses. But myopia isn't settled with a pair of glasses — it's worth the effort to delay it and keep it under control. How to follow up after a diagnosis: card 12 (cycloplegic refraction). Don't buy products claiming to cure it: card 9 (curing myopia).
Sources (2 references)
Haarman AEG, Enthoven CA, Tideman JWL, Tedja MS, Verhoeven VJM, Klaver CCW (2020). The complications of myopia: a review and meta-analysis. Investigative Ophthalmology & Visual Science, 61(4), 49. https://doi.org/10.1167/iovs.61.4.49 ; General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2023] No. 278). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284…
7

Read the annual school physical report yourself, and take any abnormal findings to a hospital the same year

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

Primary and secondary schools run a student physical every year. The priorities on the report sheet are overweight, obesity, malnutrition, abnormal spinal curvature, poor vision, and dental caries — the items most easily left to slide. Don't glance at height and weight and fold the sheet away. If any of these come back abnormal, take your child to a specialist that same year and get it checked out.

Cost
Costs nothing. During compulsory education, the physical exam fee comes out of the school's operating funds; parents pay nothing extra.
Benefit
The Measures for Health Physicals of Primary and Secondary School Students (2021 edition) require primary and secondary schools to organize 1 health physical a year for enrolled students. The surgical exam covers head, neck, chest, spine, limbs, skin, and lymph nodes. The eye exam covers the external eye, distance vision, and refraction (the degree of nearsightedness or farsightedness). The report sheet given to each individual must include the findings, an overall assessment, and health guidance. Overweight, obesity, malnutrition, abnormal spinal curvature, poor vision, and dental caries (tooth decay) must be treated as guidance priorities. Education administrative departments must open a file for students with health problems and follow up (write it down and check back later). During compulsory education, student physical exam costs are paid from the school's operating funds; parents pay nothing extra (nationwide, issued September 2021)
Note
Grade B because this is a document on how schools must operate, not an effectiveness study. It guarantees "checked every year, these items checked, abnormalities followed up" — not that anyone will actually handle what turns up. A physical is a first pass at screening, not a diagnosis. Poor vision needs cycloplegic refraction at an ophthalmology department (card 12). Abnormal spinal curvature needs orthopedics or spine surgery (card 2 — don't put off treatment until after the exams). Both steps require the parents to take the child themselves.
Sources (1 reference)
National Health Commission and Ministry of Education (2021). Measures for Health Physicals of Primary and Secondary School Students (2021 edition) (Guo Wei Yi Fa [2021] No. 29). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-10/21/content_564…
8

Have kids aged 12 to 18 screened once for depression, and don't treat the school's psychological assessment as a diagnosis

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

US preventive guidelines recommend screening children aged 12 to 18 for major depression; for age 11 and under the evidence isn't there. Suicide is the second leading cause of death among 10-to-19-year-olds. The school's yearly psychological assessment is a population-wide screen, not a diagnosis. If your child says they're struggling, or eating, sleeping, interests, or grades suddenly change, book psychiatry or clinical psychology directly.

Cost
0 to a few dozen yuan for a screening questionnaire filled out at a community clinic or hospital outpatient department. Calls to the 12355 and 12356 hotlines are free.
Benefit
The US Preventive Services Task Force issued a recommendation statement in 2022. It recommends screening adolescents aged 12 to 18 for major depressive disorder (a B recommendation). A B means moderate certainty and a moderate benefit on balance — worth doing. For screening children aged 11 and under for major depression, the evidence is insufficient (an I statement — evidence lacking, no recommendation possible). For screening children and adolescents specifically for suicide risk, the evidence on both benefit and harm is insufficient (an I statement). The document notes that suicide is the second leading cause of death among people aged 10 to 19. It also notes that major depression in children and adolescents is closely tied to many later problems: depression recurring in adulthood, other mental disorders, and elevated risk of suicidal thoughts, suicide attempts, and suicide death. The Ten Measures to Further Strengthen Mental Health Work in Primary and Secondary Schools require building a three-tier service system of homeroom teachers, full-time and part-time mental health teachers, and psychiatrists. Each student takes a psychological assessment once per school year at most, as a general rule. The document also calls for advancing mechanisms for referring mental illness to medical care and for returning to school after recovery, and for making use of the 12355 youth service desk and the 12356 psychological assistance hotline (nationwide, issued October 2025)
Note
Grade B because the source grades the strength of a recommendation, not an effect that can be turned into a number. It is also a US recommendation; China has no corresponding official screening guidance. A positive screening result only means another evaluation is needed — it is not a diagnosis. What to do when there are suicidal thoughts: Section 1, card 25. How to respond at home: Section 29.
Sources (2 references)
US Preventive Services Task Force (2022). Screening for Depression and Suicide Risk in Children and Adolescents: US Preventive Services Task Force Recommendation Statement. JAMA. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.2022.16946; General Office of the Ministry of Education (2025). Ten Measures to Further Strengthen Mental Health Work in Primary and Secondary Schools (Jiao Ji Ting [2025] No. 2). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528…
9

Don't buy products or services claiming to 'cure myopia' or 'reduce your prescription'

Grade BValue: HighBasis: moneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

The market regulator says it outright: "Under current medical technology, myopia cannot be cured." Marketing built on claims like "recovery," "lower the prescription," "myopia cure," or "prescription repair" is to be investigated and punished to the full extent. See words like these and cross the product off — no need to compare prices. Eye-care devices count as medical devices, and e-commerce platforms are responsible for checking whether sellers are qualified to sell them.

Cost
Costs nothing — it saves you this money instead.
Benefit
A notice from the General Office of the State Administration for Market Regulation on a special rectification campaign running from November 2021 to March 2022 states explicitly: "Under current medical technology, myopia cannot be cured." The notice requires law-based, strict punishment of marketing children's and adolescents' myopia-prevention products with misleading phrases such as "rehabilitation," "recovery," "lower the prescription," "myopia cure," "nemesis of myopia," or "prescription repair." It calls for greater enforcement, aimed at conduct that trades on the name of traditional Chinese medicine, or borrows TCM theory and techniques, to market products and deceive consumers. It also requires cracking down hard on two kinds of false and illegal advertising: ads that use a patient's name or image for before-and-after comparisons, and ads that make guaranteed promises about the safety or efficacy of treatment. E-commerce platforms must strictly fulfill their responsibility to vet business qualifications for medical devices such as eye-care devices and related special goods (find out whether the seller is qualified to sell) (nationwide)
Note
Grade B because the basis is the regulator's enforcement position, not a controlled trial of the products. But on "myopia cannot be cured," the health authorities and the market regulator speak with one voice: the Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents says "myopia can be prevented and controlled, but not reversed." The two things with real evidence are card 4 (outdoors) and card 12 (proper refraction, glasses, and follow-up). Blue-light glasses: Section 6.
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the State Administration for Market Regulation (2021). Notice on Launching a Special Rectification Campaign Against Illegal and Irregular Commercial Marketing and Advertising of Children's and Adolescents' Myopia-Prevention Products. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-11/12/content_565…
10

Sleep, homework, PE, and exam rankings all have explicit written rules — if the school doesn't meet them, you can raise it

Grade BValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The documents are explicit: primary students sleep 10 hours a day, junior high 9 hours, senior high 8 hours. Morning classes generally start no earlier than 8:20 in primary school and no earlier than 8:00 in secondary school. Rules issued in 2025 add at least 2 hours of physical activity a day and a ban on ranking students by exam scores. If your child is chronically short of sleep, check against these rules first — don't start by blaming the child for dawdling.

Cost
Costs nothing. Know the rules, and if necessary raise them with the school or the local education administrative department. The hard part is speaking up.
Benefit
The Notice on Further Strengthening Sleep Management for Primary and Secondary School Students provides: primary students should sleep 10 hours a day, junior high students 9, senior high students 8. Morning classes generally start no earlier than 8:20 in primary school and 8:00 in secondary school. Schools may not require students to arrive early for unified teaching activities. Primary students should generally be in bed no later than 21:20, junior high students no later than 22:00, senior high students no later than 23:00. Offline training institutions must finish no later than 20:30, and live online classes no later than 21:00. From 22:00 to 8:00 the next day, no online game services may be provided to minors (nationwide, issued March 2021). The Ten Measures to Further Strengthen Mental Health Work in Primary and Secondary Schools add several rules: fully implement at least 2 hours of combined daily physical activity for primary and secondary students, and encourage a "15-minute break between classes." It also provides that students may not be ranked by exam scores, strictly prohibits mechanical, repetitive, and punitive homework, and encourages setting aside one "no-homework day" each week (nationwide, issued October 2025)
Note
Both are documents issued by the responsible authorities. How thoroughly they are enforced varies enormously from place to place and school to school — hence Grade B. Their use is to tell you which things the school is supposed to be doing already, so you go into the conversation with grounds in hand. The sleep accounting for adults: Sections 2 and 3.
Sources (2 references)
General Office of the Ministry of Education (2021). Ten Measures to Further Strengthen Mental Health Work in Primary and Secondary Schools (Jiao Ji Ting [2025] No. 2). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528…
11

A child who can't cope can take a leave of absence; the school must hold the enrollment for up to 1 year

Grade BValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

There is a formal leave-of-absence system. The parents or other guardians apply, the school confirms it and reports upward for approval. Up to 1 year at a time; if leave is still needed when it ends, apply again. While on leave, the school must keep the child's enrollment on record, and on returning the child picks up where they left off. Each province sets its own procedures — ask the school's academic affairs office or the local education bureau.

Cost
Costs nothing. The parents or other legal guardians apply to the school. The hard part is first accepting that the child needs to stop for a while.
Benefit
Article 16 of the Measures for Student Status Management of Primary and Secondary School Students sets out how leave works. Leave is applied for by the parents or other legal guardians. The school confirms it and reports to the higher-level student status management department for approval. When the student returns, the school must process the formalities promptly. One leave application runs no more than 1 year; if leave genuinely must continue past that, apply again. While a student is on leave, the school must keep their enrollment status (their standing and place are held). The detailed procedures for taking and resuming leave are set by provincial education administrative departments (nationwide, issued January 2025). The Ten Measures to Further Strengthen Mental Health Work in Primary and Secondary Schools require advancing mechanisms for referring mental illness to medical care and for returning to school after recovery, and guiding schools to draw up plans for handling sudden psychological crisis events on campus
Note
Before you go, get three things clear: what medical certificate is needed, how the leave is recorded in the enrollment system, and whether returning means going back to the original grade or repeating one. Grade B because the conditions for leave, the paperwork, and how re-entry works are all set by provincial education departments; the national level only provides the framework. The Regulations on the Protection of Minors in Schools also require compulsory-education schools to register students who drop out, take leave, or are absent long-term — so leave is something schools have handled before, not a special exception made for you alone.
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of Education (2025). Ten Measures to Further Strengthen Mental Health Work in Primary and Secondary Schools (Jiao Ji Ting [2025] No. 2). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202510/content_7045528…
12

If poor vision is found, get a cycloplegic refraction at a hospital, then recheck at the intervals the doctor gives

Grade BValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

Cycloplegic refraction means first putting in eyedrops that relax the muscle inside the eye responsible for focusing, then measuring the prescription. It is done at a hospital and is the most accurate way to diagnose myopia. The health commission states that the drops cause no damage to healthy eyes and everything returns to normal once they are stopped. Don't treat a one-off automated refraction at a glasses shop as a diagnosis, and don't refuse glasses out of fear that "the prescription will keep climbing."

Cost
A few dozen to a few hundred yuan in exam fees and glasses. After the drops, the child will be sensitive to light and blurry up close; it takes half a day to a day or two to wear off.
Benefit
The Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents spells out how cycloplegic refraction works. Cycloplegic drops first, then refraction. A cycloplegic is an eyedrop that relaxes the muscle in the eye responsible for focusing. Cycloplegic refraction is a medical refraction done at a hospital — the "gold standard" (the most accurate method) for diagnosing myopia. The drops cause no damage to healthy eyes; light sensitivity and blurry near vision can appear for a short time after use, and everything returns to normal once they are stopped. Once myopia is diagnosed, intervene promptly and scientifically, correcting with properly fitted glasses or the like. Properly fitted glasses effectively correct blurred vision and slow the progression of myopia. For those with normal corrected vision: preschool children and primary students recheck every 3 to 6 months, junior and senior high students every 6 to 12 months, with glasses replaced depending on the circumstances. Children should receive periodic refractive screening (prescription checks) at ages 1 to 3, 4 to 6, and after 7, to monitor the hyperopia reserve (nationwide, issued July 2023)
Note
Grade B because this is the guidance in an official health-education document, not primary research with hard numbers. High myopia leads to retinal detachment and similar problems, so follow-up isn't just about new glasses. "Poor vision" found at a school physical is only a first-pass screen; it still needs a full eye exam at a hospital — see card 7.
Sources (1 reference)
General Office of the National Health Commission (2023). Ten Core Messages for Myopia Prevention and Control Among Children and Adolescents (Guo Wei Ban Fu You Han [2023] No. 278). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202307/content_6894284…
13

Get pit-and-fissure sealants once the permanent molars come in

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: noBenefit: medium

A pit-and-fissure sealant seals the grooves on the chewing surfaces of the big molars with resin, so food debris cannot get packed in. Two years after sealing, the chance of a cavity is about one-eighth that of unsealed teeth. Without sealing, 16% of tooth surfaces decay; sealed, only about 5%. Still effective at four years.

Cost
A few dozen to one or two hundred yuan per tooth. No anesthesia, no drilling; a few minutes each time. Many places run free programs for children of the eligible age.
Benefit
38 trials with 7,924 children aged 5 to 16, systematically assembled by Cochrane and pooled. Resin sealants compared with no sealing. For first permanent molars in children aged 5 to 10, at 24 months the odds of decay were OR 0.12 (95% CI 0.08–0.19) — about one-eighth the chance of decay compared with no sealant. This figure comes from 7 trials, with 1,548 children randomized and 1,322 finally examined; evidence quality moderate. If 16% of surfaces in the control group decay within 24 months, the sealed figure is 5.2% (3.13%–7.37%). If the control rate is 40%: 6.25% (3.84%–9.63%). At 70%: 19% (12.3%–27.2%). At 48 to 54 months, OR 0.21 (0.16–0.28) — still about one-fifth of unsealed. The authors conclude that resin sealants produce 11% to 51% less decay than no sealing at 24 months. In the 4 trials that recorded adverse effects, none appeared. Between alternative sealing materials such as glass ionomer, there is not enough evidence to say which is better
Note
The first permanent molar (the big tooth that is never replaced) usually erupts around age 6, the second around age 12. Seal soon after the tooth comes in, before it decays — once it has a cavity, only a filling will do. Many regions list sealants for age-eligible children as a free service; ask your local CDC or community health service center. This section found no national document that could be verified word for word, so coverage and age ranges are not given. Dental caries is also a priority guidance item in school physicals — see card 7.
Sources (1 reference)
Ahovuo-Saloranta A, et al. (2017). Pit and fissure sealants for preventing dental decay in permanent teeth. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD001830.pub5
14

If your child games a lot, first check whether sleep, homework, and outdoor time are being squeezed out — don't just stare at hours played

Grade BValue: FairBasis: timeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: small

Only about two or three in a hundred people actually meet the bar for "gaming disorder." Questionnaires with low thresholds, aimed at teenagers, push the rate artificially high. Judging by real records from game companies, how much someone plays and how they feel are barely related. Under the rules, minors may only play from 8 to 9 p.m. on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and public holidays.

Cost
Costs nothing. Once a week, take note of when the child goes to sleep, whether homework was handed in, and whether they got outside.
Benefit
A meta-analysis pooled 53 studies from 17 countries, 226,247 people. The prevalence of gaming disorder was 3.05% (95% CI 2.38–3.91 — that is the confidence range). Counting only studies with stricter sampling: 1.96%. Results differed widely across studies; 77% of the difference was attributable to which questionnaire was used. Teenage samples, low threshold scores, and small samples all push the rate up. Another study obtained data from 7 game companies and connected 38,935 players' actual playtime over six weeks with their self-reported well-being. Almost no evidence turned up that hours played affects well-being. The National Press and Publication Administration requires that game companies provide only 1 hour of service to minors, from 20:00 to 21:00, on Fridays, Saturdays, Sundays, and statutory holidays (nationwide / international, from 2021)
Note
Grade B because prevalence swings too much with the questionnaire, and the well-being study followed only six weeks. Gaming's most common cost is squeezing out sleep and time outdoors. The written requirements on sleep: card 10 of this section (sleep, homework, PE). Outdoors: card 4 (2 hours outdoors a day). Screen time: card 5 (no more than 1 hour a day of non-study use). Top-ups and refunds: Section 5, card 9 (children topping up and tipping on a phone). When grades, sleep, and family relationships all slide at once and nothing you say stops it, take the child to psychiatry or child psychology. Don't send them to a locked-down internet-addiction school — card 18 of this section (internet-addiction schools). The beneficiary is the child.
Sources (3 references)
Stevens MW, Dorstyn D, Delfabbro PH, King DL. (2021). Global prevalence of gaming disorder: A systematic review and meta-analysis. 15

If your child says they like the same sex, don't scold, don't kick them out, don't send them to be 'corrected': your attitude at home is tied to whether they might attempt suicide

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Among Chinese middle and high school students, children attracted to the same sex or to both sexes attempted suicide over the past year at roughly 3 to 5.5 times the rate of the others. International research finds that adolescents strongly rejected by their families attempt suicide far more often later on. Those sent by their parents to be "corrected" attempted suicide the most.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is the parents first digesting their own emotions and not saying something harsh in the moment.
Benefit
A Chinese survey covered 506 middle schools in 7 provinces, 150,822 students from the first year of junior high through the last year of senior high. Attempted suicide in the past year: among boys, 2.2% of those attracted only to the opposite sex, 6.9% of those attracted only to the same sex, and 12.2% of those attracted to both. For girls the figures were 3.1%, 8.9%, and 10.9%. That works out to roughly 3 to 5.5 times the rate of classmates attracted only to the opposite sex. The researchers adjusted for age, academic pressure, family finances, and being bullied. Afterward, the two boys' groups showed ORs of 3.13 (95% CI 2.28–4.28) and 3.83 (2.85–5.14) — about two to three times higher. A meta-analysis pooling 35 studies found that sexual-minority adolescents attempted suicide at OR 3.50 (2.98–4.12). A US study interviewed 224 gay and bisexual young adults aged 21 to 25, asking them to recall how their families had reacted in adolescence. Compared with peers whose families barely rejected them, those with high family rejection had OR 8.4 for attempted suicide. In another study, where the parents themselves tried to change their child's sexual orientation, the child's odds of a suicide attempt were OR 3.08 (1.39–6.83); where the parents also sent the child to therapists or religious figures, 5.07 (2.38–10.79) (China / multiple countries / US)
Note
Grade B because these are all one-off surveys, and the degree of family rejection was recalled in adulthood — they can show association, but not who causes what. Parents don't have to accept anything right away; just don't do things that hurt the child. In law, parents may not abuse or abandon a child, and may not commit domestic violence against them. Repeated verbal abuse and intimidation also count as domestic violence. If the child is low and says they don't want to live, call 12356 first — Section 1, card 25 (call 12356 when there are suicidal thoughts). You can also go to psychiatry per card 8 of this section (one depression screen at ages 12 to 18). Why "correction" must be avoided: Section 6, card 28 (don't do sexual-orientation correction). The beneficiary is the child — and you yourself.
Sources (6 references)

16

Discipline without hitting, yelling, or calling them stupid: kids who are regularly hit or berated have more behavioral and emotional problems

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Regularly spanked children show more aggression and more psychological problems, are more distant from their parents, and are also on the receiving end of harsher beatings more often. Whether hitting makes a child obey on the spot, the evidence can't say. Children who at 13 are regularly yelled at and called stupid have more conduct problems and depression afterward — and however warm the parents are otherwise, it doesn't cancel out.

Cost
Costs nothing. The hard part is stopping your hands and your mouth at the moment the temper flares, and switching to a way of disciplining without hitting or yelling. What to switch to: card 17 of this section (a parenting course that teaches concrete techniques).
Benefit
First, hitting. A meta-analysis counted only "open-handed spanking on the buttocks or limbs." It pooled 75 studies, 111 effect sizes, 160,927 children in total. Of 17 outcomes, 13 were significantly related to being spanked, all in the bad direction. d is effect size: 0.2 counts as small, 0.5 as medium. Aggression in childhood: d = 0.37 (95% CI 0.13–0.61, the confidence range). Externalizing problems 0.41 — hitting people, breaking rules, that kind. Internalizing problems 0.24 — anxiety, depression, that kind. Mental health problems 0.53; a worse relationship with parents 0.51; lower self-esteem 0.15; weaker cognitive ability 0.17. Being physically abused by the parents 0.64. Antisocial behavior in adulthood 0.36; mental health problems 0.24. All 111 effect sizes pooled: d = 0.33 (0.29–0.38). Whether the child complied on the spot was not clearly related to being hit (d = 0.14, −0.19–0.47) — and that item rests on only 5 effect sizes. Another review looked only at studies that tracked children over time, 69 in total. Physical punishment consistently predicted more behavior problems later on; no link to any long-term good outcome was seen. In the 7 of those studies that counted how often children were hit, 5 found the more hitting, the worse the problems. Now yelling. A US study followed 976 two-parent families. When parents at the child's age 13 frequently yelled, cursed, or called the child stupid or lazy, the child's conduct problems and depressive symptoms both increased between ages 13 and 14. However warm the parents were otherwise, it did not offset the association. It ran both ways: children with more conduct problems at 13 were also yelled at more afterward. In law, parents may not commit domestic violence against their children. Article 2 of the Anti-Domestic Violence Law lists its forms: beating, binding, maiming, restricting personal freedom, as well as recurring verbal abuse and intimidation. Article 12 of the law requires guardians to carry out family education in a civilized manner. Where parents infringe the child's rights and interests, the residents' or villagers' committee is to admonish and stop them, and to report to the police in serious cases. Where the police, procuratorates, or courts discover it, they should admonish the parents and may order them to receive family education guidance (nationwide)
Note
Contested. Almost all of these studies only track what happens, without comparison groups, so they cannot show who causes what. In the spanking meta-analysis, 72% of the studies only looked at whether two things occurred together, or relied on later recall. Another meta-analysis, taking only prospective studies and subtracting the child's prior behavior, left the association between spanking and externalizing problems at just 0.07, and with internalizing problems at just 0.10. That paper's authors consider the effect very small. Yet another meta-analysis found that "conditional spanking" worked better than 10 of 13 other discipline tactics at reducing noncompliance and antisocial behavior. It also found that when spanking was too harsh or was the main tool, it did worse than the alternatives. So what the other side can establish is: hitting a little, conditionally, is not necessarily worse than other tactics. Hitting hard, or hitting and yelling often, both sides agree is worse. An occasional swat or shout is not what the statutes name as domestic violence — they name beating and recurring verbal abuse and intimidation. The main beneficiary is the child. If someone else in the household is hitting the child: calling the police and applying for a protection order — Section 8, card 43 (personal safety protection order). Anyone who sees a child being beaten at length in another family has the right to dissuade them, or to report to the public security, civil affairs, or education authorities. For a stranger's household, calling 110 or telling the residents' committee is enough — don't go and break up the fight yourself.

17

If your child is hard to manage and you can't stop hitting or yelling, take a parenting course that teaches concrete techniques

Grade AValue: FairBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Courses that teach parents concrete techniques: in lottery-assigned trials, children's hitting and rule-breaking went down, and parents' moods improved too. Parents also hit and yelled at their children less — most marked right after the course, still there one or two years later, but much smaller. Shanghai has tried this kind of course too; it worked.

Cost
Parenting schools run by schools, kindergartens, and communities are public-interest and free of charge. The courses with evidence meet weekly or every other week, one to two hours a session, for anywhere from four to twenty-four weeks. You practice at home between sessions. The hard part is seeing the course through and practicing every day.
Benefit
Cochrane pooled 13 trials, 10 of them lottery-assigned, covering 1,078 parents. The children were 3 to 12 years old and all had behavior problems. Among parents who took a course, children's behavior problems went down. By the parents' own ratings: SMD −0.53 (95% CI −0.72 to −0.34, the confidence range); by independent observers: −0.44 (−0.77 to −0.11). SMD and d are the same yardstick; 0.5 counts as medium. The parents' mental health improved: −0.36 (−0.52 to −0.20). Negative or harsh discipline went down: parents' own ratings −0.77 (−0.96 to −0.59), observers' −0.42 (−0.67 to −0.16). The authors call these short-term effects. Another meta-analysis screened 346 lottery-assigned trials, 60 of which measured behaviors like hitting and berating children, spread across 22 countries. Hitting and berating went down right after the course: d = −0.46 (−0.59 to −0.33). At 1 to 6 months: −0.24 (−0.37 to −0.11). At 7 to 24 months: −0.18 (−0.34 to −0.02) — the further out, the smaller. Most of these data were reported by the parents themselves. There are trials in China too. In Shanghai, 81 parents were lottery-assigned, some to a group Triple P course. After the course, the children's adjustment problems and the parents' discipline and mood were all better than among the parents still waiting for the course, and still better at 6 months. At one rural kindergarten, 191 adults caring for children took part; some worked through an online course on their own, plus two group discussions. After two weeks, they reported about 33% less maltreating behavior than those given only a book to read (IRR 0.67). Three months later, the children's behavior problems had gone down too (d = −0.40). The Family Education Promotion Law requires parents to consciously learn about family education. Primary and secondary schools and kindergartens may run parenting schools and regularly organize public-interest family education guidance. Residents' and villagers' committees may run community parenting schools. Governments at the provincial level and above must open public-interest online parenting schools and service hotlines. Family education guidance organizations may not organize for-profit training (nationwide, effective January 1, 2022)
Note
Grade A because there are pooled numbers from Cochrane and multiple lottery-based trials. The courses in the trials share several features. The instructor teaches concrete techniques, such as playing with the child, praise, rewards, and discipline. Parents practice and rehearse in class, with homework to do at home. Courses that only handed out materials or only held discussions were excluded, so the evidence does not cover the one-off lecture kind. What public-interest parenting schools in China teach, and how, varies from place to place and may not be this type. When picking a course, check whether it runs for several weeks in a row and makes you practice concrete techniques. Names that come up: Triple P, Incredible Years, Parent-Child Interaction Therapy (PCIT). This book does not recommend specific providers or paid products. The reduction in hitting and yelling shrinks after a year or two — keep practicing after the course ends. The beneficiary is the child, and you too. If the child already has serious emotional problems, take them to psychiatry or child psychology — card 8 of this section (depression screening).
Sources (5 references)

Never send your child to locked-down 'internet addiction schools' or 'boot camps': the law bans methods that harm body and mind, and children have already died in confinement

Grade CValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

The law explicitly bans methods that harm a child's body or mind to break internet addiction. At a boot-camp school in Hefei, a boy newly sent there was handcuffed inside a confinement room; after about 44 hours he was dead. At Yuzhang Academy in Nanchang, students were locked in solitary; several people in charge were sentenced, and the parents' demand for tuition refunds got no support from the court.

Cost
Costs nothing — it saves a tuition fee. The hard part is holding back, when the child is at their most out of control, from handing them over to outsiders for "locked-down discipline."
Benefit
Article 68 of the Law on the Protection of Minors provides that no organization or individual may intervene in a minor's internet addiction in ways that harm the minor's physical or mental health. Both cases below have court judgments. The first was in Hefei, Anhui. In August 2017, the parents of an 18-year-old boy signed an agreement with a boot-camp school to send him there for internet-addiction treatment. School staff took him away by force, locked him in a confinement room, and handcuffed both his hands to the window bars. They restricted his food, water, and rest, and beat him. About 44 hours later, the boy died. The forensic conclusion: death from water-electrolyte disturbance caused by high temperature, a restrained posture, lack of food and drink, and physical injury. On October 31, 2018, the Hefei Intermediate People's Court ruled at first instance: the school's person in charge, guilty of intentional injury and unlawful detention, was sentenced to 16 years; four instructors were sentenced to 1 year to 8 years 6 months. On December 28, 2018, the Anhui Higher People's Court upheld the original judgment on appeal. The appellate ruling states that the school had never been approved by the relevant authorities, and that none of the defendants held teaching qualifications. The second case was in Nanchang, Jiangxi. Yuzhang Academy opened in 2013 and was deregistered and closed in November 2017. While operating, the school took some students into a "vexation-relief room" for solitary confinement, with a dedicated guard watching, three to ten days at a time. On April 28, 2023, the Anyuan District Court of Pingxiang announced the first-instance verdict on retrial: five defendants guilty of unlawful detention. Four were sentenced to terms ranging from 11 months to 2 years 10 months and barred from education-related work for a set period; one was exempted from criminal punishment. The parents demanded the tuition and round-trip travel costs back; the court did not support them (nationwide / Anhui / Jiangxi)
Note
Grade C because there are only individual cases, with no statistics on how often such schools go wrong. The Hefei case is known only through media reports, which cite the first-instance judgment and the appellate ruling; the full judgment text was not found on the courts' official websites. The Yuzhang Academy case is Xinhua's report of the court announcing the verdict. If your child games a lot, first follow card 14 of this section (a child who games a lot): check whether sleep, homework, and time outdoors are being squeezed out. If grades, sleep, and family relationships collapse together and nothing you say stops it, take the child to psychiatry or child psychology and let a doctor diagnose before treating. If the child has already been sent to one, bring the child home. If the child says they were locked up or beaten, call the police. The beneficiary is the child.
Sources (7 references)

Verdict in the Jiangxi "Yuzhang Academy case": all 5 defendants accept the judgment and will not appeal. http://www.news.cn/2023-04/28/c_1129579126.htm (web archive http://web.archive.org/web/20230428212544/http://www.news.c…)

31. Your Options After Turning Eighteen

16 items

This section is about money and time; the refusal-to-serve entry also touches personal freedom. This is a route map, not a manual for any one route. The section first lays the legal thresholds of each path side by side, then goes through them one by one, covering the things you only need once you know them: what you get from military service, what doors into the system exist besides the civil-service exam, which two college majors point straight at an establishment position when you file your preferences, whether a missing degree can be made up later, what kind of company to look for if you want to work abroad, what people without an employer do about social insurance, and whether there is a loan with part of the interest paid by the state when you have no startup capital. The roads open after eighteen go far beyond what this section covers. Only the ones backed by nationwide public documents, with thresholds and benefits that can be checked line by line, are included here. Joining a state-owned enterprise, working in a factory, crewing ships, freelancing, or continuing into high school and college are all viable paths too. They just have no single document to check against, and this book won't write their conditions from impressions. Choosing a path is your own business. This section offers two things only: which document each threshold is written in, and which deadlines and expiring qualifications go void once you set out. For how to work out studying versus working and how to pick a skill, see Section 23. For overtime pay, workplace injury, and severance once you are in a job, see Section 19. For the capital and exit of opening a shop or company, see Section 12. Studying abroad is in Section 32. Coverage after unemployment is in Section 7. None of that is repeated here.

1

First check yourself against the thresholds: the age and education requirements of all twelve paths are spelled out in hard rules

Grade AValue: HighBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The age and education thresholds for these twelve paths are all spelled out in writing. For regular work you must be at least 16. For military service, men must be 18, with the limit relaxed to 24 for university graduates. The civil-service exam requires 18 to 35 years old and an associate degree or above. The self-taught exam and registering as a sole proprietor look at neither education nor age.

Cost
Costs nothing. Spend ten minutes checking yourself against the list to see what you qualify for.
Benefit
For military service see the Military Service Law: "Male citizens who have reached the age of eighteen shall be drafted for active service; those not drafted in that year may still be drafted for active service before the age of twenty-two. The drafting age may be relaxed to twenty-four for graduates of regular institutions of higher education and to twenty-six for graduate students." For the civil-service exam see Article 18 of the Civil Servants Recruitment Rules. Application conditions include "aged eighteen or above but under thirty-five" and "an educational level of junior college (associate degree) or above." These two items may be appropriately adjusted with approval from civil-service authorities at the provincial level or above. Article 19 of the rules lists five categories of people who may not apply, such as those who received criminal punishment for a crime, those dismissed from public office, and those listed as subjects of joint disciplinary action for dishonesty. For firefighters see the Measures for Recruiting Firefighters of the National Comprehensive Fire and Rescue Teams. Article 5: "aged 18 or above and under 22" and "educated at senior high school level or above." Article 6: "people with an associate degree or above, and veterans of the PLA and the People's Armed Police … may have the age relaxed to 24." For military civilian positions see Article 9 of the Regulations on Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army; basic conditions include "having reached the age of 18." Article 19 of the regulations states that for lower-rank positions the maximum age for first-time recruitment is 35. Lower-rank positions are entry-level positions. For public institutions see Article 8 of the Regulations on Personnel Management of Public Institutions: "When public institutions newly hire staff, they shall conduct open recruitment from society." For sole proprietorships see the Regulation on Promoting the Development of Individual Industrial and Commercial Households: "Citizens with business capability … who register as individual industrial and commercial households in accordance with law are governed by this regulation." For the self-taught exam see the Interim Regulations on Self-Taught Higher Education Examinations. Article 3: "Citizens of the People's Republic of China, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, race, or level of education already received, may take the self-taught higher education examinations in accordance with these regulations." Article 20: "Students currently enrolled in full-time schools of all levels and types may not register." For publicly funded teacher-training students see Article 2 of the Implementation Measures for Government-Funded Teacher Education with Integrated Undergraduate-Master's Training at Normal Universities Directly under the Ministry of Education. Recruitment happens only at six ministry-affiliated normal universities: Beijing Normal University, East China Normal University, Northeast Normal University, Central China Normal University, Shaanxi Normal University, and Southwest University. The undergraduate and master's stages are designed as one program with staged assessment; after finishing the bachelor's you go straight into the master's. Tuition and dormitory fees during enrollment are covered by the central treasury, plus a living stipend. Article 5 of the measures: "Recruitment of publicly funded teacher-training students uses early-batch admission" — that is, admitted before the regular batch. For targeted medical students see the Notice on Employment Placement and Contract Performance Management of Rural Order-Targeted Free Medical Students. It states: "After admission but before receiving the admission letter, students must sign an agreement with the training school and the county-level health … and human resources and social security departments where the targeted employment is located." For working abroad see the Regulation on the Administration of Foreign Labor Cooperation. Article 5: engaging in foreign labor cooperation requires a business qualification approved by the commerce authorities. Article 7, paragraph 4: "Without obtaining the foreign labor cooperation business qualification certificate and completing registration in accordance with law, no one may engage in foreign labor cooperation." A company without this certificate that organizes people to work abroad is itself breaking the law. Article 8, paragraph 2: "No organization or individual may organize workers to go abroad for work under the guise of business, tourism, or study." Taking orders via platforms and flexible employment have no statutory education threshold; for enrolling yourself in insurance and occupational-injury protection see items 11 and 12 of this section. The Compulsory Education Law "prohibits employers from hiring school-age children and adolescents who should be receiving compulsory education" (nationwide)
Note
Once you clear the threshold, you still have to pass political conditions, the physical exam, and the political review. These gates have no public scoring standards; you won't find them in the text. For entry into secondary vocational schools, technical colleges, and through-track vocational enrollment see item 5 of Section 23; for financial aid when the family can't afford it see item 4 of Section 23. The sole-proprietor path looks at no credentials, but opening a shop isn't easy. For capital, personal guarantees, and the cost of closing down see Section 12. A personal guarantee means if the company can't repay, you repay yourself. For whether startup money can be borrowed with the state covering part of the interest, see item 16 of this section. The publicly funded teacher-training and targeted medical student paths are locked in on the day you file college preferences; the price is in item 13. The threshold for working abroad isn't on you but on whether the company is qualified; how to verify that is in item 14. Which path is the better deal is not compared here.

Register for military service before October 31 of the year you turn 18; conscripts serve exactly two years of active duty

Grade AValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Military service registration is a legal obligation, not enlisting; registering doesn't mean you have to go. Males who turn 18 that year must complete registration online before October 31. If you don't register, the county will order you to correct it within a time limit; if you still don't, you can be compelled to perform military service duty and fined. If you actually serve, conscripts serve exactly two years of active duty.

Cost
Costs nothing. Registration is a one-time online form that takes a few minutes. If you actually serve, the cost is two years full time — during those two years you can't do anything else alongside.
Benefit
For registration see the Provisions on Military Service Registration Work. It states: "The military service organs of the people's governments of counties, autonomous counties, cities not divided into districts, and municipal districts shall, before October 31 each year, organize initial military service registration for male citizens in their jurisdictions who reach the age of 18 before December 31 of that year." The same provisions state: "Initial military service registration is conducted mainly online, completed independently by citizens through the military service registration online platform." What happens if you don't register: see Article 57, paragraph 1 of the Military Service Law, which covers "those who refuse or evade military service registration." The penalty is "the county-level people's government orders correction within a time limit; if not corrected within the time limit, the county-level people's government compels performance of military service duty and imposes a fine." The Military Service Law also states "the term of active service for conscripts is two years" and "citizens who have reached 17 but not 18 may, based on the military's needs and personal willingness, be enlisted for active service." NCOs "who have served twelve years of active duty or meet other conditions set by the state are given jobs by the local government at or above the county level in the place of resettlement." NCOs "who have served thirty years of active duty, reached fifty-five years of age, or meet other state-set conditions are resettled under retirement arrangements." Being given a job means the government provides one; retirement resettlement means you are processed out as a retiree. The Regulations on Conscription Work state that priority goes to "the recruitment of graduates of regular institutions of higher education and of personnel with special political, physical, or professional-skill requirements." The regulations also state that "enlisted citizens who are full-time students or fresh graduates of regular institutions of higher education may enlist at their pre-enrollment household registration location or where their school is located" (nationwide)
Note
Registration and enlisting are two different things, with hugely different costs. The string of penalties including the two-year exit ban only punishes those who renege after enlisting; see item 3 (refusal to serve). Women are not required to do initial registration and are recruited based on military needs. Conditions for enlisted soldiers applying to military academies, or for outstanding soldiers becoming officers (promotion from the ranks), are in internal military regulations and can't be found outside. The Military Service Law says only two things: active-duty officers are selected from "outstanding active-duty soldiers" and similar personnel, and military academy admissions are not bound by drafting age limits. Specific cutoff scores and quotas are not given in this book.
Sources (3 references)
General Office of the State Council, General Office of the Central Military Commission (2025). Provisions on Military Service Registration Work (Guoban Fa [2025] No. 41). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202512/content_7051363…; NPC Standing Committee (2021). Military Service Law (2021 revision, Articles 20, 25, 26, 54, 57). http://www.mod.gov.cn/regulatory/2021-08/20/content_4892491… (published by the Ministry of National Defense); State Council, Central Military Commission (2023). Regulations on Conscription Work (State Council and CMC Decree No. 759, Article 5). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2023/content_5753313.htm

Refuse to serve after being drafted, and for two years you can't leave the country or resume studies, and you're barred from the civil service and state-owned enterprises

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Sign up and then refuse to serve, and the consequences come in a chain. You can't be hired as a civil servant, and state-owned enterprises and public institutions can't take you either. For two years you may not leave the country, may not advance to further schooling, and may not return to resume studies at your school. You'll also be placed on the roster of seriously dishonest subjects in fulfilling national defense obligations. So "sign up first and back out later if it doesn't work" is an expensive idea.

Cost
Costs nothing. The cost is deciding clearly whether you'll go before you sign up.
Benefit
Article 57, paragraph 1, item 2 of the Military Service Law covers "enlisted citizens who refuse or evade being drafted for active service." The penalty is likewise "the county-level people's government orders correction within a time limit; if not corrected, the county-level people's government compels performance of military service duty and imposes a fine." Paragraph 2 of the same article: "Those who commit the act in item 2 of the preceding paragraph and refuse to correct it may not be hired as civil servants or as staff managed with reference to the Civil Servant Law of the People's Republic of China, may not be recruited or employed by state-owned enterprises or public institutions, may not leave the country or advance to or resume studies for two years, and are placed on the roster of seriously dishonest subjects in fulfilling national defense obligations for joint disciplinary action." Joint disciplinary action means multiple departments enforce the above restrictions together off the same roster. Article 58 extends the same penalties to those already enlisted. When a soldier refuses to perform duties or deserts the unit to evade military service, the consequences depend on the disposition. Those removed from the rolls, expelled from military status, or criminally prosecuted are punished under Article 57, paragraph 2; among them, those removed from the rolls are additionally fined (nationwide, effective October 1, 2021)
Note
What's tallied here is personal freedom and employment eligibility, not money. This chain of penalties punishes only two kinds of people: those who "refuse or evade being drafted for active service," and those who after enlisting are removed from the rolls, expelled from military status, or criminally prosecuted. Merely failing to register is not included — registration is item 2. The penalty requires "refusal to correct," determined and imposed by the county-level people's government. How much the fine is, each locality decides; this book doesn't give it. Whether to go is your call, but make it before you sign up.
Sources (1 reference)
NPC Standing Committee (2021). Military Service Law (2021 revision, Articles 57, 58). http://www.mod.gov.cn/regulatory/2021-08/20/content_4892491… (published by the Ministry of National Defense)

The two most tangible perks of serving as a college student: tuition subsidies up to 20,000 yuan a year, enrollment held for two years, and special tracks for graduate admissions

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Current students, fresh graduates, and newly admitted students who enlist get their tuition for the years of study paid by the state, reimbursed at what you actually paid — up to 20,000 yuan a year for undergraduate and vocational students, up to 25,000 yuan for graduate students. If your tuition is already low, you're reimbursed only up to what you actually paid. Your enrollment status is held for two years. For graduate school there is a separate special plan open only to veteran college-student soldiers.

Cost
Costs nothing. After discharge, submit materials to apply as your school requires, a trip or two in all.
Benefit
A 2024 notice from the Ministry of Finance and three other departments says college students who go serve in the military get three benefits: tuition compensation, repayment on their behalf of national student loans used for tuition, and tuition waivers. Repayment on your behalf means the state pays off that student loan for you. The standard for all three was "adjusted accordingly to a maximum of 20,000 yuan per student per year for undergraduate and vocational students and 25,000 yuan per student per year for graduate students." The new standard takes effect from the fall semester of 2024. How much you get depends on this sentence: "implemented at the higher of the two amounts — the tuition the student actually paid or the national student loan obtained (including principal and interest accrued before full repayment)." A later sentence adds "the portion exceeding the standard is not compensated, repaid, or waived." So what you get each year is the smaller of "the higher of actual tuition and the student loan" and the cap. If tuition is 5,000 yuan a year, you get 5,000. The number of years covered counts your years of study, not your years of service. The 2019 Measures for Managing Student Financial Aid Funds state: "The prescribed years of study completed before enlistment are the years counted for tuition compensation or national student loan repayment; the remaining prescribed years of study completed after resuming studies following discharge are the years counted for tuition waiver." For fresh graduates who enlist, the tuition for the entire program is compensated. For enrollment status see the Veterans Support Law: "Active-duty personnel who before enlistment were admitted to or were already studying at a regular institution of higher education retain their admission status or student status during active service; within two years after discharge they are allowed to enroll or resume studies, and may transfer to another major at the same school under relevant state rules." The law also states: "Institutions of higher education may, under national overall arrangements, admit veterans through separate quotas and independent recruitment." For graduate admissions see the Ministry of Education General Office's 2026 notice. The plan is called the "Veteran College-Student Soldier Plan." The notice states: "It is issued as a separate quota within the total scale of the national master's admissions plan and used exclusively for this purpose; it may not be converted into regular plans or other special plans. Admitting institutions independently set … the preliminary-exam score requirements (generally no higher than those for regular-plan applicants in the corresponding discipline) … and, under equal conditions, applicants with longer service are admitted with priority." Separate and exclusive means this quota is carved out and can only be used to admit veteran college-student soldiers. In 2026 the plan is carried by 532 regular institutions of higher education (nationwide)
Note
There are two more channels. One is the exam-free associate-to-bachelor upgrade: vocational students who enlist can, after discharge and finishing their vocational degree, apply for exam-free admission to a bachelor's program, with schools testing vocational skills and admitting the best. This applies from the 2022 admissions cycle; see your province's notice from that year for details. The other is 10 extra points on the graduate preliminary exam: veteran college-student soldiers get 10 points added to their preliminary-exam total if they apply within 3 years of discharge. If you apply through the special plan you don't also get the bonus points; the two can't be combined. Those awarded a second-class merit citation or above can apply to skip the preliminary exam for graduate school. The list of schools running the special plan changes yearly — 523 schools in 2025. The tuition standard has been adjusted twice: 8,000/12,000 in 2019, changed to 16,000/20,000 in fall 2023, and to 20,000/25,000 in fall 2024. A 2022 summary from the Ministry of Veterans Affairs still carries the earliest version — don't copy it.

After discharge, only six situations get a government-arranged job; those going into self-employment must report within 30 days

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

"Join the army and you're guaranteed a job" is long gone as a general rule. Now only six situations get a government-arranged job, and most conscripts who serve two years and leave don't fall into any of them. The category without government job placement is called self-employment, and it has a hard deadline: you must report within 30 days of leaving active duty. Exceed 30 days without a valid reason and you're treated as forfeiting your resettlement benefits.

Cost
Costs nothing. Take your discharge certificate and make one trip to the veterans affairs department in the resettlement area.
Benefit
Article 25 of the Regulation on the Resettlement of Veterans lists six situations where the resettlement-area people's government arranges a job. The text: "(1) NCOs who have served 12 years of active duty; (2) those who personally earned a medal or honorary title during active service; (3) those who personally won a third-class combat merit award or a second-class merit award or higher during active service; (4) those who personally received a first-class commendation during active service; (5) those rated disability grade 5 to 8 from war-related disability; (6) children of martyrs." The regulation also states: "The resettlement-area people's government shall complete the task of arranging work for discharged NCOs and conscripts within 6 months of receiving them." Employers "shall sign with them a medium-to-long-term employment contract or labor contract of no less than 3 years as required. Among these, enterprises taking discharged NCOs with more than 10 years of military service shall sign open-ended labor contracts with them." Open-ended means the contract carries no end date. While awaiting job placement, a living allowance "is paid monthly at the local monthly minimum wage standard." If placement is delayed for reasons not your own, a living stipend "is paid monthly at no less than 80% of the average wage of comparable personnel at the unit until you start the job." Situations where job-placement resettlement is not allowed include expulsion from the Communist Party of China and criminal punishment. The self-employment deadline is in Article 51: "Discharged NCOs and conscripts going into self-employment shall report to the veterans affairs department of the resettlement-area people's government within 30 days of being approved to leave active duty. Failing to report on time beyond 30 days without a valid reason is deemed forfeiture of resettlement benefits." (nationwide, effective September 1, 2024)
Note
On the same day this regulation took effect, the 2011 Regulation on the Resettlement of Retired Soldiers (State Council and CMC Decree No. 608) was repealed. Many online guides still cite the old regulation; the conditions have been reworded — the old version said "won a second-class merit award or above in peacetime or a third-class merit award or above in wartime." The 30-day deadline applies only to the self-employment category; other resettlement types require reporting "at the prescribed time." At reporting you'll be issued the veterans preferential-treatment card; the discharge payment, employment and startup support, and education aid that follow all hook onto this.
Sources (2 references)
State Council, Central Military Commission (2024). Regulation on the Resettlement of Veterans (State Council and CMC Decree No. 787, promulgated July 29, 2024, effective September 1; Articles 25, 31, 32, 35, 51, 75). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2024/issue_11526/202408/content_…; NPC Standing Committee (2020). Veterans Support Law (Articles 13, 14, 15). http://www.mod.gov.cn/gfbw/fgwx/flfg/16048597.html (published by the Ministry of National Defense)
6

Three tallies after discharge: the one-time discharge payment, military service counting as work years, and a 20,000-yuan annual tax deduction if you work for yourself

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

There are three tallies after discharge. The first is the one-time discharge payment for those going into self-employment, paid by years of active service, with an uplift for merit citations. The second: your service years are not a blank in social insurance — military service counts as work years, and contribution years are combined with those before enlistment and after discharge. The third is tax: if you open your own shop or business, you can pay up to 20,000 yuan less in taxes each year for 3 years.

Cost
Costs nothing. At discharge the military transfers out your social insurance account and money. You then go to the social insurance handling agency (the social insurance window) in the resettlement area to complete the transfer.
Benefit
For the first, see the Regulation on the Resettlement of Veterans. It states: "Discharged NCOs and conscripts going into self-employment are paid a one-time discharge payment based on their years of active service." Who pays: "It is specially arranged by the central treasury; the specific standard is set by the State Council's veterans affairs department and the CMC's political work department together with the State Council's finance department … and adjusted as appropriate." The uplift has five tiers: 25% extra for a medal or honorary title; 20% for a first-class combat merit or first-class commendation; 15% for a second-class combat merit, first-class merit, or second-class commendation; 10% for a third-class combat merit or second-class merit; 5% for a fourth-class combat merit or third-class merit. The regulation also states: "Veterans who have not found employment in time may claim unemployment insurance benefits from the human resources and social security department where their household is registered; their years of active service are deemed contribution years, except for veterans resettled through retirement or support arrangements." Deemed contribution years means even though you paid nothing those years, they count as if you had. For the second, see the Veterans Support Law: "Veterans' years of active service count as work years and are cumulative with years at their post-discharge employer." Work years are years in the workforce; the service years and the years after discharge add together. The law also states that years of active service and the pre-enlistment and post-discharge pension, medical, and unemployment contribution years "are combined in accordance with law," and that "the active-service experience of discharged NCOs and conscripts is regarded as grassroots work experience." The Military Insurance Law: "A servicemember's years of active service are deemed employee basic medical insurance contribution years and are combined with contribution years under employee basic medical insurance before enlistment and after leaving active duty." For the third, see Announcement No. 14 [2023] of the Ministry of Finance, the State Taxation Administration, and the Ministry of Veterans Affairs. It covers retired soldiers going into self-employment: "Within 3 years (36 months, same below), per household and per year, up to a 20,000-yuan limit, they may deduct in sequence from the value-added tax, urban maintenance and construction tax, education surcharge, local education surcharge, and individual income tax actually payable that year. The cap may be raised by up to 20%." Deduction means subtracting in sequence from the taxes actually due that year, up to the limit — it is not money paid to you. For enterprises that hire them, "the fixed quota is 6,000 yuan per person per year, which may be raised by up to 50%." The policy runs January 1, 2023 to December 31, 2027. Those who haven't reached 3 years when it expires can keep claiming until the term is up (nationwide)
Note
The regulation only says the amount is set separately by the competent departments. The only official figure findable is in a 2020 article on the Ministry of Veterans Affairs website: "4,500 yuan for each full year of active service"; the same piece says it is "adjusted as appropriate." The uplift percentages in that article no longer match the current regulation — the regulation governs. An August 2024 article by the Guizhou Provincial Department of Veterans Affairs, under the new regulation, still says "the standard currently in effect: 4,500 yuan for each full year of active service." TODO (to be verified: no formal standard document found; all that can be confirmed is that as of August 2024 provincial departments still wrote this). Also, don't confuse it with local "one-time economic subsidies" — a separate sum each locality sets and pays itself, e.g. Yantai paid 6,000 yuan per year of service to those discharged in 2024. Most new figures in online guides have no source; some just mix these two sums together. While a conscript serves, the family can also claim a separate family preferential payment. The Military Service Law says only that "the standard is set by local people's governments, with a fixed subsidy from the central treasury" — ask the county-level people's government that approved your enlistment for the amount. The tax item is a cap on how much less tax you can pay each year. If the business doesn't take off, you won't use it up — that's why this item's benefit is rated only "medium." The Regulation on Promoting Veterans Employment and Entrepreneurship, effective August 1, 2026, adds one more thing: vocational-skill certificates earned during service are valid nationwide after discharge.

Extra Uplift to the One-Time Discharge Payment — Important Changes!: "The standard currently in effect: 4,500 yuan for each full year of active service". http://tyjrswt.guizhou.gov.cn/zfxxgk/fdzdgknr/zdlyxx_562115…; Muping District People's Government, Yantai (2025). Government jobs aren't only via the civil-service exam: finish two years on a grassroots service program and you can apply for the 10% targeted recruitment quota

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

Wanting into the system isn't only about the civil-service exam. Complete two years on a grassroots service program like "Three Supports and One Assistance" with a passing evaluation, and you can apply for targeted recruitment plans open only to such people. Each province must set aside around 10% of its civil-service recruitment plan for them each year. Within three years, graduate applicants also get 10 extra points on the preliminary exam. The price is that those two years pay a fiscal subsidy.

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is two years serving at the township grassroots level. Those two years pay a fiscal subsidy, not a market wage; the hard part is lasting through them.
Benefit
The fourth-round "Three Supports and One Assistance" plan notice states a "service period of two years." It also states: "Each province (region, municipality) should set aside around 10% of its civil-service recruitment plan each year for targeted recruitment of personnel from grassroots service programs such as the 'Three Supports and One Assistance' plan. When county- and township-level public institutions conduct open recruitment, they should, based on local conditions, set aside a certain number or share of positions for special recruitment of 'Three Supports and One Assistance' personnel whose service is complete and evaluation passed … and may waive the probation period after hiring." Targeted recruitment and special recruitment mean these quotas are competed for only among people who have done grassroots service programs; no one else can apply. The same notice states: "'Three Supports and One Assistance' personnel who pass the final evaluation and take the national master's admissions exam within three years get 10 points added to their preliminary-exam total and priority under equal conditions … Vocational (associate) graduates who complete service and pass evaluation may enter adult higher-education associate-to-bachelor programs without an exam." Exam-free entry means no further exam — straight into the bachelor's upgrade. The notice also states: "Participants without prior work experience who complete service and pass evaluation enjoy, for two years, fresh-graduate policies on equal terms in agency and enterprise recruitment exams, self-employment, household registration, and further schooling. 'Three Supports and One Assistance' personnel's grassroots service years count as work years, with the start of work dated from the day of reporting to the grassroots post." The central subsidy standard is 30,000 yuan per person per year in the western region, 24,000 yuan in the central region, and 12,000 yuan in the eastern region. The opinion of the General Offices of the CPC Central Committee and the State Council states: "For participants without prior work experience, within 2 years after completing service and passing evaluation, they enjoy fresh-college-graduate policies on equal terms in public-sector recruitment, hiring by all kinds of enterprises, self-employment, household registration, and further schooling." The opinion also states: "Provincial-level and above agencies recruiting civil servants must, except for special positions and per relevant rules, recruit only from people with 2 or more years of grassroots work experience." Another path is the Western Plan. It is jointly organized and implemented by "the Communist Youth League Central Committee, the Ministry of Education, the Ministry of Finance, and the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security." It recruits fresh college graduates and current graduate students "for 1 to 3 years of volunteer service at the western grassroots" (nationwide)
Note
The fourth-round Three Supports and One Assistance plan covers 2021 to 2025. No fifth-round document or 2026 notice was found this time — check that year's recruitment announcement before applying. In 2025 the central treasury supported 34,430 recruits. The Western Plan's implementation scheme text isn't findable online; the policy section of its official site won't open. Its post-service benefits follow the central document that governs all grassroots service programs. Those two years pay a fiscal subsidy, not a market wage — weigh that cost together with the targeted recruitment two years later.

8

Special-post teachers who finish three years of service, pass evaluation, and want to stay should be added to the permanent staff promptly

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: large

The special-post plan is one of the few paths that explicitly says "permanent staff status after the term." Conditions: bachelor's degree or above, mainly teacher-training majors, age not over 30, and the corresponding teacher qualification certificate. The service period is three years, with pay and benefits equal to permanent teachers at local public schools. Those who finish three years, pass evaluation, and want to stay must be added to the permanent staff promptly per the document.

Cost
Costs nothing. The price is three years teaching in rural compulsory-education schools, and you need to pass the teacher qualification exam before entering. The hard part is sticking out those three years.
Benefit
The 2024 special-post plan notice lists recruitment conditions: "Bachelor's degree or above required, mainly teacher-training majors; primary schools may also recruit graduates of teacher-training colleges where appropriate." "Age not over 30." The corresponding teacher qualification certificate is also required. The notice adds: "Volunteers who took part in the 'College Student Volunteer Service Western Plan' or have teaching experience, and graduates of teacher-training colleges with over half a year of internship teaching, are given priority under equal conditions." "Veterans who meet the conditions are supported and encouraged to teach in primary and secondary schools, and their age limits may be relaxed accordingly with service years and other factors considered." For pay and staff status, see these lines. "From January 1, 2024, the wage subsidy standard for special-post teachers is raised; the central treasury … raises the per-capita annual amount in the central region from 35,200 yuan to 38,800 yuan, and in the western region from 38,200 yuan to 41,800 yuan." "Under equal conditions they enjoy the same treatment as permanent teachers at local public schools in pay, professional-title evaluation, awards, and annual assessment." "Special-post teachers who complete three years of service, pass evaluation, and are willing to stay are guaranteed prompt addition to the permanent staff with a job position assigned; personnel and payroll relationships are transferred accordingly, work years and teaching years are counted consecutively, and no probation period applies" (nationwide)
Note
The benefit is rated "large" because permanent staff status after the term means a long-term staffed position worth far more than ten thousand yuan. The latest findable document is the 2024 notice; the 2025 and 2026 versions haven't entered the policy database. For specific positions, subsidy standards, and age, go by that year's notice and your province's implementation plan. The center sets the broad frame; the province sets the details. The teacher qualification certificate must be earned before entry — it can't be made up after being hired.
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Education General Office, Ministry of Finance General Office (2024). Notice on Implementing the 2024 Special Post Plan for Teachers in Rural Compulsory Education Schools (Jiaoshiting [2024] No. 1). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202405/content_6950803…
