Firefighter and military civilian positions are two more open-recruitment doors, with lower bars than the civil-service exam

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Neither of these paths is blocked by the "associate degree or above" bar. Firefighters are recruited at 18 to 22 with senior high school education or above; associate-degree holders and veterans can go up to 24. Military civilian positions only require being 18; entry-level positions top out at 35 for first-time recruitment. The common cost is that the political review and physical exam screen people out.

Cost
Costs nothing. From application to hiring you pass a physical exam, political review, physical fitness test, psychological test, and interview, taking months in all. The hard part is that each gate eliminates people, one after another.
Benefit
For firefighters see the Measures for Recruiting Firefighters of the National Comprehensive Fire and Rescue Teams. Article 5 basic conditions include "aged 18 or above and under 22" and "educated at senior high school level or above." Article 6: "People with an associate degree or above, veterans of the PLA and the People's Armed Police, and full-time government firefighters and full-time government forestry firefighting personnel with over 2 years of real firefighting and rescue experience may have the age relaxed to 24; for urgently needed special professionals in firefighting and rescue, the age may be further relaxed with approval of the Ministry of Emergency Management, in principle not exceeding 28." Article 7: "Firefighters are openly recruited from society, mainly from the permanent resident population of the province-level region, and may also be recruited from other provinces as needed." Article 9 gives the procedure: "publicity and mobilization, organizing registration, qualification review, physical examination, political review, fitness test and job adaptability test, psychological test and interview, public notice, hiring." For military civilian positions see Article 18 of the Regulations on Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army: "The military implements a civilian personnel recruitment and hiring system combining open examination, direct introduction, and special recruitment." That's three lines: hiring through open exams, directly bringing in ready-made talent, and special recruitment aimed at particular groups. Article 9 of the regulations gives basic conditions including "having reached the age of 18," "meeting the political conditions for military recruitment and hiring of civilian personnel," and "meeting the education level, professional competence, and work ability required by the position." Article 19 states that for lower-rank positions the maximum age for first-time recruitment is 35. The regulations also state that "civilian personnel positions should give priority to recruiting qualified veterans" (nationwide)
Note
The Regulation on Promoting Veterans Employment and Entrepreneurship, effective August 1, 2026, adds two things. One: firefighter recruitment must set aside a certain share to recruit discharged NCOs and conscripts specifically. Two: when recruiting police auxiliary officers (auxiliary police), veterans are given priority under equal conditions. For both paths, each year's quotas, positions, and specific conditions go by that year's announcement; this book only states the thresholds fixed in the measures. Firefighter is a disciplined-services job — think through the occupational risks before entering.
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, Ministry of Emergency Management (2021). Measures for Recruiting Firefighters of the National Comprehensive Fire and Rescue Teams (MHRSS Fa [2021] No. 58, Articles 5, 6, 7, 9). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-08/27/content_563…; State Council, Central Military Commission (2022). Regulations on Civilian Personnel of the Chinese People's Liberation Army (second revision, State Council and CMC Decree No. 757, effective January 1, 2023; Articles 9, 18, 19, 20). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808181857bca5e01859ee5a6… (National Laws and Regulations Database)

Credentials aren't a one-shot deal: the self-taught exam has no age or prior-education limits, and the adult college entrance exam and the Open University can both fill gaps

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: littleTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

If school didn't work out at eighteen, three legitimate channels remain: the self-taught exam, the adult college entrance exam, and the Open University. The self-taught exam has no age limit and doesn't check your prior level of schooling, but current full-time students can't register. The adult entrance exam requires a high school or associate diploma first. All three are slow, but none of them cares how you scored at eighteen.

Cost
Registration and textbook fees run a few hundred yuan a year. The cost is long-term self-study, or after-work classes; the part-time (studying while working) associate-to-bachelor track takes at least two and a half years. The hard part is sustaining it long term.
Benefit
For the self-taught exam see the Interim Regulations on Self-Taught Higher Education Examinations. Article 3: "Citizens of the People's Republic of China, regardless of gender, age, ethnicity, race, or level of education already received, may take the self-taught higher education examinations in accordance with these regulations." Article 20: "Students currently enrolled in full-time schools of all levels and types may not register." Article 25 gives three conditions for the diploma: passing all courses, completing the graduation thesis or practical task, and passing the ideological and moral assessment. Meet all three and you get the diploma. That article also states "holders of associate (foundation) or bachelor's diplomas have their qualifications recognized by the state." Article 32 covers pay for diploma holders: "Non-employed persons, once hired, receive pay equal to that of regular-institution graduates of the same kind." Article 21 of the Higher Education Law: "The state implements the self-taught higher education examination system; those who pass the examinations are issued the corresponding academic credential or other study certificates." For the adult entrance exam see the 2025 National Adult Higher Education Admissions Measures. Applicants are "working people and other members of society other than students currently enrolled in state-recognized senior and secondary schools." "Candidates for the high-school-to-bachelor's or high-school-to-associate tracks should have graduated from senior secondary school or hold equivalent education. Candidates for the associate-to-bachelor track must already hold … an associate diploma, a bachelor's completion certificate, or above." "Minimum study time for full-time study: four years for high-school-to-bachelor's, two years for high-school-to-associate and associate-to-bachelor; minimum for part-time study: five years for high-school-to-bachelor's, two and a half years for high-school-to-associate and associate-to-bachelor." Full-time means leaving your job to study on campus all day; part-time means keeping the job and studying alongside. For the Open University see the Ministry of Education's Opinion on Running the Open University Well. It states: "The Open University practices open enrollment; students who complete courses and earn the corresponding credits receive course certificates; those who complete the prescribed credits and meet the relevant requirements receive the corresponding degree and non-degree certificates, and those meeting degree-conferral conditions should be granted the corresponding degree" (nationwide)
Note
There is also the regular associate-to-bachelor upgrade for fresh full-time vocational graduates. The publicly available national document is the Ministry of Education's 2007 notice, which set the upgrade plan at no more than 5% of that year's fresh associate graduates. From 2020 the ministry expanded the program, adding 322,000 places year over year, and the 5% line is no longer applied in practice. The yearly arrangement comes as a letter from the Ministry of Education's Department of College Students — for 2026, Jiaoxisihan [2025] No. 53. The letter isn't published publicly; its number can only be seen in provincial forwarding documents. Who can apply is set by each province, basically only that year's full-time associate graduates of that province, so the main text doesn't list its conditions. From fall 2025, continuing higher education no longer uses the names "correspondence" or "part-time attendance" — everything is called "non-full-time." Continuing higher education is the category for adults making up credentials later; be wary of marketing still using the old names. Making up credentials and "which skill is worth learning" are two different matters — the latter is in Section 23. Paid "fast credentials" and fake certificates are in item 8 of Section 23.

Higher Education Law (Article 21). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f20df64… (National Laws and Regulations Database); Ministry of Education General Office (2025). Notice on 2025 National Adult Higher Education Admissions (Jiaoxueting [2025] No. 6) and annex, 2025 National Adult Higher Education Admissions Measures. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202509/content_7040877…; Ministry of Education (2016). Opinion on Running the Open University Well (Jiaozhicheng [2016] No. 2). http://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2016/content_5067956.htm; Ministry of Education (2007). Outside a formal employer you're a flexible worker: enroll yourself in pension and medical insurance where you work — household-registration restrictions have been lifted

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: a lotTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

Not having an employer doesn't mean social insurance goes away — it just means no one pays your half. The documents require localities to lift household-registration restrictions so flexible workers can enroll where they work; a few megacities may lift them gradually. So don't read "freedom" as forgetting about social insurance. If you stop paying, both your pension and your medical reimbursement are calculated under the rules for missed contributions.

Cost
Pension and medical insurance you pay in full yourself, based on the local contribution base — over a thousand yuan a month. The contribution base is the reference number used to compute premiums. This is the fixed expense most easily left out of the flexible-work budget; the hard part is paying on time every month.
Benefit
For enrollment see the Guiding Opinion on Safeguarding Labor Security Rights of Workers in New Employment Forms. It states: "Localities shall lift household-registration restrictions on flexible workers enrolling in basic pension and basic medical insurance at their place of work; where individual megacities cannot do so in one step, they shall, based on local conditions, actively create the conditions to lift them gradually. Flexible workers not enrolled in employee basic pension or employee basic medical insurance shall be organized to join urban-rural resident basic pension and medical insurance as required, achieving coverage for all who should be covered. Enterprises shall be urged to participate in social insurance as required by law. Enterprises shall guide and support workers in new employment forms who do not fully meet the criteria for establishing labor relations to join the corresponding social insurance according to their situation." The same document sorts employment into three types: "Where labor relations are established, enterprises shall sign labor contracts with workers as required by law. Where the criteria for labor relations are not fully met but the enterprise manages the workers' labor … it shall be guided to sign written agreements with them … For individuals running businesses independently through platforms or freelancing, the parties' rights and obligations are governed by civil law" (nationwide, from 2021)
Note
The original says "lift" the household-registration restrictions, with a carve-out for megacities — it does not say "abolished nationwide." How far the lifting goes, ask the city where you'll enroll. The benefit is rated "large" because a contribution gap loses the pension and medical benefits themselves, worth far more than ten thousand yuan. But the cost is real too — full self-payment runs over a thousand yuan a month. For making up missed payments and how years accumulate, see item 18 of Section 7 (social insurance gaps). Also: selling farm products or daily goods at government-designated places and times, or using your own craft for convenient services that don't require a license, needs no business license. That's in Guoban Fa [2020] No. 27.
Sources (2 references)
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and seven other departments (2021). Guiding Opinion on Safeguarding Labor Security Rights of Workers in New Employment Forms (MHRSS Fa [2021] No. 56, Articles 2, 8). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2021-07/23/content_562…; General Office of the State Council (2020). Opinion on Supporting Flexible Employment through Multiple Channels (Guoban Fa [2020] No. 27). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2020-07/31/content_553…

Delivering food, driving ride-hail, hauling same-city freight: the platform pays occupational-injury insurance per order — you don't pay it yourself

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

If you deliver food, drive ride-hail, or haul same-city freight, the platform must pay occupational-injury insurance for you per order — you pay not a cent, and every order you take is covered. This is still a pilot; before taking orders, check whether your province and platform are covered. Those who already have a labor relationship with the platform fall under work-injury insurance, not this scheme.

Cost
Costs nothing — the platform pays it. Your job is to check whether the platform you take orders on is in the pilot. Two ways: look for "occupational injury insurance" in the app's protection or rights page, or call your province's human resources and social security bureau and ask whether this platform has been enrolling.
Benefit
This protection is in the Measures on Occupational Injury Insurance for New Employment Form Workers (Trial). Article 2: "Platform enterprises shall participate in occupational injury insurance for new employment form workers per these measures … and pay occupational injury insurance premiums for new employment form workers who register and take orders through the platform, providing labor such as mobility services, instant delivery, and same-city freight in the platform enterprise's name for pay or income — covering every order and every person. Workers covered by the Regulation on Work-Related Injury Insurance shall have work-injury insurance arranged for them by the enterprise as required by law; these measures do not apply." Article 9: "During the trial period, the mobility sector pays 0.01 yuan per order; the instant delivery sector pays 0.07 yuan and 0.25 yuan per order; the same-city freight sector pays 0.18 yuan per order." How the pilot expands, from this passage: "From July 1, 2025, building on the 7 provinces and 7 platform enterprises already piloting … 10 more provinces are added, including Tianjin, Hebei, Liaoning, Zhejiang, Anhui, Fujian, Shandong, Hubei, Guangxi, and Ningxia … In 2026, the occupational injury insurance pilot is to be implemented across all 31 provinces and the Xinjiang Production and Construction Corps, with platform enterprises in the three sectors of mobility, instant delivery, and same-city freight brought into the pilot as a whole" (pilot, expanding yearly)
Note
This is still a pilot, not a formal nationwide system. Before taking orders, confirm your province and platform are covered; if not, your only layer is commercial insurance you buy yourself. Another document, the Guiding Opinion on Safeguarding Labor Security Rights of Workers in New Employment Forms, adds several requirements: pay for normal work must be no less than the local minimum wage, paid in full on time, with no withholding or unreasonable delays, plus reasonable pay for statutory holidays. That document is MHRSS Fa [2021] No. 56, also cited in the flexible-employment item — see item 11. If something happens, follow this process first; don't settle privately with the station. Medical and pension insurance you still must enroll in yourself — see item 11 for flexible-employment enrollment.
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and eight other departments (2025). Two paths that lock in an establishment position the day you file college preferences: publicly funded teacher-training students and targeted medical students — the price is a 6-year service commitment

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: large

On both paths the state pays first, and after graduation you work 6 years where the agreement sends you. Publicly funded teacher-training students are recruited only at six ministry-affiliated normal universities, via early-batch admission. Targeted medical students must sign a three-party agreement before receiving the admission letter. Breaking the contract means repayment, penalty fees, and a mark on your credit record. Decide whether you can accept those 6 years before filing your preferences.

Cost
Tuition and dormitory fees are covered, plus a living stipend. The price is 6 years after graduation without free choice of job; breaking the contract means repayment, penalty fees, and a credit-record entry. The hard part is that you can't relocate during those 6 years.
Benefit
For publicly funded teacher-training students see the Implementation Measures for Government-Funded Teacher Education with Integrated Undergraduate-Master's Training at Normal Universities Directly under the Ministry of Education (2024; the 2018 measures repealed simultaneously). Article 2: the central treasury covers tuition and dormitory fees during enrollment and provides a living stipend. Article 3: training focuses on prefecture (city, league, prefecture) level and below outside provincial capitals in the central and western regions. It also states "no placement to teach in the main urban districts of directly-administered municipalities, cities with independent planning, or provincial capitals (except the five autonomous regions, provinces with land borders, Hainan, Guizhou, and Qinghai)." Article 9: after graduation you generally return to your home province to teach in primary and secondary schools in the targeted prefecture (city, league, prefecture), "pledging to work in primary and secondary education for more than 6 years." Those working in urban schools "must serve at least 1 year teaching at a rural compulsory-education school." Article 13: those who fail to perform or don't complete the term bear responsibility under the agreement. One consequence is "the breach is entered into the credit record and promptly shared with the national credit information sharing platform, and breach-related materials are filed in the person's personnel dossier." Another line: "Before completing the service obligation, no teaching outside the targeted prefecture (city, league, prefecture), and no recruitment (hiring) as other public servants. Upon completing the obligation, the related credit is repaired." Until the agreed service term is worked out, other public-sector posts are off-limits; only after completing it is the credit record restored. Article 6: those who after admission are found unsuited to teaching upon assessment refund the government-funded education benefits received within 1 year of enrollment and are transferred to a non-teacher-training major. Article 14: those who fail to obtain the Master of Education degree certificate and teacher qualification certificate within the prescribed study period are treated as breaching, refund fees, and pay a penalty. Article 21: localities resolve the staffing quota needed for publicly funded teacher-training students to teach in primary and secondary schools within the existing total of establishment positions. For rural order-targeted free medical students see another notice. After admission and before receiving the admission letter, students must sign an agreement with the training school and the county-level health and human resources departments where the targeted employment is located. The agreement must "pledge 6 years of service at the targeted rural grassroots medical institution after graduation." Performing means working out the term where the agreement sends you. After reporting for duty under the agreement, you must complete 3 years of standardized residency training in general practice, known as guipei — the post-graduation stage of training in a hospital under uniform standards. Personnel and payroll relationships are unchanged during training. Breach records go into the personal personnel dossier and serve as integrity-assessment grounds for public recruitment by medical and health institutions and other public institutions, residency training intake, and graduate admissions. Those who breach in bad faith are publicized nationwide via the "Credit China" website and placed under joint disciplinary action for dishonesty. Breach years of training don't count toward the service term. Those who fail to refund fees and penalties per the agreement are pursued by the county-level health department through legal channels (nationwide)
Note
The 2024 measures changed the publicly funded teacher-training program into "integrated undergraduate-master's training" (bachelor's followed by a Master of Education). The 2018 measures are repealed; the "teach straight after the bachelor's" version still circulating online is the old rule. Those who signed agreements before the measures were issued follow the original agreements. "Having a staffing slot" doesn't mean "get in and stop worrying": the slot has to be freed up within the existing total, and specific positions are recruited specially by prefecture-level cities with the hiring schools — you and the school choose each other. Targeted medical students may leave when the term is up — the document says "when the service term is completed, those choosing their own employment shall be approved." Even those who already breached have a way to clear the record: the price is working at least 6 more years, per the original agreement or reassigned to other rural grassroots institutions in the province; fees already paid and penalties are not refunded. Medical students must also add the 3 years of residency training, making the whole cycle longer than the teaching path. Provinces also have their own publicly funded teacher-training and targeted medical student plans with province-set conditions — check that year's provincial admissions documents before filing preferences.
Sources (2 references)

Notice on Forwarding the Implementation Measures for Government-Funded Teacher Education with Integrated Undergraduate-Master's Training at Normal Universities Directly under the Ministry of Education (Guoban Fa [2024] No. 27, Articles 2, 3, 6, 9, 13, 14, 21). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202406/content_6957261…; National Health Commission, State Commission Office of Public Sectors Reform, National Development and Reform Commission, Ministry of Education, Ministry of Finance, Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security, National Administration of Traditional Chinese Medicine (2019). Notice on Employment Placement and Contract Performance Management of Rural Order-Targeted Free Medical Students. https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2019-11/13/content_545…

To work abroad, first check whether the company holds an overseas labor cooperation business qualification: it may not charge you a deposit

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

With working abroad, the law doesn't regulate you — it regulates the company organizing your departure. Only enterprises holding the foreign labor cooperation business qualification certificate and completing registration may do this. Hearing "get a tourist visa first and switch to a work visa there" tells you the other side is breaking the law right there. The company also may not charge you a deposit under any name, or demand property as security.

Cost
Costs nothing. Spend ten-odd minutes before departure verifying the company's qualifications, then read both contracts through.
Benefit
The Regulation on the Administration of Foreign Labor Cooperation. Article 5: engaging in foreign labor cooperation requires a business qualification approved by the provincial or districted-city commerce department. This qualification is the foreign labor cooperation business qualification certificate; without it, no one may organize people to work abroad. Article 7: the list of qualified enterprises is reported to the State Council commerce department and relayed to Chinese embassies and consulates abroad. It also states "without obtaining the foreign labor cooperation business qualification certificate and completing registration as required by law, no one may engage in foreign labor cooperation." Article 8: "No organization or individual may organize workers to go abroad for work under the guise of business, tourism, or study." Article 9: within 5 working days of registration, the enterprise shall deposit at a designated bank "no less than 3 million yuan as a foreign labor cooperation risk-handling reserve fund," with the list of depositors made public. Article 10: the reserve fund pays service fees to be refunded, labor remuneration, and legally compensable losses that the enterprise refuses or cannot bear, and also "the costs of workers returning home or receiving emergency assistance when an emergency occurs." Article 11: workers may not be organized to go abroad for work related to gambling or prostitution. Article 12: those without arranged training may not be organized to go abroad. Article 13: personal accident insurance must be purchased for workers covering their overseas work period. Articles 21 and 23: written contracts must be signed separately with the foreign employer and with the workers; without them, no organizing departure. Article 25: "No deposit may be collected from workers under any name, nor may workers be required to provide property security." Article 26: contracts are filed with the commerce department within 10 working days of signing. Article 29: where workers' actual entitlements differ from the contract, the enterprise shall assist in claims; where due compensation wasn't received, the worker has the right to demand the enterprise bear compensation liability. Article 31: where a country's or region's security situation cannot guarantee personal safety, the enterprise may not organize workers to go there. Article 37: the commerce department maintains adverse credit records and a publication system. Penalty provisions follow. Article 39: those operating foreign labor cooperation without qualification are investigated and shut down, with criminal liability where a crime is constituted. Article 40: organizing departures under the guise of business, tourism, or study, lending out the qualification, or organizing work related to gambling or prostitution — the business qualification certificate is revoked. Article 43: organizing departures without contracts, or by concealing information or providing false information, draws fines of 100,000 to 200,000 yuan, plus fines of 20,000 to 50,000 yuan on the main responsible person (nationwide)
Note
The compliant process: the company first signs a written labor cooperation contract with the foreign employer, then signs a written service contract or labor contract with you. The contract must state the work content, term, pay, hours, leave, social insurance, and personal safety risks. Within 10 working days of signing, the company files it with the commerce department. The company must also arrange training in skills, safety precautions, the local language, and local laws and customs, and buy you personal accident insurance covering the overseas work period. A company that won't show you the contract, asks for a deposit, or pushes you to leave first and complete paperwork later is the kind to avoid. Overseas high-pay recruitment scams and cyber-fraud compounds are in item 5 of Section 21; the safety advisories to check before departure and the 12308 hotline are in Section 21 — not repeated here. The regulation sets no education or age threshold for the workers themselves; the threshold is the company's qualification, and whether the destination country grants a permit. The company can only sign with enterprises or institutions approved by that country, not with foreign individuals. The reserve fund is drawn on by the competent department when the company defaults — you can't withdraw it yourself. So if something really goes wrong, first complain to the commerce department; Article 20 gives you that right. Dispatching over 100 people to the same country or region requires accompanying management personnel, reported to the embassy or consulate. Smaller projects lack that layer of protection, so keep your contract and transfer records all the more carefully.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2012). Regulation on the Administration of Foreign Labor Cooperation (State Council Decree No. 620; Articles 5, 7, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 21, 23, 25, 26, 29, 31, 37, 39, 40, 43). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2012-06/11/content_109…
15

Working remotely from home for an overseas company counts as domestic-source income under tax law: file your own income tax, and receive payments as 'employee compensation'

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Whether this income counts as domestic or foreign depends on where you work, not where the money is sent from. If you're in China working remotely for an overseas company, it's domestic-source income and you owe income tax in China. The overseas company has no establishment in China and nobody withholds for you, so you must file this tax yourself. Incoming payments go through the "employee compensation" channel.

Cost
Costs nothing. Once a year you file the annual reconciliation, from March 1 to June 30 of the following year. When incoming payments exceed the annual quota, you also need an employment contract and proof of income ready. The hard part is remembering to file the tax yourself.
Benefit
Whether this income is domestic-source: see Article 3 of the Implementation Regulations of the Individual Income Tax Law (State Council Decree No. 707, effective January 1, 2019). It states: "Except as otherwise provided by the State Council's finance and taxation departments, the following income, regardless of where it is paid, is income sourced within China: (1) income from providing services within China through employment, engagement, or contract performance." Article 6 of the same regulations defines two tax categories. One is wages and salaries: "Wage and salary income means wages, salaries, bonuses, year-end raises, labor dividends, allowances, and subsidies obtained by an individual from employment or engagement, and other income related to the position or employment." The other is labor remuneration: "Labor remuneration income means income an individual obtains from providing services, including design, decoration, installation, drafting, laboratory testing, testing, medical care, legal work, accounting, consulting, lecturing, translation, manuscript review, calligraphy and painting, carving, film and video, audio recording, video recording, performance, acting, advertising, exhibition, technical services, referral services, brokerage services, agency services, and other services." Article 6 of the Individual Income Tax Law gives how taxable income is computed: "A resident individual's comprehensive income, after deducting 60,000 yuan in expenses plus special deductions, special additional deductions, and other deductions determined by law from each tax year's income, is taxable income." The same article states that "labor remuneration, author's remuneration, and royalty income use income minus a 20% expense deduction as the income amount." The 20% deduction line lists only those three items; wages and salaries are not among them. So wages and salaries count in full as income, and the two categories produce different tax. Article 9: "The income earner is the taxpayer in individual income tax; the unit or individual paying the income is the withholding agent." Article 10: "In any of the following situations the taxpayer shall file a tax return as required by law: … (2) taxable income is obtained without a withholding agent; … (4) income from abroad is obtained." Article 11: "A resident individual's comprehensive income is taxed on an annual basis … where an annual reconciliation is required, it shall be handled between March 1 and June 30 of the year following the income." For incoming payments see the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (PBOC Decree No. 3 [2006], effective February 1, 2007). Article 9: "Individual foreign exchange sales and domestic individuals' foreign exchange purchases are subject to an annual quota. Within the annual quota, transactions are handled at banks with valid identity documents; beyond the annual quota, current-account transactions are handled at banks with valid identity documents and relevant materials proving the transaction amount." Article 7: "In handling individual foreign exchange business, banks and individuals shall observe these measures, may not evade quota supervision through splitting or other means, and may not evade authenticity management with false commercial documents or vouchers." The Detailed Rules for Implementing the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (Huifa [2007] No. 1), Article 2: "Individual foreign exchange sales and domestic individuals' foreign exchange purchases are subject to an annual quota — 50,000 US dollars equivalent per person per year." Article 10: "When a domestic individual's non-operating current-account foreign exchange sales exceed the annual quota, they are handled at banks with valid identity documents and the following supporting materials: … (7) employee compensation: employment contract and proof of income" (nationwide)
Note
Which category applies depends on your relationship with the payer. Signed an employment contract with the work arranged by the other side: wages and salaries. Taking work by project and delivering results yourself: labor remuneration. The two produce different tax — figure out which one you are before filing. For incoming payments, within the 50,000 US dollar annual equivalent, settling at the bank with your ID is enough; above that, hand the bank the employment contract and proof of income. Don't split receipts through other people to dodge the quota. All of the above assumes you're in China and not leaving the country. Actually going abroad to work for an overseas employer is a different regime — see item 14 of this section (checking the company's foreign labor cooperation qualification). Four items this book hasn't covered yet; each may carry real costs, but no verifiable authority could be found word for word. First, whether this income owes value-added tax and whether invoices must be issued on your behalf. Second, whether doing this long-term requires a business license or registration as a sole proprietor. Third, whether you can claim labor-law rights against an overseas employer, such as annual leave, overtime pay, or termination compensation. Fourth, data export and confidentiality.
Sources (5 references)
State Council (2018). Implementation Regulations of the Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (State Council Decree No. 707, Articles 3, 6). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-12/22/content_535…; Standing Committee of the National People's Congress (2018). Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (seventh amendment, 2018; Articles 6, 9, 10, 11). http://www.npc.gov.cn/zgrdw/npc/xinwen/2018-09/05/content_2…; State Taxation Administration Policy and Regulation Database. Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (Article 6). https://fgk.chinatax.gov.cn/zcfgk/c100009/c5193028/content.…; People's Bank of China (2006). Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (PBOC Decree No. 3 [2006], Articles 7, 9). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/content/2007/content_786257.htm; State Administration of Foreign Exchange (2007). Detailed Rules for Implementing the Measures for the Administration of Individual Foreign Exchange (Huifa [2007] No. 1, Articles 2, 10). https://www.safe.gov.cn/safe/2007/0105/22509.html
16

Working for yourself instead of an employer, fund the start with guaranteed startup loans: up to 300,000 yuan for individuals, with the treasury subsidizing half the interest

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

If you must borrow to start, look first at this one with its treasury interest subsidy. Individuals can borrow up to 300,000 yuan, for up to 3 years, with the treasury paying half the interest. One hard condition is often missed: at application, you and your spouse must have no other loans — only student loans, poverty-alleviation microcredit, mortgages, car loans, and small consumer loans under 50,000 yuan don't count against it.

Cost
Asking costs nothing. First make one trip to the human resources and social security department for eligibility review, then complete paperwork once each with the guarantee agency and the handling bank (the bank that lends). The hard part: borrowed money still has to be repaid.
Benefit
Individual application conditions are in Article 6 of the Measures for Managing Inclusive Finance Development Special Funds (Caijin [2023] No. 75). The first condition is belonging to a key employment group. The document lists registered urban unemployed, people with employment difficulties (including persons with disabilities), veterans, and persons released after serving sentences; plus college graduates (including student village officials and returning overseas students), and workers and unemployed from industries cutting overcapacity; plus returning migrant workers starting businesses, online merchants, people lifted out of poverty, and rural residents starting businesses on their own. The second condition is no other loans: "Apart from student loans, poverty-alleviation microcredit, housing loans, car loans, and small consumer loans under 50,000 yuan (including credit card spending), the applicant, when submitting the guaranteed startup loan application, and their spouse have no other loans." Article 9: "For qualifying guaranteed startup loans, the finance department provides an interest subsidy of 50% of the loan's actual interest rate. For extended or overdue guaranteed startup loans, the finance department in principle provides no subsidy." The subsidy means the treasury pays half your interest. Extension is pushing back the due date; overdue is not repaying past it — in both cases the treasury stops paying. Article 10: individually applied guaranteed startup loans under 100,000 yuan in principle require no counter-guarantee — no need to find another person, or pledge property, to secure the guarantee agency. Article 11: individual guaranteed startup loans within the incentive-subsidy support scope are "capped at 300,000 yuan with a term of no more than 3 years." Partnerships may be raised appropriately, up to 110% of the sum of the individual caps. The interest-rate caps for subsidized loans have three tiers: LPR+50BPs in the eastern region, LPR+150BPs in the central and western regions, LPR+250BPs in areas lifted out of poverty. LPR is the loan prime rate quoted by banks; BPs (basis points) is a unit of interest rate — the more added, the higher the interest. Those who "repay actively, create jobs strongly, and run a good startup project" may apply again after the term, up to 3 times in total. Article 8: the applicant first applies to the local human resources and social security department for eligibility review, then submits the application to the guarantee agency and the handling bank. Article 12: with provincial government consent, localities may expand the support scope and raise amounts and subsidy rates (nationwide)
Note
The treasury paying half your interest doesn't change the fact that borrowed money must be repaid. This book's stance in Section 12, item 1 is unchanged: start a business only with money you can afford to lose, don't touch the family's savings, never sign a personal guarantee on a company loan, and above all don't let your spouse co-sign. If you've already decided to borrow, this policy loan is the lowest-interest tier — stay away from consumer loans and informal lending. Amounts and scope can be raised by each province; how much you'll actually get, go by what your local human resources and social security department says that year. The 2020 pandemic-era notice capping individuals at 200,000 was a temporary document — the current one is these measures. For whether to register a sole proprietorship or a company, licenses, taxes, and exit, see Section 12. For training subsidies, social insurance subsidies, and job internships during unemployment, see item 13 of Section 7 (vocational training subsidies).
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Finance (2023). Notice on Issuing the Measures for Managing Inclusive Finance Development Special Funds (Caijin [2023] No. 75, Articles 6, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/202309/content_6903691…

32. Studying Abroad: Status, Working, Insurance, and Credential Recognition Back Home

10 items

This section runs two ledgers — money and personal freedom. It does not debate whether you should go abroad, and it does not rank schools. Four things you will pay for not knowing: how to keep your visa status from breaking, where the cap on work hours sits, which insurance premiums and fees you must pay, and whether the diploma will be recognized back home. Coverage spans four countries — the US, Canada, the UK, and Australia — with figures listed country by country. The sources are the official web pages of each country's immigration authority and of China's Ministry of Education. Study-abroad policies in every country change often — more often than Chinese regulations do. All figures in this section are current as of September 2026. Before departure and before every visa renewal, re-check them yourself through the links in the Sources column. For how to reach your embassy or consulate when something goes wrong overseas, what 12308 can handle, and how to buy overseas medical and medical-evacuation insurance, see Section 21. For the study-versus-work calculation, see Section 23. Stolen accounts are covered in Section 14, telecom fraud in Section 8. None of that is repeated here.

1

Before paying tuition, check the school is on the CSCSE's list of recognized institutions

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

If the diploma will be used back home — for civil-service exams, state-owned enterprise jobs, hukou registration, or professional-title reviews — it must first pass verification. Verification is done by the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) under the Ministry of Education. If the school is not on the list of institutions that can be verified, the tuition and the years are wasted, and the diploma is unusable in China. Checking the list costs nothing. Check first, then pay tuition.

Cost
Free. Enter the school's name once in the CSCSE's "recognized institution lookup" — the whole check takes a few minutes
Benefit
The Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) runs a recognized-institution lookup. You can search by country or by school name; what you are checking is whether the degrees and diplomas this school issues fall within the scope of verification. In addition, the Ministry of Education's foreign-related supervision information network publishes regulatory information on Chinese-foreign cooperative programs and institutions run abroad
Note
An agent's claim that the school is "Ministry of Education recognized" counts for nothing — go by what you find yourself online. The list changes: a school on it when you enroll may not be on it when you graduate, so re-check once a year while you study. Chinese-foreign cooperative programs follow a separate verification and registration system. Those who enrolled in 2008 or later can look up their registration number on the foreign-supervision network using their name and ID number.
Sources (2 references)
Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (Ministry of Education). Recognized Institution Lookup. http://yxcx.cscse.edu.cn/; Ministry of Education Foreign-Related Supervision Information Network. https://jsj.moe.gov.cn/
2

Watch the lawsuit over the new US F-1 rules: 'four years maximum, leave within 30 days of finishing' was set to take effect on September 15, 2026, but was suspended by a court the day before — for now 'duration of status' still applies

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The US planned to change F-1 status to a maximum of four years, with 30 days after finishing to leave. The day before it was to take effect, a federal court suspended it. So for now the old rule stands: you stay as long as you are enrolled, and after finishing you get 60 days to pack up and go. A suspension is not a repeal — the government can still appeal, and the rule could change again at any time.

Cost
Free. Copy the program end date on your I-20 into your calendar and set one reminder 90 days ahead. The I-20 is the certificate of study eligibility your school issues you. Also check your school's international student office announcements once a semester for news on the lawsuit
Benefit
On July 17, 2026, the Department of Homeland Security published a rule, originally set to take effect on September 15, 2026. Under it, F-1 students would no longer be admitted for "duration of status" but for a fixed period of up to four years, with a separate extension application required at expiration. After finishing studies or practical training, only 30 days would remain to leave. On September 14, 2026, Judge Saylor of the US District Court for the District of Massachusetts, invoking Section 705 of the Administrative Procedure Act, postponed the rule's effective date. The nationwide pause covers the entire rule. The court did not vacate the rule — the request to vacate was denied, but it may be raised again later. The case is still being heard. Under the court's order, holders of F, J, and I visas remain admitted for "duration of status," the 60-day departure grace period stays as before, and no separate extension application is needed
Note
Current as of September 25, 2026. The government can appeal to the First Circuit Court of Appeals, and DHS can revise the rule and reissue it. So if you will be studying for several years, do not assume the old rule will hold indefinitely. The court set October 2, 2026 for another hearing to hear both sides report on progress — after that date, check the school's announcements once more. If the new rule takes effect later, an extension must be applied for before the fixed period expires; it will not renew automatically. Under the old rule, the departure deadline for those who stop studying early differs from that for those who finish — ask the school's international student office first. J visas are covered by the same rule, but the details differ from F-1 — check according to your own visa category.
Sources (5 references)

Establishing a Fixed Time Period of Admission and an Extension of Stay Procedure for Nonimmigrant Academic Students, Exchange Visitors (published 2026-07-17, originally set to take effect 2026-09-15). https://www.federalregister.gov/documents/2026/07/17/2026-1…; Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security, No. 1:26-cv-13799-FDS (D. Mass. Sept. 14, 2026), court docket. https://www.courtlistener.com/docket/74661796/presidents-al…; Yale Office of International Students & Scholars (2026-09-14). Important Update: Court Action on the D/S Rule. https://oiss.yale.edu/news/important-update-court-action-on…; AILA (2026). One Day Before Taking Effect, Federal Court Postpones the F, J, and I Fixed Admission Period Rule. https://www.aila.org/blog/think-immigration-one-day-before-…; 8 CFR 214.2(f). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B…
3

Work-hour caps are hard red lines in all four countries — the US, Canada, the UK, and Australia; one hour over is a visa violation

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

All four countries cap work hours on student visas. Exceed the cap and you are violating your visa conditions — the visa can be cancelled, you can be deported, and every future application will draw questions. The caps: US, 20 hours a week; UK, 20 hours a week for degree-level study and 10 hours below degree level; Canada, 24 hours a week; Australia, 48 hours per fortnight. Two jobs means the hours count together.

Cost
Free. Keep a week-by-week log of your hours yourself. The hard part is employers who say "a few extra hours, nobody checks" — do not believe it
Benefit
In the US, F-1 students may work no more than 20 hours a week on campus during the semester. Approved off-campus part-time work carries the same 20-hour weekly limit. Full-time work is allowed during breaks. Basis: US federal immigration regulation 8 CFR 214.2(f)(9). On a UK student visa, those studying at degree level or above may work 20 hours a week during term; those below degree level, 10 hours a week. Part-time programs carry no work rights at all. Self-employment (working for yourself) is barred, as is work as a professional athlete or entertainer. Basis: the part of the UK Immigration Rules governing students, Appendix Student ST26.1 and ST26.5. In Canada, eligible full-time students may work off campus up to 24 hours a week; the basis is section 186(v) of Canada's Immigration and Refugee Protection Regulations (IRPR). On an Australian student visa, the cap is 48 hours per fortnight while the course is in session. Research master's and doctoral students and their family members are exempt from this limit
Note
In the US, off-campus work must be approved first. While the I-765 employment authorization application is still pending, you may not start work. Old Canadian permits printed "20 hours a week," but if you still meet the conditions you can in fact work up to 24 hours — current rules govern. The UK's self-employment ban is written broadly: taking private gigs, running an online shop, and freelancing all count.
Sources (4 references)
8 CFR 214.2(f)(9). https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B…; UK Home Office. Immigration Rules Appendix Student (ST26.1, ST26.5). https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-r…; IRCC. Work off campus as an international student. https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/s…; Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. Student visa (subclass 500). https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-l…
4

The root of your status is 'full-time enrollment': during leave, withdrawal, or transfer gaps, working is off the table entirely

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Whether you can work depends on whether you are currently enrolled full-time. The moment you take leave, withdraw, get expelled, or are between schools without attending classes, your work eligibility ends on the spot. Working past that point is illegal work. Many assume that as long as the visa has not expired they are fine — in fact their status broke long ago.

Cost
Free. Before pausing studies, taking leave, or switching schools, go to the school's international student office first and confirm your status
Benefit
Canada states explicitly that off-campus work is not allowed during an approved leave of absence. Students not studying during a transfer are likewise barred from off-campus work; only after resuming studies may they begin working again. In the US, on-campus work eligibility applies only to F-1 students whose SEVIS record shows Active. SEVIS is the US status-record system for international students; Active means enrolled and in valid status. These students must also maintain a full-time course load. In the UK, work permission is tied to the course type; part-time programs carry no work rights
Note
If course pressure has you thinking of dropping classes, first ask how far you can go before you stop counting as full-time. This one trips you up earlier than the work rules do. Those expelled, or whose program is terminated, usually lose status that same day. Do not wait for a formal letter from the school to act.
Sources (3 references)
IRCC. Work off campus as an international student. https://www.canada.ca/en/immigration-refugees-citizenship/s…; U.S. Department of Homeland Security, Study in the States. Working in the United States. https://studyinthestates.dhs.gov/students/work/working-in-t…; UK Home Office. Immigration Rules Appendix Student (ST26.1). https://www.gov.uk/guidance/immigration-rules/immigration-r…

US: report a new address within 10 days of moving

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

In the US, when you change where you live, the law requires notifying the immigration authorities within 10 days. Not reporting is not a small matter: it is itself a violation, and mail USCIS sends you will go astray.

Cost
Free. One online change-of-address filing, ten minutes
Benefit
US federal immigration regulation 8 CFR 265.1 requires aliens subject to registration to report within 10 days of changing address. Report to USCIS, in the manner it requires, both the fact that your address changed and the new address
Note
Reporting to USCIS is separate from updating your SEVIS record (your international-student status file) at the school. The other three countries also require notifying the immigration authorities or the school after a move. Deadlines and methods differ by country — follow the web pages of the immigration authority where you live.
Sources (2 references)
8 CFR 265.1. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-8/chapter-I/subchapter-B…; USCIS. AR-11, Alien's Change of Address Card. https://www.uscis.gov/ar-11

Before departure and while enrolled, keep an eye on the Ministry of Education's study-abroad alerts

Grade AValue: HighBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The Ministry of Education issues alerts targeted at a specific country or region, flagging that its recent security situation or policies are unfavorable to Chinese students. These are officially published risk warnings, there in black and white for anyone to check — more reliable than an agent's word. Looking costs nothing.

Cost
Free. Check once before departure, then once a semester
Benefit
The Ministry of Education publishes study-abroad alerts through its foreign-related supervision information network. Four were issued in 2025. No. 1 flagged negative China-related provisions in higher-education bills passed by certain US states (2025-04-09). Nos. 2 and 3 twice warned of frequent incidents targeting Chinese nationals and a poor study environment in the Philippines (2025-07-18 and 2025-08-30). No. 4 warned of Japan's security situation and poor study environment, advising caution in planning study there (2025-11-16)
Note
An alert is not a ban, and it does not mean you cannot go — it gives you an official yardstick for weighing local risks. The alert list changes with the situation; this section does not track it continuously, so go by the current pages on the website. For personal safety abroad and consular protection, see Section 21.

Australia: OSHC must cover the whole stay with no gaps in between — arrive without proof of insurance and you may be refused entry

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: a lotTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Australia wrote health insurance for international students into the visa conditions — it is not optional. The insurance must cover the entire stay. When renewing the visa and switching policies, there must be no gap in between. Arrive without proof of insurance and you may be refused entry on the spot. Family members who come along each need their own policy.

Cost
Several thousand to over ten thousand yuan. Buy in one lump sum for the length of the visa — study several years, buy several years
Benefit
Australia's Department of Home Affairs requires student visa applicants and their family members to hold Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), continuously for the whole stay in Australia, with no interruption. The insurance must be provided by an Australian-approved insurer, except where an exemption from the requirement applies. There must be no gap between the new insurance and the insurance under the previous visa. Arriving without proof of coverage can mean refusal of entry. For those entering earlier than the course start date, the policy start date should be the actual day of arrival in Australia
Note
If the school arranges the insurance, get the insurer's name, the policy's start and end dates, and the policy number — these must be entered in the visa application. Buying too short a term causes trouble at renewal; better to buy through graduation plus a little extra.
Sources (1 reference)
Australian Government Department of Home Affairs. Student visa (subclass 500). https://immi.homeaffairs.gov.au/visas/getting-a-visa/visa-l…
8

UK: on top of the visa fee there's an annual healthcare surcharge — £776 a year for students, paid in one lump sum when applying

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: a lotTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Going to the UK costs more than the visa fee. You must also prepay the healthcare surcharge for each year of the visa — only then can you use the UK's National Health Service. A two-year visa means paying £1,552 in one go. Add the visa fee itself, and this sum must be paid in full before departure — do not leave it out of the budget.

Cost
Visa fee £558. Healthcare surcharge £776 a year. Both paid in full at application
Benefit
The UK student visa fee is £558 — the same whether you apply from outside the UK, or extend or switch status in-country. On top of that comes the healthcare surcharge, required to use the UK's National Health Service, prepaid in one lump sum at application for each year of the visa. Students and their family members pay £776 a year — a 2-year visa is £1,552. Applicants in other categories pay £1,035 a year. Visas longer than 6 months but less than 1 year are charged as a full year
Note
Amounts and exchange rates change — use the current figures on the two source pages. Degree-level students aged 18 or over can generally stay up to 5 years; below degree level, 2 years. Use that length to estimate the surcharge.
Sources (2 references)
UK Government. Student visa. https://www.gov.uk/student-visa; UK Government. Pay for UK healthcare as part of your immigration application. https://www.gov.uk/healthcare-immigration-application
9

Allow time for credential verification before returning home: CSCSE verification takes 10 to 20 working days

Grade AValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

To use a foreign degree back home, it must first be verified. The review alone takes 10 to 20 working days. Job-hunting season or documents returned for correction stretch it longer still. Autumn recruitment, civil-service exam registration, and hukou applications all have deadlines — do not start when you already need the paper.

Cost
Apply online, pay online. Preparing the materials plus the review, counted in working days, comes to about a month end to end
Benefit
Verification of foreign academic degrees and diplomas is handled through the online service hall of the Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE). The process has four steps: register with real-name verification, submit the application and materials online, pay online, and wait for evaluation and review. The published processing time is 10 to 20 working days. Working days exclude weekends and holidays; this is the CSCSE's own review time
Note
The materials to submit are: the diploma or degree certificate, passport or travel permit, residence card or visa/entry endorsement, an ID photo, and an authorization statement. Entry-exit records from your time abroad are pulled by the system itself, so do not discard the visa pages from your years overseas. The CSCSE website also posts announcements voiding certain verification certificates and suspending verification applications from particular schools. Before you apply, check whether your school is named.
Sources (1 reference)
Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (Ministry of Education). Online Service Hall — Degree and Diploma Verification. http://zwfw.cscse.edu.cn/
10

The list of schools under 'enhanced review' for credential verification grows every year — the pay-for-a-diploma route is now a dead end

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The CSCSE names batches of foreign institutions whose credential verification gets extra scrutiny, and it also suspends verification applications from individual schools. The named schools are often exactly the type advertised as "no language requirement, no leaving China, a master's in a few months." Searching the school's name once before enrolling saves far more trouble than appealing afterwards.

Cost
Free. Before enrolling, search the school's name once in the CSCSE's announcements
Benefit
The Chinese Service Center for Scholarly Exchange (CSCSE) has issued a running series of announcements strengthening verification review of the credentials of certain foreign institutions (an extra layer of checking for diplomas from those schools). The latest is No. 9 (2025-10-28). The CSCSE has also announced the suspension of verification applications from particular overseas institutions, and issued warnings that some people use foreign credential verification to run scams
Note
"Enhanced review" does not mean verification is impossible, but you will be asked to submit more documents and it takes longer. Any agent promising "guaranteed verification" or "expedited through insider channels" is running a scam — the CSCSE has issued specific anti-fraud warnings. Having someone ghostwrite papers or take your online classes for you across borders, if caught, voids the credential and may also stain your visa record.
