33. How to Live After a Disability

20 items

This section is about life after a disability has already happened. How to prevent disability is covered in Sections 1 and 13; it is not repeated here. The four bases are tallied separately and not converted into one another. The entries on acute emergencies and complications are weighed by mortality. Those on subsidies, benefits, and lawsuits are weighed by money. Those on schooling and getting things done are weighed by time. Those on psychiatric hospitalization, legal capacity, and guardianship are weighed by personal freedom. The World Health Organization's fact sheet gives three numbers. About 1.3 billion people worldwide live with significant disability — 16% of the world's population, roughly one in six people. Some disabled people die up to 20 years earlier than people without disabilities. Disabled people face twice the risk of depression, asthma, diabetes, stroke, obesity, or poor oral health. A large share of these gaps comes not from the disability itself but from being unable to see a doctor, go to school, find a job, or leave the house. So this section's entries are half about the body, half about paperwork and rights. Five things already covered elsewhere are pointed to, not repeated: how to get a disability certificate and how the seven categories and grades 1 through 4 are assessed — Section 24, item 10 (Disability certificate); when to schedule a disability assessment — Section 24, item 9 (Disability assessment); how to claim the two subsidies for disabled people — Section 7, item 8 (The two subsidies); how work-injury work-capacity assessments and disability grades convert into money — Section 19, item 14 (Work-capacity assessment); and how to apply for long-term care insurance for severe disability — Section 17, item 7 (Long-term care insurance). That last entry sits in the "elderly at home" section, but the benefit has no age threshold — young people can claim it too. For most entries in this section, the beneficiary is you and your family — the top two tiers. Where others are affected, it is noted separately in the notes. This section's entries fall into the following groups by theme; item numbers are in parentheses. Body and rehabilitation: sudden severe headache after spinal cord injury (item 1), switching to a pressure-relief wheelchair cushion (item 5), not buying "cures for paralysis" (item 6), rehab at a proper facility (item 16), hearing aids for hearing loss (item 17). Benefits and subsidies: getting the full list of benefits in one visit to the disabled persons' federation (item 7), rehabilitation assistance for disabled children (item 8), subsidies for ramps, handrails, and bathroom modifications (item 9), personal income tax reductions (item 11). Jobs and asserting your rights: proactively disclosing your certificate when job hunting (item 10), suing when refused a job over disability (item 20). School and mobility: guide dogs in public places (item 12), reasonable accommodations on the gaokao (item 13), schools may not reject disabled children (item 14), and a driver's license is possible even without both legs (item 15). Mind and caregivers: suicide risk in the first ten years after disability (item 2), caregivers minding their own health (item 4). Mental disorders and guardianship: psychiatric hospitalization is voluntary in principle (item 3), capacity determinations require a court application (item 18), guardians are set by the statutory order (item 19).

1

After a spinal cord injury, sudden severe headache and sweating: sit the person upright, loosen their clothing, and call 120 at the same time

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

With a spinal cord injury, part of the body's alarm wiring is cut. A full bladder, clothing digging in — the person may feel none of it, while blood pressure surges. The warning signs are sudden severe headache and sweating. First sit the person upright, loosen tight clothing, check for a full bladder — and call 120 at the same time.

Cost
Free. Three actions, done in under a minute.
Benefit
The episode is called autonomic dysreflexia. A systematic review searched four databases — Medline, CINAHL, EMBASE, and PsycINFO — and included 31 studies, 6 of them randomized controlled trials. The review states that the non-drug response during an episode has three steps: place the patient upright, loosen tight clothing, and remove the triggering stimulus. These three steps rest on clinical consensus and physiological data — level 5 evidence. Antihypertensive drugs are used only when blood pressure stays elevated; prazosin has level 1 evidence, nifedipine and prostaglandin E2 level 2. The review also notes that prevention strategies mainly target the two most common triggers — urogenital problems and surgery — and most are backed only by level 4 and level 5 evidence
Note
Rated B because the three on-the-spot actions have no randomized controlled trials behind them — only consensus and physiological reasoning. The review itself says most of these measures rest on uncontrolled studies. The medication part is for doctors; do not give antihypertensives at home on your own. Laying the person flat raises blood pressure further — that is why you sit them up. Family members and aides should learn these three steps too. Do not tough it out as if it were an ordinary headache.
Sources (1 reference)
Krassioukov A, Warburton DE, Teasell R, Eng JJ; Spinal Cord Injury Rehabilitation Evidence Research Team (2009). A systematic review of the management of autonomic dysreflexia after spinal cord injury. Archives of Physical Medicine and Rehabilitation, 90(4):682-695. https://doi.org/10.1016/j.apmr.2008.10.017
2

The first ten years after becoming disabled are a high-risk window for suicide — not something to wave off with 'think positive'

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

In the first years after a disability, the injured person or the family falling apart emotionally is common — it is not a matter of willpower. Long-term follow-up at two UK spinal cord injury centers found this group's suicide rate was five times the general population's. Over ninety percent of the suicides happened within ten years of injury. For those whose injury was caused by their own suicide attempt, the risk climbs higher still.

Cost
Free. One phone call, or one appointment.
Benefit
The study followed 2,304 traumatic spinal cord injury patients admitted between 1991 and 2010 who survived their first year after injury and had neurological deficits at discharge, tracking them through the end of 2014. For 63 of them (2.7%), the cause of injury was itself a suicide attempt. By the end of follow-up, 533 had died; 4.2% of the deaths were suicide, and 91% of the suicides occurred within ten years of injury. The age-standardized suicide mortality rate was 62.5 per 100,000 per year (95% CI 36.4–88.6, credible interval), five times the 2014 suicide rate for the general population of England and Wales (12.2 per 100,000). Those injured in suicide attempts, compared with other causes of injury, had an odds ratio of 4.32 for death (P<0.001) and 9.46 for suicide (P<0.001)
Note
The study looked only at spinal cord injury; applying it to blindness, amputation, burns, and other causes of disability is extrapolation. What it does establish is the time window: the risk does not end at discharge — keep watch for ten years. For someone to talk to, call 12356 — see Section 29, item 11 (12356). Do not stockpile sleeping pills or pesticides at home — see Section 1, item 25 (Suicidal thoughts). If grief or low mood is still stuck in place after six months, book an appointment in psychiatry or clinical psychology — see Section 29, item 8 (Grief past six months).
Sources (1 reference)
Savic G, DeVivo MJ, Frankel HL, Jamous MA, Soni BM, Charlifue S (2018). Suicide and traumatic spinal cord injury - a cohort study. Spinal Cord, 56(1):2-6. https://doi.org/10.1038/sc.2017.98
3

Psychiatric hospitalization is voluntary in principle; only two situations allow admission without the person's consent

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

A word from family or an employer cannot keep a person hospitalized in a psychiatric ward. The law recognizes only two situations: the person has harmed themselves or poses that danger, or has endangered others or poses that danger. In the first situation, admission also requires the guardian's consent. If the diagnosis is disputed, a second diagnosis can be requested within three days, and afterwards an appraisal can be independently commissioned.

Cost
Free. Memorize the two situations so you can say them out loud when it matters.
Benefit
Article 30 of the Mental Health Law states: "Hospitalization for mental disorders follows the principle of voluntariness." Inpatient treatment shall be imposed only when the diagnostic conclusion and condition assessment show the patient has a severe mental disorder and one of the following applies: first, "they have already harmed themselves or pose a danger of harming themselves"; second, "they have already endangered the safety of others or pose a danger of doing so." Article 31: in the first situation, the medical institution may hospitalize only with the guardian's consent; if the guardian does not consent, it may not. Article 32: in the second situation, if the person or their guardian objects, they may request a second diagnosis — filed within three days of receiving the diagnostic conclusion and made by two licensed psychiatrists other than those who made the initial diagnosis; if they still dispute the second diagnosis, they may independently commission a legally qualified appraisal body to conduct a medical appraisal of the mental disorder. Article 35: if the second diagnosis or the appraisal report shows the person cannot be confirmed as having a severe mental disorder, or does not need hospitalization, the medical institution may not hospitalize them. Article 78: deliberately sending a person who does not have a mental disorder to a medical institution for treatment as a psychiatric patient carries liability for compensation under law (nationwide, effective May 1, 2013, amended 2018)
Note
The reverse is also true: it is not that nobody can be taken in for evaluation. Article 28 provides that where a person suspected of having a mental disorder has already harmed themselves or endangered others' safety, or poses that danger, their close relatives, employer, or local public security organ shall immediately take measures to stop it and send them to a medical institution for diagnosis. A medical institution that receives such a patient may not refuse to make a diagnosis. So "being sent for diagnosis" and "being kept in the hospital" are two different doors — the first is low, the second is high. Article 75 lists medical institutions' responsibilities: conducting restraint or segregation in violation of the rules, or diagnosing a person without a mental disorder as having one, is punishable by sanctions up to revocation of the practice license. For what to do when someone nearby has violent impulses, see Section 8.
Sources (1 reference)
Mental Health Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 amendment, Articles 30, 31, 32, 35, 78). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf744…
4

The one caring long-term for a disabled family member needs someone watching their own health too

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: large

A caregiver breaking down is not melodrama. A US study followed more than 800 older adults for four years. Those who cared for a disabled spouse while reporting mental strain had a death risk about 60% higher than non-caregivers. Caregivers who did not feel strained showed no such increase. So what needs watching is not the caregiving itself — it is the chronic strain.

Cost
Free. Hand off part of the caregiving, and get yourself a checkup.
Benefit
The study was a prospective population cohort, 1993 to 1998, average follow-up 4.5 years, conducted in four US communities: 392 caregivers and 427 non-caregivers, aged 66 to 96, all living with their spouse. Over four years, 103 participants (12.6%) died. After adjusting for sociodemographic factors, pre-existing illness, and subclinical cardiovascular disease, those who both provided care and reported mental or emotional strain had a 63% higher death risk than the non-caregiver controls (RR 1.63, 95% CI 1.00–2.65, credible interval). Caregivers who did not report strain (RR 1.08, 95% CI 0.61–1.90) and those whose spouse was disabled but who were not caregivers (RR 1.37, 95% CI 0.73–2.58) showed no elevated mortality after adjustment
Note
Controversy: the lower bound of this study's credible interval sits exactly at 1.00, so "no difference" is not fully ruled out. The population was older Americans living with their spouses, caring for disabled elderly spouses — applying it to people caring for young disabled family members is extrapolation. What it does show is the direction: the strained ones carry the higher risk. Hand off whatever care tasks can be handed off; ask the local disabled persons' federation and civil affairs office about residential care and day-care services. Caregivers should not stop their own chronic-disease medication — see Section 16, item 1 (Take medication as prescribed, the full course). The beneficiary of this entry is you yourself.
Sources (1 reference)
Schulz R, Beach SR (1999). Caregiving as a risk factor for mortality: the Caregiver Health Effects Study. JAMA, 282(23):2215-2219. https://doi.org/10.1001/jama.282.23.2215
5

Full-time wheelchair users: switch to a pressure-relief cushion and check your sit bones and tailbone every day

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: littleTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Ordinary foam cushions, pressed on long enough, break the skin — and broken skin heals slowly and infects easily. Nursing-home residents using pressure-relief cushions had markedly fewer pressure ulcers at the sit bones, but no difference showed once the tailbone was counted in. The wheelchair itself also needs to be fitted to the person — do not just buy a one-size-fits-all model.

Cost
A pressure-relief cushion runs a few hundred to over a thousand yuan. The daily check takes one minute.
Benefit
This randomized clinical trial ran in 12 nursing homes, enrolling 232 residents aged over 65 who sat in a wheelchair more than 6 hours a day with a Braden score of 18 or below, recruited from 2004 to 2008. Everyone first received a fitted wheelchair, then was randomized to two groups: one used skin-protective cushions (air, viscous fluid plus foam, or gel plus foam), the other used 7.6 cm segmented foam cushions. Follow-up ran 6 months or until a pressure ulcer appeared. At the ischial tuberosities, the segmented-foam group had 8 ulcers (6.7%) versus 1 (0.9%) in the skin-protective cushion group, P=0.04. Counting ischial and sacrococcygeal ulcers together, it was 21 (17.6%) versus 12 (10.6%), P=0.14 — no demonstrated difference
Note
Two reasons for the B rating. First, the sample was only 232, the primary endpoint's P value of 0.04 just cleared the line, and the secondary endpoint showed no difference. Second, the population was very old nursing-home residents — applying it to younger wheelchair users is extrapolation. Everyone in the trial first got a fitted wheelchair, so "fitting" and "cushion" worked together; do not just swap the cushion. For pressure-ulcer prevention for those bedridden long-term — air mattresses and regular turning — see Section 17, item 8 (Pressure ulcers). For how to apply for basic assistive-device subsidies, see item 7 of this section (Get the full list at the county disabled persons' federation).
Sources (1 reference)
Brienza D, Kelsey S, Karg P, et al. (2010). A randomized clinical trial on preventing pressure ulcers with wheelchair seat cushions. Journal of the American Geriatrics Society, 58(12):2308-2314. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1532-5415.2010.03168.x
6

Don't buy therapies or devices claiming to 'cure paralysis, blindness, or deafness'

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The Advertising Law closes the door on this. Ads for medical care, drugs, and medical devices may not guarantee efficacy, may not cite cure rates or effectiveness rates, and may not use people giving testimonials. So claims like "standing up after three courses of treatment" or "so many people have already recovered" are themselves illegal ads — no need to study the theory behind them. Products that are not medical devices are not even allowed to mention treating disease.

Cost
Costs nothing — it saves money. The hard part is family members full of hope whom you cannot talk out of it.
Benefit
Article 16 of the Advertising Law provides that ads for medical care, drugs, and medical devices may not contain: "(1) assertions or guarantees of efficacy or safety; (2) statements of cure rates or effectiveness rates; (3) comparisons with the efficacy and safety of other drugs or medical devices or with other medical institutions; (4) use of advertising spokespersons to make recommendations or give testimonials." Article 17 provides that apart from medical, drug, and medical-device advertising, "any other advertisement involving disease-treatment functions is prohibited, and medical terminology, or wording easily confused with drugs or medical devices, may not be used to promote goods." Article 4 provides that advertisements may not contain false or misleading content, may not deceive or mislead consumers, and advertisers are responsible for the truthfulness of their content (nationwide, 2021 amendment)
Note
There is only one test: does it dare to promise everything? A real hospital's rehabilitation department will never promise you will stand up after a few courses. Run into such advertising, report it to 12315 or the local market regulator. Health-supplement sales pitches run the same playbook — see Section 6, item 10 (Health supplements). Already bought it and want your money back — follow the online-shopping and prepaid-consumption routes — see Section 5, item 29 (Online shopping: the platform's rules govern). The beneficiaries of this entry are you and your family.
Sources (1 reference)
Advertising Law of the People's Republic of China (2021 amendment, Articles 4, 16, 17). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817ab231eb017abd6bd8…
7

Once the disability certificate comes through, visit the county disabled persons' federation and ask for the complete list of what you can apply for

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The disability certificate itself pays nothing — it is a key. Behind it sit several independent benefits, each of which must be applied for separately; none arrives automatically. On the first visit to the disabled persons' federation, walk through every item on the list one by one — it beats making several trips.

Cost
Free. One trip to the county disabled persons' federation, a morning of asking. More than one department will follow.
Benefit
At least six benefits hook onto the certificate, each with its own source. First, the living subsidy for disabled people in financial difficulty and the nursing-care subsidy for severely disabled people — see Section 7, item 8 (The two subsidies). Second, rehabilitation assistance for disabled children — see item 8 of this section (Rehabilitation assistance). Third, subsidies for basic assistive devices, based on Article 26 of the Regulation on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation. Fourth, home accessibility modification subsidies — see item 9 of this section (Ramps, handrails, and bathroom modifications). Fifth, quota employment and employment services — see item 10 of this section (Disclose your certificate). Sixth, personal income tax reductions — see item 11 of this section (Income tax reduction). Article 26 of the Regulation on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation also provides that the state delivers basic rehabilitation services to poor urban and rural disabled people and severely disabled people through key rehabilitation programs, and "subsidizes the provision of basic assistive devices in accordance with relevant state regulations." Article 20 provides that relevant departments of governments at or above county level and disabled persons' federations shall use community resources to establish rehabilitation facilities or purchase services, carrying out community rehabilitation work such as rehabilitation guidance, daily-living-skills training, rehabilitative nursing, assistive-device fitting, information consulting, and referrals (nationwide, effective July 1, 2017)
Note
For the certificate application process itself, see Section 24, item 10 (Disability certificate). Subsidy standards and implementation details are mostly set at the provincial level — the same benefit can differ severalfold between two provinces. As you ask, write down the name of each benefit, then at home look up the original documents by that name on the local federation's and the government's websites; do not rely on the counter clerk's verbal account. Do not expect one visit to cover everything — go ask again a year later, because policies change.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2017). Regulation on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation (Articles 20, 26). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-02/27/content_517…
8

For a child under 7 with a disability or autism, apply for rehabilitation assistance at the county disabled persons' federation

Grade AValue: HighBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: large

The state runs a rehabilitation assistance system for disabled and autistic children aged 0 to 6, covering surgery, assistive devices, and rehabilitation training. Assistance prioritizes families in difficulty; where local finances allow, the age and financial-condition limits can be relaxed. This stretch of life is the window when rehabilitation works best — do not wait until school age to deal with it. Pick the facility from the federation's designated list.

Cost
Free. File one application at the county disabled persons' federation, then choose one designated facility.
Benefit
The State Council Opinion on Establishing a Rehabilitation Assistance System for Disabled Children specifies that beneficiaries are eligible disabled children aged 0–6 with visual, hearing, speech, physical, or intellectual disabilities, and autistic children. This includes disabled children from urban and rural minimum-livelihood-guarantee households and from registered poverty-alleviation households, disabled children taken in and raised by child welfare institutions, disabled orphans, disabled children covered by support for people in extreme difficulty, and disabled children from other financially struggling families; the specific determination rules for other financially struggling families are set by local governments at or above county level. The document also states that "regions with the capacity may extend the age range for rehabilitation assistance for disabled children and may also relax restrictions on the family financial condition of beneficiaries." Funding standards are set by category by local governments at or above county level based on local fiscal capacity, the number of beneficiaries, disability type, and other factors, with a dynamic adjustment mechanism. The higher-level basis is Article 26 of the Regulation on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation: the state establishes a rehabilitation assistance system for disabled children, "gradually ensuring that children aged 0–6 with visual, hearing, speech, physical, or intellectual disabilities, and autistic children, receive surgery, assistive-device fitting, rehabilitation training, and other services free of charge" (nationwide, from 2018)
Note
Assistance standards are set by each province — first check the local federation's website for the "implementation measures for rehabilitation assistance for disabled children." The list of designated facilities is also in the federation's hands. The document requires federations, working with relevant departments, to tighten oversight of designated facilities' entry and exit, establish regular inspection and comprehensive evaluation mechanisms, and set up a blacklist system. A facility not on the list means you pay everything yourself and have little recourse when things go wrong. The beneficiary of this entry is your child — the second tier. Facilities promising "guaranteed results" are handled per item 6 of this section (Cures for paralysis).
Sources (2 references)
State Council (2018). Opinion on Establishing a Rehabilitation Assistance System for Disabled Children (Guo Fa [2018] No. 20). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2018-07/10/content_530…; State Council (2017). Regulation on Disability Prevention and Rehabilitation (Article 26). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-02/27/content_517…
9

Ramps, handrails, and bathroom modifications at home can qualify for subsidies from governments at or above county level

Grade BValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The Law on Building a Barrier-Free Environment contains this line: governments at or above county level shall support and guide accessibility modifications to homes and give appropriate subsidies to qualifying disabled and elderly households. These programs are generally led by the disabled persons' federation and run on annual quotas, so register early. How much is subsidized and which modifications are covered are set locally.

Cost
Applying is free. Most of the modification itself is subsidized, but you may still have to cover part. It means visits to the federation and the subdistrict office.
Benefit
Article 19 of the Law on Building a Barrier-Free Environment: "Governments at or above county level shall support and guide accessibility modifications to homes. Appropriate subsidies shall be given to disabled and elderly households that meet the conditions." Article 18: for existing residential buildings, residential areas, public buildings, public places, transport facilities, urban and rural roads, and the like that fail to meet accessibility construction standards, governments at or above county level shall formulate targeted accessibility modification plans according to actual conditions and organize their implementation. Article 62: any organization or individual has the right to submit opinions and suggestions on strengthening and improving the barrier-free environment to the relevant government departments, and to file complaints and reports about violations of this law; departments receiving complaints or reports "shall handle them promptly and give a reply." Article 63: for violations that harm the public interest, people's procuratorates may issue procuratorial recommendations or file public-interest lawsuits (nationwide, effective September 1, 2023)
Note
Rated B because the law only says "appropriate subsidies shall be given" — how much, and who counts as qualifying, are left entirely to localities, with no nationwide figure. First check the local federation's website for "accessibility modifications for households of disabled people with severe disabilities in difficulty." Quotas are mostly allocated by year, so queue up early. Elevator installation in residential compounds and stairwell modifications follow a separate process through the housing and construction department. For public accessibility that falls short, complain to the responsible department under Article 62 — it owes you a reply.
Sources (1 reference)
Law of the People's Republic of China on Building a Barrier-Free Environment (Articles 18, 19, 62, 63). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80818188d7430b0189018493…
10

When job hunting, proactively state that you hold a certificate — hiring you earns the company a deduction

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Employers must employ disabled people at no less than 1.5% of their total workforce — the exact ratio is set by each province. Falling short means paying the disability employment security fund for the shortfall in headcount, with each missing person billed at the company's average annual wage per employee from the previous year. So hiring you is not charity — it is real money saved. State clearly at the interview that you hold a certificate; the other side can do the math themselves.

Cost
Free. One extra sentence at the interview. The hard part is saying it.
Benefit
Article 8 of the Regulation on the Employment of Disabled People: "The ratio of disabled people employed by an employer shall be no lower than 1.5% of its total active workforce. The specific ratio is set by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or directly administered municipality according to local conditions." Article 9: employers below the ratio set by the provincial-level people's government where they are located shall pay the disability employment security fund. Article 8 of the Measures for the Collection and Use of the Disability Employment Security Fund gives the formula: "annual fund payment = (number of active employees in the previous year × the employment ratio for disabled people set by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or directly administered municipality where the employer is located − the number of disabled employees actually employed in the previous year) × the average annual wage per active employee in the previous year." Article 16: small and micro enterprises within 3 years of business registration that employ disabled people below the required ratio and have a total workforce of 20 or fewer (20 included) are exempt from the fund. Article 36 of the Law on the Protection of Disabled Persons provides that the state grants tax preferences under law to employers that meet or exceed the required ratio of disabled employees or employ disabled people in concentrated settings (nationwide; Regulation on the Employment of Disabled People effective May 1, 2007)
Note
For small or micro firms within three years of registration and with fewer than 20 employees, this argument does not hold — do not count on it. The fund's exemption policies have been adjusted over the years; go by that year's announcements from the Ministry of Finance. Also, quota employment requires genuine employment. Being on the payroll in name only so a company can offset the fund is fraud, and you would be dragged in too. For employment-difficulty status and social insurance subsidies, see Section 7, item 12 (People facing employment difficulties). For vocational training subsidies, see Section 7, item 13 (Vocational training subsidies). The beneficiary of this entry is you yourself.
Sources (3 references)
State Council (2007). Regulation on the Employment of Disabled People (Articles 8, 9). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_664…; Ministry of Finance, State Taxation Administration, China Disabled Persons' Federation (2015). Measures for the Collection and Use of the Disability Employment Security Fund (Cai Shui [2015] No. 72, Articles 6, 8, 16). http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2015-09/15/content_5650…; Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Disabled Persons (Article 36). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c…
11

Personal income tax can be reduced for disabled people; call the provincial tax bureau to find out by how much

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: small

The Individual Income Tax Law provides that the income of disabled people can receive a tax reduction. But how much, and for how long, are left to provincial governments, so provinces differ. Some provinces set an annual reduction cap; some reduce by a percentage. The way to find out is to call 12366 and ask the local tax bureau, or look for the reduction item in the Individual Income Tax app.

Cost
Free. Tick one item when filing, or submit filing materials once.
Benefit
Article 5 of the Individual Income Tax Law: "In any of the following circumstances, individual income tax may be reduced; the specific extent and duration are set by the people's government of the province, autonomous region, or directly administered municipality and filed for the record with the standing committee of the people's congress at the same level: (1) income of disabled people, widowed elderly people, and families of martyrs; (2) major losses suffered from natural disasters." Article 36 of the Law on the Protection of Disabled Persons further provides that the state grants tax preferences under law to disabled people running their own businesses and exempts them from administrative and institutional fees (nationwide; Individual Income Tax Law effective January 1, 2019)
Note
The benefit is rated "small" because the law itself gives no figures — in most provinces the reduction runs a few hundred to a few thousand yuan a year. Not much money, but one filing keeps working for years, so the trip is worth it. For your province's exact reduction, only the local tax bureau's announcements count — the comparison tables circulating online are permanently out of date. If you run your own small shop, administrative and institutional fees are waived under Article 36 of the Law on the Protection of Disabled Persons — raise it yourself when getting your license.
Sources (2 references)
Individual Income Tax Law of the People's Republic of China (2018 amendment, Article 5). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=2c909fdd678bf17901678bf724…; Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Disabled Persons (Article 36). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c…
12

Guide dogs can enter public places and public transport, and blind riders ride city buses free

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The law states that public places and public transport must accommodate disabled people accompanied by guide dogs, hearing dogs, or assistance dogs. Blind people ride city buses, subways, and ferries free with valid credentials, and disabled people may bring essential personal assistive devices free of charge. When someone blocks you, say these two provisions out loud; if that fails, file a complaint.

Cost
Free. Being stopped means speaking up and citing the law — you may have to hold your ground for a while.
Benefit
Article 46 of the Law on Building a Barrier-Free Environment: "Operators of public places, transport facilities, and public transport services shall provide convenience for disabled people accompanied by service dogs such as guide dogs, hearing dogs, and assistance dogs." Article 35: government-service hotlines and emergency call systems — police, fire, traffic accidents, medical emergencies — shall progressively acquire accessibility features such as voice, large text, braille, and one-touch calling. Article 62: any organization or individual has the right to file complaints and reports about violations of this law, and the responsible departments shall handle them promptly and give a reply. Article 50 of the Law on the Protection of Disabled Persons: "Blind people holding valid credentials ride city buses, trolleybuses, subways, ferries, and other public transport free of charge. Mail of braille reading materials is delivered free of charge." The same article provides that governments at or above county level shall give disabled people convenience and discounts when riding public transport, and disabled people may carry essential personal assistive devices free of charge (nationwide; Law on Building a Barrier-Free Environment effective September 1, 2023)
Note
The law says "provide convenience" but attaches no penalty, so in a standoff on the spot the other side will not necessarily back down at once. A screenshot of the law stored on your phone works better than memorizing article numbers. If it cannot be settled on the spot, file a complaint under Article 62 — the responsible department must reply. Railways and civil aviation have their own rules; confirm with customer service before traveling. Which "valid credentials" qualify for free rides is not entirely uniform across localities — ask the local disabled persons' federation which one is accepted.
Sources (2 references)
Law of the People's Republic of China on Building a Barrier-Free Environment (Articles 35, 46, 62). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff80818188d7430b0189018493…; Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Disabled Persons (Article 50). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c…
13

Disabled gaokao takers can apply for reasonable accommodations; those using braille papers get 50% more exam time

Grade AValue: FairBasis: TimeMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

Disabled gaokao takers can apply for braille papers, large-print papers, exemption from the foreign-language listening test, a separate exam room, and entry with hearing aids and a wheelchair — and exam time can be extended. None of this is automatic: a written application must be filed within the deadline set by the province, attached to a second-generation or later disability certificate. Unhappy with the result, you can ask the provincial education department for a review.

Cost
Free. One written application must be filed within the province's deadline, plus on-site confirmation.
Benefit
Article 5 of the Provisions on Disabled Persons Taking the National Unified College Entrance Examination lists twelve reasonable accommodations. They include providing current braille papers, large-print papers, or ordinary papers for visually disabled takers; exempting hearing-disabled takers from the foreign-language listening test; allowing visually disabled takers to bring assistive devices such as braille pens, braille slates, braille typewriters without storage, electronic video magnifiers without storage, white canes, and optical magnifiers; allowing hearing-disabled takers to bring hearing aids and cochlear implants; and allowing takers with limited mobility to use wheelchairs and walkers, with special desks and chairs permitted for those with special needs. The time extension is set in Article 5, item 6: "For visually disabled takers using braille papers, exam time is extended by 50% on top of the subject's total allotted time; for visually disabled takers using large-print or ordinary papers, and for takers with especially severe writing difficulty — such as those unable to write normally with their upper limbs because of cerebral palsy or other illnesses, or without upper limbs — exam time is extended by 30% on top of the subject's total allotted time." Also included: priority entering the test site and exam room, separate standardized exam rooms, and guides and sign-language interpreters. Article 7 sets the application procedure: the taker files a formal written application by the time, at the place, and in the manner prescribed by the provincial education examination authority, and provides their own disability certificate of second generation or later; an expert panel confirms on site and conducts a comprehensive evaluation, and the provincial education examination authority issues a Notification. Article 8: a taker who disputes the Notification may submit a written review application to the provincial education administrative department. Article 9: for those exempted from the foreign-language listening test, the foreign-language score is computed as "written-test score × total points of the foreign-language subject / total points of the written portion." Article 18: disabled persons needing reasonable accommodations in other national education examinations may proceed by analogy with these provisions (nationwide, issued and effective April 7, 2017)
Note
The application window is set by each province, written into that year's gaokao registration rules — miss it and it is gone. So confirm the dates on the provincial education examination authority's website in the first semester of senior year. Article 18 also provides that the postgraduate entrance exam, the adult gaokao, and other national education examinations may proceed by analogy. For the rule that schools may not reject disabled children, see item 14 of this section (Schools may not reject). The beneficiary of this entry is you or your child.
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Education and China Disabled Persons' Federation (2017). Provisions on Disabled Persons Taking the National Unified College Entrance Examination (Jiao Xue [2017] No. 4, Articles 5, 7, 8, 9, 18). http://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-04/12/content_5650…
14

Schools may not reject a disabled child's application for enrollment; those who can't reach school get home teaching arranged by the education bureau

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Kindergartens and schools of every type may not reject a qualifying disabled child's application for enrollment — ordinary vocational schools included. A child who needs dedicated nursing and cannot reach school gets home teaching or remote classes arranged by the county education bureau, with enrollment status all the same. Enrollment and transfers are decided by the education bureau after an expert committee's evaluation — not by the school's own word.

Cost
Free. One application, possibly one evaluation. When the school stalls, take it up the chain to the education bureau.
Benefit
Article 7 of the Regulation on the Education of Disabled Persons: "Preschool institutions, schools of all types and at all levels, and other educational institutions shall implement education for disabled persons in accordance with this Regulation and the relevant national laws and regulations; for disabled persons whose applications meet the conditions set by laws and regulations, they may not refuse admission." Article 29: "Ordinary vocational schools may not refuse to admit disabled persons who meet nationally prescribed admission standards, and ordinary vocational training institutions shall actively admit disabled persons." The Regulation further provides that school-age disabled children and adolescents who need dedicated nursing and cannot attend school receive compulsory education arranged by the education administrative department of the county-level people's government through home teaching, distance education, and similar means, with their status incorporated into enrollment management. Article 20: the county-level education administrative department, together with the health administrative department, the civil affairs department, and the disabled persons' federation, shall establish an expert committee on the education of disabled persons composed of experts in education, psychology, rehabilitation, social work, and related fields; the committee evaluates physical condition, ability to receive education, and ability to adapt to school life, and makes enrollment and transfer recommendations; the evaluation results are the child's privacy, and the relevant units and staff bear a duty of confidentiality. Article 23: disabled students studying in ordinary classes may follow the ordinary compulsory-education curriculum plans, standards, and textbooks, but their learning requirements may have appropriate flexibility. Article 52: disabled persons needing necessary support and reasonable accommodations in national education examinations may apply (nationwide, effective May 1, 2017)
Note
A school's verbal "we do not have the conditions here" counts for nothing. Demand a written reply and take it to the county education bureau. The evaluation is commissioned by the education bureau to the expert committee. The phrase in Article 23 — "learning requirements may have appropriate flexibility" — is very useful when a school tries to push your child out over grades. For how to preserve evidence of bullying at school and which procedures the school must follow, see Section 30, item 3 (School bullying). For gaokao accommodations, see item 13 of this section (Reasonable accommodations). The beneficiary of this entry is your child.
Sources (1 reference)
State Council (2017). Regulation on the Education of Disabled Persons (Articles 7, 20, 23, 29, 52). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2017-02/23/content_517…
15

Losing a right leg or both legs doesn't bar you from a driver's license — the vehicle class is called C5

Grade AValue: FairBasis: FreedomMoney: a lotTime: a lotWillpower: someBenefit: medium

People who have lost a right leg or both legs, or cannot move them, but can sit up steadily on their own and have adequate arm function can test for the disabled-only small automatic car license, class C5. Those missing one hand can apply too. People with single-eye vision impairment or hearing impairment each have classes they can test for. The physical exam must be done at a specialized hospital designated by the province.

Cost
Lessons cost about the same as an ordinary license — a few thousand yuan in most places. The car must be converted to hand controls. A physical exam every three years.
Benefit
Annex 1 of the Provisions on the Application and Use of Motor Vehicle Driving Licenses sets the physical conditions in fine detail. Item 8: "Those with a missing right leg or both legs, or loss of motor function in them, who can sit up and stand unaided, and whose upper limbs meet the conditions of item 5 of this provision, may apply for a motor vehicle driving license of the disabled-special small automatic passenger vehicle class. Those missing one hand whose other hand has a sound thumb and two other sound fingers, with normal motor function of the upper limbs and fingers, and whose legs meet the conditions of item 6 of this provision, may likewise apply for the disabled-special small automatic passenger vehicle class." Item 6: those missing only the left leg or having lost its motor function, with a normal right leg, may apply for the small automatic car class. On vision: "those with single-eye vision impairment whose better eye, uncorrected or corrected, reaches 5.0 or above on the logarithmic visual acuity chart, and whose horizontal visual field reaches 150 degrees," may apply for the small car, small automatic car, low-speed goods vehicle, three-wheeled car, and disabled-special small automatic passenger vehicle classes. On hearing: those with hearing impairment who can distinguish the direction of sound sources while wearing hearing devices may apply for the small car and small automatic car classes and must wear the hearing devices while driving. Article 85: the physical-condition certificate submitted for the disabled-special small automatic passenger vehicle license must be issued by a specialized medical institution accredited by the provincial health administrative department. Holders of this class must have a physical exam every three years and submit the certificate within 30 days after the end of each scoring cycle. Article 78: when driving, the dedicated disabled motorist sign must be displayed on the vehicle as required (nationwide; amended by MPS Order No. 172, effective January 1, 2025)
Note
The far lower-barrier option is the disabled motorized wheelchair. Article 119 of the Road Traffic Safety Law classifies it as a non-motor vehicle, so no license is needed; Article 58 provides that when traveling in non-motor-vehicle lanes its maximum speed must not exceed 15 km/h. A C5 car needs hand-operated throttle and brake; the conversion must be done by a qualified manufacturer, and after conversion the change must be registered at the vehicle administration office. Fail to submit the physical-condition certificate within one year after the end of three consecutive scoring cycles and the license is cancelled.
Sources (1 reference)
Ministry of Public Security Order No. 172. Provisions on the Application and Use of Motor Vehicle Driving Licenses (Articles 78, 85, Annex 1). https://www.gov.cn/gongbao/2025/issue_11866/202502/content_…
16

Do rehab at a proper facility with a rehabilitation medicine department; the intensity follows your therapist, and harder isn't better

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: a lotTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: large

Taking the person home to lie down and wait for natural recovery is the most common mistake. After a stroke, organized care by a multidisciplinary team leaves more people alive and living at home a year later. But do not add intensity on your own: after a stroke, training earlier, more often, and harder within the first 24 hours makes the three-month outcome worse. How much to train and when — follow the rehabilitation department and the therapists.

Cost
Inpatient rehabilitation runs several hundred yuan a day; the out-of-pocket share varies by place. Time is counted in months. Practice every day, and it is tedious.
Benefit
A Cochrane systematic review included 29 trials with 5,902 participants, comparing organized inpatient (stroke unit) care with other forms of care. At the final follow-up (median 1 year), the odds ratio for poor outcome (death, disability, or need for institutional care) was 0.77 (95% CI 0.69–0.87, credible interval), for death 0.76 (95% CI 0.66–0.88), and for death or dependency 0.75 (95% CI 0.66–0.85), with moderate-quality evidence. Converted to absolute numbers, for every 100 people receiving stroke unit care, 2 more survive, 6 more live at home, and 6 more manage daily life independently. On the other hand, the AVERT trial randomized 2,104 patients across 56 acute stroke units in 5 countries, comparing "usual care" with "usual care plus very early high-dose mobilization." At three months, good outcomes (modified Rankin Scale 0–2) were 480 (46%) in the very-early group versus 525 (50%) in the usual-care group, adjusted odds ratio 0.73 (95% CI 0.59–0.90, P=0.004). Deaths were 88 versus 72, with no demonstrated difference (odds ratio 1.34, 95% CI 0.93–1.93, P=0.113)
Note
Controversy: both pieces of evidence come from stroke; applying them to spinal cord injury, amputation, burns, and other causes of disability is extrapolation. What AVERT shows is that "earlier and more aggressive" does not hold — not that early mobilization is useless. In the trial, the vast majority in both groups were out of bed within 24 hours; what differed was frequency and total volume. When picking a facility, check whether it has a rehabilitation medicine department and dedicated rehabilitation therapists and occupational therapists — do not go by the word "rehab" on the signboard. For referrals between primary-level and tertiary hospitals and how deductibles are counted, see Section 24, item 1 (Step-by-step referral). For community rehabilitation and assistive-device fitting, see item 7 of this section (Get the full list at the county disabled persons' federation).
Sources (2 references)
Langhorne P, Ramachandra S; Stroke Unit Trialists' Collaboration (2020). Organised inpatient (stroke unit) care for stroke: network meta-analysis. Cochrane Database of Systematic Reviews, 4:CD000197. https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD000197.pub4; AVERT Trial Collaboration group (2015). Efficacy and safety of very early mobilisation within 24 h of stroke onset (AVERT): a randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 386(9988):46-55. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(15)60690-0
17

When hearing declines, get hearing aids — the reason is to hear, not to prevent dementia

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MortalityMoney: a lotTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

The claim that "hearing aids prevent dementia" has not held up so far. A three-year trial with nearly a thousand people found no overall difference. A difference appeared only in the subgroup already at higher risk of cognitive decline. So the reason to get hearing aids is to hear now — to talk with people and hear cars when crossing the street — not for your brain decades from now.

Cost
Hearing aids run several thousand to tens of thousands of yuan, mostly out of pocket. They need professional fitting and several trips back for adjustment.
Benefit
The ACHIEVE trial ran in 4 US communities, enrolling 977 people aged 70 to 84 with untreated hearing loss and no significant cognitive impairment. They were randomized to a hearing intervention (hearing counseling and hearing aids) or a health-education control, with follow-up every 6 months. The primary endpoint was the 3-year change in overall cognitive score. In the primary analysis pooling the two source populations, there was no significant difference between groups: hearing intervention −0.200 (95% CI −0.256 to −0.144), control −0.202 (95% CI −0.258 to −0.145), difference 0.002 (95% CI −0.077 to 0.081), P=0.96. A prespecified sensitivity analysis showed the intervention effect differed between the two source populations (interaction P=0.010). Participants drawn from that long-running observational Cardiovascular Health Study were older, had more risk factors for cognitive decline, and scored lower on baseline cognition. The researchers' conclusion: hearing intervention may reduce 3-year cognitive change in people at higher risk of cognitive decline, but not in those at lower risk. The trial reported no serious adverse events attributed to the intervention
Note
Controversy: the widely shared claim online that "hearing aids cut cognitive decline by nearly half" comes from a subgroup of this trial, not its primary result — the primary result was no difference between the groups. Keep "getting hearing aids" and "preventing dementia" separate: the former is worth doing; do not make the latter the reason. Hearing-disabled gaokao takers can be exempted from the foreign-language listening test — see item 13 of this section (Reasonable accommodations). People with hearing impairment must wear hearing devices when driving — see item 15 of this section (C5).
Sources (1 reference)
Lin FR, Pike JR, Albert MS, et al.; ACHIEVE Collaborative Research Group (2023). Hearing intervention versus health education control to reduce cognitive decline in older adults with hearing loss in the USA (ACHIEVE): a multicentre, randomised controlled trial. Lancet, 402(10404):786-797. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(23)01406-X
18

Declaring an adult 'unable to manage their own affairs' requires applying to a court for a ruling — family members don't get the final say

Grade AValue: FairBasis: FreedomMoney: littleTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Whether an adult is "without civil capacity" or "with limited civil capacity" can be determined only by a court. Family members, employers, and neighborhood committees do not get to decide on their own. An interested party or a relevant organization must apply to the court. The reverse holds too: when intellect or mental health recovers, a ruling that capacity has been restored can be requested. This procedure is both a restriction and a protection.

Cost
Applying to the court carries a filing fee, generally tens to one hundred yuan. The appraisal fee is separate, usually several thousand yuan, advanced by the applicant. The whole process takes months.
Benefit
Article 21 of the Civil Code: "An adult unable to comprehend their own conduct is a person without civil capacity, whose civil juridical acts are performed on their behalf by their statutory agent." Article 22: "An adult unable to fully comprehend their own conduct is a person with limited civil capacity; their civil juridical acts are performed on their behalf by their statutory agent or with the statutory agent's consent or ratification — but they may independently perform juridical acts that purely benefit them or that match their intellectual and mental condition." Article 24: "For an adult unable to comprehend, or unable to fully comprehend, their own conduct, an interested party or a relevant organization may apply to the people's court to have the adult declared a person without civil capacity or with limited civil capacity." The same article provides that after such a declaration, upon application by the person, an interested party, or a relevant organization, the people's court may, based on the state of their intellectual and mental recovery, declare them restored to limited or full civil capacity. Relevant organizations include: residents' committees, villagers' committees, schools, medical institutions, women's federations, disabled persons' federations, lawfully established organizations for the elderly, and civil affairs departments, among others. Article 23: the guardian of a person without or with limited civil capacity is their statutory agent (nationwide, effective January 1, 2021)
Note
The application goes through the court's special procedure — faster than an ordinary civil case, but still a few months. A hospital diagnostic certificate must be submitted, and the court will in most cases commission a forensic appraisal; the appraisal fee, usually several thousand yuan, is advanced by the applicant. Sign for someone or dispose of their property without this procedure and the act may later be declared invalid — a sold house may have to be handed back. One more thing to remember: limited civil capacity does not mean they can do nothing. Matters matching their intellectual and mental condition, and matters that purely benefit them, they can do themselves — do not take over everything. For how the guardian is set, see item 19 of this section (Guardian).
Sources (1 reference)
Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 21, 22, 23, 24). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…
19

An adult's guardian is set by the statutory order; if the ward hurts someone, the guardian pays

Grade AValue: FairBasis: FreedomMoney: noneTime: moderateWillpower: someBenefit: medium

Once an adult loses capacity, guardians follow a set order: spouse; then parents and children; then other close relatives; finally other individuals or organizations willing to serve. Disputes are settled by designation from the residents' committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department; if you dispute the designation, go to court. While the person is still of sound mind, a future guardian can be designated in writing. If the ward hurts someone, the guardian pays.

Cost
Free. Disputes take you to the residents' committee, villagers' committee, civil affairs department, or court.
Benefit
Article 28 of the Civil Code: for adults without or with limited civil capacity, guardians serve in the following order from among those with the capacity to guard: "(1) spouse; (2) parents and children; (3) other close relatives; (4) other individuals or organizations willing to serve as guardian, subject to the consent of the residents' committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department of the ward's place of residence." Article 31: disputes over who is to be guardian are resolved by designation by the residents' committee, villagers' committee, or civil affairs department of the ward's place of residence; a party disputing the designation may apply to the people's court for designation, or apply directly to the people's court. In designating, "the ward's true wishes shall be respected, following the principle of what most benefits the ward." Where the ward's interests are left unprotected before a designation is made, the residents' committee, villagers' committee, a legally designated organization, or the civil affairs department serves as temporary guardian. Article 33: "An adult with full civil capacity may, through prior consultation with their close relatives or other individuals or organizations willing to serve as guardian, designate their own guardian in writing." Article 1,188: "Where a person without or with limited civil capacity causes harm to others, the guardian bears tort liability. A guardian who has diligently performed their guardianship duties may have the tort liability mitigated." Where the ward has property, compensation is paid from the ward's own property, and the guardian covers any shortfall. Article 1,189: where a guardian entrusts guardianship duties to another, the guardian still bears tort liability, and the entrusted party bears corresponding liability when at fault (nationwide, effective January 1, 2021)
Note
Article 33 is voluntary guardianship. Settling on the person in writing while the individual is still of sound mind eliminates most later disputes — for how to write it, see Section 17, item 1 (Voluntary guardianship). Be careful with the compensation part: handing the ward to a care institution or a relative does not shift the guardian's responsibility — the entrusted party bears liability only when themselves at fault. So buying guardian liability insurance for the ward is worthwhile. Article 78 of the Mental Health Law also provides that a guardian who abandons a patient or fails to perform guardianship duties, causing damage, bears compensation liability under law.
Sources (1 reference)
Civil Code of the People's Republic of China (Articles 28, 31, 33, 1,188, 1,189). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff808081729d1efe01729d50b5…
20

Being refused a job, denied a permanent post, or underpaid over disability is grounds to sue — but first count the cost of the process

Grade AValue: FairBasis: MoneyMoney: a lotTime: a lotWillpower: yesBenefit: medium

The law forbids discriminating against disabled people in hiring, conversion to permanent status, promotion, professional-title evaluation, pay, or social insurance. You can complain to the responsible department, or sue in court. But even winning the lawsuit does not make the other side pay your lawyer. So complain first, apply for legal aid at the same time, and only then consider litigating.

Cost
Lawyer fees run several thousand to tens of thousands of yuan, paid by you. First-instance ordinary procedure starts at 6 months and can be extended. Evidence is yours to preserve.
Benefit
Article 3 of the Law on the Protection of Disabled Persons: "Discrimination on the basis of disability is prohibited. Insulting or infringing upon disabled people is prohibited." Article 38: "In the hiring of staff, conversion to permanent status, promotion, professional-title evaluation, labor remuneration, welfare, rest and leave, social insurance, and other aspects, disabled people may not be discriminated against." The same article provides that the employer of a disabled employee shall provide appropriate working conditions and labor protection suited to the employee's characteristics and, as actually needed, modify workplaces, labor equipment, and living facilities. Article 64: "Where this law is violated by discrimination against disabled people in the hiring of staff and other matters, the responsible department shall order correction; disabled workers may file suit with the people's court under law." Article 4 of the Regulation on the Employment of Disabled People: "Discrimination in employment is prohibited." Article 13: employers may not discriminate against disabled employees in promotion, advancement, professional-title evaluation, remuneration, social insurance, welfare, or the like. Article 42 of the Legal Aid Law provides that an applicant with materials proving they belong to "specific groups such as minors, elderly people, or disabled people without a fixed source of livelihood" is exempt from the financial-hardship check. Article 45: legal aid institutions providing legal aid services to elderly and disabled people shall provide accessible facilities, equipment, and services according to actual conditions (nationwide)
Note
Count the process cost first. First-instance ordinary procedure runs from 6 months and can be extended; the simplified procedure, 3 months. Lawyer fees are not among the litigation costs listed in Article 6 of the Measures on the Payment of Litigation Fees, and Article 29's rule that the losing party bears the costs does not include lawyer fees. So take the two low-cost routes first: complain to the human resources and social security department or the disabled persons' federation, and the responsible department will order correction; meanwhile apply for legal aid — Article 42 exempts disabled people from the financial-hardship check. Evidence is the hardest hurdle. When refused after an interview, the other side rarely leaves a written reason; record audio and keep chat logs wherever you can. If already employed, go through labor-dispute arbitration; for preserving evidence and time limits, see Section 19, item 8 (Preserve evidence before leaving). The beneficiary of this entry is you yourself.
Sources (3 references)
Law of the People's Republic of China on the Protection of Disabled Persons (Articles 3, 38, 64). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8080816f135f46016f1d134c…; State Council (2007). Regulation on the Employment of Disabled People (Articles 4, 13). https://www.gov.cn/zhengce/zhengceku/2008-03/28/content_664…; Legal Aid Law of the People's Republic of China (Articles 42, 45). https://flk.npc.gov.cn/detail?id=ff8081817b6472a3017b657782…

34. Don't Let Your Home Medicine Cabinet Hurt You

11 items

Fever reducers, painkillers, cold medicines, stomach remedies, anti-diarrheals — many of these you can buy yourself at a pharmacy. Being able to buy them without a prescription doesn't mean you can take them however you like. This section does not cover which medicine to take for every ailment; it picks out the few things where one single action keeps a serious outcome away. All entries are tallied on a mortality basis, counting health endpoints such as liver failure, stomach bleeding, and newborn kidney failure. Most of the benefits amount to "one fewer serious accident." Studies cannot give a number for "how much less often this happens if you do it," so the benefit rating is judged by how severe the consequence is, and each entry's Note explains what it was based on. Topics already covered elsewhere get only a pointer here. For what to do first when a medicine or cleaner is swallowed by mistake, see Section 13, item 20 (accidental swallowing). For finishing chronic-disease medicines exactly as prescribed, see Section 16, item 1 (finish medicines as prescribed). For the prescription review required before buying prescription drugs online, see Section 28, item 6 (get weight-loss drug prescriptions at the hospital). The beneficiaries of this section's entries are you yourself and your family — the two highest tiers.

1

Before taking two cold or pain medicines at once, read the ingredient lists — acetaminophen should be in only one of them

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Many cold medicines have acetaminophen mixed in. Take two boxes together and you have taken a double dose, and an overdose damages the liver. In the US, of the patients whose acute liver failure it caused, nearly three in ten died before a liver transplant could happen. Chinese package inserts recommend at most 2 grams a day, and no alcohol while taking it.

Cost
Free. One look at the ingredient list on each box, a minute or two.
Benefit
22 US hospitals continuously registered 662 cases of acute liver failure over 6 years. Of these, 275 (42%) were caused by acetaminophen, with a median ingested dose of 24 grams. Of those 275 people, 131 (48%) had overdosed by accident, not on purpose. Among the accidental overdoses, 38% had taken two or more medicines containing this ingredient at the same time. Of the 275, 27% died before a transplant could happen and 8% received a liver transplant. In 2020, China's National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) required OTC package inserts to state that overdose causes serious liver injury and to recommend a maximum daily amount of no more than 2 grams. The insert must also say to avoid combining it with other medicines containing acetaminophen or other fever- and pain-relieving drugs. US regulations require such OTC drugs to put three liver-harming situations at the top of the warning: exceeding the maximum daily amount; taking it together with other medicines containing acetaminophen; and drinking 3 or more alcoholic drinks a day while using it.
Note
Acetaminophen is also called paracetamol. Combination cold medicines whose generic names contain "anfen" (the Chinese shorthand for acetaminophen) — such as Anfen Weima or Anka Huangmin — contain this ingredient. If you are not sure, take all the boxes to the pharmacist at the drugstore. Rated B because the US figures come from a case registry with no control group, so there is no way to calculate how many accidents reading ingredient lists prevents. Benefit is rated "large" on the severity of the consequence: nearly three in ten with acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure die.
Sources (3 references)
Larson AM, Polson J, Fontana RJ, et al.; Acute Liver Failure Study Group (2005). Acetaminophen-induced acute liver failure: results of a United States multicenter, prospective study. Hepatology, 42(6):1364-1372. https://doi.org/10.1002/hep.20948; NMPA announcement on revising the package inserts for immediate-release and sustained-release acetaminophen preparations (No. 15 of 2020), with Annex 2, "Revision Requirements for the OTC Package Insert of Immediate-Release Acetaminophen Preparations" (republished by the Hunan Provincial Medical Products Administration). http://mpa.hunan.gov.cn/mpa/xxgk/tzgg/wjtz/202003/t20200311…; 21 CFR 201.326(a)(1)(iii)(A) Liver warning. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-…
2

No aspirin, nimesulide, or metamizole for a child's fever, and no cold medicines containing metamizole for minors either

Grade BValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

For a child's fever, steer clear of all three drugs. Aspirin is linked to Reye's syndrome, a disease that damages the brain and liver; in US statistics about three in ten affected children died, and after the warning went out, cases fell by more than 90%. Nimesulide is banned under 12; metamizole is banned under 18.

Cost
Free. One look at the generic name and ingredient list when buying fever medicine.
Benefit
Reye's syndrome causes encephalopathy and fatty change in the liver, usually after flu or chickenpox. In US national surveillance from 1981 through 1997, 1,207 cases were reported in people under 18. Salicylates — the drug class aspirin belongs to — were detectable in the blood of 82% of the sick children. Overall fatality was 31%. Warnings on salicylate drugs began in 1980. That year 555 cases were reported, the peak; from 1987 on, no more than 36 a year. In 2011, China's State Food and Drug Administration ruled that oral nimesulide preparations are banned in children under 12. In 2020, the NMPA banned metamizole tablets in children and adolescents under 18. Compound artemisia–metamizole tablets, Zhongganning tablets, and Zhongganning capsules, which contain metamizole, are likewise banned under 18.
Note
Metamizole is not a first-choice drug for adults either. Its insert states it can cause agranulocytosis, aplastic anemia, and anaphylactic shock, and it is for short-term use only when the illness is acute and severe and no other effective drug is available. Zhongganning sounds like an ordinary cold medicine, but it contains metamizole. For which fever medicine a child should take and how much by body weight, ask a pediatrician or pharmacist. A fever in a baby under 3 months means going straight to the hospital — see Section 20, item 8 (go straight to the hospital at 38°C). Rated B because the Reye's syndrome figures come from surveillance reports; the drop in cases followed the warnings — a before-and-after relationship, not a controlled trial. Benefit is rated "large" because after the warnings, cases fell from 555 a year to under 36.
Sources (3 references)
Belay ED, Bresee JS, Holman RC, Khan AS, Shahriari A, Schonberger LB (1999). Reye's syndrome in the United States from 1981 through 1997. New England Journal of Medicine, 340(18):1377-1382. https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJM199905063401801; Notice on strengthening the management of the use of oral nimesulide preparations (State FDA [2011] No. 209). https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/xxgk/fgwj/gzwj/gzwjyp/2011051514510…; NMPA announcement on revising the package inserts of metamizole-related products (No. 34 of 2020), with Annexes 1 to 3. https://www.nmpa.gov.cn/directory/web/nmpa/xxgk/ggtg/ypggtg…
3

If you're over 60, have had stomach bleeding, or take anticoagulants or steroids, ask a doctor before taking ibuprofen-type painkillers

Grade AValue: ExceptionalBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: large

Painkillers like ibuprofen, naproxen, and aspirin injure the stomach. In high-dose trials, people taking ibuprofen had about 4 times the risk of stomach bleeding or perforation as those not taking it. The risk is higher for people who are older, have had stomach bleeding, also take anticoagulants or steroids, or drink alcohol every day.

Cost
Free. One question to a doctor or pharmacist.
Benefit
These drugs are called NSAIDs — non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs; common ones are ibuprofen, naproxen, and diclofenac. A meta-analysis pooled 280 randomized trials of these drugs against placebo, 124,513 people in all. Versus placebo, the risk of upper gastrointestinal perforation, obstruction, or bleeding: ibuprofen RR 3.97 (95% CI 2.22–7.10, about 4 times), naproxen 4.22 (2.71–6.56), diclofenac 1.89 (1.16–3.09). Every drug in this class roughly doubles the risk of heart failure. US regulations require this class of OTC drugs to carry a stomach bleeding warning. The warning lists six groups at higher risk: people over 60; those who have had stomach ulcers or bleeding; those taking anticoagulants or steroids; those taking other drugs of this class; those who drink 3 or more alcoholic drinks a day while using the product; and those who take more, or for longer, than the label says.
Note
The paper's conclusions concern high-dose use. It gives no separate numbers for taking it occasionally for a day or two at label doses. Many combination cold medicines also contain this class of ingredient; taking them together with a painkiller doubles up, so read the ingredient list first. If a doctor has you on long-term low-dose aspirin to prevent blood clots, do not stop it on your own, and do not add another painkiller on your own either.
Sources (2 references)
Coxib and traditional NSAID Trialists' (CNT) Collaboration; Bhala N, Emberson J, Merhi A, et al. (2013). Vascular and upper gastrointestinal effects of non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs: meta-analyses of individual participant data from randomised trials. Lancet, 382(9894):769-779. https://doi.org/10.1016/S0140-6736(13)60900-9; 21 CFR 201.326(a)(2)(iii)(A) Stomach bleeding warning. https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/chapter-I/subchapter-…
4

For a cold in a child under 2, don't give combination cold medicines or cough medicine on your own

Grade BValue: HighBasis: mortalityMoney: noneTime: littleWillpower: noneBenefit: medium

The NMPA requires 14 children's combination cold medicines to add a warning: parents are not advised to give them to children under 2 on their own; use them only under a doctor's or pharmacist's guidance. In trials done on children, cough suppressants and antihistamines performed no better than placebo.

Cost
Free, and it saves the money you would have spent on the medicine.
Benefit
In Announcement No. 57 of 2021, the NMPA revised the package inserts of 14 products, including Anfen Mamei oral solution, Xiao'er Anfen Huangnamin granules, and Xiao'er Anfen Wan'an granules. The new warning statement is "It is not recommended that parents or guardians give this product to infants and toddlers under 2 on their own; it should be used under the guidance of a physician or pharmacist." The precautions add "Use strictly according to the directions and dosage in the package insert and avoid overdose" and "Avoid combining with other cold medicines that contain the same or similar active ingredients." A Cochrane systematic review included 29 randomized controlled trials, 10 of them in children. In the children's trials, none of these drug classes beat placebo: cough suppressants; antihistamines (the anti-allergy ingredients); antihistamines plus decongestants (the nose-clearing ingredients); and cough suppressants plus bronchodilators. 21 trials reported adverse effects, and preparations containing antihistamines and dextromethorphan had more of them.
Note
Many of the 14 products carry "anfen" (the Chinese shorthand for acetaminophen) in their names and contain acetaminophen as well; taking them together with a fever reducer doubles up — see item 1 of this section (acetaminophen). One trial in that review found honey worked better than placebo, but babies under 1 must not be given honey — see Section 20, item 6 (honey). Rated B because the trials per drug class in the review were few, and the authors did not pool the numbers. Benefit is rated "medium" by judgment: these drugs have no proven benefit for small children, and the risks are mainly overdose and duplicated ingredients.
